note: Synthetic. Every person, company, publication, project and patent is invented; any resemblance to real ones is a coincidence. Institutions are real faculties of the University of Novi Sad, used as a setting only.

projects.title: AGROSAT: satellite monitoring of field crops in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (synthetic)
projects.summary: AGROSAT addresses the need for timely, spatially detailed monitoring of field crops across Vojvodina, the dominant agricultural zone of Serbia. Led by Prof. Stanković as principal investigator, the project develops an end-to-end satellite analytics platform that ingests Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery in near real time and produces a suite of agronomically relevant maps at the parcel level, including crop type, phenological stage, above-ground biomass, and early-season yield forecasts. The system is designed for direct integration with national agricultural advisory infrastructure and with the digital farming platforms of participating agri-tech partners. A key objective is to benchmark satellite-derived estimates against an instrumented field network of 60 monitoring sites distributed across the main soil types of Vojvodina, ensuring traceability and operational accuracy standards. AGROSAT also includes a citizen-science component in which farmers contribute ground-truth observations via a mobile application, creating a self-sustaining label acquisition mechanism for ongoing model refinement.

projects.title: SOILSCAN: soil health indicators from space
projects.programme: Horizon Europe (synthetic)
projects.summary: SOILSCAN is a Horizon Europe collaborative project that develops novel remote sensing indicators of soil health by exploiting the synergy between multi-source satellite observations and advanced soil biogeochemical modelling. Prof. Stanković leads the work package responsible for producing spatially continuous maps of soil organic carbon, nitrogen mineralisation potential, and compaction risk across the Pannonian lowlands and two additional European pilot regions. The project integrates Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 multispectral, and EMIT hyperspectral satellite data with a harmonised in-situ soil sampling dataset contributed by six partner institutions across four countries. Machine learning emulators trained on process-based soil model outputs are used to propagate satellite observations into subsurface soil health indicators not directly observable from space. SOILSCAN outputs will be made freely available through a FAIR-compliant open data portal and are designed to directly inform the EU Soil Health Law monitoring framework currently under development.

projects.title: WATERWISE: irrigation advice for smallholders
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education (synthetic)
projects.summary: WATERWISE was a two-year applied research project funded by the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education, led by Nenad Ilić as principal investigator. The project aimed to develop and validate a low-cost, user-friendly irrigation advisory system tailored specifically to smallholder farmers in Vojvodina who lack access to agronomic consultancy services. The core output was a mobile decision support application integrating Penman–Monteith evapotranspiration calculations with readings from inexpensive capacitive soil moisture probes. The system was piloted on 20 smallholder farms growing vegetables and sugar beet across three municipalities. Training workshops were delivered to participating farmers, and feedback was incorporated into iterative improvements of the interface. The project also produced calibrated crop coefficient datasets for key Vojvodina crops and a publicly accessible guide to affordable soil moisture monitoring, disseminated through the provincial agricultural extension service.

projects.title: FIELDNET: rural sensor networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (synthetic)
projects.summary: FIELDNET: Rural Sensor Networks is a research project funded by the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, running from 2022 to 2024. The project addresses the practical challenges of deploying and sustaining large-scale LoRaWAN-based wireless sensor networks in rural agricultural environments, with a focus on the flat and semi-hilly terrain of the Vojvodina region. Key research activities include field characterisation of LoRa propagation in open farmland, development of energy-harvesting node platforms capable of multi-year unattended operation, design of adaptive duty-cycling and network scheduling algorithms to maximise packet delivery ratio under dense deployment conditions, and investigation of gateway placement strategies for heterogeneous node populations. Ana Kovačević contributes to the hardware design, firmware development, and field measurement campaigns within the project, working alongside agronomists and telecommunications engineers to ensure that network performance meets the data quality requirements of precision agriculture decision-support systems.

projects.title: ORCHARD-IPM: pest warning service
projects.programme: Ministry of Agriculture (synthetic)
projects.summary: The ORCHARD-IPM project, funded by the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Serbia, aimed to establish a real-time pest warning service for apple and pear growers across northern Serbia. Led by Prof. Pavlović as principal investigator, the project deployed a network of over fifty pheromone trap stations across Vojvodina and the Fruška Gora area, collecting weekly codling moth flight data that were fed into a degree-day forecasting model accessible through a web portal and SMS alert service. Over its four-year duration, the project enrolled more than 180 registered orchard farms and demonstrated a documented reduction in fungicide and insecticide application events through timely, model-based spray window recommendations. The project also produced standardised field protocols for trap deployment, validated lure replacement schedules, and delivered training workshops for agricultural extension advisors in three districts. Infrastructure developed under ORCHARD-IPM directly underpinned subsequent research into automated IoT-based trap stations and image-recognition tools for insect counting.

projects.title: FRESHROUTE: cold chain for Serbian berries
projects.programme: Innovation Fund (synthetic)
projects.summary: FRESHROUTE addressed the systemic cold-chain weaknesses that reduce the competitiveness of Serbian raspberry, blueberry, and strawberry exports in EU markets. As academic partner, Professor Marković's team contributed validated predictive microbial growth models, MAP packaging specifications, and field sensor studies to a consortium that also included fruit exporting companies and a logistics technology provider. The project mapped temperature abuse events across 18 commercial export routes, quantified their microbiological consequences, and translated findings into revised pre-cooling protocols and MAP gas-mix recommendations adopted by partner exporters. A digital dashboard incorporating predictive shelf-life models was prototyped for real-time logistics decision support. FRESHROUTE resulted in three peer-reviewed publications, one conference presentation, and directly influenced cold-chain standard operating procedures at two partner export facilities, contributing to measurable reductions in consignment rejection rates at Western European destinations.

projects.title: BRANVALUE: from milling waste to food ingredients
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (synthetic)
projects.summary: BRANVALUE is a 2023–2025 project led by Ivana Lukić as principal investigator, funded under the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. The project addresses the valorization of wheat bran, a major milling industry by-product generated in significant quantities across Serbia. Its central objective is to develop scalable bioprocess routes—primarily solid-state and submerged fermentation combined with enzyme-assisted extraction—for converting wheat bran into commercially viable food ingredients including dietary fibre fractions, protein-enriched ingredients, and phenolic compound extracts such as ferulic acid. The project integrates process optimisation, functional characterisation, and preliminary techno-economic analysis, aiming to provide a complete scientific and technological basis for industry adoption. BRANVALUE is designed with direct relevance to Serbian flour milling enterprises and food ingredient manufacturers, with dissemination activities targeting both scientific and industrial audiences.

projects.title: GRIDHEALTH: condition-based maintenance for the distribution grid
projects.programme: Horizon Europe (synthetic)
projects.summary: GRIDHEALTH is a Horizon Europe research project running from 2022 to 2025, led by Professor Marko Petrović as principal investigator. The project develops a comprehensive condition-based maintenance (CBM) framework for medium-voltage distribution grids, with particular emphasis on oil-immersed power transformers as the most critical and failure-costly asset class. Core activities include: the deployment of online dissolved gas analysis sensors at a network of instrumented substations; the development and validation of machine-learning failure prediction models trained on multi-operator historical datasets; the design of a health-index aggregation methodology that integrates DGA, oil quality, thermal history, and electrical test data; and the creation of a decision-support tool for maintenance scheduling under budget constraints. The project involves collaboration with two distribution system operators and an industrial sensor manufacturer, ensuring that all methods are validated under real operating conditions and are deployable within existing grid management infrastructure. Results are being disseminated through open-access publications and a publicly available data schema standard.

projects.title: SRB-NLP: open language resources for Serbian
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (synthetic)
projects.summary: The SRB-NLP project aims to build a comprehensive suite of open language resources for Serbian, addressing a long-standing gap in the NLP ecosystem for South Slavic languages. The project encompasses the creation of large pre-training corpora, fine-tuning datasets for core NLP tasks including named entity recognition, question answering, semantic similarity, and intent detection, as well as the training and public release of transformer-based language models tailored to Serbian. A central objective is ensuring that all resources support both Latin and Cyrillic scripts on equal footing. The project also includes the design and dissemination of standardised evaluation benchmarks to enable reproducible comparison of future Serbian NLP systems. Running from 2023 to 2026 with funding from the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, the project involves collaboration between linguists and computer scientists and is committed to open science through the public release of all data, model weights, and code.

projects.title: FLEXGRID-RS: flexibility markets for Serbia
projects.programme: Horizon Europe (synthetic)
projects.summary: FLEXGRID-RS: Flexibility Markets for Serbia is a Horizon Europe research project running from 2023 to 2026 that aims to design, pilot, and evaluate flexibility market mechanisms tailored to the institutional and technical context of the Serbian power system. The project addresses the full value chain of demand-side flexibility, from the characterisation of available flexibility assets at industrial, commercial, and residential sites, through aggregation and virtual power plant architectures, to the clearing algorithms and settlement rules of local flexibility markets operated by distribution system operators. Prof. Simić contributes her expertise in renewable forecasting and demand response modelling to the project's workpackage on forecast-driven flexibility scheduling, developing probabilistic tools that allow DSOs to procure flexibility resources in response to anticipated renewable generation imbalances. The project maintains active links with Serbian energy regulators and a regional DSO partner.

projects.title: VISIONQC: AI quality control for SMEs
projects.programme: Innovation Fund (synthetic)
projects.summary: VISIONQC aims to bring AI-powered quality control capabilities within reach of small and medium enterprises that lack the data infrastructure and machine learning expertise of large manufacturers. The project develops a modular inspection platform combining few-shot defect detection, synthetic data augmentation, and edge-deployable quantized models, enabling SMEs to configure reliable inspection pipelines with minimal labeled data and without cloud dependency. As academic partner, Stojanović leads algorithm development and validation, ensuring that research outputs are translated into production-ready components. Pilot deployments are conducted at two regional manufacturing SMEs producing metal and polymer components, with key performance indicators targeting detection accuracy above 90% and setup time under two working days per new product type. The project runs from 2023 to 2025 under the Innovation Fund (synthetic) program.

projects.title: LASTMILE-NS: city logistics for Novi Sad
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education (synthetic)
projects.summary: LASTMILE-NS: City Logistics for Novi Sad is a research project funded by the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education, running from 2021 to 2023, with Professor Luka Vuković as principal investigator. The project addresses the growing challenges of urban freight distribution in Novi Sad, focusing on the design and evaluation of optimised last-mile delivery strategies for the city. Key activities include the collection and analysis of real parcel-demand and traffic data, the development of vehicle routing models that account for time windows, traffic congestion, and environmental constraints, and the assessment of consolidation and crowdsourcing strategies. The project also examines the potential deployment of urban consolidation centres and electric vehicle fleets within the Novi Sad urban network. Results are intended to inform municipal logistics policy and provide a modelling toolkit transferable to other cities in the Vojvodina region.

projects.title: KORPUS-NS: a reference corpus of contemporary Serbian
projects.programme: Ministry of Science (synthetic)
projects.summary: KORPUS-NS aims to create a 500-million-token reference corpus of contemporary Serbian serving as the primary large-scale resource for linguistic research, lexicography and natural language processing in Serbia. Led by Professor Nikolić as principal investigator, the project encompasses text collection from journalism, literature, academic writing, legal texts, social media and transcribed speech, as well as the development of a full annotation pipeline covering tokenisation, lemmatisation, part-of-speech tagging and morphosyntactic description. A custom morphological lexicon, a web concordancer, and open-source processing tools are being released progressively throughout the project period. KORPUS-NS is expected to become the standard empirical reference for Serbian linguistics and to supply training and evaluation data for downstream computational applications in industry and academia.

projects.title: HEARTWATCH: remote cardiac monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (synthetic)
projects.summary: HEARTWATCH is a three-year research project funded by the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, running from 2022 to 2025, with Associate Professor Maja Popović serving as principal investigator. The project addresses the clinical need for reliable, long-term remote cardiac monitoring outside hospital settings, targeting particularly the early detection of atrial fibrillation in high-risk populations. The core technical objective is the development of a complete algorithmic stack—spanning signal quality assessment, motion-artifact suppression, real-time arrhythmia classification, and adaptive false-alarm reduction—capable of executing on a low-power wearable ECG patch. A secondary objective is the creation of a clinically annotated benchmark dataset in partnership with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. By project completion, HEARTWATCH aims to deliver open-source firmware validated in a prospective pilot study involving at least 120 participants, providing a translational foundation for commercialization through collaboration with medical device companies.

projects.title: TELECARE-HF
projects.programme: Ministry of Health (synthetic)
projects.summary: The TELECARE-HF project is a prospective, multi-centre randomised controlled trial investigating the impact of structured telemonitoring on clinical outcomes in patients discharged after acute heart failure hospitalisation. Funded by the Ministry of Health and running from 2021 to 2024, the study enrols patients at three cardiology centres across Vojvodina, comparing a daily remote monitoring intervention—encompassing weight, blood pressure, heart rate, and symptom reporting via a dedicated application—against standard outpatient follow-up. Primary endpoints include all-cause mortality and unplanned rehospitalisation at six months, with secondary endpoints covering quality of life, medication adherence, and healthcare resource utilisation. Professor Tomić serves as principal investigator, overseeing study design, ethics approval, site coordination, and data analysis. The project also functions as a platform for validating patient-reported outcome instruments and for assessing the feasibility of integrating telemonitoring infrastructure within the regional public health system. Industry co-funding for device procurement and connectivity infrastructure is a central component of the project's sustainability model.

projects.title: AQUALOSS: reducing water losses in Vojvodina towns
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat (synthetic)
projects.summary: The AQUALOSS project, funded by the Provincial Secretariat for Science and Technological Development of Vojvodina, addresses the persistent problem of high water losses in small and medium-sized towns across the Vojvodina region of Serbia. Led by Zoran Kostić as principal investigator, the project combines calibrated hydraulic modelling, district metered area establishment, pressure management interventions, and sensor-based leak localisation to deliver an integrated water loss reduction methodology adapted to the specific infrastructure characteristics of Vojvodina municipal networks. Partner utilities in three towns provide field access, flow and pressure monitoring data, and operational co-operation. Expected outcomes include a transferable protocol for active leakage control, a set of regionally calibrated benchmarks for non-revenue water performance, and capacity building for utility staff in the use of hydraulic model tools for day-to-day operational decision-making.

projects.title: SECURE-ICS: security monitoring for factories
projects.programme: Innovation Fund (synthetic)
projects.summary: SECURE-ICS addresses the growing need for robust cybersecurity monitoring in industrial manufacturing environments. The project develops an integrated security monitoring platform tailored specifically to factory automation systems, encompassing network traffic analysis, anomaly detection, and real-time alerting for operational technology networks. As academic partner, the University of Novi Sad team led by Professor Đukić contributes expertise in intrusion detection algorithm design, threat modelling for ICS environments, and evaluation methodology. The platform targets Modbus, PROFINET, and EtherNet/IP protocol stacks commonly found in Serbian manufacturing facilities. Deliverables include a deployable monitoring agent, a validated anomaly detection model trained on representative factory traffic, and a set of security assessment guidelines for small and medium enterprises in the industrial sector. The project runs from 2023 to 2025 under the Innovation Fund programme.

projects.title: SMARTHERD: sensor-based herd health
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (synthetic)
projects.summary: SMARTHERD is a three-year applied research project (2023–2026) funded through the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, led by Professor Nevena Bošković as principal investigator. The project aims to develop a validated, integrated sensor-based herd health monitoring platform tailored to the operational realities of commercial dairy farms in Vojvodina. Core research activities include the deployment and longitudinal evaluation of activity, rumination, and bolus-based sensor systems across a network of partner farms, followed by the development and training of multi-parameter disease prediction algorithms for mastitis, ketosis, and lameness. SMARTHERD also incorporates a data architecture workstream focused on creating an open, interoperable data pipeline that can connect sensor outputs with existing farm management software. A field validation phase in the final project year will benchmark the integrated platform against individual sensor systems. The project has a strong knowledge-transfer component, with plans to produce extension guidelines and engage NTP Novi Sad agri-tech companies in co-development activities.

projects.title: Formal Model-Driven Interface Generation and Adaptation for Heterogeneous Enterprise Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FORMIGA developed a toolchain for specifying enterprise integration architectures in a formal DSL and automatically generating executable interface adapters from detected mismatches. The project produced three tool components: a metamodel editor built on Eclipse EMF, a mismatch analyser using constraint solving, and an ATL-based code generator targeting Apache Camel. Validation was carried out with two companies in the Vojvodina region operating heterogeneous ERP and MES systems. The project trained two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. A public repository containing the toolchain and all benchmark models was released under an open-source licence at project completion.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Mathematical Institute, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts

projects.title: Integration Middleware for Edge-Cloud Continuum in Smart Manufacturing
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: INTEDGE addresses the challenge of integrating edge computing nodes with cloud-hosted enterprise systems in small and medium manufacturing enterprises along the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Bošković leads the work package on formal interface specification and automated adapter generation for edge device protocols. The project involves four partners across two countries and targets deployment pilots in two manufacturing SMEs. The formal methods component builds directly on the adapter generation framework from earlier research, extending it with resource-constrained runtime profiles suitable for edge hardware. Expected outputs include a reusable pattern library for edge-cloud integration and two pilot deployments.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Bay Zoltán Nonprofit Ltd. for Applied Research, Miskolc

projects.title: Adaptive Parametric Templates for Multi-Format Print and Digital Publishing in Small and Medium Enterprises
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated how small and medium-sized printing and design companies in Serbia can adopt parametric template workflows without the large upfront authoring investment that such systems typically require. Research activities included a needs survey of 41 SMEs in Vojvodina, development of a simplified template authoring toolkit with a graphical constraint editor, and a pilot deployment at three partner companies over a period of eight months. The project produced a reference methodology for template migration from flat layout files and a set of 14 open document template archetypes covering the most common SME document types. Two master's theses and one doctoral chapter were produced within the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Grafotisak Novi Sad d.o.o.

projects.title: Automated Testing Strategies for Legacy-to-Cloud Migration Pipelines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TESTMIG investigates how automated test generation and fuzzing techniques must be adapted when software systems are migrated from monolithic on-premise deployments to cloud-native architectures. The project produces a methodology covering three migration phases: pre-migration characterisation of testability impediments, migration-parallel differential testing, and post-migration regression suite maintenance. Empirical validation is conducted on a testbed of five anonymised legacy applications provided by two industrial partners under non-disclosure agreement. Deliverables include an open-source toolchain integrating the methodology with standard CI/CD platforms, a dataset of annotated migration artefacts, and a training module for practitioners. The project supports two PhD students and multiple master's theses.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Cloud Testing and Service Reliability for Regional Digital Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CLOTSER is a cross-border cooperation project addressing software testing capacity in the Hungary–Serbia border region, where a growing number of small software companies lack access to automated testing expertise and tooling for cloud deployments. The project establishes a shared testing competence centre with nodes at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and a Hungarian technical college, provides training workshops to regional SMEs, and funds applied research into lightweight test automation suitable for small development teams. Andrea Jovanović leads Work Package 3, which covers the technical research component on coverage measurement and fuzzing for SME-scale cloud services. Two joint pilot deployments with regional software companies are planned for the final project year.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Pannon Institute of Technology, Pécs (invented)

projects.title: Stochastic Resource Management Models for Elastic Cloud Infrastructures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STOCRES addresses the gap between classical queuing theory and the operational complexity of elastic cloud platforms. The project develops analytical and simulation-based models for auto-scaling, spot-instance bidding, and fault-tolerant scheduling, validated on a private cloud testbed hosted at the Faculty of Sciences. The team consists of four researchers from the Faculty of Sciences and one collaborator from the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad. Key deliverables include a publicly released simulation library, three journal publications, and a short course on stochastic methods for cloud engineers offered once per year. The project also funds two PhD students working on edge-cloud offloading and serverless latency modelling, respectively.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Mathematical Foundations of Latency-Aware Scheduling in Edge-Cloud Continuum Networks
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: EDGEMATH is a bilateral research and capacity-building project between the University of Novi Sad and the Budapest University of Technology and Economics. The Serbian team, led by Đukić, is responsible for Work Package 2 covering stochastic modelling and optimal control of offloading decisions at edge nodes. The Hungarian team contributes network measurement infrastructure and machine-learning expertise. The project includes three joint workshops, a summer school for doctoral students, and the co-development of a shared dataset of edge-node workload traces. Expected outputs include joint publications, a prototype offloading policy library, and recommendations for testbed operators on dimensioning warm-standby capacity.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Department of Networked Systems and Services, Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

projects.title: Green ICT Infrastructure Assessment for Serbian Digital Transition
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a localised life-cycle inventory dataset for ICT infrastructure components reflecting the energy mix, logistics, and end-of-life conditions specific to Serbia and the wider Western Balkans. Existing global LCA databases systematically underrepresent regional conditions, leading to inaccurate carbon footprint calculations for domestic operators and policymakers. The project combines primary data collection from data centres, mobile operators, and enterprise IT departments with process modelling to extend the ecoinvent database with Serbian-specific unit processes. A public-access LCA tool for SME-scale ICT operators is being developed as a deliverable. Partners include the Faculty of Technical Sciences, the Institute for Standardisation of Serbia, and two ICT companies from Science and Technology Park Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Standardisation of Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Environmental Assessment Framework for Digital Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: ECODIGIT addressed the absence of harmonised environmental assessment methods for cross-border digital infrastructure investments co-financed by EU pre-accession funds. Tešić led the work package responsible for developing a common carbon accounting protocol applicable to fibre network and mobile backhaul projects spanning the Romanian–Serbian border region. The work package produced a practical handbook adopted by two regional development agencies as a reference document for environmental pre-feasibility assessments. The project also conducted training workshops for 34 engineers and planners from both countries. Collaboration with Politehnica University of Timișoara was central to the methodological harmonisation effort.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Morphological Resources and Transfer Methods for Extremely Low-Resource Slavic and Finno-Ugric Language Pairs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MORPHEX addressed the absence of usable parallel corpora and morphological tools for minority and regional language varieties spoken in northern Serbia and neighbouring regions: Rusyn, Bunjevac, Romani as spoken in Vojvodina, and Vojvodina Hungarian. The project assembled new annotated corpora, trained and evaluated morphological analysers using finite-state and neural methods, and tested cross-lingual transfer strategies for machine translation into and out of Serbian. A particular focus was placed on measuring how paradigm overlap between donor and recipient language predicts transfer efficiency. The project produced open-licensed lexicons, a shared-task dataset, and a web demonstrator for morphological analysis of the four target languages.
partners: Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Belgrade

projects.title: Shared Language Technology Infrastructure for Adriatic and Pannonian Languages
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: ADRIA-NLP is a consortium of eleven institutions across six countries building shared NLP infrastructure—corpora, annotation tools, and pre-trained language models—for eleven under-resourced languages of the Adriatic and Pannonian region, including Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian, Hungarian, Romanian, Albanian, and Macedonian. Uroš Janković leads the work package on cross-lingual morphological processing, responsible for harmonising tagsets across languages, delivering a shared morphological annotation pipeline, and coordinating evaluation campaigns. The work package also produces training materials for annotators and a data-sharing protocol compliant with GDPR and the European Language Data Space framework.

projects.title: Sparse-Data Recommendation Strategies for Small and Medium Retailers in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SPAREC brought together researchers from Subotica and Debrecen to collect, anonymise, and jointly analyse transaction data from small retailers operating in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region. The project aimed to produce recommendation methods and practical implementation guidelines suited to retailers with fewer than five hundred active customers and limited IT infrastructure. Erić led the work package responsible for algorithm development and evaluation, coordinating the construction of the shared benchmark dataset later published in 2022. The project also delivered a publicly available technical report and two workshops for regional retailers on practical data collection practices that improve recommendation feasibility without requiring expensive system upgrades.
partners: Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen, Hungary

projects.title: Transfer Learning Methods for Retail Recommendation Under Data Scarcity
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RETRANSFER investigates the conditions under which item and user representations learned in data-rich retail environments can be transferred to data-scarce ones, with a focus on the small independent retail sector in Serbia. The project develops alignment methods that require only partial catalogue overlap between source and target retailers, establishes empirical thresholds for transfer viability, and examines how transferred representations interact with cold-start recommendation pipelines. Research is conducted on datasets collected through ongoing retail partnerships and through the shared dataset established under SPAREC. The project involves collaborators from the University of Pavia and is expected to produce four journal papers, one publicly released software toolkit, and training materials for retail technology practitioners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Computer Science, University of Pavia, Italy

projects.title: Formal Verification Methods for Workflow Execution Engines in Industry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FORMWORK investigated scalable formal verification techniques for workflow execution engines used in industrial process management software. The project developed modular reachability analysis methods, incremental re-verification algorithms after workflow updates, and a translation toolchain from BPMN 2.0 to verifiable Petri net representations. Industrial workflow specifications were obtained from four partner companies in the manufacturing and logistics sectors in Vojvodina. The project produced eleven peer-reviewed publications, two open-source tool extensions (LoLA and CPN Tools plugins), and a publicly available benchmark suite of 320 annotated workflow nets. One master's thesis and two doctoral dissertations were completed within the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Compositional Verification of Concurrent Business Processes Across Organisational Boundaries
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CONCVER addressed the formal verification of cross-organisational business processes, where separate companies operate workflow engines that interact via message exchange. The project developed a compositional verification framework based on communicating workflow nets, with interface compatibility checking and deadlock analysis for multi-party collaboration diagrams. Serbian and Hungarian academic and industrial partners contributed process models from the agri-food supply chain sector. Aleksa Lazić led Work Package 3, responsible for formalisation of the collaboration model and the design of the verification algorithms. The project organised three joint workshops attended by 74 participants from both countries.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics

projects.title: Interoperable Telematics Infrastructure for Cross-Border Freight Corridors in the Vojvodina–Romania Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed a shared telematics data infrastructure connecting freight operators in the Vojvodina region of Serbia and in the Timiș and Caraș-Severin counties of Romania. Mamužić led the work package on data standards and interoperability, responsible for defining the shared positional event schema, designing gateway APIs, and coordinating integration tests with four participating logistics companies. The work package produced a reference implementation deployed at the border crossing at Vršac–Moravița, along with an open technical specification document. The project also funded two PhD students, one at each side of the border, and delivered training workshops for transport authority staff in both countries.

projects.title: Probabilistic Real-Time Arrival Estimation for Public Transport Using Heterogeneous Data Sources

projects.title: Scalable Finite Element Solvers for Industrial Real-Time Simulation on Heterogeneous Architectures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SCALEFEM develops domain decomposition-based finite element solvers that achieve real-time or near-real-time performance on heterogeneous CPU–GPU computing hardware, targeting industrial simulation tasks in structural mechanics and computational fluid dynamics. The project focuses on three specific bottlenecks: coarse-space construction cost in BDDC methods, dynamic load balancing across heterogeneous nodes, and mixed-precision solver pipelines that exploit GPU half-precision throughput without sacrificing solution accuracy. The project involves close collaboration with colleagues at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering in Kragujevac, and funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher. A database of in-service PSD profiles for four machinery classes was compiled. The framework was demonstrated on three industrial case-study structures, with predicted lives compared against fleet service data. projects.title: Optimisation Methods for Transport Workforce Scheduling in Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: OPTRANS addresses workforce scheduling challenges faced by public transport operators in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region, where different national labour laws complicate driver assignment across borders. Malešević leads the work package on mathematical modelling and algorithm development, responsible for formulating a unified multi-jurisdiction rostering model and implementing a branch-and-price prototype. The project produces a comparative analysis of Hungarian and Serbian labour-law constraints, a shared benchmark dataset of anonymised driver scheduling instances from partner operators, and a decision-support prototype demonstrated at two transport companies. Training workshops for transport planners are delivered in Subotica and Pécs.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Operations Research, Corvinus University of Budapest, Hungary
Vojvodina Public Transport Research Institute (fictional)
South Transdanubia Regional Transport Development Centre (fictional)

projects.title: Probabilistic Short-Term and Long-Term Workforce Absence Forecasting Using Survival Analysis and Transfer Learning
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the problem of predicting employee absence events and durations in organisations with limited historical records. The core methodological contributions covered three areas: survival models adapted for interval-censored absence durations, transfer learning strategies for adapting models across organisational units with distributional shift, and online Bayesian updating procedures for maintaining model performance as workforce composition changes over time. The project involved collaboration with three partner organisations in Vojvodina that provided anonymised HR data under data-sharing agreements. A prototype forecasting tool with an API was developed and tested in pilot deployments at two partner sites. The project supported two PhD students and resulted in eight peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Economics Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Public Health of Vojvodina
Logistika Vojvodina d.o.o. (fictional company)

projects.title: Federated and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning for Cross-Organisational Human Resources Analytics
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: This Horizon Europe project brings together eight partners from Serbia, Germany, Hungary, and Greece to develop federated learning frameworks for HR analytics use cases, with absence prediction and employee retention modelling as primary demonstrators. Knežević leads the work package on statistical modelling and evaluation methodology, responsible for defining common evaluation protocols, implementing federated survival analysis components, and coordinating the privacy impact assessment of gradient-sharing schemes. The project combines methodological research with technology transfer activities including two open-source software releases and a standardised benchmarking dataset constructed from synthetic data calibrated to real HR distributions. Three industrial partners contribute use-case requirements and serve as deployment environments for pilot evaluations.
partners: TU Dresden, Faculty of Computer Science
University of Debrecen, Faculty of Informatics
Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, School of Informatics
DataVantage GmbH (fictional company)
PannonSoft Kft. (fictional company)
