projects.title: Constraint-Based Spatial Content Generation for Training and Simulation Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SPACEGEN investigates the combination of constraint-satisfaction methods and graph-grammar formalisms to generate spatial layouts for use in emergency-response training simulations and serious-game platforms. The project develops a middleware library that exposes a unified API to both a CSP solver backend and a graph-transformation engine, allowing designers to specify spatial requirements declaratively. Validation work involves partners from a regional civil-protection agency who supply domain requirements and evaluate generated training scenarios. The project funds two PhD students, produces open-source tooling, and contributes benchmark datasets for the procedural generation research community. A secondary strand examines formal verification of safety properties in generated scenarios.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Regional Civil Protection Agency of Vojvodina (fictional)

projects.title: Cross-Border Procedural Planning Support Tools for Small Municipalities
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSPLAN develops grammar-based decision-support tools for small municipalities on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border that lack dedicated urban-planning departments. The tools allow planning officers without technical backgrounds to specify high-level spatial requirements through a web interface; a procedural back-end generates compliant layout proposals for pedestrian zones, green spaces, and small public squares. Sanja Krstić leads the work package responsible for grammar design, constraint encoding of accessibility and zoning regulations, and integration testing. Two Serbian and two Hungarian municipalities serve as pilot sites. The project also includes training workshops for municipal staff.
partners: Department of Urban Planning, University of Pécs, Hungary
Municipality of Bački Petrovac, Serbia (fictional representative municipality)
Municipality of Mohács, Hungary (fictional representative municipality)
Center for Urban Development Research Subotica (fictional)

projects.title: Visual Speech Animation for Accessible Talking Interfaces in Low-Resource Languages
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat VISATALK bavio se razvojem sistema za animaciju lica pokretanu govorom prilagođenog jezicima sa ograničenim resursima, pre svega srpskom i albanskim. Osnovna istraživačka pitanja bila su: koliko parnih snimaka govora i animacije je minimalno potrebno za upotrebljiv sistem, i kako tehnike transfera znanja mogu smanjiti tu granicu. U okviru projekta snimljen je novi korpus od 4,8 sati parnih audio i performance-capture snimaka, razvijeni su evaluacioni protokoli, a finalni demonstrator integrisao je sistem u web-zasnovanu aplikaciju za pristupačnost. Projektom su finansirane dve doktorske stipendije.
partners: Filozofski fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Institut za veštačku inteligenciju Srbije, Novi Sad

projects.title: Multilingual Facial Animation Corpus and Benchmark for South-East European Languages
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MULTIFACE je transnacionalni projekat koji za cilj ima izgradnju zajedničke višejezičke baze podataka animacija lica i govornih snimaka za srpski, mađarski i hrvatski jezik, uz definisanje zajedničkih vizem skupova i evaluacionih protokola prilagođenih ovim jezicima. Uloga Dunje Erić obuhvata koordinaciju paketa rada za akviziciju podataka i normalizaciju anotacija vizema. Baza će biti javno dostupna po završetku projekta. Planirano je prikupljanje najmanje 20 sati parnih snimaka ukupno na tri lokacije.
partners: Pécsi Tudományegyetem, Mađarska
Sveučilište u Osijeku, Hrvatska
Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Diagnostic Inference from Behavioural Trace Data in Digital Learning Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated psychometric and statistical methods for inferring cognitive skill states from the behavioural trace data produced by digital learning platforms, specifically focusing on contexts where traditional item-level ground-truth labels are unavailable or unreliable. Research activities included simulation studies of model identifiability, empirical calibration studies in Serbian primary and secondary schools, and the development of an open-source R package for label-free knowledge tracing. A pilot deployment in six schools in Vojvodina tested the pipeline end-to-end. The project involved collaboration with the Institute for Educational Research in Belgrade and the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad, and produced eight peer-reviewed outputs and one publicly released software toolkit.
partners: Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade, Serbia
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Cognitive Flexibility Assessment and Cross-Cultural Comparability in South-East European Adolescents
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project designed, calibrated, and administered a computer-based cognitive flexibility assessment battery to adolescent samples in Serbia and Romania, with the goal of establishing measurement comparability across the two educational systems. Emilija Zec led the psychometric calibration and measurement invariance work package, overseeing IRT item banking and multi-group confirmatory factor analyses. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian/Romanian) assessment instrument, a joint data repository shared between the two partner universities, and a report submitted to educational authorities in both countries. A three-day methodological workshop on IRT and invariance testing was delivered to school psychologists in Timișoara and Novi Sad.
partners: Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Provincial Institute for the Evaluation of Education Quality, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Inclusive Digital Learning Environments for Students with Attention and Processing Differences in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated barriers to and enablers of UDL implementation in inclusive primary and secondary schools in Serbia, focusing specifically on students with attention-related and auditory/visual processing differences. The project combined a large-scale survey of 620 teachers across 38 schools, three school-based design-and-test cycles for UDL-adapted digital materials, and the development of an open-access audit toolkit for school teams. A teacher professional development model was piloted in 12 schools in Vojvodina and validated through pre/post measurement and independent observer evaluation. Final deliverables include the audit toolkit, a freely downloadable material template library, and a policy brief submitted to the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Serbia.
partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Pedagogical Institute of Vojvodina
Primary School Đura Daničić, Novi Sad

projects.title: Accessible Digital Learning across the Adriatic–Danube Region: Framework Development and Pilot Validation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ADRIADL brought together educational research institutions in Serbia, Hungary, and Croatia to develop a shared framework for assessing and improving the accessibility of digital instructional materials in primary education. Fejsa led the work package responsible for empirical validation of the framework across Serbian pilot schools, coordinating a team of four researchers who conducted classroom observations, student assessments, and teacher interviews in 14 schools. The project produced a trilingual framework document, a validated teacher self-assessment instrument available in Serbian, Hungarian, and Croatian, and a series of open-access training videos. Findings were disseminated through national teacher in-service training networks in all three partner countries.
partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Informatics, Hungary
Faculty of Teacher Education, University of Rijeka, Croatia
National Institute of Education Research, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Behavioural Stream Analysis for Integrity Monitoring in Online Interactive Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: BEHASTREAM investigates semi-supervised and self-supervised machine learning methods for detecting integrity violations in high-frequency behavioural telemetry streams produced by online interactive systems, primarily game clients and simulation platforms. The project addresses three interconnected problems: robust feature extraction from variable-rate event logs, adaptation to concept drift under limited labelling budgets, and cross-session identity consistency verification. The research is conducted on datasets contributed under non-disclosure agreements by two software companies from Novi Sad. Deliverables include open-source preprocessing libraries, benchmark datasets with synthetic ground truth, and a deployable detection pipeline evaluated under realistic server load conditions. The project funds two PhD students and supports collaborations with partners in Poland and Romania.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Computer Science, University of Warsaw
Faculty of Automation, Computers and Electronics, University of Craiova

projects.title: Anomaly Detection Methods for Real-Time Integrity Monitoring in Online Game Platforms
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contracted research engagement with Veridian Interactive d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based game development studio, to evaluate and adapt semi-supervised anomaly detection models for deployment on the studio's live game backend infrastructure. The scope covered telemetry ingestion pipeline design, model selection and benchmarking on the studio's historical ban records, threshold calibration to meet a false-positive budget agreed with the moderation team, and a six-month shadow-mode evaluation period running the model in parallel with existing rule-based filters. Final deliverables included a technical report, a model integration specification, and a training data curation guide for ongoing maintenance by the studio's engineering team.
partners: Veridian Interactive d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Scheduling Algorithms for Heterogeneous Resource-Constrained Distributed Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed theoretical foundations and practical algorithms for scheduling in distributed systems where nodes differ in CPU architecture, memory bandwidth, and storage speed. The core contributions were: (1) an extended bin-packing framework accommodating three resource dimensions with correlated item sizes; (2) a Lyapunov-based dynamic consolidation policy validated on a local OpenStack testbed; (3) sensitivity analysis of SLA derivation under arrival-process misspecification. The project funded two PhD students, produced eight peer-reviewed publications, and delivered an open-source scheduling simulator released under MIT licence. Collaboration was established with the University of Bologna and Warsaw University of Technology.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
University of Belgrade, School of Computing
University of Bologna, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Italy

projects.title: Multi-Site Workload Trace Collection and Benchmarking Infrastructure for Cloud Scheduling Research
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRACE4CLOUD establishes a shared infrastructure for collecting, anonymising, and publishing workload traces from academic computing centres in Serbia and Hungary, with associated partners in Croatia and Romania. Popović leads the work package on trace characterisation and synthetic trace generation, which produced a calibrated generator described in the 2026 Future Generation Computer Systems paper. The project also organises annual workshops for researchers and computing centre operators, and maintains a publicly accessible trace repository. A secondary objective is developing a common anonymisation protocol that satisfies GDPR requirements while preserving statistical properties relevant to scheduling research.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences, Hungary
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, Serbia
Ruđer Bošković Institute, Croatia
West University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Procedural Soundscape Synthesis for Simulation and Cultural Heritage Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PROSONIKA investigated methods for synthesising contextually appropriate ambient soundscapes in two application domains: interactive simulation tools for urban planning and immersive installations at cultural heritage sites. The project extended corpus-based granular synthesis pipelines with occupancy-driven control models and developed perceptual evaluation protocols suited to non-expert audiences. Field recording campaigns were conducted at six sites across Vojvodina, and a public dataset of annotated heritage soundscapes was produced. The project involved collaboration between the Academy of Arts and the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad, and resulted in three journal papers, two conference contributions, and a prototype installation exhibited at the Museum of Contemporary Art Vojvodina. Three postgraduate students were supervised within the project.
partners: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Museum of Contemporary Art Vojvodina

projects.title: Spatial Audio Processing Laboratory Equipment Upgrade
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This equipment grant funded the expansion and upgrade of the Spatial Audio and Interaction Laboratory at the Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad. Key acquisitions included a 32-channel ambisonics microphone array, a 12-channel loudspeaker diffusion system, four dedicated audio workstations, and a set of binaural dummy heads for perceptual measurement studies. The upgraded facility enabled studies requiring controlled multichannel playback that could not previously be conducted on site, reducing dependence on borrowed facilities at partner institutions. The laboratory has subsequently supported several doctoral and master's thesis projects and provided infrastructure for the PROSONIKA project.
partners: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: A Reference Corpus of Serbian Prose Registers 1890–1945
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project built the SerbProsRef corpus, a 2.4-million-token stratified collection of Serbian prose texts published between 1890 and 1945, annotated for morphosyntax, dialogue spans, free indirect discourse, and orthographic normalisation. Source material was digitised from holdings at the Matica srpska library, the National Library of Serbia, and the Vojvodina Archives. The corpus is designed to support research in historical linguistics, stylistics, and related computational applications. The project employed three research assistants and one software developer, produced eight publications, and deposited the corpus data and annotation guidelines with the Faculty of Philosophy institutional repository. A searchable web interface was developed in collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
National Library of Serbia, Digital Collections Department
Institute for the Serbian Language, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts

projects.title: Diachronic Dialogue Stylistics Across South Slavic Literary Traditions
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral scientific exchange project between the Faculty of Philosophy in Novi Sad and the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Rijeka, Croatia, focusing on parallel developments in dialogue representation in Serbian and Croatian prose between 1890 and 1945. The project supported four researcher exchanges per year, a shared annotated subcorpus of 200,000 tokens from each tradition, and three joint publications. The principal comparative questions concerned tense-aspect choices in dialogue, the pace of standardisation pressure on literary registers, and the extent to which developments in one tradition preceded or mirrored those in the other. The project was funded through the bilateral cooperation programme of the ministries of science of Serbia and Croatia.
partners: Faculty of Humanities, University of Rijeka

projects.title: Pannonian Rural Architecture: Mapping Material and Spatial Typologies for Conservation Planning
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PANMAP produced a georeferenced catalogue of vernacular building types across 94 settlements in Vojvodina, based on field survey, archival cadastral data, and photogrammetric recording. The project developed a classification protocol for rural building fabric that distinguishes construction period, structural system, plan type, and current condition. The resulting database contains entries for 1,247 structures and has been made available to the Provincial Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments for use in municipal spatial plan preparation. Two early-career researchers were supported on the project. Field data collection was completed in 2023 and the final report submitted in early 2024.
partners: Provincial Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments of Vojvodina, Petrovaradin
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Subotica

projects.title: Earthen and Timber Wall Heritage of the Middle Danube Region: Cross-Border Documentation and Condition Baseline
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HERIWALL is a cross-border project establishing a shared documentation standard and condition-baseline database for earthen and timber-frame vernacular structures in the border region of southern Hungary and northern Serbia. Biljana Petrović leads the work package responsible for developing the joint recording methodology and training municipal technicians on both sides of the border in its application. The project involves two field survey seasons, a series of capacity-building workshops, and production of a bilingual technical guide for municipal heritage officers. The database is targeted to cover at least 600 structures by the project's end in 2026.
partners: Faculty of Architecture, University of Pécs
Municipality of Senta
Municipality of Baja, Hungary
Centre for Built Heritage Documentation, Subotica

projects.title: Dynamic Stability Assessment Methods for Automated Lifting Equipment in Smart Warehouses
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DYNLIFT investigates dynamic stability limits of automated forklifts and stacker cranes operating in smart warehouse environments where floor conditions, payload configurations, and travel speeds vary continuously. The project develops a library of parameterised simulation models covering three vehicle classes—counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks, and unit-load AGVs—validated against measurements from an instrumented laboratory vehicle and industrial data provided by a Vojvodina logistics operator. A central deliverable is a stability-monitoring algorithm that estimates the tip-over risk index in real time using onboard IMU and wheel-load sensor data. The project involves two graduate students and one postdoctoral researcher and produces open-access simulation datasets.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Industrial Systems, Novi Sad
Vojvodina Logistics Centre d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Transfer of Mechanical Testing Competences for Packaging and Handling Equipment
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project established shared testing and simulation competences between two engineering faculties—one in Subotica and one in Pécs—for small and medium enterprises manufacturing packaging and material handling equipment. Marković contributed to work package 3, which focused on dynamic load testing of conveyor and elevator components. Activities included joint experimental campaigns, staff exchanges of four weeks each way, and co-development of a testing protocol handbook distributed to 11 SMEs across the border region. The project funded the acquisition of a portable vibration measurement kit and a signal conditioning unit that remain available to partner institutions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad – Branch in Subotica
Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Oculomotor Correlates of Cognitive Workload Across Vocational Training Stages
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated how oculomotor parameters change as workers in two vocational domains—metalworking and logistics—progress from novice to competent performance. Longitudinal data were collected at eight time points per participant over approximately 18 months, combining remote and head-mounted eye-tracking with secondary-task probes and self-report measures. A central aim was to derive normative workload trajectories for each domain that could inform training curriculum design and readiness-to-advance criteria. A secondary aim was to compare the sensitivity of entropy-based gaze metrics against conventional fixation measures at each training stage. The project produced a dataset of longitudinal eye-tracking records from 45 trainees and contributed to the development of open analysis scripts released under a Creative Commons licence.
partners: Vocational Training Centre Novi Sad
Institute for Education Research, Belgrade
Institute of Cognitive Science, University of Pécs

projects.title: Augmented Reality Interfaces in Warehouse Logistics: Workload and Performance Monitoring
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This applied project examined how augmented reality picking guidance systems affect warehouse operator workload and error rates in a simulated logistics environment built at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Eye-tracking, error logging, and task completion time were used as outcome measures across three interface conditions. The project involved close collaboration between the psychology group and engineers developing the AR overlay software. Findings fed directly into interface redesign recommendations. A secondary aim was to pilot a lightweight eye-tracking monitoring protocol compatible with existing safety helmets, intended for eventual transfer to a partnering regional logistics firm. The project funded one doctoral student jointly supervised between psychology and industrial engineering.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Logistics Research Centre

projects.title: Scalable Hierarchical Simulation Methods for Embedded GPU Platforms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SIMBED investigated the co-design of spatial data structures and GPU scheduling policies for particle-based simulations on embedded platforms with unified memory and restricted power envelopes. The project produced: a linearised octree layout optimised for unified-memory TLB behaviour; a frame-budget-aware LOD allocation framework for multi-emitter scenes; and a benchmark suite of five standardised particle workloads covering fluid, granular, gaseous, and debris dynamics. Partners contributed expertise in low-power hardware characterisation and perceptual quality assessment. The project supported two Ph.D. students and one postdoctoral researcher, and produced eight peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Computer Science and Automation, University of Kragujevac
RT-Sim d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry associate)

projects.title: Particle Visualisation Tools for Industrial Process Simulation on Constrained Devices
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: Contract research project with SiloViz d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based company developing monitoring software for bulk material handling facilities. The project adapts and packages the particle rendering pipeline developed in SIMBED into an embeddable library compatible with the company's existing OpenGL ES 3.2 visualisation stack running on industrial ARM single-board computers. Deliverables include the library, integration documentation, performance acceptance tests, and one round of on-site validation at a client granary facility. The project also supports a master's thesis student who contributes to the integration layer.
partners: SiloViz d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Imbalanced Ensemble Methods for Anomaly Detection in Industrial Behavioural Data
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the theoretical and practical limits of ensemble-based supervised anomaly detection when training data exhibit extreme class imbalance (ratios exceeding 1:200). Core activities included a systematic benchmark study across 30 tabular datasets, development of evaluation protocols resistant to data leakage, and design of a calibration pipeline combining Beta calibration with windowed recalibration for streaming data. The project produced nine peer-reviewed publications, two defended master's theses, and an open-access dataset repository of industrial sensor logs collected in collaboration with three manufacturing partners in the Novi Sad region. All code and data are published under open licences on a university-hosted repository.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Precizija d.o.o. Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptive Anomaly Detection Under Concept Drift for Smart Manufacturing Environments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DRIFTGUARD addresses the degradation of deployed anomaly detection models caused by temporal distribution shift in manufacturing sensor streams. Vukica Grujić leads the work package on drift-adaptive ensemble retraining, which covers drift detection benchmarking, integration of drift detectors with random forest and gradient boosting base models, and field validation on two CNC machining lines—one in Subotica and one in Pécs. The project also includes a dissemination work package aimed at SMEs in the cross-border region. Partners share labelled operational data under a joint data governance agreement. Outcomes are expected to include three conference papers, one journal article, and a software toolkit for drift-aware anomaly monitoring.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad (lead)
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
Metalform Kft., Pécs, Hungary
TechnoMetal d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Credit Risk Decomposition and Stress Testing for the Serbian Banking Sector
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated econometric frameworks for decomposing credit default risk in Serbian commercial bank portfolios into systematic macro-financial and idiosyncratic borrower-level components. A core deliverable was a panel database merging credit registry microdata with macroeconomic series, covering roughly 400,000 corporate and retail borrower observations from 2008 to 2022. The team estimated dynamic factor models, system GMM panel regressions, and scenario-based stress-testing tools calibrated to Serbian supervisory requirements. Results were disseminated through four peer-reviewed articles, two policy briefs submitted to the National Bank of Serbia, and one methodological handbook distributed to participating banks. The project also supported the training of two doctoral students in quantitative credit risk analysis.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Economic Research Novi Sad

projects.title: Regional Credit Market Conditions and SME Financing Constraints in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project examined how regional macro-financial conditions in the Hungary–Serbia border zone affect SME access to bank credit and default outcomes. Ostojić led the work package responsible for econometric analysis, coordinating data collection from the Amadeus database and Hungarian and Serbian central bank statistical releases. Panel regression models with regional fixed effects were estimated to isolate the role of local economic conditions from firm-level characteristics. The project produced a joint dataset of 1,200 SMEs with matched financial statement and credit outcome data, a comparative report on cross-border financing gaps, and two conference papers. Findings were presented to regional development agencies and the Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina Development Agency, Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Sensor-Driven Probabilistic Risk Models for SME Asset Management
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a modular software pipeline for ingesting high-frequency IoT sensor streams, extracting interpretable statistical features, and fitting hierarchical Bayesian risk models suitable for small and medium enterprises that lack dedicated data science teams. Use cases were developed in collaboration with three SMEs in Vojvodina operating in food processing, cold-chain logistics, and metal fabrication. A reference implementation was released as open-source software. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed outputs. A key output was a calibration protocol that allows a new site to obtain reliable risk scores after as little as 60 days of sensor history by borrowing strength from previously observed sites via the hierarchical model structure.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research, Novi Sad
Vojvodina SME Development Agency (fictional)

projects.title: Statistical Modelling for Precision Agriculture Sensor Networks in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project linking agricultural research stations in Vojvodina and southern Hungary to develop statistical models for disease risk, irrigation need, and microclimate characterisation from low-power IoT sensor grids. Struhár leads the work package on probabilistic modelling and uncertainty quantification, contributing Gaussian process and Bayesian hierarchical methods tailored to irregular and energy-constrained sampling schedules. The project deploys sensor networks across 28 partner farms and two experimental stations. Expected outputs include operational decision-support tools, a joint training programme for agronomists, and at least 12 scientific publications. The project runs alongside the research group's existing vineyard collaboration and extends it to wheat, sunflower, and paprika cultivation.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Research Institute for Soil Science, Subotica (fictional)
Institute of Plant Protection, University of Pécs
Pannonian Agricultural Cooperative Association, Szeged (fictional)

projects.title: Convective Precipitation Hazard Mapping for the Serbian Pannonian Sector Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат је имао за циљ израду висококвалитетних карата хазарда конвективних падавина за северну Србију интеграцијом тридесетогодишњег радарског архива, плувиометријских мрежа и сателитских производа. У оквиру пројекта развијени су алгоритми за детекцију и праћење олујних ћелија, хомогенизацију дугих радарских архива и процену ретких повратних периода екстремних сатних падавина. Резултати су коришћени за ажурирање карата поплавног ризика у сарадњи са РХМЗС и Управом за управљање ванредним ситуацијама. Пројектом је финансирано запошљавање двоје истраживача на позицијама постдокторанада и набавка додатних дистрометара за теренска мерења.
partners: Републички хидрометеоролошки завод Србије, Београд
Факултет техничких наука, Универзитет у Новом Саду

projects.title: Cross-Border Flash Flood Early Warning System for the Sava and Tisa Catchments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Интеррег IPA пројекат окупља партнере из Србије и Мађарске у циљу развоја прекограничног система раног упозорења на изненадне поплаве у сливовима Саве и Тисе. Тошић руководи радним пакетом задуженим за QPE производе и просторну интерполацију падавина. Систем у реалном времену преузима оперативне радарске производе обеју земаља, меша их са плувиометријским подацима и прослеђује хидролошком моделу који управља мађарски партнерски универзитет. Крајњи корисници система су локалне самоуправе и ватрогасно-спасилачке службе у Бачкој и Барањи. Планирано је да систем буде у пилот-оперативном режиму до краја 2025. године.
partners: Универзитет Сечени Иштван, Ђер, Мађарска
Покрајински секретаријат за пољопривреду, водопривреду и шумарство АП Војводине
Управа за ванредне ситуације, Подручна јединица Нови Сад

projects.title: Scalable Real-Time Stream Reconciliation for Cross-Organisational Industrial Data Pipelines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STRECON investigated the design and performance of distributed stream processing pipelines used to reconcile data originating from multiple independent organisational data sources in industrial settings. The project focused on three technical challenges: entity resolution at stream ingestion speeds, join algorithm performance under skewed key distributions, and fault recovery in multi-stage pipelines where sources have heterogeneous reliability. The project produced a reference pipeline implementation, a benchmark dataset derived from synthetic manufacturing scenarios, and a set of published results covering latency, throughput, and correctness metrics. Two PhD students were funded through the project, one of whom defended their thesis in 2024.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
School of Computing, Union University Belgrade

projects.title: Cloud-Edge Data Stream Processing for Cross-Border Industrial Monitoring
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CEDS-BRIDGE was a cross-border cooperation project addressing real-time monitoring of industrial processes that span manufacturing sites in northern Serbia and southern Hungary. The project developed a shared cloud-edge data platform capable of ingesting sensor data streams from both sides of the border, applying configurable reconciliation and alerting logic, and presenting unified dashboards to operators at both sites. Nedić's work package covered the stream processing core: operator placement across edge and cloud nodes, latency characterisation under cross-border WAN conditions, and the adaptation of open-source tooling for deployment in resource-constrained edge environments. Field trials were conducted at a pilot water treatment facility and a logistics sorting centre.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina
Pannonia Industrial Automation Kft. (fictional)

projects.title: Few-Shot Forecasting Methods for Small and Medium E-Commerce Enterprises in Cross-Border Markets
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FEWCAST addressed the challenge that small and medium e-commerce businesses operating across the Hungary–Serbia border lack the historical data volume required to build reliable revenue forecasting models. The project developed and validated a suite of transfer learning and meta-learning methods tailored to this data constraint, producing a freely available Python toolkit and a methodological handbook for practitioners. Field validation was conducted with four partner companies from Subotica and Szeged. The project also included two training workshops for data analysts employed at participating companies and produced a shared dataset repository subject to a data-sharing agreement. Total budget allocated to the Serbian partner was approximately 95,000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodinský Digital Commerce Cluster, Subotica
South-Transdanubian Innovation Agency, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Meta-Learning Architectures for Short Financial Sequences in Data-Scarce Business Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: METAFIN investigates gradient-based and metric-based meta-learning algorithms for revenue and cash-flow forecasting in business contexts where fewer than 30 historical observations are available. The project develops theoretical bounds on expected forecast error as a function of adaptation set size, empirically tests these bounds on real e-commerce and retail datasets collected from Serbian companies, and explores synthetic data augmentation as a means of expanding meta-training corpora. A secondary objective is to produce open-access educational material on few-shot time-series methods for graduate students in business informatics. The project funds one doctoral student and supports collaboration with partners in Italy and Romania. Total budget is approximately 140,000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Department of Statistical Sciences, University of Bologna, Italy
Bucharest University of Economic Studies, Romania

projects.title: Robust OCR and Structured Information Extraction for Degraded Financial Documents in South-East European Archives
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FINDOC addressed the digitisation and machine reading of historical and contemporary financial documents held by Serbian state archives, tax authorities, and commercial banks. The project produced the SerbBankScan-2018 extension corpus with 5,000 additional annotated pages, developed domain-adaptive pretraining protocols for CRNN and transformer-based OCR models, and built an end-to-end extraction pipeline for balance sheets and tax forms. A secondary workstream investigated synthetic data generation as a privacy-preserving alternative to collecting sensitive financial originals. Results were validated with two partner institutions from the public sector that integrated the pipeline into their archival workflows on a pilot basis.
partners: Archives of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Serbian Business Registers Agency, Belgrade
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Document Digitisation Interoperability for Public Administration in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSDOC aimed to improve the digitisation interoperability of civil registry and land administration documents in municipalities along the Hungary–Serbia border. Vojnović led the work package on automated recognition and metadata extraction, contributing OCR components and quality assessment tools adapted to bilingual (Serbian and Hungarian) document scans. The project established shared digitisation quality standards adopted by six partner municipalities and produced an open dataset of 900 annotated bilingual administrative page images. Training workshops for archival staff at partner institutions were also delivered as part of the work package activities.
partners: City of Subotica, Serbia
Csongrád-Csanád County Archives, Hungary
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Municipal Archive of Senta, Serbia

projects.title: Annotation Infrastructure and Tagger Development for Informal Serbian in Digital Service Domains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce reusable annotated corpora and retrained tagger components covering three informal Serbian service domains: e-commerce, customer support chat, and classified advertising. Activities included corpus collection under data-sharing agreements with four domestic companies, development of normalisation rules for 12 recurring orthographic variability patterns, and fine-tuning of two open morpho-syntactic taggers on the resulting data. A total of approximately 95,000 tokens were annotated and deposited with the CLARIN-SR repository. The project also produced annotation guidelines revised through four internal calibration rounds, and contributed supplementary treebank sentences to the Serbian UD treebank. Two junior researchers were trained in corpus annotation methods through the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mathematics, University of Belgrade
CLARIN-SR National Centre, Belgrade

projects.title: Building a Shared Lexical Resource for Low-Resource Serbian NLP Across Regional Institutions
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral cooperation project between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Banja Luka, focused on harmonising and extending morphological lexicons for Serbian, Bosnian, and closely related varieties. Rajić leads the work package on informal variant coverage, contributing the informal morphological variant lexicon developed in earlier work and coordinating its extension with Ijekavian and Bosnian lexical variants. The project includes two joint annotation campaigns, exchange visits for doctoral students, and preparation of a shared evaluation benchmark for morphological analysis tools across the three standard varieties. A shared digital repository for the resulting resources is hosted at the University of Banja Luka.
partners: Faculty of Philology, University of Banja Luka
Institute for Language and Literature, Sarajevo

projects.title: Field-Scale Rainfall Mapping for Agricultural Insurance Applications in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RAINFIELD developed and validated a production-grade geostatistical downscaling pipeline for converting coarse-resolution satellite precipitation products into field-scale (1 km) daily rainfall grids over Vojvodina and adjoining cross-border agricultural zones. Core activities included deployment of a temporary dense rain-gauge network, construction of a 25-year historical archive, and a formal actuarial burn analysis for parametric maize and sunflower insurance products. The project produced open-access gridded datasets, published R and Python processing scripts, and a technical design guide intended for agricultural insurers. Collaboration with the Faculty of Agriculture and the Faculty of Economics at the University of Novi Sad ensured the agronomic and financial dimensions of the outputs were grounded in local practice.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Agricultural Data Infrastructure for Climate Risk Management in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGRIDATA-CROSS builds a shared meteorological data infrastructure and climate risk assessment platform serving agricultural stakeholders in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Žarko Pejić leads the work package responsible for harmonising national meteorological station records, generating consistent cross-border gridded precipitation climatologies, and providing spatial input layers to a joint drought monitoring dashboard. The project links national hydrometeorological services, regional agricultural extension offices, and university research groups on both sides of the border. Outputs include a web-accessible map viewer, an annual climate risk bulletin, and training workshops for farmers and insurance intermediaries on interpreting spatial weather data.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Data Quality Assurance in Cross-Organisational Real-Time Streaming Integrations
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DAQSTREAM addressed the gap between theoretical data quality frameworks and the operational realities of streaming API integrations shared by multiple organisations. The project developed monitoring components for schema drift detection, cross-source consistency validation, and anomaly alerting, targeting Kafka-based pipeline architectures. Pilot deployments were conducted with two partner organisations in logistics and retail sectors in Vojvodina. The project produced a reference architecture, an open-source monitoring toolkit, and a set of evaluation datasets released publicly. Four journal papers and three conference contributions were produced. The project also supported the doctoral work of two Ph.D. students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
LogiFlow d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner)

projects.title: Automated Pipeline Integrity Monitoring for API-Mediated Business Data Exchange
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: APIGUARD is a smaller regionally funded project focused specifically on integrating data quality monitoring components directly into existing API gateway infrastructure used by small and medium enterprises in Vojvodina. The project develops lightweight agents deployable alongside standard API management tools, requiring no modification to existing service code. Activities include requirement analysis with five SME participants, prototyping, and a controlled usability evaluation. The project also supports a master thesis programme in which students implement and test specific monitoring modules. Results are intended to be transferable to companies at NTP Novi Sad that operate API-based integrations with partners or public registries.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad

projects.title: Actuarial Extreme-Value Methods for Agricultural Insurance in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops statistical methods for fitting extreme-value distributions to agricultural loss data when historical records are short, as is common in South-East European crop and livestock insurance. Specific objectives include constructing credibility-weighted GPD estimators for spatially grouped portfolios, designing Bayesian prior elicitation protocols based on agronomic expert knowledge, and validating the methods against satellite-derived precipitation and yield anomaly data. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher at the Department of Mathematics and Informatics. Deliverables include an open-source R package, three peer-reviewed articles, and a policy brief aimed at the Serbian National Agricultural Insurance Fund.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences, Hungary

projects.title: Catastrophe Modelling Tools for Small Non-Life Insurers in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border applied research project that produced an open decision-support toolkit for underwriting and reserving departments of small non-life insurance companies operating in Hungary and Serbia. Péter Szabó led the work package on statistical methodology, overseeing implementation of GPD-based tail models and Bayesian updating routines in a user-facing R Shiny application. The toolkit was piloted with two regional insurers. The project also delivered two training workshops for actuarial staff and a technical manual translated into Serbian and Hungarian. Total budget for the Serbian side was approximately 180,000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Debrecen, Faculty of Economics and Business
Balkans Insurance Analytics d.o.o., Novi Sad
PannonRe Consulting Kft., Debrecen

projects.title: Drift-Aware Semi-Supervised Monitoring for Low-Label Industrial Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DRIFTGUARD addresses the combined challenge of label scarcity and concept drift in industrial condition monitoring. The project develops a unified framework in which a semi-supervised classifier is coupled with a lightweight drift detector; when drift is flagged, the system selects a small targeted query set using active learning rather than retraining from scratch on all historical data. The framework is validated on sensor streams from two partner facilities: a food-processing conveyor line and a district heating pump station. Expected outcomes include an open benchmark dataset with documented drift events, a reference software implementation, and design guidelines for practitioners. The project funds one PhD student and two master student thesis positions at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Edge-Deployable Streaming Analytics for Smart Manufacturing in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: STREAMWISE is a cross-border cooperation project targeting the deployment of data stream analytics in small and medium enterprises in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Olivera Rakić leads the work package on model compression and edge deployment, responsible for adapting anomaly detection and classification pipelines to resource-constrained hardware installed in partner SME facilities. The work package produces deployment-ready software containers, an evaluation report comparing accuracy–latency trade-offs across hardware tiers, and a training curriculum for engineers at partner companies. The project is coordinated by the Hungarian partner and involves three Serbian and two Hungarian organisations.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Latency-Controlled Query Execution in Multi-Node Transactional Databases
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: LATCORE investigates methods for enforcing configurable latency budgets on individual queries and transactions in distributed relational databases without requiring changes to storage engines. The project covers three main activities: (1) characterisation of latency variability sources in multi-node PostgreSQL deployments under realistic mixed workloads; (2) design and implementation of a scheduling middleware layer that intercepts query plans and applies deadline-aware dispatching; and (3) evaluation on a dedicated twelve-node cluster using both synthetic benchmarks and traces contributed by two industrial partners in the logistics and financial services sectors. The project funds two research assistant positions and supports collaboration with partners at Budapest University of Technology and Economics and the University of Padova.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
University of Padova, Italy

projects.title: Cross-Border Data Synchronisation Protocols for Small and Medium Enterprises
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANSSYNC addresses the practical challenge faced by small and medium enterprises operating across the Hungarian–Serbian border that must maintain consistent data across sites with intermittent connectivity. The project develops lightweight synchronisation protocols based on conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) and optimistic replication, adapted for the resource constraints of SME infrastructure. Strahinja Radović leads the work package responsible for protocol specification and performance evaluation, coordinating with a Hungarian partner responsible for SME requirements gathering and a Serbian software house contributing a pilot deployment. The project also produces training materials and a reference implementation released under an open-source licence.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Széchenyi István University, Győr, Hungary
DataBridge Solutions d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Probabilistic Models for Irregular Cash-Flow Forecasting in Small and Medium Enterprises
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a suite of probabilistic forecasting methods tailored to cash-flow sequences from Serbian SMEs, where observations arrive irregularly, distributional assumptions are routinely violated, and historical records are short. The research programme combined Bayesian structural time-series models, conformal prediction, and distributional shift detection into an integrated pipeline. Methods were validated on anonymised datasets from 60+ enterprises across manufacturing, retail, and services sectors in Vojvodina, obtained through collaboration with the Vojvodina Development Agency. Outputs include four journal articles, an open-source R package, and a technical report delivered to the funding agency. Three master's students and one PhD candidate were supported.
partners: Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts
Faculty of Economics, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Development Agency

projects.title: Cross-Border Cash-Flow Risk Assessment for SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed the specific liquidity forecasting challenges faced by SMEs operating across the Hungarian–Serbian border, where currency exposure, differing VAT settlement cycles, and seasonal agricultural demand create compounded uncertainty in cash positions. The Novi Sad team led the work package on quantitative forecasting model development and benchmarking, contributing Bayesian and quantile regression tools evaluated on 28 cross-border trading firms. Partners in Pécs contributed accounting data standards and firm-level surveys. The project produced a bilingual practitioner guide, two conference papers, and a shared anonymised dataset deposited with both universities. Final outcomes were presented to regional chambers of commerce in Subotica and Pécs.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina
Regional Development Agency Southern Transdanubia

projects.title: High-Resolution Agroclimatic Downscaling for Sustainable Agriculture in the Pannonian and Dinaric Zones
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a multi-source satellite downscaling pipeline producing 500 m agroclimatic grids for Serbia. Core deliverables included the benchmark dataset of 18 agroclimatic indices (2001–2020), a Web Map Service interface, and a documented open-source Python processing chain. Field validation campaigns were conducted across three growing seasons in Vojvodina and the Mačva basin. The project also assessed the utility of the derived grids as forcing data for DSSAT and AquaCrop crop simulation models, finding that spatially disaggregated inputs reduced maize yield simulation error by 9–14 % relative to nearest-station forcing. Three researchers from BioSense and two doctoral students were involved.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia

projects.title: Harmonised Gridded Climate Products for the Middle Danube Agricultural Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration producing harmonised agroclimatic grids for the Hungary–Serbia transboundary region at 1 km resolution. Đukić led Work Package 3 (spatial downscaling and grid production) and coordinated exchange of station data under a bilateral data-sharing agreement between the Hungarian Meteorological Service and the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. The project delivered 30-year climatological normal grids, a drought monitoring prototype, and a joint training workshop for 22 operational forecasters. Outputs were incorporated into both national agrometeorological advisory systems.
partners: Hungarian Meteorological Service (OMSZ), Budapest

University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Non-Invasive Sensor Fusion for Real-Time Cognitive Load and Fatigue Estimation in Commercial Vehicle Drivers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DRIVESENSE addressed the problem that existing driver monitoring solutions for commercial vehicles rely on single-modality sensing with high false-alarm rates. The project developed a multi-sensor platform integrating a remote eye tracker, two-channel ECG, and a four-electrode EEG headband, all synchronised to a Raspberry Pi CM4 compute module. Field trials involved 38 professional truck drivers on real routes between Novi Sad and Subotica. The main deliverables were: a subject-adaptive fusion algorithm reducing false alerts by 28 % compared with the commercial baseline; a labelled dataset made publicly available; and a prototype certified for in-cab installation under Serbian traffic safety regulations. Two journal papers and three conference papers were produced.
partners: Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia
Faculty of Occupational Safety, University of Niš
TransLogix d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Eye-Tracking-Based Assessment of Cognitive Workload in Mixed Traffic Environments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project compared cognitive workload profiles of drivers navigating mixed traffic environments in Novi Sad and Szeged, Hungary, where autonomous and human-driven vehicles share the road. Csaba Fehér led the work package responsible for physiological data acquisition and signal processing. Both fixed-base driving simulators at the partner universities were configured with identical eye-tracking and ECG setups, allowing direct cross-site comparison. Results showed that encountering an autonomously behaving vehicle in an otherwise conventional traffic stream increased saccade rate by 22 % and pupil diameter by 0.31 mm relative to fully human-traffic baselines. The project produced harmonised data collection protocols usable in future multinational studies.
partners: Department of Transport and Vehicle Engineering, University of Szeged
City of Novi Sad – Directorate for Transport
Pannonian Traffic Safety Foundation, Subotica

projects.title: Adaptive Deep Learning Models for Cross-Domain Infrastructure Damage Assessment
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated fine-tuning and domain adaptation techniques for convolutional networks applied to visual assessment of damage in civil infrastructure. Key activities included construction of a multi-source annotated image database covering concrete, masonry, and steel structures across Vojvodina and neighbouring regions, controlled experiments on freeze-depth selection and learning rate scheduling, and development of an open evaluation protocol for cross-domain comparison. The project funded two doctoral researchers and supported fieldwork at eight infrastructure sites. Outputs include six peer-reviewed papers and the open benchmark dataset described in the 2025 IEEE Transactions paper. An end-of-project report was submitted to the Science Fund in early 2025.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade
Public Enterprise Roads of Serbia

projects.title: Visual Damage Monitoring for Cross-Border Transport Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project addressed automated visual monitoring of road and bridge infrastructure along the Hungary–Serbia corridor. Lidija Lukić leads the machine learning work package responsible for adapting pre-trained damage classifiers to the joint image archive assembled by Hungarian and Serbian road maintenance authorities. The work package delivered a shared annotation scheme, a harmonised dataset of 18,000 images from both sides of the border, and a fine-tuned segmentation model for crack and pothole detection deployed in a pilot monitoring dashboard operated by the Serbian project partner. Results feed into policy recommendations for cross-border road maintenance protocols.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
National Directorate General for Roads, Pécs, Hungary
Public Enterprise Roads of Serbia
Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Real-Time Multi-Constraint Routing Algorithms for Urban Freight and Emergency Logistics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ROUTECORE develops exact and heuristic algorithms for routing problems in which vehicles must simultaneously satisfy constraints on time, payload, energy consumption, and legal driving regulations. The project focuses on three application contexts: urban last-mile freight, emergency medical supply distribution, and municipal waste collection in mid-size Serbian cities. Core research tasks include formulating time-expanded graph models with constraint propagation modules, designing and benchmarking tabu search and large neighbourhood search heuristics, and integrating the solvers with a lightweight open-source simulation environment. The project involves two PhD students at the University of Novi Sad and a collaboration with Politehnica University of Timișoara. A dataset of anonymised GPS traces collected in cooperation with a local logistics operator in Novi Sad is used for calibration.
partners: Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Computer Science, Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Optimisation of Agricultural Goods Transport in the Hungary–Serbia Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: LOGI-CROSS addressed inefficiencies in the road transport of perishable agricultural goods across the Hungary–Serbia border by developing decision-support tools for route selection and vehicle scheduling. Paunović contributed graph-modelling and shortest-path components, specifically adapting time-dependent routing algorithms to account for variable border crossing durations estimated from historical truck-queue data. The project produced an openly available prototype routing tool and two peer-reviewed publications. Partners included a Hungarian agricultural cooperative and a Serbian regional development agency. Field data were gathered from 14 border crossing events monitored over eight months, covering approximately 320 individual truck runs and recording waiting times, cargo temperatures, and fuel consumption.
partners: Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Scalable Row-Crop Monitoring Using Multi-Sensor UAV Platforms and Object-Based Analysis for Vojvodina Agriculture
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ROWSENSE develops a repeatable workflow for monitoring row-crop canopy status across maize, soybean, sunflower, and sugar beet fields in Vojvodina using UAV-mounted hyperspectral and multispectral sensors. The project addresses the lack of standardised processing pipelines that work across crop types and phenological stages without full re-parameterisation. Activities include systematic field campaigns at Rimski Šančevi and three commercial farms, development of transferable segmentation rulesets, and integration with meteorological and soil data layers. An open-source Python toolbox is under development for dissemination to regional agronomists. The project involves two postdoctoral researchers, one PhD student, and collaboration with the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border UAV Data Infrastructure for Sustainable Agriculture in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DRONAGRI-IPA established a shared UAV remote sensing data infrastructure and processing capacity across Hungarian and Serbian partner institutions to support sustainable agriculture monitoring in the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal region. The project created joint field campaign protocols, a shared raw-data archive accessible to both country teams, and a harmonised quality-control procedure for multispectral and RGB UAV products. Anna Turčanová contributed the spectral calibration methodology and led the object-based canopy classification component for the Serbian field sites covering approximately 2 400 ha of arable land near Zrenjanin and Kikinda.
partners: Research Institute for Agricultural Engineering, Gödöllő, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Novi Sad
BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Low-Power Wireless Sensor Infrastructure for Soil and Crop Monitoring in Pannonian Agricultural Landscapes
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed and deployed a LoRaWAN-based sensor infrastructure across four pilot agricultural sites, two in Vojvodina and two in Csongrád-Csanád County, Hungary. Uzelac led the work package on radio channel characterisation and network planning, coordinating the 868 MHz measurement campaigns in maize, sunflower, and soybean fields that produced the datasets underlying several of his publications. The project also produced an open-access link budget calculator for sub-GHz agricultural deployments, disseminated through both universities. Total instrumented area across all sites was approximately 120 ha. The project involved one doctoral student and two master's students from the Novi Sad side.

projects.title: MAC-Layer Optimisation for Scalable LPWAN Deployments in Smart Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigates MAC-layer protocol design for LoRaWAN networks that must sustain reliable communication when node counts scale beyond a few hundred devices per gateway. The research combines Markov-chain analytical modelling, discrete-event simulation, and experimental validation on a software-defined radio testbed. Key topics include adaptive transmission probability control, duty-cycle coordination across multiple gateways, and the interaction between spreading factor assignment and collision rates. The project has produced three journal papers to date and supports one doctoral student. A secondary thread examines the 868 MHz spectrum occupancy baseline needed to calibrate coexistence models for future dense deployments.

projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the gap between EU regulatory labelling requirements and actual label production practice in small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises in Serbia, with comparative data from North Macedonia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Activities included an audit of label files and workflows at 22 participating companies, development of a freely available preflight profile set for compliance label artwork, and a training programme delivered to 68 QA and production staff across three countries. The project produced an open-access repository of reference label templates for 11 product categories and a Serbian-language practitioner guide to CLP, EU 1169/2011, and EU MDR labelling requirements.

projects.title: Harmonised Long-Term Sensor Data Infrastructures for Agronomic Modelling in the Pannonian Region

projects.summary: SENSODAT established a cross-border data infrastructure connecting existing soil and microclimate sensor networks in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. The BioSense Institute team led the work package on data quality assurance, harmonisation, and machine-learning-ready feature archive generation. Activities included designing a shared metadata schema, implementing automated gap-detection and imputation pipelines, and producing a curated multi-year archive of 47 stations with documented provenance. The archive was made openly accessible under a Creative Commons licence and was used as the primary data source for several subsequent modelling studies. projects.title: Data-Driven Early Warning System for Crop Stress Events in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CROPWATCH developed and field-validated a modular early warning system for four agronomically significant crop stress events — frost, drought, powdery mildew onset, and waterlogging — affecting the principal field crops grown in Vojvodina. The project combined multi-source sensor data fusion, transfer learning across station networks, and conformal prediction for uncertainty-aware alert generation. A prototype web dashboard was built and tested with agronomic advisors from two regional agricultural extension services during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. The system issued alerts at least 24 hours in advance for 79 % of observed events across the pilot fields. The project also trained two MSc students who contributed to the machine-learning pipeline development.

projects.title: Wind-Aware Closed-Loop Spray Control for Low-Altitude Agricultural UAVs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate an integrated wind-aware spray control system for hexarotor agricultural UAVs operating over typical Vojvodina field crops. The core deliverable was a combined wind estimation module—based on motor current signatures and a compact pressure probe array—feeding a model predictive attitude controller and an adaptive nozzle pressure regulator. Wind tunnel characterisation campaigns, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and three seasons of field trials were conducted across partner farm sites in Srem and Bačka. The project produced 6 peer-reviewed papers, 2 M.Sc. theses, and a functional prototype sprayer platform.

projects.title: Aerodynamic Characterisation and Control Strategies for Guarded Multirotor Systems in Wind-Exposed Environments
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: AEROGUARD investigated the aerodynamic penalties and control implications of propeller guard geometries on multirotor UAVs used in windy outdoor and near-infrastructure inspection scenarios. Systematic wind tunnel experiments were conducted across four guard types at wind speeds up to 16 m/s, and the resulting thrust and moment data were used to calibrate compensating control allocation strategies. The project also examined structural loads on guard mounting brackets under combined thrust and sideslip conditions, informing revised design recommendations. Two early-career researchers received project funding for their doctoral work, and results were disseminated through three conference presentations and two journal submissions.

Field trials were conducted on 14 farms in Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád County covering winter wheat, sunflower, and maize. The project produced an open decision-support module, documented sampling protocols, and trained 45 farm advisers from both countries in two workshops held in Novi Sad and Szeged.

projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SOILPRES investigated how multiple proximal soil sensing modalities can be fused into a single prescription model without requiring prohibitively dense destructive sampling. The project combined EM38 surveys, drone multispectral imaging, and vis-NIR core scanning across 20 commercial fields in Vojvodina. A key output was a Bayesian data-fusion framework that weights sensor contributions according to their field-specific predictive performance, implemented in an R package made publicly available. The project also validated the framework on six external fields not used in algorithm development, demonstrating robust transferability. Three journal papers, one conference paper, and training materials for MSc students were produced.

projects.title: Accelerated Degradation Assessment and Service-Life Modelling of Protective Coatings on Buried Steel Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project combined laboratory accelerated testing and a two-year field burial study to build a quantitative model linking EIS parameters to remaining coating service life on buried carbon steel pipelines. Soil electrolytes spanning the range of agricultural and urban soils in Vojvodina were characterised in terms of pH, resistivity, chloride, and sulphate content. EIS data collected at multiple degradation stages were used to train a regression model that predicts time to first coating breakdown within ±15% accuracy on a validation dataset. The project delivered a test protocol recommended to Serbian standards bodies and open-source data processing scripts for equivalent circuit fitting. Four journal articles and one conference paper were published within the project period.

Activities include a joint round-robin measurement exercise using circulated reference phantoms, a training school for early-career researchers, and the publication of harmonised measurement guidelines. projects.summary: HYDROCROSS brought together research groups and SMEs from Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád County to develop and validate hydrophobic surface treatments for valve and pump components used in water-treatment plants along the Tisa river basin. Jokić led the work package on tribological characterisation and lifetime prediction of fluoropolymer coatings under particle-laden water conditions. The project delivered a joint testing protocol accepted by both national certification bodies and a demonstrator batch of coated valve seats installed in a water-treatment plant in Kanjiža for an 18-month trial.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Szeged

projects.title: Geostatistical Mapping of Salt-Affected Soils in Vojvodina for Sustainable Agricultural Land Management
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce a systematic, georeferenced database of saline and sodic soil properties for five municipalities in the central Vojvodina region covering approximately 4 000 hectares of agricultural land. Field campaigns combined EM38 surveys, pXRF scanning, and targeted soil coring to obtain ECe, ESP, pH, texture, and organic carbon. Regression-kriging was applied to generate 1:10 000-scale prediction maps and associated uncertainty surfaces. Outputs were delivered to local agricultural extension services in open GIS formats. The project also produced a standardised field protocol for cost-effective saline soil surveys intended for use by other research teams and agricultural advisory bodies in the province.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Provincial Directorate for Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, Vojvodina
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Salt-Affected Soil Dynamics in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSALT investigates the spatial extent and temporal dynamics of saline-sodic soils across a 120 000-hectare study region straddling the Serbia–Hungary border. Kosanović leads the work package responsible for harmonising Serbian and Hungarian soil sampling protocols, joint EM38 field campaigns, and cross-border regression-kriging mapping. The project integrates Sentinel-2 spectral indices as additional covariates alongside proximal sensor data to extend mapping to areas without dense ground surveys. Outputs include a bilingual soil data portal, unified salinity hazard maps, and recommendations for transboundary land management. A training workshop for farmers and extension officers is planned for the final project year.
partners: Institute for Soil Sciences, Budapest, Hungary
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Vojvodina Agricultural Land Agency, Serbia
