projects.title: Automated Document Stream Processing for Accredited Testing Laboratories in Cross-Border Regulatory Workflows
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the administrative burden faced by accredited testing laboratories that exchange reports across the Hungarian–Serbian border, where differing national LIMS formats require manual re-entry. The Novi Sad team developed the OCR and extraction core of a processing pipeline capable of ingesting laboratory reports in PDF and TIFF formats and outputting structured data conforming to a jointly defined cross-border schema. A pilot deployment covered four laboratories, two in Subotica and two in Pécs, processing approximately 12,000 reports over a six-month validation period. The Hungarian partner contributed LIMS integration expertise and access to Hungarian-language report corpora. The project produced the FormBank-WB-Extended dataset and a publicly documented API specification for cross-border report interchange.
partners: Faculty of Information Technology, University of Pécs
Institute for Environmental Testing Subotica (fictional)
Pécs Regional Laboratory Services Ltd. (fictional)

projects.title: Template-Agnostic Machine Reading of Laboratory Reports for Small and Medium Enterprises
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Small and medium enterprises that are required to submit laboratory test results to regulatory bodies typically lack IT capacity to automate report ingestion. LABREADER developed a general-purpose extraction service requiring no template specification from the user. The core contribution is a cascade of layout segmentation, field detection, and value normalisation components trained on the annotated corpora accumulated by the group over fifteen years. The project included a usability study with eight SME participants in the food and construction materials sectors, measuring time saved in regulatory report submission workflows. Median time per submission fell from 23 minutes to 4 minutes in controlled trials. The service prototype was deployed on infrastructure at NTP Novi Sad for a six-month pilot.
partners: NTP Novi Sad (Science Technology Park Novi Sad)
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina (fictional engagement)

projects.title: Soil Buffering Capacity Indicators for Sustainable Amelioration Planning in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SOLBUFF aims to produce a regionally validated set of buffering capacity indicators that can be measured in routine soil testing laboratories and translated directly into amelioration recommendations. The project covers chernozem, hydromorphic, and solonetz soil associations across Vojvodina, sampling approximately 400 profiles over three years. Laboratory work includes potentiometric buffer curve construction, organic matter fractionation, and X-ray diffraction clay mineralogy. The outputs will include a published calibration dataset, an open-access decision-support tool for lime and gypsum dose calculation, and draft amendments to the national soil testing protocol currently used by agricultural extension services.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Pedological Research Centre Zrenjanin

projects.title: Humus Quality Monitoring for Smart Liming in the Tisa River Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HUMSMART brought together soil science teams from Serbia and Hungary to harmonise organic matter characterisation methods and examine links between humus quality indicators and soil acid buffering across the Serbian–Hungarian border region of the Tisa basin. Igor Marić led Work Package 3 covering laboratory inter-calibration and the development of a shared soil sample archive. The project produced joint sampling campaigns on 14 paired transects, a bilingual laboratory manual, and a dataset of 520 soil profiles shared between partners. The project also funded two short researcher exchanges to the University of Debrecen. Results fed into a joint policy brief submitted to both national agricultural ministries.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
University of Debrecen, Institute of Land Use Technology
Regional Agricultural Chamber of Csongrád-Csanád County, Hungary
Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad

projects.title: Interoperable Communication Middleware for Heterogeneous Agricultural Vehicle Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AGRILINK addressed the practical interoperability gap between ISOBUS and CANopen subsystems on small and medium farm machinery common in the Western Balkans, where operators maintain mixed fleets spanning multiple decades of production. The project developed a configurable middleware layer running on a dual-CAN embedded platform that dynamically maps process-data between the two protocol worlds, with a focus on minimal latency and flash footprint suitable for low-cost ECUs. A reference implementation was validated on two commercially sourced implements supplied by a regional agricultural machinery dealer. The project also produced an open test harness and a set of training materials for Serbian agricultural engineering students.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Transfer of Agricultural Fieldbus Expertise Between Serbian and Romanian Universities
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: FIELDBUS-IPA established a joint laboratory protocol and student exchange programme between the Faculty of Technical Sciences Novi Sad and the Faculty of Agriculture Timișoara (fictional) focused on CAN-based fieldbus diagnostics for agricultural machinery. Zarić leads the work package responsible for curriculum development and laboratory equipment sharing, including remote access to bus-analysis hardware at both sites. The project has so far produced two joint master's thesis topics, one co-supervised doctoral candidate, and a jointly authored laboratory manual covering ISO 11783 and CANopen diagnostics procedures that has been adopted in both partner institutions.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Timișoara (fictional)
Technical College of Zrenjanin

projects.title: Fused Proximal and Satellite Sensing for Nitrogen Management in Pannonian Basin Arable Crops
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: NITROFUSE addressed the gap between high-density ground-sensor data and broad-coverage satellite imagery for within-season nitrogen management. The project developed and validated data assimilation algorithms that combine active optical sensor transect data with Sentinel-2 red-edge composites to produce full-field nitrogen status maps at field-management resolution. Field validation was conducted on winter wheat, maize, and sunflower across 14 commercial farms in Vojvodina. The project produced an open-source processing library, three peer-reviewed publications, and a QGIS plugin adopted by two agricultural consultancy firms during the project period. BioSense Institute served as the lead institution, with collaboration from the Faculty of Agriculture Novi Sad and the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Standardised Canopy Sensor Protocols for Cross-Border Precision Nitrogen Management
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CANSENS aimed to establish jointly agreed calibration and field-operation protocols for active optical canopy sensors used in Hungarian and Serbian farming systems, which differ in dominant crop varieties, machinery fleets, and soil types. Todić led the work package responsible for sensor calibration harmonisation and inter-platform validation trials. The project ran side-by-side sensor trials across six farms on both sides of the Danube, developed a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) field technician handbook, and produced a shared calibration database covering winter wheat, maize, and soybean. Outcomes fed directly into the NITROFUSE project's methodology.
partners: Research Institute of Agricultural Engineering, Gödöllő, Hungary
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Debrecen Agricultural Cooperative Research Centre, Hungary

projects.title: Federated Anomaly and Reliability Monitoring for Networked Agricultural Machinery
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FARMWATCH developed privacy-preserving, distributed anomaly detection methods for agricultural machinery fleets operating across multiple ownership boundaries. The project designed federated learning protocols adapted for ensemble anomaly detectors and validated them on real telemetry from tractor and harvester fleets in Vojvodina and partner sites in Romania. A secondary workstream produced an annotated benchmark dataset of multivariate agricultural telemetry with verified fault labels, which was released publicly at project close. The project trained two Ph.D. students and resulted in four journal publications. Total budget was approximately 2.8 million RSD over three years.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics, Bucharest
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Sensor Fusion and Fault Detection in Smart Agricultural Equipment
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SENSEFAULT addressed the integration of heterogeneous sensor modalities—CAN-bus, inertial measurement units, and near-field acoustic emission sensors—into unified fault detection pipelines for field machinery operating across the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. Pejić led the data processing and anomaly detection workpackage, contributing multivariate drift detection and change-point methods to a shared software library. The project included field trials on farms in Bačka Topola and Kecskemét, and produced a joint technical report and two conference papers. A small demonstrator system was installed on two tractors and monitored for 14 months.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
University of Debrecen, Faculty of Engineering
Agricultural Research Institute Kecskemét
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Vojvodina

projects.title: Plant-Derived Antioxidant Concentrates for Stabilisation of Cold-Pressed Edible Oils from the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PLANSTAB investigated the use of by-product-derived polyphenol concentrates (grape pomace, rosemary, buckwheat hull) as natural antioxidant additives for cold-pressed edible oils. The project combined analytical oxidation chemistry with extraction process development and sensory evaluation. Laboratory-scale enrichment trials in camelina, hemp, and walnut oils were validated under accelerated and real-time storage conditions. A small database of antioxidant–oil interaction parameters was assembled to support concentration optimisation without requiring full factorial experiments for each new oil–additive combination. The Faculty of Technology was the lead institution, with collaboration from the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops in Novi Sad and a private cold-press enterprise.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, Serbia
Uljarnica Sunce d.o.o., Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia

projects.title: Quality Mapping and Shelf-Life Characterisation of Cold-Pressed Oils from Underutilised Oilseeds in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This regional project produced a systematic physical-chemical database of cold-pressed oils from seven underutilised oilseed species grown in Vojvodina. Fatty acid profiling, tocopherol content, phytosterol composition, and a full suite of oxidation markers were determined for oils pressed from seeds collected across three growing seasons. The dataset was intended to provide evidence for agricultural and food-processing authorities in AP Vojvodina regarding diversification potential. Project deliverables included a published comparative study and a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat. The project supported one doctoral student.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, AP Vojvodina, Serbia

projects.title: Optimisation of Filtration Processes in Cold-Pressed and Refined Vegetable Oil Production in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to characterise filtration behaviour of crude and winterised cold-pressed oils produced by small and medium enterprises in Vojvodina, where inconsistent raw material quality leads to unpredictable filter performance and high filter-aid costs. Laboratory and pilot filtration experiments were conducted on sunflower, pumpkin seed, and camelina oils across a range of seasonal feed compositions. Cake compressibility parameters and filter-aid dosage guidelines were compiled into a practical decision-support document distributed to six participating oil producers. The project funded construction of a temperature-controlled dead-end filtration cell and a pilot cross-flow rig at the Faculty of Technology, which now serve as shared infrastructure for collaborative projects.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Zlatno Polje d.o.o., Sombor
Voćarstvo i uljarstvo Janković, Bačka Palanka

projects.title: Membrane-Based Clarification as a Replacement for Diatomaceous Earth Filtration in Edible Oil Refining
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MEMFOOD investigates whether polymeric and ceramic membrane modules operated in cross-flow mode can substitute diatomaceous earth filtration in the bleaching step of sunflower and rapeseed oil refining, reducing solid-waste generation and worker exposure to crystalline silica dust. The project covers membrane material screening, fouling characterisation under industrially relevant feed compositions, and techno-economic comparison with conventional leaf filtration. A life-cycle assessment component evaluates environmental trade-offs of membrane manufacture and cleaning-chemical consumption against eliminated diatomite waste. Pilot-scale trials are planned in cooperation with an industrial partner. The project involves researchers from the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad and a collaborating group from the University of Ljubljana.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, University of Ljubljana
Rafinerija ulja Bačka d.o.o., Srbobran

projects.title: Encapsulation strategies for maintaining probiotic viability across cold-chain distribution in functional dairy and plant-based products
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the loss of probiotic viability that occurs during refrigerated distribution of functional food products, particularly where temperature fluctuations are unavoidable. The research team at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, collaborates with the Institute of Food Technology to develop and test encapsulation matrices optimised for mechanical stability and low-pH resistance at the same time as cold-chain robustness. The work combines bench-scale formulation trials with pilot-scale spray drying and extrusion, mathematical modelling of survival kinetics, and consumer-relevant sensory assessment. A secondary objective is producing survival prediction tools in the form of simplified model equations for use in industrial quality assurance contexts.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-border exchange for sustainable dairy fermentation technologies in the Vojvodina–South Hungary region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project brought together researchers and small dairy enterprises from Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád County in Hungary to exchange knowledge on fermentation control and starter culture management. Anja Rakić contributed to the microbiology workpackage, conducting comparative survival tests of local and commercial Lactobacillus strains used in traditional cheese and yoghurt production in both regions, and co-authored a joint technical report on cold-storage practices in partner enterprises. The project organised two joint training workshops for dairy SME employees at University of Szeged and the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Food Engineering, University of Szeged, Hungary
Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica
Mlekoprodukt d.o.o. (fictional dairy enterprise, Zrenjanin)

projects.title: Integrated Scale-up and Control Strategies for Sustainable Lactic Acid Production at Pilot Scale
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the engineering gap between laboratory-proven lactic acid fermentation processes and commercially relevant pilot-scale operation. Core activities included characterisation of the group's 150 L bioreactor using hydrodynamic similarity analysis, implementation and comparison of three pH-stat control architectures, and integration of a whey-permeate-based fed-batch feeding strategy. The project produced a validated pilot-scale operating protocol, a soft-sensor framework for real-time product monitoring, and a life cycle assessment comparing feedstock scenarios. Industrial relevance was assessed through discussions with two regional dairy processors interested in valorising whey permeate streams. Four journal papers were published and two MSc theses were completed under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Industrial Chemistry and Environmental Engineering, Politehnica University Timișoara

projects.title: Cross-Border Training Network for Fermentation Process Scale-up in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FERMSCALE established a joint training and research infrastructure between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Miskolc for scale-up of industrial fermentation processes, with an emphasis on lactic acid and citric acid production. The work package led by the Novi Sad group covered bioreactor characterisation, staff and student exchanges, and development of shared laboratory protocols. Three PhD students (two from Serbia, one from Hungary) conducted research placements of three to six months under the project. Joint pilot experiments were conducted at both sites, and a shared database of kLa and mixing-time measurements at 2–50 L scale was compiled and made publicly available.
partners: Department of Biotechnology, University of Miskolc
Vojvodina Development Agency

projects.title: Energy Recovery and Process Optimisation in Batch Drying for the Agri-Food Sector in the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project targeted energy efficiency improvements in batch drying operations at small and medium agri-food enterprises on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. The Novi Sad team led the work package on thermal modelling and energy audit, developing and applying the standardised audit protocol described in the benchmarking publication. Twelve facilities in Vojvodina and southern Hungary were audited. The Hungarian partner team at the University of Szeged led the instrumentation and sensor work package. A joint training course on energy-efficient drying was delivered to 38 facility operators and technicians across three workshops held in Subotica, Szeged, and Novi Sad. A guidance document summarising best-practice measures was published in Serbian and Hungarian.
partners: Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Szeged
Regional Development Agency of Southern Transdanubia, Pécs
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce, Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermal Characterisation and Control Improvement of Batch Drying Chambers in the Serbian Meat-Processing Industry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to build a validated multi-scale modelling chain for batch drying chambers, spanning from CFD-level airflow characterisation to facility-level energy simulation, and to use the chain to develop and test improved control strategies. Key activities included construction of a 64-channel thermocouple data-acquisition system for the faculty pilot chamber, systematic CFD model validation across three chamber sizes, and dynamic zonal model development. The project also supported a doctoral student working on model-predictive fan control. Industrial collaboration with two Vojvodina meat-processing companies provided access to full-scale chambers and operating data. Results fed directly into the 2024 Applied Thermal Engineering publication and the 2026 Energy Conversion and Management paper.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Mesarstvo Đorđević d.o.o., Sremska Mitrovica
Sušara Bačka d.o.o., Vrbas

projects.title: Molecular Basis of Listeria monocytogenes Persistence in Ready-to-Eat Meat Processing Environments in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project examined the genomic and phenotypic determinants that enable specific L. monocytogenes lineages to persist in ready-to-eat meat processing environments for extended periods. Using longitudinal WGS data collected from four Serbian processing facilities, the project characterised accessory genomic content associated with persistence, assessed biofilm formation capacity under processing-relevant conditions, and developed an evidence-based decision framework for corrective action. The project produced a curated WGS dataset of over 150 isolates, contributed to three peer-reviewed publications, and delivered two technical workshops for meat industry food safety practitioners in Serbia. Collaboration with the Institute of Meat Hygiene and Technology in Belgrade and a partner institution in Hungary enabled regional comparison of circulating clonal lineages.
partners: Institute of Meat Hygiene and Technology, Belgrade
Department of Food Microbiology, University of Szeged, Hungary
Veterinary Specialist Institute Novi Sad

projects.title: Harmonised Risk-Based Environmental Monitoring for Listeria in Ready-to-Eat Food SMEs across Southeastern Europe
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project aimed to develop and pilot a harmonised framework for Listeria monocytogenes environmental monitoring in SME ready-to-eat food processors in Hungary and Serbia. Kosanović leads the work package on sampling strategy design and validation, coordinating microbiological data collection from eight participating facilities across both countries. The project involves joint training activities for food business operators and competent authority staff, development of bilingual guidance materials, and a comparative study of monitoring outcomes under existing versus harmonised approaches. Final guidance documents are intended to be compatible with EU Regulation 2073/2005 requirements and applicable to other Southeastern European countries considering alignment with EU food safety standards.
partners: Department of Food Microbiology, University of Szeged, Hungary
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina
National Food Chain Safety Office, Budapest, Hungary
Veterinary Specialist Institute Novi Sad

projects.title: Functional Characterisation of Natural Casings for Improved Dimensional and Mechanical Predictability in Automated Meat Processing Lines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of standardised functional parameters for natural animal-derived casings accepted in procurement specifications across Serbian meat processing companies. Work covered collagen microstructure, tensile testing protocols, moisture permeability benchmarks, and calibre mapping methodology applied to sheep, hog, and bovine casing types obtained from 12 domestic suppliers. A reference dataset of 4,800 specimens was assembled and used to propose threshold values for five mechanical and geometrical parameters that could be incorporated into national or regional quality standards. The project included a pilot trial at two industrial partner sites comparing production outcomes before and after applying the proposed procurement criteria.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Mesnati Kombinat Fruška d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Natural Casing Quality Harmonisation Across the Western Balkans Processing Chain
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration addressing inconsistencies in casing grading practices between Serbian and Hungarian processing sectors. Nikolić led the work package on physical and mechanical characterisation, coordinating sample collection from grading centres in both countries and establishing a shared testing protocol. The project produced a bilingual technical guide on casing acceptance testing adopted by three member companies. A calibre imaging prototype was transferred to a partner facility in Hungary for six-month industrial evaluation. Results contributed to a draft annex for regional casing grading guidelines submitted to the Codex Alimentarius national contact point.
partners: Faculty of Food Science, University of Szeged
Balkán Bél Kft., Szeged
Mesnati Kombinat Fruška d.o.o., Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina

projects.title: Stability and Flow Behaviour of Plant-Based Protein–Carbohydrate Powder Blends Under Variable Humidity Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the physical instability of plant-based protein–carbohydrate dry blends during storage and handling, which is an increasing technical problem as manufacturers reformulate products to use pea, faba bean, rice and hemp protein isolates in place of dairy-derived ingredients. The work involves systematic measurement of sorption isotherms, particle surface energetics and shear rheology for a matrix of blends, combined with long-term storage trials at controlled humidity. Mathematical models relating blend composition and water activity to caking rate and flowability loss are being developed and validated against pilot-scale storage data. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Technology, Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Food Science and Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, University of Debrecen

projects.title: Robust Calibration Transfer Strategies for NIR Protein Monitoring in Grain Processing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the problem of deploying a single NIR calibration model for protein quantification across multiple instruments and measurement sites in grain processing. The core objectives were to benchmark direct standardisation, piecewise direct standardisation and spectral space-based transfer methods on datasets collected from two university laboratories and one industrial partner. Reference protein data were generated by Kjeldahl and Dumas combustion methods on matched wheat and wheat–rye flour samples. The project produced validated protocols for minimum transfer set composition and size, and quantified the influence of instrument age and detector type on transfer performance. A practical decision tree for selecting a transfer strategy given available update samples was published as an open-access guide.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Food Technology and Biotechnology, University of Osijek, Croatia
Mlinprodukt d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Near-Infrared Screening of Protein Fraction Composition in Pulse-Enriched Flour Blends for Reformulated Bakery Products
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project examined flour blends enriched with chickpea, lentil and faba bean flours as partial wheat flour replacers for higher-protein bakery products. The University of Novi Sad team was responsible for developing and validating NIR chemometric models for protein fraction screening in the resulting ternary and quaternary blend matrices. Activities included preparation of a reference sample library, selection of preprocessing and variable selection strategies, and delivery of calibration files to the Hungarian partner laboratory. The project also assessed the sensitivity of NIR models to changes in pulse variety and geographic origin, with implications for raw material traceability. Outcomes include two peer-reviewed articles and training materials for quality control staff at two participating food companies.
partners: Department of Food Science, University of Szeged, Hungary
Bakotex Élelmiszeripari Kft., Baja, Hungary
Žitopromet a.d., Novi Sad

projects.title: Chemical Markers of Thermal Processing Intensity and Adulteration in Serbian Paprika Products
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated heat-induced chemical markers in Serbian paprika and ajvar products, with dual objectives: developing analytical methods for estimating thermal treatment intensity and detecting adulteration by admixture with lower-grade pepper raw material. HPLC-based HMF and furfural quantification, HS-SPME-GC-MS volatile fingerprinting, and stable isotope ratio analysis were combined in a multi-method authentication platform. Sixty producers and market samples were analysed. A provisional discrimination threshold for smoked versus unsmoked paprika was established and submitted to the Serbian Institute for Standardisation as input for a draft standard. Two junior researchers received training in GC-MS and HPLC method validation.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Serbian Institute for Standardisation, Belgrade
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Flavour Engineering of Fermented Capsicum Products Using Autochthonous Lactic Acid Bacteria
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project maps the effect of autochthonous Serbian Lactobacillus strains on volatile and polyphenol profiles of fermented pepper mash, with the aim of identifying starter culture candidates that reduce off-flavour precursors while maintaining characteristic carotenoid-derived aroma. Screening of 30 strains from traditional Vojvodina fermented pepper was carried out in year one. Three candidate strains were selected based on targeted metabolite profiles and are being tested at 50-litre pilot scale in collaboration with an industrial partner. The project supports one doctoral student and includes a knowledge-transfer component towards two regional pepper processing cooperatives.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Agro-Prehrambena Zadruga Futog, Futog, Serbia
Biotechnical Faculty, University of Ljubljana, Slovenia

projects.title: Formulation and Process Design for Microbiologically Safe Reduced-Brix Fruit Preserves Using Alternative Bulking Agents
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the gap between consumer demand for reduced-sugar fruit preserves and the technical constraints imposed by the interdependence of gel network formation, water activity, and microbiological safety in such products. The core research programme covers: (i) rheological characterisation of HM/LM-pectin blends at 45–58 °Brix across a matrix of bulking agents (maltitol, xylitol, isomaltulose, short-chain inulin); (ii) construction of predictive water-activity and shelf-life models; and (iii) laboratory-scale hot-fill process optimisation to minimise post-process syneresis. Results are disseminated via open-access journal publications and a freely available formulation-support spreadsheet tool intended for small and medium food processors.
partners: Department of Microbiology, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad (FINS)
Faculty of Food Technology, Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek, Croatia

projects.title: Packaging Barrier Requirements for Reduced-Sugar Fruit Preserves: Linking Sorption Behaviour to Shelf-Life Modelling
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This smaller provincial project builds directly on sorption isotherm data generated during the LOWBRIX project to establish practical guidance on packaging material selection for reduced-Brix preserves. Activities include determination of moisture sorption isotherms for a defined set of commercial-scale formulations, measurement of water vapour transmission rates of candidate packaging laminates, and coupling of both datasets through a mass-transfer model to predict time-to-failure (defined as aw exceeding 0.92) under typical distribution conditions in the Western Balkans. The main output is a decision-support document co-developed with two partner companies from the Vojvodina fruit-processing sector.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Food Industry Association (VFIA), Novi Sad

projects.title: Data-Driven Optimisation of Wheat Flour Blend Specifications for Industrial Milling in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CEREOPT aimed to develop transferable blend optimisation tools for wheat flour mills operating in the Vojvodina and southern Hungary regions. The project combined rheological and thermal characterisation databases from partner institutions with mathematical programming models to deliver open-source software for mill laboratories. Đurđica Ljubojević led the work package responsible for experimental characterisation of mill streams, calibration of predictive models, and validation of blends at two industrial partner mills. The project produced a shared database of 310 characterised mill streams, two peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype graphical software tool deployed at one Serbian and one Hungarian partner mill for a six-month operational trial.
partners: Cereal Research Centre, Szeged, Hungary
Mlinotest Flour Mill, Subotica, Serbia (fictional)
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Starch Fraction Specification in Wheat Milling Streams: Physicochemical Bases and Industrial Applicability
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STARCHSPEC addresses the gap between laboratory-scale starch gelatinisation characterisation and its application in industrial flour blend specification. The project systematically maps gelatinisation onset, enthalpy, and retrogradation parameters across granule size fractions from eighteen wheat genotypes over three growing seasons, correlates these with agronomic and milling variables, and incorporates the resulting empirical relationships into a constraint-based optimisation model for industrial use. Secondary objectives include assessment of how year-to-year climate variability in the Pannonian region propagates into specification uncertainty, and development of simplified rapid-test proxies for DSC parameters. The project involves one postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students at FINS, with experimental milling support from the pilot mill at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Embedded Sensor Intelligence for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Drive Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SensiDrive addressed the gap between laboratory bearing-fault research and deployable embedded diagnostic hardware. The project developed a complete pipeline from data acquisition — using both piezoelectric and MEMS accelerometers — through on-chip feature extraction and compressed neural network inference, to wireless condition reporting. A test rig simulating a three-bearing drive shaft was designed and built at FTN Novi Sad. Algorithms were validated on the rig under controlled fault conditions and in a limited field trial at a partner manufacturing facility. The project produced open benchmark data, embedded firmware, and two peer-reviewed publications. A total of four researchers and two graduate students were involved over the project duration.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute for Automation and Control, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer for Industrial Predictive Maintenance in SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CrossMaintain targeted small and medium enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia border region with limited internal engineering capacity for implementing condition monitoring. The project developed a modular training curriculum covering sensor installation, data interpretation, and maintenance decision-making, delivered in Serbian and Hungarian. FTN Novi Sad led the work package on technical content development and equipment demonstration. Two demonstration workshops were held at the NTP Novi Sad premises and one at a partner technical college in Subotica. The project also produced a bilingual technical handbook and a software tool for guided fault-frequency calculation accessible without specialist signal-processing knowledge.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Széchenyi István University, Győr, Hungary
Technical College Subotica, Serbia
Northern Hungary Industrial Cluster, Miskolc, Hungary

projects.title: Ventilation and Explosion Risk Reduction in Agro-Industrial Grain Handling Facilities of the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGRIVEX addressed the combined occupational and fire-safety risks arising from grain dust in handling and processing facilities across the Hungary–Serbia border region. The Serbian team at the Faculty of Technical Sciences led the work package on ventilation system auditing and engineering control design, carrying out on-site surveys at eight facilities in Vojvodina and two in southern Hungary. Activities included measurement of dust concentrations and airflow parameters, CFD modelling of dust dispersion under varying operational scenarios, and the preparation of a bilingual practical guide for facility operators. The project trained 34 safety officers and provided specific retrofitting recommendations for five partner facilities. Outputs were shared with the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research.
partners: Department of Fire Protection and Safety Engineering, Óbuda University, Budapest
Vojvodina Grain Processors Association, Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency Pannonia, Subotica

projects.title: Air Quality and Worker Exposure Assessment Framework for Small and Medium Milling Enterprises in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MILLAIR develops a structured, resource-efficient framework for assessing and improving air quality in small and medium flour and oilseed milling enterprises that lack in-house occupational hygiene capacity. The project combines field measurement campaigns at 20 SME facilities across Serbia, a validated simplified CFD workflow using open-source tools calibrated against full-scale measurements, and a decision-support tool that generates prioritised engineering control recommendations from basic facility inputs. A key output is an open-access database of measured dust concentrations, hood dimensions, and airflow parameters intended to serve as a regional benchmark. The project involves collaboration with the Institute of Public Health Vojvodina and runs parallel internship placements for engineering students at participating facilities.
partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia — Food Processing Cluster, Belgrade
Faculty of Occupational Safety, University of Niš

projects.title: Harmonisation Methods for Radiological Images in Networked Oncology and Neurology Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: HARMONIA addressed the lack of standardised pipelines for integrating radiological image data from heterogeneous clinical sites in Serbia and the wider Balkan region. The project developed retrospective harmonisation tools for MRI and CT modalities, validated on multi-site datasets collected from six partner clinical institutions. Key outputs included a phantom-free intensity calibration method for archival MRI, a benchmark dataset of 1,100 paired pre- and post-harmonisation volumes with expert segmentation annotations, and an open-source Python library for site-effect correction. The project involved three PhD students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and established data-sharing agreements with participating hospitals.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Oncology Institute of Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Federated Medical Image Analysis Across Hungary and Serbia
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FEDMED-IPA established a cross-border federated learning infrastructure connecting clinical and academic partners in Vojvodina and southern Hungary for privacy-preserving medical image analysis. Vojnović leads the work package on domain harmonisation, responsible for ensuring that models trained under the federated framework remain robust to scanner differences between the Serbian and Hungarian partner sites. The work package delivered a federated domain adversarial training protocol evaluated on brain MRI lesion segmentation and chest CT pathology detection tasks. The project also includes a training programme for clinical staff on data governance requirements for federated infrastructures.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Health Sciences
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Subotica

projects.title: Annotation Workflow Optimisation for Iterative Supervised Learning in Resource-Constrained Domains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops methods and open-source tooling for managing annotation workflows in active learning settings where domain expert time is the binding constraint. Research threads include adaptive batch sizing driven by real-time annotator performance proxies, disagreement-aware label aggregation, and protocols for re-querying potentially stale labels collected in early iterations. The project produced the AnnotoLoop platform, a lightweight web application that integrates with standard machine learning training pipelines via a REST API. Evaluation is conducted on three partner datasets in clinical text, environmental monitoring, and industrial quality control. The project also includes a series of user studies with annotators from partner institutions to calibrate cognitive load models.
partners: Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Environmental Monitoring, Novi Sad
Precizija d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Human-in-the-Loop Learning for Multilingual Document Processing in Public Administration
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration addressing the need for efficient supervised model development in Hungarian and Serbian public administration document processing. Kristina Ilić leads the work package on active learning query strategy adaptation for multilingual and code-switching text, coordinating data collection protocols between two public sector partners and two university teams. The project targets document classification and information extraction tasks on administrative forms, legal notices, and regional planning documents. Annotation guidelines are developed jointly to ensure cross-language label consistency. The project delivers a reusable annotation pipeline and trained baseline models released under open licences to both countries' regional administrations.
partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Informatics, Hungary
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
County Government of Csongrád-Csanád, Hungary
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Sub-microwatt Sensor Front-ends for Secure Continuous Cardiac Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENSEC addressed the power and security gap in wearable cardiac monitoring by developing analogue front-end circuits consuming below 1 µW alongside a lightweight authenticated wake-up protocol that prevents replay attacks on the wireless link. The project combined CMOS IC design in 130 nm and 65 nm processes with protocol-level work implemented on nRF5340 and STM32L4 platforms. Clinical relevance was established through a pilot recording campaign at a partner hospital cardiology ward involving 22 volunteer subjects. Deliverables included two fabricated prototypes, open-source firmware, and a dataset of annotated ECG recordings. The project funded one doctoral student who completed her thesis in 2024.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute of Biosensing Technologies, Ljubljana

projects.title: Heterogeneous Energy-Harvesting Radio Modules for Extended-Lifetime Body-Area Networks
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HERMES-BAN is a cross-border collaboration between research groups in Novi Sad and Subotica on the Serbian side and Pécs on the Hungarian side. The project develops multi-source energy harvesting boards combining thermoelectric and photovoltaic elements with a shared power management IC, targeting ambulatory patient monitoring in rural primary-care settings where battery replacement is difficult. The Novi Sad team leads the work package on power management circuit design and protocol-level duty-cycle adaptation. Expected outcomes include two prototype boards, a joint dataset from a 30-subject field trial, and two joint publications. The project also funds a student mobility scheme for three M.Sc. students per year.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Subotica Tech — College of Applied Sciences
Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs

projects.title: Physiological Signal Compression for Low-Power Telemetry in Remote Patient Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates compression algorithms suitable for deployment on low-power microcontrollers in wearable and implantable patient monitoring devices. Work packages cover beat-synchronous transform coding, sparse dictionary methods, and lightweight learned entropy models with a shared emphasis on keeping encoder complexity below 10 mJ per minute of single-lead ECG. The project includes a clinical validation component in collaboration with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, where compressed and reconstructed signals are assessed for diagnostic equivalence by cardiologists. A reference software library with documented APIs is being developed for use by regional medical-device developers. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Telemedicine Data Infrastructure for Cardiac Monitoring
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border infrastructure project aiming to establish shared telemedicine data pipelines between partner hospitals in southern Hungary and the Vojvodina region. Šarić leads the work package on signal compression and transmission standards, contributing ECG and PPG codec implementations compliant with the SCP-ECG data standard. The work package also produces interoperability guidelines for compressed signal exchange between different hospital information systems used on the two sides of the border. Deliverables include a compression middleware component integrated into the project's shared telemedicine platform and a joint training session for clinical IT staff at both partner sites.
partners: Somogy County Health Authority, Kaposvár
General Hospital Subotica
Mediconn d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Wearable Acoustic Computing for Elderly Health Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a prototype wearable tracheal sound monitor targeting three clinical events—wheeze, cough, and apnoea—that can operate autonomously for at least seven days on a single battery charge. Research tasks included design of the analogue front end, implementation of noise-robust feature extraction on a Cortex-M4 platform, collection of annotated clinical recordings at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, and validation of the detection algorithms in a simulated home environment. A secondary workstream produced personalised threshold adaptation algorithms validated on data from 54 older adults. The project trained two doctoral students and produced six journal and conference publications. A functional prototype was demonstrated at the Institute of Gerontology, Belgrade.
partners: Institute of Pulmonology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Institute of Gerontology, Belgrade
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Acoustic Remote Observation Systems for Cross-Border Healthcare Applications
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs focused on deploying low-power acoustic sensor networks in rural primary health care centres in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. The Novi Sad team, led by Đukić, is responsible for the embedded signal processing workpackage: developing and validating classifiers for respiratory and activity-monitoring events that operate on sub-milliwatt hardware without cloud connectivity. The project includes a pilot installation in four health centres involving continuous 30-day deployments. Results feed into a jointly maintained open dataset and a clinical protocol for acoustic-based pre-screening of respiratory conditions in underserved communities.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
Primary Health Care Centre Subotica
Primary Health Care Institute Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Digital Accessibility for Aging Populations in Vojvodina Public Services
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project conducted structured usability evaluations of six publicly accessible digital services offered by provincial and municipal authorities in Vojvodina, with a focus on users aged 60 and above. Evaluation methods included task-based usability testing, heuristic analysis by trained evaluators, and short interviews with 120 participants recruited across urban and rural sites. Findings were synthesised into a set of practical accessibility guidelines translated into Serbian and distributed to participating institutions. A secondary aim was to build local capacity for in-house usability evaluation in public administration by delivering two training workshops for civil servants responsible for digital services. The project involved collaboration with two municipal information technology departments and the Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina.
partners: City Administration of Novi Sad, IT Department
Municipality of Zrenjanin, Digital Services Office
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina

projects.title: Cross-National Benchmarking of Older-Adult User Experience in Central and Southeast Europe
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: SILVER-UX is a multi-site study coordinating usability and user-experience measurement across eight countries in Central and Southeast Europe, with the aim of establishing comparable national benchmarks for older adult interaction with public digital infrastructure. The University of Novi Sad team is responsible for data collection in Serbia and for contributing to the development of a shared measurement protocol that accommodates linguistic and cultural variation. Radomir Simić leads participant recruitment and testing at the Novi Sad site, working with a sample target of 150 older adult participants over the project period. The consortium includes universities, public health institutes, and one software standards body.
partners: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Arts
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Department of Ergonomics
Charles University Prague, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics
Romanian National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics
Croatian Institute for Brain Research

projects.title: Hygroscopic Fatigue Mechanisms in Engineering Polymers for Implantable and Reusable Biomedical Devices
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the coupled effects of moisture absorption and cyclic mechanical loading on fatigue life and dimensional stability in PA6, PA66-GF30, PEEK, and TPU as representative materials used in implantable and reusable biomedical devices. Work packages cover experimental characterisation of moisture-dependent fatigue properties, development of predictive lifetime models incorporating hygroscopic swelling as an internal stress source, and validation against representative component geometries tested in a custom environmental fatigue chamber. The project also includes a screening workstream evaluating DMA-based non-destructive indicators of residual fatigue life. Results are targeted at informing ISO 10993-compatible ageing test design for polymer medical device components.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Orthopaedic Research Unit, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Dimensional Stability of Thermoplastic Components in Medical Device Assembly: Cross-Border Materials Database
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project between universities in Novi Sad and Budapest establishing a shared experimental database of hygroscopic dimensional change data for ten engineering thermoplastics under controlled humidity and temperature conditions relevant to medical device assembly environments. The Novi Sad team was responsible for specimen preparation, CMM dimensional measurement, and moisture uptake characterisation, while the Budapest team contributed FEA modelling and tolerance analysis. The database is accessible to SMEs in the Vojvodina–Southern Great Plain region through a web interface developed within the project. A joint workshop series for industrial partners was held in both cities.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina

projects.title: Spirometric Reference Equations for the Central Balkans: A Multi-Centre Derivation and Validation Study
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SPIRAREG coordinated data collection at five clinical and occupational health sites across Serbia and established a shared spirometric repository of approximately 3,800 healthy adults. The project produced sex-, age-, and height-stratified reference equations for FVC, FEV1, and FEV1/FVC using both ordinary least-squares and LMS approaches, with validation against GLI-2012 global equations. A secondary objective was to evaluate whether systematic differences between urban and rural Vojvodina populations warranted separate equations; the final analysis found no clinically meaningful difference. Results are publicly released as R and Python packages and submitted to the GLI working group for consideration. The project also trained two PhD students in advanced statistical modelling of physiological data.
partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Clinic for Occupational Diseases, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Department of Physiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Kragujevac
Institute of Pneumology, University of Timișoara

projects.title: Cross-Border Surveillance of Occupational Lung Function in Agriculture and Food Processing Along the Danube Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANULUNG compared occupational spirometric surveillance practices and outcomes in agricultural and food-processing workforces on both the Serbian and Hungarian sides of the Danube basin. Crnković led the work package responsible for harmonising spirometric protocols and deriving a joint reference dataset applicable across the two national populations. The project enrolled 1,140 workers at eleven sites, performed baseline and two-year follow-up spirometry, and integrated personal dust exposure measurements. Key outputs included a practical surveillance guideline adopted by three occupational health services in Vojvodina, and a cross-border early-detection algorithm for at-risk workers whose annual FEV1 decline exceeded modelled trajectories.
partners: Faculty of Medicine, University of Pécs
National Institute of Occupational Health, Budapest
Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, Vojvodina
Agro-Health Centre Subotica

projects.title: Optimisation of Low-Volume Medical Device Assembly Lines under Regulatory and Demand Uncertainty
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the gap between generic assembly line optimisation methods and the specific constraints of regulated medical device manufacturing in Serbia. Key objectives include: development of stochastic and robust ALBP formulations that incorporate regulatory qualification requirements for operators; construction of a calibrated discrete-event simulation test bed using anonymised production data from two partner manufacturers; and integration of inventory cost models into sequencing decisions for lines producing 2–8 model variants at daily volumes of 20–150 units. Results are disseminated through open-access journal publications and a practical decision-support tool validated with industry partners. The project involves two researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and one from the Faculty of Economics, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Novi Sad
MedAssemble d.o.o. Novi Sad (observer partner)

projects.title: Cross-Border Competency Development in Production Systems Optimisation for SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project aimed at improving the capacity of small and medium-sized manufacturers in the Hungary–Serbia border region to apply quantitative production optimisation methods. The University of Novi Sad team led the work package on assembly line design and scheduling training, delivering four two-day workshops attended by a combined total of 63 enterprise participants. Training materials covered line balancing fundamentals, practical use of simulation tools, and basic inventory cost modelling. Sekulić's team also conducted pre- and post-training capability assessments in five participating companies and developed a publicly available workbook with spreadsheet-based ALBP tools. The project produced a comparative report on production planning practices across 12 SMEs in the region.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce
Baranya County Enterprise Agency, Pécs

projects.title: Wearable Real-Time In-Situ Self-Calibrating Force Tracking for Upper-Limb Occupational Health Assessment
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WRISTRACK develops a wrist-worn force measurement band targeted at assembly-line workers performing repetitive upper-limb tasks. The core technical objective is an end-to-end self-calibrating measurement chain that compensates for sensor drift over a full eight-hour shift without removal from the wrist. Janković leads the project and is responsible for the sensor characterisation workpackage and the in-situ reference cell design. A second workpackage, led by the Faculty of Sport and Physical Education partner, focuses on ergonomic scoring methodology. The project runs for 36 months and includes a 12-week field validation at a partner manufacturing facility in Zrenjanin. Target performance is drift-corrected force accuracy better than 0.5 N over an eight-hour session.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sport and Physical Education, University of Novi Sad
Precizija d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Flexible Sensor Calibration Infrastructure for Biomedical Wearables
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: FlexSensCal established shared measurement infrastructure at BioSense Institute for the characterisation of flexible and stretchable sensors intended for biomedical wearables. Janković led the workpackage on long-term drift and ageing, which included procurement and commissioning of a humidity-controlled cyclic loading rig and a temperature-cycling impedance spectroscopy station. The project produced a characterisation protocol document adopted by two other research groups in the institute and contributed baseline drift data used in her subsequent journal publications. Total budget for the drift and ageing workpackage was approximately 1.8 million RSD.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Bridging Laboratory Gait Analysis and Primary Care Through Sparse-Observation Wearable Protocols
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GAITBRIDGE developed and validated a clinical workflow for gait-based fall risk screening that requires only two 8-second walking passes and a single waist-worn IMU, making it compatible with standard primary care consultation constraints. The project enrolled 140 participants across three age groups and two clinical sites in Vojvodina. Core activities included construction of a labelled multivariate time-series dataset, systematic benchmarking of sequence classifiers under sparse-observation conditions, and a pilot deployment study with four general practitioners. The project also produced open-source software for feature extraction and a calibration-free preprocessing pipeline. Results fed directly into three journal publications and one conference paper.
partners: Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Gerontology, Belgrade
Health Centre Novi Sad

projects.title: Mobile Quality Assessment of Gait in Post-Surgical Orthopaedic Rehabilitation Across the Serbia–Hungary Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MOBIQUALGAIT addresses the need for gait monitoring tools usable by physiotherapy teams in district hospitals and outpatient rehabilitation centres in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The project focuses on total knee and hip arthroplasty patients tracked from 6 weeks to 6 months post-surgery. The University of Novi Sad team (led by Urošević) is responsible for algorithm development and validation, while the Hungarian partner handles clinical data collection and physiotherapist training. The project will produce a validated assessment module, a training manual, and a data-sharing agreement template for cross-border clinical research. Two regional hospitals in Subotica and Pécs are partner clinical sites.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Somogy County Kaposi Mór Teaching Hospital, Kaposvár
Rehabilitation Institute Subotica

projects.title: Standardised Biomechanical Symmetry Metrics for Stroke Rehabilitation Assessment Across Clinical Sites
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SYMMETRA aimed to develop and clinically validate a standardised battery of biomechanical symmetry metrics for monitoring motor recovery in post-stroke rehabilitation, and to establish cross-site measurement equivalence across three Serbian clinical sites. The project recruited 210 stroke patients across Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Niš and administered a common IMU-based protocol at three standardised time points. Key deliverables included a harmonised data collection protocol, normative symmetry ranges stratified by stroke severity and age, MCID estimates for core metrics, and an open-access dataset. Collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences at the University of Novi Sad provided signal processing and data infrastructure support. The project also produced a clinician training programme and accompanying assessment manual adopted by two participating clinics.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Neurology Clinic, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Neurology Clinic, Clinical Centre of Serbia, Belgrade
Neurology Clinic, University Clinical Centre Niš

projects.title: Wearable Sensor Systems for Home-Based Neurological Rehabilitation Monitoring in South-East Europe
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: REHAB-SENSE addresses the gap in continuous motor monitoring between supervised rehabilitation episodes and community living for stroke and Parkinson's disease patients. The project develops and field-tests a wearable sensor package with a companion application designed for independent daily use by neurological patients in home settings. Todić leads the clinical validation work package, responsible for defining measurement protocols, coordinating patient recruitment at the Novi Sad site, and benchmarking wearable outputs against reference laboratory assessments. The project will produce validated home-use monitoring guidelines, a harmonised dataset from Serbian and Hungarian sites, and a prototype application suitable for evaluation in a future randomised feasibility trial. The consortium includes engineering, clinical, and patient organisation partners from both countries.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Novi Sad
Department of Neurology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Pécs
Hungarian Stroke Patient Association

projects.title: Harmonisation of Electronic Health Records for Cross-Border Clinical Research in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: HARMON-EHR brought together seven institutions from Serbia, Croatia, Hungary, and Romania to develop shared data models, ICD-to-SNOMED mapping pipelines, and federated imputation tools enabling the assembly of harmonised longitudinal patient cohorts across borders. Vera Vuković led Work Package 3, which covered terminology alignment and missing-data methodology. The project produced two open-source software packages, four benchmark datasets released under controlled-access licences, and a set of recommendations for regional health data governance adopted as input to a national digitisation strategy document. The consortium trained fourteen early-career researchers through a series of cross-site secondments.
partners: University of Pécs Medical School, Hungary
Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, University of Zagreb
Institute for Medical Informatics, University of Ljubljana
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Real-Time Readmission Risk Assessment Using Continuously Updated EHR Streams
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: READICAST develops methods for updating readmission risk scores in real time as new laboratory results and clinical notes arrive during a hospital stay, rather than relying solely on data available at admission. The project combines online learning techniques with the ontology-mapping and imputation infrastructure developed in earlier work. A pilot deployment is planned at two Vojvodina hospitals in the final project year. The team consists of four researchers at BioSense Institute and two clinical collaborators. Outputs will include a validated prototype system, three peer-reviewed publications, and open methodology documentation sufficient for replication at other regional centres.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin

projects.title: Variable-Bandwidth Adaptive Streaming Protocols for Underserved Regional Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VARSTREAM addresses video streaming quality in rural and peri-urban areas of Vojvodina where fixed broadband availability is limited and mobile coverage is variable. The project combines field measurement campaigns on LTE and satellite backhaul links with protocol-level work on adaptive bitrate controllers designed for high-latency, low-bandwidth conditions. A WAN emulation testbed calibrated from field measurements supports reproducible testing of candidate solutions. Outputs include a bitrate-ladder design methodology, an open-source ABR controller implementation, and a dataset of 18 months of link-quality traces from three rural measurement sites in Vojvodina, released publicly. Two PhD students are supported.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina (RDA Vojvodina)
Institute for Telecommunications and Electronics Novi Sad (ITEN)

projects.title: Cross-Border Transport Protocol Interoperability for Multimedia Services in the Hungary–Serbia Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSTRANS investigated interoperability of QoS-sensitive multimedia transport protocols across national network operator boundaries in the Subotica–Szeged corridor. Mirjana Bošković led the work package on protocol conformance testing, which deployed passive measurement probes at four cross-border handover points to characterise DSCP re-marking behaviour and delay variation introduced by carrier-grade NAT. The project produced a conformance test suite, a jointly operated monitoring dashboard, and recommendations for bilateral peering agreements. Results informed network configuration changes at both the Serbian and Hungarian partner institutions, reducing inter-domain jitter for VoIP flows from 22 ms to 6 ms on the primary test path.
partners: University of Szeged, Department of Computer Science (Hungary)
Telecom Infrastructure Operator Subotica d.o.o. (Serbia)
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences (Serbia)

projects.title: Subject-Specific Soft-Tissue Finite-Element Tools for Prosthetic Socket Fitting
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SOFTFIT aimed to build a computationally efficient, clinically deployable pipeline for patient-specific socket design. The project combined MRI-based tissue segmentation, automated statistical shape modelling and gradient-free FEA optimisation to generate initial socket geometries requiring minimal clinical adjustment. A wearable pressure-mapping array developed within the project provided in-socket validation data from 40 amputee volunteers over two walking trials each. The pipeline was piloted at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina in collaboration with two prosthetists and validated against a matched retrospective control cohort. Final deliverables included an open-format segmentation dataset of 47 residual limbs and a documented FEA workflow released to academic users.

projects.title: Biomechanical Modelling Framework for Lower-Limb Orthotic Devices in Cross-Border Rehabilitation Centres
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project established shared computational and clinical protocols for lower-limb orthotic assessment at rehabilitation centres in Novi Sad and Pécs. Kapor led the modelling work package, which standardised MRI acquisition parameters, tissue segmentation procedures and FEA boundary conditions across both sites to ensure inter-site reproducibility. The project delivered a bilateral training workshop for clinicians and engineers, a comparative dataset of AFO interface pressures across 30 subjects from both sites, and draft bilateral guidelines for FEA use in orthotics prescription. Clinical partners identified trim-line geometry and liner selection as priority decision points where simulation support would most reduce fitting iterations.

projects.title: Service-Life Prediction for Laser-Sintered Polymer Components under Realistic Loading Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: POLYLIFE investigated fatigue and damage accumulation in selective laser sintered PA12 parts subjected to realistic variable-amplitude load histories representative of lightweight structural applications. The project combined micro-CT void characterisation, digital image correlation during cycling, and modified cumulative damage modelling to produce a validated life-prediction framework. A reference dataset of over 400 specimens tested under defined conditions was assembled and made publicly available. Three industrial partners provided component geometries and loading spectra drawn from their production applications. The project supported two doctoral students and resulted in six peer-reviewed publications. A simplified spreadsheet tool implementing the modified damage rule was distributed to project partners.

projects.title: Additive Manufacturing Quality Assurance for Small and Medium Enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project aimed to build shared capacity for quality assurance in additive manufacturing among SMEs located in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Erzsébet Nagy led the work package on materials characterisation and testing protocol development, delivering harmonised test procedures for SLS polymer parts and organising three joint training workshops for company technicians. The project equipped a shared reference laboratory at the University of Novi Sad with a micro-CT scanner accessible to SME partners. A catalogue of process-parameter–property relationships for commercially available SLS powders was produced as an open-access technical report. projects.title: Automatizovano praćenje aditivne proizvodnje vizuelnom inteligencijom
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj razvoj modularne, hardverski nezavisne platforme za praćenje kvaliteta u realnom vremenu tokom FDM štampe, zasnovane na kombinaciji konvolucionih neuronskih mreža i višemodalnih senzorskih sistema. Projekat je uključivao saradnju s industrijskim partnerima radi validacije prototipa u realnim proizvodnim uslovima. projects.title: Warehouse Pose Estimation Under Real-World Conditions for Worker Safety Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated monocular pose estimation methods adapted to logistics warehouse environments where occlusion, mixed artificial lighting, and heavy machinery create severe domain shift from standard benchmark conditions. Research activities included collection and annotation of the WarePose dataset, design of source-free adaptation procedures, and integration of kinematic constraint layers into detection pipelines. Collaboration with two logistics companies in Vojvodina provided access to real facilities for data collection and for pilot deployment of a software monitoring prototype. The project also supported two PhD students and produced six peer-reviewed publications. The resulting software prototype estimates ergonomic risk indicators from monocular CCTV footage without modifying existing camera infrastructure.

projects.title: Adaptive Visual Perception for Human Pose Estimation Across Heterogeneous Industrial Deployments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project addressing the gap between laboratory performance and real-world deployment of pose estimation systems in manufacturing and logistics settings in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The Novi Sad team leads the work package on domain-adaptive training strategies, contributing test-time adaptation algorithms and the WarePose benchmark. The Hungarian partner contributes automotive assembly-line datasets and sensor fusion expertise. Joint student exchanges and a shared annotated dataset repository are planned outputs. The project targets SMEs in the region that cannot afford bespoke sensor installations and instead rely on existing monocular camera infrastructure.
