projects.title: Low-Resource Skeleton-Based Recognition for Intelligent Rehabilitation Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REHABIT addressed the shortage of labelled motion data in clinical rehabilitation settings by combining transfer learning from public motion-capture corpora with systematic data augmentation. The project produced an open rehabilitation exercise benchmark, a suite of few-shot classifiers, and a prototype monitoring application evaluated in collaboration with the Institute of Orthopedic Surgery at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. The team consisted of four researchers at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, and one clinical partner. Deliverables included six peer-reviewed publications, the public benchmark dataset, and an open-source software library implementing the few-shot evaluation protocol. The project also supported two PhD students who contributed to the benchmarking and augmentation workstreams.

projects.title: Cross-Domain Transfer for Skeletal Motion Analysis in Sport and Healthcare
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMOVE is a joint Hungarian-Serbian project exploring whether motion-capture data collected in sport science institutes can serve as pre-training material for healthcare applications including gait pathology classification and post-operative rehabilitation monitoring. Vojnović leads the work package responsible for domain-gap analysis and adapter-based fine-tuning methods. Partner institutions contribute motion datasets from athletics and swimming biomechanics. The project includes a joint data collection campaign harmonising skeleton topology and metadata standards across sites to enable meaningful cross-domain transfer experiments. Three joint publications and one shared dataset are planned as primary outputs by the project end.

projects.title: Rapid Immunochromatographic Screening Tools for Regulated Mycotoxins in Vojvodina Cereal Chains
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project developed and validated lateral-flow immunoassay strips for the four mycotoxins most prevalent in Vojvodina cereals: aflatoxin B1, deoxynivalenol, zearalenone, and fumonisin B1. Activities included antibody characterisation by SPR, strip fabrication and optimisation, and field validation across 15 agricultural sites. A portable strip reader was evaluated for semi-quantitative use by grain inspectors. The project produced validated protocols adopted by two regional grain inspection bodies and provided the basis for the multiplexed strip format developed in subsequent work. Two master's theses and one PhD chapter were completed under this project.

projects.title: Antibody Binding Kinetics Under Capillary Flow: Modelling and Experimental Validation for Immunochromatographic Format Design
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: BINDFLOW addresses the gap between equilibrium SPR measurements and actual antibody performance in capillary-flow immunochromatographic systems. The project combines experimental SPR kinetics measurements for a library of 18 anti-mycotoxin and anti-bacterial antibodies with computational modelling of advection–diffusion–reaction kinetics on nitrocellulose and cellulose acetate membranes. Outputs include a publicly available parameter database and a web-accessible strip design simulation tool. Collaboration with the University of Ljubljana provides flow visualisation by confocal microscopy, and a bilateral component with the University of Debrecen covers agricultural application validation. One postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students are funded by the project.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Statistical Process Control Methods for Reproducible Laboratory-Scale Membrane Fabrication
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to transfer statistical process control methodology from industrial manufacturing to laboratory-scale membrane casting and to quantify the main sources of variability in phase-inversion processes. Activities included an eight-month baseline monitoring campaign covering 87 membrane batches, development and validation of the laser triangulation in-line thickness measurement system, and statistical modelling of the relationship between environmental variables (humidity, temperature) and membrane performance indicators. A protocol document for SPC implementation in academic membrane fabrication laboratories was produced as a key deliverable. Two junior researchers were trained in SPC methods and membrane characterisation during the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-border Knowledge Transfer in Polymeric Membrane Materials for Water Treatment Applications
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMEM brought together two universities and one technology park entity to exchange knowledge and research infrastructure in membrane fabrication for water treatment. Bačić led the work package on membrane characterisation harmonisation, establishing shared protocols for SEM image analysis and permporometry across the two partner institutions. The project included three joint workshops, two student exchange visits totalling 12 months, and a jointly operated online repository of reference SEM images and analysis scripts. A mixed-matrix membrane demonstrator for low-pressure nanofiltration was produced as a proof-of-concept at the end of the project.
partners: Department of Chemical Technology, Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

projects.title: Cost-Sensitive Classification Algorithms for Laboratory Decision Support in Resource-Constrained Settings
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CLASSLAB addressed the gap between classification algorithm research and practical laboratory deployment by developing a modular software toolkit for cost-sensitive threshold optimisation and model calibration. The project collected retrospective laboratory datasets from three hospitals in Vojvodina under data-sharing agreements and used them to benchmark methods across a range of imbalance ratios and cost structures. A secondary objective was to develop standardised protocols for eliciting misclassification cost estimates from clinical staff. The toolkit was implemented in Python and released as open-source software. The project supported two doctoral students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. User testing with laboratory informaticians at the partner hospitals informed two revision cycles of the software interface.

Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina

Kmeťová led the work package on algorithm harmonisation, responsible for ensuring that classifiers trained on pooled data from both countries achieved performance equivalent to site-specific models. The work package developed a federated evaluation protocol that avoids direct data transfer and produced benchmarking results for six classification tasks across haematology and clinical chemistry. Challenges related to differing reference interval standards between Serbian and Hungarian laboratories were addressed through a normalization layer described in a technical deliverable submitted in year two.

projects.title: Cross-Border Surveillance of Antimicrobial-Resistant Enterococci in Livestock and the Environment Across the Danube Region

projects.summary: ENTRODAN established a harmonised cross-border monitoring system for AMR enterococci in swine and poultry farms, slaughterhouse effluents, and riverine water at shared Serbia–Hungary border zones. Bulatović led the work package responsible for microbiological methods harmonisation, ensuring that both partner laboratories used identical broth microdilution panels and applied EUCAST ECOFF values consistently. The project collected over 2,400 environmental and animal samples across three seasons, generated a joint resistance database, and produced a bilingual technical guidance document for regional veterinary authorities. Training workshops for farm veterinarians and laboratory technicians were conducted in Novi Sad and Pécs. The project also funded an equipment upgrade for the Novi Sad laboratory, including a semi-automated MIC reader.

projects.title: Genomic Epidemiology of Transferable Antimicrobial Resistance in Food-Animal Enterococcus spp. in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VETO-AMR is a national research project aimed at generating the first comprehensive genomic dataset of livestock Enterococcus spp. from Serbia that combines whole-genome sequencing with conjugation phenotype data. The project collects isolates from swine, cattle, and poultry farms across four districts of Vojvodina per year, performs Illumina sequencing, and uses bioinformatic pipelines to track resistance gene mobility via mobile genetic elements. A secondary objective is to assess the overlap between livestock and human clinical Enterococcus sequence types using publicly available clinical genome databases. The project employs one postdoctoral researcher and one PhD student, and involves a collaboration with the Institute of Medical Microbiology at the University of Belgrade Clinical Centre for comparative human clinical isolate data.

projects.title: Decentralised Genotyping Workflows for Livestock Traceability in Cross-Border Agricultural Zones
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia

Velimir Bjelica led the work package on nucleic acid extraction standardisation and quality assessment, coordinating protocol testing at seven participating farms across Vojvodina and Baranya county. The project produced a field-usable Standard Operating Procedure booklet for bead-beating extraction from ear-notch and hair samples, validated against a 12-microsatellite genotyping panel. Training workshops were delivered to 34 veterinary technicians in both countries. The project did not develop new reagents but consolidated existing extraction chemistry into a deployable, equipment-light format.

projects.title: Optimisation of Nucleic Acid Recovery from Environmentally Degraded Biological Matrices for Biosurveillance Applications

projects.summary: NUCLOPTA addresses the systematic characterisation of chemical inhibitors co-purified from five environmentally challenging matrices: agricultural soil, dried blood spots, paraffin-embedded tissue, buccal swabs stored at ambient temperature, and processed food homogenates. The project benchmarks extraction chemistry modifications including alternative chaotropic agents, novel elution buffers, and inhibitor-sequestering additives against a standardised amplification fidelity panel. A key output is an open-access decision-support tool that recommends extraction protocol modifications based on matrix type and downstream assay sensitivity requirements. The project employs two doctoral students and one research assistant at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, with validation work carried out in collaboration with a public health laboratory in Subotica.

projects.title: Cloud-Adaptive Genomic Workflow Orchestration for Clinical Research in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GENOMFLO addresses the high computational cost and long turnaround time of clinical WGS and WES pipelines at research hospitals in Serbia and the region. The project develops and validates a cloud-cost-aware orchestration layer that dynamically selects between on-premises HPC and spot-instance cloud execution depending on queue state, sample priority, and real-time cloud pricing. It also provides standardised containerised workflow components for alignment and variant calling that can be deployed by laboratories with limited bioinformatics staff. Pilot deployments are planned at two regional clinical partners. The project includes training activities for clinical bioinformaticians and releases all software under an open-source licence.

projects.title: Scalable Variant Detection Pipelines for Plant Breeding Genomics
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: AGRIVAR focused on adapting variant-calling pipelines originally designed for human clinical genomics to the needs of plant breeding programmes in Vojvodina, where large polyploid crop genomes and population-scale resequencing studies create distinct computational challenges. The project produced benchmark datasets for two commercially important crop species and a set of open workflow templates deposited in the group's public repository.

Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Health Literacy and Accessible Communication in Regulatory Patient Information across the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined how health literacy standards are applied—or absent—from regulated patient-facing documents in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. Activities included a comparative corpus analysis of package inserts and consent forms, development of a shared readability evaluation protocol for the three regulatory contexts, and a series of participatory workshops with patient associations and regulatory professionals. A key output was a set of evidence-based revision guidelines submitted to the Serbian Medicines and Medical Devices Agency for consideration in their ongoing standardisation process. The project supported two early-career researchers and produced seven peer-reviewed outputs.

projects.title: Speciation Analysis and Safety Assessment of Trace Elements in Microalgal Phycobiliprotein Products

The University of Novi Sad team led process modelling and energy auditing, while the Hungarian partner contributed agro-climatic data analysis and strain selection. A key objective is developing a reward function that balances short-term exercise performance with estimated long-term knowledge retention, measured through delayed post-tests administered at 4-week intervals. projects.title: Fairness-Aware Knowledge Tracing for National Assessment Platforms
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: KT-FAIR examines sources of demographic disparity in knowledge tracing model outputs when models are deployed in national-scale assessment preparation platforms. The project combines empirical analysis of existing interaction datasets with targeted data collection across school types in Vojvodina. It develops and tests mitigation strategies including reweighted training objectives and post-hoc calibration adjustments. Collaboration with the Department of Educational Technology at TU Kaiserslautern provides access to comparative datasets from German secondary-school platforms, enabling cross-country analysis. Expected outputs include a fairness evaluation framework, two journal articles, and a policy brief directed at the Institute for Education Quality and Evaluation of Serbia.

projects.title: Learning Analytics Statistical Toolbox for Higher Education Institutions in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a suite of statistical models for predicting student competency outcomes from learning management system log data in Serbian and regional universities. Work packages covered data collection protocol design, longitudinal modelling methodology, fairness auditing of deployed models, and integration of model outputs into a Moodle plugin that generates adviser-facing dashboards. Partner institutions contributed log datasets spanning approximately 18,000 students, enabling cross-institutional model evaluation. The project also produced an open-access methodological handbook for institutional analytics practitioners and organised two regional training workshops for academic staff at partner faculties. All analysis code and anonymised benchmark datasets are published under a Creative Commons licence.

Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Kragujevac

projects.title: Cross-Institutional Learning Trace Data Harmonisation for Comparative Analytics
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSLEARN addresses the lack of interoperability between learning management system log formats at universities on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border, which prevents comparative analytics research. The project is producing a shared data schema and an open-source transformation pipeline covering Moodle, Canvas, and one proprietary system used by a Hungarian partner. Mitrović leads the work package on statistical harmonisation, which develops procedures for aligning feature distributions across institutions before joint model training. An ongoing longitudinal study tracks 2,600 students across four partner universities from enrolment through first degree, with annual data extracts. Outputs include a harmonised benchmark dataset and two cross-border student mobility analytics pilots.

projects.title: Heritage Language Instruction and Cross-Border Curriculum Alignment in Hungarian Minority Schools of the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project brought together teacher education institutions and regional education authorities in Hungary and Serbia to document and partially harmonise curriculum frameworks for Hungarian heritage-language instruction in primary schools. Kecman led the work package on learner profiling and diagnostic tool development. Activities included classroom observations at 12 partner schools, joint teacher training workshops in Subotica and Pécs, and production of a shared guidance document for curriculum alignment. The project produced a freely available diagnostic screening battery (see 2021 publication) and a bilingual practitioner handbook distributed to 340 teachers across participating regions. A small learner corpus of 1,800 oral and written samples was compiled and is maintained at the Subotica faculty.

projects.title: Pedagogical Approaches to Morphosyntactic Acquisition in Minority-Language Bilingual Classrooms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MINPED investigates whether explicit contrastive grammar instruction, introduced at structured points in the grade three to six curriculum, improves morphosyntactic accuracy in heritage-Hungarian learners compared to a matched control group receiving standard instruction. A quasi-experimental design with pre-, mid-, and post-tests is running across eight primary schools in Vojvodina. The treatment group receives a contrastive module developed by the project team, covering nominal case, verb prefixation, and postpositional phrases. Primary outcome measures are written accuracy rates and elicited oral production scores; secondary outcomes include learner metalinguistic awareness. Data collection for grades three and four is complete; grade five data collection is ongoing. The project also funds a part-time research assistant and visiting collaboration with the University of Szeged.

projects.title: Bandwidth-Efficient Tile-Based Rendering Pipelines for Low-Power Embedded Devices
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated bandwidth reduction strategies for tile-based deferred rendering on mobile and embedded GPU architectures. The main research directions were G-buffer format optimisation, render-pass merging under Vulkan, and power-aware pass scheduling. The group built a measurement infrastructure combining hardware GPU performance counters with external current monitors to produce fine-grained power and bandwidth profiles. Results were validated on five distinct ARM Mali and Qualcomm Adreno devices. The project funded two doctoral students and produced six peer-reviewed publications. Collaboration with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš provided access to thermal measurement equipment and expanded the experimental device pool.

Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Embedded Vision Processing for Autonomous Guided Vehicles in Smart Factory Environments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration addressing real-time visual processing pipelines on embedded hardware for autonomous guided vehicles deployed in light manufacturing facilities. Vranješ led the work package on GPU-accelerated image processing, responsible for adapting mobile rendering pipeline techniques — particularly depth pass management and shader complexity control — to computer vision preprocessing tasks running on automotive-grade embedded SoCs. The work package delivered a prototype preprocessing pipeline achieving 30 fps processing of 1080p camera feeds on a hardware platform drawing under 5 W. Partner institutions contributed vehicle hardware, factory testbed facilities, and application domain expertise.

projects.title: Аутоматска анализа аргументације у писаним радовима студената: ка адаптивним системима за повратну информацију у српском образовању
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат ArgWrite-RS бавио се изградњом алата за аутоматску дијагностику аргументационе структуре у студентским есејима на српском језику. Основни резултати укључују: анотирани корпус од 2.200 есеја, скуп модела за препознавање аргументационих компоненти и прототип веб-платформе за формативно оцењивање у складу с рубриком. Платформа је пилотирана на три факултета Универзитета у Новом Саду током академске 2023/2024. године; учествовало је 340 студената. Пројекат је финансирао и развој јавно доступног бенчмарка SrpCohBench. Сарадници укључују истраживаче са Факултета техничких наука, Педагошког факултета у Сомбору и Института Јожеф Стефан из Љубљане.
partners: Факултет техничких наука, Универзитет у Новом Саду

projects.title: Discourse Resources and Evaluation Benchmarks for Central and Eastern European Languages
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: DISC-CEE окупио је осам партнерских институција из шест земаља са циљем изградње упоредивих ресурса за анализу дискурса у мање ресурсираним европским језицима, укључујући српски, пољски, чешки, мађарски, румунски и словачки. Филип Арсић водио је радни пакет посвећен анотацији дискурсних конектора и кохеренцијских релација у српском и хрватском. У оквиру пројекта објављени су заједнички анотациони приручник, вишеједзична верзија корпуса и скуп алата за аутоматску сегментацију дискурса. Резултати су депоновани у CLARIN-овој инфраструктури и остају доступни за академску употребу.

projects.title: Reliable Real-Time Media Transport Architectures for Heterogeneous Access Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates protocol-level and architectural mechanisms for maintaining acceptable quality of experience in real-time media sessions when the underlying network is heterogeneous—mixing wired, Wi-Fi, and cellular access. Work packages cover WebRTC signalling optimisation, SFU cluster coordination, and adaptive bitrate control under variable conditions. The project established a dedicated multi-node streaming testbed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and produced a set of open-source measurement tools released on the group's public repository. Six journal and conference papers were produced during the project period, and two master's theses were completed under its umbrella.

projects.title: Cross-Border Multimedia Delivery Optimisation for Public Broadcasters in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSSTREAM addressed the specific challenges faced by regional public broadcasters delivering live and on-demand video streams across the Hungary–Serbia border, where CDN footprint is limited and last-mile connectivity varies widely. Kuzmanović led the work package on adaptive streaming protocol selection and configuration, conducting a measurement campaign in six towns on both sides of the border using standardised playback clients. Recommendations on segment duration, codec profile, and TURN server placement were delivered to the two broadcaster partners. The project also produced a joint training workshop for technical staff at both broadcasters attended by 34 participants.

projects.title: Behavioural and Psychometric Signatures of Academic Burnout: Toward Validated Early Warning Indicators in Serbian Higher Education
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: BURNSIG aimed to establish a validated set of observable and self-reported indicators of academic burnout that could be operationalised within existing university administrative systems. The project combined large-scale survey measurement with extraction of passive behavioural data from LMS logs and student administrative records across four Serbian universities. Key outputs included the registered replication study of behavioural disengagement indicators, the cluster-analytic profiling paper, and a technical report delivered to partner universities. The project also produced an open dataset (anonymised) for secondary use and a practical guide for student affairs offices on interpreting burnout-risk scores. Three junior researchers completed their master's theses within the project.

projects.title: Hybrid Game Interventions for Mathematical Cognition in Primary Education: A Cross-National Evaluation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: HYBRIMATH investigated whether digital-physical hybrid game interventions produce superior arithmetic and fraction outcomes compared to digital-only and conventional instruction across diverse primary school contexts. The project coordinated data collection in 24 schools in Serbia, developed and validated a battery of mathematics cognition instruments calibrated for grades three through five, and produced open-access intervention materials including teacher facilitation guides. A secondary strand examined log data from tablet sessions to identify behavioural predictors of learning gain. The project produced seven journal articles, two conference papers, and one open dataset. It also supported two doctoral students at the Faculty of Education in Sombor.

projects.title: Bridging Arithmetic and Spatial Reasoning Through Hybrid Educational Games: A Serbia–Hungary Collaboration
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MATHBRIDGE addressed the under-researched connection between spatial reasoning and number sense in children aged eight to eleven through a jointly developed series of hybrid games targeting number line understanding and geometric pattern recognition. Partners in Hungary and Serbia developed parallel interventions adapted to national curricula, enabling direct cross-national comparison. The project trained 48 teachers across both countries in game facilitation and embedded assessment, ran controlled evaluations in 16 schools, and produced a bilingual teacher resource package. Findings informed an updated teacher training module adopted by both partner faculties. The project also established a shared digital repository of game materials accessible to regional educators.

projects.title: Bio-based Barrier Coatings for Fibre Packaging: Performance Under Central European Humidity Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: BIOBAR investigated the performance envelope of bio-derived barrier coatings — primarily PLA dispersions, starch blends, and cellulose nanocrystal composites — on recycled and virgin paperboard grades under humidity and temperature conditions representative of the central European food distribution chain. The project combined laboratory synthesis and characterisation with accelerated and natural ageing trials and a shelf-life modelling component. Six academic and two industrial partners contributed material samples, analytical capacity, and distribution-chain humidity datasets. An open-access dataset of WVTR, OTR, and mechanical degradation curves for twelve bio-based coating formulations on eight substrate grades was released at project conclusion.

projects.title: Cross-Border Competence Platform for Sustainable Paper Packaging
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSPACK established a joint testing and knowledge-transfer platform between Hungarian and Serbian research groups and packaging sector SMEs. The project involved comparative round-robin WVTR measurements across four laboratories to assess inter-laboratory variability, which was found to be up to 18 % for recycled-board substrates. Short training courses for SME technical staff were delivered in Novi Sad and Pécs. A shared equipment-access agreement for the WVTR rigs at the Novi Sad and Budapest sites remained in effect after project close.

projects.title: Изградња и лингвистичка анотација корпуса говора деце на српском за потребе аутоматског препознавања и патологије говора
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)

Поред изградње ресурса, пројекат је обухватао развој базних линија АПГ система и алата за аутоматску детекцију патолошких образаца говора у сарадњи са логопедима. projects.title: Voice-Enabled Educational Tools for Bilingual Primary Schools in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: EduVoice-RS-HU развија прототипове образовних апликација са гласовним интерфејсом намењених ученицима у двојезичним основним школама у прекограничном региону Србија–Мађарска. Задатак новосадске групе обухвата прилагођавање акустичких и језичких модела за двојезичне говорнике српског и мађарског, уз израду смерница за педагошку употребу гласовних технологија. Мађарска страна обезбеђује паралелни рад на препознавању мађарског говора деце. Крајњи корисници су наставници и ученици у 12 основних школа. Пројекат укључује теренска тестирања у школама и итеративно побољшање система на основу повратних информација.

projects.title: Distributed Diagnostics and Monitoring of Power Electronic Converters in Renewable Energy Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DIAMON addressed the challenge of scalable, non-intrusive health monitoring for fleets of grid-connected converters in renewable energy installations. The project developed and validated signal-processing algorithms for on-line estimation of IGBT degradation indicators and DC-link capacitor ESR, implementable within existing converter control loops without additional sensing hardware. A secondary work stream produced a distributed monitoring architecture based on IEC 61850 MMS, allowing aggregation of diagnostic data from up to 16 nodes on a single edge gateway. The algorithms were tested on laboratory hardware and in a 14-day field trial at a 110 kW rooftop photovoltaic installation. The project supported two doctoral students and resulted in four journal publications.

projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project brought together the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the Budapest University of Technology and Economics to develop shared training materials, joint laboratory exercises, and a pilot demonstrator for condition monitoring of small-scale renewable energy converters. Vojnović led the work package on algorithm development and embedded implementation, contributing wavelet-based and RLS-based diagnostics modules. The project also included two staff exchange visits and a joint student workshop held in both Novi Sad and Budapest. projects.title: High-Resolution Solar Resource Mapping for Urban and Peri-Urban Areas of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SolarVoj produced photogrammetric digital surface models and shadow-aware solar irradiance maps for six municipalities in Vojvodina Province. The project combined UAV surveys, Pleiades satellite stereo pairs, and a 15-year climate dataset to generate rooftop solar cadastres at 0.5 m resolution. Outputs were delivered as GIS layers to each municipality's urban planning department. The project also produced a methodology handbook adopted by the Provincial Energy Agency and trained six municipal GIS officers in basic solar resource assessment interpretation. Total covered area was approximately 18 km² of urban fabric.

projects.title: Three-Dimensional Cast-Shadow Modelling for Building-Integrated Renewable Energy Systems in Dense Urban Cores
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: 3DCAST addresses the gap between rooftop and façade solar modelling by developing a unified shadow simulation framework that handles vertical and tilted surfaces simultaneously. The project generates quarterly-updated DSMs from a dedicated UAV monitoring programme covering three test districts in Novi Sad and Subotica, including deciduous street trees. A physics-based anisotropic sky-diffuse model replaces the isotropic approximation used in most cadastre tools. Validation relies on a network of 48 calibrated pyranometers distributed across the test sites. The project includes a dissemination component targeting architects and urban planners through workshops co-organised with the Chamber of Architects of Serbia.

projects.title: Seal Geometry and Material Optimisation for Climate-Resilient Outdoor Enclosures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of quantitative design guidelines for gasket geometry and material selection in outdoor electrical and photovoltaic enclosures subject to the continental climate of the Western Balkans. Activities included an experimental programme measuring vapour permeability and ageing behaviour of six gasket materials, development and validation of a coupled hygrothermal finite-element model, and construction of a parametric design chart relating seal geometry to the condensation-free service life under Vojvodina climate statistics. The project produced three journal publications, one conference contribution, and a freely downloadable design calculation spreadsheet. It also supported two doctoral students and provided experimental data that formed the basis for a subsequent industry collaboration.

projects.title: Low-Cost Wireless Sensor System for Internal Humidity Monitoring in Sealed Industrial Enclosures
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project developed a prototype wireless sensor node small enough to be enclosed permanently inside a standard IP65 cabinet, transmitting temperature and humidity readings via LoRaWAN. Sabo's group led the work package on enclosure climate modelling and sensor placement optimisation, using CFD and hygrothermal simulations to identify locations within the cabinet where the sensor reading is most representative of the condensation-risk state of the enclosure. projects.title: Text Mining for Asset Reliability in Electrical Distribution Grids
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TEXTGRID investigates methods for transforming unstructured maintenance text into inputs suitable for quantitative reliability analysis of distribution grid assets. The project involves five researchers from the University of Novi Sad and one researcher from the University of Belgrade, and has produced an annotated corpus increment of approximately 20,000 sentences and four peer-reviewed publications.

projects.title: Cross-Border Data Frameworks for Predictive Reliability in Energy Infrastructure

projects.title: Residential Storage Sizing Under Heterogeneous Ageing and Demand Uncertainty
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RESHADE addresses the gap between idealised laboratory-based battery degradation models and the irregular operating conditions experienced by residential storage systems in Serbia and the broader Western Balkans region. projects.title: Electromagnetic Compatibility Challenges in Smart Low-Voltage Networks: Measurement Protocols and Mitigation Strategies
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between research groups in Novi Sad and Miskolc addressing the harmonisation of EMC measurement practice and mitigation strategies for low-voltage smart grid infrastructure in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The Faculty of Technical Sciences leads the work package on supraharmonic emission measurement methodology, contributing a jointly operated monitoring station on a 400 V cross-border feeder segment and co-authoring draft measurement guidelines submitted to CENELEC TC210. The project also supports student exchange and co-supervision of two doctoral candidates, one from each partner institution.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Miskolc, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina – Nord

projects.title: Relaxation-Based Decomposition Methods for Distribution Network Optimisation Under Renewable Uncertainty
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RESDOPT investigates decomposition and relaxation methods for the optimal operation of medium- and low-voltage distribution networks with high shares of solar and wind generation. The project develops SOCP-based lower bounds within a branch-and-bound framework, together with warm-start and feasibility-recovery procedures suited to rolling-horizon dispatch cycles of 5 to 15 minutes. Computational experiments use anonymised feeder data from a distribution system operator in Vojvodina. The project funds two Ph.D. students and provides access to the University of Novi Sad HPC cluster. Results are expected to reduce average OPF computation time by a factor of three compared with commercial solver defaults on the target problem class.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Cross-Border Energy Network Optimisation Tools for the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSOPT aims to develop shared computational tools and data exchange protocols for coordinated optimal power flow across the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border transmission corridor. Slađana Paunović leads the work package on optimisation algorithm development, responsible for adapting SOCP relaxation methods to account for cross-border line constraints and different national grid codes. The project includes a pilot demonstration using a synthetic but geographically representative 180-bus cross-border network model. Other work packages cover regulatory harmonisation, communication infrastructure, and operator training. The consortium comprises university partners, a regional transmission system operator, and a technology company from Subotica.
partners: Department of Power Systems, University of Pécs, Hungary
Energolink d.o.o., Subotica
Regional Energy Agency of South Pannonia, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Robust Data Recovery for Cyber-Physical Energy Monitoring Under Communication Disruptions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates theoretical and practical aspects of recovering missing or corrupted measurements in real-time cyber-physical energy monitoring systems. It addresses three interrelated problems: (1) characterisation of real-world gap patterns in distribution-grid SCADA and smart-meter archives, (2) development of hybrid estimators that couple Kalman-filter recursions with learned gap-filling modules, and (3) formulation of a standardised evaluation framework enabling fair comparison of imputation methods. The project funds two PhD students and involves a collaboration with a regional distribution system operator that supplies anonymised historical SCADA data. Results are expected to include open-source software tools and a publicly available benchmark dataset.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektromreža Vojvodine d.o.o. (fictitious distribution operator)
Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana

projects.title: Cross-Border Low-Voltage Grid Monitoring and Anomaly Detection
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMON is a cross-border cooperation project between Serbian and Hungarian partners aimed at deploying pilot low-voltage monitoring nodes in two suburban distribution areas, one in Vojvodina and one in southern Hungary. Zorica Rakić leads the work package on data quality and state estimation, responsible for designing the data-collection protocol, implementing online imputation pipelines for missing sensor readings, and delivering anomaly-detection dashboards used by both operators. The project includes three field sites, hardware procurement, and staff exchange visits. It also funds undergraduate student internships at partner institutions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektromreža Vojvodine d.o.o. (fictitious distribution operator)
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology
Dél-Alföldi Energia Kft. (fictitious Hungarian distribution operator)

projects.title: Measurement and Verification Capacity Building for Energy Performance Contracting in Western Balkan SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between the regulatory framework for energy performance contracting and practical verification capacity in small and medium enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. Activities included development of a training curriculum for M&V practitioners, delivery of four training workshops attended by 112 participants, and creation of an open-access toolbox of regression-based baseline models implemented in R. The project also produced a comparative analysis of EPC dispute cases from both countries, identifying measurement uncertainty disagreements as the most frequent source of conflict. Tóth coordinated the Serbian research team and led the methodological workpackage. Three partner organisations contributed practical case study data under non-disclosure agreements.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Budapest University of Technology
Regional Energy Agency of Vojvodina (REAV)
Hungarian Energy Efficiency Institute (HEEI), Budapest
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Adaptation of IPMVP Protocols to Serbian Industrial Conditions: Statistical Frameworks and Contractual Standardisation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project develops Serbia-specific guidance for applying IPMVP Option C in industrial facilities, where variable production conditions, ageing metering infrastructure, and multi-product manufacturing complicate standard verification approaches. The research programme comprises three components: an empirical study of baseline model performance across 25 facilities; a simulation study of uncertainty propagation under realistic metering conditions in Serbian industry; and a stakeholder consultation process to produce draft national technical guidelines. The project partners include two ESCOs that provide access to anonymised contract data. Outputs include peer-reviewed publications, a national guidelines document submitted to the Serbian Energy Agency, and a PhD thesis in progress.
partners: Serbian Energy Agency (SEA)
Termovolt ESCO d.o.o., Novi Sad
EnergoPartner d.o.o., Belgrade

projects.title: Report-Based Operational Analytics for Regional Infrastructure Portfolios
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REPORA addressed the gap between the large volumes of engineering project reports produced by regional infrastructure agencies and the limited analytical use made of them. The project developed and validated a full pipeline from semi-structured PDF ingestion through field extraction, schema normalisation, and dimensional warehousing, to a configurable KPI dashboard layer. Three partner organisations in Vojvodina served as application sites, providing access to historical report repositories totalling over 2,100 documents. Research outputs included the versioned metadata registry approach to schema drift, the multilingual extraction comparison, and the reference architecture paper. The project also produced an open annotated corpus of 300 engineering report excerpts in Serbian and Hungarian made available to the research community under a CC-BY licence.
partners: Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning, Construction and Environmental Protection of Vojvodina
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
JP Vojvodinašume (fictional analogue – Forestry and Infrastructure Agency Vojvodina)

projects.title: Cross-Border Business Intelligence Capacity Building for SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSBI aimed to raise BI adoption among small and medium enterprises and public bodies on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. Andrea Molnár led the work package on data warehouse design and training, responsible for developing a modular training curriculum covering dimensional modelling, ETL configuration, and dashboard deployment, and for delivering workshops to 14 participating organisations. The project produced translated documentation for the reference architecture in Hungarian and Serbian, and a self-assessment tool allowing organisations to gauge their data readiness before committing to a full BI implementation. Molnár's group contributed technical assistance to four pilot deployments during the project period.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Pannon Business Network Association, Pécs, Hungary
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Bács-Kiskun County, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Bačka, Serbia (fictional)

projects.title: Integrated Demand Management for Industrial Utility Systems with Distributed Renewable Generation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат развија методологију и софтверске алате за интегрисано управљање потрошњом у индустријским помоћним системима који обухватају фотонапонску производњу, компримовани ваздух и расхладна постројења. Централни резултат је оквир за ко-симулацију који повезује постојеће специјализоване алате преко заједничког електричног чвора. Валидација је спроведена на три индустријска локалитета у Vojvodini. Пројекат финансира Фонд за науку Републике Србије у оквиру програма IDEAS, са укупним буџетом од 4,8 милиона динара. Тим чине четири истраживача са Факултета техничких наука и два спољна партнера.
partners: Факултет техничких наука, Универзитет у Новом Саду
Машински факултет, Универзитет у Београду

projects.title: Cross-Border Industrial Utility Efficiency: Measurement, Modelling and Good-Practice Transfer
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Прекогранични пројекат у оквиру Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia програма окупља партнере из Новог Сада и Сегедина са циљем успостављања заједничке методологије за енергетске аудите индустријских помоћних система и преноса добре праксе малим и средњим предузећима у пограничном региону. Радни пакет којим руководи проф. Ковачевић обухвата развој протокола мерења, обуку инжењера и израду упутства за управљање вршним оптерећењем прилагођеног тарифним системима обеју земаља. Планирани исход укључује заједничку базу података о енергетским профилима 80 предузећа и три демонстрациона пројекта.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Szeged, Faculty of Engineering
Regional Energy Agency of Vojvodina (fictional)
South Transdanubia Regional Development Agency (fictional)

projects.title: Shading-Aware Distributed Maximum Power Point Tracking for Complex Urban Rooftops
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the gap between standard PV design assumptions and the actual behaviour of residential and commercial rooftop systems in Serbian urban environments, where irregular roof geometries and inter-building shading cause substantial energy losses that are rarely quantified at the planning stage. The core deliverables are: a validated string-level simulation library calibrated against rooftop measurements in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin; a LiDAR-based shading loss estimation tool for municipal-scale planning; and an embedded MPPT controller prototype capable of global peak search within two seconds on a Cortex-M4 platform. The project involves one PhD student and two final-year M.Sc. students. Partners at the University of Belgrade contribute expertise in power converter design.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
School of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Performance Assessment and Grid Integration Standards for Small-Scale PV in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BALCANPV brought together four institutions from Serbia and Hungary to compile field performance data from 38 small-scale PV installations, develop a shared measurement protocol aligned with IEC 61724-1, and produce a bilingual technical guide for installers and energy auditors. Ivona Trifunović led the work package on partial-shading characterisation, coordinating field measurement campaigns at eight Serbian sites and contributing the string simulation methodology used to interpret yield shortfalls. The project produced a publicly available database of anonymised performance data and an online tool for preliminary shading loss estimation.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Regional Energy Agency of Vojvodina
Bay Zoltán Applied Research Institute, Hungary

projects.title: Diagnostic Analytics for Solar Asset Performance in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project collected and harmonised SCADA telemetry from eleven PV installations totalling approximately 18 MWp across Serbia and one site in North Macedonia. The main research objectives were to develop site-agnostic fault classifiers, validate soiling estimation methods under Pannonian climate conditions, and build an open benchmark dataset for researchers in the region. The project funded two doctoral students, equipment for the HIL testbed, and a series of joint workshops with the partner university. A public data repository was established at the end of the project period containing anonymised telemetry and fault labels from six consenting site operators.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technologies, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje
Institute for Power Systems and Energy, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Predictive Maintenance Frameworks for Distributed Renewable Energy Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MAINTAIN-IPA is a cross-border cooperation project addressing the fragmented and predominantly reactive maintenance practices applied to small and medium renewable energy installations on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. Igor Starčević leads the work package on data integration and machine learning pipeline development, which involves aligning heterogeneous SCADA data from Hungarian and Serbian partners into a common schema and training shared predictive maintenance models. The project includes a pilot deployment at two sites—one wind farm in Bács-Kiskun county and one PV park in the Vojvodina region—with live anomaly alerting integrated into each operator's existing SCADA dashboard.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs
SunField Energy Kft., Kecskemét
Vojvodina Renewables d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Satellite-Based Soiling Load Assessment and Cleaning Optimisation for Ground-Mounted Solar Farms in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SOLSOIL developed an end-to-end processing chain converting Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 imagery into site-specific soiling maps and cleaning trigger recommendations for PV operators in the Pannonian Basin. The project established a network of sediment trap and spectroradiometer reference stations at four Serbian PV plants, built a dust-deposition model driven by WRF-Chem and fused MODIS-SEVIRI AOD inputs, and validated the satellite-derived soiling index against gravimetric and electrical measurements. An operational prototype delivering daily soiling risk maps via a web API was demonstrated to two plant operators. The project produced seven journal articles, one master thesis, and one dataset released under an open licence.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia

projects.title: Remote Sensing of Solar Energy Infrastructure in the Danube Region: Soiling, Shading, and Land-Use Change
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RSOLENVI is a cross-border project addressing satellite-based monitoring challenges common to large-scale PV installations on both sides of the Serbia–Hungary border. Čolić leads the work package on soiling and reflectance analysis, responsible for harmonising the Sentinel-2 processing chain across the two national teams, coordinating joint field campaigns at four sites (two per country), and producing a shared soiling index time series covering 2017–2024. Additional work packages address shading from vegetation encroachment and land-use change around PV plants. The project targets knowledge transfer to regional energy planners and contributes data to the European benchmark dataset initiative. Two early-career researchers at BioSense Institute are supported through the project.
partners: Balaton Regional Energy Agency, Pécs
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Prosumer-Ready Low-Voltage Grid Planning Tools for Vojvodina Distribution Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a suite of open-source planning tools for distribution system operators in Serbia to assess and manage the integration of prosumers into existing 0.4 kV infrastructure. Work included development of the stochastic hosting capacity framework, a feeder classification methodology, and an interface for visualising results at municipal scale. Field data were collected from two pilot distribution areas in the Vojvodina region in collaboration with the regional distribution system operator. The project produced four journal papers, one conference paper, and a publicly available software repository. Two master thesis students completed their work within the project activities.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektrovojvodina d.o.o. Novi Sad (regional distribution system operator)

projects.title: Cross-Border Approaches to Distributed Generation Integration in Hungarian–Serbian Low-Voltage Networks
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project compares regulatory frameworks and technical approaches to photovoltaic and small wind integration in Hungarian and Serbian low-voltage distribution networks. The University of Novi Sad leads the technical work package covering hosting capacity assessment and reactive power management, while the Hungarian partner leads the regulatory and market analysis work package. Joint field measurement campaigns were conducted on selected feeders on both sides of the border during 2023. A shared database of feeder topologies and measurement data is being established. The project also includes a training programme for distribution system operator engineers in both countries, with two workshops completed as of early 2025.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Széchenyi István University, Győr
Elektrovojvodina d.o.o. Novi Sad
DÉMÁSZ Hálózati Kft. (fictional Hungarian DSO)

projects.title: Carbon Accounting Standards and Monitoring Protocols for Electricity Distribution Networks in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed standardised carbon accounting protocols adapted to the regulatory and data conditions of Western Balkan electricity distribution utilities, with pilot implementation at two Serbian regional distribution companies. Key outputs included a sector-specific GHG inventory template aligned with ISO 14064-1 and GHG Protocol, a measurement protocol for SF6 leakage combining infrared survey and mass-balance methods, and a loss-disaggregation tool that attributes technical and non-technical losses to consumer categories using smart-meter data. The project trained twelve utility staff in GHG inventory preparation and delivered a public guidance document adopted as a reference by the Serbian Chamber of Engineers. Budget approximately 45 000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektrodistribucija Vojvodina d.o.o. (fictional utility)
Institute for Environmental Research Novi Sad (fictional)

projects.title: Life-Cycle Environmental Assessment of Transformer Fleet Modernisation Pathways in South-East European Distribution Grids
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANSPATH is a joint Serbian–Romanian project examining the environmental and economic trade-offs of transformer fleet renewal strategies in two regional distribution utilities, one in Vojvodina and one in Banat, Romania. The Serbian team, led by Bačić, is responsible for the life-cycle assessment work package, including primary data collection from transformer manufacturers and repair workshops, development of a shared LCA database for electrical steels and insulating oils, and scenario modelling for fleet-level cumulative emissions to 2040. The Romanian partner leads economic modelling and regulatory analysis. Total project budget is 890 000 EUR, with the University of Novi Sad receiving approximately 310 000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University Timișoara, Romania

Elektrodistribucija Vojvodina d.o.o. (fictional utility)

projects.title: Subsurface Utility Mapping for Safe Urban Excavation in Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SUBMAP addressed the lack of harmonised subsurface utility mapping practice across the Hungary–Serbia border region, where cross-border infrastructure projects regularly encounter undocumented buried assets. The project developed joint field survey protocols combining GPR and EMI detection, a shared GIS data model aligned with both Hungarian and Serbian national standards, and a training programme for municipal geodetic services. Jeremić led the work package responsible for Serbian pilot surveys covering 62 km of streets in Subotica and Kanjiža, producing quality-level-attributed cadastre outputs. The project trained 34 municipal surveyors and produced a bilingual Hungarian–Serbian field manual for subsurface utility detection, freely distributed to partner municipalities.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Municipality of Subotica
Municipality of Kanjiža

projects.title: Geodetic Methods for Reconstruction Planning of Ageing Underground Distribution Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GEOMREKON investigates whether a combination of GPR surveys, precision GNSS and aerial photogrammetry can generate sufficiently accurate underground asset inventories to support cost estimation and route planning for distribution network reconstruction projects, replacing expensive manual test-hole programmes. The project tests three urban and two peri-urban study areas in the South Bačka and Srem districts. Deliverables include a decision-support GIS tool that flags cable and pipe segments exceeding age or condition thresholds based on as-surveyed depth, material classification and available failure records. The project involves doctoral supervision of two PhD candidates and collaboration with a regional electricity distribution operator providing access to maintenance records and operational data.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade
Infravoltaj d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Kinetics and Catalyst Design for Manganese and Trace Metal Removal from Vojvodina Groundwater
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between laboratory-derived rate constants for Mn(II) oxidation and actual filter performance at Vojvodina waterworks, where high carbonate alkalinity, intermittent operation, and variable Fe/Mn ratios frequently cause non-compliant effluent. Work packages covered (i) fundamental kinetic characterisation of MnOx coatings on natural zeolite and quartz carriers, (ii) pilot-column testing at two municipal waterworks, and (iii) development of a design tool integrating mass-transfer and surface-reaction sub-models. The project supported two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. A simplified calculation spreadsheet for filter sizing was delivered to the two waterworks partners as a practical outcome.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Waterworks and Sewerage Public Utility Sombor
Waterworks Sremska Mitrovica

projects.title: Affordable Packed-Bed Aeration and Filtration Technologies for Small Rural Water Systems in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AQUAPAKT brought together chemical engineers, civil engineers, and public health authorities from Novi Sad, Subotica, and Pécs to design, build, and evaluate low-cost aeration–filtration units suitable for settlements supplying fewer than 2 000 inhabitants from groundwater with elevated Fe, Mn, or As. Todorović led the work package on reactor design and media selection, coordinating bench-scale testing of three candidate media configurations before field installation of modular units at two pilot villages. Performance monitoring over 18 months showed consistent compliance with Serbian and Hungarian drinking-water standards for Fe and Mn. The project produced design guidelines adapted to local material availability and operator skill levels.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, Subotica
Department of Water Supply Engineering, University of Pécs
Provincial Institute of Public Health Novi Sad

projects.title: Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion in Drinking Water Distribution Networks: Mechanisms, Monitoring, and Mitigation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the mechanisms by which SRB biofilms accelerate passive film breakdown on austenitic stainless steels in potable water distribution conditions representative of Serbian municipal networks. Laboratory work combined electrochemical noise monitoring, XPS surface analysis, and culture-based microbiology. Field campaigns at two municipal networks in Vojvodina collected in-situ coupon data across four seasons. The project produced a stochastic pitting model calibrated to local water chemistry ranges and a monitoring protocol for municipal water managers. Three M.Sc. students and one Ph.D. student were trained within the project. Results have been published in four peer-reviewed journal articles and presented at two international conferences.
partners: Department of Microbiology, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Public Utility Company Vodovod Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade

projects.title: Corrosion Monitoring Technologies for Water Infrastructure in Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between Serbian and Hungarian partners aiming to harmonise corrosion monitoring practices in drinking water infrastructure. The Novi Sad team was responsible for the work package on electrochemical monitoring sensor validation, which involved calibrating commercial corrosion probes against laboratory EIS and LPR measurements in controlled water chemistry conditions. The project also included joint training workshops for utility engineers and produced a bilingual technical guideline document for corrosion inspection in stainless steel water installations. Pavlović led the laboratory validation activities and co-organised two cross-border workshops held in Novi Sad and Subotica.
partners: Department of Water Technology, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Regional Water Authority of Southern Transdanubia, Pécs
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Optimisation of Infrastructure Maintenance Logistics in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the planning and coordination of road and utility maintenance fleets operating across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Đorđe Nikolić led the work package on routing algorithm development, responsible for adapting multi-depot VRP solvers to cross-border regulatory differences in working-time rules and vehicle weight limits. The project produced a shared optimisation toolkit deployed by two regional road authorities and a pilot dataset of cross-border maintenance corridors. Partners from Hungary contributed traffic count data and depot location analysis. The Serbian side provided historical maintenance logs and crew scheduling records. Total budget allocated to the University of Novi Sad component was approximately €180,000.
partners: Regional Road Directorate of South Transdanubia (Hungary) – fictional
Public Enterprise Roads of Vojvodina (Serbia) – fictional

projects.title: Robust Optimisation Models for Maintenance Fleet Scheduling Under Operational Uncertainty
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: OPTMAIN developed robust and stochastic optimisation frameworks for maintenance fleet scheduling where task arrival times, service durations, and road travel times are subject to uncertainty. The project combined scenario-based robust optimisation with data-driven uncertainty set construction using historical maintenance records. A rolling-horizon decision support prototype was built and tested in a simulation environment. The project supported two doctoral students and produced six journal publications. Collaboration with the University of Žilina extended the models to railway track inspection scheduling. The Science Fund grant covered personnel, computing infrastructure, and two international research visits.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Žilina, Department of Transport Networks (Slovakia)

projects.title: Real-Time Hyperspectral Classification Architecture for High-Purity Polymer Recovery
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: POLYSPEC addressed the gap between laboratory NIR classifier performance and field deployment by developing a full hardware-software stack for real-time polymer sorting at belt speeds above 2 m/s. The project built a pilot conveyor line at the Faculty of Technical Sciences with two NIR line-scan cameras, embedded GPU processing, and pneumatic ejectors. Research activities covered spectral library construction for 12 polymer types including black-pigmented grades, drift compensation algorithms, and a benchmarking protocol for industrial noise conditions. The project produced an open spectral dataset of 95 000 annotated spectra and trained two doctoral students. Results were validated in cooperation with a regional municipal waste operator.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia, Novi Sad
JP Čistoća Novi Sad (municipal waste operator)

projects.title: Sensor Fusion Strategies for Circular Economy Packaging Recovery Across the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CIRCPACK is a cross-border cooperation project examining complementary sensor technologies — NIR hyperspectral, Raman, and X-ray fluorescence — for high-purity recovery of post-consumer packaging from joint Hungarian-Serbian waste streams. Krstić leads the work package on NIR sensor integration and real-time classification, coordinating with Hungarian partners on dataset harmonisation and shared spectral libraries. The project has installed a joint pilot sorting line at the Óbuda University campus and a corresponding test facility in Novi Sad. Deliverables include a comparative evaluation report on sensor fusion architectures, three peer-reviewed papers, and a training curriculum for sorting facility operators delivered in both countries.
partners: Óbuda University, Budapest, Hungary
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Hajdú-Bihar County Waste Management Company, Debrecen, Hungary
