projects.title: Alluvial Aquifer Protection from Waste Facility Leachate in the Pannonian Lowland: Monitoring Networks, Transport Models, and Passive Containment Design
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the inadequate protection of shallow alluvial aquifers in Vojvodina from leachate originating at municipal solid waste landfills and transfer stations. Research activities include installation of a dense piezometer network at four representative sites, quarterly sampling and physico-chemical analysis, construction and calibration of coupled unsaturated-saturated transport models, and development of region-specific passive containment design guidelines. A secondary objective is the compilation of a geodatabase of waste-facility hydrogeological site investigations in the province to support regulatory decision-making by the Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning and Environmental Protection. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Institute for Water Management, Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning and Environmental Protection, Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment and Rehabilitation of Leachate Drainage Infrastructure at Legacy Landfills in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project inventoried 17 legacy municipal landfills within 30 km of the Hungary–Serbia border, assessing the condition of existing leachate collection and drainage infrastructure, groundwater contamination status, and closure compliance. The Serbian team led the work package on groundwater monitoring and transport modelling. Four sites received remedial drainage improvements co-financed through the project. The team developed a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) technical manual for passive leachate interceptor drain design in alluvial settings, distributed to municipal authorities and environmental inspectorates on both sides of the border. Two master thesis projects and one journal publication resulted from this work.
partners: Dél-Alföldi Vízügyi Igazgatóság (South-Alföld Water Directorate), Szeged
Institute for Water Management, Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged

projects.title: Optimisation of Biochar Production from Vojvodina Agricultural Residues for Soil Amendment and Carbon Sequestration
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project systematically mapped the pyrolysis parameter space—temperature, residence time, and feedstock type—for the three dominant agricultural residues of Vojvodina: sunflower husks, wheat straw, and corn stover. Over 200 biochar samples were produced and fully characterised against European Biochar Certificate criteria. A decision-support matrix was developed to guide producers in selecting process conditions based on intended agronomic use (soil amendment versus carbon sequestration credit). Field verification was conducted through a two-season pot experiment in collaboration with the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops. Results fed directly into four journal publications and one conference paper.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agrokompleks Vojvodine d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Linking Thermochemical Conversion Kinetics to Biochar Functional Properties Across European Lignocellulosic Feedstocks
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: PYROLINK is a four-country consortium addressing the lack of harmonised kinetic and characterisation datasets for biochar produced from diverse European feedstocks. The University of Novi Sad leads the work package on kinetics and structural characterisation, contributing TGA modelling, Py-GC/MS analysis, and Raman spectroscopic assessment. Partners cover feedstocks from Italy, Germany, Hungary, and Serbia. The project aims to produce an open-access kinetic parameter database and validate a rapid Raman-based certification screening protocol against established incubation methods. The Novi Sad team contributes approximately 0.8 FTE per year, including one PhD student funded through the project.
partners: University of Bologna, Italy
Leibniz Institute for Agricultural Engineering, Potsdam, Germany
University of Debrecen, Hungary
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Condition-Based Maintenance Protocols for Small-Scale Biomass Densification Facilities in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the widespread absence of structured maintenance practice in small- and medium-scale biomass pellet and briquette facilities operating across the Vojvodina–Southern Hungary border region. Partners inventoried 34 facilities, documented failure histories, and collected feedstock quality records over 18 months. The Novi Sad team developed condition monitoring protocols calibrated to the variable feedstock profiles of the region; the Miskolc team contributed failure database infrastructure. A set of maintenance planning tools—including a moisture-adjusted bearing replacement nomogram and a simplified RBD-based availability calculator—was packaged into a freely distributable spreadsheet toolkit distributed to cooperatives and processing companies in the cross-border region.
partners: University of Miskolc, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Hungary
Agricultural Cooperative Zlatna Njiva, Subotica, Serbia
Regional Energy Agency of Southern Transdanubia, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Reliability-Centred Operation of Biomass Densification Systems under Variable Feedstock Quality
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RELIODENSE addresses the gap between laboratory degradation models and field-deployable maintenance decision tools for biomass densification equipment. The project integrates on-line NIR feedstock sensing, low-cost MEMS vibration loggers, and Bayesian degradation models into a prototype decision support system tested at two commercial pellet facilities in Vojvodina. Research tasks include calibration of NIR regression models for mixed agricultural residues, development of the particle-filtering RUL estimator, discrete-event simulation of full production lines, and a field validation campaign. The project supports one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher. The primary output is a validated software prototype and an open dataset of bearing vibration and feedstock quality records from the two field sites.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad
Bioenergo d.o.o., Vrbas, Serbia

projects.title: Mechanisms and Control of Biogenic Hydrogen Sulphide in Ion Exchange Water Treatment Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the biological and chemical mechanisms by which sulphate-reducing bacteria generate hydrogen sulphide in sulphonate cation exchange resins under intermittent service conditions. Key activities included stable isotope tracing of sulphonate group degradation, transcriptomic profiling of colonising SRB strains, and development of a quantitative risk-scoring tool for water utilities. Field validation was conducted at two municipal water-treatment plants in Vojvodina. The project produced eight peer-reviewed publications, one doctoral thesis, and a freely accessible spreadsheet model for predicting H2S accumulation in exchange columns. Collaboration with the Provincial Institute of Public Health Novi Sad provided epidemiologically relevant field data.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Institute of Public Health Novi Sad
BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Biofilm Ecology and Management in Ion Exchange Systems for the Food and Beverage Sector
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research project with a regional manufacturer of ion exchange equipment for the food and beverage industry. The project evaluated the effectiveness of five sanitisation protocols—including peracetic acid, hydrogen peroxide, ozone and two proprietary formulations—in eliminating SRB biofilms from sulphonate resins used in process water preparation. Testing was carried out on both pilot-scale columns at the university and on-site at the client's facility. Deliverables included a confidential technical report, a standard operating procedure for resin sanitisation, and an anonymised dataset retained by the university for future academic publication. The client has an option to co-file a patent on one of the proprietary protocols.
partners: AquaTech Systems d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Matrix Interference Mapping and Correction for Portable Water Quality Analysis in Vojvodina Aquifer Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project systematically characterised the chemical matrix variability of shallow and intermediate-depth aquifers across Vojvodina, with an emphasis on parameters that affect portable colorimetric and photometric measurements: alkalinity, hardness, ionic strength, dissolved organic carbon, and redox-sensitive speciation. A dataset of 350 groundwater samples from 70 monitoring locations was assembled over three field campaigns. Based on the dataset, analyte-specific interference correction models were developed for iron, manganese, phosphate, ammonium, and nitrite. The models were implemented in a freely downloadable spreadsheet calculator and in a printed field reference card distributed to water utility technicians in three municipalities. The project involved collaboration with two Vojvodina water utilities and the Jaroslav Černi Institute in Belgrade.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Jaroslav Černi Institute for the Development of Water Resources, Belgrade

projects.title: Danube Region Aquifer Quality Assessment Using Harmonised Portable Analytical Protocols
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project aimed at harmonising field measurement practices for groundwater quality monitoring in the shared alluvial aquifer system of the Danube corridor between Serbia and Romania. The project produced a joint sampling and field analysis protocol document adopted by partner water authorities in both countries. Radulović led the work package on matrix interference assessment, contributing the iron, manganese, and phosphate correction procedures developed in his laboratory. Approximately 200 cross-border samples were analysed in parallel by partner laboratories using portable and fixed instruments; proficiency testing results and round-robin exercises were coordinated between the two institutions. Training workshops for municipal water authority staff were held in Novi Sad and Timișoara.

projects.title: Impedance-Based Non-Invasive Diagnostics for Lithium-Ion Cells in Second-Life Energy Storage Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated EIS-based protocols for assessing the state of health of lithium-ion cells at partial states of charge, targeting cells destined for second-life use in stationary storage. Activities included construction of a 16-channel parallel impedance measurement fixture, acquisition of 180 aged cells from three chemistry types, and development of regression and machine-learning models for capacity prediction from sub-20-minute measurement protocols. The project produced four journal articles, one conference contribution, and an open dataset of impedance spectra made available through the University of Novi Sad repository. Two master's theses were defended under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Self-Diagnosing Sensor Networks for Autonomous Precision Agriculture in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project deployed and evaluated a cross-border agricultural sensor network spanning eight farm sites in Hungary and Serbia. Žarko Jakovljević led the work package responsible for node-level fault detection firmware and gateway-side data quality validation. The work package produced a reference firmware architecture supporting three diagnostic modules (drift detection, connectivity health scoring, and battery state estimation) and a validation protocol used to certify sensor data before ingestion into partner farm management systems. Field trials covered approximately 1,100 hectares of maize, sunflower, and wheat. The project produced two open datasets published through the Pannonian Environmental Data Repository and contributed results to two of the journal publications listed in this profile.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, University of Pécs, Hungary
Provincial Institute for Agriculture Novi Sad
AgroData Solutions Kft., Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Distributed In-situ Data Quality Assurance for Low-Power Environmental Monitoring Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DIAQUAL addresses the absence of standardised data quality assurance methods for resource-constrained IoT nodes used in environmental monitoring. The project is developing a layered diagnostic framework in which lightweight statistical tests execute at node level, aggregation logic runs at gateway level, and a calibration traceability module operates at the cloud backend. The framework targets NB-IoT and LTE-M deployments and is being validated on soil, water-level, and air-quality sensor networks operated by project partners. The project employs two research assistants based at BioSense Institute and includes a measurement campaign at ten instrumented sites across the Fruška Gora protected area. A hardware reference design and open-source firmware library are planned deliverables.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Disassembly Line Analysis and Redesign for Circular Economy Facilities in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DISLAN addressed the practical challenge that most end-of-life processing facilities in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region operate without formal work measurement or ergonomic standards, leading to both productivity losses and occupational health risks. The project conducted on-site assessments at six facilities—three in Vojvodina and three in southern Hungary—covering electronics, appliances, and power tools. Stefan Ivanović led the work package responsible for time study data collection, MTM-UAS coding, and ergonomic risk assessment. Outputs included a set of sector-specific workstation design guidelines, a simplified cycle-time estimation spreadsheet tool, and two training workshops delivered to facility supervisors. The project also produced a comparative report on regulatory frameworks for ergonomics in end-of-life facilities in Serbia and Hungary.
partners: Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs
Regional Development Agency Subotica
EkoLogik d.o.o., Novi Sad
Zöld Kör Recycling Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Real-Time Line Balancing Support for Flexible Disassembly Operations
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REBALANCE investigates whether lightweight sensor data—specifically cycle-time logging via RFID bin tags and operator-worn wrist accelerometers—can be used to trigger dynamic rebalancing of a disassembly line when the incoming product mix shifts unexpectedly. Stefan Ivanović contributes the work measurement and ergonomic assessment components, providing empirically grounded task time distributions and ergonomic constraint data that feed the rebalancing algorithm developed by colleagues in operations research. The project is coordinated from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, and involves a pilot deployment at a partner facility in Zrenjanin processing end-of-life IT equipment. A secondary objective is to assess whether dynamically rebalanced workloads reduce peak ergonomic risk scores compared to statically balanced lines.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
TehnoReciklaža d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Iron and Manganese Speciation Dynamics in Vojvodina Groundwater: Treatment and Risk Assessment
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project characterised the speciation and seasonal variability of dissolved iron and manganese in twelve representative groundwater sources across Vojvodina and correlated speciation data with the performance of existing waterworks using oxidation–filtration technology. Field sampling campaigns were conducted quarterly over three years. Laboratory kinetic studies provided rate parameters for Fe(II) oxidation and Mn(II) catalytic oxidation as functions of pH, alkalinity, and organic matter content specific to Vojvodina aquifer chemistries. Outcomes included a database of speciation measurements and a decision-support spreadsheet tool for treatment plant operators to estimate required aeration and coagulant doses. Two journal papers and one conference contribution resulted from the project.
partners: Public Water Management Company 'Vode Vojvodine', Novi Sad
Institute for Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Transition Metal Speciation and Removal in Cross-Border Watercourses: Tisa and Danube Sub-Basins
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed the speciation, transport, and removal of iron, manganese, copper, and chromium in shared watercourses. The Serbian team led by Prof. Žigić was responsible for the analytical work package, coordinating field sampling and laboratory speciation analysis at Serbian monitoring stations while partner laboratories in Hungary performed parallel measurements under identical protocols. Joint calibration exercises ensured inter-laboratory comparability; z-scores were within ±2 for all analytes. The project produced a harmonised sampling and analysis protocol for metal speciation in cross-border surface waters and a joint report submitted to the International Sava River Basin Commission. Serbian co-financing was provided by the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research.
partners: Department of Environmental Engineering, Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Directorate for Water Management of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Research Institute for Water Management, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Simulation and Optimisation of Compact Industrial Water Reuse Circuits in the Food and Beverage Sector
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to develop and validate a modular steady-state and dynamic simulation toolkit for compact water reuse circuits in food and beverage manufacturing. The work covers instrument data reconciliation for existing plants, calibration of unit-operation models using plant data from five partner facilities in Vojvodina, and application of multi-objective mass-balance optimisation to identify feasible operating envelopes. A secondary objective is to produce a sizing methodology for membrane polishing steps within reuse circuits that can be used by plant engineers without specialist simulation expertise. Validation is performed against six-month logging data from each partner facility. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Water Resources Management, Novi Sad
Vojvodina Food Processors Association (Novi Sad)

projects.title: Transboundary Groundwater Quality Modelling and Treatment Process Assessment in the Upper Tisa Sub-basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The TRANS-WATER project addressed nitrate and hardness management in shared groundwater bodies straddling the Hungarian–Serbian border. Hriešik led the work package on treatment process assessment, applying ion-exchange and softening simulation models to evaluate treatment options at eight community waterworks on both sides of the border. The work package delivered a comparative cost–performance analysis of five treatment configurations and a guidance document for local water utilities. The University of Novi Sad team was responsible for data collection at four Serbian sites and for the mass-balance optimisation component of the assessment. The project ran for 36 months and involved field campaigns in two hydrological years.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Microbial Risk Indicators in Drinking Water Distribution Networks of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project characterised microbial communities and opportunistic pathogen occurrence in drinking water distribution networks across six municipalities in Vojvodina, combining culture-based enumeration, flow cytometry, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. Field sampling was conducted in collaboration with three public utility companies and one public health institute. Data from approximately 400 water and biofilm samples were used to develop a risk scoring matrix relating physicochemical parameters, hydraulic residence times, and microbial indicators to network-specific risk levels. The project produced a publicly available dataset and a guidance document for utility operators. Two MSc students completed their theses within the project.
partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad
JKP Vodovod i Kanalizacija Novi Sad

projects.title: Non-Biocidal Approaches to Biofilm Control in Industrial Recirculating Cooling Water Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: COOLCLEAN investigates alternatives to conventional biocide treatment for controlling biofilm in industrial cooling water circuits, focusing on plant-derived quorum sensing inhibitors and physical surface modification strategies. The project combines laboratory flow-cell biofilm assays, pipe-loop simulations, and a pilot-scale trial at an industrial partner's cooling tower in the Novi Sad industrial zone. Molecular community profiling (metagenomics and amplicon sequencing) is used to track how tested treatments reshape community composition over time. The project aims to produce a comparative efficacy dataset for at least eight candidate inhibitory compounds tested under conditions representative of regional industrial water chemistry. One industrial PhD candidate is enrolled within the project.
partners: Department of Chemistry, Biochemistry and Environmental Protection, University of Novi Sad
NTP Novi Sad tenant company Aquaflex d.o.o.

projects.title: Low-Power Wide-Area Connectivity for Smart Greenhouse Monitoring in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGRILINK develops and validates a LoRaWAN-based sensor network architecture for monitoring temperature, humidity, CO₂, and soil moisture in greenhouse clusters across northern Serbia and southern Hungary. The University of Novi Sad component is responsible for radio propagation characterisation of greenhouse structures, network planning methodology, and gateway placement optimisation. Tihomir Urošević leads the work package on propagation modelling and link-budget validation, coordinating measurement campaigns at partner greenhouse sites. The project also produces an open-access planning guide for small agricultural producers considering IoT adoption, and delivers a pilot deployment covering approximately 3 hectares of greenhouse area near Subotica.

projects.title: Propagation-Aware Indoor Localisation for Industrial IoT Asset Tracking
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: INDORLOC investigated the relationship between multipath propagation structure and the accuracy of fingerprint-based and geometry-based localisation algorithms in industrial halls. The project combined channel sounding campaigns in three factory environments near Novi Sad with ray-launching simulations calibrated to measured data. Tihomir Urošević contributed antenna design for the measurement platform and conducted the 868 MHz wideband measurement campaigns. The project produced a calibrated propagation dataset made publicly available, and demonstrated that localisation error below 2 m is achievable with a four-gateway LoRa infrastructure when gateway positions are chosen to minimise delay-spread variance across the coverage area.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Mihajlo Pupin Institute, Belgrade (fictional division)

projects.title: Real-Time Software Infrastructure for Heterogeneous System-on-Chip Platforms in Industrial Automation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how RTOS kernels and their porting layers must be adapted when deployed on the real-time subsystem of a heterogeneous SoC that also hosts a Linux application core. Work packages cover context-switch primitives for each target ISA, inter-processor communication drivers, and automated timing regression tests integrated into CI pipelines. A secondary goal is producing open toolchain configuration templates that industrial users can apply without deep knowledge of linker scripts or GCC internals. Partners contribute evaluation hardware and case studies from factory automation and motion-control domains. The project funds one PhD student and supports short-term research visits to partner institutions.
partners: Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, University of Zagreb
Industrijska Automatika d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Toolchain-Aware Validation Methods for Safety-Critical Embedded Firmware
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: EMBIVAL addresses the problem that firmware validation results obtained with one compiler version may not transfer to another version, which complicates certification workflows. The project develops a lightweight regression harness that automatically re-runs a defined set of timing, stack, and binary-size checks whenever the toolchain is updated. The harness targets Cortex-M and RISC-V boards available in the laboratory. A database of known GCC version-to-version behavioural differences is being compiled from publicly available bug trackers and from experiments conducted within the project. Expected outputs include the harness software, the database, and a practitioner guide.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
NTP Novi Sad Embedded Cluster (informal association of tenant companies)

projects.title: High-Efficiency Power Conversion Chains for Controlled-Environment Horticultural LED Lighting
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigates the full power conversion chain from the AC mains to the LED junction in controlled-environment agricultural lighting installations, with particular focus on PFC stage efficiency at partial load and harmonic compliance over wide dimming ranges. The project combines circuit design, electromagnetic simulation, hardware prototyping, and field measurement at a partner greenhouse facility in Vojvodina. Deliverables include validated circuit topologies, a design methodology for BCM and CCM PFC stages, and a set of power quality measurement data from operating horticultural installations. The project supports two Ph.D. students and includes collaboration with researchers at the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Vegetable Crops Smederevska Palanka
Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology

projects.title: Power Quality and Harmonic Distortion Assessment in Low-Voltage Distribution Networks of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A regional measurement and modelling project that deployed calibrated power quality instruments at forty low-voltage distribution panels across urban and rural sites in Vojvodina over a twelve-month monitoring period. Puzović led the work package responsible for harmonic source identification and aggregation modelling. The project produced a publicly available anonymised dataset of harmonic measurements and a statistical aggregation model for mixed residential and commercial loads. Findings informed a technical recommendation submitted to the relevant distribution system operator regarding harmonic emission limits for new LED street-lighting installations.

projects.title: Spectral Determinants of Photomorphogenetic Responses in Crops Grown Under Artificial Light
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated how spectral composition of artificial light sources, independently of total photon flux, governs key developmental and metabolic outcomes in three crop species: lettuce, basil, and tomato. Experimental work combined controlled-spectrum LED growth cabinets with spectroradiometric characterisation, physiological phenotyping, and targeted metabolite profiling. A parallel modelling strand extended the team's existing ODE-based phytochrome model to include blue-light signalling through cryptochromes and generated species-specific parameter sets. The project trained two PhD students and produced open datasets deposited at the national open research data infrastructure. Findings were communicated to practitioners through a short-course workshop co-organised with the Faculty of Agriculture in Novi Sad.

projects.title: Energy-Efficient Light Environments for Urban and Peri-Urban Food Production in the Adriatic–Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ADRIALIGHT is a cross-border cooperation project bringing together plant scientists, engineers, and small urban farming enterprises to develop energy-use guidelines for LED-lit indoor food production. Tamara Kecman leads the work package on photobiological specification of light recipes, translating photoreceptor-based models into simplified decision tools usable by farmers without a research background. The work package produces a web-accessible calculator for recommended spectral parameters given a target crop and growth stage. A pilot installation at a partner site in Subotica serves as a validation testbed. The project runs alongside technology transfer activities co-ordinated by the Hungarian partner.

projects.title: Resource-Constrained Scheduling Algorithms for Low-Power Embedded Control Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RESCALE investigates schedulability analysis and task allocation algorithms for embedded distributed control systems operating under strict memory and energy constraints. The project targets microcontroller-class nodes (ARM Cortex-M and AVR families) interconnected by CAN and FlexRay buses. Research activities include derivation of tighter analytical bounds, development of constraint-programming and ILP formulations, and construction of a public benchmark suite. A secondary objective is validating theoretical results on physical prototype hardware using STM32 and NXP development boards. The project funds two PhD students and supports collaboration with partner universities in the Czech Republic and Sweden.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Distributed Real-Time Control Platforms for Industrial Automation in Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DISTRIB-RT aimed to develop and validate modular distributed control platforms suitable for small and medium manufacturing enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. Tešić led the work package on scheduling and resource management, which produced the simulated-annealing task-mapping method and the FlexRay message scheduling formulation. The project involved laboratory demonstrations at both partner sites and two short industrial feasibility studies with a conveyor-system integrator and an irrigation-equipment manufacturer. Hardware prototypes used NXP Kinetis MCUs and custom carrier boards developed by the Hungarian partner.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

Institute for Applied Computer Science, University of Pécs

projects.title: Sealing Performance of Outdoor Electromechanical Enclosures under Pannonian Climate Conditions
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project set up a networked outdoor test rack with 24 instrumented enclosures across three sites in Vojvodina to collect simultaneous internal humidity, temperature, and condensation-event data over 30 months. Gasket specimens from each enclosure were retrieved at 10-month intervals for laboratory characterisation. The data collected formed the basis for the regression model relating enclosure configuration and gland fill ratio to condensation frequency, and provided field-correlation reference points for the accelerated ageing protocol developed subsequently. Two M.Sc. theses and one Ph.D. thesis were completed within the project scope.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektrovojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Modelling Moisture Transport and Condensation Risk in Sealed Enclosures for Low-Voltage Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MOISTMOD targets the development of validated computational models for predicting moisture accumulation and condensation onset in sealed outdoor enclosures used in low-voltage electrical distribution infrastructure. The project combines laboratory climate-chamber experiments with two-dimensional coupled heat-moisture FEM simulations. A parametric study covering five enclosure sizes, three gasket materials, and four regional climate profiles is being conducted. An open-access Python-based tool for condensation-onset prediction is under development. The project involves collaboration with a meteorological data provider and an enclosure manufacturer. One postdoctoral researcher and two doctoral students are supported under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia, Belgrade
Termoplast Enclosures d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Solar Resource Characterisation and Storage Sizing Methodology for Remote Low-Power Installations in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate an integrated methodology for simultaneously characterising the solar irradiance resource and sizing battery storage for small stand-alone PV systems operating in the Pannonian Plain climate. Work included establishment of a five-station pyranometer network in Vojvodina, development of a harmonised LOLP-based sizing procedure accounting for battery degradation, and production of bias-corrected gridded irradiance datasets for the region. The project delivered a publicly accessible sizing web tool and published six peer-reviewed papers. A workshop for engineering practitioners was held in Novi Sad in 2023 with participants from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. The project had a total budget of approximately 56 000 EUR.

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Off-Grid PV Power Supply for Small Agricultural Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between research institutions and agricultural extension services in Vojvodina and the Southern Great Plain region of Hungary. The Novi Sad team led the work package on energy resource assessment and system sizing methodology, providing harmonised design guidelines applicable across both national contexts. Field demonstrations were installed at two agricultural sites, one in Serbia and one in Hungary, each comprising a 500 Wp PV array with LFP battery storage powering irrigation control and environmental monitoring equipment. Monitoring data from both sites were pooled for comparative analysis. The project produced bilingual technical guidelines disseminated through agricultural advisory networks.
