projects.title: Sensor Data Fusion for Field-Scale Agrometeorological Services in the Pannonian Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGROFUSE established a shared sensor infrastructure spanning 180 km² of agricultural land across the Hungary–Serbia border region, deployed and maintained by teams at BioSense Institute and the University of Szeged. Gajić led the data fusion work package, which developed and validated the Bayesian updating scheme for combining IoT sensor observations with ALADIN NWP output. The project delivered real-time agrometeorological maps to pilot farms and a regional advisory service. Outcomes included validated data fusion software released under an open licence, a cross-border calibration protocol for low-cost sensors, and training workshops for extension officers in both countries. The project involved four partner institutions and approximately 180 sensor nodes.
partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Science and Informatics, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Vojvodina
Agricultural Extension Service Subotica

projects.title: High-Resolution Thermal Mapping for Frost Risk Advisory in Vojvodina Horticulture
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TERMOPLJE addresses the need for sub-field frost risk estimates in vegetable and fruit production in Vojvodina, where frost events in April and October cause significant annual losses. The project combines a 45-node wireless sensor network with statistical downscaling methods and calibrated ensemble NWP output to produce 100-metre resolution probabilistic frost forecasts with a 48-hour horizon. A mobile app delivers advisory outputs to registered farms. The project also investigates the contribution of surface soil moisture heterogeneity to nocturnal cold pool formation in flat terrain. Three academic partners and one commercial horticulture cooperative are involved. Gajić is principal investigator and manages a team of two PhD students and one technician at BioSense.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Agroprodukt Vojvodina d.o.o. (horticulture cooperative)

projects.title: Pre-Compliance EMI Methodology for High-Speed Mixed-Signal Electronics in Industrial and Automotive Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a structured pre-compliance methodology for predicting radiated and conducted electromagnetic emissions from mixed-signal PCBs before formal certification testing. Work packages covered automated layout rule checking, near-field scan data processing and far-field transformation, and parametric FDTD simulation libraries for common PCB geometries. The methodology was validated on test vehicles designed at the faculty and on prototype boards provided by two partner companies from the Vojvodina electronics manufacturing sector. The project trained two doctoral students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. An open-source rule-checker tool was released under a permissive licence. The project supported calibration and upgrade of the faculty's near-field scanning bench, including a new motorised Z-axis stage.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektronika Inženjering d.o.o., Novi Sad
Induktivna Tehnika a.d., Subotica

projects.title: Signal Integrity and EMC Co-Design for Automotive Data Acquisition Modules
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A short-term contract research engagement with a Novi Sad-based company developing data acquisition modules for automotive powertrain test benches. The faculty team carried out PDN impedance characterisation, signal integrity simulation of LVDS interfaces at 800 Mbit/s, and pre-compliance conducted emission measurements to CISPR 25 on two hardware revisions. A root-cause analysis of a conducted emission failure near 7 MHz identified a common-mode resonance in the input filter that was resolved by substituting a nanocrystalline-core common-mode choke. The second hardware revision passed CISPR 25 Class 3 limits without further iteration.
partners: Meritron Automotive Electronics d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Diagnostic Coverage Assessment Methods for Safety-Critical Embedded Automotive Hardware
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops validated methods for experimentally determining diagnostic coverage of hardware safety mechanisms in automotive ECUs, addressing the known gap between analytically derived FMEA estimates and empirically observed fault detection rates. The work combines boundary-scan fault injection, FPGA-emulated ECU benchmarks, and statistical analysis of component aging effects to produce coverage estimates with quantified uncertainty bounds. Target applications include powertrain and chassis ECUs seeking ASIL-B through ASIL-D certification under ISO 26262. The project also produces an open-access component failure mode database populated with data from accelerated life tests conducted in the group's laboratory, intended as a shared resource for Serbian automotive electronics suppliers.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Technical University of Cluj-Napoca

projects.title: Safety-Compliant In-Vehicle Network Architectures for Autonomous Driving Subsystems
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SAFELINK addresses the safety certification of in-vehicle network interfaces in prototype autonomous driving subsystems developed by cross-border research teams in Serbia and Hungary. The project covers CAN FD, Ethernet AVB, and FlexRay communication links, producing FMEA worksheets, diagnostic coverage measurements, and ASIL allocation recommendations for each link type. The Faculty of Technical Sciences team leads the hardware FMEA work package, contributing fault injection infrastructure and worksheet generation tooling developed in earlier research. Results are validated against three prototype vehicle platforms maintained by the Hungarian partner. The project also includes a training component for engineering students at both institutions covering practical ISO 26262 hardware assessment.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology
Pannonia Automotive Research Institute (fictional, Győr, Hungary)

projects.title: Visual Inspection Adaptation for Heterogeneous SMT Manufacturing Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VIADAPT addressed the practical barrier of retraining AOI deep learning models each time a solder inspection system is deployed on a new production line or introduced to a new component type. The project developed domain adaptation and few-shot classification methods that require minimal labelled data from the target environment. Activities included construction of a multi-line benchmark dataset in collaboration with two Serbian electronics manufacturers, development of prototype-alignment and adversarial adaptation algorithms, and a pilot deployment on a partner's SMT line. The project trained two doctoral students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications. Publicly released datasets and code are hosted on the Faculty's institutional repository.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Elektronik Produkcija d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry observer)

projects.title: Cross-Border Quality Intelligence for Electronics Assembly: Shared Methods and Benchmarks
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSQUAL is a bilateral Interreg project between the University of Novi Sad and Budapest University of Technology and Economics, targeting shared methodological infrastructure for AI-based quality inspection in electronics assembly. Bulatović leads the work package on benchmark dataset construction and evaluation protocols, which involves defining annotation guidelines, cross-site data collection procedures, and inter-rater agreement measurement for defect labelling. The project also includes a researcher exchange programme and joint training workshops for industry personnel from SMT facilities in both countries. A shared data platform is being developed to allow secure, privacy-preserving access to multi-site inspection data across the national border.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Szerb-Magyar Elektronika Kft., Subotica
Precíziós Gyártás Zrt., Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Sensor Node Energy Autonomy Through Accurate Cell Lifetime Modelling
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENWATT aims to replace empirical rules of thumb for primary-cell sizing in long-lived IoT deployments with physics-informed parametric models calibrated on systematic laboratory ageing data. The project involves construction of an automated 48-channel pulse-load cycling station, a three-year ageing experiment on Li/SOCl₂ and Li/MnO₂ cells under nine IoT traffic profiles, and development of an open-source lifetime estimation library targeting resource-constrained microcontrollers. Validation deployments are planned in agricultural and hydrological monitoring networks in Vojvodina. A secondary objective is a public dataset of cell impedance and capacity data to support reproducible research in the field.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade

projects.title: Danube Basin Environmental Sensor Infrastructure for Water-Quality and Flood Early Warning
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBESENS deployed a cross-border network of 120 water-quality and river-level sensor nodes along the Serbian and Romanian stretches of the Danube. Vuk Bačić contributed to the power-systems work package, responsible for specifying primary-cell types and sizes for each node class, defining adaptive duty-cycle policies to extend cell life in high-traffic alarm conditions, and conducting post-deployment energy audits using the embedded energy meters developed in his group. The project delivered 18 months of continuous monitoring data and a maintenance protocol for battery replacement scheduling.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania
Institute for Water Management Jaroslav Černi, Belgrade
National Institute of Hydrology and Water Management, Bucharest

projects.title: Strengthening EMC Pre-Compliance Testing Capacity for Small Manufacturers in the Vojvodina Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between in-house pre-compliance EMC testing capabilities of small and medium-sized electronics manufacturers in Vojvodina and the requirements of the Radio Equipment Directive. Activities included the development of a shared pre-compliance testing protocol, procurement and commissioning of a near-field probe scanning system for the faculty laboratory, and a series of hands-on training workshops attended by technical staff from eleven regional companies. The project produced a publicly available pre-compliance testing handbook in Serbian and a database of correction factors for the near-field-to-far-field extrapolation procedure validated against the faculty semi-anechoic chamber.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina
NTP Novi Sad resident company cluster (anonymous consortium)

projects.title: Measurement Chain Traceability and Uncertainty Quantification for Wireless Device Compliance Testing in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RADIOCHAIN aims to establish traceable measurement chain verification procedures for radiated emissions and antenna efficiency testing in university and accredited laboratory environments in the Western Balkans, where calibration infrastructure is less developed than in EU member states. The project develops reference artefacts and uncertainty models for three measurement configurations: semi-anechoic chamber radiated emissions, reverberation chamber antenna efficiency, and near-field scanning. A proficiency testing round involving eight laboratories in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina is planned. Results are being prepared for submission to ETSI and CISPR working groups as regional input to the revision of EN 55032 and CISPR 16-4-2.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Sarajevo
Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje

projects.title: Thermal-Stress-Aware Test Coverage Assurance for Long-Lifetime Mixed-Signal Electronic Assemblies
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the degradation of in-circuit and boundary-scan test coverage that occurs as solder joints, contact pads, and board laminates age under repeated thermal excursions. The core deliverables are a set of empirically validated coverage-lifetime models parameterised by thermal profile severity, board material, and component package type, and a software tool that uses these models to predict coverage at any point in a product's operating lifetime. The tool was demonstrated on board designs provided by two industrial partners. The project also produced a revised DFT guideline document tailored to boards used in outdoor electronics enclosures in continental European climate conditions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektronik Produkcija d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of East Sarajevo

projects.title: Boundary-Scan Interconnect Integrity Monitoring for Automotive and Industrial PCB Assemblies
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: BOUNDLINK investigated whether periodic boundary-scan resistance measurements could serve as a non-destructive health indicator for BGA and fine-pitch connector solder joints in automotive-grade assemblies. The project combined accelerated life testing, four-wire resistance measurement through scan chains, and statistical process control methods to define alert thresholds for joint degradation. Results were validated against cross-section microscopy on a sample of 40 boards. The project delivered a monitoring protocol and a set of threshold tables for three thermal stress classes, and findings informed the design-for-testability guidelines developed in the subsequent THERMOTEST project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Electronics Technology, Budapest University of Technology and Economics

projects.title: Sub-Surface LoRaWAN Sensing for Urban Infrastructure Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SUBSENSE addressed the absence of standardised propagation models and deployment guidelines for LoRaWAN sensor networks in below-grade urban infrastructure, including utility tunnels, underground car parks, and building basements. The project combined controlled laboratory measurements of material-specific signal attenuation with large-scale field campaigns in Novi Sad. A parametric link budget toolkit was developed that accepts building material properties, structure geometry, and gateway position as inputs and outputs coverage probability maps. The toolkit was validated in three pilot environments provided by municipal partners. Results were disseminated in four journal papers and three conference contributions. A freely downloadable software package was released under an open-source licence at the end of the project.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences
Public Utility Company Novi Sad Waters – fictional
Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania – fictional

projects.title: LoRaWAN Gateway Optimisation and Adaptive Rate Control for Smart City Applications in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: LOROPT brought together partners from Novi Sad and Pécs to develop jointly validated tools for LoRaWAN network planning in mid-size Pannonian cities, which share similar low-rise building stock, flat terrain, and continental vegetation patterns. Branislava Janković led the work package on propagation model calibration and gateway placement optimisation. The project produced a shared measurement dataset of approximately 30 000 RSSI records across both cities, a calibrated ray-tracing model, and a genetic-algorithm-based placement tool. Two pilot networks were commissioned, one monitoring air quality sensors in Subotica and one monitoring soil moisture in an agricultural periurban zone near Pécs. The project trained six early-stage researchers across the two institutions.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary – fictional
City of Subotica, Department of Environmental Protection – fictional

projects.title: Integrated Quality Assurance Methodology for Pre-Weld Surface Preparation in Automated Thin-Sheet Joining Lines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a structured quality assurance methodology covering measurement methods, acceptance criteria, and control chart templates for pre-weld surface cleanliness on cold-rolled mild-steel blanks in automated MIG/MAG joining lines. Work includes characterisation of residual contamination types (lubricants, rust-preventive oils, press shop dust) by FTIR-ATR and TOC analysis, quantification of their influence on arc stability and weld quality, and translation of laboratory findings into practical process capability targets. Two partner companies from the Vojvodina automotive supply sector provide industrial test cases. The final deliverable is a guidance document and training module targeting quality engineers at small and medium-sized fabricators.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Metalform d.o.o., Novi Sad
Presing Komponente d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Process Monitoring and Control Tools for Small-Scale Electrostatic Powder Coating Pre-Treatment Lines
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project addressed the lack of structured process monitoring in small powder coating operations in Vojvodina. Activities included a baseline survey of bath chemistry management practices at seven local contractors, instrument calibration audits, and a pilot SPC deployment at two volunteer companies. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian/English) SPC implementation guide for pre-treatment lines, freely distributed to members of the Vojvodina Coating Contractors Association. Results from the pilot companies were subsequently published in peer-reviewed form. Total funding was 1.2 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Coating Contractors Association

projects.title: Scalable Formal Verification Methods for Interrupt-Driven Firmware in Industrial Embedded Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FIRMVER investigated compositional and incremental model-checking techniques to make formal verification of real-time interrupt-driven firmware feasible for industrial-scale codebases. The project developed the MisraFix automated repair tool, the incremental Promela extraction pipeline, and a library of verified component stubs for common peripheral driver patterns on ARM Cortex-M devices. Three Ph.D. students were supported. Deliverables include a publicly available toolchain prototype, five peer-reviewed journal publications, and a technical report on integration with the CMake build system. The project collaborated with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and with Czech Technical University in Prague for external validation of the methodology on independently developed firmware.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Czech Technical University in Prague, Czech Republic

projects.title: Methodology and Tool Support for Safe Migration of Legacy Embedded C Code to MISRA-C:2012
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SAFE-MIGRATE developed practical methods and tool support to assist small and medium embedded-systems companies in the Vojvodina region in migrating legacy C firmware to MISRA-C:2012 compliance. The project produced the initial version of the MisraFix rewriting tool, a catalogue of refactoring patterns for safety-relevant firmware, and a training programme delivered to engineers at two local companies working on automotive and industrial control products. The project included a pilot application in which the methodology was applied to a 47 kB motor-controller firmware under an industry collaboration agreement. A total of four peer-reviewed publications resulted from the project.
partners: NTP Novi Sad — tenant company Embeddium d.o.o.
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermal and Mechanical Error Modelling for In-Process Accuracy Recovery in Articulated Robot Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the full chain from thermal field characterisation through unified error identification to embedded closed-loop compensation in six-axis industrial robots. Activities included instrumentation of three robot testbeds, design of a physics-based reduced-order thermal model, development of the unified geometric-thermal identification algorithm, and implementation of the extended Kalman filter recalibration scheme on embedded controller hardware. The project funded two doctoral researchers and one postdoctoral position. Experimental validation was conducted both in the university laboratory and at a partner company's assembly facility in Novi Sad. Deliverables included four journal publications, an open dataset of 90-day thermal drift records, and a software library for kinematic parameter management released under an open-source licence.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Produktronika d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Accuracy-Driven Robot Integration in Small-Batch Manufacturing Across the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project addressing the adoption of precision robot-based manufacturing by small and medium enterprises in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. Ivanović leads the work package on measurement methodology and error compensation, providing calibration services, training workshops, and transferable software tools to partner SMEs. Other work packages cover process planning, fixturing, and business model development. The project includes a shared demonstration cell installed at the University of Novi Sad and a mirror cell at the partner university in Hungary, enabling joint student supervision and staff mobility. Expected outputs include a calibration service protocol, training materials in Serbian and Hungarian, and at least two pilot implementations at industrial partner sites.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Miskolc, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Informatics
Vojvođanska Industrija Preciznih Delova d.o.o., Subotica
Pannonia Gépgyár Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Standardised Cost Modelling Toolkit for Engineer-to-Order SMEs in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a practical cost modelling toolkit targeting Serbian SMEs in the ETO manufacturing sector, where dedicated cost engineering departments rarely exist. The toolkit comprises a data-collection protocol, a parametric model calibration procedure, and a spreadsheet-based implementation. The research team is collecting historical order data from eight partner companies in metalworking, fluid power, and special-purpose machinery. In addition to model development, the project is producing training materials for production engineers and conducting a structured evaluation of toolkit adoption across six companies in a pilot deployment phase. Results are being disseminated through open-access publications and practitioner workshops organised in cooperation with the Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina
Kovaform d.o.o., Zrenjanin
Fluidomont d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Work Measurement and Standard Time Systems for Project-Based Manufacturing Enterprises
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigated the state of work measurement practice in project-based manufacturing companies in Vojvodina and developed guidance for implementing work-content standardisation systems suited to non-repetitive production. Field studies were conducted at five companies, including observations of current estimation and time-recording practices. The project produced a classification scheme for non-repetitive work elements, a pilot standard-time database covering 40 common assembly operations, and a set of implementation guidelines. A final workshop attended by representatives from eleven companies was held in Novi Sad. The project also supported two master's theses and contributed to curriculum revision for the industrial engineering programme at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvođanski privredni savet – Advisory Board of Vojvodina Economy

projects.title: Fatigue Reliability of Welded Steel Structures Under Combined Mechanical and Thermal Cyclic Loads in Cold Continental Climates
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap in design codes regarding fatigue assessment of welded structural steel exposed simultaneously to mechanical service loads and seasonal thermal cycling in climates where ambient temperatures regularly fall below −20 °C. The work combined fatigue testing at controlled sub-zero temperatures, X-ray diffraction residual stress measurements, digital image correlation, and sequentially coupled FE simulations. Key deliverables included a dataset of fatigue curves at four temperatures for S355 and S460NL welded details, a validated residual-stress relaxation model under thermo-mechanical loading, and draft provisions for a temperature correction factor compatible with the IIW fatigue design recommendations. The project supported one doctoral student and two master's theses.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš
Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade

projects.title: Structural Integrity Assessment Methods for Welded Components in Adriatic–Pannonian Infrastructure
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral cooperation project between the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Naval Architecture in Zagreb. The Serbian team was responsible for the work package on fracture mechanics testing and FE-based fitness-for-service assessment of welded joints in high-strength steels, while the Croatian partners contributed expertise in non-destructive evaluation and probabilistic life assessment. Joint workshops were held in Novi Sad and Zagreb; two joint journal papers were produced. Erić led the experimental testing and simulation activities on the Serbian side and co-supervised a doctoral student enrolled at Zagreb.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Naval Architecture, University of Zagreb

projects.title: Product-Line Code Generation Infrastructure for Configurable PLC Software
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The PLCGEN project developed an end-to-end toolchain for model-driven software product-line engineering targeting IEC 61131-3 Structured Text. Work packages covered metamodel design, feature model integration, incremental generation, and round-trip recovery of variation points from legacy code. The project delivered an Eclipse-based IDE plugin, a library of reusable transformation modules, and the benchmark suite reported in the 2026 journal paper. Two Ph.D. students were funded through the project. Industry validation was carried out with one automation equipment manufacturer in Novi Sad and one in Subotica under non-disclosure agreements. The project produced nine peer-reviewed publications and one master thesis.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Safety-Aware Product-Line Modelling for Certified Automation Software
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SAFEPLL addressed the integration of functional safety requirements into model-driven PLC product-line workflows, targeting IEC 62061 SIL 1 and SIL 2 certified applications. The project brought together researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest with two SME automation integrators. Veljko Pantelić led the work package on traceability from HAZOP artefacts to generated code, contributing the SysML parametric diagram transformation described in the 2021 conference paper. The project produced a methodology document adopted by both industrial partners as an internal development guideline, and delivered training workshops for engineering staff at both companies.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Automatika-Pro d.o.o., Novi Sad
RoboSystems Kft., Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: EMC Characterisation and Filter Validation Methods for SiC-Based Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between laboratory IEC 61800-3 compliance and field performance of EMC filters for SiC MOSFET motor drives. The work covered three main activities: systematic conducted emission characterisation of SiC drives from 2.2 kW to 22 kW, development of a measurement uncertainty budget specific to high-di/dt inverter systems, and design and experimental validation of filter topologies robust to realistic PE impedance variation encountered in Serbian industrial installations. Forty-seven sites were surveyed for PE impedance. Deliverables included a filter design procedure, a dataset of emission spectra and PE impedance profiles made publicly available, and two validated simulation models. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Institute for Power Engineering and Automation, Subotica

projects.title: Harmonic and EMC Interaction in Multi-Drive Industrial Power Systems
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: HARMONIA examined harmonic and conducted EMI interactions arising when multiple variable-speed drives share a common AC supply or DC bus in manufacturing plant environments. The project combined controlled laboratory experiments on two- and three-drive configurations with simulation studies using measured drive models. Key findings concerned the conditions under which inter-drive harmonic coupling can cause individual drives to fail IEC 61800-3 limits even when each drive passes in isolation, and the degree to which switching frequency offset reduces this risk. Practical installation guidelines were produced for plant electrical engineers. The project funded one master's thesis and supported the development of the Faculty's multi-drive test bench.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Perception and Grasping of Transparent and Translucent Objects for Flexible Robotic Assembly
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TRANSBOT addresses the gap in robotic bin-picking performance when the target objects are transparent or translucent, conditions under which standard RGB-D sensors fail. The project develops a multi-modal perception unit combining a polarisation camera, a near-infrared photometric stereo dome, and a phase-shift structured-light projector, together with a unified calibration and fusion framework. The primary application domains are food-packaging assembly and pharmaceutical laboratory automation, where transparent containers and translucent plastic components are common. Deliverables include a public benchmark dataset of 3D ground-truth scans for 60 object types, an open-source ROS2 package, and a demonstrator cell with a six-axis manipulator. The project involves a postdoctoral researcher and two Ph.D. students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research, Novi Sad

projects.title: Vision-Guided Servo Control for Precision Assembly of Small Specular Components
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A short-term research contract with Mekosystems d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based manufacturer of automated screwdriving and fastener-insertion equipment. The project adapted the group's structured-light and photometric stereo pipeline for integration into Mekosystems' existing machine vision controller, targeting sub-millimetre positioning of shiny M3–M6 fasteners during automated insertion. Work included sensor miniaturisation to fit within the company's existing machine enclosure, latency reduction to meet a 1.5-second cycle time requirement, and on-site validation over a two-week production trial. The deliverable was a validated perception module and an integration specification document; IP rights for the implementation were transferred to the company.
partners: Mekosystems d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Real-Time Scheduling and Replanning for Heterogeneous Robot Fleets in Partially Observable Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the problem of online task scheduling and motion replanning for fleets of 4–16 heterogeneous robots operating in warehouses and light manufacturing facilities where full observability cannot be assumed. The core research questions concern the computational complexity of replanning under partial observability, the design of anytime algorithms with bounded suboptimality guarantees, and the integration of task-level planning with geometric motion planning. Work packages cover algorithm design, benchmark development, hardware experiments on the Faculty's robot testbed, and technology transfer to a partner company developing logistics software. The project funds one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences
Logiflow Systems d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cooperative Planning Methods for Cross-Border Autonomous Vehicle Deployments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral Serbia–Hungary project investigating cooperative planning algorithms for small autonomous vehicle deployments at cross-border logistics terminals. The Novi Sad team leads the work package on combinatorial optimisation and scheduling, contributing multi-agent pathfinding algorithms adapted to the terminal environment. The Hungarian partner contributes simulation infrastructure and vehicle hardware. Ratko Simić leads the algorithmic work package, which is responsible for designing and validating the planning layer of the software stack. The project includes joint student mobility visits and a shared dataset of terminal operations collected at a pilot site near Subotica.
partners: University of Szeged, Department of Computer Science
TermiLog Hungary Kft., Szeged
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences

projects.title: Interoperability Middleware for Heterogeneous Manufacturing Networks in SMEs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the practical difficulty that small and medium-sized manufacturers in Serbia face when integrating legacy shopfloor equipment with newer IIoT monitoring systems. Knežević led Work Package 2, which covered middleware architecture design and the development of a reference gateway stack supporting Modbus RTU, Modbus TCP, Profibus DP, and OPC UA. The gateway stack was deployed and evaluated at two pilot sites: a plastics injection moulding company and a food packaging line, both in the Vojvodina region. The project produced three peer-reviewed publications, an open-source software repository, and a set of training materials for automation engineers. Total budget approximately 4.8 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia, Novi Sad
Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Automation and Digitalisation for Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border initiative between Hungarian and Serbian higher education institutions aimed at transferring automation and digitalisation knowledge to manufacturing SMEs along the Danube corridor. Knežević contributed to the technical workstream responsible for developing a shared laboratory module on industrial communication standards, including OPC UA and TSN, which was piloted with SME engineers from both countries in two five-day training workshops in 2023 and 2024. He was also involved in producing a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) technical guide on gateway selection criteria for brownfield integration scenarios. The project served approximately 140 SME engineers across both countries by the end of its third year.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Miskolc, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Informatics, Hungary
Regional Development Agency of Bács-Kiskun County, Hungary
Business Incubator Subotica

projects.title: Reliability Data Infrastructure for Pneumatic Final Elements in Serbian Process Industry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the absence of locally calibrated failure rate data for pneumatic control and on-off valves in Serbian process plants. In collaboration with two Vojvodina refineries and a gas compression operator, a structured failure reporting and recording system was deployed at three facilities covering approximately 310 pneumatic final elements. Data were collected over 30 months and used to derive posterior failure rate distributions via Bayesian updating against generic OREDA entries. The project produced a pilot failure rate dataset covering five valve categories, a guidance document for plant operators on data collection procedures, and updated SIL verification calculation templates consistent with IEC 61511-1:2016. Results were disseminated to six partner companies through two industrial workshops held in Novi Sad.
partners: NTP Novi Sad — tenant company Autosafe d.o.o.
Energoprojekt Entel, Belgrade
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Functional Safety of Hybrid Control Architectures in Cross-Border Industrial Zones
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HYSAFEX addressed the safety assessment of hybrid control systems at industrial facilities operating across the Serbian-Hungarian border region, where differing national implementation practices for IEC 61511 create inconsistencies in safety case documentation. Mladenović led the work package on methodology harmonisation, which produced a bilingual HAZOP facilitation guide and a set of common worksheets accepted by both Serbian and Hungarian regulatory reference bodies. The project included a joint training programme for 34 process safety engineers from 11 companies across the two countries. A shared database of cross-validated IPL credit claims was established and made available to participating facilities under a data-sharing agreement. The University of Novi Sad contributed its process control rig as a demonstration platform for cross-border functional testing exercises.
partners: Department of Chemical Engineering, University of Pécs
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina (RORS)
Pannonia Industrial Safety Consulting Kft., Pécs
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Variable-Amplitude and Reversing-Load Effects on Contact Fatigue Life of Case-Hardened Gear Flanks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated how realistic variable-amplitude and reversing-torque load histories alter micropitting initiation and propagation relative to ISO 6336 constant-load equivalence assumptions. A systematic experimental programme on carburised spur and helical gears was combined with TEHL film modelling at instantaneous operating points along each load spectrum. Results produced an empirically fitted correction function for allowable contact stress under reversing torque, validated against three industry-relevant load spectra. The project included a collaboration with the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering in Niš for fractographic analysis and with Leibniz University Hannover for traction coefficient characterisation. Two journal articles and one conference paper were produced.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš
Leibniz University Hannover, Institute for Machine Design

projects.title: Tribological Performance of Gear Contacts in Automation and Precision Drive Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project focuses on small-module and thin-case-layer gears used in precision drive and automation equipment manufactured in the Vojvodina region. It examines how low-temperature thermochemical treatments, superfinishing, and lubricant selection interact to determine micropitting and wear resistance under reversing and variable-amplitude loads representative of robotic joint and linear actuator duty cycles. The experimental work uses the Tribology and Machine Elements Laboratory at FTN Novi Sad. An industry partner from the NTP Novi Sad Science Technology Park contributes application requirements and provides prototype gear sets for testing. Student internship placements are planned for two Master's students per year.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad (host)
Precizna Transmisija d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Smart In-Process Tool-Wear Estimation for Small-Batch Precision Turning Using Embedded Sensor Fusion
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate an embedded sensor-fusion system for real-time tool-condition monitoring in small-batch CNC turning, addressing the gap between research-grade monitoring systems and what is deployable in Serbian precision-machining SMEs. Work covered sensor selection, feature engineering, particle-filter algorithm development, and embedded implementation on ARM-based hardware connected to standard CNC drive buses. The system was tested in a 6-week production trial at a regional valve-component manufacturer. Deliverables included an open hardware reference design, a documented dataset of 90 tool-life experiments across three steel grades, and three journal publications. Two master's theses and one doctoral thesis were completed within the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš
Precizno d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Digitally Enhanced Manufacturing Processes for Regional Industry Competitiveness
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project involving four partners in Hungary and Serbia with the goal of transferring digital-monitoring methods from research to regional manufacturing SMEs. Katarina Malešević led Work Package 3, covering sensor-based process monitoring for machining operations. Activities included training workshops for 34 SME technicians, site assessments at six companies, and preparation of two pilot monitoring installations (one in Subotica, one in Pécs). The project produced a joint methodological guide for SPC implementation in machining cells, published in Serbian and Hungarian. Collaboration with the Hungarian partner produced a shared dataset used in the 2022 particle-filter publication.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Budapest University of Technology and Economics

projects.title: Bio-Based and Biodegradable Synthetic Gear Lubricants for Enclosed Drive Systems: Formulation, Tribochemical Evaluation, and Environmental Fate
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project addressed the formulation and tribochemical characterisation of gear lubricants based on renewable base stocks, primarily phospholipid-modified vegetable oils and estolides, with zinc-free antiwear additive packages. The work combined laboratory tribological testing (four-ball, FZG, MTM), thermal-oxidative stability assessment (PDSC, RBOT), and surface analysis (XPS, AFM) to develop a performance comparison framework against conventional PAO-based references. Environmental fate was assessed through BOD/COD ratio measurements and OECD 301B biodegradability testing of the candidate formulations. The project involved collaboration with an agricultural research institute supplying modified crop-oil feedstocks and resulted in two journal papers, a conference contribution, and formulation guidelines submitted to a domestic gear-drive manufacturer.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Nanoadditive-Enhanced Boundary Films in Industrial Gear Lubricants: Mechanistic Studies and Stability Assessment
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates the tribochemical mechanisms by which graphene oxide and layered double hydroxide nanoadditives form protective boundary films on gear-steel contacts. Emphasis is placed on understanding the relationship between nanoparticle surface chemistry, dispersion stability in PAO and ester base stocks, and the resulting tribofilm structure as characterised by Raman spectroscopy, XPS, and AFM. A secondary objective is to establish the compatibility of these nanoadditives with commercial antioxidant and antiwear additive packages, including long-term storage stability under humidity cycling. The project involves one doctoral student and one master's student. Results are expected to inform formulation strategies for moderate-load enclosed gearboxes operating under intermittent lubrication conditions.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Safety Verification Methods for Collaborative Robot Workspaces in Serbian SME Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SafeCoWork aimed to develop practical tools and methods for deploying ISO/TS 15066-compliant collaborative robot systems in small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises in Serbia, where dedicated safety engineering expertise is scarce. The project produced the CobotAudit software tool for retrospective compliance auditing, a sensor fusion reference design validated in laboratory conditions, and a set of task-redesign guidelines based on field measurements at five industrial sites. Training workshops were delivered to 34 engineers from 11 companies in Vojvodina. The project also established a shared-workspace cobot testbed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences that remains available for industrial partner use after project completion.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Occupational Health Novi Sad
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer for Collaborative Robot Safety in Light Manufacturing
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COLLABSAFE addressed the gap in collaborative robotics safety knowledge on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. The Novi Sad team led the work package on technical standardisation and measurement methodology, developing a harmonised experimental protocol for benchmarking occupancy-detection systems under comparable conditions at partner laboratories in Subotica and Pécs. Joint test campaigns produced a comparative dataset of sensor performance under conditions specific to local light-manufacturing sectors, including textile handling and food-packaging environments with elevated humidity and airborne particulates. A jointly authored best-practice guide was translated into Serbian and Hungarian and distributed through both countries' industry associations.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology

projects.title: Skill Library Frameworks for On-Demand Robot Program Generation in Regional SME Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SKILLFORGE addressed the gap between academic skill-based programming research and its practical uptake in small and medium enterprises in the Vojvodina region. The project built a validated skill library covering pick-and-place, welding, and screw-driving operations, and developed a web-based tool for library browsing, skill instantiation, and program synthesis targeting KUKA KRC4 and Universal Robots Polyscope controllers. Three manufacturing SMEs participated as validation partners, contributing archived robot programs for library construction and hosting pilot deployments. The project produced eight peer-reviewed publications, one defended doctoral dissertation, and a publicly released ontology and tool chain under an open licence. A benchmark evaluation framework developed within the project was later extended into the community benchmark preprint submitted in 2025.

projects.title: Semantic Reconfiguration Management for Shared Human-Robot Workstations
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RECONMAN was a cross-border cooperation project between research groups in Serbia and Hungary aimed at reducing the time and expertise required to reconfigure shared human-robot workstations when product variants change. The project combined the semantic workcell description approach from Novi Sad with safety zone modelling expertise from Óbuda University and a shared demonstrator workcell installed at the Hungarian partner site. Simić's group led the work package on knowledge representation and program synthesis, contributing the OWL-based workcell model, the reconfiguration rule engine, and integration with the safety system API. The project also supported two student exchange visits and co-supervised one master's thesis.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
John von Neumann Faculty of Informatics, Óbuda University, Budapest

projects.title: Thermal State Estimation and Adaptive Parameter Control for Robotic Arc Welding
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: THERMARC addressed the problem of unknown and varying thermal boundary conditions in robotic GMAW production cells. The project developed sensor fusion methods combining infrared pool imaging with arc electrical signals to estimate workpiece thermal state in real time, and built closed-loop controllers that use these estimates to adjust process parameters. Work was conducted on a dedicated robotic GMAW cell at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Outcomes included validated observer algorithms, a dataset of 600 annotated welding runs, three journal publications, and a technology demonstrator evaluated with an industrial partner manufacturing structural steel subassemblies in Novi Sad. Two PhD students were funded through the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Metalprodukt Inženjering d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptive Robotic Welding for Small and Medium Manufacturers in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ADRIWELD aimed to transfer adaptive robotic welding knowledge and equipment to small and medium-sized manufacturers in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Valentina Simić led the work package on process control methodology, responsible for developing training materials, conducting technology audits at four SME partner sites, and adapting control software for two commercially available robot controller platforms. The project provided hands-on training to 34 technicians and engineers across partner companies. A shared robotic welding demonstration cell was established at the Hungarian partner university for ongoing use after project closure.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Verification and Runtime Analysis for Safety-Critical Embedded Control Software
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VERITAS addressed two interrelated problems in safety-critical embedded software engineering: the cost of exhaustive formal verification and the limited coverage of runtime assertion checking. The project developed lightweight static pre-filters that reduce the verification search space before handing off to model checkers, and a runtime monitor generator that instruments binaries with safety properties at the machine-code level without modifying source code. Verification experiments were conducted on firmware from the automotive and building-automation domains. The project produced six peer-reviewed publications, an open-source Frama-C plugin for incremental MISRA-C checking, and a cooperation agreement with one Serbian automation equipment manufacturer for follow-on contract research. Two MSc students and one PhD candidate were funded through the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Formal Methods Training and Tool Integration for Small Embedded Software Teams in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FORMBASE aimed to lower the barrier to formal methods adoption in small software teams developing embedded control systems in Hungary and Serbia. Stefan Kostić led the work package responsible for curriculum development and tool-integration workshops. The project produced a three-day training course covering CBMC, Frama-C, and UPPAAL, delivered to 68 engineers from 11 companies across the two countries. A companion open-access textbook of 180 pages was written in Serbian and Hungarian. The project also ran a tool evaluation study comparing six open-source formal verification tools on a shared benchmark of embedded firmware, with results published as a technical report. Two pilot adoptions in participating companies were documented as case studies.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Validation on Open Platforms for Regional Automotive Suppliers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate a complete open-source HiL framework—comprising real-time kernel configurations, FPGA I/O boards, fault injection hardware, and test automation scripts—targeting small and medium-sized automotive ECU suppliers in the Vojvodina region who cannot afford commercial HiL systems. Three reference bench configurations were developed and documented, covering powertrain, body, and chassis domains. The framework was tested in collaboration with two regional suppliers under non-disclosure agreements. Deliverables include hardware design files, kernel build scripts, and a test case library with over 400 parametric test vectors. A graduate-level course module on open-source HiL was developed as a secondary outcome.

projects.title: Cross-Border Training Network for Embedded Automotive Systems Engineers
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border training initiative involving three universities and two technology parks in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Ninkov led the work package on practical HiL laboratory training, coordinating the design of shared laboratory exercises and the procurement of bench equipment installed at two partner sites. The work package delivered ten hands-on workshop modules, trained 84 engineering students and 12 industry practitioners over three years, and produced a jointly authored laboratory manual released under Creative Commons. The project also established a shared equipment loan scheme between the Novi Sad and Subotica partner sites.

projects.title: Dynamic Optimisation Methods for Real-Time Public Transport Management in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated rolling-horizon and online metaheuristic methods for real-time management of public bus fleets, focusing on disruption recovery and electric vehicle integration. The team built a simulation testbed using timetable and incident data from two Serbian cities, implemented a prototype decision-support tool for dispatchers, and produced a suite of open benchmark instances for dynamic vehicle scheduling. Collaboration with a regional transport operator provided access to anonymised operational data. The project supported two PhD students and resulted in five journal publications and three conference papers. A final dissemination workshop was held in Novi Sad in October 2024 with participants from transport operators, municipal authorities, and research groups from Hungary and Romania.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Optimisation of Last-Mile Freight Logistics in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSS-FREIGHT addresses the coordination of last-mile urban freight deliveries in border-zone cities in Hungary and Serbia, where different regulatory environments and infrastructure standards complicate joint scheduling. Obradović leads the work package on algorithmic methods, responsible for adapting multi-modal rolling-horizon scheduling tools to the specific constraints of cross-border freight zones, including customs clearance time windows and restricted delivery hours. The work package budget covers one postdoctoral researcher and computing resources. Progress is measured against a jointly developed benchmark suite. The project also includes stakeholder workshops with municipal logistics coordinators and small freight operators in Subotica and Szeged.

projects.title: Real-Time Learning Models for Bus Network Reliability in Mid-Sized Balkan Cities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REALBUS addresses the gap between research-grade travel time predictors and deployable tools for cities with limited IT infrastructure. The project develops lightweight Bayesian and neural network models that can be retrained nightly on a standard server using the previous week of AVL data, without requiring GPU hardware. Pilot deployments are planned in Novi Sad and one partner city. The project produces open-source software, a curated benchmark dataset under a public licence, and a methodology report addressed to transport planners. A secondary objective is to build a labelled dataset of disruption events (roadworks, accidents, protests) linked to AVL anomalies, to support future work on event-triggered model adaptation.

projects.title: Cross-Modal Telemetry Fusion for Urban Mobility Analysis in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRIMODDATA brings together research teams from Novi Sad and Pécs to build a shared methodology for fusing AVL, bike-sharing, and floating-car data into unified travel time surfaces for urban corridors. Novaković leads the work package on public transport telemetry, responsible for harmonising AVL preprocessing standards between the two cities and for producing stop-level travel time estimates as inputs to the joint fusion model. The project includes two student exchange visits per year and a joint summer school on urban mobility data. Outputs include a bilingual (Serbian/Hungarian) data-sharing protocol and a web dashboard for corridor performance monitoring.

projects.title: Automated Road Infrastructure Monitoring Using UAV and Satellite Remote Sensing Data Fusion
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ROADSCAN addressed the development and validation of an automated monitoring pipeline for the Serbian classified road network, integrating UAV LiDAR surveys with Sentinel-2 satellite time series. The project produced open-source software modules for change detection, road furniture extraction, and map update scheduling. Paunović led the LiDAR data processing component and contributed to the integration of results into a GIS-based decision support tool piloted with the Public Enterprise Roads of Serbia. The project covered four test corridors totalling approximately 85 km and produced two open benchmark datasets released under a Creative Commons licence.

projects.title: Cross-Border Road Asset Mapping and Condition Assessment Using Shared Remote Sensing Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMAP is a cross-border cooperation project aimed at harmonising road asset inventory practices between Serbian and Hungarian road authorities along the shared border region. The project establishes joint UAV survey protocols, a shared point cloud data repository, and a common data model for road asset attributes aligned with EU INSPIRE standards. Paunović leads the work package responsible for UAV data acquisition methodology, quality control procedures, and training workshops for technical staff at both road administrations. The project also pilots an automated change-flagging service for the border crossing approaches at two locations.

projects.title: Automated Quality Assurance for Road Map Formats Used in Autonomous Vehicle Simulation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ROADFIX developed a suite of automated tools for detecting and repairing geometric and topological errors in road map files used by ADAS simulation platforms, with a primary focus on OpenDRIVE and Lanelet2 formats. The project produced an annotated corpus of 120 map files with labelled errors, a rule-based checker covering 23 error classes, and prototype repair algorithms for 15 of those classes. The tools were validated in collaboration with one domestic automotive electronics company and one regional academic partner. The project also contributed to a proposed extension of the OpenDRIVE standard addressing three specification ambiguities identified during the research. Two journal papers, three conference papers, and one open-source software release resulted from the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Simulation Corridor for Cooperative Driving Testing on the Novi Sad–Subotica Axis
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SIMCOR aims to create a georeferenced, simulation-ready digital road map of the approximately 95 km corridor connecting Novi Sad and Subotica, extending across the Hungarian border toward Baja. Radmila Radović leads the work package responsible for map data acquisition, format harmonisation, and delivery of validated OpenDRIVE and Lanelet2 files to project partners. The corridor map will be used by consortium members to develop and test cooperative adaptive cruise control and platooning algorithms in simulation before physical trials. The project involves mobile LiDAR surveys, OSM integration, and the incremental update methodology developed under ROADFIX. Deliverables include a publicly accessible map repository and a standard operating procedure for corridor map maintenance.

projects.title: Compression and On-Device Inference Strategies for Industrial Vibration IoT Nodes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between theoretical compression ratios achievable on vibration data and the practical compute and memory constraints of sub-1 MHz microcontrollers used in industrial sensor nodes. Work packages covered adaptive frame boundary detection, structured neural network pruning, and integer-only inference engine integration. The team built a test infrastructure consisting of four bearing rigs instrumented with Kistler piezoelectric sensors and a reference DAQ system for ground-truth labelling. Deliverables included a software library for STM32 targets, a publicly released labelled dataset of 480 hours of bearing vibration under controlled fault conditions, and four peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Energy-Efficient Edge Vibration Monitoring for Smart Manufacturing
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: EDGEVIB focuses on the integration of adaptive sampling, lightweight data compression, and on-device neural inference within a single firmware stack targeting coin-cell-powered BLE sensor nodes. The project collaborates with two companies at NTP Novi Sad for pilot deployments on conveyor drive motors and CNC spindle units. Key research questions concern the trade-off between inference duty cycle and battery longevity, the robustness of int8 models after incremental over-the-air updates, and the minimum sensor bandwidth needed to detect early-stage bearing faults. A secondary outcome is a teaching module on TinyML incorporated into the embedded systems curriculum at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

projects.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Multi-Fault Diagnosis in Industrial Drivetrains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops fault diagnosis methods for industrial gearboxes and rolling-element bearings that incorporate physical knowledge of machine kinematics directly into the structure of machine learning classifiers and feature spaces. Work covers three threads: (1) physics-constrained feature engineering for SVM and RF classifiers, (2) domain adaptation strategies enabling classifiers trained on laboratory rigs to transfer to field machines, and (3) construction and publication of a labelled benchmark dataset from the FTS drivetrain test rig. The project supports two doctoral students and involves a collaboration with Politehnica University of Timișoara. All software and datasets are released openly at project end.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Low-Cost Condition Monitoring Systems for Small and Medium Wind Turbines in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project addressed the lack of affordable condition monitoring infrastructure for the small and medium wind turbine fleet in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Gordana Kuzmanović led the work package responsible for vibration signal processing algorithms and alarm logic, adapting laboratory-developed spectral trending methods to operate on low-cost single-board computers with intermittent connectivity. Field installations on three turbines in Vojvodina provided long-term measurement data used to validate alarm thresholds. The project produced a hardware–software monitoring prototype and a deployment guide for turbine operators, and supported two master's thesis projects at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Bay Zoltán Applied Research Institute, Miskolc, Hungary

projects.title: Thermomechanical Reliability of Encapsulant Systems for Power Electronics in Harsh Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the lack of standardised fatigue life prediction methods for polymer encapsulants used in power electronics modules operating under harsh thermal environments such as automotive and industrial drives. The research team at Novi Sad combined accelerated ageing campaigns, DMA characterisation, scanning acoustic microscopy and finite-element cohesive zone modelling to build a predictive framework relating material microstructure to seal lifetime. Work packages covered material selection and characterisation, protocol development, modelling and validation on representative test vehicles. Four graduate students participated as research assistants throughout the project. Key outcomes include a calibrated cohesive zone parameter database for five commercial encapsulant systems and a draft accelerated testing protocol submitted to a Serbian standardisation body.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Faculty of Electronics

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Polymer Bonding Reliability in Electronic Components for Regional Industry
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project between Serbian and Hungarian research groups and regional electronics manufacturers aimed to establish shared testing capabilities and common reliability benchmarks for polymer bonding materials used in local electronics assembly firms. Andrić led the work package on thermomechanical fatigue testing methodology, coordinating specimen exchange between Novi Sad and Budapest partners, establishing common DMA and ATC protocols, and compiling comparative material performance data. The project supported the purchase of additional climate chamber capacity at the Faculty of Technology. Three companies from the Vojvodina region participated as industrial observers, and two undergraduate final-year projects were co-supervised with Budapest University of Technology and Economics.

projects.title: Model-Driven Engineering Methods for Verified Automotive Embedded Software
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates formal and semi-formal methods for verifying the correctness of model transformations used in AUTOSAR toolchains. Activities include: formalising ATL transformation semantics in a subset of Z notation, developing a property-based test generation framework for Ecore-based transformations, and building a prototype transformation verification tool integrated into the Eclipse ecosystem. The project collaborates with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava. Industrial relevance is maintained through a liaison with a regional embedded-software consultancy that provides representative AUTOSAR model corpora for evaluation. The project supports two doctoral students and targets six journal publications over its four-year duration.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

Embron d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Toolchain Support for AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform Adoption in the Western Balkan Automotive Supply Chain
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AUTOCHAIN-AP addresses the limited readiness of small and medium-sized automotive suppliers in Hungary and Serbia to adopt the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. The Faculty of Technical Sciences leads the work package on toolchain adaptation, developing open-source Eclipse-based tools for service architecture modelling, SIM generation, and AP-specific consistency checking. The Hungarian partner contributes expertise in functional safety assessment. An associated training programme targets engineering staff at three participating supplier companies. The project includes a shared model repository and a joint evaluation campaign using industrial-grade AP reference implementations. Expected outputs include two open-source Eclipse plug-ins, four technical reports, and a practitioner training curriculum.
partners: Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen

projects.title: Contract-Based Integration Testing for Multi-Supplier CAN Networks in Small-Series Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CONTRACE addressed the integration testing burden faced by small-series manufacturers who assemble CAN-based control systems from components sourced from multiple suppliers. The project produced the CAN-CL contract language, the AutoCL synthesis tool and the CovBench-CAN benchmark suite. It validated these artefacts with three Serbian industrial partners producing agricultural equipment controllers and building-automation gateways. The project also developed training material used in a graduate course module on contract-based testing. Total budget was approximately 28 million RSD over 36 months. The project employed two doctoral students, both of whom completed their theses within the project period.
partners: AgroElektronika d.o.o., Subotica
ControlSoft d.o.o., Novi Sad
