projects.title: Embedded Software Dependability by Compositional Specification and Testing
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: EMBEDS was a bilateral research project between the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the Faculty of Automation and Computing at Politehnica University of Timișoara. The project focused on compositional verification and interaction testing for industrial embedded stacks, with a shared hardware-in-the-loop testbed operated jointly across the two sites via remote instrument access. Lačoková led the work package on combinatorial test generation and was responsible for integration of the timed automata checking toolchain developed in Timișoara with the CAN-CL framework. The project produced joint publications and established a student exchange mechanism that supported two short research visits per year.
partners: Faculty of Automation and Computing, Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Multilingual Document Digitization and Retrieval for the Cultural Heritage of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VOJDOC addressed the digitization, automated transcription, and full-text indexing of approximately 180,000 pages of multilingual archival material from Vojvodina covering the period 1880–1990. The project developed annotated training corpora for Latin, Cyrillic, and Hungarian scripts, adapted transformer-based HTR models to regional handwriting styles, and integrated the resulting pipeline into an open-access web portal operated by the Archive of Vojvodina. A search interface supporting simultaneous queries across all three scripts was delivered. The project produced the VojDoc-ML benchmark corpus and several peer-reviewed publications. Three doctoral students were funded through the project.
partners: Archive of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
National Library of Serbia, Belgrade

projects.title: Robust OCR and Key–Value Extraction for Small and Medium Enterprise Business Documents
projects.programme: Innovation Fund of Serbia
projects.summary: FORMREAD is an industry-oriented project in which the research team collaborates with a local document management software company to develop an OCR and information extraction module for SME business documents (invoices, delivery notes, customs forms). The project targets robustness to low-quality scan inputs and diverse typography. Deliverables include a fine-tuned TrOCR model adapted to Serbian business document typography, a key–value extraction component, and a REST API integrated into the partner's document management platform. Accuracy targets were set jointly with the industrial partner based on requirements from four pilot enterprises. The project also supports one master's thesis.
partners: DocFlow Solutions d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Dynamic and Robust Routing Optimisation for Urban Transport Operators
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DIROUTE addressed the gap between static route planning tools used by Serbian urban logistics operators and the dynamic conditions they face daily. The project developed a rolling-horizon dispatch engine that accepts real-time GPS feeds and demand updates, and tested it with data provided by two cooperating courier companies in Novi Sad and Subotica. The main research contributions were a stochastic demand model calibrated on six months of operational data, an adaptive replanning trigger policy, and a software prototype evaluated in a closed simulation environment. The project funded one PhD student and produced four journal papers. Final results were disseminated to the cooperating companies as a technical report with deployment recommendations.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
DostavaLogistika d.o.o., Novi Sad
Vojvodina Courier Services d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Cross-Border Freight Optimisation in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSFREIGHT investigates routing and scheduling challenges for goods flows crossing the Hungary–Serbia border at three main crossings. Gordana Lekić leads the work package on operational dispatch modelling, which develops multi-depot fleet assignment models that account for variable border waiting times as stochastic arc costs. The project collects border-crossing duration data from freight operators and integrates them with road network models on both sides. Partner universities contribute expertise in customs IT systems, freight demand modelling, and driver behaviour. Results are intended to inform policy recommendations for both national transport ministries and the participating logistics companies.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Data-Driven Prognosis Framework for Rotating Machinery in Process Industries
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PROGEN developed and validated a modular software framework for remaining useful life estimation of rotating machinery components—primarily bearings and gears—in pump, compressor, and gearbox applications. The project combined multivariate vibration and thermal feature extraction with a library of interchangeable prognosis model backends, including particle filters, Gaussian process regression, and LSTM networks. Experimental validation was conducted on purpose-built accelerated life test rigs at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and on instrumented equipment at two partner industrial sites in Vojvodina. The project produced open benchmark datasets for two failure modes, contributed to two journal publications, and trained three doctoral students. A lightweight deployable version of the framework was tested on embedded hardware at the end of the project period.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Fusion of Vibration and Infrared Thermography Data for Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Industrial Machinery
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: THERMOVIB addressed the diagnostic gap for machinery operating at shaft speeds below 100 rpm, where standard vibration-based fault indicators are unreliable. The project developed synchronised data acquisition protocols combining piezoelectric accelerometers and thermal cameras, and constructed fusion algorithms that exploited the complementary sensitivity of each modality to different fault types and severity levels. Field experiments were conducted at a grain handling facility and a river port conveyor installation in the Vojvodina region. The project delivered sensor placement guidelines, fusion algorithm code, and a practical handbook for maintenance engineers working with slow-speed conveyor and elevator machinery. Two master's theses and one conference paper resulted from the project.
partners: Žitopromet Vojvodina d.o.o., Zrenjanin, Serbia
Lučka Uprava Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Probabilistic Low-Flow Forecasting and Water-Balance Monitoring for the DTD Canal System
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to build an operational probabilistic forecasting system for low-flow events in the DTD canal network, targeting 7- to 30-day lead times. Work packages covered installation of an automated gauging station near Bečej, ensemble model development using four hydrological models combined with ECMWF NWP outputs, and a Bayesian model averaging combination layer. Forecast performance was evaluated against a three-year hindcast. A simplified decision-support tool was delivered to Vode Vojvodine for integration into their summer operational planning workflow. The project also funded graduate student involvement and three peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Vode Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia, Belgrade
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Hydrological Drought Indicators and Early Warning in Lowland Canal Networks of the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANNONDRY is a cross-border project coordinated by a Hungarian partner and addressing drought monitoring, indicator development, and early warning for canal-dependent agriculture in the Pannonian lowlands on both sides of the border. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on hydrological modelling, responsible for calibrating water-balance models for the Serbian canal network, producing climate-change scenario runs under EURO-CORDEX forcing, and developing a shared drought indicator database accessible to both national water authorities. The project also includes training workshops for water managers and a joint monitoring protocol for canal flow measurement.
partners: North Hungarian Water Directorate, Miskolc, Hungary
Vode Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Debrecen University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Hungary
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Consolidation and Volume Optimisation in Cross-Border Freight Flows: Models and Algorithms
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CONSOLVO addressed the operational inefficiency of consolidated freight movements across the Hungarian–Serbian border, focusing on road and rail corridors through Subotica and Horgoš. Đurić led the modelling work package, responsible for formulating integer programming models for joint load consolidation and border-crossing slot allocation under stochastic transit times. The project collected shipment data from three logistics operators and one rail freight company over 14 months. Deliverables included a validated optimisation prototype, a policy brief for customs authorities, and two peer-reviewed publications. The project brought together mathematicians, transport engineers, and economists from both sides of the border.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Stochastic Graph Optimisation Methods for Sustainable Regional Transport Planning
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STOGROPT investigates algorithmic foundations of stochastic optimisation on transport graphs with application to regional freight and public transit planning in Serbia. The project focuses on three interrelated problems: distributionally robust consolidation scheduling, periodic vehicle scheduling under demand variability, and hub location under uncertain flows. The research programme combines polyhedral analysis, decomposition algorithms, and simulation-based evaluation. A secondary objective is to construct a publicly available benchmark library of transport graph instances derived from anonymised Serbian logistics and transit data. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher at the Department of Mathematics and Informatics, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade

projects.title: Simulation-Optimisation Methods for Adaptive Warehouse Layout and Slotting Under Variable Demand
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WAROPT develops a computational framework that couples metaheuristic optimisation with discrete-event simulation to support adaptive layout and slotting decisions in warehouses facing non-stationary demand. The project addresses three problem classes: facility layout reconfiguration, dynamic storage assignment, and fleet sizing under demand uncertainty. Benchmark instances are drawn from partner companies in the agri-food and spare-parts distribution sectors in Vojvodina. The framework is implemented as a modular Python library with an AnyLogic simulation back-end. Expected outputs include validated algorithms, a publicly released benchmark dataset, and decision-support guidelines targeted at warehouse managers without advanced optimisation expertise. The project employs two junior researchers and supports two doctoral students.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Industrial Systems, Novi Sad
Logistika Panonija d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Logistics Efficiency in the Hungary–Serbia Corridor: Simulation and Process Improvement
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSS-LOG examined inefficiencies at freight terminals and border crossings along the Hungary–Serbia logistics corridor through process mapping, data collection, and simulation modelling. Jakovljević contributed simulation models of two Serbian-side cross-docking terminals and conducted bottleneck analyses for inbound and outbound flows at each site. The project produced a set of harmonised process templates for terminal operators in both countries, a comparative throughput analysis across six terminals, and a short course delivered to terminal managers on simulation-based planning. The project was coordinated by the University of Szeged and involved two Serbian and two Hungarian partners.

projects.title: Forecasting Support Infrastructure for E-Commerce SMEs in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FORESITE developed a shared forecasting infrastructure and methodology toolkit targeted at small and medium-sized e-commerce enterprises in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region that lack internal data science capacity. The project produced an open-source data preprocessing library, a model selection guide benchmarked on regional retail data, and a short-course training programme for analysts at participating companies. Three SME partners from Subotica and two from Pécs piloted the toolkit over twelve months, with forecast accuracy improvements documented across 140 product lines. The project also produced a comparative analysis of data quality practices across the partner companies and formulated minimum data collection standards for forecasting readiness.

projects.title: Machine Learning Pipelines for High-Variance Demand Series: Methods and Validation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DEMANDLAB investigates the robustness of machine learning forecasting pipelines when applied to retail and e-commerce demand series characterised by high variance, intermittency, and irregular promotional events. The project has three work streams: systematic benchmarking of decomposition-plus-regression architectures on a curated multi-retailer dataset; development of automatic covariate construction methods for settings without structured promotional logs; and an evaluation of recalibration methods for probabilistic forecasts under promotional uncertainty. Results are disseminated through open-access publications and a publicly available benchmark dataset compiled from anonymised partner retailer data. The project employs one postdoctoral researcher and supports two doctoral students.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Field-Based Shock Environment Characterisation for Protective Packaging Design in Southeast European Logistics Chains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project collected and analysed tri-axial shock and vibration data from instrumented parcels circulated through road distribution networks in Serbia, Romania, and Hungary. Data loggers were deployed in 120 test packages across four parcel weight classes over 18 months. The resulting empirical shock environment database was used to derive regionally specific design shock levels for three packaging performance tiers. A publicly available web tool was developed that allows packaging engineers to query design shock levels by route type, parcel weight, and acceptable damage rate. The database and tool are intended to supplement ISTA and ASTM test protocols, which do not adequately represent logistics conditions in Southeast Europe.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Bucharest, Romania
Institute for Packaging Technology, Subotica

projects.title: Mechanical Performance and Life-Cycle Assessment of Bio-Based and Recycled Foam Materials for Protective Packaging
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: GREENPAD evaluates five bio-based and recycled-content foam materials as substitutes for conventional EPS in protective packaging applications. The project combines mechanical characterisation (quasi-static and dynamic testing), finite element model development, and simplified life-cycle assessment to produce a comparative ranking of candidate materials. A key output is a material selection framework that balances cushioning performance, mass efficiency, moisture sensitivity, and end-of-life recyclability. Results are being validated with two regional packaging producers who supply corrugated and foam inserts to the electronics and small appliance sector. One PhD student and two master's students are enrolled on the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Packaging Research Centre, Novi Sad
EkoFoam d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Variable-Data Quality Assurance Systems for Distributed Digital Print Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between theoretical colour management standards and actual production practice in distributed variable-data printing operations. It developed and validated automated pre-flight and in-line quality monitoring tools for PDF/VT-based workflows operating across geographically separated print sites. The work included construction of a reference test corpus of variable-data jobs, development of a rule-based pre-flight engine extension, design of statistical process control protocols for digital press fleets, and a field study at three commercial print service providers in Vojvodina. Software tools developed within the project were released as open-source components. Two master theses and one PhD thesis were completed within the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Štamparija Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Network for Colour Standardisation in Printed Packaging and Publication
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project established a shared testing infrastructure and joint training programme for colour standardisation in print production across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project equipped a shared colour measurement laboratory at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and a partner facility at the University of Pécs. Joint workshops for print technologists from SMEs in both countries were held annually. The work package led by Ostojić covered workflow integration aspects, specifically pre-flight rule harmonisation and device profiling protocols applicable to both book publication and flexible packaging print production. A multilingual technical guidance document for SME adopters was produced as a key output.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology

projects.title: Dynamic Energy Modelling and Optimisation of Cold-Chain Transport Flows in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COLDFLOW brought together four partners from Serbia and Hungary to develop and validate dynamic thermal models of refrigerated road transport under Danube region climate conditions. The University of Novi Sad team led the modelling and experimental validation work package, contributing the Modelica TRU library and the instrumented trailer test data. Hungarian partners provided fleet telematics data and logistic network analysis. The project produced a freely downloadable simulation toolkit and a set of recommendations for fleet operators seeking to reduce TRU fuel consumption and refrigerant emissions. Two joint publications and one MSc thesis completed at the University of Novi Sad resulted from this collaboration.
partners: Department of Energy and Process Engineering, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Optimisation of Refrigeration Cycles for Low-GWP Refrigerants in Mobile Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REFOPTIM addresses the practical transition from high-GWP refrigerants to low-GWP alternatives in transport refrigeration, focusing on cycle-level adjustments required to maintain performance when R-404A is replaced by R-452A or R-454C. The project combines laboratory testing on the departmental refrigeration test rig with simulation-based parametric studies. Key tasks include compressor oil compatibility testing, expansion valve re-sizing guidelines, and discharge temperature safety assessment under extreme ambient conditions relevant to the Western Balkan region. A graduate student and a doctoral candidate are supported by the project. An industry advisory group comprising two Serbian refrigerated transport operators provides access to commercial vehicles for validation trials.
partners: Department of Energy and Process Engineering, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Automated Compliance Verification Tools for Cross-Border Road Freight in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project developed and validated software tools for automated checking of drivers' hours and working time compliance in cross-border freight operations involving Serbian carriers. The work addressed the specific regulatory context in which Serbian carriers operate simultaneously under domestic transport law and, on the EU leg of their routes, under EU regulations. A dataset of approximately 85,000 DDD files collected from 14 partner carriers was used for development and benchmarking. The project produced an open-source rule engine, a web-based reporting interface, and a set of annotated test cases for benchmarking alternative compliance checkers. Dissemination activities included workshops with Serbian transport inspection authorities and a training module for carrier compliance officers.

projects.title: Interoperable Logistics Regulation Data Exchange Along the Danube Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBELOG addresses the fragmentation of freight regulatory data along the Danube logistics corridor between Romania and Serbia, focusing on tachograph record exchange, border crossing documentation, and cabotage notification interoperability. Halász leads the work package on regulatory data standards, which is responsible for mapping existing national data formats against EU digital transport document standards and proposing a common data exchange schema. The work package produces a prototype API enabling Serbian and Romanian transport authorities to share enforcement-relevant data in near-real time. The project also includes a pilot deployment involving three logistics operators and two national inspection bodies.

projects.title: Fine-grained Refrigerated Supply Chain Observability across the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FRESCO addressed gaps in cold-chain monitoring infrastructure shared between Hungarian and Serbian food exporters operating cross-border transport. The project deployed a shared LoRaWAN gateway infrastructure along the M5/E75 corridor between Subotica and Kecskemét and developed a common data platform for thermal excursion reporting accessible to both Serbian and Hungarian competent authorities. Ivan Zec led the sensor network design and deployment work package, overseeing installation of 11 gateways and integration of 200 sensor nodes across 14 partner transport operators. The project produced a public dataset of 8 months of anonymised temperature and logistics event records, and a practical guide for SME transport operators on deploying compliant monitoring systems under EU and Serbian food safety legislation.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő

projects.title: Attributed Thermal and Logistics Anomaly Spatiotemporal Sensing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ATLASS developed methods for automatically attributing cold-chain temperature excursions to specific logistics events by fusing multi-point sensor data with transport management system records. The project built on prior feasibility work by implementing and validating probabilistic attribution algorithms, including the hidden Markov model approach, on a dataset spanning 18 months and over 300 transport routes in Vojvodina and along export corridors to Western Europe. Outcomes include an open-source Python library for excursion attribution, a labelled benchmark dataset for algorithm evaluation, and guidelines submitted to the Institute for Standardisation of Serbia for consideration in national cold-chain traceability standards. Three doctoral students were trained within the project.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Vision-Integrated Robotic Control for High-Speed Conveyor Sorting
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VIROCON addressed the gap between laboratory-grade machine vision results and reliable performance under the vibration, variable illumination and throughput demands of real production conveyor lines. The project built and instrumented a conveyor test platform with configurable roller spacing, variable-speed drives and interchangeable lighting rigs. Research tasks covered strobe-synchronised image acquisition, embedded CNN deployment on ARM and FPGA targets, closed-loop trajectory correction for a six-axis arm, and OPC-UA integration with a pilot MES. Four M.Sc. theses and one doctoral thesis were completed within the project. Partners provided access to two production facilities for field validation trials on pharmaceutical and food packaging lines.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Automation and Robotics, Belgrade
Pharmapack Solutions d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Embedded Recognition for Curved-Surface Code Reading in Recycling and Logistics
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: RECUSOR targets the specific problem of decoding 1D and 2D codes printed or embossed on non-planar packaging such as beverage cans, cosmetic tubes and plastic bottles, for use in automated recycling sorting and warehouse logistics. The project develops curvature-aware rectification algorithms, evaluates strobe duration and exposure trade-offs documented in companion experimental work, and assembles the open dataset described in the 2026 preprint. A demonstrator sorter cell using a Jetson-based classifier and a three-axis Cartesian gantry is being constructed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences lab. Collaboration with the Czech Technical University in Prague provides access to additional annotated image data from a European logistics operator.

projects.title: Dinamički modeli optimizacije za urbanu logistiku sa vremenski kritičnim replannigom
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat razvija skup algoritamskih metoda za rešavanje dinamičkih problema rutiranja vozila u gradskoj logistici, sa fokusom na hibridizaciju tačnih i heurističkih pristupa koji mogu da generišu prihvatljiva rešenja u roku od jedne do dve sekunde po narudžbini. Istraživanje obuhvata: (1) formulaciju i analizu vremenski kritičnih VRP varijanti sa ubacivanjem narudžbina, (2) razvoj benchmark skupova zasnovanih na anonimizovanim operativnim podacima, (3) implementaciju i vrednovanje hibridnih solvera na klaster infrastrukturi FTN-a. Planira se saradnja sa jednom distributivnom kompanijom iz Vojvodine radi validacije metoda na realnim tokovima podataka. Projektom su finansirana dva istraživačka stipendiste na doktorskim studijama.

projects.title: Cross-border Freight Optimisation for Small and Medium Enterprises in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSLOG aims to improve freight routing efficiency for small and medium logistics operators in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project collects route and order data from eight participating SME carriers, develops a shared optimisation platform with a web-based dispatcher interface, and provides training workshops. Emilija Vranješ leads Work Package 3, which covers the algorithmic core: dynamic routing models capable of handling cross-border regulatory constraints such as mandatory rest stops, customs clearance windows, and bilateral transport permits. Deliverables include a deployable routing engine and a public benchmark dataset representing cross-border delivery patterns in the region.

projects.title: Forecasting and Risk Estimation for Sparse Imbalanced Transactional Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FORESITE addressed the practical gap between probabilistic forecasting research and operational deployment in data-scarce or heavily imbalanced transactional settings. The project developed methods for temporal feature construction from categorical event histories, calibration-aware training under class imbalance, and distribution shift detection for scoring models in production. The work was validated on synthetic datasets calibrated to resemble retail banking, insurance, and logistics use cases. A secondary output was an open-source Python toolkit for practitioner-oriented probabilistic model evaluation. The project supported two doctoral students and resulted in five journal publications. Collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences and an industry advisory board drawn from regional financial-sector organisations informed the choice of research problems.

projects.title: Methods for Evaluation and Threshold Selection in Industrial Risk Classification
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: METRIX investigated evaluation metrics and operating-threshold selection procedures for binary classifiers deployed in industrial risk assessment contexts, including equipment fault detection and financial risk scoring. The project examined the sensitivity of common metrics—AUPRC, F-beta, G-mean—to label noise and class imbalance and proposed robust alternatives. Experimental work used synthetic datasets modelled on manufacturing sensor logs and transaction records provided in anonymised form by two partner organisations from the Novi Sad region. The project produced a methodological guide for industrial analysts and a conference tutorial delivered at BCAMI 2020. Two master's theses were completed under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
NTP Novi Sad – Technology Transfer Office

projects.title: Geospatial Data Infrastructure for Vojvodina: High-Density LiDAR Acquisition and Automated Feature Extraction
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project established a regional test dataset of airborne LiDAR strips covering 420 km² across five Vojvodina municipalities at densities between 6 and 12 points per square metre. Bošković led the work package on automated feature extraction, coordinating development of a modular processing pipeline for ground classification, building footprint extraction, and vegetation height mapping. The pipeline was validated against cadastral data and independent field measurements. Deliverables included processed raster products delivered to two municipal GIS offices and an open benchmark dataset released through the Faculty repository for use by other research groups. The project funded acquisition of an additional GPU node for the Faculty cluster.
partners: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, Vojvodina
Geodetic Institute of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
City Administration for Urban Planning, Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Domain Classification of Airborne LiDAR Data Using Adaptive Machine Learning
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CLASSAIR addresses the practical challenge of applying point cloud classification models trained on one airborne LiDAR dataset to surveys acquired with different sensors, flight altitudes, or seasonal conditions. The project develops domain adaptation methods based on feature distribution alignment and selective fine-tuning, and evaluates them on paired datasets from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. A secondary objective is to quantify how much target-domain labelled data is sufficient for reliable adaptation under different landscape types. The project funds two PhD student positions and includes a three-month research visit exchange with a partner institution in Vienna. Outputs include open-source adaptation tools, labelled benchmark datasets, and peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia
Department of Civil Engineering and Geodesy, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, TU Wien, Austria
Faculty of Geography, Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Cadastral Data Harmonisation and Transformation Infrastructure for the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CADASTRANS addressed technical barriers to sharing and comparing cadastral parcel data across the Hungary-Serbia border, with a focus on coordinate reference system alignment, attribute schema mediation, and topological quality assurance. The project produced a shared transformation grid for the border zone, a feature manipulation engine workflow for schema conversion between Hungarian and Serbian national formats, and a prototype cross-border data access service conforming to INSPIRE OGC WFS standards. Katarina Đorđević led the work package on data quality assessment and transformation infrastructure, supervising two research staff and one PhD student at the Novi Sad side. Outputs included four technical reports, two peer-reviewed papers, and a publicly accessible demonstration geoportal operated by the Vojvodina Institute for Nature Conservation as associated partner.
partners: Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Department of Cartography and Geoinformatics
Institute for Geodesy and Geoinformatics, University of Pécs
Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia, Novi Sad Regional Office
Vojvodina Institute for Nature Conservation

projects.title: Foundations for a 3D Subsurface Utility Cadastre in the Republic of Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SUBSURFACE3D is developing the methodological and technical foundations required for a future national 3D cadastre of subsurface utility infrastructure in Serbia. The project covers three main themes: harmonisation of heterogeneous data from utility operators into a unified 3D data model based on CityGML Utility Network ADE; quantification and modelling of depth uncertainty for utilities with incomplete as-built records; and assessment of legal and institutional preconditions for integrating 3D utility data into the formal Real Estate Cadastre. Fieldwork involves GPR surveys and GNSS-referenced direct measurement at exposed utility points in two pilot municipalities. The project team at Novi Sad consists of Đorđević and three researchers from geodesy and civil engineering. A stakeholder working group including the Serbian Geodetic Authority and four utility companies meets quarterly.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade
Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia

projects.title: Structural Performance of Cross-Laminated Timber Connections Under Combined Loading and Moisture Variation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates CLT connection behaviour under combinations of shear, tension, and bending that arise in real building platforms but are rarely studied in isolation in standard test programmes. The work plan includes 200 specimens across six connection types tested under monotonic, cyclic, and long-term loads, complemented by non-linear finite element models. A secondary strand examines how controlled moisture cycling modifies stiffness and residual strength. Deliverables include a design guidance document aligned with Eurocode 5, an open-access experimental database, and training activities for practising engineers in Vojvodina. The project is executed entirely within the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica with subcontracted timber fabrication.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Timber Trade and Processing Association of Vojvodina (invented)

projects.title: Timber Structural Systems for Low-Rise Buildings in Moderate Seismic Zones of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TIMSEIS brought together civil engineering faculties in Subotica and Pécs to develop design guidance for platform-frame glulam and CLT buildings in areas of moderate seismicity straddling the Hungarian–Serbian border. Ivona Marić led the work package on connection detailing and energy dissipation, coordinating cyclic racking tests on CLT wall specimens and compiling a comparative assessment of Serbian and Hungarian national seismic design practice against Eurocode 8 provisions. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) design manual and a two-day short course delivered to practitioners on both sides of the border.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs
Regional Development Agency Subotica-Bačka (invented)

projects.title: Vulnerability Assessment of Unreinforced Masonry Building Stock in Autonomous Province of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project supported systematic field survey and laboratory characterisation of the URM building stock across eight municipalities in Vojvodina. Activities included flat-jack campaigns, collection of construction-period documentation from municipal archives, and development of a regional building classification matrix. The project funded two research assistant positions and the procurement of additional flat-jack instrumentation. Outputs included the building typology database used in the 2022 cross-border exposure model and methodological groundwork for the Bayesian fragility updating procedure published in 2023. Collaboration with the Institute for Material Testing in Novi Sad was formalised through a cooperation agreement during the project period.
partners: Institute for Material Testing, Novi Sad
Municipal Civil Protection Office, Subotica
Municipal Civil Protection Office, Sombor

projects.title: Cross-Border Seismic Risk Model and Early Warning Protocols for the Hungary–Serbia Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSRISK is a transnational project developing harmonised seismic exposure and risk models for the Hungary–Serbia border region, combining Hungarian and Serbian datasets, hazard models, and civil protection protocols. Bálint leads the work package on building typology and fragility function development, contributing the Serbian-side survey data and the regional empirical fragility curves. The project involves joint field campaigns in both countries and training workshops for municipal civil protection staff on the use of RVS tools. The cross-border exposure model and the seismic risk dashboard described in the 2026 preprint are direct outputs of this work package. The project is scheduled to conclude with a joint civil protection exercise in the second half of 2024.
partners: Seismological Observatory, Hungarian Academy of Sciences
Department of Geophysics, Eötvös Loránd University

Civil Protection Directorate of Vojvodina

projects.title: Automated Roof Geometry Mapping for 3-D City Model Generation in Vojvodina Settlements
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project developed and validated an end-to-end pipeline for generating CityGML LoD2 models of municipalities in Vojvodina from existing cadastral footprints and low-density airborne LiDAR. Work covered roof type classification, parametric geometry generation, CityGML export, and a web-based dissemination portal for municipal users. The project produced the labelled Serbian roof dataset, the web API described in the 2022 journal paper, and pilot deployments in four municipalities. A technical handbook for municipal GIS officers was prepared and distributed through the Association of Municipalities of Vojvodina. The project employed two research assistants and involved close collaboration with the Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia.
partners: Urbanism Institute of Vojvodina
Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia
Computing Centre, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Parametric Libraries and Reconstruction Workflows for Historical Urban Morphologies in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HISTMORPH3D brought together three universities and two municipal planning offices to build a shared library of parametric building components representing historical urban typologies common across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project digitised and georeferenced cadastral archives from the 1880–1920 period in six towns on both sides of the border, constructed parametric typology models calibrated to these archives, and integrated the library into the LoD2 generation pipeline. A joint training programme for municipal GIS staff was delivered in Novi Sad and Szeged. The project also produced comparative morphological analyses examining similarities and divergences in urban development trajectories on either side of the border during the Austro-Hungarian period.

Csongrád-Csanád County Planning Office, Szeged

projects.title: Thermal Comfort Assessment and Green Infrastructure Planning for Climate-Resilient Urban Spaces in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed a shared methodological framework for outdoor thermal comfort assessment and green infrastructure planning applicable across Hungarian and Serbian municipalities along the Danube corridor. Đorđe Malešević led the work package on microclimate modelling, coordinating ENVI-met simulation campaigns for six pilot sites across the two countries and producing a joint calibration dataset from field measurements conducted in summer 2021. The project delivered a bilingual technical handbook for municipal practitioners, a geodatabase of thermal comfort indicators for the pilot sites, and a series of design guidelines for tree-planting and pavement material selection. Results were presented to planning departments in Novi Sad, Sombor, and Baja. Total project budget for the Serbian partner consortium was approximately 380,000 EUR.
partners: City of Novi Sad Urban Planning Institute
Faculty of Architecture, Budapest Metropolitan University
Municipality of Baja, Department of Environmental Management
Institute for Lowland Forestry and Environment, Novi Sad

projects.title: Solar Radiation Mapping and Rooftop Energy Potential Assessment for the Urban Area of Novi Sad
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project produced the first high-resolution solar irradiance map of the Novi Sad urban area based on airborne LiDAR-derived surface models and RADIANCE simulations. Đorđe Malešević served as principal investigator and coordinated collaboration between the Faculty of Technical Sciences and the City of Novi Sad GIS Centre. The team processed approximately 18 km² of point cloud data and validated simulation results against pyranometer measurements at six rooftop monitoring stations installed for the project. Outputs include an open geodatabase of annual rooftop irradiance, a report on technically viable photovoltaic capacity by urban district, and a Python-based processing toolkit released under an open-source licence. Total project value was 4.2 million RSD.
partners: City of Novi Sad GIS and Urban Data Centre
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Quantification and Correction of Datum Distortions for Cadastral Renewal in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project collected and harmonised benchmark coordinate data from four Vojvodina districts to characterise systematic distortions in the Serbian cadastral coordinate system. Field campaigns delivered 180 new GNSS-derived reference positions tied to ETRS89 via processing against AGROS and EUREF sites. A prototype correction grid covering approximately 8 000 km² was computed and tested in collaboration with the Provincial Geodetic Directorate. The project also produced a web-based tool allowing municipal geodetic offices to retrieve shift values for arbitrary coordinates within the covered area. Two master's theses were completed within the project, and results fed directly into the ongoing NTv2 grid estimation effort.
partners: Provincial Geodetic Directorate of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Municipal Cadastral Office of Zrenjanin

projects.title: Harmonised Geodetic Reference Frames for Cross-Border Spatial Planning in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BORDERFRAME brought together geodetic institutions from Serbia and Hungary to address coordinate inconsistencies that hamper joint spatial plans and environmental monitoring along the Danube border. Mihajlo Kovačević led the work package responsible for datum comparison and residual analysis, overseeing joint GNSS campaigns at 40 common control points and the development of a unified transformation procedure for the border corridor. Outputs included a technical protocol adopted by both national geodetic authorities for cross-border survey projects, a shared dataset of border-zone control coordinates released under open licence, and a training workshop attended by 34 practitioners from both countries.
partners: Institute of Geodesy, Cartography and Remote Sensing, Budapest
Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia, Belgrade
Provincial Geodetic Directorate of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Department of Geodesy and Surveying, Budapest University of Technology and Economics

projects.title: Automated Subsurface Utility Mapping Using Machine Learning on GPR Data for Municipal Infrastructure Management
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SUBMAP addressed the need for reliable, low-cost automated mapping of buried utilities in medium-sized Serbian municipalities where manual GPR interpretation is the dominant practice. The project developed an integrated software pipeline covering B-scan preprocessing, CNN-based hyperbola detection, multi-class object classification, and export to standard GIS formats compatible with municipal cadastral systems. Field validation surveys were conducted in three municipalities in Vojvodina totalling over 42 km of survey lines. The project produced an open dataset of 95 annotated GPR profiles, a public benchmark, and a prototype desktop application. Two MSc theses were completed under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
City Institute for Urban Planning and Construction, Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Geophysical Sensing for Joint Infrastructure Asset Management
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: GEOSENSE-CB brought together research groups and municipal partners from Vojvodina and southern Hungary to develop shared protocols for subsurface utility survey and data exchange across the border region. Milena Nedić led the work package on automated GPR data processing, contributing the hyperbola detection algorithms developed in SUBMAP and adapting them to the soil conditions and antenna configurations used by the Hungarian partner. The work package also produced a bilingual Serbian–Hungarian technical guideline document for municipal survey teams. Data collected during joint field campaigns in the Subotica–Szeged corridor formed a cross-border GPR benchmark dataset deposited in a shared repository.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
University of Szeged, Department of Geophysics
Municipal Public Utility Company Subotica

projects.title: Multi-Source Monitoring of Land Subsidence in Vojvodina: GNSS, InSAR and Borehole Integration
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established a coordinated monitoring framework for land subsidence across Vojvodina, combining long-term GNSS time-series analysis at 14 permanent stations with Sentinel-1 InSAR displacement maps and stratigraphic data from 37 deep boreholes maintained by the Geological Survey of Serbia. The primary objective was to separate anthropogenic subsidence (groundwater extraction, hydrocarbon production) from natural compaction and tectonic signals at spatial scales from individual fields to the provincial level. Rajić's group led the GNSS processing component and the data fusion methodology. A subsidence velocity map covering approximately 21,000 km² was produced with spatial resolution of 250 m. Results were shared with the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture and Water Management for use in flood-risk planning.
partners: Geological Survey of Serbia, Belgrade
Provincial Hydrometeorological Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Mining and Geology, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Vertical Land Motion along the Danube in Serbia and Romania: Joint GNSS and Levelling Analysis for Infrastructure Safety
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUVLM addressed the need for a consistent cross-border vertical motion dataset to support the safety assessment of Danube river infrastructure, including bridges, flood-protection embankments, and port facilities. The project deployed four new dual-frequency GNSS monuments at critical infrastructure sites near Drobeta-Turnu Severin and Negotin on the Romanian and Serbian banks respectively, and connected them to existing national CORS networks. Rajić led the work package responsible for GNSS data processing, velocity estimation, and uncertainty quantification. Levelling ties were performed by partnering geodetic agencies to provide an independent check. Final deliverables included a georeferenced velocity map and a technical report submitted to transport ministries of both countries.
partners: National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration, Timișoara Regional Office, Romania
Republic Geodetic Authority, Zaječar Branch Office, Serbia

projects.title: Hygrothermal Performance of Locally Sourced Bio-Based Wall Systems for Residential Buildings in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project characterised the hygrothermal properties of wall systems made from bio-based materials available in Vojvodina — hemp shiv, sunflower stalk, and corn cob aggregate — combined with lime and clay binders. Laboratory measurements covered sorption isotherms, vapour diffusion resistance, thermal conductivity, and capillary coefficients. Results were used to parameterise DELPHIN 6 models for typical Vojvodina residential wall assemblies, and risk maps for interstitial condensation and mould growth were produced for the regional climate. The project also delivered a publicly accessible material property database for the tested combinations and organised two training workshops for construction practitioners in the region.

Regional Housing Agency of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade

projects.title: Bio-Based Thermal Insulation Materials for Cross-Border Sustainable Housing
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between institutions in Serbia and Hungary aiming to develop and test bio-based insulation panels and render systems suitable for both new construction and retrofit of traditional rural housing stock in the border region. Ksenija Stojanović leads the work package on hygrothermal material characterisation and simulation, coordinating measurement activities across the two partner laboratories and ensuring comparability of test protocols. The project involves demonstration installations in two test houses, one on each side of the border, with continuous monitoring of interior climate and wall moisture conditions. A joint training module for construction students is also being developed.
partners: Department of Materials Engineering, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Architecture, University of Pécs, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Subotica, Serbia
Pécs County Construction Chamber, Hungary

projects.title: Recycled Aggregate Concrete for Reliable Precast Production in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the gap between laboratory characterisation of recycled aggregate concrete and the requirements of industrial precast production. It combines a structured experimental programme covering aggregate variability, ITZ microstructure, mechanical and durability properties, and probabilistic strength modelling with a case-study application at a precast facility in Vojvodina. The main output is a set of adapted mix design and quality control procedures that account for the additional variability introduced by recycled aggregates, formulated in a format compatible with existing EN production standards. The project involves three partner institutions and a precast manufacturer as an associated industrial partner.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Durability Assessment Methods for Recycled Aggregate Concrete Wall Panels in Central European Climate Zones
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DURAWALL brought together two Serbian and two Hungarian institutions to compare and cross-validate durability testing methods for recycled aggregate concrete under climate conditions representative of the Pannonian basin. Vera Zorić contributed to the work package on chloride transport testing, coordinating accelerated laboratory exposure trials and the harmonisation of test protocols between partner laboratories. The project produced a joint technical guideline document and a publicly available dataset of chloride diffusion coefficients for regionally sourced recycled aggregates. A stakeholder workshop was held in Subotica in 2022 to communicate results to regional precast producers.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

projects.title: Environmental Product Certification for Construction Products in Southeast Europe
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to harmonise EPD preparation practices between Hungarian and Serbian construction product manufacturers by developing a shared methodology guide, training programme, and pilot EPD dataset repository. Ristić led the work package responsible for life-cycle inventory data collection protocols and the adaptation of background datasets to reflect the energy infrastructure of both countries. The project produced 12 pilot EPDs across six product categories, a publicly available LCI dataset collection, and a bilingual practitioner manual. Training workshops were delivered to 34 industry representatives at partner institutions in Subotica and Pécs.

projects.title: Life-Cycle Inventory Data Infrastructure for the Building and Construction Sector in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: LCIBAL is building a publicly accessible LCI dataset library for energy-intensive construction material production processes in Serbia, with an initial focus on cement, brick, and precast concrete. The project involves primary data collection at eight manufacturing facilities, critically reviewed by an independent expert panel following ISO 14048 documentation requirements. Datasets will be formatted in EcoSpold2 and integrated into the openLCA Nexus platform. A secondary objective is to develop a data collection guideline document suitable for adoption by the Serbian standardisation body as a national annex to EN 15804. The project employs one postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Cost Transparency and Production Efficiency in Precast Concrete Manufacturing in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to improve cost transparency and production efficiency in small and medium precast concrete manufacturers operating across the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region. The Faculty of Technical Sciences Novi Sad led the work package on process measurement and cost modelling, conducting on-site value-stream mapping and TDABC model development at four partner companies—two in Serbia and two in Hungary. Outputs included a shared cost benchmarking database, a practitioner-oriented mapping toolkit translated into both Serbian and Hungarian, and two joint training workshops attended by 47 company representatives. A final comparative report on production performance indicators across the eight participating manufacturers was published and is publicly available.
partners: Betonelem Kft., Subotica

projects.title: Lean Production Methods for Construction Component Manufacturers: Barriers, Enablers and Transfer Mechanisms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: LEANCON investigates the preconditions under which lean production methods can be systematically transferred to small and medium construction component manufacturers in Serbia, with a focus on precast concrete and prefabricated steel component producers. The project combines survey methods, longitudinal case studies at three manufacturing sites, and simulation modelling to identify which lean tools produce measurable results in batch-variable, seasonally driven production environments. A particular focus is the development of adapted implementation roadmaps that account for the limited staff capacity and informal management structures typical of companies in the 20–80 employee range. The project has so far produced four journal articles, one conference paper, and a practitioner guide distributed through the Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Automated Scan-to-BIM Workflows for Road and Bridge Infrastructure Asset Management in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated automated pipelines for converting LiDAR point clouds of road and bridge infrastructure into georeferenced IFC models suitable for integration with municipal and national asset management databases. Work included algorithm development for feature extraction, a benchmarking campaign across 22 structures in Vojvodina and Šumadija, and a pilot deployment with a regional road authority. The project produced an open-source Python library for scan-to-BIM preprocessing and trained four PhD and MSc students. Results informed a draft technical guideline submitted to the Roads of Serbia public enterprise on minimum scan specifications for as-built BIM deliverables.

Roads of Vojvodina Public Enterprise

projects.title: Cross-Border 3D Infrastructure Data Standards and Capacity Building in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project addressing the lack of harmonised standards for 3D geodata in civil infrastructure documentation between Serbia and Hungary. Vlaisavljević leads the work package on LiDAR data acquisition standards and quality control, developing a joint protocol for airborne and mobile scanning campaigns that satisfies both Serbian geodetic legislation and Hungarian national BIM guidelines. The project includes joint training workshops, exchange visits for technical staff from road authorities on both sides of the border, and a shared online repository of annotated LiDAR test datasets for algorithm benchmarking. Two pilot corridors, one on each side of the border, are documented under the harmonised protocol.

projects.title: Optimised Cadastral Data Publishing Infrastructures for Western Balkan Pre-Accession Countries
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CADOPT addressed the technical gap between legacy cadastral land information systems in Serbia and Hungary's border region and modern INSPIRE-compliant web tile services. The project developed a reference pipeline covering topological error correction, coordinate precision normalisation, spatial grid partitioning, and incremental tile cache management. A shared test environment was established at the Faculty of Sciences in Novi Sad, hosting production-scale datasets from two Hungarian and three Serbian municipalities. Project outputs include open-source pipeline components, operator training materials, and a technical handbook for cadastral SDI administrators. The Serbian partner municipalities achieved full OGC WFS 2.0 compliance by project end.

projects.title: Vector Tile Rendering Performance Benchmarks for Serbian National Spatial Data Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VEKTOR-RS investigates rendering pipeline performance across the full national cadastral dataset of Serbia, comprising approximately 20 million parcels. The project benchmarks tile generation throughput, cache strategies, and client-side rendering across three JavaScript libraries, producing publicly available benchmark datasets and a methodology transferable to other national SDIs. A secondary focus is on incremental update latency for near-real-time cadastral change publication. Results are being integrated into a white paper submitted to the Republic Geodetic Authority to inform technology selection for the next generation of the national cadastral web portal. Two PhD students are funded under this project.

projects.title: Probabilistic Subsurface Characterisation of Alluvial Corridors for Flood Infrastructure Safety Assessment
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed geostatistical workflows for probabilistic characterisation of alluvial subsurface conditions along flood protection levees in the Vojvodina region. Field data collection involved 68 CPT soundings and 14 boreholes along three levee reaches. Sequential Gaussian simulation was used to generate ensembles of subsurface realisations, which were subsequently coupled with limit-equilibrium slope stability analysis to produce probabilistic levee failure curves. The project produced open-access datasets and a freely distributed Python toolbox for CPT-based geostatistical modelling. Collaboration with the Provincial Directorate for Water Management provided access to historical investigation archives. Results were disseminated to practitioners through two workshops held in Novi Sad and Sombor.

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Geotechnical Investigation Standards and Geostatistical Practice for Infrastructure Projects
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: GROUNDLINK addresses inconsistencies in geotechnical investigation and data interpretation practice between Serbia and Hungary, particularly for cross-border infrastructure such as road bridges and canal structures along the Tisa River. The project compiles a harmonised CPT and borehole database from both sides of the border, develops bilingual guidance documents for geostatistical interpolation in shared alluvial formations, and delivers joint training for practising geotechnical engineers. Nada Bulatović leads Work Package 3, covering geostatistical data analysis and uncertainty reporting. The project includes a pilot application to a planned pedestrian–cycle bridge over the Tisa near Horgoš. Expected outputs include a bilingual practitioner guide and a shared online geotechnical data portal.

projects.title: Adaptive Anomaly Detection Frameworks for High-Velocity Industrial Log Streams
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STREAMGUARD investigates adaptive unsupervised methods for detecting anomalies in log streams generated by industrial control and IT infrastructure, with a focus on handling concept drift and heterogeneous log sources in real time. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher. Work packages cover log parsing standardisation, streaming algorithm design, EVT-based threshold adaptation, and evaluation on datasets from regional industrial partners. Hardware procured under the project includes two GPU workstations and an expansion of the Kafka testbed. projects.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Log Analytics for Cross-Organisational Threat Intelligence

projects.title: Slavic Language Corpora for Cybersecurity Named-Entity Recognition
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SLCYNER addresses the shortage of annotated cybersecurity text in Serbian and neighbouring Slavic languages by building a suite of openly licensed corpora and evaluation benchmarks. The project collects data from national CERT advisories, security mailing lists, and translated vulnerability databases, producing annotated datasets for NER, temporal relation extraction, and event detection. A shared annotation platform developed within the project supports distributed annotation by security-domain experts. Secondary goals include releasing a domain-adapted language model for Serbian cybersecurity text and establishing evaluation protocols that allow direct comparison across Slavic languages. The project involves collaborators at the University of Zagreb and Sofia University, and an advisory board member from a domestic private cybersecurity firm.
partners: Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, University of Zagreb, Croatia
Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics, Sofia University, Bulgaria
InfoShield d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Bridging Structured and Unstructured Cyber Threat Intelligence for Small and Medium Enterprises in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CTIBRIDGE aims to lower the barrier for SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region to consume and act on cyber threat intelligence. The project combines NLP-based extraction of threat indicators from open sources with a lightweight structured knowledge graph tailored to the capacity of non-specialist security staff. Katalin Szabó leads the work package responsible for NLP pipeline development, covering IOC extraction, event linking, and summary generation in Serbian and Hungarian. The consortium also includes an SME association and a regional IT services company that provides real-world deployment scenarios and end-user evaluation. A publicly accessible demonstration portal is planned for the final project year.
partners: Pest County Enterprise Development Foundation, Hungary
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
NetGuard Solutions Kft., Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad

projects.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography for Hardware Security Modules in Critical Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the performance and security constraints of deploying post-quantum cryptographic algorithms on hardware security modules used in Serbian energy and transport infrastructure. Work packages cover algorithm selection and adaptation, FPGA and secure microcontroller implementation, side-channel and fault-injection evaluation, and a migration roadmap document targeting IEC 62443 compliance. The team collaborates with the RT-RK Institute in Novi Sad for industrial system integration testing. Outputs include an open benchmarking dataset, two software libraries released under an open-source licence, and a technical report delivered to the Serbian Ministry of Information and Telecommunications.
partners: RT-RK Institute for Computer Based Systems, Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of East Sarajevo
Informatika d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Securing Embedded Controllers in Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems Against Quantum-Capable Adversaries
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: SECURED-ICS is a 3-year Horizon Europe project bringing together eight partners from six countries to develop and validate a reference architecture for quantum-resistant security in industrial cyber-physical systems. Milica Nikolić leads Work Package 3, which covers hardware-level implementation and benchmarking of NIST-standardised post-quantum schemes on programmable logic controllers and remote terminal units. The work package produces a common evaluation board, a porting guide for firmware engineers, and a set of test vectors and timing datasets. Results feed into Work Package 5 on certification methodology. The project targets IEC 62443 and the forthcoming ETSI EN 303 645 annex on quantum-resistant requirements.
partners: TU Dresden, Germany
Politehnica University of Bucharest, Romania
