projects.title: Scalable Real-Time Certificate Status Query Resolution for High-Volume Distributed Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat SCALOCSP bavi se projektovanjem i evaluacijom arhitektura distribuiranih baza podataka prilagođenih zahtevima OCSP sistema koji opslužuju infrastrukture s više od pet miliona aktivnih sertifikata. Istraživanje obuhvata razvoj skalabilnih struktura podataka, strategija keširanja s formalnim granicama zastarelosti i tehnika particionisanja prilagođenih promenljivim stopama izdavanja sertifikata. Planiran je razvoj otvorenog referentnog okruženja za merenje performansi koje će biti dostupno istraživačkoj zajednici. Projekat uključuje partnerske institucije iz Srbije i Rumunije i predviđa obuku dva doktoranda.
partners: Departman za matematiku i informatiku, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Faculty of Automatic Control and Computers, Politehnica University of Bucharest, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Data Infrastructure for Trusted Digital Services in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSDATA ima za cilj uspostavljanje zajedničke istraživačke infrastrukture za testiranje distribuiranih sistema za upravljanje digitalnim identitetom i statusom sertifikata u prekograničnom kontekstu između Srbije i Mađarske. Andrea Malešević vodi radni paket posvećen dizajnu i evaluaciji baza podataka, uključujući WAN testiranje latencije i razvoj zajedničkih protokola za merenje performansi. Projekat predviđa organizaciju dve zajedničke letnje škole i razvoj otvorenih obrazovnih materijala na srpskom, mađarskom i engleskom jeziku.
partners: Departman za matematiku i informatiku, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Department of Computer Science, University of Pécs, Hungary
Naučno-tehnološki park Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermal Fatigue and Stress Accumulation in Encapsulant Materials for Harsh-Environment Electronics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how repeated thermal shock cycles between −40 °C and +130 °C cause progressive mechanical degradation in thermoset encapsulants used in automotive and industrial electronics. The core activities are: (1) experimental characterisation of stress relaxation and fracture toughness evolution with cycle count and ageing time; (2) development and validation of a viscoelastic FE model that incorporates cycle-dependent material parameter updates; (3) scanning acoustic microscopy mapping of delamination growth at die-attach and substrate interfaces. Partners include the Faculty of Engineering in Kragujevac and the Faculty of Electrical Engineering in Zagreb. The project funds two research assistants and covers equipment consumables and one international research visit per year.
partners: Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac, Serbia
Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, University of Zagreb, Croatia

projects.title: Graph-Based Attack Surface Management for Heterogeneous Enterprise and Industrial Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GRAPHSEC developed a unified framework for constructing, maintaining, and querying attack surface graphs that span both enterprise IT and operational technology network segments. The project produced an ontology for cross-domain vulnerability data normalisation, incremental graph-update algorithms validated on synthetic benchmarks, and a prototype scanning pipeline with Kubernetes awareness. Research outputs include six journal articles and four conference papers. The project also delivered an open-source toolchain released under the EUPL licence, and provided two industry partners from the Novi Sad technology sector with pilot assessments of their internal networks. Two doctoral students were trained under the project, one of whom defended in 2024.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Cerberus Systems d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Affordable Security Assessment Tools for Small and Medium Enterprises in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SECSME targeted the gap between enterprise-grade security tooling and the resources available to SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The Novi Sad team led the work package on automated vulnerability enumeration, adapting existing scanning pipelines to operate within the constrained network environments typical of small businesses. A lightweight deployment package was piloted at eight SMEs in Subotica, Szeged, and Novi Sad. The project also produced training materials and hosted two regional workshops attended by 140 participants in total. Assessment of the pilot sites revealed an average of 34 exploitable vulnerabilities per organisation prior to remediation guidance.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Szeged
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Csongrád-Csanád County

projects.title: Retraining Pathways for Adults in the Pannonian Region: Curriculum Models and Assessment Tools
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RETRAIN-AP addressed the shortage of portable, recognised retraining programmes for adults affected by industrial restructuring in the Vojvodina–Southern Great Plain cross-border region. The project brought together two universities, one regional development agency, and two vocational training centres. Tanja Simić led the work package responsible for developing and piloting competency-based curriculum templates and the corresponding assessment tools across four occupational domains. The project produced a shared curriculum repository of twelve retraining modules, a multilingual assessor training package, and a policy brief submitted to the relevant ministries in both countries. Approximately 340 adults participated in piloted programmes over the project period.
partners: Faculty of Education, University of Szeged, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina Nord, Subotica
Vocational Training Centre Novi Sad
South Transdanubia Training Institute, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Competency-Based Assessment Practices in Serbian Adult Technical Education
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: KOMPAS investigates the gap between formally declared competency-based assessment practices in Serbian adult technical education and the assessment instruments and grading behaviours actually used by trainers. The project combines a national survey of 120 accredited training centres, qualitative case studies in eight centres, and a randomised rubric-training intervention with trainer cohorts. Primary outcomes include a diagnostic instrument for assessing assessment quality in training centres, an evidence base on the factors that support or hinder consistent competency assessment, and a trainer development module. The project is hosted at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, with collaboration from the Institute for Educational Research in Belgrade.
partners: Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade
Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Incremental and Calibrated Anomaly Recognition for Operational SCADA Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ICAROS addressed the calibration and incremental update of unsupervised anomaly detectors deployed on live SCADA networks. The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data, incremental Gaussian mixture and autoencoder update algorithms suited to concept drift induced by planned process changes, and a set of evaluation protocols for comparing detectors across different ICS protocol environments. A labelled Modbus/TCP and DNP3 benchmark dataset was produced and released. Partners included a regional energy distributor that provided controlled access to a monitoring mirror port on an operational substation network, enabling validation under real traffic conditions. The project supported two doctoral candidates and produced nine peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Elektrodistribucija Bačka d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional regional energy distributor)
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Federated Anomaly Detection Across Distributed Industrial Control System Sites
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FEDICS developed federated learning protocols enabling anomaly detection models trained at geographically distributed ICS sites to be aggregated without exchanging raw network traffic. The project addressed privacy constraints common in critical infrastructure contexts and evaluated ensemble aggregation strategies for combining site-level one-class classifiers. Pilot deployments were conducted at two water utility control centres and two district heating substations across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project also produced a joint curriculum module on ICS cybersecurity delivered at partner universities. Key deliverables included open-source federated aggregation software, two datasets, and six joint publications by the consortium.
partners: Department of Automation and Applied Informatics, Budapest University of Technology
Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen
Vodovod Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional regional water utility)

projects.title: Secure and Authenticated Firmware Lifecycle Management for Low-Power Industrial Wireless Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат SAFELINK бави се дизајном, формалном анализом и практичном имплементацијом протокола за управљање животним циклусом фирмвера у индустријским бежичним мрежама са малом потрошњом енергије. Обухвата три главна правца: развој протокола за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера усклађених са ограничењима LPWAN технологија, процену примењивости пост-квантних потписних схема на уређајима класе 1 и класе 2, и методологију за верификацију усклађености са индустријским безбедносним стандардима. Пројекат укључује лабораторијско тестирање на тестбеду са 40 чворова и сарадњу са два партнерска универзитета из региона. Планирани резултати укључују шест журналских радова, отворени репозиторијум имплементације протокола и нацрт техничке препоруке за индустријске кориснике.
partners: Електротехнички факултет, Универзитет у Београду
Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, University of Zagreb

projects.title: Cross-Border Deployment of Secure LPWAN Telemetry Infrastructure for Environmental and Industrial Monitoring
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANS-LPWAN је прекогранични пројекат који развија заједничку инфраструктуру за телеметријски мониторинг животне средине и индустријских постројења у пограничном подручју Србије и Мађарске. Главни технички допринос тима са Факултета техничких наука односи се на безбедносни слој: дефинисање протокола за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера на уређајима расположеним дуж прекограничних руских обала Тисе, управљање кључевима у административно хетерогеном окружењу са два различита национална оператора мреже, и успостављање процедуре за безбедну даљинску надоградњу уређаја без физичког приступа. Пројекат подразумева пилот-инсталацију на 35 теренских чворова.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
ЈВП Воде Војводине, Нови Сад
Tiszamenti Vízügyi Igazgatóság, Szolnok, Hungary

projects.title: Quantitative Cyber Risk Models for Financial Institutions in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a suite of calibrated frequency–severity models for cyber operational risk specific to the Western Balkans financial sector, where publicly available loss data are scarce and internal bank databases are small. Activities included collection of anonymised loss data from six participating banks under a data-sharing protocol approved by the National Bank of Serbia, development of a Bayesian LDA toolbox implemented in R, and delivery of three training workshops for bank risk managers. The project produced six journal papers, two conference contributions, and an open-access R package (CyLDA) deposited on GitHub. A policy brief was submitted to the National Bank of Serbia recommending adoption of a standardised loss data taxonomy compatible with ORX and the forthcoming DORA framework.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Kragujevac
Vojvođanska bančarska asocijacija (fictional banking association, Novi Sad)

projects.title: Cross-Border Operational Risk Data Infrastructure for SMEs in the Subotica–Pécs Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project builds a shared operational risk data collection infrastructure for SMEs in the Subotica–Pécs corridor. The project collects standardised cyber and fraud incident reports from approximately 200 SMEs on both sides of the border, develops a joint anonymisation and pooling protocol, and constructs baseline actuarial models for frequency and severity by sector. Bálint leads Work Package 3, responsible for statistical model development and validation. Outputs include a bilingual (Hungarian–Serbian) self-assessment tool for SME cyber risk, a joint academic report, and a prototype data portal accessible to registered SME participants. The project addresses the absence of credible loss data for non-financial SMEs, which is the primary barrier to affordable cyber insurance in the region.
partners: Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica (fictional)
Pécs Innovation and Enterprise Centre (fictional)

projects.title: Formal Regression Methods for Testing Embedded Control Firmware
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a coherent toolchain for specification-driven regression testing of embedded firmware, covering model authoring in a constrained EFA dialect, automated test case generation, hardware-in-the-loop execution adapters for STM32 and NXP platforms, and mutation-based suite adequacy assessment. Research activities included empirical studies on maintenance cost across firmware release histories and the development of the SpecMutate framework. The project funded two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher and resulted in six peer-reviewed publications. Dissemination included a publicly released open-source toolchain prototype and a two-day industrial workshop held in Novi Sad attended by engineers from three regional firms.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Test Oracle Synthesis from Temporal Specifications
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral collaboration with Instituto Superior Técnico, Lisbon, focusing on the automated construction of test oracles for HIL test environments using Signal Temporal Logic. The project combined expertise in temporal logic parameter synthesis from the Lisbon group with embedded testing infrastructure in Novi Sad. Joint work produced the STL oracle mining approach published in a journal article and a shared experimental dataset of motor control and temperature regulation firmware traces. Researcher exchanges included two short-term visits to Lisbon and one visit to Novi Sad by Portuguese collaborators.
partners: INESC-ID, Instituto Superior Técnico, Lisbon, Portugal

projects.title: Rule-Driven Parametric Artwork-to-Structure Registration for Sustainable Folding-Carton Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PACKRULE addressed the gap between structural dieline design and graphic artwork placement in folding-carton production, where manual registration adjustments account for a disproportionate share of make-ready time and material waste. The project built a rule engine that reads a structural dieline in CFF2 format, extracts registered feature positions (score lines, cut edges, window apertures), and automatically constrains artwork element positions in a linked PDF document. Registration correction rules were derived from a database of 1,800 production runs covering four board grades and three printing processes. The project produced a validated software prototype, three journal papers, and two master's theses. One regional packaging converter participated as an industry observer and provided production data under a non-disclosure agreement.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University Timișoara, Romania (associated partner)

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Color-Managed Packaging Prepress: Curriculum and Laboratory Development
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project supported the development of shared teaching materials and laboratory protocols in color-managed prepress between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs. Ildikó Papp led the work package responsible for harmonizing laboratory measurement procedures and developing a joint practical course module on ICC profile construction and verification. The project equipped both partner laboratories with matching measurement devices to enable reproducible inter-laboratory comparisons and produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) practical handbook distributed to over 140 students across both institutions during the project period. A joint summer school held in Novi Sad in 2020 attracted 38 participants from four countries.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Media Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Colour Accuracy and Substrate Adaptability in Sustainable Packaging Reproduction
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the growing complexity of colour management in packaging reproduction caused by the transition to environmentally certified substrates including recycled board, bio-based films, and water-based inks. Existing ICC characterisation standards were developed for conventional fossil-based substrates and perform inconsistently on recycled or coated-with-barrier materials. The project built characterisation data sets for twelve packaging substrates, developed correction models for optical brightener and batch variation effects, and produced an open spectral measurement dataset for the Serbian packaging sector. A set of measurement protocol guidelines was submitted to the Serbian Institute for Standardisation as a contribution to national technical committee work on colour in packaging. Two early-career researchers completed their master's theses within the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Niš, Serbia
Štamparija Budućnost d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner)

projects.title: Spectrophotometric Colour Control Methods for Digitally Printed Functional Textiles
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project brought together textile engineering and graphic engineering expertise from institutions on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border to develop colour control methods for digitally printed textiles intended for sportswear and medical applications. Kristina Erić led the work package on spectrophotometric characterisation, responsible for establishing measurement protocols on textile surfaces, building ICC profiles for reactive and sublimation inkjet processes, and validating gamut mapping approaches for brand-colour reproduction on fabric. The project produced a shared measurement database of 28 textile substrate–ink system combinations and a set of training materials distributed to SMEs in both countries. Results informed a subsequent bilateral cooperation between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs.
partners: Department of Graphic Engineering and Design, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Applied Arts and Design, University of Pécs, Hungary
Tekstil Vojvodina d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia
Printex-Color Kft., Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Semantic Embeddings for Regional Audio Content Metadata in Low-Resource Languages
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat SERACOM istražuje primenu semantičkih ugrađivanja za automatsku obradu i klasifikaciju metapodataka audio sadržaja na jezicima sa ograničenim resursima, pre svega na srpskom, mađarskom i rumunskom. Aktivnosti obuhvataju izgradnju anotiranih skupova podataka, razvoj metoda cross-lingvalnog prenosa znanja i evaluaciju preporučivačkih sistema u saradnji sa regionalnim distributerima sadržaja. Projektni tim broji pet istraživača, a posebna pažnja poklonjena je primenljivosti rezultata u malim i srednjim preduzećima koja upravljaju digitalnim katalozima. Finansiran iz programa IDEAS Fonda za nauku Republike Srbije.
partners: Departman za matematiku i informatiku, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, West University of Timișoara, Romania
Department of Informatics, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Cross-Border Digital Archive Interoperability through Semantic Metadata Harmonisation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSARCH za cilj ima unapređenje interoperabilnosti digitalnih arhiva audio i audiovizuelnih sadržaja u pograničnom regionu Srbije i Rumunije harmonizacijom metapodatkovnih šema i uvođenjem zajedničkih semantičkih modela. Zahorecová vodi radni paket posvećen razvoju metoda automatskog mapiranja između različitih šema opisa sadržaja, koristeći tehnike ugrađivanja teksta. Planirani rezultati uključuju zajednički semantički repozitorijum sa 50 000 anotiranih stavki i prototip alata za interoperabilnost dostupnog javnim arhivima. Projekat uključuje partnere iz bibliotečko-informacijske i audiovizuelne oblasti.
partners: Departman za matematiku i informatiku, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Digital Heritage Centre Timișoara (fiktivna organizacija)
Gradska biblioteka Novi Sad (fiktivna organizacija)
Romanian Audiovisual Archive Foundation (fiktivna organizacija)

projects.title: Digital Media Inventory Pricing in Transitional Advertising Markets: Conjoint and Hedonic Approaches
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates price formation mechanisms for digital display and video advertising inventory in Serbia and neighbouring markets, where programmatic auction data are limited and rate card pricing remains prevalent. The research combines CBC experiments with media buyers, hedonic regression on transaction datasets obtained through data agreements with regional ad-tech operators, and simulation modelling of floor price strategies. Deliverables include a publicly available R package for publisher-side conjoint pricing audits, three peer-reviewed journal papers, and a practitioner guide distributed through the Serbian Association of Digital Publishers. The project also supports two PhD candidates working on related dissertation topics.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Serbian Association of Digital Publishers
Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Advertising Valuation Benchmarks for Central and Eastern European Digital Media Markets
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral research collaboration between the Faculty of Economics in Subotica (University of Novi Sad) and the Faculty of Commerce at the University of Economics in Bratislava, this project developed harmonised conjoint survey instruments and hedonic regression benchmarks applicable across the Serbian and Slovak digital advertising markets. Joint fieldwork recruited matched samples of media buyers in both countries, enabling cross-market comparisons of attribute importance weights for programmatic inventory. The project produced two co-authored journal papers, a shared dataset archived at both institutions, and a working methodology document used in subsequent national-level funding applications.
partners: Faculty of Commerce, University of Economics in Bratislava, Slovakia

projects.title: Dialogue Restoration Tools for Regional Independent Film and Broadcast Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DIALREST addressed the practical gap between published noise reduction algorithms and tools accessible to low-budget Serbian and regional independent film and broadcast producers who lack access to expensive proprietary software. The project developed and tested open-source spectral noise reduction components calibrated on location-audio data gathered from Serbian independent productions. An extended version of the NovSAD-Loc corpus was produced, doubling the corpus size and adding annotations for reverberation conditions. Evaluation involved practitioner listening panels recruited through the Independent Producers Association of Vojvodina. The project delivered a documented open-source processing library and a set of calibration guidelines distributed via the Academy of Arts online platform.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Independent Producers Association of Vojvodina
Faculty of Dramatic Arts, University of Arts Belgrade

projects.title: Accessible Sound in Broadcast Drama for Hearing-Impaired Audiences in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SONACCES investigates how broadcast drama audio post-production practices affect intelligibility for hearing-impaired viewers in Hungary and Serbia, where subtitling coverage and audio description services remain uneven. Valentina Milić leads the work package on signal processing evaluation, coordinating collection of test material and listening test protocols across both countries. The project brings together audiologists, broadcast engineers, and post-production educators. Expected outcomes include recommendations for noise reduction intensity limits compatible with common hearing-aid processing chains, a training module for broadcast post-production students, and a joint position paper submitted to national broadcast regulators. The work builds directly on the pilot study conducted in 2024.
partners: Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Audiology Department
Hungarian National Broadcast Training Centre, Budapest
Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Bilingual Learner Error Detection Technologies for Minority-Language Educational Settings in Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BILEDTECH aims to develop and evaluate computational tools for detecting and explaining morphosyntactic errors in bilingual school contexts along the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project combines corpus expansion, model development, and classroom pilot studies across eight partner schools. Activities include: extending the SHLC corpus by 400,000 tokens of new spoken and written data; fine-tuning multilingual NLP models for error detection; developing the GrEDSH teacher tool; and running structured teacher-training workshops. Evaluation follows a pre–post design with control and intervention schools. Outputs include the expanded corpus (open access), the GrEDSH tool (open source), a practical teacher handbook available in Serbian and Hungarian, and at least four peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Hungarian Language Teacher Training Faculty, University of Novi Sad, Subotica
Eszterházy Károly Catholic University, Eger, Hungary
Regional Centre for Professional Development of Educators Novi Sad
Civic Association for Minority Language Education Subotica

projects.title: Corpus and Computational Study of Code-Switching in Vojvodina: Patterns, Constraints, and NLP Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: COSWICH funded the sociolinguistic data collection and initial computational modelling reported in the 2021 journal paper and the 2023 conference paper on transformer adaptation. The project collected 312,000 tokens of informal written and 96,000 tokens of spoken code-switched data, developed annotation guidelines, and trained two research assistants in corpus annotation. It also supported a three-month visiting research stay by a collaborator from Budapest. The project produced three publications, one shared dataset deposited in the CLARIN.SI repository, and a public online demonstration of the language-identification component.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Research Institute for Linguistics, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Social-Media Temporal Dynamics and Content Scheduling for SMEs in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SOCTIME investigated how small and medium enterprises on both sides of the Hungarian-Serbian border could improve organic social-media reach through data-driven scheduling. The project collected longitudinal engagement data from 140 SME accounts, developed a set of open-source Python tools for time-series diagnostics and posting-window recommendation, and ran two cohorts of practitioner training workshops in Novi Sad and Subotica. A cross-border benchmark report comparing engagement norms by sector and account size was produced for public download. The project also generated a shared anonymised dataset made available to academic partners for further research.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina
Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs
Regional Enterprise Development Agency Csongrád-Csanád

projects.title: Audience Behaviour Segmentation Methods for Digital Content Platforms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AUDSEG develops and validates machine-learning segmentation methods for digital content platforms operating in small language markets. The project focuses on situations where platform operators have access to longitudinal behavioural logs but limited personal data due to privacy constraints. Work packages cover: (1) evaluation of clustering stability under data sparsity, (2) development of temporal encoder architectures suitable for medium-scale platforms (100,000–2,000,000 registered users), (3) field validation with two partner platforms, and (4) a policy brief on privacy-preserving audience analytics. The project funds two PhD students and supports a six-month research exchange with a partner group in Ljubljana.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Economics, University of Ljubljana

projects.title: Sequential Bayesian Testing Methods for Digital Experiments with Sparse Traffic
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project develops a coherent family of Bayesian sequential testing procedures tailored to digital experiments where daily traffic per experimental arm is below 500 observations. The work covers three main axes: theoretical analysis of stopping rule properties (type I error, power, expected duration) under conjugate and non-conjugate models; development of an open-source R package implementing the procedures with diagnostic tools; and an applied study in collaboration with two technology companies located at NTP Novi Sad. The project employs two researchers and funds one doctoral student. Deliverables include peer-reviewed publications, the software package, and a short practitioner's guide targeting product analysts without a statistics background.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Orbis Analytics d.o.o., Novi Sad
Lumiq Software d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptive Statistical Methods for Small-Sample Industrial Quality Control
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs addressing the problem of statistical quality control in small-batch manufacturing, common in both regions. Kuzmanović led the work package on adaptive sampling plans, applying multi-armed bandit concepts to inspection lot sequencing. The project produced jointly authored publications, exchange visits for doctoral students, and a workshop series for manufacturing SMEs in the Vojvodina and Southern Transdanubia regions. The adaptive sampling plans developed were piloted at two partner manufacturing companies, reducing average inspection sample sizes by approximately 20% without increasing defect escape rates.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Statistics, University of Pécs
Metalform Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad
Precíziós Alkatrész Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Scalable Clustering Methods for Interaction Log Streams in Enterprise Software Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated scalable unsupervised clustering methods suited to interaction-log data generated continuously in enterprise software environments. The main objectives were: (1) to benchmark existing clustering algorithms on log datasets of varying scale and structure, (2) to develop and test a grid-based spatial aggregation preprocessing step that reduces data volume without significant loss of cluster quality, and (3) to produce open-source tooling for the full pipeline from raw log ingestion to cluster reporting. The project involved researchers from the Faculty of Sciences in Novi Sad and a collaborating group at the Politehnica University of Bucharest. Two journal papers and one conference paper were produced, along with a publicly released Python library. Four master's students participated in project activities.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Automatic Control and Computers, Politehnica University of Bucharest, Romania

projects.title: Digital Work Behaviour Monitoring and Profiling in Cross-Border SME Contexts
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DIGIWORK examined how small and medium enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region could benefit from structured analysis of employee interaction logs for workflow optimisation and training needs assessment, while respecting privacy constraints. Lalić led the data analysis work package, responsible for designing the anonymisation pipeline and the unsupervised profiling methods applied to log data collected from partner SMEs. The project produced anonymisation guidelines, a clustering-based profiling dashboard prototype, and a set of policy recommendations for SMEs. Fieldwork involved four companies in Subotica and two in Pécs. The collaboration also produced a jointly supervised master's thesis between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Information Systems, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad
South Transdanubia Regional Innovation Agency, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Sentiment Resources and Disambiguation Tools for Contemporary Serbian Journalistic Corpora
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SentiSrpKor aimed to produce a suite of reusable resources for sentiment-oriented text analysis in Serbian: an expanded and genre-balanced news corpus of 500,000 annotated sentences, a reconciled sentiment lexicon covering 18,000 lemmas, and a benchmarked disambiguation pipeline. The project involved teams from the Faculty of Philosophy and the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad, with an advisory contribution from a computational linguistics group in Ljubljana. Deliverables include the SentiNoviSad-News 2.0 corpus, released under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence, and two open-source Python modules for preprocessing and classification of Serbian news text. The project supported one doctoral student and funded participation in four international conferences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Slovenian Studies, Faculty of Arts, University of Ljubljana

projects.title: Sensor-Driven Adaptive Display Infrastructures for Smart Public Spaces
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the full stack from raw sensor data acquisition through middleware integration to adaptive content rendering on public display networks. Work packages covered: (1) a reference middleware architecture for heterogeneous sensor-to-display pipelines, (2) a declarative scheduling language and its compiler toolchain, (3) field deployments in two public-sector buildings in Novi Sad. The project operated a testbed with 55 heterogeneous sensors and a 12-panel signage installation. Three journal papers and four conference papers were produced. Two master's students completed theses within the project. Collaboration with the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, provided occupancy ground-truth data from a lecture-hall monitoring sub-study.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Smart Environment Monitoring and Visualisation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project establishing shared IoT monitoring infrastructure covering air quality, noise, and pedestrian flow at six public sites in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. Sredojević led the work package on data integration and visualisation, responsible for deploying federated MQTT broker infrastructure, designing a unified data model for cross-border sensor interoperability, and building a web-based public dashboard. Her team at FTS contributed the broker federation software, configuration tooling, and real-time anomaly filtering components. The dashboard served live data to an average of 340 daily visitors during the final operational year. Results informed local environmental management decisions at two participating municipalities.
partners: City of Subotica Environmental Inspectorate
University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences, Hungary
Regional Environmental Agency Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Trust in Media Across the Western Balkans: Longitudinal and Comparative Perspectives
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TRUSTMED-WB coordinated a comparative longitudinal study of media trust in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia using harmonised survey instruments administered annually from 2020 to 2023. The project produced a shared dataset of approximately 4,500 respondents per wave, allowing cross-country and within-country cohort comparisons. Research activities included content analysis of 15 outlets across the three countries, a series of framing experiments, and methodological workshops on panel design for small media markets. Outputs include four journal articles, a comparative report distributed to public broadcasting councils in all three countries, and a teaching module on audience research methods.
partners: Faculty of Political Sciences, University of Sarajevo
Institute for Sociological, Political and Juridical Research, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Framing Dynamics and Misinformation Checkpoints: Automated Detection Tools for Serbian-Language News
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: FRAMCHECK developed and validated a hybrid pipeline for detecting dominant news frames and potential misinformation markers in Serbian-language online news. The project combined an NLP preprocessing module adapted for Serbian morphology with a supervised frame classifier trained on a manually annotated corpus of 6,000 articles. A secondary strand produced an updated version of the Vojvodina Audience Panel questionnaire to include items on misinformation recognition and algorithmic awareness. Results were shared with two regional fact-checking organisations and with the journalism faculty at Novi Sad to inform curriculum updates.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Regional Media Literacy Centre Novi Sad (invented NGO)

projects.title: Cross-Lingual Alignment of Legal Corpora for Automated Compliance Checking in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi razvijanjem metoda za automatsko uparivanje i semantičko poravnavanje pravnih normi između zakonodavnih sistema Srbije, Severne Makedonije i Bosne i Hercegovine, sa ciljem olakšavanja usklađivanja sa EU propisima. Istraživački tim gradi višejezični paralelni korpus od najmanje 50.000 normativnih paragrafa i razvija model semantičke sličnosti koji uzima u obzir pravne sisteme specifičnih jurisdikcija. Pored toga, istražuju se metode detekcije anomalija za identifikaciju normi koje su u direktnom sukobu između jurisdikcija. Praktični ishod je softverski prototip dostupan pravosudnim ministarstvima partnerskih zemalja.
partners: Pravni fakultet Univerziteta u Novom Sadu
Fakultet za pravne i poslovne studije dr Lazar Vrkatić, Novi Sad

projects.title: Text-Based Automated Compliance Monitoring for SMEs in the Energy and Finance Sectors
projects.programme: Innovation Fund of Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat razvija prototip SaaS alata koji malim i srednjim preduzećima u energetskom i finansijskom sektoru omogućuje automatsku provjeru usklađenosti internih dokumenata sa relevantnim zakonskim propisima. Tehničko jezgro čini model semantičke sličnosti treniran kontrastivnim učenjem, nadopunjen modulom za detekciju out-of-distribution dokumenata. Sistem je integrisan sa pretragom pravnih baza podataka putem API-ja i prezentuje rezultate kroz veb interfejs sa objašnjenjima na nivou rečenice. U projektu učestvuju dva privredna partnera koji obezbeđuju realne testne dokumente i učestvuju u evaluaciji prototipa u produkcijskim uslovima.
partners: NTP Novi Sad – portfolio kompanija RegTech Solutions d.o.o. (fiktivna)
Energodata Consulting d.o.o., Novi Sad (fiktivna)

projects.title: Vojvodina Language Resources: Computational Infrastructure for Minority Languages in a Multilingual Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VoiLaRes aims to build a coordinated set of computational language resources—lexicons, annotated corpora, and baseline NLP tools—for the four official minority languages of Vojvodina: Hungarian, Slovak, Pannonian Rusyn, and Romanian. The project involves linguists from three Novi Sad institutions and one partner from Timișoara. Core outputs include morphological lexicons for Rusyn and Slovak adapted for computational use, a 250,000-token multi-genre corpus for each language with part-of-speech annotation, and a publicly accessible web interface for corpus search. The project also develops annotation guidelines that are deliberately cross-compatible with those used for Serbian, allowing future cross-lingual experiments. All resources are deposited in the CLARIN infrastructure under open licences.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Morphology as a Bridge: Transfer Learning Across South Slavic and Finno-Ugric Language Families
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MorphBridge is a cross-border research and capacity-building project bringing together linguists and NLP researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest to study whether shared morphological feature spaces can systematically improve transfer learning between Serbian and Hungarian. The project constructs parallel annotated data sets in both languages across three domains (legal, medical, and news), runs a series of controlled transfer learning experiments comparing feature-based and representation-based transfer methods, and organises two joint summer schools for doctoral students from both sides of the border. Đurđica Kuzmanović leads the work package on data collection and annotation methodology. Project outputs include shared model checkpoints, a jointly authored technical report for language policy stakeholders, and course materials for the summer schools.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Mixed-Script Information Retrieval for South Slavic Administrative and Legal Documents
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat MixIR bavio se izgradnjom pretražnih sistema prilagođenih srpskim administrativnim i pravnim dokumentima koji sadrže mešovito pismo. Cilj je bio razvoj metodoloških osnova i softverskih alata za normalizaciju pisma, transliteraciju i rangiranje koji se mogu primeniti u javnom sektoru. U okviru projekta izgrađen je anotiran korpus od 150 000 dokumenata, razvijen je open-source modul za normalizaciju pisma kompatibilan s popularnim okvirima za pretragu, i sprovedene su tri pilot implementacije u saradnji s jednom opštinskom upravom i jednim regionalnim sudom. Rezultati su objavljeni u sedam naučnih radova i prezentovani na tri međunarodne konferencije.
partners: Pravni fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Opštinska uprava Novi Sad — Služba za informatiku
Viši sud u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Serbian–Romanian Cross-Language Information Retrieval with Script and Morphology Normalization
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat SERIR istražuje višejezičnu pretragu između srpskog i rumunskog, s posebnim fokusom na dokumentima pogranične administracije koji se čuvaju u oba jezika i, na srpskoj strani, u oba pisma. Stefan Dragić rukovodi radnim paketom koji pokriva normalizaciju skripte i transliteraciju na srpskoj strani, dok partnerski tim iz Temišvara razvija morfološku normalizaciju za rumunski. Zajednički test korpus sadrži 40 000 dokumenata u četiri žanra. Projektom se finansiraju dva doktoranda i jedno postdoktorsko istraživačko mesto.
partners: Departman za matematiku i informatiku, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Facultatea de Informatică, Universitatea de Vest din Timișoara

projects.title: Interoperable HR Workflow Components for Small and Medium Enterprises in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate a library of reusable, interoperable HR workflow components—covering recruitment, onboarding, performance review, and payroll exception handling—for SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. Components were specified in BPMN 2.0 and packaged with localisation layers for Hungarian and Serbian legal contexts. Five SMEs from each country participated as pilot sites. The project produced a publicly accessible component repository, a deployment guide, and a training curriculum delivered to 48 HR and IT practitioners across both countries. Vasić led the Serbian technical team and coordinated overall project reporting.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Business and Economics, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina, Serbia
Chamber of Commerce of Bács-Kiskun County, Hungary

projects.title: Formal Methods for Statutory Payroll Rule Representation and Automated Compliance Verification
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated formal representations of Serbian statutory payroll rules with the goal of enabling automated compliance verification of ERP payroll modules against current legislation. The core output was a domain-specific language (DSL) for payroll rules with a formal semantics defined in terms of a small-step operational model. A model checker was implemented and used to verify four open-source payroll modules against a rule corpus covering the Labour Law, Personal Income Tax Law, and mandatory social contribution regulations as of 2023. The project produced four peer-reviewed publications, one M.Sc. thesis, and an open-source toolchain released under a permissive licence. Industry engagement included two workshops with ERP vendors and an advisory panel of payroll practitioners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Applied Mathematics and Informatics, Niš

projects.title: Regulatory Change Absorption in Labour and Administrative Bodies of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REGLABS examined how public administrative and inspection bodies in the Western Balkans absorb statutory change—particularly legislative changes arising from EU accession harmonisation obligations. The project combined documentary analysis of inspection authority circulars, structured interviews with enforcement officials in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and a vignette study of inspector interpretive behaviour. The central output was a Regulatory Change Management Procedure framework comprising six procedural stages and twelve control points, validated against 24 documented reform episodes. Secondary outputs included a policy brief addressed to the Serbian Ministry of Public Administration and a curriculum module on regulatory change management adopted by the Higher School of Public Administration in Novi Sad. Total budget was approximately 3.8 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Law, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje, North Macedonia

projects.title: Compliance Monitoring Frameworks and Their Institutional Conditions: Comparative Evidence for Policy Transfer
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COMPMON was a cross-border project that compared compliance monitoring framework design in Vojvodina (Serbia) and the South Transdanubia region of Hungary, with the aim of identifying transferable design elements in the areas of labour, environmental, and food safety inspection. Simić led the work package on labour inspection frameworks, responsible for data collection through inspection authority records and expert interviews, comparative analysis, and a joint policy report submitted to both the Serbian Labour Inspectorate and the Hungarian National Labour Authority. The project produced four joint reports and a graduate elective course on comparative compliance monitoring taught simultaneously at the partner faculties. Total project budget approximately €480,000, of which the Novi Sad team administered €110,000.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Law, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Workplace Wellbeing Monitoring in Small and Medium Enterprises: Validated Tools and Implementation Protocols for the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WELLSME aimed to produce a suite of psychometrically validated, short-form occupational health instruments suitable for deployment in Serbian SMEs, together with a standardised implementation protocol covering survey administration, data analysis, and feedback to management. The project proceeded in three phases: (1) systematic review and meta-analysis of short-form burnout and engagement measures; (2) multi-site validation across 17 SMEs in Vojvodina and Central Serbia; (3) development and piloting of a web-based survey platform with automated reporting. Deliverables include the adapted OCM-SR, a validated short burnout battery, normative databases stratified by sector and company size, and an open-access implementation guide. The project involved collaboration with the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia.
partners: Faculty of Economics and Engineering Management, University Business Academy in Novi Sad
Faculty of Occupational Safety, University of Niš
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia – Vojvodina Regional Office

projects.title: Digital Work Design, Algorithmic Management and Occupational Stress in the ICT Sector of the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DIGISTRESS is a cross-border project examining how algorithmic management practices in ICT and business-process-outsourcing companies affect employee stress, autonomy and turnover intention in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region. The University of Novi Sad team leads Work Package 2, which covers instrument development (including the PAMS scale), quantitative data collection in Serbian companies, and cross-national comparison of findings. A secondary aim is co-design of evidence-based workplace guidelines for HR practitioners. Fieldwork involves surveys and semi-structured interviews in 12 Serbian and 10 Hungarian companies. Project outputs include a publicly available dataset, policy briefs in Serbian and Hungarian, and a joint training module for HR professionals.
partners: Department of Work and Organisational Psychology, Eötvös Loránd University
Hungarian Chamber of Commerce – Csongrád-Csanád County
NTP Novi Sad – Business Incubation Centre

projects.title: Legal Text Classification for Under-Resourced Balkan Languages
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: LEXICO addressed the absence of annotated legal corpora and pretrained language models tailored to Balkan languages with limited digital legal resources. The project assembled a multilingual corpus covering Serbian, Macedonian, and Bosnian court decisions (approximately 18,000 documents in total), established annotation guidelines for outcome and procedural-stage labels, and trained lightweight transformer models suitable for deployment on modest hardware. Deliverables included two publicly released datasets, three peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype web interface for case outcome screening used in a demonstration with a Belgrade-based legal aid organisation. The project was carried out entirely within Serbian institutions, with informal advisory input from collaborators at Masaryk University.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
School of Computing, Union University, Belgrade

projects.title: Data Augmentation Methods for Judicial Decision Support in Small-Data Regimes
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: DAJURIS investigates the boundary conditions under which synthetic data generation improves downstream legal classification, focusing on corpora with fewer than 1,000 labelled instances. The project compares rule-based paraphrasing, conditional generative models, and diffusion-based text augmentation on four task types drawn from Serbian administrative and civil law. A secondary objective is the development of an evaluation protocol that incorporates domain expert judgment alongside automatic metrics, addressing the gap between perplexity-based assessment and legal coherence. Results feed into practical guidelines for legal informatics practitioners. The project involves two PhD students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and a collaboration with the Faculty of Law for expert annotation.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Verification and Explanation of AI-Generated Text in High-Stakes Domains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated automated fact verification and explanation methods for AI-generated text with a focus on legal, medical, and financial documents in Serbian and English. The team built annotated corpora for hallucination detection, developed lightweight NLI models fine-tuned on domain-specific data, and designed a modular verification pipeline applicable to retrieval-augmented generation architectures. The project funded two PhD students and supported collaboration with the Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade, and the University of Pécs. Outputs include three datasets released under open licences, seven peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype verification module tested with a regional legal information provider.
partners: Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade
Department of Computer Science, University of Pécs
Regional Legal Information Centre Novi Sad (observer partner)

projects.title: Explainability Standards for Machine Learning in Clinical Decision Support
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: XPLAIN-MED was a seven-partner European project addressing the gap between regulatory expectations for clinical AI explainability and available technical methods. Tešić led the work package on benchmarking explanation methods across heterogeneous clinical data types, coordinating annotation studies and the development of a shared evaluation toolkit. The University of Novi Sad team contributed expertise in post-hoc explanation methods and organised two cross-site annotation exercises. The project produced an open-source evaluation library, a position paper submitted to the European Medicines Agency, and informed a draft technical standard for explanation reporting in medical device software. Total project budget was approximately €3.2 million; the Novi Sad share was €310 000.

projects.title: Efficient Vector Search Infrastructures for Multilingual Document Repositories
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the co-design of approximate nearest-neighbour index structures and multilingual text encoders for document retrieval in public-sector repositories. Work packages cover: (1) encoder fine-tuning for South Slavic languages with limited supervision, (2) quantisation-aware index construction balancing recall and storage, and (3) a prototype retrieval service validated on a 10-million-document legal and administrative corpus provided by a partner institution. The project funds two PhD students and covers compute costs on the PARADOX-IV HPC cluster. An open benchmark dataset covering Serbian and Croatian legal documents is a planned deliverable.

projects.title: Cross-Lingual Document Discovery in Regional Public Administration Archives
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSDOC aims to improve access to administrative documents held by Hungarian and Serbian public bodies by building a shared cross-lingual retrieval layer. The Serbian technical team, led by Todorović, is responsible for the index infrastructure work package, including the design of a federated index architecture that allows each national partner to retain custody of its documents while exposing a unified query interface. The system will be piloted with two municipal archives containing approximately 400,000 documents each. Hungarian-language tokenisation and transliteration components are contributed by the University of Debrecen partner.

projects.title: Competency Framework Standards for Technical Occupations in the Vojvodina Manufacturing Sector
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce draft sector competency reference frameworks for three manufacturing sub-sectors prominent in Vojvodina: food and beverage processing, rubber and plastics goods, and agricultural machinery production. Activities included systematic job analysis fieldwork at 24 participating companies, development of occupational family structures, and competency element specification using standardised descriptor templates. Outputs included three draft framework documents, a methodological guide for HR practitioners, and two workshops attended by company HR managers and representatives of the Vojvodina Employers' Association. The project also produced recommendations addressed to the Provincial Secretariat on governance mechanisms for maintaining and updating sector frameworks.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce and Industry
Institute for Quality and Standardisation Vojvodina

projects.title: Skills Transferability and Worker Reclassification During Manufacturing Technology Transitions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SKILLTRANS investigates how existing operator competency profiles map onto newly required competency profiles when manufacturing firms introduce automation or digitalisation investments, and what reclassification decisions result. The project combines longitudinal task-analysis observation at six Vojvodina plants undergoing technology transitions, analysis of internal HR reclassification records, and a structured employer survey covering 110 firms. The project develops and pilots a transferability index—a metric expressing the proportion of a worker's existing certified competencies that remain relevant after a defined technology change—and tests its predictive validity against actual reclassification outcomes. A practitioner toolkit for HR managers and a policy brief for the Serbian National Employment Service are planned as end-of-project deliverables.
