projects.title: Psychometric Foundations of Personnel Selection Instruments in the Serbian Labour Market
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to build an evidence base for the validity and fairness of cognitive ability and personality instruments used in personnel selection in Serbia. Activities included large-scale criterion validity studies in manufacturing, ICT, and public administration sectors, systematic DIF investigations across gender, age, and educational subgroups, and the development of updated national norm tables for two widely used cognitive ability subtests. Partners contributed samples from Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, enabling preliminary cross-national equivalence analyses. A freely available technical manual summarising validity coefficients and fairness statistics for practising psychologists was produced as a primary dissemination output. The project supported two PhD students and funded fieldwork in five regional companies.
partners: Department of Psychology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Philosophy, University of East Sarajevo
Croatian Psychological Chamber (Hrvatska psihološka komora)

projects.title: Fair Testing Practices in Cross-Border Recruitment: A Hungary–Serbia Collaboration
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project addresses the growing use of standardised cognitive and personality tests by companies recruiting simultaneously in the Hungarian and Serbian labour markets. Bogdan Kapor leads the work package on measurement equivalence and DIF analysis, coordinating joint data collection across four partner organisations. The project develops bilingual test forms with documented translation equivalence, conducts cross-national norming studies, and produces practitioner guidelines for HR professionals in both countries on interpreting test scores fairly across linguistic and cultural groups. Training workshops for HR staff in both countries are planned for 2025 and 2026. The project also examines test score differences attributable to language of administration versus genuine latent trait differences.
partners: Institute of Psychology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina (РОЙАС)
Dunavski HR Consulting, Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Baranya County, Hungary

projects.title: Data Protection Compliance Frameworks for Automated Workforce Management Systems in EU Candidate Countries
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines how companies registered in Serbia and other EU candidate countries can build legally compliant data protection frameworks when deploying automated workforce management systems — covering recruitment, performance evaluation, and termination — that process personal data of employees and job applicants. The research team combines legal doctrinal analysis with a survey of fifty companies operating in the Vojvodina region and qualitative interviews with data protection officers, HR managers, and legal counsel. Deliverables include a compliance toolkit adapted to Serbian law, a comparative legal report covering six Western Balkan jurisdictions, and three peer-reviewed publications. The project involves collaboration with the Faculty of Law in Kragujevac and the Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Kragujevac
Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection, Belgrade
Science and Technology Park Novi Sad

projects.title: Privacy Awareness and Compliance Readiness of Technology Start-ups in the Vojvodina Innovation Ecosystem
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This small-scale project assessed baseline data protection compliance among thirty-seven technology start-ups resident at or affiliated with business incubators in the Vojvodina region, including NTP Novi Sad. Using a structured audit questionnaire and follow-up interviews, the project documented gaps in privacy notice quality, data processing agreement coverage, and internal DPO or privacy contact designation. Findings were used to develop a two-day training programme delivered to start-up founders and developers in late 2021. The project also produced a short practical guide to GDPR and Serbian data protection law obligations specifically written for early-stage technology companies, made freely available through the Provincial Secretariat's website.
partners: Science and Technology Park Novi Sad
Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research

projects.title: Optimisation of Thermal and Rheological Conditions in Injection Moulding of Thick-Section Engineering Thermoplastics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between standard injection moulding simulation assumptions and the physical reality of processing thick-section (6–20 mm) parts from engineering thermoplastics. The main activities comprised experimental characterisation of rheological and thermal material properties under industrially representative pressure and cooling-rate conditions, development of extended boundary-condition models for mould-wall temperature non-uniformity, and construction of a validated simulation workflow for defect prediction and process parameter selection. Four industrial case studies covering polycarbonate, PA66, and PP were carried out in collaboration with a domestic tooling company. Results were disseminated through peer-reviewed journals and one book chapter.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Plastikum d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Polymer Process Simulation for SME Tool Makers
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project aimed to improve the simulation competence of small and medium-sized injection mould makers in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The University of Novi Sad team led the work package on material characterisation and simulation methodology, providing rheological testing services to eight participating SMEs and developing a shared database of fitted constitutive model parameters for 14 commercially available thermoplastic grades. Training workshops were organised at partner sites in Subotica and Pécs. The project produced a bilingual technical handbook distributed to 120 regional tool-making companies. Anja Babić coordinated the Novi Sad-side activities and contributed directly to three SME case studies addressing warpage and filling-balance problems.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged
Műanyag Szakkollégium Kft., Pécs
Unitool d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Carbon Footprint Management Tools for Manufacturing SMEs in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CARBMAN aimed to develop and pilot a freely available carbon footprint calculation toolkit tailored to the data constraints of manufacturing SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The project produced a web-based data entry interface pre-loaded with regional emission factors, a report generator aligned with ISO 14067, and a training curriculum delivered through four workshops across Novi Sad, Subotica, and Pécs. Milan Sabo led the work package responsible for methodology development and tool validation, coordinating testing at five Serbian pilot companies. The project trained 68 company representatives. The toolkit was handed over to the Vojvodina Development Agency for ongoing maintenance after project closure.
partners: Regional Development Agency of South Transdanubia, Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina Development Agency, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Greenhouse Gas Emission Mapping and Reduction Pathways for Serbian Automotive Supply Chain Tier 2 and Tier 3 Suppliers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GREENCHAIN-RS is a three-year applied research project funded under the IDEAS programme of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. The project develops an industry-applicable methodology for Scope 1–3 GHG mapping tailored to Tier 2 and Tier 3 automotive suppliers in Serbia, where supply chain emission data are sparse and verification infrastructure is nascent. Research activities include factory-floor measurement campaigns at twelve partner companies, development of Serbian-specific background emission factors for common manufacturing inputs, and a scenario modelling tool for evaluating cost-effective decarbonisation measures. A secondary objective is to train a cohort of in-company LCA practitioners. Milan Sabo leads the project as principal investigator with a team of three researchers and two doctoral students based at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Serbian Automotive Cluster, Belgrade
Institute for Industrial Ecology, University of Kragujevac

projects.title: Developing Standardised Characterisation Protocols for Post-Industrial Thermoplastic Recyclates in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the absence of harmonised testing procedures for post-industrial thermoplastic recyclates accepted across Serbian manufacturing and recycling sectors. Activities included an inter-laboratory measurement comparison study across eight regional institutions, development of a proposed characterisation protocol specifying minimum test parameters (MFI, GPC, OIT, impact, colour), and validation of the protocol against commercial recyclate streams. The protocol was piloted with three industrial partners collecting packaging-grade polypropylene and PET recyclate. A freely downloadable technical guideline document was produced and submitted to the Institute for Standardisation of Serbia as input material for a future national standard. The project trained four graduate students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade
Faculty of Chemical Engineering, University of Zagreb
Plastičar d.o.o., Bačka Palanka
Ekoplast Recycling d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Recyclate Quality Monitoring and Contamination Control in Polyolefin Processing Lines
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research engagement with Polimer Inženjering d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based compounder processing post-industrial polyolefin waste. The Faculty of Technology group provides quarterly characterisation of incoming recyclate batches (GPC, MFI, OIT, ash content, tensile properties) and produces a structured quality report identifying out-of-specification batches before they enter the production line. Additional work includes root-cause analysis of two contamination incidents that caused visible defects in extruded profiles, and recommendation of sorting and blending strategies to maintain minimum mechanical property thresholds. The contract covers equipment operating costs and funds one technician position.
partners: Polimer Inženjering d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Humidity-Adaptive Process Windows in Corrugated and Folding-Carton Converting
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the quantitative relationship between ambient relative humidity and the mechanical performance of corrugated and folding-carton packaging at each stage of the converting process. Laboratory experiments characterised moisture sorption, crease mechanics, and crush resistance across humidity ranges representative of converting-plant conditions in northern Serbia. Field measurement campaigns at four plants provided real-world validation data. Based on the combined dataset, process-window maps were constructed that specify acceptable RH ranges for die-cutting, creasing, and stack conditioning as a function of board grade. The project produced practical guidelines adopted voluntarily by two participating companies and generated four peer-reviewed journal publications. One doctoral student was trained.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Pakoproiz d.o.o., Novi Sad
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad

projects.title: Regional Assessment of Climate Effects on Corrugated Packaging Logistics in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: REGIOBOX was a cross-border cooperation project addressing the seasonal degradation of corrugated packaging performance in the Pannonian climate zone, which affects both Serbian and Hungarian supply chains. Đorđe Cvetković led the work package on material characterisation and laboratory testing, coordinating parallel measurement activities at the University of Novi Sad and the University of Miskolc. The project established a shared humidity-testing protocol adopted by all partner institutions, conducted a region-wide survey of converting plant conditions, and produced a publicly available database of RH-dependent mechanical properties for 24 corrugated board grades commercially available in Serbia and Hungary. Industry engagement activities included two workshops attended by packaging technologists from 18 regional companies.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Miskolc, Institute of Logistics
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina
North Hungarian Packaging Cluster, Miskolc

projects.title: Water-Based Inks for Cold-Chain Flexible and Corrugated Packaging: Formulation, Surface Interaction, and Performance Standards
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of systematic knowledge on the behaviour of water-based flexographic inks on recycled fibre substrates at sub-zero temperatures. Work packages covered binder selection and formulation modification for low-temperature flexibility, surface energy characterisation of recycled and virgin board under cold and humid conditions, development of a combined distribution-simulation test protocol, and dissemination to packaging converters. Partners contributed expertise in rheology, DMA, and XPS surface analysis. The project produced 6 peer-reviewed publications and contributed input to a working group considering cold-chain print performance criteria at national level. Two MSc students and one PhD student were trained through the project.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Chemistry, University of Belgrade
Institute for Testing Materials, Belgrade

projects.title: Surface Heterogeneity of Recycled Fibre Boards and Its Consequences for Functional Coating Adhesion
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: RECOSURF examined the spatial and compositional heterogeneity of surfaces of recycled containerboard and testliner grades sourced from Serbian and regional mills. XPS mapping, SEM imaging, and contact-angle mapping were combined to relate filler particle clusters, fibre orientation, and residual coating fragments to local variability in surface energy and ink adhesion. The project demonstrated that within-sheet variation in peel adhesion (coefficient of variation up to 18 %) is strongly predicted by surface energy heterogeneity rather than mean surface energy alone. Recommendations for corona-treatment uniformity monitoring were prepared for one industrial partner. One PhD thesis was initiated under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Center for Surface Analysis, Institute of Physics, University of Belgrade
Vojvodina Packaging Research Centre, Novi Sad

projects.title: Flexible Packaging Inline Verification: Photometric and Substrate Criteria for Reliable 2D Code Reading
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between laboratory-established ISO verification standards and the practical conditions of high-speed flexographic packaging lines. The research team developed photometric models for inline camera illumination design, characterised 26 flexible packaging substrate types with respect to surface texture and NIR reflectance, and constructed a pilot inline verification rig on the Department's narrow-web press. A set of substrate qualification criteria and illuminator design guidelines were produced as the main deliverable, targeting SME label converters and packaging printers in Vojvodina that lack in-house optics expertise. The project involved collaboration with food packaging companies in the region and produced six peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Packaging Converters Cluster (fictional industry association)

projects.title: Pharmaceutical Label Quality Assurance in Short-Run Flexographic Production: Resolution and Contrast Standards for Serialisation Codes
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Serialisation requirements for pharmaceutical unit-dose packaging mandated by EU Directive 2011/62/EU increased demand for reliable small-X-dimension DataMatrix printing on narrow-web flexographic presses operated by Serbian contract printers. This project characterised the resolution limits of eight narrow-web presses operating in Serbia, derived press-specific MTF curves, and produced a simplified resolution budget tool for prepress engineers. Substrate qualification protocols for three pharmaceutical label facestock types were validated against GS1 Healthcare recommendations. Training workshops were held with two contract label printers, and the qualification protocols were adopted by one partner company within the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
NovaMed Labels d.o.o. (fictional company, Novi Sad)
Institute for Standardisation of Serbia (fictional participation)

projects.title: Aluminium Sludge Valorisation: From Anodising Effluent Treatment Residues to Functional Inorganic Products
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the full conversion chain from raw anodising sludge to three product families — polyaluminium coagulants, zeolitic adsorbents, and construction binders — at laboratory and pilot scale. Objectives include establishing compositional variability limits for regional sludge sources, optimising synthesis conditions for each product route, testing product performance against commercial benchmarks, and conducting a comparative life cycle assessment. The project funds two PhD students and includes analytical infrastructure upgrades (ICP-OES autosampler, 27Al solid-state NMR access via national facility). Industry engagement is pursued informally with a surface-finishing company in Vojvodina that supplies sludge and contributes operational knowledge.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of General and Physical Chemistry, Belgrade
Aluminijska Obrada d.o.o., Novi Sad (in-kind partner)

projects.title: Residue-Based Water Treatment Materials for Cross-Border Applications in Drinking Water and Industrial Effluent
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project addressing the preparation and application of low-cost adsorbents and coagulants derived from industrial residues generated on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. Lazić's group led the work package on aluminium-bearing residues, supplying characterised sludge-derived coagulants and calcined adsorbents for joint testing at the Hungarian partner's pilot water treatment facility. The project also included training workshops for water utility engineers and a joint summer school for PhD students from both institutions. A joint application for a regional product standard for sludge-derived coagulants was initiated but not completed within the project period.
partners: Department of Applied and Environmental Chemistry, University of Szeged
Regional Water Utility Consortium Subotica–Horgoš
Research Institute for Environment and Agriculture, Debrecen

projects.title: Optimisation of Nitriding Cycles for Extended Service Life of Hot-Work Tool Steel Extrusion Dies
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish quantitative relationships between plasma and gas nitriding process parameters (temperature, duration, nitriding potential) and the fatigue and tribological performance of AISI H11 and H13 extrusion dies under industrially representative cyclic loading conditions. Work packages covered specimen-level nitriding, residual stress characterisation by X-ray diffraction, thermal shock testing, finite element stress analysis, and a short industrial validation trial with a regional aluminium profiles producer. The project produced three journal publications and a set of process windows for nitriding temperature and duration that reduce heat-check cracking frequency in production dies. Two MSc theses were completed within the project scope.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš
Aluminijumski Profili Panonija d.o.o., Zrenjanin (fictional)

projects.title: Industrial Benchmarking of Die Geometry and Surface Treatment for Aluminium Extrusion Tooling
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A twelve-month contract research engagement with a regional tooling manufacturer to evaluate five bearing land geometries and two nitriding treatments across three production profiles. The scope included die design support, pre-production nitriding supervision, on-press data logging, post-mortem metallographic examination of retired dies, and a written technical report with recommendations. The engagement led directly to a geometry modification that the company implemented in standard production; results from this work were subsequently incorporated into the 2021 journal publication on bearing land geometry and tool life.
partners: Alumerged Tools d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional)

projects.title: Energy Management Systems for Small and Medium Manufacturers in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to build capacity for ISO 50001-aligned energy management in manufacturing SMEs across Hungary and Serbia, with a focus on electrochemical and metal-forming industries. The Faculty of Technical Sciences team led the work package on audit methodology development and tool validation. Activities included: development of a simplified audit procedure calibrated against full instrument-based audits at twenty-two sites; training of forty-seven plant energy managers; and production of sector-specific guidance documents in Serbian and Hungarian. The project demonstrated average verified energy savings of 11.4% at fourteen pilot sites over a twelve-month monitoring period following audit implementation. Outputs were incorporated into a freely accessible online self-assessment platform maintained by the project consortium.
partners: University of Miskolc, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Informatics, Hungary
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina, Serbia
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Csongrád-Csanád County, Hungary

projects.title: Peak-Demand Reduction Strategies for Electrochemical Manufacturing Under Evolving Tariff Structures in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated how changes in Serbian electricity tariff regulation affect the feasibility and design of load-shifting programmes at electrochemical manufacturing facilities. Research activities included: longitudinal monitoring of fourteen metal-finishing SMEs over three years; development and validation of a linear programming scheduling tool parameterised by process constraints and real-time metering; tariff sensitivity analysis covering four regulatory scenarios; and a comparative study of sites that had and had not implemented structured energy management. The project produced verified evidence that schedule optimisation under the 2021 revised tariff structure is economically attractive for a broader set of process configurations than under the previous structure. A freely available scheduling tool and user documentation were released under an open-source licence at project close.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Energy Research and Development, Belgrade

projects.title: Mono-Material Polyolefin High-Barrier Packaging for Mechanically Recyclable Food Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MONOBAR investigated the feasibility of replacing conventional EVOH-containing multilayer films with all-polyolefin or compatibilised polyolefin–amorphous PET coextruded structures that can enter existing PE recycling streams without down-cycling. The project characterised oxygen and water vapour transport mechanisms in candidate film architectures across relevant temperature and humidity ranges, established structure–property relationships for barrier optimisation, and assessed recyclate quality after multiple reprocessing cycles. Film production was conducted on the laboratory coextrusion line at the Faculty of Technology; analytical work used DSC, FTIR-ATR, GPC and permeability testing infrastructure. Two MSc theses and one ongoing doctoral study have been completed within the project. Results have been communicated to a regional packaging film producer and a food manufacturer.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Polymer Technology, University of Ljubljana
PoliFlex d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Temperature-Resolved Gas Permeability Reference Data for Polyolefin Packaging Films
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: PERMTEMP aimed to produce a systematically collected reference dataset of temperature-dependent oxygen, carbon dioxide and water vapour permeability for ten commercially relevant polyolefin film grades, covering the range 5–50 °C. Arrhenius activation energies and pre-exponential factors were determined by least-squares regression on multi-temperature OTR and WVTR datasets. The dataset was made available to Serbian food-industry companies through a technical report and an online spreadsheet tool for shelf-life estimation. The project also calibrated the Faculty of Technology permeability laboratory instruments against certified reference films, establishing a documented calibration protocol that remains in use.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Optimisation of Seal-Layer Formulations for Extended Thermal Processing Windows on High-Speed Packaging Lines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the relationship between seal-layer formulation variables—resin type, comonomer content, blend ratios, and film thickness—and the achievable thermal processing window on VFFS packaging lines running at up to 300 bags/min. Work was conducted across four tasks: rheological and thermal characterisation of candidate resins; cast-film extrusion trials on the laboratory line at the Faculty of Technology; heat-seal testing using a gradient sealer and a laboratory VFFS unit; and statistical modelling of composition–property relationships using RSM. The project produced seven publications and validated two target formulations with an industrial partner. A trained PhD student and two master's students were involved. Equipment procured under the project included an updated hot-tack tester and an ATR-FTIR accessory.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
FlexoPak d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Heat-Sealable Multilayer Films for Food Packaging: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer and Process Validation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad and the Department of Plastics Technology at Budapest University of Technology, co-funded under Interreg IPA. The project addressed gaps in the regional packaging film industry by developing shared test protocols for heat-seal quality assessment and transferring extensional rheology measurement competence to the Serbian side. Grbić led Work Package 2, covering heat-seal and hot-tack testing protocol harmonisation and the comparative study of 180° peel versus burst test methods. Joint workshops were held in both Novi Sad and Budapest. A shared database of polymer melt rheology and seal-performance data was compiled and made available to packaging SMEs in both countries.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Plastics Technology, Budapest University of Technology
Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica

projects.title: Safety Assessment Framework for Digitally Printed Flexible Packaging in the Food Sector
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SAFEFLEX addresses the gap between rapid adoption of digital inkjet printing on flexible food packaging films and the absence of validated testing protocols for ink migration safety under conditions specific to digitally printed polyolefin substrates. The project combines migration modelling (Piringer approach), experimental migration testing across multiple food simulants and temperature conditions, and surface characterisation of treated polyolefin films. A key output is a draft testing protocol for UV-curable and water-based inkjet inks intended for food-contact flexible packaging, suitable for submission to the relevant CEN working group. The project team includes food chemists from the Institute of Food Technology in Novi Sad and printing technologists from the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Two industry advisory partners contribute real production samples and process parameters.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Fleksprint d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Digital Printing Technologies for Sustainable Flexible Packaging in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DIGIPACK-IPA was a cross-border cooperation project between the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology at the University of Pécs in Hungary. The project aimed to transfer knowledge on digital direct printing on flexible packaging substrates to small and medium enterprises on both sides of the border. Stojanović contributed to the work package on surface treatment optimisation and inkjet printability evaluation, conducting substrate characterisation and adhesion testing. The project delivered a jointly operated open-access testing service for packaging converters and trained 14 company technologists through a short-course programme. Equipment procured under the project, including a contact angle measurement system, remains accessible at both partner sites.
partners: Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina, Serbia
CsomagTech Kft., Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Adaptive Springback Compensation for Mixed-Material Press-Brake Production Lines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a self-tuning closed-loop control system for CNC press-brake bending that adapts to within-coil and between-batch material variability without requiring pre-production tensile tests. The core technical work comprised: construction of a 360-simulation FEM training database, development of a POD-based surrogate model, integration of an unscented Kalman filter for real-time material identification, and laboratory validation on instrumented press-brakes at Novi Sad and the partner institution in Niš. Three steel grades (S235, S355, DP600) and one aluminium alloy (AA6016-T4) were studied. The project produced four journal papers, one granted patent application, and a set of open-source software tools deposited in the university repository. Two M.Sc. students completed theses within the project.
partners: Department of Production Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Automatic Control, Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Digital Twin Architectures for Sheet-Metal Forming Machines in SME Environments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FORMTWIN brings together two Serbian and two Hungarian academic institutions with three SME partners operating sheet-metal job shops to develop practically deployable digital twin prototypes for press-brake and stamping machines. Bogićević leads Work Package 3, covering press-brake digital twin design, sensor integration, and FEM-based state estimation. The work package is producing a reference instrumentation kit (sensor selection, mounting guidelines, data-acquisition hardware) that the SME partners are piloting on their production machines. Deliverables include a software framework released under an open licence, two joint journal publications, and a training workshop held at the Science Technology Park Novi Sad. The project runs until mid-2026.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Department of Manufacturing Science and Technology, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Institute for Logistics and Production Systems, University of Miskolc
Metaloform d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Energy Monitoring and Mapping Tools for Small Manufacturing Enterprises in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to transfer energy monitoring and VSM methodology to SMEs in the Vojvodina–Csongrád-Csanád cross-border region. The Novi Sad team was responsible for the work package covering methodology development and training delivery. Ten SMEs participated across both countries; six were metalworking companies with welding operations. Activities included a two-day practitioner training course, on-site measurement campaigns, and preparation of company-specific energy improvement reports. The Novi Sad team also developed a freely available spreadsheet toolkit for energy VSM construction. The project produced a joint methodology guide published in Serbian and Hungarian.
partners: Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged, Hungary
Vojvodina Development Agency, Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Csongrád-Csanád County, Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Per-Process Energy Tracking and Optimisation in Robotic Arc Welding Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WELDTRACK investigates methods for continuous, low-cost energy monitoring of robotic MIG and MAG welding cells and the use of collected data to support scheduling and process parameter optimisation. The project has three phases: instrumentation and data-collection protocol development; model building for energy prediction from robot controller outputs; and integration of the models into a scheduling decision-support tool. Two industrial partners provide access to production cells. The project funds one full-time PhD student and supports collaboration with Politecnico di Milano on digital-twin architecture. An open dataset of welding cell load profiles is planned for release at project end.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Metalkon d.o.o., Novi Sad
AgroWeld Tehnika d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Kinetic and Thermodynamic Modelling of Fe–Zn Intermetallic Growth in Reactive Batch Galvanizing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and experimentally validate a coupled thermodynamic–kinetic model for Fe–Zn intermetallic layer growth applicable to silicon-reactive steels. Work packages covered: re-optimisation of the Fe–Zn–Si ternary thermodynamic database using new experimental calorimetric and phase boundary data; systematic interrupted-immersion experiments at three bath temperatures; DICTRA diffusion simulations incorporating a silicon-dependent interface mobility term; and dissemination to Serbian galvanizing industry through a freely distributed practical datasheet. Partners contributed experimental TEM and EPMA capabilities. Results fed directly into journal publications and one MSc thesis completed in 2023.
partners: Institute of Technical Sciences, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade
Faculty of Materials Science and Technology, Slovak University of Technology, Bratislava

projects.title: Optimisation of Flux Chemistry and Bath Composition for Lead-Free Batch Hot-Dip Galvanizing of Recycled-Steel Structural Sections
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: An industry-funded contract research project in collaboration with a Serbian batch galvanizing company (Vojvodina Metalna Zaštita d.o.o., Zrenjanin). The project addressed two practical problems: transition from Pb-containing to Bi–Sn lead-free zinc baths and increasing frequency of Sandelin-range silicon in incoming structural steel from EAF scrap. The research group conducted laboratory galvanizing trials with twelve bath compositions and delivered flux bath monitoring protocols and bath composition recommendations. Findings from this project informed two journal publications. The company implemented revised flux titration procedures as a direct outcome.
partners: Vojvodina Metalna Zaštita d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Thermomechanical Modelling and Experimental Validation of Residual Stress Formation in Semi-Crystalline Injection Mouldings
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses a gap in predictive capability for residual stresses and warpage in injection-moulded semi-crystalline thermoplastics. The core activities include calibration of crystallisation kinetics models for PA6 and PP at industrially relevant cooling rates, implementation of a fully coupled thermomechanical simulation chain, and systematic experimental validation using in-mould sensors and post-ejection CMM and structured-light scanning. The project team of four researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences collaborates with the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad for DSC characterisation and with partners at the University of Maribor for material modelling. By the end of the project, a validated simulation workflow and a material parameter database will be made available as open data for Serbian polymer processing industry users.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, University of Maribor, Slovenia

projects.title: Optimisation of Mould Cooling Systems for Reduced Warpage in High-Volume Thermoplastic Production
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A two-year applied research contract with a regional plastic components manufacturer producing PP and PA6 parts for the automotive supply chain. The project objective was to reduce scrap rates caused by out-of-tolerance warpage in three production parts by developing and implementing a simulation-based cooling channel redesign procedure. The faculty team performed process simulation, surrogate-based optimisation of cooling channel geometry, and validation trials at the company's injection moulding facility. Scrap rates on the three target parts were reduced from an average of 6.8% to below 2.1% over a six-month production period following implementation of the redesigned moulds.
partners: Plastoteh d.o.o., Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Environmental Performance Benchmarking and Compliance Support for Polymer Processors in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed a shared environmental performance benchmarking toolkit for small and medium polymer processors operating in the Serbia–Hungary cross-border region. Activities included primary data collection at twenty-two facilities, construction of sector-specific environmental performance indicator sets, delivery of four compliance workshops attended by a total of 187 company representatives, and publication of a freely accessible online benchmarking platform. The Serbian side, coordinated by the University of Novi Sad team, focused on regulatory mapping and effluent characterisation, while the Hungarian partner contributed process energy monitoring data and LCI datasets. The project produced a multilingual guidance document on ISO 14001 implementation aligned with current Serbian and Hungarian permit requirements.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina (RDEV)
West Pannon Regional and Economic Development Public Nonprofit Ltd., Győr

projects.title: Life-Cycle Assessment Database for Mechanically Recycled Plastics from Southeast European Post-Consumer Streams
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RECYCLCA aims to close a critical data gap in LCA practice by constructing verified, primary-data-based life-cycle inventory datasets for five categories of mechanically recycled plastics sourced from Serbian and regional post-consumer collection systems: HDPE bottles, PET bottles, PP packaging, mixed polyolefin film, and EPS. The project combines on-site measurement campaigns at three Serbian recycling facilities with uncertainty quantification and pedigree-matrix-based data quality assessment. Datasets are formatted for ecoinvent 3.x integration and will be made available under an open licence. A secondary objective is to train a cohort of twelve industry practitioners in LCA methodology through a structured workshop series delivered at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Serbian Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA)

projects.title: Unapređenje kontrole površinske aktivacije fleksibilnih polimernih supstrata za primenu u ambalažnoj štampi
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj razvoj protokola za brzu procenu adekvatnosti korona i plazma predtretmana u štamparijama fleksibilne ambalaže, bez potrebe za laboratorijskim merenjima kontaktnog ugla na liniji. Ispitane su korelacije između standardnih pokazatelja kvaliteta otiska (optička gustina, sjaj, granula boje) i izmerjenih vrednosti slobodne površinske energije na BOPP, LDPE i PET folijama. Rezultati projekta uključuju skup preporuka i kalibracionih procedura za operatere prese, primenjivih sa postojećim densitometrima. Partneri su bili laboratorija za nauku o materijalima iz Beograda i jedan štamparski pogon iz Vojvodine.
partners: Institut za fiziku, Beograd
FlexoPak d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Multivariate Monitoring Tools for Scale-Adaptive Film Coating in Solid Dosage Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the problem of monitoring model transfer when film-coating processes are scaled from laboratory to pilot and production equipment. Key objectives included developing time-alignment strategies for multi-scale batch trajectory data, constructing cross-scale PLS prediction models for coating end-point parameters, and validating the monitoring framework on aqueous ethylcellulose and HPMC coating of tablets and pellets. The project funded one PhD student and supported access to the 30-litre pan coater and in-line NIR instrumentation at the Faculty of Technology pilot plant. Collaboration with the University of Graz provided access to larger-scale equipment for validation experiments. The project produced four journal publications and one conference contribution.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Pharmaceutical Technology, University of Graz

projects.title: Process Analytical Technologies for Pharmaceutical Coating: Serbia–Austria Research Exchange
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral mobility project between the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad and the Institute of Pharmaceutical Technology, University of Graz supporting researcher exchange visits and joint experimental work on in-line Raman spectroscopy for coating thickness monitoring. The project funded three reciprocal visits by PhD students and senior researchers, enabling shared instrument access and co-authorship on publications addressing calibration uncertainty and scale-up of spectroscopic monitoring models. The bilateral framework was funded under the Serbia–Austria scientific cooperation programme administered through the Ministry of Science of the Republic of Serbia and the Austrian Agency for International Cooperation in Education and Research.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Pharmaceutical Technology, University of Graz

projects.title: Механистички модели растварања за QbD дизајн орално примењених система с контролисаним ослобађањем
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат се бавио развојем и валидацијом механистичких рачунских модела растварања за два типа формулација с продуженим ослобађањем: хидрофилне матрикс таблете и облоговане пелете у тврдим капсулама. Циљ је био интеграција ових модела у QbD оквир за дефинисање дизајн простора. Израђена је библиотека параметара за десет полимерних система, а модели су валидовани на независним скуповима података добијеним у сарадњи са партнерским институцијама у Љубљани и Сплиту. Пројекат је финансиран у оквиру програма IDEAS Фонда за науку Републике Србије.
partners: Факултет фармације, Универзитет у Љубљани
Хемијско-технолошки факултет, Универзитет у Сплиту

projects.title: Water Activity and Antioxidant Synergism as Dual Stability Levers in Preservative-Reduced Cosmetic Emulsions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how simultaneously reducing water activity through targeted humectant blending and optimising antioxidant combinations can maintain microbiological and oxidative stability in cosmetic emulsions formulated with reduced preservative concentrations. The study covers oil-in-water and water-in-oil emulsion architectures across three representative product categories: facial moisturisers, body lotions, and hair-conditioning emulsions. Work packages address measurement standardisation, mechanistic modelling of aw–preservative interactions, and scale-up validation with a local contract manufacturing partner. Outputs include validated formulation design rules, an open-access dataset, and updated internal guidelines for the industrial partner. Three PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher are supported under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Belgrade
Laboratorija za kontrolu kozmetike Vojvodine d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Predicting Emulsion Stability Loss Across Cold-Chain Distribution: From Rheological Fingerprinting to Shelf-Life Modelling
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: EMULCHAIN addressed the problem of stability failures in cosmetic and food emulsions subjected to temperature fluctuations during cross-border transport between Serbia and Hungary. Željko Zarić led the work package on rheological characterisation and accelerated stress testing at the Novi Sad site. The project developed a shared protocol for temperature-cycling stress tests and established regression models linking rheological parameters measured after cycling to real-time stability outcomes. A joint database of 48 emulsion formulations was compiled. Outputs include a bilingual technical guide for small cosmetic and food manufacturers and a jointly supervised master's thesis. The Hungarian partner contributed sensory evaluation capacity absent at the Novi Sad site.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

Regionalna razvojna agencija Vojvodine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Optimizacija parne destilacije aromatičnog bilja u Vojvodini: od parcele do pilota
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je bio usmeren na sistematsko mapiranje faktora koji utiču na prinos i kvalitet etarskog ulja kod pet vrsta aromatičnog bilja koje se gaje u Vojvodini (lavanda, žalfija, nana, origano, kamilica). Ispitivani su agronomski parametri (vreme berbe, metod sušenja) i procesni parametri (tip i skala destilacije, trajanje, protok pare) u kontrolisanim uslovima na pilot postrojenjima Tehnološkog fakulteta. Baza podataka sa 380 eksperimentata korišćena je za razvoj preporuka za lokalne uzgajivače i prerađivače. Rezultati su objavljeni u dva naučna rada i prezentovani na dva stručna skupa u Novom Sadu i Subotici.
partners: Pokrajinski zavod za razvoj poljoprivrede, Novi Sad
Zadružni savez Vojvodine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Aromatic and Medicinal Plant Residue Valorisation through Integrated Extraction and Separation Networks
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ARIANES addresses the underutilisation of spent plant biomass after essential oil distillation across the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The project combines steam and hydrodistillation optimisation (WP2, led by the Novi Sad team) with downstream recovery of polyphenols from spent biomass by pressurised liquid extraction (WP3, led by Hungarian partner). A shared pilot facility protocol was developed to allow cross-border operators to benchmark their processes. Enikő Varga leads WP2, responsible for standardising distillation protocols and generating yield and composition data for six target species. The project targets small and medium aromatic plant processing enterprises in both countries.
partners: Pannon Növényi Technológia Kft., Pécs, Mađarska
Debreceni Egyetem, Agrártudományi Kar, Debrecen, Mađarska
Udruženje prerađivača lekovitog bilja Vojvodine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermomechanical Integrity of Structural Polymer Components in Electromobility Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the lack of validated simulation workflows for predicting crack initiation and residual deformation in glass-fibre-reinforced thermoplastic components used in light electric vehicles, where thermal excursions are more severe than in conventional drivetrains. Work packages cover material characterisation under combined thermal and mechanical loading, extension of the mould-flow-to-structural simulation chain to include moisture effects, and development of a strain-energy-density fatigue criterion calibrated for three commercially relevant polyamide and polyester grades. An industrial demonstrator component—a motor housing—will be redesigned using the developed methodology and validated by accelerated thermal cycling tests. The project employs one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Materials Testing, Belgrade

projects.title: Structural Performance of Recycled-Content Polymer Components for White Goods
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A bilateral research contract with a regional appliance manufacturer to evaluate whether structural polymer parts moulded with up to 30% recycled-content polyamide and polypropylene meet the same service life targets as virgin-material parts. The scope covers tensile, fatigue, and thermal cycling characterisation of blended material grades at three recycled-content levels, combined with mould-flow and structural simulation of two specific part geometries supplied by the company. Final deliverables include property data tables, revised simulation model parameters, and a recommendation on the maximum permissible recycled-content fraction for each part category. Results remain confidential for two years following project completion.
partners: Vetropack Industries d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional)

projects.title: Curated Spectral Databases and Machine Learning Pipelines for Small-Molecule Structure Verification
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed two interconnected bottlenecks in computational structure elucidation: the low quality of publicly available NMR and MS spectral metadata, and the absence of well-validated machine-learning pipelines adapted to the compound families most relevant to regional research groups working in natural products and pharmaceutical synthesis. Activities included systematic curation of open spectral repositories, development of a metadata harmonisation pipeline, training and benchmarking of graph neural network and transformer models for shift prediction, and integration of validated models into the SPECINT-2 platform. The project produced a publicly released cleaned spectral dataset of 73 000 structures and updated SPECINT-2 modules used by three partner groups in Serbia and Slovenia.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Computer and Information Science, Slovenia
Institute for Medicinal Plant Research Pančevo, Serbia

projects.title: Automated NMR Quality Control Tools for Synthetic Chemistry Workflows
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A short-term industry contract with SynthoCheck d.o.o., a Novi Sad company providing synthetic chemistry services, to develop and deploy an automated artifact-detection and integration module for their routine ¹H NMR quality-control pipeline. The module was based on a convolutional neural network trained on annotated spectra recorded on the company's 300 MHz instrument. Deliverables included the trained model, an integration plugin for their existing data management system, documentation, and a three-month post-deployment support period. The project resulted in a published methodology paper and provided the group with labelled spectral data that expanded the training corpus for subsequent academic work.
partners: SynthoCheck d.o.o., Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Quantitative Solvent Substitution Maps for Priority Reaction Classes in Serbian Fine Chemical Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated HSP-based solvent substitution protocols for three reaction classes—reductive amination, esterification, and cross-coupling—prioritised through a survey of nine fine-chemical producers in Vojvodina. For each class, a structured workflow combining HSP sphere mapping, LCA screening, and bench-scale yield verification was tested and compiled into a freely accessible decision-support tool distributed as a web application hosted at the Faculty of Technology. Fourteen solvent substitution recommendations were validated at bench scale; six were further tested at 1–10 kg scale at partner companies. The project also funded the construction of the automated HSP mapping station described in the 2024 instrumentation publication.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce – Chemistry and Pharmaceutics Cluster

projects.title: Bio-Based Solvent Integration in Danube Region Specialty Chemical Industries
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project involving three universities and two industry partners from Hungary and Serbia, focused on accelerating the industrial uptake of bio-based solvents in specialty chemical synthesis and polymer processing. Turčanová leads Work Package 2, which covers quantitative solubility parameter characterisation of bio-derived candidates and preparation of comparative LCA profiles for target applications identified by the industry partners. The work package is also responsible for a joint student training school held annually in Novi Sad and Szeged. Results feed into a shared repository of solvent property data accessible to SMEs in both countries.

projects.title: Surface Alkali Phase Dynamics and Carbonate Formation in Fatty Acid Salt Systems Under Variable Atmospheric Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the physical chemistry of residual alkali distribution and CO2-driven carbonate precipitation in sodium and potassium soap matrices under controlled atmosphere conditions representative of storage and distribution environments in the western Balkans. Activities included the development of the depth-resolved micro-titration method, Raman mapping of polymorph gradients, and construction of kinetic phase diagrams for vaterite-to-calcite transformation as functions of CO2 partial pressure and temperature. The project also produced a reference dataset of field carbonation rates for five commercial bar formulations under Novi Sad climate conditions. Three journal articles and one conference contribution resulted from the project.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade

projects.title: Environmental Fate of Soap-Derived Carbonate Particles in Vojvodina Waterways
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project examined the discharge and downstream fate of carbonate-containing soap curd particles generated when laundry and personal care wastewater meets hard groundwater in Vojvodina's drinking water distribution and drainage network. Sampling was conducted at four municipal wastewater treatment plant inlets and three canal sites during summer and winter. Particle characterisation by XRD, SEM-EDS, and ICP-OES showed predominantly calcite with minor proportions of magnesium carbonate. Dissolution modelling suggested that most soap-derived carbonate particles dissolve within 2–5 km under summer conditions but may persist significantly longer in winter. The findings informed a guidance note submitted to the Vojvodina Environmental Protection Agency on curd deposition in drainage channels.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Environmental Protection Agency, Novi Sad
Public Utility Company Vodovod i Kanalizacija, Novi Sad

projects.title: Карактеризација и стандардизација хладно пресованих уља Војводине за примену у прехрамбеној и козметичкој индустрији
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Пројекат је обухватио систематску липидну карактеризацију петнаест врста хладно пресованих уља произведених у Војводини. Узорковање је вршено директно код произвођача у три узастопне производне сезоне. Коришћене аналитичке методе укључивале су GC-FID за масне киселине, HPLC-ELSD за триацилглицероле и HPLC-FLD за токофероле. Паралелно је испитивана оксидативна стабилност Ранцимат тестом. Резултати су обједињени у базу података која служи произвођачима за декларисање и компаративну оцену квалитета. Пројекат је резултовао са три научна рада и пет техничких извештаја достављених произвођачима уља.
partners: Naučni institut za prehrambene tehnologije, Novi Sad
Udruženje proizvođača hladno presovanih ulja Vojvodine (fiktivno)

projects.title: Lipid-Based Emollient Systems from Regional Plant Oils: Composition–Function Relationships for Dermatological Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates correlations between the lipid composition of cold-pressed regional plant oils and their measurable emollient performance in topical preparations. Work packages cover: (1) detailed TAG and minor lipid profiling of twelve selected oils; (2) preparation and stability testing of model w/o and o/w emulsions; (3) in vitro assessment of membrane permeation and occlusion; and (4) a small-scale in vivo study of TEWL and hydration. The aim is to develop a composition-based scoring tool that allows formulators to rank oils by predicted emollient performance without conducting full in vivo trials for each candidate. The project involves one PhD student and two master's students at the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad, with a dermatological validation component carried out in collaboration with the Faculty of Medicine.

Dipartimento di Farmacia, Università degli Studi di Trieste, Italy

projects.title: Procena požarnog rizika višeslojnih tekstilnih konstrukcija u vozilima javnog prevoza
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je usmeren na sistematičnu karakterizaciju požarnog ponašanja višeslojnih tekstilnih sklopova koji se koriste u autobusima i železničkim vozilima. Primenom konusne kalorimetrije, TGA/FTIR sprezanja i testova toksičnosti produkata sagorevanja, formirana je baza podataka za 24 komercijalna materijala. Poseban fokus stavljen je na uticaj starenja (hidrolitičkog i foto-oksidativnog) na promenu parametara zapaljivosti. Rezultati projekta dostavljeni su Privrednoj komori Srbije kao tehnički input za planiranu izmenu domaćih pravilnika o zaštiti od požara u vozilima. U projektu učestvuju istraživači Tehnološkog fakulteta u Novom Sadu i partneri sa Saobraćajnog fakulteta u Beogradu.
partners: Saobraćajni fakultet, Univerzitet u Beogradu
Institut za standardizaciju Srbije

projects.title: Integrated physicochemical–biological treatment strategies for complex textile process effluents in the Pannonian region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TEXWAT brought together research groups from Novi Sad and Pécs to develop and validate combined treatment sequences for textile effluents characteristic of small and medium-sized dyeing and finishing enterprises in the Pannonian basin. The project included laboratory optimisation of coagulation, ozonation and activated sludge steps, a field characterisation campaign covering eight textile plants on both sides of the border, and a pilot demonstration at a partner facility in Vojvodina. Branislava Jovanović led the work package responsible for advanced oxidation process optimisation and integration with biological post-treatment. The project produced treatment design guidelines in Serbian and Hungarian and trained twelve process engineers from participating companies.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Civil Engineering, Hungary
Regional Environmental Protection Agency of Vojvodina, Serbia
Textilpromet d.o.o., Sombor, Serbia

projects.title: Behaviour and removal of mixed surfactant systems in coagulation-based textile wastewater treatment
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SURFCLEAN investigated how mixtures of anionic, nonionic and cationic surfactants, representative of modern textile auxiliaries, interact with coagulants under conditions relevant to industrial practice. The project combined surface tension measurements, zeta potential titration, TOC and HPLC analysis to characterise surfactant behaviour across coagulation pH windows. A secondary objective was to assess the ecotoxicological profile of coagulation sludges arising from surfactant-containing effluents using earthworm and seed germination bioassays. Two master's students and one doctoral candidate contributed experimental work. Outcomes include a dataset of coagulant performance parameters for fourteen surfactant–coagulant combinations and guidance for sludge classification under Serbian waste regulations.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute for Chemistry and Environmental Protection, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Material Yield Optimisation in Small and Medium Textile and Leather Enterprises through Advanced Nesting and Scheduling Methods
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between academic nesting research and production-ready tools usable by small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the Serbian textile and leather sector. Three industrial partners provided real production data, access to their CAD/CAM cutting systems, and pilot environments. The research team developed an integrated software prototype combining an NFP-based nesting solver with a cutting-plan scheduling module and a fabric roll inventory interface. The prototype was tested at two garment manufacturers and one leather goods producer. Key outputs included the CEE benchmark dataset, improvements to cutting-plan roll-assignment algorithms, and a set of practical guidelines for SME adoption. The project supported two Ph.D. students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications.

projects.title: Cross-Sector Benchmarking and Knowledge Transfer for 2D Nesting Optimisation in Central European Manufacturing
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSNEST was a bilateral project between the University of Novi Sad and the Budapest University of Technology and Economics aimed at characterising nesting problem difficulty across manufacturing sectors in both countries and establishing shared benchmark repositories. Activities included joint data collection in Serbian and Hungarian factories, development of a common polygon format and metadata standard, and organisation of two cross-border industrial workshops. The project produced the CEE nesting benchmark dataset and two jointly authored publications. A lightweight web-based nesting assessment tool allowing SMEs to upload their polygon files and receive reference utilisation estimates was developed and made publicly accessible. projects.title: Inclusive Sizing for Apparel: Anthropometric Foundations for Underrepresented Body Groups in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project conducts a multi-region anthropometric survey targeting three population groups underserved by current commercial sizing: women over 60, women with bust circumference above 100 cm, and men with waist-to-hip ratios above 1.0. The core output is a set of evidence-based size system proposals for each group, with accompanying grading rule tables and block pattern templates distributed to SME apparel manufacturers. A web-based tool allowing manufacturers to input their own customer measurement distributions and receive size coverage estimates is under development. Partners include the Faculty of Design and Technologies in Skopje, the Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, and three regional apparel SMEs.

projects.title: Digital Fit Workflow Integration for Small Apparel Manufacturers
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project supported three small apparel manufacturers in Vojvodina in adopting digital fit tools, specifically 3D body scanning for customer measurement collection and CLO3D for pre-production virtual sampling. Activities included staff training, adaptation of existing pattern libraries to digital formats, validation trials comparing virtual and physical samples, and documentation of process changes. The Faculty of Technical Sciences provided scanner access, technical consultancy, and conducted accuracy assessments at each implementation stage. The project produced a practical implementation guide in Serbian and a set of benchmark datasets for fabric simulation parameter calibration relevant to fabric types commonly used by local manufacturers.
partners: Sportika d.o.o., Novi Sad
Konfekcija Bečej d.o.o., Bečej

projects.title: Consumer Data Practices and Behavioural Analytics Capacity in Cross-Border Fashion E-Commerce: Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project examined how small and medium-sized fashion e-retailers in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region collect, store, and use consumer behavioural data for marketing decisions. Tóth led the work package responsible for primary data collection, including the industry survey and retailer case studies, as well as the development of a self-assessment toolkit enabling companies to benchmark their analytics maturity. The project produced three joint publications, a practitioner handbook distributed to 140 companies, and a curriculum module on data-driven marketing incorporated into continuing education programmes at both partner universities. projects.title: Psychographic Drivers of Sustainable Purchase Choices in Online Retail
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PSYSHOP investigates whether and how psychographic consumer characteristics mediate the relationship between stated environmental attitudes and actual sustainable product choices in online retail settings. The project combines survey-based psychographic profiling with behavioural experiments on real e-commerce platforms. Tóth contributes expertise in psychographic segmentation methodology and customer journey modelling, and is responsible for designing and analysing two conjoint experiments on sustainable fashion product pages. The project is coordinated by the Faculty of Economics in Subotica and involves partners from the University of Ljubljana. Expected outputs include four journal articles and a set of evidence-based guidelines for e-retailers seeking to promote sustainable product lines.

projects.title: Environmental Cost Accounting for Natural-Fibre Textile Chains in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FIBRECOST aimed to develop a shared environmental cost accounting toolkit for small and medium textile enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region that source natural fibres. The project produced a harmonised LCA-based inventory template covering flax and hemp cultivation in Vojvodina and southern Hungary, wet processing in both countries, and transport logistics. Filipović led the work package on inventory data collection and quality assessment, coordinating field measurement campaigns at four partner facilities. The project delivered an open-access database of 18 unit process datasets and a simplified screening tool for SME use, tested by two pilot companies. A joint training workshop for 34 enterprise representatives was held in Subotica in 2022.

projects.title: Life Cycle Environmental Impact Quantification of Serbian Natural-Fibre Garment Producers
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: NATIMPACT is a two-year applied research project supporting five Serbian garment manufacturers that use domestically grown linen and hemp to quantify and reduce their product-level carbon and water footprints. The project develops sector-specific foreground inventory data through on-site measurements and combines these with updated background datasets in openLCA. For each participating company, a cradle-to-gate LCA report is produced in a format compatible with emerging EU Green Claims requirements. A secondary objective is to test simplified screening calculators against full LCA results to determine at what level of accuracy the simplified tools can substitute for detailed studies for routine company reporting. Filipović serves as principal investigator, with two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher involved.

projects.title: Ambulatory Autonomic Monitoring for Occupational Stress Assessment Using Multi-Modal Wearables
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AUTONOVA addressed the gap between controlled laboratory stress studies and real occupational environments by developing an end-to-end pipeline for ambulatory autonomic monitoring. The project produced hardware firmware updates for the in-house wristband platform, a cloud-compatible data management schema, and a validated set of signal quality and feature extraction algorithms suited to noisy daily-life recordings. A field study was conducted with 80 administrative and production staff at two companies in Vojvodina over four-week periods. The resulting dataset and open-source processing toolkit were released publicly. The project supported two doctoral students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications.

Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Physiological Load Estimation for Adaptive Driver Assistance Using Wearable Biosensors
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SENSEDRIVE investigated the feasibility of estimating driver cognitive load in real time from wrist-worn EDA and PPG signals and transmitting load estimates via CAN bus to a prototype adaptive assistance system developed by the industry partner. The project combined simulator-based protocol development at the University of Novi Sad with road trials in instrumented vehicles. A lightweight edge classifier meeting automotive timing constraints was a primary deliverable. The project established the methodological basis for a larger Horizon Europe application currently in preparation.

Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad – Chair of Mechatronics

projects.title: Motivational Communication Strategies for Chronic Disease Prevention in Primary Care Settings in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated the translation of laboratory-tested motivational communication principles into scalable brief interventions delivered in primary care consultations. The project trained 45 general practitioners and nurses in autonomy-supportive communication, developed and validated a Serbian-language motivational communication fidelity coding scheme, and conducted a stepped-wedge cluster trial across 12 primary care centres in Vojvodina targeting physical inactivity and poor dietary behaviour in adults with elevated cardiometabolic risk. The trial enrolled 680 patients followed over 18 months. Secondary objectives included identifying patient-level moderators of intervention response and producing a freely accessible practitioner training manual in Serbian.

projects.title: Persuasion Research and Health Communication in Central and Eastern Europe: A Collaborative Network
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral scientific cooperation project between the University of Novi Sad and the Institute of Experimental Psychology at the Slovak Academy of Sciences in Bratislava, co-funded by the Serbian and Slovak science ministries. The project established a shared dataset of health communication experiments conducted in both countries, enabling cross-national comparison of message framing effects across linguistic and cultural contexts. Lekić led the work package responsible for harmonising experimental protocols and outcome measures across sites. A jointly authored monograph on health persuasion research in post-socialist European contexts is planned as a final output.
partners: Institute of Experimental Psychology, Slovak Academy of Sciences, Bratislava

projects.title: Terrain-Adaptive Quantification of Training Load in Competitive Road Cycling
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops and validates a terrain-adaptive framework for quantifying both external and internal training load in competitive road cyclists operating across the diverse terrain of the Western Balkan region. Core activities include the construction of a gradient-corrected normalised power metric, longitudinal validation of perceived exertion anchoring protocols, and integration of HRV-based fatigue indices with mechanically derived load scores. Field data are collected across three competitive seasons in collaboration with two regional cycling clubs. A software toolkit enabling coaches to apply the framework using commercially available devices is being developed and will be made freely available to sports federations.

Institute of Sports Medicine, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Sport Adaptation of Internal–External Load Coupling Models for Endurance Athletes
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A provincially funded project that extended terrain-based load modelling originally developed for road cycling to two additional endurance disciplines—cross-country skiing (roller ski) and triathlon cycling segments—practised competitively in Vojvodina and neighbouring regions. The project produced a comparative dataset of internal–external load coupling across disciplines, identified discipline-specific calibration constants, and delivered a short-course training programme for sports science graduates in applied load monitoring methodology. Four master's theses were completed within the project framework.
