Vojvodina Triathlon Association, Novi Sad

projects.title: Modular Reconfigurable Fixturing for In-line Quality Control in Miniature Electronic Assembly
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MICROFIX addressed the lack of flexible, quickly reconfigurable fixturing solutions for small-scale contract electronics manufacturers in Serbia who process short-run, high-mix product portfolios. The project developed a kinematic coupling-based modular fixture platform, a sensor suite for confirming correct insert seating, and integration software linking fixture identity to in-line inspection parameter sets. A prototype cell was deployed and evaluated at a partner facility. The project produced eight journal and conference publications, one defended Ph.D. thesis, and a functional prototype transferred to the industry partner for continued evaluation. Total budget was approximately 4.8 million RSD.

projects.title: In-line Assembly Measurement Methods for Cross-Border Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ASSMEAS brought together three universities and two industrial partners from Serbia and Hungary to transfer and adapt in-line optical and tactile measurement methods to the capabilities of small and medium-sized electronics manufacturers in the border region. The University of Novi Sad team led the work package on measurement uncertainty quantification and wrote the shared calibration protocols adopted by both industrial partners. The project delivered workshops for 47 SME technicians, two freely available calibration guideline documents, and validated in-line inspection setups at the two partner manufacturing sites. projects.title: Tile-Based Spatial Data Infrastructure for the Vojvodina Region: Optimised Rendering and Progressive Delivery
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to design and validate a complete web-based spatial data infrastructure for the Vojvodina Administrative District, replacing an ageing WMS-based geoportal with a modern vector tile delivery system. Work packages covered: spatial data harmonisation and import from cadastral, land-use, and hydrological databases; tile generation pipeline optimisation; progressive transmission protocol design; and a public-facing web mapping application. The project produced a reference tile server implementation, three peer-reviewed publications, and a demonstration geoportal integrating data from 45 municipalities. One MSc thesis and two undergraduate theses were completed within the project.

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Spatial Data Tile Services for Environmental Monitoring
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSGEO addressed inconsistencies in spatial data tile services on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border that hampered cross-border environmental monitoring workflows. Ivković led the work package on tile format harmonisation and rendering pipeline alignment, ensuring that vector tile outputs from Serbian cadastral and land-cover databases could be consumed by Hungarian regional GIS platforms without manual reprojection or re-encoding. The project developed a shared tile schema specification and a conversion toolkit released under an open-source licence. Two pilot applications were deployed for flood risk mapping in the Bačka and Baranya border zones.

projects.title: Wearable Sensor Monitoring of Lower-Limb Symmetry for Injury Prevention in Sub-Elite Football
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SYMFOOT investigates whether longitudinal IMU-based lower-limb symmetry monitoring can reduce soft-tissue injury incidence in sub-elite Serbian football clubs. The project follows 120 male players across two full competitive seasons, collecting fortnightly screening data and linking asymmetry indices to prospective injury outcomes. A secondary aim is to develop and validate a lightweight data-processing pipeline suitable for use by club physiotherapists without specialised software. Partner clubs provide access to players and training calendars, while the Faculty of Technical Sciences contributes embedded systems expertise for firmware optimisation of the Shimmer3 platform. Outputs will include normative symmetry reference data for the regional-league population, a practitioner-facing interpretation guide, and at least three peer-reviewed publications.

projects.title: Biomechanical Criteria for Safe Return-to-Play After Lower-Limb Surgery in Team Sport Athletes
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BIORETURN was a cross-border project comparing return-to-play biomechanical profiles between post-surgical athletes at clinical rehabilitation centres in Novi Sad and Pécs. The Serbian team contributed IMU-based field assessments of 45 post-ACLR and 22 post-Achilles tendon repair athletes, while the Hungarian partners provided laboratory-grade isokinetic and force plate data. The shared dataset was used to establish bilateral symmetry thresholds that combined IMU metrics with strength ratios. The project produced a joint clinical recommendation document distributed to physiotherapy departments at both partner universities and resulted in two joint conference presentations and one journal co-authored publication.

projects.title: Adaptive Visualisation Interfaces for Expert Users in Regional Public Institutions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ADAPTA-VIS examined how adaptive information visualisation interfaces can be designed and evaluated for expert users in Serbian regional public institutions—specifically in environmental monitoring, archival management, and agricultural advisory services. The project combined longitudinal user studies at partner institutions with iterative prototype development cycles. A central output was a design pattern library for adaptive disclosure in data-dense professional interfaces, validated through controlled experiments with approximately 120 participants across three domains. The project also produced a freely available usability evaluation toolkit tailored to domain-specific expert interfaces, which has been adopted by two partner institutions for internal procurement assessments. projects.title: Digital Craft Interfaces: Bridging Traditional Craft Knowledge and Digital Fabrication Tools for Small Producers
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DIGICRAFT addressed the interface barriers that prevent small craft producers in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region from adopting digital fabrication tools such as laser cutters and CNC milling machines. Ninkov led the work package on interface design and user testing, which produced localised interface guidelines and a set of simplified control panel prototypes evaluated with 30 craft producers at partner makerspaces in Subotica and Szeged. The project found that vocabulary mismatch between engineering terminology embedded in standard machine interfaces and craft-domain language was a primary barrier to adoption, and proposed a domain-vocabulary substitution layer for machine control software. The project resulted in three tested interface prototypes and a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) practitioner guide.

projects.title: Image-Based Faunal Monitoring Platform for Pannonian Protected Areas

Activities included expansion of the Pannonian Coleoptera image reference collection to over 18,000 specimens and 600 species, retraining and validation of CNN identification models, deployment of image-trap hardware at monitoring sites, and integration of outputs into the provincial nature conservation information system. The project also produced standardised monitoring protocols adopted provisionally by the Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province for routine invertebrate surveys.

projects.title: Life Cycle Assessment Methodologies for Tourism Systems in the Danube Region

A joint capacity-building programme trained 34 hotel and travel agency representatives in simplified carbon footprinting. Project outputs include a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) LCA practitioner guide and an open-access dataset of 62 regionally calibrated emission factors for tourism activities.

projects.title: Robust Ensemble Learning for Imbalanced Operational Data in Serbian Industry

The main scientific outputs were a set of empirically grounded recommendations for pipeline configuration, a benchmark suite of ten operational datasets with standardised imbalance statistics, and a publicly released Python package implementing the recommended pipeline with configurable components. projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between general-purpose columnar databases and the specific write and query patterns of high-frequency industrial sensor deployments. Work packages covered codec selection heuristics, mixed-rate schema design, and cost-model-guided query planning. A prototype engine extension was developed and tested against live data streams from two partner facilities in Vojvodina. The project funded two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. Hardware acquired includes a four-node NVMe cluster used for reproducible benchmarks. Collaboration with the Budapest University of Technology and Economics provided access to complementary datasets from Hungarian utility-monitoring infrastructure.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia

projects.title: Low-Cost Data Infrastructure for Precision Agriculture Sensor Networks in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGRISENSE deployed a network of 180 low-cost soil and microclimate sensors across agricultural land in Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád County. Hadžić led the data management work package, responsible for the on-premises storage layer, compression pipeline, and a web-based dashboard for agronomists. The irregular-timestamp columnar layout work published in 2024 emerged directly from this project. The storage system runs on a single rack-mounted server provided by the Serbian partner and has been operational since mid-2023, ingesting approximately 2 million records per day.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Csongrád-Csanád County Agricultural Advisory Centre (invented)
NTP Agro Solutions d.o.o. Novi Sad (invented)

projects.title: Integrated Sensor Fusion and Kinetic Modelling for Real-Time Control of Wine and Bioethanol Fermentation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FERMSENSE addresses the gap between laboratory-validated process analytical tools and their routine deployment in Serbian fermentation industries. The project combines dielectric spectroscopy, inline NIR, and off-gas analysis into a unified sensor fusion architecture connected to a real-time kinetic model running on an embedded computing platform. The model issues control recommendations for substrate feeding rate and cooling setpoint. Field trials are conducted at two partner sites: a mid-sized winery in Fruška Gora and a bioethanol producer in Zrenjanin. The project employs two PhD students and is expected to deliver a validated soft-sensor package with open-source model code and operator-facing dashboard software. Industry partners contribute process data and co-fund consumables.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Vinarija Sunčani Breg d.o.o., Irig
BioEtanol Zrenjanin d.o.o.

projects.title: Kinetic and Stoichiometric Modelling of Hexose–Pentose Co-Fermentation for Second-Generation Bioethanol
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HEXYPENT aimed to improve bioethanol yields from agricultural lignocellulosic residues—primarily corn stover and sunflower husks available in the Vojvodina–southern Hungary border region—through better understanding of co-fermentation kinetics in engineered yeast strains. Mamužić led the work package responsible for kinetic model development and parameter estimation, working alongside Hungarian partners who provided strain engineering and hydrolysate preparation. The project produced shared datasets on xylose co-fermentation kinetics, a joint parameter estimation protocol, and training materials used in two student exchange visits. Results fed into a feasibility study for a small demonstration biorefinery.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Bioengineering, University of Szeged
Regional Development Agency Subotica–Szabadka

projects.title: Scalable Optimisation Methods for Skill-Constrained Workforce Scheduling in Service Industries
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates decomposition and hybrid metaheuristic methods for workforce scheduling problems that arise in healthcare, logistics, and field service contexts. The primary research objectives are: developing tighter formulations for skill-assignment sub-problems, designing adaptive large neighbourhood search operators that exploit problem structure, and constructing an open benchmark library for the skill-constrained scheduling problem class. The project supports two doctoral students and one postdoctoral researcher. Industrial data were contributed under confidentiality agreements by three companies operating in Vojvodina. A secondary objective is a web-based scheduling prototype intended for validation with hospital scheduling staff. The project is funded through a competitive IDEAS grant.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Mathematics, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Scheduling Practices in Public Health Institutions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSCHED brought together scheduling researchers and hospital administrators from Hungary and Serbia to compare scheduling regulations, tool availability, and staff satisfaction in public health institutions on both sides of the border. Kapor led the work package on computational methods, responsible for developing a shared modelling framework that could accommodate both Hungarian and Serbian collective labour agreement rules. The project produced joint training materials for scheduling coordinators, a comparative regulatory report, and a prototype scheduling assistance tool deployed in a pilot ward at two partner hospitals. The project also supported an exchange visit programme for doctoral students.
partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Science and Informatics, Hungary
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Bács-Kiskun County Hospital, Kecskemét, Hungary

projects.title: Wellbeing Measurement Standards for Organisations in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to establish psychometric standards for measuring occupational wellbeing in Serbian and regional organisational contexts. Activities include a systematic audit of instruments currently used in HR and occupational health practice in Serbia, the construction and cross-validation of a modular wellbeing assessment battery adapted for different occupational groups (healthcare, education, ICT, and public administration), and the development of open-access scoring norms. The project involves data collection from approximately 2,400 employees across four sectors and three geographic regions of Serbia. A methodological focus is placed on measurement invariance testing and the conditions under which cross-sector comparisons are valid. Outputs will include validated instruments, published norm tables, and a freely available R package for scale scoring and reporting.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Psychology, Belgrade
Faculty of Medicine, University of Kragujevac

projects.title: Human-Capital Metrics and Financial Performance Linkages in Serbian Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project built and validated a suite of quantitative linkage models connecting firm-level human-capital indicators—training expenditure, turnover rates, competence assessments—to financial performance metrics including return on assets, operating margin and market-to-book ratios. The empirical backbone was an original panel dataset covering 380 Serbian manufacturing firms over seven years, assembled by combining Business Registers Agency financial data with a repeated HR survey conducted by the project team. The project produced methodological guidelines for constructing human-capital stock indices under data constraints typical of transition economies, delivered three peer-reviewed publications and trained two PhD students in advanced panel econometrics.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Niš
Science Technology Park Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Human Capital Accounting Harmonisation in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSHCAP investigates whether harmonised human-capital accounting templates can be applied consistently across the Hungarian–Serbian border region, where firms frequently operate in both jurisdictions under different accounting regimes. Edit Horváth leads the work package responsible for developing the harmonised template and piloting it in 40 firms (20 per country). The work package involves structured interviews, document analysis and a validation workshop with accountants and HR professionals. Outputs include a bilingual accounting guidance note, a comparative regulatory analysis and a set of recommendations directed at the relevant national standards bodies. The project runs in parallel with a complementary package on workforce mobility led by the Hungarian partner.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs

Baranya County Enterprise Development Foundation

projects.title: Adaptive Data-Driven Anomaly Detection for Cyber-Physical Production Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a family of adaptive anomaly detection methods for multivariate sensor streams in manufacturing cyber-physical systems, with particular focus on handling non-stationarity caused by regime changes and gradual drift. Core contributions included the extreme-value-theory adaptive thresholding scheme, a federated monitoring architecture for multi-site deployment, and an annotated benchmark collection of six industrial datasets with reproducible evaluation protocols. The laboratory testbed was extended with additional vibration and pressure sensors during the project period. Two doctoral dissertations were completed under project funding, and seven journal papers were published. Results were transferred to two manufacturing companies in the Vojvodina region through technology-transfer workshops.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Kragujevac
Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia

projects.title: Interoperable Monitoring Middleware for Industrial IoT with Embedded Statistical Quality Control
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project addressed the integration of statistical process control logic into IoT middleware platforms used by small and medium-sized manufacturers in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The Novi Sad team led the work package on SPC algorithm design and embedded deployment, contributing drift-robust anomaly scoring modules certified to run on Cortex-M class microcontrollers. The Hungarian partner coordinated middleware architecture and communication protocols, while a regional chamber of commerce facilitated access to pilot companies. Three pilot deployments were completed: a food-packaging line, a metal-pressing workshop, and a grain-drying facility. Evaluation covered detection latency, energy consumption, and false-alarm frequency over 12-month monitoring periods.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Information Technology and Bionics, Pázmány Péter Catholic University, Budapest

projects.title: Interoperable Data Integration Methods for Regional Public Administration
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed reusable ontology-driven integration components for public administration data in the Western Balkans region, focusing on cadastral, civil registry, and urban planning datasets. Work packages addressed schema matching under multilingual conditions, probabilistic record linkage for cross-registry deduplication, and declarative data quality rule specification adapted to the legislative constraints of Serbian administrative data. The project produced an open-source toolkit, two benchmark datasets released publicly, and a set of integration guidelines adopted in a pilot by two municipal administrations in Vojvodina. Four researchers and two PhD students were involved throughout the project duration.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Sarajevo

projects.title: Cross-Platform Agricultural Data Linkage for Precision Farming Decision Support
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: AGRILINK brought together researchers in data integration and agronomists to develop a data linkage layer connecting soil analysis laboratories, precision irrigation platforms, and remote sensing providers active in the AP Vojvodina region. Slađana Ranković led the work package on schema harmonisation and ontology construction, producing a shared agricultural data ontology and a set of tested schema-to-ontology mapping procedures. The project resulted in a pilot integration covering three farms with a combined area of approximately 900 hectares and informed subsequent larger-scale integration work published in a journal article in 2022.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
AgroSense d.o.o. (fictional SME, Novi Sad)

projects.title: Serbian Language Resources for Specialised Natural Language Processing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SRSLAN aimed to expand and systematise annotated language resources for Serbian in three specialised registers: legal, medical, and financial. The project produced three domain corpora totalling approximately 7 million annotated tokens, an updated version of the SrpNovine NER benchmark, and a valency dictionary for 3,200 Serbian verbs. A secondary objective was the development and public release of morphological processing tools adapted to each domain. The project employed two postdoctoral researchers and four student annotators at the University of Novi Sad and collaborated with the Jožef Stefan Institute in Ljubljana for cross-Slavic resource alignment. All outputs were deposited in the CLARIN.SI repository under open licences.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana
Institute for Serbian Language of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade

projects.title: Multilingual Information Detection Across the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MIDANUBE addressed the need for multilingual text analysis tools in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region, focusing on Serbian and Hungarian as administratively and economically important language pairs. Dragišić led the work package responsible for Serbian-side corpus collection and annotation, covering approximately 3 million tokens of cross-border news and public administration documents. The project developed a bilingual named-entity linking system capable of aligning entity mentions across the two typologically dissimilar languages. End-user evaluation was conducted with two regional public administration bodies. The Serbian annotation infrastructure and trained models produced within MIDANUBE were integrated into the NERSrp 2.0 benchmark release.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

Regional Development Agency of Bačka, Novi Sad
Pázmány Péter Catholic University, Budapest

projects.title: Stability and Control of DC Microgrids with High Penetration of Constant-Power Loads
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigates the conditions under which DC microgrids with a large fraction of CPLs remain stable and recoverable after faults or large disturbances. The work combines analytical large-signal stability assessment (sum-of-squares polynomial methods, Lyapunov functions) with hardware-in-the-loop validation on a multi-node testbed. Biljana Grbić contributes to the converter-level control design and experimental validation tasks, specifically implementing and testing sliding-mode and passivity-based controllers on the laboratory prototype. The project also examines interactions between individual converter controllers when multiple units share a common bus, and develops guidelines for droop coefficient selection that balance current sharing accuracy with stability margins.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
School of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Thermal Reliability Assessment Methods for IGBT Modules in Traction Inverter Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between standardised accelerated power-cycling tests and the variable-amplitude thermal loading experienced by IGBT modules in real railway traction inverters. Work packages covered: (i) thermal impedance characterisation of commercially available traction-grade modules using controlled transient measurements; (ii) development and validation of a damage accumulation framework based on rainflow-counted junction-temperature histories; (iii) implementation of a real-time remaining-useful-life estimator on embedded hardware. An 110 kW laboratory traction drive was instrumented as the primary test platform. The project resulted in three journal papers and a publicly available dataset of power-cycling results for two die-attach materials.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Niš, Faculty of Electronic Engineering

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Thermal Testing Procedures for Rail Power Electronics
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RAILHEAT brought together research groups at the University of Novi Sad and the Budapest University of Technology and Economics to compare and harmonise thermal testing methodologies for power electronic modules used in rail rolling stock. The Novi Sad group contributed thermal transient measurement infrastructure and power-cycling test protocols, while the Budapest group provided finite-element validation models and access to industrial module samples. The project produced a joint testing guideline document adopted by both institutions, a comparative study of measurement uncertainty across the two laboratories, and three jointly supervised master theses covering thermal characterisation topics.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Department of Electric Power Engineering
Vojvodina Regional Development Agency

projects.title: Gate Driver Circuits and Loss Characterisation Methods for GaN-Based High-Frequency Power Converters
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates gate-driver design constraints and switching-loss measurement methodology for enhancement-mode GaN HEMTs in hard-switched converters operating between 500 kHz and 2 MHz. Core activities include construction of a calorimetric loss bench traceable to national standards, experimental characterisation of common-source inductance effects across a library of fifteen PCB layout variants, development of a SPICE-compatible behavioural switching model, and validation of an adaptive gate-drive voltage controller. The project involves two researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and one from the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš. Results are disseminated through peer-reviewed journal articles and one short course offered to industry engineers at NTP Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Wide-Bandgap Power Electronics for High-Efficiency Industrial Converters
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral research and capacity-building project between the University of Novi Sad and the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca aimed at developing shared testing infrastructure and joint educational materials for wide-bandgap power semiconductor characterisation. The Novi Sad team led the work package on switching-transient measurement methodology, contributing the double-pulse test fixture and calorimetric bench designs. The Cluj-Napoca team led thermal modelling activities. Joint summer schools were held in 2020 and 2021, each attended by approximately 25 students and engineers from both countries. Two jointly supervised doctoral students are registered under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania

projects.title: Compressed Sensing Architectures for Real-Time Spectrum Monitoring in Heterogeneous Wireless Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SPECTRA-CS investigates sub-Nyquist compressed sensing architectures for continuous wideband spectrum monitoring across the 80–900 MHz range, with deployment scenarios drawn from urban and industrial environments in the Vojvodina region. The project combines theoretical work on structured measurement matrices and recovery algorithm design with a hardware prototyping activity centred on FPGA and embedded platforms. A key deliverable is an open dataset of annotated spectrum occupancy recordings collected at four monitoring sites in Novi Sad and surrounding municipalities, available for use by the research community. The project team comprises four researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and one external collaborator from the Faculty of Electronic Engineering, Niš.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Intelligent Spectrum Management for Dense IoT Deployments in Smart City Environments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: IoT-SENSE addresses spectrum congestion in sub-GHz ISM bands caused by growing LoRaWAN and Sigfox deployments in cross-border smart city pilot sites in Subotica (Serbia) and Baja (Hungary). The project deploys a network of low-cost compressed sensing receiver nodes that perform distributed spectrum occupancy estimation and report aggregated occupancy maps to a central server. Jokić leads the work package on reconstruction algorithm design and adaptation, focusing on structured sparsity models suited to the periodic transmission patterns of IoT devices. The project involves two university partners and one municipal technology company from each country.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics
City of Subotica Smart Infrastructure Office
Baja Municipal Technology Centre

projects.title: Millimeter-Wave Backhaul Modeling for Dense Urban Heterogeneous Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed analytical models for millimeter-wave backhaul performance in dense urban deployments, combining stochastic geometry with empirical blockage data from the city of Novi Sad. Activities included field measurement campaigns to characterize building density and height distributions in three urban zones, construction of calibrated blockage process models, and derivation of end-to-end coverage and rate expressions for integrated access and backhaul architectures. Software tools implementing the analytical framework were released as open-source MATLAB packages. The project supported two doctoral students and produced six peer-reviewed publications. A technical report was submitted to the Serbian Ministry of Science summarizing deployment guidelines for operators.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
School of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Cooperation in Next-Generation Wireless Network Modeling
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project brings together researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest to build shared tools and datasets for modeling next-generation wireless networks in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Tibor Pásztor leads the work package on stochastic channel and interference modeling, responsible for constructing joint measurement databases, harmonizing propagation measurement methodologies across both institutions, and developing a common simulation platform. The project also includes a student exchange program and two joint workshops per year. Outputs include a shared open dataset of urban propagation measurements from Novi Sad, Subotica, and Pécs, and a prototype network planning tool validated against these datasets.
partners: Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Óbuda University, Budapest
City of Subotica Development Agency

projects.title: Ricean Channel Modelling and Statistical Signal Processing for Massive MIMO Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated channel estimation, covariance acquisition, and pilot contamination mitigation for massive MIMO systems under spatially correlated Ricean fading conditions relevant to fixed wireless access and dense urban deployments. The work combined analytical derivations based on random matrix theory and Bayesian estimation with Monte Carlo simulation campaigns and a limited measurement component using the USRP testbed at FTN. Key deliverables included closed-form MSE bounds for Ricean MMSE estimators, a pilot assignment algorithm exploiting the angle-domain structure of covariance matrices, and an open-source simulation package for Ricean massive MIMO system-level evaluation. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight journal and conference publications.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Signal Processing and Estimation Algorithms for Massive and Large-Scale Systems towards 6G
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: SEAMLESS-6G is a collaborative European research project targeting channel estimation and interference management for next-generation radio access networks, including extremely large aperture arrays and cell-free architectures. The Faculty of Technical Sciences team leads the work package on near-field channel modelling and estimation, contributing analytical frameworks for polar-domain sparse recovery and measurement-based validation. Partners from Germany, Italy, Turkey, and Serbia jointly develop simulation platforms, channel models, and prototype demonstrations. The FTN group's specific contributions include the compressed-sensing estimator for near-field conditions and the data-aided covariance tracking algorithm for slowly time-varying environments. Project outcomes will feed into standardisation contributions to 3GPP Release 20 and beyond.
partners: Institute for Communications Technology, Leibniz University Hannover (coordinator)
Department of Information Engineering, University of Padova
Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Middle East Technical University
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Secrecy Rate Enhancement in Cooperative Relay Networks with Active and Passive Threats
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated information-theoretic secrecy capacity in cooperative relay topologies under both passive eavesdropping and active jamming threats. The main activities included deriving tighter secrecy capacity bounds for multi-relay and full-duplex architectures, developing power allocation and relay selection strategies that optimise secrecy outage probability, and validating analytical results using the department's software-defined radio testbed. The project supported two doctoral students and produced nine journal and conference publications. A secondary objective was the development of a MATLAB-based toolbox for numerical evaluation of secrecy metrics under arbitrary fading statistics, which has been made publicly available through the Faculty of Technical Sciences repository.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
School of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Wideband Linearisation of Power Amplifiers for Next-Generation Wireless Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WIDELIN addresses the growing bandwidth demands on base-station power amplifiers driven by 5G carrier aggregation. The project develops behavioural models that capture both fast electrical and slow thermal memory effects across signal bandwidths up to 200 MHz, and implements corresponding DPD algorithms on FPGA hardware. Activities include: construction of a wideband measurement testbed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences; development of a GaN PA device characterisation library; design and hardware-in-the-loop testing of LSTM-based and GMP-based DPD; and co-design of crest factor reduction and DPD to minimise joint distortion. The project employs two PhD students and produces open measurement datasets for the regional research community.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

projects.title: Dual-Band PA Linearisation Techniques for Coexisting 4G and 5G Deployments
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This shorter project, funded by the Provincial Secretariat, explored concurrent dual-band DPD for scenarios where mobile operators simultaneously serve legacy LTE and new 5G NR users from a single shared PA hardware platform. The work covered sub-band observation receiver design, polyphase filter bank decomposition, and cross-band intermodulation characterisation. Practical experiments were conducted on a broadband GaN Doherty amplifier testbed. The project supported one master's thesis student and produced two conference papers and one journal submission.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Channel Characterisation and Beamforming Optimisation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces in Indoor Sub-6 GHz Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates channel modelling and passive beamforming for RIS deployments in indoor sub-6 GHz environments, targeting enterprise and industrial WiFi scenarios. Activities include measurement campaigns in office and industrial floor plans, development of geometry-based stochastic channel models calibrated to measured data, and derivation of computationally tractable beamforming optimisation algorithms under partial channel state information. A 32×32 PIN-diode RIS prototype was designed and fabricated for over-the-air experiments. The project has produced seven peer-reviewed publications and one co-supervised doctoral thesis. Partners include the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca and TU Dresden, who contribute measurement infrastructure and algorithmic validation.
partners: Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania
TU Dresden, Germany
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Smart Indoor Coverage Extension Using Passive and Semi-Passive Reflective Elements
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SMARTCOVER focused on the experimental assessment of fixed and tunable passive reflective panels for indoor 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz coverage extension in university and small-office environments. The project funded a channel sounder upgrade, acquisition of PIN-diode component sets, and fabrication of three prototype panels of different element spacings. Measurement data were collected in five buildings on the University of Novi Sad campus. Key outputs included a path-loss dataset released publicly and two conference publications. The project provided preliminary results that informed the subsequent RISINDOOR application.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Graph Neural Network Methods for Topology-Aware State Estimation in Active Distribution Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed GNN-based methods for the joint problem of topology identification and state estimation in medium-voltage distribution networks operating under incomplete observability. Activities included construction of a benchmark simulation framework using anonymised feeder topology data from Vojvodina, training and evaluation of GCN, GAT, and GraphSAGE architectures under varying measurement densities, and investigation of transfer learning and physics-informed training strategies. A dataset of synthetic feeder operating snapshots was produced and made available to the research community. The project involved collaboration with the University of Niš and the Politehnica University of Bucharest and supported the doctoral work of two PhD students. Results were published in four journal papers and two conference proceedings.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Politehnica University of Bucharest, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Distribution Network Monitoring with Shared Data Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMON addressed the technical and regulatory challenges of monitoring distribution network operating states along the Hungary–Serbia border, where power flows across interconnections are observable from neither side alone. The project established a shared data exchange protocol and a joint state estimation framework combining measurements from both grid operators. Nedeljković led the work package on estimation algorithms, contributing the WLS and early GNN methods for incomplete observability. A pilot deployment using synthetic data mirroring the actual cross-border feeder was demonstrated to both grid operators. The project also produced training materials for technical staff at the participating utilities on smart metering data quality management.

projects.title: Flexibility Resources in Residential Distribution Networks: Aggregation, Optimisation, and Market Integration
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FLEXRES developed methods for quantifying, aggregating, and commercially deploying the flexibility of residential electric loads—primarily heat pumps and EV chargers—in the Serbian distribution system. The project produced validated virtual battery models for three appliance classes, a distributed MPC scheduler for multi-feeder networks, and a market-readiness assessment for demand response aggregators under the post-2021 Serbian balancing market rules. An instrumented testbed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences monitored 65 EV charging sessions and 120 smart meter endpoints over 18 months. Results were shared with the Serbian Energy Agency through two workshops and contributed to a public consultation on aggregator access rules.

projects.title: Adriatic–Danubian Corridor Flexibility Exchange for Residential and Commercial Prosumers
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: ADRIAFLEX is a Horizon Europe research and innovation action involving seven partners from Serbia, Romania, Slovenia, Italy, and Greece. The project develops cross-border flexibility exchange mechanisms for prosumer aggregators operating in different national regulatory contexts. Nataša Milošević leads Work Package 3, which covers optimal scheduling algorithms and aggregator decision support tools. The Novi Sad team contributes the virtual battery aggregation library developed in FLEXRES and conducts hardware-in-the-loop validation experiments. The project aims to produce open-source scheduling software and policy briefs for three national regulators by 2026.

projects.title: Frequency and Energy Management in Inverter-Based Islanded Microgrids
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi razvojem strategija upravljanja frekvencijom i energijom u autonomnim mikromrežama sa visokim udelom inverterskih izvora. Istraživanjem su obuhvaćene metode emulacije inercije, koordinisano upravljanje baterijskim sistemima za skladištenje energije i algoritmi za rekonfiguraciju mreže pri ispadu jednog od izvora. Vladimir Bogićević učestvuje u razvoju algoritama za adaptivnu emulaciju inercije i sprovođenju eksperimentalne verifikacije na laboratorijskoj platformi FTN-a. Planirana je izrada i validacija sveobuhvatnog simulacionog modela mikromreže koji objedinjuje termalne, fotonaponske i baterijske jedinice. Rezultati su namenjeni primeni u industrijskim i komunalnim mikromrežama na području AP Vojvodine.
partners: Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Elektrotehnički fakultet, Univerzitet u Beogradu

projects.title: Hybrid Energy Storage Control and Sizing for Reliable Off-Grid Power Supply in Rural Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the absence of validated sizing and control methods for supercapacitor–battery hybrids in the specific load and climate conditions of rural Serbia. It combines three-year field measurement campaigns at four off-grid sites (two agricultural, one telecom, one small workshop) with laboratory ageing tests and the development of open-source sizing and control software tools. Key deliverables include a degradation-aware sizing toolbox, an embedded adaptive power-split controller prototype, and a publicly available dataset of off-grid load profiles. Two Ph.D. students are supported within the project. The tools are intended to be transferable to small engineering firms and rural electrification planners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Institute for Electrical Engineering Mihajlo Pupin, Belgrade

projects.title: Green and Affordable Storage Technologies for Off-Grid Microgrids in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: GREENSTORE is a cross-border cooperation project between Serbian and Romanian partners aimed at demonstrating hybrid energy storage prototypes at two pilot sites: an off-grid agri-tourism facility near Vršac (Serbia) and a rural health post in Timiș County (Romania). The Serbian team, led by Vlaisavljević, is responsible for work package 2, covering system design, control implementation, and performance monitoring. The project deploys 1.2 kWh LiFePO4 battery modules paired with 1200 F supercapacitor banks at each site, both controlled by the MPC algorithm developed within the team. Monitoring data are shared via a joint web platform and will inform regional rural electrification guidelines prepared by the Romanian partner.

projects.title: Harmonic Mitigation Strategies for Multi-Level Inverter-Fed Industrial Drives in Medium-Voltage Distribution Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated harmonic emission and mitigation strategies for cascaded H-bridge and neutral-point-clamped inverter drives connected to 6 kV and 10 kV industrial distribution networks. Work packages covered reformulated SHE-PWM methods, passive and hybrid active filter design, network-level harmonic interaction modelling in PSCAD, and a measurement campaign at two industrial sites in Vojvodina. The project involved collaboration with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and a local industrial partner from the food processing sector. Results included improved SHE-PWM formulations tolerant to DC-link imbalance, validated filter design procedures, and a publicly available measurement dataset from the industrial sites.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia
Agroind Vojvodina d.o.o., Zrenjanin, Serbia

projects.title: Upgrade of Multi-Level Drive Laboratory for Medium-Voltage Power Electronics Research and Teaching
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This equipment-focused project funded the procurement and integration of a seven-level cascaded H-bridge inverter testbed, a Yokogawa WT1800E precision power analyser, and associated gate-driver boards into the power electronics laboratory at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The upgraded facility supports both research on SHE-PWM and model predictive control strategies and postgraduate laboratory exercises. A set of six structured laboratory exercises was developed alongside the equipment installation and has been used in the graduate Motor Drive Control course since 2021.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Torque Quality Improvement in Switched Reluctance Drive Systems for Industrial Variable-Speed Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the full chain from motor design through power converter topology to real-time control algorithms, with the goal of making switched reluctance drives more competitive with permanent-magnet alternatives in variable-speed industrial applications. Tasks included FE-based sensitivity studies of stator and rotor pole geometry, experimental comparison of asymmetric bridge and split-capacitor converter topologies, and implementation of position-dependent current profiling on an embedded microcontroller platform. Olivera Grujić led the work package on control algorithm design and hardware-in-the-loop validation, contributing the FE-calibrated TSF methodology and the sensorless estimation scheme. The project produced eight journal and conference papers and one M.Sc. thesis supervised jointly by project members.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Institute for Electrical Engineering Nikola Tesla, Belgrade

projects.title: Robust Online Parameter Identification Methods for Permanent-Magnet Motor Drives in Industrial Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates identification algorithms robust to sensor noise, inverter nonlinearities, and varying thermal conditions for PMSM drives used in light industrial automation. The work covers recursive least-squares methods with adaptive forgetting factors, Kalman filter variants, and hybrid approaches combining both. Experimental validation is performed on a dedicated motor test bench at the Faculty of Technical Sciences equipped with a programmable dynamometer and real-time control hardware. Stefan Vulin is responsible for implementing and benchmarking the Kalman filter routines and for maintaining the test bench instrumentation. Results are intended to produce openly documented algorithm templates suitable for adoption by regional drive manufacturers.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Power Electronics and Automation, Novi Sad

projects.title: Dynamic Wireless Charging Infrastructure for Low-Speed Urban Electric Mobility
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DYNACHARG addresses the design and experimental validation of a segmented wireless power transfer track intended for low-speed urban electric vehicles travelling at 5–20 km/h. The project covers coil geometry optimisation for combined lateral and longitudinal misalignment tolerance, segment switching logic, and thermal characterisation of road-embedded transmitter pads under repetitive short-duration loading. The experimental platform is a 6 m indoor track at the Faculty of Technical Sciences with real-time position feedback and a 3.3 kW power stage. Target outputs include a geometry design methodology, a switching controller prototype, and a public data set of efficiency measurements over a two-dimensional misalignment grid.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Cross-Border Test Infrastructure for Electric Vehicle Charging Technologies
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project established shared laboratory facilities and testing protocols for electric vehicle charging technologies at partner institutions in Hungary and Serbia. Simić led the work package on wireless charging coupler characterisation, coordinating joint measurement campaigns and the harmonisation of test procedures between the Novi Sad and Subotica sites. The project produced a common test methodology document and jointly supervised two student theses comparing wired and wireless charging energy losses at low state-of-charge conditions. Infrastructure investments included a shared impedance measurement kit and a portable data acquisition system for field measurements.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Széchenyi István University, Department of Mechatronics, Győr
Subotica Tech – College of Applied Sciences, Subotica

projects.title: Resonant DC-DC Stages with Predictive Loss Management for Modular Battery Storage Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the design and loss characterisation of bidirectional resonant DC-DC converters for modular stationary battery storage in the 5–15 kW range. Activities included development of frequency-domain loss models calibrated by calorimetric measurements, fabrication and testing of CLLC prototypes using GaN and SiC devices, and derivation of frequency scheduling algorithms that minimise total losses over a charge-discharge cycle. The project delivered two journal publications, one conference paper, a validated loss modelling tool, and two prototype converters. A cooperation agreement with the Faculty of Electrical Engineering in East Sarajevo provided co-supervision of one doctoral student.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of East Sarajevo

projects.title: DC Microgrid Interface Converters for Industrial Prosumers
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A provincially funded project investigating DC microgrid architectures for small industrial facilities with on-site photovoltaic generation and battery storage. Hadžić led the work package on isolated DC-DC interface converters, contributing resonant topology selection criteria and a comparative efficiency evaluation of LLC and phase-shifted full-bridge converters at the 10 kW level. The project involved two other departments at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and resulted in one conference paper and a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat. One M.Sc. thesis was completed within the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad – Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad – Department of Energy and Process Engineering

projects.title: Digital Twin Framework for Condition Monitoring and Remaining Useful Life Estimation of High-Voltage Underground Cable Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a modular digital twin platform for 110 kV underground cable circuits operated by the Serbian transmission system. The platform integrates SCADA load data, distributed fibre-optic temperature measurements, and periodic offline diagnostic results into a continuously updated state estimation model. Core outputs include a validated lumped-parameter ageing model, a machine-learning-based partial discharge classifier trained on laboratory-generated PRPD datasets, and a Kalman filter assimilation scheme for DTS data. The platform was piloted on a 4.2 km cable route and produced condition reports used by the asset management team of the transmission operator for two scheduled maintenance decisions during the project period.

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in High-Voltage Asset Digitalisation for Underground Transmission Networks
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project supports exchange of expertise and joint methodology development between research groups in Serbia and Romania working on digital asset management of high-voltage underground infrastructure. Lekić leads the work package on data acquisition protocols, responsible for harmonising partial-discharge measurement procedures and DTS calibration standards across the two partner laboratories. Joint training workshops for PhD students and network engineers were conducted in Novi Sad and Timișoara. The project produced a shared open dataset of PRPD measurements from cable joint specimens tested under identical protocols in both laboratories, available for further machine learning benchmarking studies.

projects.title: Coordinated Surge Protection Strategies for Low-Voltage Photovoltaic Plants in High-Flash-Density Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project characterised the transient overvoltage environment of PV installations in Vojvodina using a network of five field monitoring stations and validated propagation models derived from laboratory impulse testing. Key deliverables included an SPD coordination methodology for multi-string plants with combiner box architecture, a varistor degradation testing protocol adapted to indirect-lightning stress profiles, and an earthing design guideline for the local soil types. The project employed two research associates and one doctoral student. Results fed directly into the book chapter submitted to the Springer handbook and into an ongoing engagement with a regional electrical contractor regarding design review services.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Surge Propagation and Protection Coordination in Distributed Renewable Energy Installations across the Adriatic–Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: ADRIASURGE addresses the harmonisation of surge protection design practices for PV and small wind installations across the Serbia–Romania border region. Zoran Tošić leads Work Package 2, responsible for field measurement campaigns at four cross-border sites, laboratory round-robin impulse testing of SPD products available on the two national markets, and the preparation of a bilingual (Serbian–Romanian) engineering guide for installers and inspectors. The project has installed long-term transient loggers at two sites in Vojvodina and two in Banat (Romania). An intermediate technical workshop was held in Timișoara in October 2024 and drew 38 practising engineers from both countries.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Probabilistic Electric Field Modelling for Composite Insulator Fleet Management in Mixed-Pollution Regions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed stochastic finite element workflows for quantifying the probability distribution of electric field peaks on medium-voltage composite insulators in regions with heterogeneous pollution. Field measurement campaigns were conducted across 35 distribution line sections in Vojvodina, providing empirical pollution statistics. Monte Carlo sampling was integrated with 2D FEM solvers to produce probabilistic exceedance curves used in insulator selection guidelines. An open dataset of 4 800 simulation cases and associated pollution characterisation measurements was compiled and deposited in a public repository. The project involved collaboration with the Elektrotehnički institut Nikola Tesla in Belgrade and the Politehnica University of Timișoara.
partners: Elektrotehnički institut Nikola Tesla, Belgrade
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Numerical and Experimental Characterisation of Medium-Voltage Composite Insulators for the Serbian Distribution Grid
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A two-year contract research project commissioned by a regional distribution system operator to provide validated numerical models and laboratory measurements for composite insulators procured for 20 kV overhead network modernisation. The work included FEM modelling of three supplier-specified insulator types under dry, polluted, and wet conditions, leakage current measurements in the high-voltage laboratory salt-fog chamber, and a technical report with field classification recommendations for different network corridors. Results were used internally by the client for specification revision and procurement decisions. No public deliverables were produced, but methodological aspects informed subsequent journal publications.
partners: Elektrodistribucija Vojvodina d.o.o. (fictional)

projects.title: Fractional-Order Parameter Characterisation of Electrochemical Capacitors for Power Electronics Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project established systematic measurement and modelling procedures for fractional-order equivalent circuits of double-layer capacitors, with a focus on datasets useful for power electronics simulation. Activities included the procurement of climate-controlled test fixtures, the development of in-house extraction software implementing Levenberg–Marquardt and vector-fitting routines, and coordinated measurement campaigns at two partner laboratories. The project produced a public dataset of impedance spectra for 60 commercial cells covering six manufacturers and four temperature levels, along with documented calibration procedures for the Solartron 1260 platform. Results fed directly into circuit-simulator component libraries used in subsequent teaching and research.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

projects.title: Formalni okvir za verifikaciju aritmetičkih jezgara u FPGA-baziranim DSP sistemima
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je bio usmeren na razvoj metodologije i pratećih softverskih alata za automatizovanu formalnu verifikaciju VHDL opisa aritmetičkih jezgara namenjenih DSP primenama na FPGA platformama. Obuhvaćeni su bili moduli za fiksnu aritmetiku (sabirači, množači, MAC, deljači, elementarne funkcije) i definisan je jednoobrazan tok verifikacije zasnovan na SMT rešavačima. Razvijeni alati testirani su na industrijskim i akademskim uzorcima RTL koda. Projektni tim je obuhvatao četiri istraživača s Fakulteta tehničkih nauka i jednog gostujućeg istraživača iz Graca. Rezultati su objavljeni u 6 radova u časopisima i 4 konferencijska saopštenja.
partners: Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sad
Graz University of Technology

projects.title: Approximate Arithmetic Engines for Extreme-Edge Image Analytics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: APEXA investigates the systematic design and verification of approximate arithmetic circuits for image analytics workloads on resource-constrained edge devices. The project develops an open library of characterised approximate adder and multiplier cells in 180 nm CMOS, complemented by a software framework for pipeline-level error propagation analysis. Application targets include demosaicing, edge detection, and compressed-domain feature extraction for industrial camera modules. The project involves three wafer shuttle slots through a European MPW service, enabling direct measurement of fabricated approximate cells. Results are disseminated through journal publications and a publicly released RTL cell library. Two doctoral students are funded through the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Institute for Microelectronics, University of Ljubljana

projects.title: Cross-Border Embedded Vision Platform for Smart Manufacturing Quality Control
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSVISION is a cross-border collaboration aimed at developing embedded vision hardware for automated surface defect inspection in manufacturing lines operating in both Hungary and Serbia. Mijatović leads the work package on low-power arithmetic hardware, supplying approximate arithmetic IP blocks to the shared platform FPGA reference design. The project integrates academic hardware research with industrial pilot lines at two manufacturing partners. Energy consumption targets for the vision pipeline are specified by the industrial partners, and the approximate arithmetic components are evaluated against these targets using representative production defect image datasets provided by the manufacturers.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Informatics, Budapest University of Technology and Economics

Precíziós Ipari Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Phase-Locked Loop Calibration Methods for Low-Power Narrowband IoT Transceivers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed digital background calibration algorithms for time-to-digital converters embedded in integer-N PLL frequency synthesisers targeting NB-IoT and eMTC frequency bands. Work packages covered TDC nonlinearity characterisation across the automotive temperature range, loop-bandwidth sensitivity analysis under varying TDC gain, and the design of a compact compensation circuit implementable in 130 nm CMOS. An FPGA-based hardware emulation platform was constructed to validate algorithms before tape-out. By the end of the project, the team demonstrated phase-noise improvement of 3–5 dB at 10 kHz offset after calibration across the −40 °C to 125 °C range on a prototype board. Two journal papers and three conference papers were produced.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Budapest University of Technology and Economics

projects.title: Integrated Circuit Design Support for IoT Node Demonstrators
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A short provincial grant that funded measurement equipment and student stipends for a group of three researchers at the Faculty of Technical Sciences working on mixed-signal characterisation of commercially available IoT transceiver chipsets. Lačok contributed phase-noise and reference-spur measurements of 868 MHz and 915 MHz synthesiser blocks in two chipsets under temperature stress. The project produced a technical report delivered to the Secretariat and supported two master's thesis projects.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Low-Voltage Analog Front-End Architectures for Wearable Biopotential Acquisition
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates analog signal acquisition chains for wearable ECG and EEG devices constrained to operate from a single 0.8–0.9 V lithium-ion cell output. The central research questions concern the minimum achievable noise figure for a three-stage readout chain at sub-1 V supply, and the topology-dependent limits on gain-bandwidth product under these constraints. Work packages cover theoretical noise modelling, CMOS circuit design and simulation in 180 nm technology, tape-out and characterisation of two test chips, and system-level integration with a 12-bit SAR ADC. The project involves one postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad, with a collaboration agreement with Politehnica University of Timișoara for complementary measurement infrastructure.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Sensitive Probe Electronics for Implantable Neural Interfaces
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project developed low-noise readout electronics for a multi-electrode neural probe prototype intended for rodent in-vivo experiments, conducted in collaboration with the Faculty of Medicine in Novi Sad. Nebojša Urošević led the work package on front-end analog circuit design, responsible for specifying and simulating OTA-based preamplifier stages with input-referred noise below 5 µVrms in the 300 Hz to 5 kHz local field potential band at a 1 V supply. The project delivered a printed circuit board prototype that was used in bench validation with saline phantom measurements. A full custom IC was outside the budget scope; the prototype used discrete OPA components and discrete passive filters.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute BioTechLab Novi Sad

projects.title: Covariance Reconstruction Approaches for Multi-Array Radio Source Localisation in Structured Interference
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses DOA estimation accuracy degradation caused by spatially correlated interference in compact multi-array deployments typical of urban IoT and industrial wireless sensor networks. The main technical objectives are: developing structured covariance reconstruction algorithms suited to arrays with fewer than ten elements; characterising algorithm behaviour under time-varying noise correlation; and validating methods on a software-defined radio testbed operating in the 433 MHz and 868 MHz ISM bands. The project runs for three years with a team of four researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and one external collaborator from the University of East Sarajevo. Deliverables include open-source implementations of the proposed algorithms and a calibrated eight-element testbed array.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of East Sarajevo

projects.title: Cyclostationary Methods for Autonomous Spectrum Monitoring in Heterogeneous Radio Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop a complete signal processing pipeline for autonomous identification and classification of radio emissions in the 70–900 MHz band without prior knowledge of transmission parameters. Work packages covered cyclostationary feature estimation under short observation windows, adaptive SNR-stratified SVM classifiers, real-time FPGA implementation, and field validation at three monitoring sites in Vojvodina. A captured dataset of annotated real-world signals was a key deliverable and has been released publicly. The project funded two doctoral students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications. Final validation demonstrated end-to-end classification latency below 2 ms on the developed FPGA prototype, meeting the target for near-real-time spectrum awareness applications.

projects.title: Cross-Border Spectrum Awareness Platform for Interference Detection
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border initiative establishing a coordinated spectrum monitoring infrastructure at four sites in Serbia and three in Romania. Milić leads the work package on signal identification and automatic classification, responsible for deploying and calibrating the modulation recognition software on distributed monitoring nodes. The platform targets detection of uncoordinated or interfering transmitters in the 400–800 MHz band relevant to emergency services and broadcast. Data collected at Serbian nodes are processed using the cyclostationary-SVM pipeline developed under CYCLOMON, with adaptations for the Romanian radio environment. Outcomes include a joint interference reporting protocol and a shared annotated signal library.

projects.title: Shallow-Water Acoustic Communication Systems for Inland Waterway Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates physical-layer design for acoustic OFDM communication systems deployed on inland waterways in Serbia, focusing on adaptive equalisation, iterative decoding, and synchronisation under realistic multipath and Doppler conditions. The work combines BELLHOP-based channel modelling, controlled tank experiments, and field campaigns on the Danube and Sava rivers. A key deliverable is a software-defined-radio prototype capable of real-time turbo equalisation at 20 kHz. The project also examines network-layer aspects, including link budget planning for multi-node monitoring arrays. Three Ph.D. students are supported, and collaboration with the University of Ljubljana and Brno University of Technology is maintained throughout the project period.

projects.title: Adaptive Waveforms for Acoustic Shallow-water COmmunications on Navigable rivers
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian institutions aimed at developing interoperable acoustic modem waveforms suitable for shallow navigable rivers shared by both countries. The project covers joint measurement campaigns on the Danube between Novi Sad and Budapest, waveform standardisation proposals, and hardware prototype validation. Stanković leads the work package on receiver algorithms, coordinating the design and testing of adaptive equalisation and synchronisation modules. Deliverables include a jointly authored technical specification document, a shared channel measurement database, and two hardware demonstrators tested under operational conditions during river navigation exercises.

projects.title: Acoustic and Impedance-Based Diagnostic Methods for Condition Assessment of High-Voltage Power Transformers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops an integrated diagnostic framework combining piezoelectric acoustic emission sensor arrays with broadband impedance spectroscopy for evaluating insulation condition in 110 kV and 220 kV power transformers. The work covers laboratory characterisation of ageing mechanisms in oil-paper insulation samples, development of a portable multi-channel acquisition system, and field validation at operating substations. The project also addresses synchronisation of acoustic and electrical PD channels under noisy substation conditions. Ivana Novaković is responsible for the time-frequency signal processing workstream, including implementation of fractional Fourier and wavelet-based methods for source localisation from the acoustic array data.

projects.title: Sensor Fixture Standardisation and Calibration Protocols for Acoustic Partial Discharge Monitoring in Distribution Transformers
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project addresses the lack of standardised procedures for mounting and calibrating piezoelectric acoustic emission sensors on power transformer tanks during field partial discharge measurements. The study produces engineering guidelines covering sensor type selection, minimum clamping force, coupling agent requirements, and reference signal verification procedures applicable to distribution transformers rated 35 kV and below. Laboratory experiments on a steel tank mockup and two decommissioned 10 MVA transformers provide the empirical basis. A draft protocol document suitable for adoption by distribution companies is one of the main deliverables. The project is conducted in cooperation with a regional distribution utility that provides access to out-of-service equipment and engineering input on practical constraints.
