projects.title: Dielectric Methods for Remaining-Life Estimation of Distribution Transformer Insulation in the Serbian Power Grid
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate a combined time-domain and frequency-domain diagnostic protocol for estimating the remaining service life of oil-paper insulation in distribution transformers operated by Serbian electricity distributors. Laboratory ageing experiments produced a reference database of dielectric spectra correlated with degree of polymerisation and moisture content. Field measurements were conducted on 30 in-service transformers, and the diagnostic protocol was tested against independent chemical ageing indicators (furans, acidity, dissolved gases). A software tool for data interpretation was developed and made available to the industrial partner. The project involved collaboration between the Faculty of Technical Sciences and the Power Utility Institute Novi Sad.

projects.title: Adaptation of Dielectric Diagnostic Procedures for Ester-Fluid-Filled Distribution Transformers
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project addresses the gap in diagnostic knowledge created by the increasing use of ester-based insulating fluids in distribution transformers in Vojvodina and wider Serbia. The work programme covers laboratory preparation of reference specimens impregnated with natural and synthetic ester fluids, measurement of their dielectric response over a wide temperature range, and comparison with mineral-oil-impregnated counterparts. The project also includes a round-robin measurement exercise with one international partner laboratory to assess inter-laboratory reproducibility. Outputs include revised activation energy parameters for temperature correction and an updated moisture estimation procedure for ester-fluid systems. One doctoral student is being trained within the project.

University of Porto, Faculty of Engineering

projects.title: Bearing Current Monitoring and Mitigation in Variable-Speed Drives Under Non-Ideal Grid Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi razvojem metoda za detekciju i smanjenje ležajnih struja u frekventno regulisanim pogonima koji rade u uslovima nesimetričnog i harmonijski izobličenog napajanja, kakvo se sreće u industrijskim mrežama u Srbiji i regionu. Istraživanje obuhvata eksperimentalnu karakterizaciju ležajnih struja, razvoj adaptivnih modulacionih algoritama i prototipsku verifikaciju na pogonima do 15 kW. Krajnji cilj je skup praktičnih preporuka i softverskog modula koji može biti integrisan u postojeće upravljačke jedinice invertora bez izmene hardvera. projects.title: Statistical Methodology for Flicker Compliance Assessment in Industrial Networks with Arc Furnace Loads
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FLIQSTAT addressed the gap between standardised power quality measurement procedures and the statistical rigour required for reliable compliance assessment at arc furnace connection points. The project developed bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification methods for high-order Plt percentiles, evaluated minimum monitoring campaign durations for different furnace utilisation regimes, and produced an open dataset of annotated long-term flicker recordings from Serbian industrial networks. A secondary outcome was a draft technical guide for distribution system operators on integrating statistical uncertainty reporting into connection assessment reports. The project involved three partner institutions and two industrial network operators, and resulted in four journal publications and two conference papers.

projects.title: Cross-Border Power Quality Monitoring Framework for Industrial Zones in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project established a harmonised power quality monitoring and reporting framework for industrial zones on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. Vesna Malešević led the work package on measurement methodology and data quality, overseeing the deployment of six class-A power quality analysers at medium-voltage substations supplying arc furnace and large motor load installations. The project produced a joint technical protocol for long-term monitoring campaigns, a comparative analysis of national grid code requirements, and a shared anonymised monitoring database accessible to researchers at partner institutions. Training workshops for network operator engineers were delivered in Novi Sad and Subotica.

projects.title: Sparse Reconstruction Methods for Wideband Vehicular Channel Characterisation in Urban Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project targets the development and experimental validation of compressive sensing-based methods for wideband V2X channel sounding and parametric channel modelling in urban environments in Serbia. Activities include design of optimised measurement matrices for sub-Nyquist channel sounders, collection of dual-band (5.9 GHz and 28 GHz) propagation data in Novi Sad, and derivation of geometry-based stochastic models calibrated to local urban morphology. A secondary objective is to establish a public open-access dataset of vehicular channel measurements representative of South-East European urban environments, which are underrepresented in international model databases. The project involves collaboration with the University of Belgrade and the University of Niš.

projects.title: Cross-border V2X Propagation Measurement and Modelling for Cooperative Driving Safety Applications
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COVEX addresses the lack of cross-border V2X propagation reference data for the Hungary-Serbia corridor, which is relevant for harmonised deployment of ITS-G5 and C-V2X road safety systems on the E75 motorway. The project conducts coordinated channel sounding campaigns on both sides of the border, including a joint measurement run spanning the Röszke–Horgoš border crossing area. Propagation models are jointly developed and validated by the two participating university teams. A secondary outcome is a set of deployment guidelines for roadside unit antenna siting and height, derived from the empirical path loss models. Danijela Trifunović leads the work package on measurement campaign design and data analysis.

projects.title: Flexible Demand-Side Management in District Heating Networks with High Shares of Variable Renewable Heat
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FLEXHEAT investigates control and optimisation methods that allow district heating operators in Serbia and the wider Western Balkans region to accommodate substantial shares of variable renewable heat—primarily solar thermal and geothermal—without compromising supply reliability. The project combines grey-box building identification, scenario-based stochastic MPC, and demand response aggregation into a coherent operational framework. A pilot demonstration is conducted in collaboration with a municipal heating company in Vojvodina on a 19-node subnetwork. The project funds two PhD students and produces open-source simulation tools. A key deliverable is a practical guideline document targeting district heating engineers without a control background.

projects.title: SMT-Assisted Formal Bounding of Scheduling Latencies in Safety-Critical Embedded Platforms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SAFEBOUND investigated the use of SMT solvers and constraint programming tools to compute tight upper bounds on scheduling latencies in mixed-criticality embedded systems, with a focus on automotive and industrial control platforms. The project developed a formal framework that combines measurement-based WCET estimation with symbolic constraint propagation to produce provably valid latency bounds without excessive pessimism. Deliverables included an open-source Python toolchain wrapping Z3 and CVC5, a benchmark suite of automotive-inspired task sets, and three peer-reviewed publications. projects.title: Resilience-Driven VNF Placement and Recovery in Multi-Domain Software-Defined Wide-Area Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RESWAN addresses the problem of maintaining service continuity in multi-domain SD-WANs under correlated link and node failures. The project develops formal resilience metrics for VNF chain placement, a migration scheduling framework that responds to failure events within sub-second decision windows, and open-source tooling for emulation-based validation. Activities include building a 40-node SDN/NFV testbed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, collecting failure traces from a Serbian ISP partner, and publishing benchmark datasets. The project funds two Ph.D. students and supports collaboration visits with partner universities in Prague and Bucharest. Three journal papers and two conference papers have been produced under this grant.

projects.title: Cross-Border SD-WAN Testbed for Research and Education Between Hungary and Serbia
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia

The project deployed OpenFlow-capable switching equipment at both sites, developed joint laboratory exercises for master-level networking courses, and ran two summer schools attended by 47 students from both countries. projects.title: Distributed Cooperative Localisation for Infrastructure-Free Heterogeneous Robot Teams
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DISCORO addresses the design and experimental validation of distributed state estimation algorithms for robot teams composed of ground and aerial platforms that share only inter-robot range and bearing measurements, with no reliance on GPS or fixed beacons. The project develops asynchronous variants of the Kalman consensus filter that handle heterogeneous sensor rates, studies the effect of communication graph topology on estimation accuracy, and validates the algorithms on a testbed of four ground robots and two quadrotors. Deliverables include open-source ROS packages, a labelled dataset of indoor multi-robot trajectories with UWB measurements, and a methodology guide for practitioners. The University of Novi Sad team of five researchers leads all activities.

projects.title: Cross-Border Robotics Research Infrastructure for Cooperative Navigation

Ristić leads the work package on algorithm harmonisation, responsible for agreeing on common data formats, filter interfaces, and evaluation protocols so that experiments at both sites can be directly compared. projects.title: Privacy-Preserving Cross-Institutional Learning for Rare Disease Imaging in Southeast Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PRIVCROSS addressed the challenge of building reliable machine learning models for rare pathologies where individual hospitals in the region hold only small patient cohorts. The project established a federated learning infrastructure connecting three clinical partners in Serbia and one in Romania under data-sharing agreements compliant with local data protection law. Research focused on differentially private aggregation under severe class imbalance and small per-silo sample sizes, the two dominant obstacles in rare-disease federated imaging. The project produced a validated DP federated pipeline for two rare pulmonary conditions, open-source tooling for privacy accounting, and a technical white paper on regulatory alignment in the Serbian context. Three doctoral students were supported.

projects.title: Federated and Privacy-Aware Machine Learning Infrastructure for Multi-Country Medical Imaging Consortia
projects.programme: Horizon Europe

projects.title: Scalable Taint-Guided Fuzzing for Security Assessment of Industrial IoT Firmware
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FIRMSHIELD develops automated tooling for security assessment of firmware used in industrial IoT gateways and network-attached sensors deployed in Serbian manufacturing facilities. The project combines offline binary analysis—control-flow recovery and protocol grammar extraction—with online dynamic taint analysis to guide a grey-box fuzzer toward inputs that reach memory-unsafe code paths. A corpus of firmware images from cooperating industrial partners is maintained under a data-sharing agreement. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher, and supports a hardware testbed of 40 physical embedded devices across four CPU architectures. Results are published as open-source tooling and peer-reviewed papers.

projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FLEXPRO investigates the design of local flexibility markets suitable for adoption by distribution system operators in Serbia and neighbouring countries, where smart meter penetration is still growing. projects.title: Topological Data Analysis Methods for Quality Control in Smart Manufacturing

projects.title: Reconfigurable Signal Processing Architectures for Embedded Sensing Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RESPACE investigates design methods that reduce the manual effort required to map signal processing algorithms onto FPGA fabric while meeting strict latency and power budgets. The project addresses three specific gaps: the unreliability of HLS-generated AXI interfaces for multi-kernel designs, the lack of automated fixed-point precision assignment methods that provide worst-case guarantees, and the limited exploitation of heterogeneous DSP block features by commercial synthesis tools. The team develops software tools implemented as post-synthesis passes and validates them on two application drivers: a compact radar front-end and an ultrasonic non-destructive testing instrument. The project involves collaboration with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and the Institute for Physics in Belgrade.

projects.title: FPGA Platform for Software-Defined Radio Prototyping in Industrial Environments
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research engagement with Velestar Communications d.o.o., a Serbian provider of private wireless network equipment, to develop an FPGA-based baseband processing platform for a proprietary narrowband protocol operating in the 400–500 MHz band. The Faculty of Technical Sciences team was responsible for designing and verifying the receive-side signal processing chain—including channel filtering, timing recovery, and packet detection—in Vitis HLS, and for integrating the chain with the client-supplied modem software running on an embedded ARM processor. projects.title: Graph-Based Parsing of Urban 3D Point Clouds for Digital Twin Construction

projects.summary: URBANPARSE develops a full processing pipeline—from raw mobile mapping and airborne LiDAR data to semantically enriched building models—suitable for input into municipal digital twin platforms. The project focuses on three technical challenges: robust semantic segmentation under seasonal and weather variation, instance-level façade element detection, and automatic Level-of-Detail (LoD) 2 and LoD 3 building model generation from detected elements. The team collects original scanning data in Novi Sad and two partner cities, constructs labelled benchmarks, and releases all trained models and datasets under open licences. A liaison with the City of Novi Sad Urban Planning Institute provides real-world validation use cases around building permit checking and heritage documentation.

projects.summary: The project develops a complete workflow for building, calibrating, and updating digital twins of ageing reinforced concrete and masonry bridges using vibration measurements. Core research tasks include: construction of parametric reduced-order models by component mode synthesis and Grassmann manifold interpolation; design of optimal wireless sensor networks for modal identification under cost constraints; and implementation of recursive Bayesian updating algorithms suitable for low-power embedded hardware. Two bridge case studies in the Vojvodina region serve as field validation sites. The project funds three research assistants and a two-year equipment grant covering wireless MEMS accelerometer nodes and a portable data acquisition system.

projects.title: Resource-Constrained AutoML for Embedded and Edge Sensing Platforms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops AutoML pipelines tailored to microcontroller and single-board computer targets common in environmental and industrial sensing. The core challenge is that standard hyperparameter and architecture search tools assume GPU availability; this project reformulates search objectives to include RAM footprint, flash memory, and inference latency alongside predictive accuracy. projects.title: Reproducibility and Error Localisation in Scientific Data Workflows

projects.summary: REFLOW addresses the growing problem that published scientific data workflows — predominantly implemented as Python notebooks — cannot be re-executed by third parties, either because of dependency drift, broken file references, or hidden execution-order assumptions. The project combines large-scale empirical measurement of reproducibility failures with the development of static analysis tools for automatic detection and repair. Specific objectives include building a curated benchmark of 5 000 annotated notebooks, extending the LeakTrace and SchemaFix tools to cover additional pipeline libraries, and releasing an open-source JupyterLab plugin that runs analyses on save. The team consists of three PhD students and two postdoctoral researchers at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, with an associated researcher at the University of Ljubljana.

projects.title: Data Quality Assurance Toolchain for Industrial Machine-Learning Pipelines
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: DAQUA is a bilateral research contract with Kognitivna Rešenja d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based software company that develops machine-learning solutions for manufacturing clients. The project applies static analysis and automated repair techniques developed in the academic research programme to the company's internal Python pipeline codebase, which consists of approximately 400 notebooks and 60 reusable pipeline scripts. Work packages cover integration of NotebookMap into the company's CI system, adaptation of AggFix to proprietary aggregation schemas, and training of company engineers. The contract includes a confidentiality clause covering specific client datasets but allows publication of methodology and aggregated evaluation results.

projects.title: Event-Based Visual Awareness for Safe Localisation in Challenging Lighting

projects.summary: The project investigates event-camera-based ego-motion estimation and 3D mapping for ground robots operating in environments with extreme lighting variability — tunnels with intermittent lighting, outdoor scenes transitioning between shade and direct sunlight, and night-time urban settings. The core technical contributions include a continuous-time estimator tolerant to event-rate bursts, a gradient-based HDR scene representation updated incrementally from event streams, and a tightly coupled event-IMU filter validated on a custom-built test vehicle. Two graduate students and one postdoctoral researcher are supported. Equipment procured includes a Prophesee Metavision EVK4 event camera and a LiDAR unit used as ground-truth reference for depth evaluation.

projects.summary: WIRE360 was a cross-border cooperation project between Serbian and Hungarian universities targeting resource allocation strategies for immersive video applications in shared wireless cells. Janković led the work package responsible for application-layer quality modelling and subjective evaluation methodology. The project established joint subjective testing infrastructure, collected a shared head-tracking database distributed to regional research institutions, and delivered two pilot demonstrations of viewport-adaptive streaming in public venues in Novi Sad and Subotica. Three bilateral staff exchanges and four joint publications resulted from the collaboration.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Széchenyi István University, Győr, Hungary

projects.title: Rigorous Parameter Enclosure Methods for Nonlinear Control Systems
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: RIGOPAR investigates the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of verified parameter identification algorithms for nonlinear control-relevant models. The project focuses on three application classes: electric drive models, biomedical regulatory systems, and chemical reactor models. Deliverables include a documented MATLAB toolbox for interval and affine arithmetic-based parameter bounding, a benchmark suite of test problems with reference solutions, and at least three journal publications. Čáni contributes to the toolbox development and is responsible for the electric drive benchmark cases, building directly on his set-membership work on DC motor models. The project is coordinated by the Department of Computing and Control Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia

projects.title: Wrist-Worn Awareness: Low-Power Architectures for Continuous Human Activity Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WRISTAWARE addresses the gap between activity recognition accuracy achievable on server hardware and what can be replicated on wrist-worn devices powered by a coin cell or small LiPo battery. The project develops a pipeline covering dataset collection, model design, compression, and on-device validation specifically for Cortex-M class microcontrollers. A dedicated data collection campaign recruits participants from student and working-age populations in Novi Sad for a free-living recording study lasting three weeks per subject. Secondary goals include establishing open benchmark datasets under a Creative Commons licence and producing reference firmware for two widely used Nordic and STMicroelectronics development kits. The project funds two doctoral students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Artificial Intelligence of Serbia, Novi Sad

projects.title: Edge-Deployable Monitoring for Clinical and Occupational Health Applications
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: EDGEMED is a cross-border project bringing together engineering and healthcare partners in Serbia and Hungary to develop prototype wearable monitoring systems for two use cases: hand hygiene compliance in clinical wards and fatigue detection in industrial assembly workers. The Novi Sad team is responsible for the signal processing and on-device inference work package, contributing compressed activity recognition models and the firmware integration layer. The Hungarian partner contributes clinical validation protocol design and recruits hospital staff as study participants. The project targets a working prototype demonstrated in a simulated clinical environment by month 24. Capacity-building activities include two joint workshops and a student exchange for master-level students from both institutions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Óbuda University, Budapest
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Automated Compliance Checking and Evidence Generation for Desktop Software Accessibility
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a toolchain that automatically generates verifiable accessibility compliance evidence for desktop applications subject to EN 301 549 procurement requirements. The work covers three main tracks: extending the programmatic assertion set to cover a wider range of EN 301 549 criteria, building an evidence-packaging module that produces structured reports compatible with the ACR format used in public procurement, and piloting the toolchain with three Serbian public-sector software suppliers. The project involves collaboration with the Faculty of Informatics at Masaryk University for independent validation of the assertion definitions and with a local assistive-technology user group that provides expert judgement on criteria classified as requiring human evaluation.
partners: Faculty of Informatics, Masaryk University, Brno
Centar za primenjenu informatiku Vojvodine (CPIV), Novi Sad
Association of Assistive Technology Users of Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Platform GUI Test Infrastructure for SMEs in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TESTBED-X established a shared GUI testing infrastructure accessible to small and medium-sized software companies in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region. The University of Novi Sad team was responsible for the work package covering tool integration and training, deploying a CI-connected GUI test harness based on the DesktopBench-40 framework and providing three two-day workshops for SME developers. Seventeen companies participated in at least one workshop; eight adopted portions of the testing toolchain in their development pipelines during the project period. The project produced a publicly available configuration guide and a set of reusable test-script templates targeting common desktop application categories.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences and Informatics
Regional Development Agency Subotica (RDASR)
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Baranya County, Pécs

projects.title: Compositional Information-Flow Enforcement for Cloud-Native Multi-Tenant Infrastructures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CONFLOW addressed the problem of enforcing information-flow policies in Kubernetes-based platforms shared among multiple independent tenants. The project developed a formal composition algebra for per-tenant policies, automated verification tooling implemented in OCaml, and an eBPF-based runtime enforcement layer. A secondary objective was characterising side-channel leakage through shared kernel resources and prototyping kernel patches to reduce it. The project supported three PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications. A prototype implementation of the FlowGuard policy language and enforcement runtime was developed and made publicly available under an open-source licence. Collaboration with one company at NTP Novi Sad provided real deployment traces used in the continuous-auditing work.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts
Orbis Software d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Security Monitoring Extensions for Open-Source Service Mesh Infrastructure
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research engagement with Orbis Software d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based company operating a multi-tenant platform-as-a-service offering. The project scope covered three deliverables: a security gap assessment of the company's existing Istio-based service mesh configuration, a prototype integration of eBPF-based inter-service policy enforcement into their deployment pipeline, and a set of Kubernetes admission webhook rules encoding their tenant isolation requirements. Results fed directly into the CONFLOW project's industry evaluation case. The engagement lasted 18 months and involved two researchers from the group.
partners: Orbis Software d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Harvested-Energy Scheduling Policies for Autonomous Edge Nodes in Industrial IoT
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops scheduling policies and hardware reference designs for edge computing nodes that operate exclusively on harvested energy in industrial IoT settings. The work covers three harvesting modalities (solar, vibration, RF ambient), two storage technologies, and runtime policies based on Lyapunov optimisation and lightweight neural controllers. A testbed of 20 custom-built nodes has been deployed at a partner manufacturing facility. Expected deliverables include open-source firmware, an energy dimensioning tool, and at least four journal publications. The project supports two Ph.D. candidates and one postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Advanced Manufacturing Automation, Kragujevac

projects.title: Congestion-Controlled Offloading Protocols for Dense Heterogeneous IoT Access Networks
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DENSEOFF targets the development and cross-border validation of offloading protocols that remain stable under high device density in both Serbian and Hungarian smart-city pilot sites. The University of Novi Sad leads the protocol design work package, while the University of Pécs contributes the Hungarian pilot deployment and traffic characterisation. Activities include joint testbed experiments, shared dataset creation, and short-term staff exchanges. The project includes a dissemination component targeting local municipalities and technology park tenants. Total project budget is approximately 420,000 EUR, with the Novi Sad team managing roughly 180,000 EUR of that amount.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
City of Subotica IT Office

projects.title: Neuro-Symbolic Visual Inference Systems for Structured Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a modular framework combining differentiable neural perception with answer set programming for scene-graph-based reasoning in structured indoor environments. Main objectives are: (1) construction of a Serbian-language annotated scene-graph corpus covering office and laboratory settings; (2) development of the Weighted Scene-Graph Datalog inference engine with learned probabilistic weights; (3) compositional generalisation benchmarks. The project team at the Faculty of Technical Sciences includes four researchers and two PhD students. Collaborating groups at West University of Timișoara and TU Dresden contribute expertise in probabilistic logic and neural architectures respectively. Results include four journal papers, the WSGD engine released as open-source software, and the CompScene-SR benchmark.
partners: West University of Timișoara, Department of Computer Science
TU Dresden, Institute for Theoretical Computer Science

projects.title: Symbolic Reasoning for Auditable Machine Vision in Smart Manufacturing
projects.programme: Innovation Fund of Serbia
projects.summary: SYMCHECK targets the manufacturing quality-control sector by adapting the group's neuro-symbolic scene-graph pipeline to automated optical inspection. The project is co-funded with an industrial partner operating a contract electronics manufacturing facility in Novi Sad. Work packages cover: adaptation of the YOLOv8 detector to PCB imagery, encoding of IPC-A-610 acceptance criteria in ASP, integration with the partner's existing manufacturing execution system, and a regulatory compliance evaluation with an external auditor. The project employs one postdoctoral researcher and one PhD student. A technology transfer agreement is in place; resulting IP is jointly owned by the university and the industrial partner.
partners: ElektroMont Novi Sad d.o.o.
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Discourse-Structured Tracking of Societal Topics in South Slavic Online Media
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DISTRACK developed a suite of discourse-aware Bayesian topic models specifically targeting Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian online media and social-media platforms. The project produced an annotated corpus of 45,000 forum and news documents with manual topic-segment and discourse-relation labels, a publicly released incremental HDP inference library compatible with morphologically preprocessed South Slavic text, and an evaluation benchmark for longitudinal topic coherence. Three PhD students were supported in part by the project. The main deliverable was a web-based monitoring service piloted with two partner organisations, a regional news agency and a public policy think tank in Novi Sad.
partners: Ruđer Bošković Institute, Zagreb
Institute for Contemporary History, Belgrade
Regional Media Association Vojvodina (RMAV)

projects.title: Multilingual Lexical Resources and Topic Analysis for Central and Eastern European Languages
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MULTILEX-CEE is a cross-border collaboration between research groups in Novi Sad and Szeged focused on building shared lexical resources—lemma lists, stop-word lists, morphological taggers—for Hungarian and Serbian, and integrating these resources into joint cross-lingual topic models. Malešević leads the work package on topic modelling and corpus construction. The project funds joint workshops, short-term staff exchanges, and a shared computational infrastructure. A bilingual annotated corpus covering news and social-media text from the Vojvodina region is the primary tangible output alongside two planned joint publications.
partners: University of Szeged, Department of Software Engineering
Provincial Institute for Culture of Vojvodina
Szeged Regional Innovation Centre

projects.title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Sparse Industrial Sensor Data in Smart Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENSREP investigated contrastive and masked-reconstruction pretraining methods adapted to the statistical properties of industrial tabular sensor data with irregular temporal sampling. The project developed benchmark datasets in partnership with three manufacturing companies in Vojvodina, designed augmentation strategies suited to the sparse tabular domain, and produced open-source tooling for evaluating self-supervised representations on downstream industrial tasks. A secondary objective was the development of lightweight deployment-time drift monitors for tracking representation quality after model handover. The project supported two doctoral students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Artificial Intelligence Research, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts
Vojvodina Industrial Analytics d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptive Contrastive Pretraining for Industrial Control Systems Across Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: ADAPT-ICS is a Horizon Europe collaborative project involving seven partners across Serbia, Germany, Romania, and the Czech Republic. The project targets self-supervised pretraining methods that can be shared across industrial SMEs with heterogeneous sensor configurations, enabling cross-company transfer without sharing raw process data. The Novi Sad team leads Work Package 3, which covers contrastive representation design for non-uniform tabular sensor data, including the TabSCL framework and its deployment onto edge hardware. The project also includes a standardisation activity aimed at proposing a common benchmark suite for evaluating industrial representation learning methods.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad (Serbia)

projects.title: Process Mining for Compliance Auditing in Serbian Public Administration
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je razvijao metodologiju i prateće softverske alate za automatizovanu provjeru usklađenosti administrativnih procesa u organima javne uprave Republike Srbije korišćenjem tehnika rudarenja procesa. Istraživanje je obuhvatalo prikupljanje i anonimizaciju realnih evidencija događaja iz pet institucija partnera, razvoj proširenih WF-net modela koji kodifikuju zakonske rokove i obavezne kontrolne tačke, te pilot primjenu u saradnji s Pokrajinskim sekretarijatom za digitalnu agendu. Projektni tim je objavio sedam naučnih radova i jedan tehnički izvještaj dostupan javnosti. Razvijeni alat za ekstrakciju evidencija predat je na korišćenje institucijama partnerima.
partners: Pokrajinski sekretarijat za digitalnu agendu i informatičke poslove AP Vojvodine
Ekonomski fakultet, Univerzitet u Subotici
Institut za informatiku i automatizaciju, Beograd

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Administrative Procedure Compliance Monitoring
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje mogućnosti usaglašavanja metodologija za praćenje usklađenosti administrativnih procedura između pograničnih regija Srbije i Mađarske, s fokusom na procese koji uključuju prekograničnu razmjenu dokumenata. Radni paket kojim rukovodi Radulović obuhvata razvoj zajedničkog referentnog modela zasnovanog na BPMN i Petri mrežama, te mapiranje razlika između srpskog Zakona o opštem upravnom postupku i odgovarajućeg mađarskog zakonodavstva u formalnim terminima. Planirano je testiranje na skupovima evidencija iz Opštine Kanjiža i partnerske mađarske lokalne samouprave.
partners: Széchenyi István Egyetem, Győr, Mađarska
Opština Kanjiža
Subotica Tech – Visoka tehnička škola strukovnih studija, Subotica

projects.title: Sub-Nyquist Broadband Spectrum Monitoring for Cognitive and Regulatory Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the hardware and algorithmic requirements for deploying low-cost sub-Nyquist spectrum monitoring nodes across urban and industrial radio environments. Work packages cover measurement matrix design under hardware-imposed constraints, adaptive reconstruction algorithms for non-stationary occupancy patterns, embedded implementation on ARM-FPGA platforms, and a field validation campaign at three sites in the Vojvodina region. The project produced open-source solver libraries, hardware schematics for a USRP-compatible sub-Nyquist front-end add-on, and a publicly available annotated spectrum capture dataset covering the 400–800 MHz and 2.4 GHz bands. Two doctoral students are supervised under this project.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia
Institute for Telecommunications and Electronics IRITEL, Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Collaborative Testbed for Compressed Sensing in Shared Spectrum Management
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSENSE establishes a joint spectrum monitoring infrastructure across the Serbian–Hungarian border region using distributed compressed sensing nodes. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on reconstruction algorithm adaptation for geographically distributed node networks, focusing on distributed OMP and consensus-ADMM approaches where each node holds a partial set of compressed measurements. A shared dataset of cross-border VHF and UHF occupancy observations is being compiled. The project also includes a training component for regulatory authority staff from both countries on interpreting sub-Nyquist monitoring outputs.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Óbuda University, Budapest, Hungary
National Media and Infocommunications Authority of Hungary (training partner)

projects.title: Synthetic Histopathology Data for Robust AI-Assisted Grading in Resource-Constrained Clinical Settings
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates systematic methods for constructing synthetic training datasets for histopathology AI systems used in hospitals where minority-class samples are scarce. Core activities include the development and evaluation of conditional GAN and diffusion model pipelines for patch-level synthesis, standardised protocols for pathologist-in-the-loop quality filtering, and a publicly released benchmark dataset of colorectal and renal biopsy patches with synthetic augmentation splits. A secondary objective is to establish calibration-aware training procedures that account for the effect of synthetic data on classifier confidence. The project involves partners at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina and the Institute of Oncology of Vojvodina, who provide annotated slide material and clinical evaluation capacity.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute of Oncology of Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Digital Pathology Infrastructure and AI Method Harmonisation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PATHBRIDGE establishes shared digital pathology infrastructure and harmonised AI-assisted grading workflows between Serbian and Hungarian university hospital partners. Nina Despotović leads the work package on generative augmentation and domain adaptation, addressing scanner heterogeneity between the two countries' pathology laboratories. The work package delivers domain-adaptive GAN pipelines, stain normalisation tooling, and cross-site validation protocols. A joint annotated dataset of cervical and colorectal biopsy slides from three hospitals is being assembled under an agreed ethical framework. The project also includes a training programme for pathology residents at partner institutions on the use and limitations of AI grading assistance.
partners: University of Szeged Faculty of Medicine, Hungary
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Subotica General Hospital, Serbia

projects.title: Causality-Aware Data Management for Geo-Distributed Edge Deployments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CADGE investigates the design space of causality tracking mechanisms for systems that span both centralised cloud regions and resource-constrained edge nodes. The project combines formal modelling of clock protocols with experimental evaluation on a heterogeneous testbed comprising cloud virtual machines and embedded ARM nodes. Key objectives include: a formal classification of clock protocols by memory footprint and communication overhead; a prototype library supporting pluggable causality substrates; and a set of workload traces from a partner municipal sensor network in Novi Sad. The project funds one doctoral researcher and supports collaborations with partners in Genoa and Cluj-Napoca. Results are expected to be directly applicable to industrial IoT data collection pipelines.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
DIBRIS, University of Genoa
Faculty of Automation and Computer Science, Technical University of Cluj-Napoca

projects.title: Thermal Model Identification Toolchain for Energy-Efficient Residential Districts
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: THERMID develops a systematic toolchain for grey-box identification of building thermal models at district scale, targeting residential neighbourhoods in Vojvodina dominated by prefabricated panel construction from the 1970s and 1980s. The project combines automated experiment-design algorithms, wireless sensor deployment protocols, and a library of physically structured state-space model templates calibrated for the local building stock. Outputs include open-source Python software for parameter estimation and a field validation dataset collected from 12 apartments across four buildings in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin. The project is carried out in collaboration with the Institute for Urban Planning and Housing of Vojvodina and an energy auditing practice.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Urban Planning and Housing of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Energoaudit d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Comfort-Aware Control of Low-Energy Wall Systems in Cross-Border Educational Buildings
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COMFORTWALL addressed thermal comfort and energy efficiency in school buildings on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border, targeting buildings constructed before 1985. Radmila Jakovljević led the work package on dynamic thermal modelling and control algorithm development, responsible for identifying grey-box state-space models from monitoring data collected in four schools (two in Subotica, two in Baja, Hungary) and implementing simplified model predictive controllers on commercial building management systems. The project installed 86 sensor nodes, collected over 14 months of occupancy-period data, and demonstrated an average heating energy saving of 13% across the four buildings during the pilot control phase.
partners: Subotica Tech – College of Applied Sciences, Subotica
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
City of Subotica Public Building Management Office
Baja Municipal Development Agency, Hungary

projects.title: Scalable Dependency Graph Analysis Methods for Industrial Polyglot Build Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DEPSCALE addressed the scalability limits of static dependency analysis when applied to industrial repositories that combine three or more programming languages and exceed one million source files. The project developed graph compression techniques that preserved correctness of reachability queries while reducing memory footprint by 40–60%, produced a benchmark suite of 20 synthetic and real-world polyglot dependency graphs with ground-truth annotations, and delivered an open-source analysis library. A core outcome was a formal model of cross-language dependency semantics used to extend standard coupling metrics. Two industry partners contributed anonymised build logs and participated in evaluation of the toolchain under real working conditions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Digitech Systems d.o.o., Novi Sad
Syncware Engineering d.o.o., Beograd

projects.title: Modular Decomposition and Component Boundary Inference for Multi-Language Software Repositories
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral Serbia–Hungary collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Szeged investigating how modular decomposition theory can guide the semi-automated identification of component boundaries in polyglot monorepos. The project combines theoretical work on extensions of modular decomposition to edge-labelled graphs with applied experiments on six industry-sourced repositories. Activities include joint workshops, researcher exchanges, and co-supervision of one doctoral student at each institution. The primary deliverable is a prototype interactive tool that presents decomposition results to software architects and collects structured feedback for algorithm refinement.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Science and Informatics, University of Szeged

projects.title: Cross-Border Recognised Educational Credentials on Distributed Chain Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CREDCHAIN developed a technical and governance framework for issuing and verifying academic credentials as W3C Verifiable Credentials anchored to a permissioned distributed ledger shared among universities in Serbia, Romania, and Hungary. The project produced a functional pilot deployment at three universities, a DID method registered with the W3C DID method registry, open-source issuance and verification tooling, and a draft governance charter endorsed by two national accreditation bodies. The project also contributed to national policy discussions on the legal recognition of digitally issued academic documents under Serbian e-document legislation. Total budget was approximately 3.2 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania
University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Digital Identity Infrastructure for Higher Education Mobility in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: EDUBALK-DI is a Horizon Europe project under the ERASMUS+ co-funded strand that aims to establish a regional digital identity and credential verification infrastructure for student and staff mobility across six Western Balkans countries. Paunović leads Work Package 3, covering technical architecture, DID method specification, and interoperability testing. The work package involves deploying a multi-node DLT consortium, integrating with national student information systems, and conducting interoperability tests with the Europass Digital Credentials Infrastructure. The project runs through 2026 and includes a policy workstream targeting alignment with eIDAS 2.0 European Digital Identity Wallet requirements.
partners: University of Ljubljana, Slovenia (coordinator)

projects.title: Simulation-Assisted Framework for Evacuation Planning in Buildings with Uncertain Map Data
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SAFEMAP addressed the gap between the topological completeness assumed in standard evacuation simulation tools and the reality of incomplete or conflicting building documentation in Serbian public infrastructure. The project developed a probabilistic topology representation layer compatible with three widely used simulation engines and produced a decision-support prototype that ingests mixed-quality floor-plan sources and reports egress time distributions with explicit uncertainty bounds. Validation campaigns were conducted in two hospitals and one secondary school building with partially outdated plans. The project delivered open-source software components, three peer-reviewed publications, and a guidance document submitted to the Serbian Chamber of Engineers for consideration in updating national fire safety assessment practice.

Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade
City of Novi Sad – Directorate for Emergency Management

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Evacuation Simulation Standards for Public Buildings in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSEVAC brings together emergency management authorities and university research groups from Vojvodina and southern Hungary to compare evacuation simulation practice and data-collection protocols across the two national systems. Stojanović leads the work package on simulation methodology harmonisation, responsible for benchmarking three simulation tools against shared drill datasets collected in six jointly selected public buildings, four in Serbia and two in Hungary. The work package also coordinates joint training workshops for local fire safety inspectors. A harmonised data-exchange schema for building topology and occupancy data is a primary deliverable, intended to facilitate future cross-border emergency response planning.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
