projects.title: Secure Leakage-Aware Cryptographic Accelerator Design for Edge Devices
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates methods for quantifying and reducing physical side-channel leakage in AES hardware accelerators intended for resource-constrained edge devices. Work packages cover leakage characterisation on FPGA and ASIC-equivalent implementations, development of placement and routing constraint methodologies for EM leakage suppression, evaluation of Boolean masking and threshold implementation schemes against second-order attacks, and construction of an open benchmark dataset of annotated power and EM traces. The project team consists of four researchers at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and one collaborating researcher at the Politehnica University of Timișoara. A ChipWhisperer Pro capture platform and a near-field scanning rig were procured under the project budget.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Device Robustness of Machine-Learning Side-Channel Evaluations
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral Serbia–Hungary cooperation project with the Budapest University of Technology and Economics. The project studies the conditions under which CNN-based profiling models trained on one cryptographic hardware device can be adapted to a target device with minimal labelled data, focusing on AES implementations on different FPGA families. Activities include joint data collection campaigns at both partner laboratories, design and benchmarking of domain-adaptation algorithms, and exchange of two Ph.D. students per year. The project has produced three joint conference papers and one journal submission, and has established a shared trace repository accessible to both partners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

projects.title: Scalable Bayesian Inference Methods for Structured Probabilistic Models in Engineering Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops variational inference algorithms and normalising flow architectures that scale to probabilistic graphical models with thousands of variables, targeting engineering applications including process monitoring, fault diagnosis, and demand forecasting. The core scientific contributions include structured variational families for dynamic Bayesian networks and flow-based posterior approximations for models with constrained parameter spaces such as correlation matrices and simplices. Evaluation is performed on both benchmark datasets and real industrial data obtained through collaboration with manufacturing and energy partners in Vojvodina. The project also produces open-source software libraries and provides training opportunities for two doctoral students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
University of Belgrade, School of Electrical Engineering
Graz University of Technology, Institute of Statistics

projects.title: Probabilistic Inference Engines for Predictive Maintenance in Smart Manufacturing
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: This bilateral contract with Velox Automat d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based industrial automation company, funds development and deployment of a Bayesian change-point detection and fault classification system for CNC machining centres. The academic team is responsible for the probabilistic modelling component, including variational inference algorithms that run within the latency constraints of an embedded industrial PC. Deliverables include a validated software module, documentation, and training of the company's engineering staff in model maintenance and recalibration. The project has resulted in a shared dataset of vibration and acoustic emission signals from 12 machining centres collected over 18 months.
partners: Velox Automat d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Sparsity-Aware Intermediate Representations and Code Generation for Reconfigurable Compute Fabrics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a compiler infrastructure centred on a typed intermediate representation that carries sparsity annotations as first-class attributes alongside standard SSA constructs. The main deliverables are: a formal semantics for the sparse-annotated IR, a suite of analysis and transformation passes implemented in LLVM, and an evaluation methodology based on reproducible benchmarks compiled to FPGA-emulated accelerator targets. The project involves three researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and one from the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš. Industrial relevance is validated through collaboration with a local FPGA design house that provides access to proprietary accelerator models under a non-disclosure agreement. Results are published in open access venues wherever journal policy permits.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Vektron FPGA Design d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Register Allocation Strategies for Heterogeneous Tensor Processing Units
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates register allocation algorithms tailored to tensor processing units that expose multiple register files of different widths. The core research questions concern how to extend classical interference-graph methods to heterogeneous file configurations and how to integrate format-selection decisions into the allocation phase. The project funds one doctoral student and supports collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology through short-term researcher exchanges. A secondary objective is to produce open-source LLVM passes that can be reused by other groups working on domain-specific accelerators. Project outputs include at least two journal publications and participation in one international compiler workshop.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany

projects.title: Fault-Tolerant Observation and Control for High-Pressure Electrohydraulic Industrial Actuators
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a unified framework for simultaneous fault detection and control reconfiguration in electrohydraulic servo systems used in forging, rolling and pressing machinery. Research activities covered observer bank design, parity-space fault isolation, and sliding mode controller reconfiguration under partial sensor and actuator degradation. A 250-bar test bench at the Faculty of Technical Sciences was upgraded with programmable fault injection capability. The project produced seven journal papers and contributed to one patent application. Three industrial partners provided access to operational data from their production lines, enabling validation beyond laboratory conditions. Two doctoral students were trained through the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
School of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade
Metalopres d.o.o., Novi Sad
Hidraulika Sistem d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Advanced Sliding Mode Methods for Electrohydraulic Servo Drives in Energy-Intensive Industries
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between the University of Novi Sad and the Budapest University of Technology and Economics targeting energy efficiency in hydraulic drive systems used in the construction materials and steel processing sectors in the Vojvodina–Southern Hungary cross-border region. The project combined data-driven disturbance modelling with sliding mode control redesign to reduce energy consumption per production cycle. A shared experimental dataset of 60,000 recorded actuation cycles was assembled across both partner sites. Five joint publications and two international student exchanges resulted from the collaboration. The project also supported curriculum development for a joint elective module on industrial hydraulics.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Mechanical Engineering, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Kőváry Nehézgép Kft., Pécs
Vojvodinasteel d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Adaptive Finger Mechanisms for Low-Cost Body-Powered Prostheses in Low-Resource Settings
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the shortage of affordable, mechanically robust prosthetic fingers suitable for body-powered hands used in rehabilitation centres with limited technical support. The research team develops a family of parametric finger designs covering the adult male, adult female, and paediatric size ranges, using FDM-printable compliant mechanisms with tunable stiffness. Clinical partners at the Institute for Rehabilitation in Belgrade and the Special Hospital for Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in Novi Sad contribute motion-capture reference data and conduct pilot fitting trials with five adult transradial amputees. The project produces an open-source design repository, a web-based parametric sizing tool, and a fabrication guide targeted at orthopaedic workshops in the Western Balkans region.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Rehabilitation, Belgrade
Special Hospital for Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Novi Sad

projects.title: Vibration Isolation for Optical Precision Instruments on Industrial Structures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VISOPTS is a three-year project coordinated by Prof. Dragan Milošević at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad. The project aims to develop a measurement protocol for characterising micro-vibration environments in Serbian manufacturing plants and to derive platform design guidelines for passive isolation of optical instruments in those environments. Filip Knežević is responsible for the experimental campaigns, the shaker-table transmissibility measurements, and the validation tests on prototype isolation platforms. The project involves a partner at Politehnica University of Timișoara who contributes finite element modelling of the isolator assemblies. An industry advisory board includes two manufacturing companies in Vojvodina that provide access to their production floors for measurement.
partners: Politehnica University of Timișoara, Department of Mechanics and Strength of Materials
Agroprom Tehnika d.o.o., Novi Sad
Precizna Optika Inženjering d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Repetitive Control Strategies for Precision Motion in Flexible-Transmission Manufacturing Cells
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REPCON investigates learning and repetitive control methods for multi-axis Cartesian gantries in which belt or cable transmissions introduce significant elastic compliance. The project has three main activities: (1) experimental characterisation of transmission dynamics across a range of belt materials and lengths representative of small and medium manufacturing cells; (2) development of MIMO NOILC filters that account for cross-axis coupling and trial-length variability; and (3) a wear-adaptive layer that updates filter parameters using motor current signatures. The project team includes four researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, with a planned exchange visit to Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. Deliverables include open laboratory data sets and software tools released under a permissive licence.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Kragujevac, Serbia

projects.title: Graded Lattice Structures in Polymer Powder Bed Fusion: Optimisation, Characterisation and Fatigue
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the design and mechanical performance of graded-density lattice structures in PA12 parts produced by selective laser sintering. The work covers three interlinked activities: (1) generation of stress-mapped TPMS graded infills and their integration with topology-optimised shells; (2) quasi-static and fatigue characterisation of graded specimens over a range of relative densities and stress ratios; and (3) development of a homogenisation-based material model that propagates mesoscale density gradients into macroscale FEA predictions. Partners contribute complementary capabilities in DSC characterisation and SEM fractography. The expected outcome is a validated computational workflow and an open dataset of mechanical test results for graded PA12 lattice components.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Institute for Materials Testing Novi Sad

projects.title: Recycled Powder Effects on Structural Reliability of Topology-Optimised SLS Components
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project systematically quantifies how powder ageing and refresh ratio affect the mechanical reliability of topology-optimised PA12 SLS components. Starting from a controlled powder ageing protocol, specimens and functional brackets are manufactured at five refresh levels. Mechanical testing covers tensile, compressive, and fatigue regimes. The project also develops a degradation-adjusted material card for use in optimisation software so that components can be designed to remain safe at refresh ratios up to 50 %. Industrial relevance is high because SLS service bureaus routinely operate near or above the 50 % refresh threshold to reduce material cost. The project includes one industrial advisory partner from the Vojvodina manufacturing sector.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Plastform d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Tactile Sensing and Control Strategies for Safe Robotic Handling of Soft and Fragile Products
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SOFTGRIP addresses the challenge of automating the handling of perishable and deformable goods — fresh produce, soft confectionery, and medical gel packages — in logistics and food-processing lines. The project develops fingertip modules that combine piezoresistive tactile arrays with proximity sensing, together with real-time algorithms for estimating the internal stress state of grasped objects from surface tactile measurements. A key deliverable is a grip-force controller that keeps von Mises stress in grasped objects below a user-defined damage threshold. The project involves two Faculty of Technical Sciences research groups and the BioSense Institute, with an advisory role from an agri-food automation company based in Novi Sad. Three Ph.D. students are funded through the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
AgroTech Automatika d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Network for Standardised Evaluation of Tactile Sensing Technologies in Collaborative Robotics
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: TACTINET is a bilateral research collaboration between the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the Warsaw University of Technology, funded through the Serbian–Polish science cooperation programme administered by the Ministry of Science. The project focuses on developing shared experimental protocols and a benchmark dataset for contact-force distribution estimation across heterogeneous tactile sensor technologies, including piezoresistive, capacitive, and optical waveguide designs. Each partner contributes two sensor platforms and participates in reciprocal staff exchanges. The primary output is a jointly authored benchmark paper and a publicly released dataset, supporting reproducibility in the field. Short-term researcher visits of two weeks each are planned annually.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Warsaw University of Technology, Poland

projects.title: Energy-Optimal Motion Planning for Cable-Driven Robotic Systems in Industrial Large-Volume Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project targets a reduction in electrical energy demand for cable-driven parallel robots used in large-volume manufacturing and construction positioning tasks. Core activities include development of an elastic dynamic model incorporating cable mass and viscoelasticity, derivation of energy-optimal trajectory planning algorithms based on direct collocation with variable regenerative braking efficiency, and real-time implementation using embedded NMPC on a dSPACE platform. The project integrates experimental validation on the group's reconfigurable six-cable CDPR testbed and benchmarks solutions for configurations up to eight cables. A secondary objective is the formulation of reconfigurable anchor placement strategies that preserve energy optimality across multi-task sequences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Ljubljana, Slovenia

projects.title: Cable-Driven Robotic Systems for Automated Positioning in Prefabricated Building Construction
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project examined the application of cable-driven parallel robots as low-cost alternatives to overhead cranes and gantry systems in prefabricated construction. The Novi Sad team led the work package on dynamic modelling and trajectory planning, adapting existing CDPR methods to the irregular workspace geometries typical of construction sites and to the high payload-to-robot-mass ratio required by panel handling. Field trials were conducted at a prefabricated concrete panel facility in Subotica. The project produced guidelines for anchor installation, cable specification, and controller parameterisation suitable for deployment by construction companies without dedicated robotics staff.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Subotica Construction Research Centre, Serbia

projects.title: Adaptive Emission Monitoring for Near-Zero-Defect Hard Milling
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a closed-loop AE monitoring and adaptive feed-rate control system for hard milling targeting near-zero-defect production. Activities included construction of a reference dataset (96 tool runs, later released publicly), design of embedded signal processing algorithms meeting 10 ms latency constraints, and integration of the controller with an OPC-UA interface on two industrial machining centres. Project outcomes included three journal publications, the open dataset, and a prototype controller board validated in collaboration with a regional tooling company. The provincial secretariat co-funded equipment maintenance and personnel; the Science Fund covered research staff and dissemination.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Precizija d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Digital and AI-Assisted Manufacturing for SMEs in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project aiming to transfer digital manufacturing capabilities — including in-process monitoring and data-driven process control — to small and medium-sized enterprises in the Vojvodina and western Romania regions. Mirković leads the work package on sensor integration and data acquisition standards, responsible for delivering training workshops, a reference hardware architecture document, and pilot installations at two SME partners. The project also includes a joint summer school for MSc students from both countries. His group contributes acoustic emission monitoring expertise and supports adaptation of monitoring algorithms to lower-cost hardware platforms available to SMEs.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Metal Forma d.o.o., Zrenjanin
Prodex Invest S.R.L., Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Wireless Power for Autonomous Docking Systems in Smart Warehouses
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WIPADS aimed to develop a validated design methodology for inductive charging pads suitable for AGV fleets operating in Serbian logistics and manufacturing facilities. The project covered coil topology selection for position-tolerant operation, ferrite shielding optimisation, and foreign-object detection. A 1 kW four-pad test track was constructed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and used to benchmark designs generated by the surrogate modelling framework developed within the project. An open dataset of 3 840 foreign-object detection events was produced and published. The project involved three partner institutions and produced seven journal articles, one book chapter, and two master's theses. It also established a continuing collaboration with researchers at the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Integration of Autonomous Vehicle Charging Infrastructure in Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSLINK-AGV addresses the adoption of wireless charging for AGVs in small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on charging pad standardisation and electromagnetic compatibility testing, providing technical guidance to pilot deployments at two participating SMEs. The project funds the development of a simplified EMC measurement protocol suited to SME quality-assurance workflows and a freely downloadable pad selection guide. Partner organisations include a Hungarian university of applied sciences and an industry association from the Vojvodina region. Total project budget is approximately 1.1 million EUR, of which the Novi Sad team manages 280 000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, Óbuda University, Budapest, Hungary
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce – Manufacturing Sector Association
Széchenyi Automotive and Robotics Research Centre, Győr, Hungary

projects.title: Soft Robotic Grasping Solutions for Fragile Produce in Automated Sorting Facilities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the lack of reliable, low-damage grasping technology in Serbian fresh-produce sorting lines, where manual handling still dominates due to the fragility of items such as berries, stone fruit, and peppers. The work covers actuator design, fabrication process standardisation, FE-based shape modelling, and closed-loop pressure control. Filip Mirković contributes specifically to the finite element surrogate pipeline and the closed-loop pressure regulation subsystem. The project partners include one company operating a vegetable packing facility in Vojvodina and a research team at the University of Kragujevac covering embedded electronics. Target outcome is a laboratory prototype gripper demonstrated at industrially relevant cycle rates.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Vojvođanski Svježi Plodovi d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Magnetically Levitated Scanning Stage for Next-Generation Semiconductor Fixture Qualification
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat razvija kompaktan magnetno levitiran pozicioni sto sa putanjom 300 mm × 300 mm i pozicionom nesigurnošću ispod 50 nm (3σ), namenjen kvalifikaciji litografskih fikstura u industrijskim uslovima. Ključni ciljevi su: (1) projektovanje modularnog sistema zavojnica koji dozvoljava rekonfiguraciju za različite veličine nosioca, (2) razvoj upravljačkog softvera sa realnovremenskim estimatorom tereta i iterativnim učećim kontrolerom, i (3) izrada protokola za prenošenje kalibracije između laboratorijskih i industrijskih okruženja. Partneri uključuju jednu kompaniju sa NTP Novi Sad specijalizovanu za preciznu elektroničku opremu. Planirani rezultati obuhvataju dva rada u časopisima sa SCI liste i jedan funkcionalni prototip.
partners: Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Precizija d.o.o., NTP Novi Sad

projects.title: Physics-informed monitoring of planetary gearboxes for industrial conveyor and wind energy applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops and validates a monitoring framework that combines multi-body torsional dynamics models with vibration signal processing to detect early-stage surface pitting in planetary gearboxes used in conveyor drives and small wind turbines. The core activities include constructing a parameterised simulation library covering gearbox ratios and planet counts common in Serbian industry, performing accelerated fatigue experiments on two physical gearboxes, and deriving operating-condition-aware detection thresholds from the combined simulation and experimental database. A prototype embedded monitoring unit is being developed for field validation at an industrial partner site. The project involves three research groups from the University of Novi Sad and one from the University of Belgrade.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade
Konvejer Tehnika d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-border network for vibration-based diagnostics in rotating machinery
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: VIBROLINK established a collaborative research and training network between two Serbian and two Hungarian university departments active in vibration diagnostics and rotating machinery maintenance. The project included joint laboratory exercises, exchange of test datasets, two joint workshops, and development of a shared online course module in vibration-based fault detection. The work package led by Ognjanov covered gearbox diagnostics methodology harmonisation and the preparation of a joint experimental dataset on spur and planetary gearbox faults under comparable test conditions at the Novi Sad and Pécs facilities.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary
Óbuda University, Budapest, Hungary
Faculty of Engineering, University of Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Torque-Transparent Exoskeleton Control for Neurological Rehabilitation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TOREX addressed the calibration burden and real-time computational demands of EMG-driven torque-transparent exoskeleton control for post-stroke and spinal cord injury rehabilitation. The project developed accelerated motor unit decomposition algorithms suitable for embedded hardware, validated fatigue-adaptive model update rules during clinical exercise sessions, and produced a prototype knee exoskeleton with integrated 32-channel sEMG acquisition. A cohort of twelve stroke patients at the University Clinical Centre Vojvodina participated in a ten-session feasibility trial. The project produced seven peer-reviewed publications and one patent application, and trained three doctoral students in the integrated methods. Equipment purchased under TOREX included an upgraded high-density EMG amplifier system and an embedded GPU compute module.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Clinic for Rehabilitation Medicine, University Clinical Centre Vojvodina
Institute for Rehabilitation, Belgrade

projects.title: Embedded Biomechanical Assistance for Rehabilitation in Key clinical settings
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: EMBARK is a cross-border cooperation project between research groups in Novi Sad and Pécs aimed at developing shared protocols and equipment for wearable exoskeleton testing across Hungarian and Serbian rehabilitation centres. The Novi Sad team leads the work package on signal processing and torque control, contributing the EMG-driven estimation pipeline developed in TOREX. The Hungarian partner contributes clinical trial capacity and patient recruitment at two rehabilitation hospitals in Baranya County. Joint training workshops for clinical physiotherapists and biomedical engineers are a key output. The project has a total budget of approximately 490 000 EUR, with the Novi Sad share covering equipment and two research positions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Pécs
Rehabilitation Centre Baranya, Pécs
Institute for Rehabilitation, Belgrade

projects.title: Real-Time Parametric Digital Twins for Overhead Crane Safety and Efficiency
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The CRANTWIN project developed methods and hardware prototypes for synchronising parametric digital twins of overhead cranes with their physical counterparts using encoder velocity and rope-tension feedback at update rates up to 500 Hz. The project addressed three specific gaps: sensor placement optimisation for parameter observability, handling of communication delays in edge-cloud monitoring architectures, and integration of twin-derived frequency estimates into adaptive input-shaping controllers. A laboratory testbed was upgraded with a new dual-sensor tension measurement system and a dedicated edge server. The project produced eight peer-reviewed publications and one master's thesis. Industrial applicability was validated through collaboration with a metal fabrication company operating five-tonne bridge cranes.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Kovinar d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Border Mechatronics Education and Research Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MECROSS established shared laboratory infrastructure and joint student exchange activities between the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Informatics at the University of Miskolc. Within the project, Đorđević contributed to the development of shared testbed protocols for crane dynamics experiments, co-supervised two student research visits, and contributed to a jointly authored technical report on encoder-based estimation methods. The project also funded a short equipment procurement enabling the group to acquire the dSPACE MicroLabBox unit that subsequently became central to the CRANTWIN project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Miskolc, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Informatics

projects.title: Simulation-Supported Workforce Flexibility Planning for Mixed-Model Assembly in Serbian SMEs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SIMFLEX developed a structured methodology and supporting software toolkit for integrating workforce flexibility planning into discrete-event simulation models of mixed-model assembly lines. The project targeted Serbian small and medium-sized manufacturers with 20–150 employees in the metalworking and electronics sectors. Activities included field data collection at five partner companies, development of a skill-matrix encoding standard compatible with Plant Simulation and open-source SimPy models, and design of a scenario generator that automatically constructs cross-training investment alternatives for evaluation. The project produced validated simulation templates, a practitioner handbook, and three peer-reviewed journal articles. Two partner companies adopted project outputs in operational planning within the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Metalprodukt Palić d.o.o.
Elektromehanika Futog d.o.o.

projects.title: Digital Twin Deployment in SME Manufacturing: Lightweight Architectures and Decision-Support Tools
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DITSME is a cross-border cooperation project examining barriers to and enablers of digital-twin adoption in small and medium-sized manufacturers in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Marković leads the work package on simulation modelling and data integration, responsible for developing and testing IoT-to-simulation pipelines at four partner companies. The work package produced the lightweight digital-shadow architecture described in the 2024 journal publication and provides training workshops for company engineers. The project also includes a comparative study of readiness levels across 60 surveyed firms in both countries, with results informing regional industrial policy recommendations submitted to the Provincial Secretariat.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Bay Zoltán Applied Research Institute, Győr, Hungary
Vojvodina ICT Cluster
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Quantitative Risk Assessment Methods for Regional Supply Chains in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project develops quantitative tools for supply chain risk assessment tailored to small and medium-sized manufacturers operating in the Vojvodina region. The team combines Monte Carlo simulation, fault tree analysis, and multi-criteria scoring to produce a practical risk assessment toolkit that can be applied without specialised optimisation software. The project involves fieldwork with eight SMEs across the food processing and light manufacturing sectors in Vojvodina, collecting disruption event histories and procurement cost data. Deliverables include a documented methodology, a spreadsheet-based tool for risk scoring, and a set of case study reports. Lukács is responsible for the stochastic simulation component and co-authors the case study reports.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Regional Chamber of Commerce Novi Sad
Institute for Industrial Systems, Novi Sad

projects.title: Ergonomic Assessment and Redesign Guidelines for Automotive Sub-Assembly Workstations in the Vojvodina Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop a practical ergonomic assessment and redesign toolkit tailored to the specific task profiles and workforce characteristics of automotive sub-assembly plants operating in Vojvodina. Field measurements were conducted at four supplier facilities, covering a total of 78 workstations. Methods applied included OWAS, RULA, the NIOSH Revised Lifting Equation, and laboratory biomechanical modelling using the Faculty's EMG and motion capture equipment. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–English) practitioner guide and a workstation data sheet format adopted by two participating companies. A set of redesign case studies with cost-benefit estimates was compiled and disseminated through a regional industry workshop attended by 34 production engineers and occupational health practitioners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Occupational Health, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Autokomponent doo, Novi Sad
Plastmont AD, Subotica

projects.title: Machinability and Process Optimisation for Lightweight Aluminium Alloy Components in Automotive Production
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates machinability characteristics of several commercial aluminium–silicon casting alloys relevant to automotive structural part production, with attention to cutting forces, tool wear progression, and surface integrity under dry and MQL conditions. Activities include systematic machining trials on a CNC machining centre, metallographic characterisation of workpiece alloys, and development of empirical and semi-analytical process models. A secondary objective is to establish a small reference dataset of machining outcomes that can be accessed by regional manufacturing companies for process planning purposes. Jokić contributes to experimental trials, data acquisition, and model fitting as part of his doctoral research activities.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Materials Testing, Novi Sad
Metalform d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Eco-efficiency Assessment of Process Chains in Vojvodina's Automotive Parts Supply Base
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aims to build a database of energy and material flow coefficients for manufacturing process chains operated by automotive parts suppliers in the Vojvodina region. Partner companies produce stamped, turned, and welded components for the regional automotive supply chain. Researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences collect shop-floor data and apply LCA and LCC methods to identify efficiency bottlenecks. Grujić is responsible for data collection protocols, energy monitoring campaigns at two partner companies, and the development of a spreadsheet-based LCC calculation tool intended for use by company engineers without specialised LCA software. The project will produce an open-access dataset and a practical guidance document.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Metalform d.o.o., Novi Sad
Preciz Tech d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Fixture-Induced Tolerance Accumulation in Multi-Stage CNC Machining of Lightweight Structural Parts
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how fixture compliance and locator geometry errors combine to produce tolerance accumulation across three or more CNC setups in lightweight aluminium and magnesium structural parts. The core activity is building validated reduced-order FE models that allow rapid evaluation of fixture layout alternatives during process planning. Experimental work is carried out on the faculty's Mazak VMC using instrumented modular fixtures. Industrial relevance is maintained through collaboration with a regional supplier of precision machined components. Expected deliverables include a publicly available influence-matrix library for common part families and a process-planner decision guide for locating scheme selection in multi-stage operations.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Precizna Obrada d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Cross-Border Transfer of Fixture Design Knowledge for Small and Medium Manufacturers
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: ADRIAFIX addressed the gap between academic fixture optimisation methods and their adoption in small and medium-sized machining workshops in the Romanian–Serbian border region. The University of Novi Sad team led the work package on training material development, translating FE-based fixture analysis methods into practical worksheets and short courses deliverable without specialised software licences. Romanian partners contributed industrial case studies from automotive sub-suppliers in Timișoara. The project ran six workshop sessions attended by a total of 74 process engineers and produced a bilingual (Serbian/Romanian) practical handbook. Sustainability is maintained through a shared online repository of case study models.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Faculty of Engineering
Regionalna Razvojna Agencija Vojvodine
Centrul de Inovare Industrială Timișoara

projects.title: Reliability-Driven Maintenance Scheduling and Spare-Parts Optimisation for SME Process Industries in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: REMSPARE addresses the limited capacity of small and medium-sized process-industry firms in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region to implement data-driven maintenance and inventory strategies. The project collects failure and maintenance cost data from twelve partner plants, develops calibrated Weibull and imperfect-repair models for each, and delivers a web-based decision-support tool that recommends maintenance intervals and reorder points without requiring in-house reliability engineers. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on modelling methodology and tool validation. A secondary workpackage deals with training workshops held alternately in Subotica and Pécs. Expected outputs include three joint publications, the decision-support tool released under an open licence, and a cross-border maintenance benchmarking database.

projects.title: Tracking Competing Failure Modes in Heterogeneous Equipment Fleets Using Bayesian Hierarchical Models
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FAILTRACK is funded under the IDEAS programme of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. The project develops Bayesian hierarchical Weibull models that borrow statistical strength across a fleet of nominally identical machines to estimate component-level competing-failure-mode intensities when individual-machine failure histories are short. Stefan Vuković contributes to the spare-parts demand module, which translates the posterior failure-intensity distributions into predictive demand distributions for use in inventory optimisation. The project works with data from three Serbian industrial partners covering turbine compressors, rolling mills, and belt conveyors. Results are being integrated into an R package for public release. Principal investigator is a colleague in the Department of Production Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
partners: Department of Production Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Optimisation-Driven Build Preparation for Load-Bearing Metal AM Components
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: OPTIBUILD addresses the disconnection between topology optimisation solvers and downstream build preparation tools in metal additive manufacturing workflows. The project develops a linked computational chain in which the topology optimisation stage receives feedback on support volume, predicted distortion, and post-process milling requirements, and adjusts objective weights accordingly. The application target is load-bearing aluminium and titanium brackets for mechanical engineering use cases. The project involves three build-and-test campaigns on an LPBF platform, producing a validation dataset of approximately 60 bracket specimens. An open-source Python interface connecting an optimisation kernel to commercial slicing software is among the planned deliverables. The project is hosted at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Materials Testing, Belgrade

projects.title: Additively Manufactured Fixture Systems for High-Speed Machining
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A short-term industry contract with a regional precision machining company to redesign two families of fixture brackets used on five-axis machining centres. The scope included topology optimisation, build orientation selection, LPBF fabrication, and functional testing under production cutting conditions. Dejan Jeremić led the academic team and served as the primary technical contact. The project produced four validated bracket designs that entered series production. Confidential details are withheld under a non-disclosure agreement, but aggregate results were reported in a 2025 journal publication.
partners: Precizija d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Spatially Resolved Wear Mechanism Mapping in PVD-Coated Carbide Cutting Tools Under Dry High-Speed Turning
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish spatially resolved maps of dominant wear mechanisms along the active cutting edges of TiAlN, TiSiN and CrAlN coated inserts after controlled turning exposures. Workpiece materials included AISI 4340 (hardened), compacted graphite iron and ADI. Characterisation relied on SEM/EDS mapping, synchrotron XRD, and FIB cross-section analysis at defined positions. A database of mechanism maps, each linked to quantified coating properties and cutting conditions, was assembled for three coating families. The database was subsequently used to calibrate the thermomechanical wear model developed in collaboration with partners in Italy and Hungary. Two PhD students were funded through the project; both theses were submitted within the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Materials Science, Brno University of Technology
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Miskolc

projects.title: Bilateral Cooperation on Multilayer PVD Coating Architecture and Wear Performance in Interrupted Cutting
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A two-year bilateral collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and Wrocław University of Science and Technology focused on multilayer TiAlN/TiN and TiAlN/CrN coatings for interrupted cutting conditions. Each side contributed deposition and characterisation capabilities; Wrocław provided coatings via their magnetron sputtering system and Novi Sad performed all turning tests and SEM/XRD analysis. Outcomes included two joint journal publications and a joint workshop held in Novi Sad in 2020. The collaboration provided foundational data for the bilayer period investigation published in Wear in 2022.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Poland

projects.title: Lean Flow Methods for High-Mix Manufacturing SMEs in Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This project supported the transfer and adaptation of lean flow methods, specifically value stream mapping and pull-system design, to small and medium manufacturers operating in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The Faculty of Technical Sciences contributed expertise in job-shop VSM and changeover reduction, while partners on the Hungarian side contributed process simulation and ERP integration knowledge. The project delivered a methodology toolkit adapted for SMEs with fewer than 100 employees, a training curriculum piloted with 11 companies, and a benchmarking database of lean performance indicators drawn from participating firms. Anja Sabo led the work package on methodology development and company case study documentation.
partners: Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Széchenyi István University, Győr, Hungary

projects.title: Setup Time Minimisation in Flexible Manufacturing Cells Through Combined Scheduling and SMED
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the combined optimisation of job sequencing and physical setup reduction in flexible manufacturing cells. The central hypothesis is that scheduling decisions and SMED-derived setup time estimates should be co-optimised rather than treated sequentially. The research involves developing scheduling models that incorporate sequence-dependent setup time matrices derived empirically via SMED studies, and testing these models in a laboratory cell at the Faculty of Technical Sciences as well as in two partner companies. Expected outputs include validated algorithms for integrated scheduling and setup optimisation, a software prototype, and at least four journal publications. The project funds one doctoral student and supports collaboration with the University of Kragujevac and the Polytechnic University of Timișoara.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Faculty of Industrial Engineering, Polytechnic University of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Measurement Strategy Standardisation for Prismatic Parts in Regional Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project addressed a documented gap in CMM inspection practice among small and medium manufacturing enterprises in Vojvodina: the absence of traceable, standardised measurement strategies for prismatic part families. Working with four manufacturing SMEs supplying the automotive and hydraulics sectors, the project developed a library of parametric measurement strategy templates covering seven prismatic part families, validated against calibrated reference artefacts and cross-checked using an accredited external laboratory. A training programme for CMM operators was also developed and delivered to 24 participants across the partner companies. Final deliverables included a template library implemented in Calypso software and a guidance document aligned with ISO 15530-3 and ISO/TR 14638.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Digital Workflow Integration for CMM-Based Quality Assurance in Advanced Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DIGIMETRO investigated the integration of CAD-based inspection planning, CMM measurement execution, and statistical process control into a continuous digital quality assurance workflow for prismatic components. Novaković led the work package on measurement uncertainty quantification and automated inspection routine generation from STEP AP242 models, contributing the feature recognition and probing point assignment system. The project involved partners from mechanical engineering and computer science faculties, with an industrial validation case study at a precision machining company. Outcomes include open-source Python tooling for STEP-to-CMM routine translation, a validated uncertainty model for automated routines, and two peer-reviewed publications. The project addresses manufacturing readiness levels 4–6.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad (lead)
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Precizna Mehanika Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Digital Integration of Process Planning in Small and Medium Manufacturing Enterprises
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project examines barriers to adoption of CAPP and PDM tools in manufacturing SMEs in the Vojvodina region, combining a survey of 35 companies with the development and pilot deployment of lightweight integration middleware. Vesna Todorović contributes to the feature-recognition module and to data-collection activities at partner companies. The project involves two industrial partners: a CNC subcontractor and a tooling manufacturer. Expected outputs include a publicly available mapping schema for CAPP–PDM data exchange, a best-practice guide for SME implementers, and two peer-reviewed publications. The work directly informs her doctoral research on knowledge-based process planning in SME contexts.
partners: Precizija d.o.o. Novi Sad
Alatnica Fruška d.o.o. Irig
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Resilient Supply Linkages for Automotive Tier-2 Networks in Cross-Border Regions of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RESILINK aimed to identify and quantify single-source dependency risks in automotive Tier-2 supply chains spanning the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region and to develop a shared decision support toolkit for procurement managers at participating companies. The project compiled a dataset of 94 Tier-2 suppliers and their material flows, conducted 63 procurement manager interviews, and produced a web-based screening tool implementing a lightweight fuzzy TOPSIS model. A training programme for procurement staff was delivered at three company sites. The project produced four technical reports, two journal papers, and one public-access dataset of anonymised supply network metrics for the region.

projects.title: Supply Chain Resilience under Geopolitical Uncertainty: Modelling and Decision Support for Serbian Manufacturers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SCREGEO develops integrated quantitative methods for assessing and mitigating the exposure of Serbian manufacturing supply chains to geopolitical disruption risks. Research activities include construction of a regional supplier database, development of scenario sets calibrated to Balkan geopolitical dynamics, and implementation of combined fuzzy TOPSIS–simulation models validated against historical disruption episodes. The project collaborates with six industrial partners and two regional universities. Expected outputs include a validated software prototype for supply chain resilience screening, three to four peer-reviewed journal papers, and guidelines for procurement policy at SME manufacturers. Mid-project review in 2024 confirmed all deliverable milestones on schedule.

projects.title: Fatigue-Aware Shift Scheduling Methods for Continuous-Process Industries in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: FATSCHED brought together six partners from Serbia, Romania, Hungary, and Germany to develop validated fatigue-risk-constrained scheduling methods for continuous-process industries. Kovač led the work package on mathematical modelling, responsible for deriving the piecewise-linear alertness approximations and the MILP formulations used across all industrial case studies. The project produced an open-source scheduling library, three validated case studies at partner companies, and training materials for occupational-health practitioners. Field validation was conducted at a glass manufacturer, a chemical plant, and a paper mill. The project also provided input to an ongoing revision of Serbian occupational-health guidance on night-shift frequency limits.

projects.title: Optimisation-Based Roster Design for Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: OPTROS addressed the gap between academic scheduling research and the practical needs of Serbian manufacturing SMEs, which typically lack operations-research expertise and use manual or spreadsheet-based scheduling. The project developed a modelling toolkit adapted to Serbian labour-law specifics, including public-holiday rules, on-call provisions, and part-time contract regulations introduced by 2019 amendments. Three SMEs in the food and packaging sectors served as living laboratories. The project produced parametric model libraries, a decision-support prototype (later extended in the 2024 DSS journal paper), and a practitioner handbook distributed through the Serbian Association of Industrial Engineers. Two PhD students were trained on the project.

projects.title: Data-Driven Maintenance Optimisation for Hydraulic Systems in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to develop and validate a maintenance decision-support toolkit tailored to the data constraints typical of small and medium-sized manufacturers in Serbia. The core methodology combines proportional hazard modelling with bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification and links predicted failure distributions to a spare-parts inventory optimiser. Field validation is conducted at three partner companies operating hydraulic pressing and assembly equipment in the Novi Sad and Zrenjanin industrial zones. The toolkit is implemented as a Python-based desktop application and tested over 18 months of prospective use. Dissemination includes training workshops for maintenance engineers and open-source release of the software under a permissive licence.

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Predictive Maintenance for Automated Production Lines
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMAINT brings together three academic institutions and two industrial partners from Hungary and Serbia to exchange methods and tools for predictive maintenance in automated production. Bogićević leads the work package on lifetime data collection protocols and statistical modelling, which produces a joint methodology guide harmonising Hungarian and Serbian industrial practice. The project includes reciprocal staff exchanges totalling eight researcher-months, joint seminars in Novi Sad and Szeged, and a shared test database of anonymised failure records from partner companies. A final workshop targets maintenance managers from both countries.

projects.title: Performance Measurement Frameworks for ISO-Transitioning SMEs in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PERFMAP aimed to develop and disseminate practical performance measurement toolkits tailored to manufacturing SMEs in cross-border regions of Hungary and Serbia undergoing ISO 9001 transitions. The project combined empirical survey research across 140 companies, participatory tool development workshops in Novi Sad and Subotica, and a 12-month pilot in 18 volunteer companies. Outputs included a validated short-form BSC instrument, a pre-certification readiness checklist, and a freely accessible web-based self-assessment platform developed by the Hungarian partner. The project also supported four joint training events attended by approximately 200 quality managers and consultants. Two peer-reviewed journal publications and five conference papers were produced during the project period.

projects.title: Evaluating Long-Term Effectiveness of Quality Management System Implementations in Serbian Manufacturing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: QMSEVAL is a longitudinal study tracking operational and financial performance outcomes in 60 Serbian manufacturing SMEs across three years following ISO 9001 certification or recertification. The project applies a repeated-measures design with annual data collection combining company records, structured manager interviews, and external audit documentation. Analysis focuses on identifying factors that sustain post-certification performance gains versus those associated with performance drift. Secondary objectives include the development of a predictive model for post-certification performance and the validation of a composite performance index against independent financial audit data. The project supports one doctoral student and collaborates with the Faculty of Organizational Sciences, Belgrade, on survey design and data analysis.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Evidence-Based Stage-Gate Frameworks for Manufacturing R&D Funding in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and tested evidence-based stage-gate frameworks adapted to the institutional and sectoral context of manufacturing R&D funding in Serbia and the broader Western Balkans region. Activities included a survey of 112 project teams from completed innovation calls, a database construction of 200+ assessed proposals, development of sector-stratified TRL scoring instruments, and a reviewer calibration protocol tested in cooperation with two national funding bodies. The project produced three peer-reviewed publications, an open-access scoring toolkit, and a policy brief submitted to the Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation. A master's thesis and a doctoral thesis chapter were produced within the project.
partners: Faculty of Organizational Sciences, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Innovation Fund of Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Manufacturing Innovation Assessment: Harmonising TRL Evaluation Practice in Hungary–Serbia Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSINNO addresses the lack of harmonised technology readiness evaluation practice between Hungarian and Serbian regional innovation programmes, which creates barriers for cross-border manufacturing R&D collaborations. Milana Lekić leads the work package on assessment methodology, responsible for comparative analysis of existing evaluation frameworks in Csongrád-Csanád County and Vojvodina, joint development of a bilingual TRL assessment guide, and delivery of three joint reviewer training workshops. Other work packages cover SME capacity building, programme management coordination, and dissemination. The project involves five partner organisations across both countries and targets manufacturing SMEs in food processing, metal fabrication, and packaging sectors.

projects.title: Practical Noise Assessment and Surveillance Tools for Metalworking SMEs in Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate a set of practical noise assessment and audiometric surveillance tools adapted to the resource constraints of metalworking SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. Vulin led the work package on measurement methodology, coordinating field surveys at 22 enterprises across the two countries. Deliverables included a bilingual field measurement guide, a spreadsheet-based exposure estimation tool tested against Class 1 instrumentation at six sites, and a surveillance scheduling template aligned with both EU Directive 2003/10/EC and national Serbian and Hungarian transposition legislation. The project trained 34 company safety coordinators in a three-day practical workshop held in Novi Sad and Pécs.

projects.title: Audiometric Surveillance Continuity in High-Noise Manufacturing: Barriers, Enablers and Protocol Optimisation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AUDWATCH investigates why audiometric surveillance programmes in Serbian high-noise manufacturing frequently lose continuity after initial implementation and tests interventions to improve adherence. The project combines a cross-sectional employer survey (target n = 80 enterprises), structured interviews with occupational physicians and safety coordinators, and a randomised comparison of two surveillance delivery models — clinic-based and mobile unit-based — in a sample of 12 metalworking SMEs. Primary outcomes are worker audiogram completion rates at 12 and 24 months. Secondary outcomes include time-to-referral for workers meeting threshold shift criteria and employer-reported administrative burden. The project is generating revised protocol guidance documents intended for submission to the national occupational safety standards body.
partners: Faculty of Occupational Safety, University of Niš
Occupational Health Centre Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Dynamic Pricing and Workload Management in Small Make-to-Order Manufacturing Firms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops and validates a suite of dynamic pricing models for small and medium-sized make-to-order job shops in Serbia, combining queueing-theoretic workload models with empirically estimated demand elasticity functions. Phase one collected order and capacity data from twelve partner firms and ran stated-preference surveys with their customers. Phase two developed and tested Bayesian learning pricing rules and lightweight surrogate models suitable for deployment in standard ERP environments. Phase three piloted pricing tools at four firms over six months and evaluated revenue and customer satisfaction outcomes. The project produced eight journal papers and one open-source pricing toolkit. Partners include industrial SMEs in the metalworking sector and one software firm supporting ERP customisation.
partners: Metalotehna d.o.o., Novi Sad
Precizija Inženjering d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Advanced Manufacturing Management for SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Miskolc aimed at transferring advanced production management methods to manufacturing SMEs in the Vojvodina and Northern Hungary regions. Hadžić led the work package on pricing and demand management, coordinating survey activities across both countries and delivering a two-day training programme for production managers on workload-based pricing. The project produced a bilingual Serbian–Hungarian practical guide on revenue management for job shops, disseminated to 85 firms through regional chambers of commerce. The project also established a shared dataset of anonymised order records for ongoing research use.

projects.title: Adaptive Statistical Process Control for Non-Normal Manufacturing Processes in the Western Balkans Plastics Industry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a framework of adaptive CUSUM and EWMA monitoring schemes tailored to non-normal quality characteristics arising in injection moulding and extrusion. The work includes derivation of exact and approximate control limits for gamma, log-normal, and Burr XII process models, development of economic-statistical design procedures incorporating variable sampling intervals, and validation on process data collected from three Serbian plastics manufacturers. Software tools implementing the designed charts as add-ins to standard statistical packages are produced. The project also provides training workshops for quality engineers at partner companies and contributes to doctoral training at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

PlastSerb d.o.o., Novi Sad, Serbia
Polymold Inženjering d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Quality Monitoring Strategies for Injection Moulding with Recycled Thermoplastics
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RECYQUAL addresses the increased process variability introduced by recycled thermoplastics in injection moulding across the Hungary–Serbia border region. Tadić leads the work package on online monitoring methods, developing SPC charts adapted to the higher and time-varying non-normality of melt viscosity and dimensional outputs from recycled-material production lines. Partner institutions contribute expertise in polymer characterisation and life cycle assessment. The project includes pilot implementations at two cross-border manufacturing sites and develops a shared laboratory protocol for Phase I data collection under non-stationary process conditions. Dissemination includes a bilingual technical guide for SME quality staff.

projects.title: Maintenance Performance Measurement and Improvement Frameworks for the Agro-Food Processing Industry in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed and tested a harmonised maintenance performance measurement methodology applicable across food and beverage processing plants in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region. projects.title: Reducing Losses in Continuous Liquid Food Production Lines Through Data-Driven Maintenance Scheduling
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SLIMLINE investigates quantitative methods for translating shift-level OEE loss data into optimised preventive and condition-based maintenance schedules for continuous liquid food processing lines. The project combines Markov-chain degradation modelling, stochastic optimisation of maintenance intervals, and field validation at two partner plants—a mineral water bottling facility and a dairy pasteurisation plant—both located in Vojvodina. projects.title: Kompetencijska dinamika u postmerger integraciji malih i srednjih prerađivačkih preduzeća u Vojvodini
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj empirijsko i simulaciono istraživanje dinamike kompetencija zaposlenih tokom i nakon integracije malih i srednjih prerađivačkih preduzeća u Vojvodini. projects.title: Simulation-Based Decision Support for Workforce Integration in Central European Manufacturing SMEs

projects.title: Resource Efficiency and Symbiosis in Industrial Parks of the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RESINPARK assessed the technical and economic potential for inter-firm resource exchange in seven manufacturing parks across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. projects.title: Feasibility Assessment Methods for Industrial Symbiosis Under Regulatory Transition in Serbia

projects.summary: The project developed and piloted a lightweight ergonomic screening and prioritisation framework tailored to the resource constraints of small and medium food-processing enterprises in Vojvodina. Activities included field assessments at eight participating plants using REBA and OWAS protocols combined with Serbian-language discomfort surveys, development of a decision-support spreadsheet tool, and delivery of training workshops for plant supervisors.
