projects.title: Quality Cost Standardisation and Data Integration for Electronics Contract Manufacturers in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This project addressed the absence of standardised quality cost measurement practices among small and medium-sized electronics contract manufacturers operating across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The Serbian consortium lead was the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad; the Hungarian partner was a technical university department in Subotica's extended catchment. Activities included a comparative baseline survey (68 companies), development of a shared CoQ data collection template compatible with common ERP systems used by regional SMEs, two pilot implementations in partner companies, and a train-the-trainer programme delivered to 14 quality engineers. The project produced a freely available CoQ measurement guide translated into Serbian and Hungarian, and a lightweight Excel-based CoQ dashboard validated against pilot company data.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Széchenyi István University, Department of Industrial Engineering, Győr (associated partner)
Regional Chamber of Commerce Vojvodina
Technomont Elektronika d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Optimisation of Quality-Related Expenditures in High-Mix Low-Volume Electronics Assembly
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops and empirically validates mathematical models for jointly optimising prevention, appraisal, and failure expenditures in HMLV electronics assembly, where batch-size variability and frequent product changeovers make standard CoQ optimisation models inapplicable. Research tasks include longitudinal data collection at three partner companies (covering defect events, inspection times, rework records, and overhead allocations), development of batch-adaptive inspection intensity policies, severity-weighted failure cost models, and a Bayesian framework for parameter estimation under sparse data conditions. Model recommendations are being tested prospectively at one partner company from month 18 onward. The project supports two PhD students and produces open datasets for the research community.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elsist Elektronika d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner)
Precizija Montaža d.o.o., Zrenjanin (industry partner)

projects.title: Ramp-Up Parameter Estimation Tools for Contract Manufacturers in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RAMPEST aims to develop a lightweight software toolkit that allows production planners at small and medium contract manufacturers in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region to fit and update learning curve parameters during new product introductions without requiring statistical expertise. The project combines empirical data collection from partner factories, development of simplified estimation procedures, and a pilot deployment phase at two manufacturing sites. Tomić is responsible for the empirical data collection workpackage and for designing the parameter estimation procedures underlying the toolkit. He also contributes to the validation study comparing toolkit outputs against manual estimation by experienced production engineers. The project involves four partner organisations across the two countries.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Pannonian Manufacturing Research Centre, Subotica
Department of Industrial Engineering, Óbuda University, Budapest
RegioMet d.o.o., Senta

projects.title: Masonry Building Stock Seismic Risk in Vojvodina: From Exposure Modelling to Urban Loss Scenarios
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce the first systematic, building-level seismic risk model for the Vojvodina region, covering approximately 47,000 residential and mixed-use structures. Work packages addressed (1) construction of a cadastre-based exposure model with image-derived typology classification, (2) derivation of refined analytical fragility functions for dominant unreinforced masonry typologies, and (3) assembly of urban-scale probabilistic loss scenarios for the ten largest municipalities. The project operated in close collaboration with the Institute of Architecture and Urban Planning of Vojvodina and the Seismological Survey of Serbia. Outputs included an open-access building inventory dataset, a set of peer-reviewed fragility functions, and two technical reports submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning and Housing.
partners: Institute of Architecture and Urban Planning of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Seismological Survey of Serbia, Belgrade
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Seismic Risk Assessment of Municipalities along the Serbia–Hungary Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project involving partners from southern Hungary and northern Serbia, aimed at producing harmonised seismic risk assessments for nine municipalities on either side of the border. Jelena Đukić led the work package on vulnerability and fragility modelling, coordinating the collection of consistent building survey data across national cadastral systems and overseeing the derivation of typology-specific fragility functions applicable to both the Serbian and Hungarian portions of the study area. The project also delivered a joint GIS-based risk atlas and a training workshop for municipal civil protection officers. A shared digital exposure model was deposited in a public repository maintained by the lead partner.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
Municipality of Subotica, Serbia
Municipality of Baja, Hungary

projects.title: Characterisation and Modelling of Soft Clay Foundations for Infrastructure in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to build a regional database of soft clay properties across the Pannonian Basin lowlands of Serbia, including index properties, consolidation parameters, and creep indices from incremental load oedometer tests. Undisturbed samples are collected from infrastructure project boreholes through cooperation agreements with road and railway authorities. Numerical models calibrated against field monitoring data from selected embankment sections are used to test the predictive accuracy of four constitutive models: Terzaghi, Biot, Soft Soil, and Soft Soil Creep. Jasna Sredojević contributes to laboratory testing, data curation, and finite element modelling tasks. The project is coordinated by the University of Novi Sad and involves a partner group from the University of Subotica.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Subotica
Public Enterprise Roads of Serbia

projects.title: Fatigue Life Assessment of Aging Steel Road Bridges Using Site-Specific Traffic Data and Probabilistic Fracture Mechanics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je usmeren na razvoj metodologije za procenu zamornog veka postojećih čeličnih drumskih mostova u Srbiji integracijom dugotrajnih WIM merenja sa probabilističkim modelima rasta prsline. Obuhvata terensku instrumentaciju četiri mosta na mreži državnih i regionalnih puteva, kalibraciju parametara modela na uzorcima izrezanim sa mostovskih nosača posle demontaže i razvoj softverskog alata za podršku odlučivanju pri planiranju održavanja. Projektom su predviđeni razvoj smernica prilagođenih srpskim uslovima saobraćajnog toka i integracija sa bazom podataka Puteva Srbije o stanju objekata.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade
Public Enterprise Roads of Serbia

projects.title: Probabilistic Flood Hazard Assessment for Transboundary Lowland Rivers in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed harmonised probabilistic flood inundation maps for three transboundary river reaches shared by Hungary and Serbia: the Tisa, the Kereš, and the Zlatica Canal. The Serbian team led by Pekez was responsible for hydrological-hydraulic model setup and uncertainty quantification, while the Hungarian partner produced the remote sensing data layers. A common geodetic reference framework and shared data exchange protocol were established between the two national flood authorities. Final outputs included 10-, 100-, and 500-year probabilistic inundation maps in a format compatible with the EU Floods Directive reporting obligations, and a joint training workshop for practitioners from both countries.
partners: Water Directorate of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Research Institute for Water and Environment, Pécs, Hungary
General Directorate of Water Management, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Compound Pluvial-Fluvial Flood Frequency in Serbian Urban Floodplains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the joint statistical behaviour of river discharge and local rainfall extremes at six peri-urban sites in Serbia where fluvial and pluvial flooding mechanisms interact. It combined long-term hydrometeorological records, copula-based bivariate frequency analysis, and 2-D coupled hydrodynamic-stormwater modelling to produce compound flood hazard maps and to quantify the degree by which single-driver approaches underestimate flood extent and depth. A secondary objective was to derive design guidelines for urban drainage systems in floodplain-adjacent settings that account for compound event probabilities. The project trained two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher and produced seven peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia, Belgrade
Institute for Urban Planning and Design of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Politecnico di Milano, Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Italy

projects.title: Durable Alkali-Activated Binders from Pannonian Industrial By-Products for Infrastructure Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the formulation and long-term durability of alkali-activated mortars and concretes produced exclusively from fly ash and slag available in Vojvodina and adjacent areas of Hungary and Romania. Work packages addressed precursor characterisation and seasonal variability, optimisation of activator chemistry, mechanical performance under accelerated curing, and durability under combined sulphate and freeze-thaw exposure. A database of over 200 mix designs with associated performance data was compiled and made publicly accessible. The project involved a PhD student and two master's students from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and a short-term exchange with the Budapest University of Technology and Economics.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade

projects.title: Circular Construction Material Flows in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project addressing the identification, quantification and valorisation of secondary raw materials (fly ash, slag, recycled concrete aggregate) generated in the border counties of Serbia and Hungary. Tamara Maksimović led the work package on binder-grade assessment of fly ash and slag stockpiles, contributing chemical and physical characterisation data for approximately 60 material batches. Pilot demonstration mixes were prepared and tested at both the Novi Sad and Budapest partner laboratories. Project outputs included a shared material registry and guidelines for procurement of alkali-activation precursors for small construction companies in the region.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Subotica Development Agency
Csongrád County Development Council, Szeged

projects.title: Low-Cost Sensor Networks for Condition Assessment of Ageing Reinforced Concrete Bridges in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project deployed and evaluated low-cost wireless accelerometer networks on eight reinforced concrete road bridges in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina with deck ages ranging from 28 to 54 years. Key objectives were to establish temperature-compensated modal baselines, develop and validate automated anomaly detection algorithms, and produce a practical deployment guideline for road administrations. Field campaigns totalled over 22 000 sensor-days of continuous data. The project also conducted a laboratory phase involving four large-scale beam specimens subjected to progressive damage, used for validating feature extraction methods developed from the field data. A draft technical guideline for low-budget bridge monitoring was submitted to the Serbian Roads directorate.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Sarajevo
Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade
Roads of Serbia Public Enterprise (observer)

projects.title: Cross-Border Infrastructure Monitoring Demonstrator for Road Bridges
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMON establishes two long-term monitoring demonstrator sites on cross-border road infrastructure—one bridge on the Serbian side and one on the Hungarian side of the Danube catchment—to pilot harmonised monitoring protocols and joint data interpretation procedures. Predrag Cvetković leads the work package responsible for sensor network design, installation, and data quality assurance on the Serbian demonstrator site. The project includes capacity-building activities for road maintenance staff from both countries and will produce a bilingual technical manual on SHM implementation. Data from the two sites are shared via a jointly operated cloud repository.
partners: Széchenyi István University, Győr
Provincial Roads Directorate of Vojvodina
Budapest Infrastructure Research Centre (fictional)

projects.title: Freeze-Thaw Adjusted Performance Prediction for Flexible Pavements in Pannonian Climate Zones
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a climate-adjusted deterioration modelling framework for flexible pavements in the Pannonian region, combining FWD-based structural assessment with 30-year regional climate data and projected EURO-CORDEX temperature and precipitation scenarios. Activities included FWD monitoring campaigns on 22 instrumented sections across Vojvodina, laboratory freeze-thaw cycling of asphalt and granular base specimens, and integration of results into a publicly available deterioration prediction tool. The tool enables road managers to estimate residual pavement life and optimal maintenance intervention timing accounting for projected changes in freeze-thaw frequency. Partners contributed climate data processing capacity and independent validation datasets from Romania and Slovakia.
partners: Institute of Transportation CIP, Belgrade
Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava, Slovakia

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer for Cost-Effective Road Maintenance Planning in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed shared challenges in rural road maintenance along the Hungary–Serbia border, focusing on sections subject to similar continental freeze-thaw cycles and heavy agricultural traffic. Filip Ilić led the work package on structural condition assessment, coordinating FWD surveys and back-calculation analysis on 60 km of regional roads on both sides of the border. Results were used to develop harmonised maintenance priority rankings and to draft a joint technical guidance document for seasonal load restrictions. The project also supported training workshops for road engineers from both countries in FWD data interpretation and mechanistic-empirical overlay design.
partners: County Directorate for Roads of Bács-Kiskun, Hungary
JP Putevi Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

projects.title: Ventilation Strategies for Energy-Efficient and Comfort-Compatible Retrofitting of Heritage Educational Buildings in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HERITVENT addresses the specific challenge of improving indoor air quality and thermal comfort in protected school buildings on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border without compromising their architectural and cultural heritage values. The project combines field monitoring campaigns, computational modelling, and stakeholder engagement with school administrators and conservation authorities. The University of Novi Sad team is responsible for CFD and building energy simulations of Serbian case-study buildings and for developing a decision-support tool that helps building managers select ventilation measures compatible with local conservation guidelines. Milena Kecman contributes to simulation tasks and field measurement activities and participates in dissemination workshops directed at practitioners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Building Services and Process Engineering, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Provincial Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments of Vojvodina (fictional stand-in)
Bács-Kiskun County Government, Hungary (fictional stand-in)

projects.title: Sediment Continuity and Morphodynamic Restoration in Regulated Rivers of the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to quantify sediment deficits in regulated river reaches shared between Hungary and Serbia, with a focus on the Tisa, Drava, and their gravel-bed tributaries. Field campaigns collected bathymetric surveys, bedload trap data, and surface grain-size distributions at 34 cross-sections. A shared morphodynamic model framework was developed and applied to assess restoration scenarios including gravel injection and partial reactivation of secondary channels. Practical outputs included a joint monitoring protocol for cross-border reaches, a database of sediment transport measurements accessible to both national water management authorities, and design guidelines for gravel augmentation programmes adapted to Pannonian hydrological conditions.
partners: University of Pécs, Department of Geography
Pécs Regional Water Directorate
Public Water Management Company Vode Vojvodine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Gravel Budget Assessment and Augmentation Design for Serbian Hydropower Tailwaters
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project addressed the lack of quantitative sediment budget data for Serbian hydropower tailwaters, which are required under updated Serbian Water Law provisions. Work packages covered (i) field measurement campaigns on four tailwater reaches, (ii) development and calibration of two-dimensional morphodynamic models for each reach, (iii) Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis of bedload transport predictions under varying operational scenarios, and (iv) preparation of augmentation feasibility reports co-developed with the dam operators. The project trained two PhD students and produced an open-access numerical model archive. Results fed directly into the ongoing revision of environmental flow guidelines by the Republic of Serbia Water Directorate.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade
Jaroslav Černi Water Institute, Belgrade
JP Elektroprivreda Srbije – Hydropower Division (observer)

projects.title: Reliability-Based Design Framework for Cut Slopes in Loess and Marl Formations of the Fruška Gora Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SLOREL developed and validated a fully coupled transient seepage and finite element limit analysis reliability framework specifically calibrated for loess–marl stratigraphy in the Fruška Gora piedmont. The project compiled a regional geotechnical database from 22 instrumented sites, derived rainfall input statistics from 60-year meteorological records, and produced design charts and a software tool allowing practitioners to compute slope failure probabilities for user-specified geometries and storm scenarios. A geodetic monitoring campaign using UAV photogrammetry and TLS monitored seasonal deformations at three active slope sites. Results were disseminated through four journal papers and two national road authority workshops. The framework is being transferred to the Provincial Secretariat for Roads for use in hazard zoning.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Rainfall-Induced Slope Hazards Along the Drava–Danube Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project mapped rainfall-induced landslide hazards in the Drava–Danube corridor shared between southern Hungary and northern Serbia, covering approximately 1,400 km² of susceptible terrain. The Serbian team led by Zorić was responsible for geotechnical characterisation and slope stability modelling. Activities included harmonisation of geotechnical databases on both sides of the border, joint field campaigns, and co-development of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) landslide inventory database. The project produced a joint hazard map at 1:25,000 scale and a cross-border protocol for data exchange between national geological surveys. Zorić led the work package on slope stability assessment methods and contributed to the final hazard zonation report.
partners: Eötvös Loránd University, Budapest, Hungary
Geological Survey of Hungary
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province

projects.title: Uspostavljanje nacionalnog programa za ekološke deklaracije prefabrikovanih betonskih proizvoda u Srbiji
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj izradu metodološkog okvira i prvih pilot EPD dokumenata za prefabrikovane armirano-betonske produkte u Srbiji, usklađenih sa EN 15804+A2 i ISO 14025. U toku projekta prikupljeni su primarni podaci od šest srpskih proizvođača, uspostavljena je saradnja sa akreditovanim verifikatorom u Sloveniji i izrađen je predlog tehničkog pravilnika za srpski EPD program. Rezultati su prezentovani Ministarstvu građevinarstva i Privrednoj komori Srbije. Projekat je finansiran od strane Fonda za nauku Republike Srbije u okviru programa PROMIS.
partners: Institut za ispitivanje materijala Srbije (IMS), Beograd
Privredna komora Srbije – Udruženje industrije građevinskih materijala
Faculty of Civil and Geodetic Engineering, University of Ljubljana

projects.title: Cross-border harmonisation of construction and demolition waste management and circular use in the Hungary–Serbia border region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addresses the divergence between Hungarian and Serbian regulatory frameworks for construction and demolition waste (CDW). Ranković leads Work Package 3, which covers LCA-based comparison of CDW treatment pathways on both sides of the border and proposes a joint technical protocol for recycled concrete aggregate acceptance in public infrastructure contracts. Partners from Pécs and Subotica are involved in pilot field campaigns. The expected output includes a bilingual technical guideline for CDW sorting and an LCA calculator tool for regional contractors, planned for publication in 2025.
partners: Department of Civil Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary
Grad Subotica – Sekretarijat za urbanizam i zaštitu životne sredine
Regionalna razvojna agencija Bačka, Novi Sad

projects.title: Integrated Levelling and Hydrostatic Monitoring Methodologies for Hydraulic Infrastructure in the Sava–Danube Corridor
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed methodological gaps in combining periodic spirit levelling and continuous hydrostatic levelling for monitoring hydraulic structures such as dams, locks, and weirs. The work included development of a unified variance component estimation framework for mixed observation types, a sensor drift correction procedure for long-term HLS installations, and a field validation campaign at three hydraulic structures in Serbia. Project outputs include a publicly available adjustment software module, technical guidelines distributed to water management authorities in Serbia, and three journal publications. The team comprised researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences Novi Sad and the Jaroslav Černi Water Institute in Belgrade. Total budget was approximately 4.2 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Jaroslav Černi Water Institute, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Exchange of Geodetic Dam Monitoring Practices and Data Standards
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between the Faculty of Technical Sciences Novi Sad and the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca aimed at harmonising geodetic monitoring methodologies and reporting standards for dams on shared river basins. Gajić led the work package on levelling network design and adjustment, contributing to a joint technical handbook and co-supervising exchange visits of graduate students. The project produced a common template for deformation monitoring reports acceptable to both Serbian and Romanian dam safety authorities, and facilitated installation of a pilot HLS system at a Romanian partner dam site. Total Interreg IPA contribution was approximately 320,000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Technical University of Cluj-Napoca
Romanian Waters National Administration – Banat Branch

projects.title: Resident-Led Energy and Spatial Retrofit of Panel Blocks in Vojvodina: Frameworks, Tools, and Pilot Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project developed and tested a structured framework for integrating resident participation into the planning of energy and spatial retrofit works in prefabricated panel-block settlements across four Vojvodinian cities. Activities included a baseline physical and socio-demographic survey of approximately 130 blocks, design and facilitation of deliberative workshop pilots in Subotica and Sombor, development of a simplified cost-benefit tool for resident-facing use, and preparation of a draft procedural guide for municipal housing departments. The project involved the City of Novi Sad Urban Planning Institute and the Association of Housing Managers of Vojvodina as non-academic partners. Three journal papers and one practitioners' handbook resulted from the work.
partners: City of Novi Sad Urban Planning Institute
Association of Housing Managers of Vojvodina
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Approaches to Regenerating Post-Socialist Residential Districts in the Hungarian–Serbian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSREGEN is a cross-border cooperation project examining shared challenges in regenerating large-panel residential districts on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. The University of Novi Sad leads the work package on physical condition assessment and retrofit scenario modelling, covering settlements in Subotica, Kanjiža, and the Hungarian partner city of Baja. The project compares regulatory frameworks, funding mechanisms, and community engagement practices in the two national contexts, aiming to produce transferable guidance and a joint training programme for municipal planners and housing administrators. Knežević coordinates the Serbian-side field survey teams and contributes to joint scenario workshops held alternately in Subotica and Baja.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology
Municipality of Baja
City of Subotica Urban Planning Directorate
Regional Development Agency of Bács-Kiskun County

projects.title: Pannonian Unreinforced Masonry Vulnerability Zoning: Building a Regional Risk Dataset for Low-Seismicity Urban Cores
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled a building-by-building exposure and vulnerability database for pre-1964 unreinforced masonry residential and public buildings in twelve municipalities of Vojvodina and the northern Serbian urban belt. Field campaigns in 2020 and 2021 covered 1,247 buildings using a standardised rapid visual screening protocol. In-situ flat-jack and shove tests were conducted at 54 pilot buildings to provide material property anchors for analytical fragility modelling. A probabilistic seismic hazard grid was procured from the Seismological Survey of Serbia and integrated into the QGIS database. The project delivered a freely downloadable QGIS plugin, a reference fragility function set for four typology classes, and a training manual for municipal building inspectors.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade
Seismological Survey of Serbia
Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments of Vojvodina

projects.title: Cross-Border Seismic Risk Assessment and Preparedness for Historic Masonry Towns in the Hungarian–Serbian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CrossRisk addresses the lack of harmonised seismic risk assessment methodology across the Hungarian–Serbian border zone, where shared Pannonian construction traditions have produced nearly identical building stocks subject to different national regulatory frameworks. The University of Novi Sad component leads Work Package 3, covering field data collection and fragility model development for the Serbian side. Three municipalities participated in pilot rapid visual screening exercises. Joint training workshops for local civil protection officers were held in Subotica and Szeged. The project also developed a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) digital inspection application piloted by municipal building departments. Outputs include a harmonised typology catalogue and joint scenario loss estimates for cross-border urban agglomerations.
partners: Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs
Municipality of Subotica
County Disaster Management Directorate of Csongrád-Csanád
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Daylight Performance Assessment Framework for Deep-Plan Office Buildings in the Pannonian Climate
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat razvija metodološki okvir za procenu i optimizaciju pokazatelja dnevnog osvetljenja u dubokim kancelarijskim zgradama tipičnim za urbanistički kontekst severnih srpskih gradova. Istraživanje obuhvata: formiranje proširene lokalne baze klimatskih podataka za Vojvodinu i Panonsku niziju pogodne za CBDM, razvoj i validaciju parametarskih simulacionih modela, kao i terensku kampanju merenja u šest kancelarijskih zgrada u Novom Sadu i Subotici. Trifunović je odgovoran za razvoj simulacionih modela i analizu rezultata godišnjeg modeliranja. Krajnji rezultat je skup projektantskih preporuka za dinamičke fasadne sisteme prilagođenih regionalnoj klimi.
partners: Departman za arhitekturu i urbanizam, FTN, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Institut za fiziku zgrade i klimatologiju, Univerzitet u Beogradu — Arhitektonski fakultet
Lumos Lighting Research d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptive Façade Systems for Energy and Comfort Co-Optimisation in Central European Office Buildings
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Zajednički srpsko-mađarski projekat koji istražuje mogućnosti adaptivnih fasadnih sistema u kancelarijskim zgradama u prekograničnom regionu između Srbije i Mađarske. Projektni konzorcijum sprovodi komparativnu analizu klimatskih podataka, simulacija dnevnog osvetljenja i energetskih performansi za lokacije Novi Sad, Subotica i Pečuj (Pécs). Trifunović doprinosi modelu vrednovanja dnevnog osvetljenja i učestvuje u terenskim merenjima u Novom Sadu. Planirani rezultati uključuju zajednički priručnik za projektante i demonstracionu instalaciju adaptivne fasade na pilot-objektu Naučno-tehnološkog parka Novi Sad.
partners: FTN, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

NTP Novi Sad — Naučno-tehnološki park

projects.title: Walkability and Commercial Gentrification in Medium-Sized Post-Socialist Cities: Spatial Syntax as a Monitoring and Planning Tool
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WALKGEN examined the relationship between spatial configuration, pedestrian movement, and commercial gentrification dynamics in six Serbian cities with populations between 50,000 and 300,000. The project combined longitudinal axial map analysis, repeated pedestrian counts, business register tracking, and structured interviews with small retail operators. The main output was a syntax-based monitoring protocol that municipalities can apply with standard GIS tools and periodic field surveys, without the need for expensive sensor infrastructure. The project also produced an open dataset of axial maps and pedestrian counts for all six cities, deposited in the University of Novi Sad institutional repository. Three doctoral students were trained within the project.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering and Architecture, University of Niš
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Institute of Urban Planning of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Pedestrian Public Space Quality: Comparative Spatial Analysis of City Centres in the Hungarian–Serbian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PEDCROSS compared public space quality and pedestrian movement patterns in five city pairs straddling the Hungarian–Serbian border, including Subotica–Baja and Sombor–Mohács. Zlata Perišić led the work package on spatial configuration analysis, responsible for producing comparable axial maps and visibility graph analyses for all ten cities and for coordinating joint pedestrian count campaigns. The project also included urban design recommendations for selected public spaces identified as underperforming relative to their integration values. Outputs included a bilingual planning guidance document distributed to all ten municipal planning departments involved.

projects.title: Hygrothermal Performance of Internal Thermal Renovation in Historic Masonry Buildings of the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of region-specific technical guidance for internal insulation of historic brick buildings in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border area. Activities included: a joint survey of approximately 80 heritage buildings in Subotica, Szeged, and Novi Sad; material property measurements on sampled brickwork and mortar; installation of long-term sensor networks in three buildings; and development of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) practitioner guide. The guide, freely downloadable, covers material selection, condensation risk assessment procedures adapted to Pannonian climate conditions, and site inspection checklists. The project trained 46 architects and conservation officers through two-day workshops held in Novi Sad and Subotica.

projects.title: Probabilistic Moisture Risk Models for Internally Insulated Solid Masonry Walls under Changing Climate Scenarios
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops probabilistic condensation and mould growth risk models for internally insulated solid brick walls, incorporating uncertainty in material properties (quantified from a new database of 48 buildings sampled across Serbia and Vojvodina) and projected climate change scenarios for the 2041–2070 period. Phase one built the material database and fitted statistical distributions to key hygrothermal properties. Phase two runs Monte Carlo HAM simulation ensembles under current and future climate forcings. Phase three will produce revised risk thresholds and a freely accessible web tool for practitioners. A PhD candidate and two master's students are funded under the project. Results are intended to inform revision of the Serbian technical regulation on energy efficiency of buildings.

projects.title: Acoustic Quality of Learning Spaces in Serbian Primary Schools: Assessment, Standards, and Retrofit Guidelines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project systematically assessed acoustic conditions in primary school buildings across four Serbian regions and produced practical retrofit guidelines oriented toward municipal-budget constraints. Activities included field measurement campaigns in 40 schools, laboratory testing of locally available absorption materials, listening experiments with non-native language learners, and a review of national building regulations against current EU practice. A freely accessible database of acoustic measurement results from participating schools was created and made available to municipal building services. The project produced draft amendments to Serbian technical regulation TP-21 on school acoustics and an online calculation tool for preliminary classroom acoustic design without specialist software.

projects.title: Cross-Border Learning Environments: Indoor Comfort Standards for Primary Schools in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSLEARN compared indoor environmental quality (acoustics, thermal comfort, and daylighting) in primary school buildings across the Hungary–Serbia border region to identify divergences in national standards and share good-practice examples. Vera Erić led the acoustics work package, responsible for measurement protocols, field campaigns in 18 schools (9 per country), and a comparative analysis of Hungarian and Serbian regulatory requirements for classroom acoustics. The project produced a joint recommendations document addressed to municipal governments on both sides of the border and organised two teacher-training workshops on recognising and reporting acoustic problems. A set of low-cost acoustic retrofit solutions validated in both countries was compiled into a bilingual technical guide.

projects.title: Brownfield Remediation and Blue-Green Infrastructure along the Danube: Cross-Border Planning Tools for Vojvodina and Baranya
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBROWN aimed to develop shared methodological tools for identifying, assessing, and planning the remediation of riverfront brownfield sites on both the Serbian and Hungarian sides of the Danube border reach. The project produced a joint brownfield register covering 52 sites, a harmonised contamination assessment protocol tested at six pilot locations, and a cross-border planning handbook circulated to municipal administrations in both countries. Three planning workshops were held alternately in Novi Sad and Pécs, attended by a total of 94 planners, municipal officials, and environmental inspectors. The project also funded two student mobility exchanges between the partner faculties.

projects.title: Flood-Risk Zoning Calibration for Riparian Brownfield Redevelopment in Vojvodina Municipalities
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: RIVZONE investigated the technical basis for flood-risk zone boundaries as applied to riverfront brownfield parcels in Vojvodina, focusing on the mismatch between hydraulic modelling assumptions embedded in existing zoning maps and the altered embankment morphology resulting from decades of industrial land reclamation. The project collected new topographic survey data at eight sites, ran updated 1D and 2D HEC-RAS flood models, and compared outputs against the regulatory flood envelopes used in current spatial plans. Recommendations for zone boundary revision were submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Spatial Planning and three municipal planning offices. A technical report and two journal papers were produced.

Vode Vojvodine (Vojvodina Waters Public Enterprise), Novi Sad

projects.title: Tactile and Wayfinding Infrastructure Standards for Vojvodina Municipalities: Audit, Gap Analysis, and Capacity Building

projects.summary: The project audited tactile and wayfinding infrastructure in six Vojvodina municipalities (Kikinda, Vršac, Sombor, Sremska Mitrovica, Zrenjanin, Subotica), producing baseline compliance maps and gap analyses for each. A training programme for municipal technical staff was developed and delivered to 34 participants from five municipalities over two one-day workshops. Project outputs include a publicly available GIS dataset of audited routes, a condensed guidance document for municipal procurement of TGSI materials, and a report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat outlining priority remediation sites. The project involved the Union of the Blind of Vojvodina as a stakeholder partner throughout.

projects.title: Cross-Border Accessible Walking Environments: Shared Standards and Good Practice Transfer Between Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral project comparing accessible pedestrian infrastructure standards and field conditions in border-region municipalities in Vojvodina (Serbia) and Csongrád-Csanád County (Hungary). Bajić leads the work package on regulatory comparison and field audit methodology, coordinating audit campaigns in four Serbian municipalities. The project produces joint guidance material available in Serbian and Hungarian, a shared GIS platform for accessibility data, and a joint training curriculum for municipal planners. A particular focus is on pedestrian routes connecting Serbian and Hungarian towns near shared border crossings, where continuity of accessible provision breaks down at the boundary. projects.title: Vacancy Mapping and Monitoring Protocols for Depopulating Municipalities in the Serbia-Hungary Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed standardised protocols for mapping and monitoring residential and commercial vacancy in twelve small municipalities, six on each side of the Serbian-Hungarian border. Activities included production of baseline vacancy inventories using GIS and satellite imagery, design of a shared cross-border geodatabase, and training workshops for 34 municipal planning staff members. A policy brief series was produced in Serbian, Hungarian, and English, targeting provincial and county planning authorities. The project also piloted annual OSM-supported vacancy change detection in four of the twelve municipalities as a cost-reduction measure. Total budget was approximately 480,000 EUR, with the University of Novi Sad team managing the Serbian component.

projects.title: Evidence-Based Planning Instruments for Shrinking Small Towns in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates whether existing Serbian planning legislation can accommodate shrinkage-responsive instruments without legislative reform, and if so, what institutional and procedural conditions enable their adoption at the municipal level. The research combines longitudinal GIS vacancy analysis in a panel of twenty Vojvodinian towns, content analysis of all local spatial plans revised since 2015, and action-research collaboration with three willing municipalities to pilot adaptive zoning instruments. A graduate student and two undergraduate research assistants are employed on the project. Output targets include four journal articles, one policy report for the Ministry of Construction, Transport, and Infrastructure, and one open-access dataset of processed vacancy geometries for the panel towns.
partners: Institute of Architecture and Urban Planning of Serbia, Belgrade
Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning and Environmental Protection, Vojvodina

projects.title: Carbon Accounting Methods for Residential Construction in Serbia: Towards Regulation-Ready Benchmarks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a methodological framework and a set of calibrated embodied carbon benchmarks for residential buildings in Serbia, suitable for use in future national building regulations. Work packages cover primary data collection from Serbian material producers (cement, brick, structural timber), development of adapted lifecycle inventory datasets, LCA of twenty reference building archetypes spanning single-family and multi-family typologies, and a comparative analysis against benchmark databases in Hungary, Romania, and Croatia. A publicly accessible database of Serbian building material carbon factors is being compiled as the main deliverable. The project involves partners from three Serbian universities and one Hungarian institution, and is supported by an advisory board of practitioners from the Serbian Chamber of Engineers.

projects.title: Timber Construction Supply Chains and Carbon Flows in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TIMBERPATH examined the structural timber supply chain connecting sawmills and prefabrication enterprises in Vojvodina, southern Hungary, and Slavonia, mapping material flows, transport patterns, and carbon emissions from harvesting through to building installation. Ninkov led the work package on embodied carbon quantification, overseeing LCA modelling of three representative prefabricated panel products using primary factory data collected on both sides of the Serbian–Hungarian border. The project produced a cross-border carbon flow map and identified bottlenecks in quality certification that currently prevent Serbian-sawn timber from qualifying for structural use under CE marking requirements. Outputs included a joint technical report and two conference papers.

projects.title: Mapiranje i valorizacija potencijala otpadne toplote u prerađivačkoj industriji Autonomne Pokrajine Vojvodine
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj sistematsko mapiranje toplotnih tokova u industrijskim postrojenjima na teritoriji AP Vojvodine kroz standardizovane energetske audite i primenu pinch metodologije. Tim je sproveo audite u 23 postrojenja iz pet sektora i razvio GIS-zasnovanu bazu podataka otpadnih toplotnih tokova sa temperaturnom i kapacitivnom karakterizacijom. Na osnovu rezultata pripremljene su tehno-ekonomske procene za deset lokacija sa najvećim potencijalom, uključujući preporuke za industrijsku simbiozu između susednih postrojenja. Rezultati projekta objavljeni su u formi sektorskog izveštaja dostupnog pokrajinskim vlastima i u recenziranim časopisima.

projects.summary: The project develops and validates practical thermoeconomic retrofit methodologies scaled for small and medium-sized enterprises in the cross-border region. The Novi Sad team leads the work package on exergy-based retrofit screening and multi-objective decision support, contributing computational tools and two industrial case studies from Serbian manufacturing sites. Hungarian partners contribute case studies from the agri-food sector and manage dissemination activities. A joint summer school for process engineers from both countries is organised annually. projects.title: Geothermal Heat Pump Potential and Long-Term Ground Thermal Balance in Vojvodina Shallow Aquifer Conditions
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project characterised the shallow geothermal resource in Vojvodina by compiling and analysing thermal response test data from 22 borehole sites, correlating ground thermal properties with available geological and hydrogeological data, and developing a simplified regional map of ground thermal conductivity. Field measurements were taken at two instrumented pilot boreholes on the faculty campus. The main deliverable was a publicly available dataset and a technical guideline document for borehole field pre-design in the province, circulated to the Vojvodina Energy Agency and relevant municipal building departments. The project also supported the doctoral research of two PhD candidates in the group.

projects.title: Hybrid Ground-Source Heat Pump Systems for Reducing Ground Thermal Imbalance in Serbian Continental Climate
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This IDEAS project investigates hybrid ground-source heat pump configurations that couple a borehole field with an auxiliary heat rejecter or solar thermal recharger to counteract long-term ground temperature drift in heating-dominated Serbian buildings. The research involves development and experimental validation of a coupled transient model, a parametric study across climate zones and building types, and a field pilot at a monitored multi-family building in Novi Sad. A secondary objective is to develop a simplified design tool for engineering practitioners. The project team includes collaborators from the University of Pécs and the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca. Two master's theses and one doctoral dissertation are planned within the project duration.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Clean Combustion Strategies for Small Biomass Appliances in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed air-quality concerns related to residential biomass combustion in the Pannonian lowland, where wood and agricultural residue pellets are burned in small boilers below 50 kW. The Serbian partner (Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad) led the work package on emission characterisation and combustion optimisation, conducting experiments on staged-air strategies and fuel quality effects. The Hungarian partner contributed dispersion modelling to link burner-level emission factors to ambient PM2.5 concentrations in three pilot municipalities. Results were compiled into a technical guidance document for boiler installers and local authorities, and a workshop for energy advisors was held in Subotica. Zahorec led the experimental campaign and co-authored the final technical report.
partners: Department of Energy and Process Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Environmental Engineering, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Regional Energy Agency Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Predictive Emission Modelling for Pellet Combustion Appliances under Variable Operating Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PELMOD develops a validated, load-aware semi-empirical model for simultaneous prediction of CO, NOx, and PM emissions from small pellet burners operating under realistic residential load profiles. The project combines controlled laboratory experiments at the Thermal Processes Laboratory with a field dataset from ten instrumented households in the Novi Sad metropolitan area. Model inputs include pellet proximate and ultimate analysis, burner geometry, and a time series of thermal load fraction; outputs are time-resolved emission factors suitable for hourly air-quality inventory calculations. A particular focus is the treatment of transient load-change events, which are underrepresented in current emission factors. The project employs one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher. Deliverables include an open-access dataset and a freely distributable Python-based calculation tool.
partners: Department of Energy and Process Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Atmospheric Physics and Environmental Research, Novi Sad

projects.title: Coupled Fouling and Flow Maldistribution in Compact Heat Exchangers for Agri-Food Industrial Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the interaction between refrigerant maldistribution and fouling deposition in brazed plate heat exchangers used in agri-food processing in Vojvodina. It combines long-term field monitoring at two partner food-processing facilities with numerical model development aimed at providing decision-support tools for maintenance scheduling. The research team develops and validates a coupled simulation framework that predicts performance degradation as a function of water chemistry, operating load, and channel flow distribution. A secondary objective is to produce open-access benchmark datasets for two-phase flow and fouling in BPHEs. The project supports two doctoral students and includes short-term staff exchanges with Politecnico di Milano and Chalmers University of Technology.

The project produces a freely accessible online screening tool and retrofit guidelines disseminated through the chambers of commerce of Novi Sad and Subotica. Field trials are conducted at four SME sites, two per country, providing validation data for the screening models.

projects.title: Greenhouse Gas Tracking and Uncertainty Quantification in Mixed-Source District Heating Networks of the Western Balkans

projects.summary: DHTRACK aims to develop a standardised methodology for greenhouse gas inventory and uncertainty reporting in district heating networks across the Western Balkans, where data quality and metering infrastructure vary widely between operators. projects.title: Dynamic Control Strategies for Waste Heat Recovery ORC Units in the Food and Ceramics Industries
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: THERMOSAVE addressed the gap between ORC simulation tools and practical deployable control systems for two Serbian industrial sectors: food processing and ceramics manufacturing. projects.title: Optimisation of Spray Drying Parameters for Thermosensitive Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Using Coupled CFD and Experimental Validation

projects.title: Thermal Performance of Passive Envelope Systems in Continental Climate Residential Buildings

projects.title: Upgrade of the Envelope Thermal Performance Laboratory with Environmental Cycling and Radiometric Measurement Capabilities

projects.summary: ENVELAB was an infrastructure grant that funded the procurement and installation of a programmable environmental chamber with a working volume of 0.8 m³ and temperature cycling capability from −10 °C to 60 °C, along with a calibrated focal-plane-array thermal camera and a set of thin-film heat flux transducers with response times below 3 seconds. Gordana Perišić led the project and managed procurement, calibration verification against national standards maintained at the Directorate for Measures and Precious Metals in Belgrade, and the development of standardised test protocols. projects.title: Energy Performance of Natural-Refrigerant Retail Cooling Systems in the Vojvodina–Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project benchmarks the energy and environmental performance of supermarket refrigeration systems operating in Vojvodina's continental climate, focusing on CO₂ transcritical and propane-based configurations as replacements for HFC systems. The Faculty of Technical Sciences team is responsible for constructing and maintaining the simulation models, running annual energy calculations with regional meteorological datasets, and preparing a design guidance document for local installers. Ildikó Tóth contributes to the gas-cooler sub-model development and experimental validation on the laboratory test rig. Partners perform site audits at three operating supermarkets in the region to gather real consumption data for model calibration. projects.title: Curtailed Renewable Electricity for Alkaline Electrolyser Systems: Degradation-Aware Sizing and Dispatch

projects.summary: The project addresses the gap between idealised electrolyser sizing methods, which assume constant or slowly varying inputs, and the reality of wind and solar curtailment signals characterised by frequent ramps and idle periods. A secondary objective is to quantify the economic value of balancing market participation for electrolyser operators in Serbia. projects.title: Orientation-Constrained Topology Optimisation for Load-Bearing Metallic Lattice Structures in Laser Powder-Bed Fusion
