projects.title: Additive Manufacturing for Reliable Structural Components in the Automotive and Rail Sectors
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ADMARIS is a cross-border applied research project aiming to establish shared expertise and infrastructure for qualification of LPBF structural components destined for automotive and rail applications in the Hungary–Serbia region. Jovana Đukić leads Work Package 3, which covers build-orientation strategies and anisotropy assessment for aluminium and stainless steel bracket geometries supplied by project industry observers. The work package produces a common testing protocol covering micro-CT inspection, tensile, and fatigue characterisation aligned with EN 13001 and automotive OEM supplier requirements. Knowledge transfer activities include two joint workshops and a short-course module on AM design for engineers hosted alternately in Novi Sad and Subotica.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Bay Zoltán Nonprofit Ltd. for Applied Research, Miskolc
Vojvodina Institute for Mechanical Engineering, Novi Sad
Ferroten d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Parametric Models and Experimental Methods for Gear-Rattle Prediction in Serbian Automotive Supply Chain
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to build experimentally validated rattle prediction tools directly applicable to gearbox development in the domestic automotive supply chain. Activities included construction of the adjustable-backlash test rig, development of the multi-pair DCT model, and a tolerance-sensitivity study. The project produced four journal papers and one conference paper, trained two doctoral students, and delivered a report to the industry partner outlining recommended backlash tolerance limits for a family of five-speed manual gearboxes then in production. The test rig and parametric simulation environment developed under the project remain in use for ongoing doctoral research.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Vojvođanska Transmisija d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Wearable Sensor Systems for Real-Time Musculoskeletal Load Monitoring in Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a lightweight monitoring system based on two wrist-worn IMUs and a waist-mounted accelerometer for estimating cumulative shoulder and lumbar loading during shift work at small and medium manufacturing enterprises. Regression models trained on matched motion-capture and IMU data from 22 assembly workers were deployed on an embedded microcontroller. Field validation was conducted at three facilities in Vojvodina over a combined 480 worker-hours of monitoring. The project produced validated estimation algorithms, a user interface for production engineers, and a protocol for periodic risk screening that does not require ergonomics expertise on-site. Results contributed to two journal publications and two conference presentations.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Occupational Medicine Vojvodina
Mekoplast d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Ergonomics Training and Assessment Network for Manufacturing Workers
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSERG established a joint Serbian–Hungarian network for ergonomic risk assessment and training in manufacturing. The Novi Sad team led the work package on biomechanical assessment methodology, developing a shared protocol for motion-capture-based workstation evaluation applicable to facilities on both sides of the border. A joint training curriculum for occupational safety officers was designed and piloted with 64 participants across four facilities. The project produced a bilingual assessment manual and an open-access library of 120 reference inverse-dynamics posture cases covering common manufacturing task types in the food, electronics, and metalworking sectors.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina
Győr Regional Occupational Safety Centre, Hungary

projects.title: Fatigue and Relaxation Limits of Monolithic Compliant Micro-Mechanisms for Precision Instrumentation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the long-term mechanical reliability of monolithic compliant mechanisms used in precision instrumentation, with emphasis on fatigue life under variable-amplitude loading and creep relaxation at ambient temperature. Experimental campaigns on standardised flexure-hinge specimens made from three aluminium alloys and two spring steels are combined with analytical model development and FEA-based parametric studies. The project aims to produce validated life-estimation procedures applicable at the early design stage, without requiring component-level fatigue tests. A secondary objective is to quantify the effect of wire-EDM surface conditions on fatigue scatter. The work involves collaboration with the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering in Belgrade and the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering in Ljubljana.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade, Serbia
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Ljubljana, Slovenia

projects.title: Compliant Mechanism Platforms for Robotic Instrumentation in Small-Scale Engineering
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COMPRISE brought together three partners from Serbia and Hungary to develop and test compliant mechanism platforms intended for integration into small-scale robotic end-effectors used in precision assembly tasks. Jelena Filipović contributed to work package 2, which covered kinematic and kinetostatic modelling of candidate mechanism topologies and the definition of performance metrics (workspace, stiffness ratio, cross-axis coupling) for comparative evaluation. The project produced two demonstrator prototypes tested at both partner laboratory sites, along with a public technical report. The collaboration established joint supervision arrangements for two M.Sc. students, one from each country.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary
InstroPrecíz Kft., Győr, Hungary

projects.title: Probabilistic Assessment and Reliability-Based Optimisation of Mechanical Joints in Lightweight Structures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PROBOJNT addresses the gap between deterministic design standards and the actual statistical variability of geometric, material, and loading parameters in mechanical joints used in lightweight transport structures. The project develops a unified computational framework that integrates finite element analysis, probabilistic methods (Monte Carlo, importance sampling, FORM), and meta-modelling to produce joint designs satisfying prescribed failure probability targets. Emilija Kostić is responsible for the fatigue sub-model development and the importance-sampling implementation for bolted and riveted connections. Experimental validation is conducted at the FTS fatigue laboratory using servo-hydraulic test rigs. Results are intended to inform revisions of the internal design guidelines used by the industrial partner.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Aerokomponent d.o.o., Novi Sad (industrial partner)

projects.title: Sensor-Assisted Failure Evaluation in Composite Sandwich Structures under Repeated Impact and Fatigue
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the absence of validated real-time monitoring protocols for composite sandwich panels used in transport and civil infrastructure. The central objective is to develop and validate an integrated AE-based monitoring framework that can identify delamination onset, track crack-growth rate, and estimate residual strength without interrupting structural service. Work packages cover laboratory impact and fatigue testing of four panel types, development of temperature-corrected wavelet classifiers, embedded implementation on low-power hardware, and a round-robin validation exercise with two partner institutions. The project produces open test datasets for three panel configurations and a calibration procedure document intended for adoption by industrial end-users in the transport sector.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Niš
Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade

projects.title: Interregional Knowledge Transfer on Composite Sandwich Manufacturing and Inspection for SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COMPSAND brought together two universities and a regional development agency to help small and medium enterprises in the cross-border region adopt composite sandwich materials for structural applications. The University of Novi Sad team led the inspection and quality-control work package, contributing AE monitoring protocols for panel acceptance testing, short training courses for SME technicians, and a practical guide to non-destructive evaluation of bonded joints. Seventeen SME staff from four companies received hands-on training at the Faculty of Technical Sciences laboratory. The project delivered a bilingual (Hungarian–Serbian) technical manual and a shared instrument loan arrangement allowing SMEs to borrow AE equipment for short-term production audits.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Széchenyi István University, Győr, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermoelastic Degradation and Life Prediction of Bolted Flanged Connections in District Heating Networks
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigated creep-fatigue degradation of bolted flange assemblies in the district heating networks of Vojvodina, where operating temperatures between 130 °C and 180 °C are lower than those in power plant but thermal cycling frequency is much higher due to daily demand variation. The research combined laboratory relaxation tests on EN 1.4301 stainless-steel spiral-wound gaskets, thermocouple-instrumented in-service measurements at two pump stations in Novi Sad, and finite element life prediction calculations. Deliverables included a maintenance prioritisation procedure for flange inspection intervals and a dataset of material parameters for district-heating-grade gasket materials. The project supported one doctoral student.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
JKP Toplane Novi Sad (district heating utility, Novi Sad)

projects.title: High-Temperature Sealing Integrity for Steam Plant: Experimental Benchmarks and Computational Methods
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS)
projects.summary: HITEMSEAL addresses the absence of a standardised experimental benchmark dataset for validating finite element models of high-temperature bolted flange sealing. The project establishes three benchmark configurations spanning DN150 class 600 to DN300 class 1500 flanges with spiral-wound and ring-type joints, instrumented with load cells, thermocouples, and DIC targets. Tests are carried out at temperatures of 350 °C, 450 °C, and 530 °C at relevant pressures. Benchmark datasets are published openly. Parallel work develops a computational framework for probabilistic leak-tightness assessment accounting for material scatter and installation variability. The project involves a research stay exchange with partners in Dresden and Timișoara. Two doctoral students are co-supervised within the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Technische Universität Dresden, Institute for Materials Testing
Politehnica University of Timișoara, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering

projects.title: Prediction and Reduction of Cavitation-Induced Degradation in Hydraulic Proportional Valves for Agricultural Machinery
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the mechanism linking metering-edge geometry, fluid properties, and cavitation erosion progression in proportional valves used in tractor hydraulics. A combined experimental and numerical campaign was carried out: 48 accelerated wear tests on valve spools with four edge geometries, parallel transient CFD simulations with the full cavitation model, and post-test surface profilometry. The project produced a geometry-resolved erosion database, an open-access validation dataset, and design guidelines recommending minimum edge radii and chamfer combinations. A prototype metering-edge profile was machined and bench-tested, showing a 35% reduction in measured surface roughness increase rate after 300 hours compared with the standard geometry.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Innovation Center, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade
AgroHidra d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Geometry Optimisation of Hydraulic Control Valve Metering Edges for Reduced Flow-Induced Noise in Mobile Machinery
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigated the connection between metering-edge geometry and audible noise emitted by hydraulic directional control valves in mobile machinery cabins. Noise measurements on a test rig were complemented by OpenFOAM-based CFD simulations feeding Lighthill source terms into a finite-element acoustic model. Six metering-edge profiles were evaluated at three flow rates. Results were used to derive a simplified design rule relating chamfer width to dominant tonal noise frequency. The project funded one doctoral student and produced three peer-reviewed publications and one conference presentation.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Metaloprojekt Hidraulika d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Friction-Induced Instabilities in Steel-Wire-Rope Lifting Systems: From Contact Mechanics to Safety-Relevant Dynamic Loads
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined how stick-slip and related friction-induced instabilities in wire-rope hoisting systems generate dynamic overloads that exceed nominal design loads by measurable margins. Work packages covered: construction of an upgraded capstan rig with dynamic load cells and high-speed imaging; development of corrected analytical models incorporating bending stiffness and lay-angle effects; field measurements on industrial cranes; and integration of the models into a simplified design calculation tool for practising engineers. The project produced seven journal and conference publications, one internally distributed design guide, and a dataset of friction and vibration measurements deposited in the institutional repository. Three master's students and one doctoral candidate were involved in the experimental programme.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac

projects.title: Durability Assessment of Wire Rope Assemblies in Overhead Crane Applications through Combined Tribological and Dynamic Testing
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: An industry-funded contract research project carried out for Agratek Dizalice d.o.o., a manufacturer of overhead travelling cranes based in Sremska Mitrovica. The project scope included accelerated wear testing of three rope constructions proposed for a new product line, characterisation of friction evolution over the rope service life, development of inspection interval recommendations, and validation of the FBG tension monitoring system on a prototype crane built by the company. Deliverables comprised a confidential technical report, an inspection protocol, and a calibration procedure for the monitoring system. The project led directly to the field trial described in the 2025 Measurement Science and Technology publication.
partners: Agratek Dizalice d.o.o., Sremska Mitrovica

projects.title: Repairability Metrics and Material Flow Data Infrastructure for Consumer Electromechanical Products in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project built a primary dataset of disassembly measurements, material compositions, and end-of-life processing data for 18 categories of small and medium electromechanical consumer products sold or collected in Serbia. A relational database was developed to store teardown records, joint type catalogues, and material fraction data. Using this dataset, the project validated and refined a repairability index methodology that is applicable at both the design stage and the point of regulatory compliance checking. The project involved three Serbian partner institutions and one Hungarian university, and produced an open-access data repository deposited with the Faculty of Technical Sciences library. Four journal papers and two conference contributions resulted from the project period.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Institute for Standardisation of Serbia
University of Pannonia, Veszprém, Hungary

projects.title: Circular Economy Pathways for Electromechanical Waste in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CIRCBALK addresses the gap between European circular economy legislation and actual end-of-life infrastructure capacity in the Western Balkans by mapping existing repair, remanufacturing, and recycling networks for electromechanical products across Serbian and Hungarian partner regions. Fejsa leads the work package on technical benchmarking, which produces standardised assessments of recovery yield, disassembly labour cost, and embodied carbon savings for representative product streams. The project will develop a publicly accessible decision tool for small enterprises operating in the repair and remanufacturing sector, and will pilot a skills certification programme for repair technicians in three cross-border municipalities. Industrial partners include two Hungarian remanufacturing SMEs and one Serbian WEEE processing company.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Bay Zoltán Applied Research Institute, Budapest
Pannonia Regional Development Agency
ObroTech d.o.o., Novi Sad
RegénTech Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Microscopic Modelling of Mixed Traffic Flows at Urban Signalised Intersections During the Automated Vehicle Transition
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MIXFLOW examines how increasing proportions of automated vehicles alter microscopic traffic dynamics at signalised intersections in medium-sized Serbian cities. The project collects drone-based trajectory data at six intersections in Novi Sad and Subotica, uses the data to calibrate stochastic car-following and cellular automaton models across AV penetration scenarios, and derives intersection capacity and delay functions applicable to the 10–70% penetration range. A secondary objective is to develop signal timing guidelines that remain robust across a range of AV penetration rates rather than being optimised for a single assumed rate. Results are being disseminated to the City of Novi Sad Traffic Management Centre for consideration in the next signal timing revision cycle.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Transport and Communications Research, Novi Sad
City of Novi Sad Traffic Management Centre

projects.title: Cross-Border Urban Mobility Data Sharing and Simulation Benchmarking
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: URBANLINK establishes a shared repository of anonymised traffic count, travel time, and turning-movement data from partner cities on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border, to be used for benchmarking microscopic and mesoscopic simulation tools. The Novi Sad team leads the work package responsible for simulation methodology standardisation, including a common protocol for model calibration and validation and a set of agreed performance indicators. The project also funds three joint workshops for practitioners from municipal transport departments. Uzelac's role involves coordinating the simulation benchmarking exercise across four city cases and contributing to the joint data governance framework.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Transport Engineering, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
City of Subotica Transport Directorate
Municipality of Szeged Infrastructure Office

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Surrogate Safety at Pedestrian Crossings Along Pan-European Corridors in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project collects video-based surrogate safety data at mid-block and signalised crossings along shared road corridors linking Novi Sad with Szeged and Subotica. The Serbian team at the Faculty of Technical Sciences is responsible for data collection at eight crossing sites in Vojvodina, automated trajectory extraction, and computation of PET and time-to-collision metrics. The Hungarian partner handles crash record linkage and GIS integration. A joint protocol for cross-border conflict observation is being developed and will be released as an open document. The project also includes training workshops for municipal traffic engineers from both countries on interpreting surrogate safety outputs for infrastructure decisions.
partners: Department of Transport Engineering, Széchenyi István University, Győr
City of Novi Sad Traffic Management Directorate
Municipality of Subotica, Department of Urban Planning and Traffic

projects.title: Cyclist Safety at Vulnerable Road Locations: Evidence-Based Measures for Medium-Sized Cities in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VELOMED systematically maps cyclist-vehicle conflict conditions at mid-block crossings, roundabout entries, and shared pedestrian-cyclist paths in four Serbian cities: Novi Sad, Kragujevac, Niš, and Subotica. Janković leads the work package on surrogate safety measurement methodology, overseeing the deployment of automated video analysis at 24 sites across the four cities over a 12-month monitoring period. The project will produce a conflict database and an open dataset for further research, as well as a practitioner guideline document addressed to Serbian municipal engineers. A final deliverable will propose revisions to the national technical regulations on cycling infrastructure at urban crossings.
partners: Faculty of Transport and Traffic Engineering, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Kragujevac
Institute for Roads and Traffic, Niš
City of Subotica Urban Planning Institute

projects.title: Deterioration Prediction and Maintenance Optimisation for Rural Road Networks under Freeze-Thaw Conditions in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addresses the lack of climate-adapted deterioration models for rural road networks on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border, where freeze-thaw cycles cause disproportionate damage relative to traffic loads. The work plan includes coordinated field monitoring on approximately 120 km of selected roads in Vojvodina and Csongrád–Csanád County, laboratory characterisation of subgrade soils, and the joint calibration of Markov chain deterioration models using merged datasets from both countries. Nada Lazić contributes to field measurement campaigns, data processing, and the development of the Serbian segment of the Markov chain model. An open-access deterioration parameter database and a maintenance decision support tool are planned as primary outputs.
partners: Department of Traffic Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Transport Infrastructure, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs
Public Enterprise Roads of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Csongrád–Csanád County Road Directorate, Szeged

projects.title: Transit Accessibility and Social Equity in Vojvodina Urban Areas
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project systematically mapped public transport accessibility across all seven urban municipalities in Vojvodina with populations above 30,000, producing a georeferenced accessibility atlas updated annually. The core outputs included a standardised GTFS collection protocol adopted by three municipal operators, a publicly accessible web map of accessibility indicators, and a policy brief submitted to the Vojvodina Secretariat for Urban Planning. The team consisted of four researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences and two from the Faculty of Sciences. The project also ran two workshops for municipal transport planners on interpreting and applying accessibility metrics in local planning decisions. Total budget was approximately 4.2 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Urban Planning Institute of Vojvodina

projects.title: Polycentric Accessibility Modelling for Medium-Sized Cities in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: POLYACCESS brings together three universities and two municipal planning agencies from Hungary and Serbia to develop shared methods for accessibility modelling suited to polycentric mid-size cities. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on data infrastructure, responsible for harmonising GTFS feeds across six partner cities and building a joint routing environment. The project will produce a transferable open-source toolkit and a cross-border accessibility report comparing outcomes in Hungarian and Serbian cities under different land use scenarios. A pilot application is planned for the Novi Sad–Sremska Mitrovica corridor. Total project budget is approximately €480,000, with the Novi Sad team receiving roughly €95,000.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology
Széchenyi István University, Department of Transport
Urban Institute of Novi Sad
Pécs City Development Agency

projects.title: Multimodal Driver Workload Monitoring for Safer Road Use in Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DRIVLOAD developed and validated a low-cost instrumentation package for measuring driver cognitive workload in naturalistic conditions, intended for deployment in transport safety studies conducted jointly by Serbian and Hungarian research teams. The project equipped two instrumented vehicles—one at the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and one at Széchenyi István University in Győr—with synchronised OBD-II, GPS, wearable ECG, and EDA loggers. A harmonised data collection protocol and shared data repository were established. The project produced a set of open-source signal processing scripts for HRV and EDA feature extraction and delivered training workshops for graduate students at both institutions. Final deliverables included a joint dataset from 90 cross-border route drives and two peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Széchenyi István University, Győr, Hungary
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Road Safety Risk Profiling Using Naturalistic Driving and Physiological Data in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project built a spatially referenced risk atlas for Vojvodina's primary road network by combining naturalistic driving metrics from an extended participant panel with crash records from the Ministry of Interior. Sixty-one volunteer drivers collected trip data over six months; hard-braking events, sharp cornering events, and physiological workload surges were geo-tagged and aggregated to 500 m road segments. Segments with elevated workload-event density were cross-referenced with five-year crash data. The study identified 23 segments where physiological workload clustering preceded crash records by one to three years, suggesting potential early-warning utility. Results were communicated to the Vojvodina Roads Directorate in a technical report. The project also funded one doctoral student position and supported field data collection infrastructure.
partners: Vojvodina Roads Directorate
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Corridor Model Validation Standards for the Pannonian Transport Area
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project sought to establish a shared protocol for calibrating and validating macroscopic traffic simulation models on cross-border corridors linking Serbia and Hungary. Partners pooled loop detector archives and coordinated a series of joint floating car data collection campaigns on three shared corridors. The project produced a bilingual technical guideline document adopted informally by both national road administrations, a harmonised GEH-based acceptance threshold table adjusted for regional traffic conditions, and a set of freely distributable MATLAB calibration scripts. The project also funded two joint workshops attended by staff from road administrations, planning institutes, and universities in both countries.
partners: Vojvodina Roads Directorate, Novi Sad
Hungarian National Road Administration, Regional Directorate Pécs
Department of Transport Engineering, Budapest University of Technology
Institute for Traffic Engineering and Transport, Subotica

projects.title: Shipper Behaviour and Policy Instruments for Modal Shift to Inland Waterways on the Danube Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUSHIFT brought together researchers from Serbia and Hungary to produce harmonised evidence on shipper mode choice behaviour along the shared Danube reach. The project conducted coordinated stated preference surveys in both countries using identical experimental designs, enabling cross-border comparison of willingness-to-pay values for transit time, reliability, and port access. Mihajlo Jakovljević led the work package responsible for survey design, data collection, and discrete choice model estimation. The project also developed a prototype policy assessment tool that translates estimated mode choice parameters into modal share forecasts under hypothetical tariff and infrastructure scenarios. Outputs included a joint database covering over 400 surveyed shippers and a set of policy briefs addressed to national and provincial transport authorities.
partners: Department of Transport Technology and Economics, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Institute for Transport and Communications Research, Belgrade
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce – Transport and Logistics Sector

projects.title: Freight Demand Quantification on the Serbian Danube: Establishing a Longitudinal Survey Infrastructure
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project established a recurring annual shipper survey covering freight flows, mode use, and logistics decision criteria for firms located in the Vojvodina region with access to Danube ports. The primary aim was to create a longitudinal dataset that could track changes in shipper behaviour over time, filling a gap left by irregular and incompatible earlier surveys. The project produced two waves of data collection (2019 and 2021), a codebook and methodology report, and an open-access microdata archive hosted at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. A secondary output was a comparative analysis of response rates and non-response bias across recruitment channels, informing future survey operations. The dataset has since been used in two journal publications.
partners: Department of Traffic Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Urban Traffic Emission and Noise Exposure Assessment for Mid-Sized Cities in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: URBANEX aimed to produce harmonised noise and air quality exposure datasets for five mid-sized Western Balkan cities with populations between 100 000 and 350 000, where regulatory monitoring is sparse. The project developed a transferable modelling workflow combining locally calibrated emission factors, AERMOD and SoundPlan, and census population grids to generate population-weighted exposure indicators comparable across cities. Field validation campaigns using portable LCS sensor arrays were conducted in Novi Sad, Niš, Banja Luka, and Bitola. The project produced open datasets, a technical guidance document for municipal authorities, and a web map interface for public communication of results. Three journal papers and one policy brief were delivered.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Niš
Faculty of Transport and Traffic Engineering, University of Banja Luka
Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Air Quality and Traffic Noise Management Along the Novi Sad–Szeged Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSAIR addressed traffic-related air and noise pollution along the main road corridor connecting Novi Sad and Szeged, which crosses the Serbia–Hungary border and passes through several smaller settlements with no existing monitoring infrastructure. Pavlović led the work package responsible for harmonising emission factor databases and running coordinated AERMOD and noise dispersion simulations for a 140 km corridor segment. The project deployed a shared network of eight roadside low-cost sensor stations and produced a joint cross-border environmental noise map submitted to both national authorities. It also piloted a joint public reporting protocol aligned with both Serbian and EU legislation.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Transport Engineering, Széchenyi István University, Győr
Environmental Inspectorate of Vojvodina (fictional)
Municipality of Subotica

projects.title: Poboljšanje bezbednosti ruralnih puteva primenom profila operativnih brzina i kriterijuma konzistentnosti geometrijskog projektovanja
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat ima za cilj razvoj lokalno kalibrisanih modela operativnih brzina za dvotračne ruralne puteve u Srbiji i njihovu integraciju u proceduru provjere konzistentnosti geometrijskog projektovanja prilagođenu srpskim standardima projektovanja puteva. U okviru projekta sprovodi se naturalističko terensko istraživanje na 120 horizontalnih krivina raspoređenih u tri geomorfološke zone (ravnica, brežuljkast teren, planinski teren). Posebna pažnja posvećena je razvoju korekcija za teška vozila, mokri kolovoz i kratke međukrivinske tangente. Rezultati će biti implementirani u smernicu za reviziju bezbednosti puteva namenjenu JP 'Putevi Srbije'.
partners: Departman za saobraćajno inženjerstvo, FTN, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Saobraćajni fakultet, Univerzitet u Beogradu
JP Putevi Vojvodine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Capacity and Level-of-Service Assessment for Bus Rapid Transit Corridors in Mid-Size Serbian Cities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce an evidence-based methodology for estimating BRT stop capacity and corridor level of service under conditions typical of Serbian mid-size cities, where full BRT segregation is rarely feasible and mixed traffic interaction is the norm. Field campaigns were conducted in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin, collecting over 18,000 stop events and 60,000 km of GNSS trajectories. The project produced a calibrated microsimulation toolset, a practitioner measurement protocol (later adopted as a reference by the Serbian Chamber of Engineers), and the data underlying several published papers. Two master's students and one doctoral student were trained within the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Subotica
JP Novi Sad Public Transport

projects.title: Transfer Mediation and Intermodal Node Performance in Cross-Border Urban Corridors
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANSMED addresses the operational performance of intermodal transfer nodes on cross-border public transport corridors between Hungary and Serbia, with focus on the Subotica–Szeged axis. Paunović leads the work package on stop-level and terminal-level capacity modelling, contributing BRT stop assessment methods to the broader intermodal framework. Other work packages address passenger information systems, fare integration, and demand modelling. The project involves four partners across two countries and is co-financed under the Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia programme. Results are intended to inform binational transport planning documents currently under preparation by national transport authorities.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Tranquil Area Identification and Protection in Vojvodina Urban Agglomerations
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project mapped candidate tranquil areas in four Vojvodina cities according to the criteria of the EU Environmental Noise Directive and the CALM project methodology. Acoustic measurements at 89 sites were combined with perceptual surveys of 310 park and green space users to assess whether low noise levels were perceived as restorative. GIS-based multicriteria analysis integrated Lden, distance from busy roads, vegetation density, and user density to rank candidate tranquil areas. The project produced designation recommendations submitted to municipal planning departments and developed a simplified screening tool for use by planners without acoustic expertise. Results informed the noise action plans of two municipalities in their 2022 END reporting cycle.
partners: City of Novi Sad Department for Environmental Protection
Urban Planning Institute of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Public Enterprise for Urban and Housing Affairs, Sremska Mitrovica

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Noise Mapping Practices in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project addresses inconsistencies in noise mapping methodologies applied on the Serbian and Hungarian sides of shared transport corridors, particularly the M5/E75 road axis and the Subotica–Kecskemét rail line. The University of Novi Sad leads the work package responsible for source emission measurement and model validation. Joint measurement campaigns were conducted at four border-region sites, producing a harmonised local emission dataset compatible with both NMPB-Routes-2008 and CNOSSOS-EU. Training workshops were delivered to municipal technical staff in Subotica and Szeged. The project will deliver a joint noise exposure atlas and a bilateral technical protocol for coordinating future END reporting cycles across the border.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Environmental Sciences, University of Szeged, Hungary

Municipality of Kecskemét, Hungary

projects.title: Quantifying Dermal Uptake of Volatile Organic Compounds in Surface-Coating Occupations: Development of Validated Measurement and Modelling Tools
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the absence of validated methods for measuring and modelling dermal uptake of VOCs in coating workplaces. Three tasks were completed: (1) in vitro permeation experiments for eight priority solvents using excised human skin and silicone membrane surrogates; (2) a field study with concurrent personal inhalation and skin wipe sampling in five coating facilities; and (3) integration of dermal submodels into existing PBTK frameworks for three target compounds, with validation against urinary biomarker data. Final outputs include a published permeability coefficient database, validated PBTK models, and a field-ready sampling and calculation protocol suitable for occupational hygienists in small enterprises.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Transition to Waterborne Formulations in the Printing and Coating Sector: Exposure Characterisation and Risk Assessment Support
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project monitored VOC exposure profiles in printing and coating workshops undergoing voluntary transition from solvent-based to waterborne ink and coating systems. Personal air and skin wipe samples were collected before and after reformulation in 14 participating facilities. The study documented reductions in aromatic hydrocarbon exposures alongside emerging exposures to glycol ether solvents such as 1-methoxy-2-propanol and its acetate. A sector-specific exposure model was constructed and disseminated to participating companies together with practical guidance on monitoring priorities for waterborne systems. Results fed directly into graduate course materials on occupational risk assessment.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Electrochemical Treatment Technologies for Heavy Metal and Cyanide Removal in Small Electroplating Enterprises of the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the practical gap between available electrochemical treatment knowledge and its uptake by electroplating SMEs in the Vojvodina–Southern Transdanubia cross-border region. Activities included a survey of 14 electroplating SMEs to characterise rinsewater compositions and existing treatment practices, laboratory development and pilot testing of optimised EC and EO protocols, preparation of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) technical guideline for SME operators, and two training workshops hosted in Novi Sad and Pécs. The University of Novi Sad led the project with responsibility for laboratory work and pilot testing; the Hungarian partner contributed techno-economic analysis and dissemination. A mobile treatment demonstration unit was exhibited at three industrial fairs.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
Regional Chamber of Commerce Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Association of Metal Finishing Enterprises Southern Transdanubia, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Resource Recovery from Electroplating Sludge: Closing the Loop for Critical Metals in Serbian SMEs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RECYPLATE investigates the feasibility of recovering copper, nickel, and chromium from EC sludge generated at Serbian electroplating SMEs, treating the sludge as a secondary raw material rather than a hazardous waste for landfill. The project combines selective hydrometallurgical leaching, solvent extraction, and electrodeposition steps tested at bench and pilot scale. A techno-economic and life cycle assessment module evaluates which metal–recovery combinations are economically viable under current Serbian conditions. Partners include the Mining and Metallurgy Institute Bor for analytical support and a pilot smelting trial, and the Faculty of Sciences Novi Sad for LCA methodology. The project targets two peer-reviewed publications per year and one technology readiness level advancement for the integrated recovery process.
partners: Mining and Metallurgy Institute Bor, Serbia
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Continuous Ergonomic Monitoring and Early Intervention in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ERGOWATCH developed and field-tested a continuous ergonomic surveillance system combining wearable IMU sensors with a structured intervention protocol for use in manufacturing SMEs. The project established reference exposure distributions for four common assembly task families (screwdriving, overhead installation, repetitive palletising, and precision fitting) based on full-shift measurements in 14 participating companies across Vojvodina. A web-based reporting dashboard was developed that translates sensor-derived posture metrics into action-level recommendations accessible to non-specialist safety officers. The project produced an open-access database of anonymised exposure records and a validated Serbian-language ergonomic risk communication toolkit. Three companies piloted workstation changes based on ERGOWATCH outputs and reported measurable reductions in reported musculoskeletal complaints at six-month follow-up.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health Vojvodina
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Cross-Border Framework for Musculoskeletal Disorder Prevention in Automotive Supply Chain Assembly
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SAFE-LINE is a cross-border project between ergonomics research groups in Serbia and Hungary addressing the prevention of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in the automotive assembly supply chain, which is a major employer in both border regions. Olivera Nikolić leads the work package on exposure assessment methodology harmonisation, coordinating the application of a common IMU-based measurement protocol and shared risk-scoring conventions across partner sites in Subotica, Szeged, and Pécs. The project is developing a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) training curriculum for occupational safety representatives and contributing to a regional MSD incidence registry. An intervention pilot targeting neck and shoulder disorders in wire-harness assembly is under way at two partner facilities.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Ergonomics, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica
Occupational Health Research Institute Pécs

projects.title: Redox-Dependent Fate of Pharmaceutical Contaminants in Alluvial Aquifers Along the Danube
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RedoxPharm investigates how shifts between oxic, nitrate-reducing, and iron-reducing conditions in Danube alluvial sediments affect the transformation pathways and persistence of twelve pharmaceutical compounds and four EDCs commonly detected in river water. The project combines quarterly field sampling at three RBF sites in Vojvodina, controlled laboratory column experiments, and geochemical modelling to derive compound-specific attenuation coefficients as a function of redox state. Outputs will include a decision-support framework for water utilities assessing RBF vulnerability. Ivana Maksimović contributes to field sampling campaigns, analytical work, and the column experiment programme. The project runs from January 2023 to December 2026 and is coordinated by the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Waterworks and Sewerage Public Utility Company Novi Sad
Institute of Environmental Assessment and Water Research, Barcelona, Spain

projects.title: Deposition Fluxes of Persistent Organic Pollutants Across Land-Use Gradients in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established the first coordinated multi-site POP deposition network in the Serbian part of the Pannonian basin, operating 12 monitoring stations across agricultural, semi-urban, and peri-industrial land-use categories. Standardised wet-only and bulk deposition collectors and PUF passive air samplers were deployed with a common sample handling and QA/QC protocol. The project delivered annual deposition flux budgets for 16 PAHs, 12 PCB congeners, and 8 organochlorine pesticides at all sites. Back-trajectory analysis was used to attribute inter-site flux differences to source regions. Data are being submitted to the EMEP Heavy Metals and POPs database. The project supported two PhD candidates and produced six peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Atmospheric Transport and Deposition of Organic Contaminants in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANAIR-CB linked monitoring infrastructure on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border to investigate whether identified PAH and PCB deposition hotspots near Subotica and Baja share common source contributions from cross-border emission sectors. The project operated six paired stations (three per country) with identical wet-only collectors and active air samplers. Marija Stojanović led the work package on harmonised sampling protocols and analytical QA, and co-developed the shared LIMS-based data management system. Bilateral source apportionment using receptor modelling was carried out jointly with the Hungarian partner. The project produced a publicly available cross-border contamination atlas and trained four early-career researchers.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Department of Environmental Sciences, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Thermal Environment Assessment Methods for Worker Protection in High-Heat Industrial Processes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: THERMAPRO developed and validated a suite of tools for assessing thermal exposure in Serbian industries where high-heat processes dominate: foundries, ceramics, glass, and rubber vulcanisation. The project combined field measurement campaigns at six partner facilities with CFD modelling and physiological monitoring of approximately 80 workers across two summer seasons. Key deliverables included a validated zonal modelling software package, a task-specific metabolic rate database covering 24 furnace-related job activities, and a guidance document for industrial hygienists. The project engaged the Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina as a co-investigator and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. Results were incorporated into a draft annexe submitted for consideration by the Serbian national occupational safety standards body.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina
Faculty of Safety Engineering, University of Zagreb
Association of Occupational Safety Professionals of Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Heat Risk Management in Small and Medium Industrial Enterprises
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HEATWISE addresses the capacity gap in occupational heat risk management among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The Faculty of Technical Sciences leads the work package on technical assessment methods, providing simplified CFD-based screening protocols adaptable by plant safety officers without engineering expertise. The project partners include the University of Pécs Department of Environmental Health and the regional chamber of commerce from both countries, which recruits and coordinates participating SMEs. Outputs include a bilingual (Hungarian–Serbian) practical guidance manual, an online training module for safety officers, and a network of 15 pilot SMEs that will trial the screening protocol over two summer seasons. Vera Lalić's team contributes field validation data from four Serbian manufacturing sites.
partners: Department of Environmental Health, University of Pécs

projects.title: Isotope-Based Verification of In-Situ Remediation Efficiency in Chlorinated-Solvent-Contaminated Vadose Zones of the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj razvoj i validaciju protokola za primenu izotopske analize specifičnih jedinjenja (CSIA) u parnoj fazi nezasićene zone kao kvantitativnog alata za verifikaciju in situ remedijacije hlorovanih rastvarača. Istraživanje je obuhvatilo laboratorijske kolumne, mikrokosmos eksperimente i terensku studiju na dva lokaliteta u Vojvodini. Razvijeni su faktori izotopskog frakcionisanja za ključne ISCR reagense i definisani kriterijumi prihvatljive efikasnosti remedijacije prepoznatljivi u CSIA dijagramima. Projekat je rezultovao revidovanim smernicama za monitoring koje su dostavljene Agenciji za zaštitu životne sredine Srbije.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Remedeko d.o.o., Beograd

projects.title: Microbial Risk in Shallow Alluvial Water Supplies of the Pannonian Basin: Exposure Characterisation and Regulation-Ready QMRA Frameworks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled comprehensive occurrence datasets for Cryptosporidium, Campylobacter, and enteric viruses in shallow alluvial wells across 12 municipalities in Vojvodina and developed full probabilistic QMRA frameworks for each pathogen. Field sampling campaigns at 48 well sites over three years were combined with hydrogeological transport modelling to attribute contamination sources. A key deliverable was a simplified QMRA spreadsheet tool designed for use by public health inspectors and small public utility operators without specialist risk assessment training. The project produced recommendations for revision of the Serbian Rulebook on drinking water quality to incorporate risk-based parametric values for protozoa and thermotolerant Campylobacter.
partners: Vojvodina Institute for Water Management, Novi Sad
Public Health Institute of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Pathogen Transport from Agricultural Diffuse Sources to Alluvial Aquifers in the Danube–Tisa–Danube Canal Network
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral Hungarian–Serbian project investigating the pathways by which agricultural runoff and livestock effluent reach alluvial groundwater through the canal network connecting the Danube and Tisa rivers. Lazić led the work package responsible for microbial sampling, pathogen quantification, and risk characterisation on the Serbian side. Seventeen monitoring stations were instrumented with automated water level loggers, and approximately 640 samples were processed for faecal indicators and protozoan pathogens over 30 months. Results were integrated with Hungarian hydrological and land-use data to produce a joint contamination vulnerability map and a cross-border QMRA report submitted to both countries' environmental agencies.
partners: University of Szeged, Department of Hydrology
Water Directorate of South Transdanubia, Pécs

projects.title: Explosion Safety of Hybrid Dust–Gas Mixtures in Biomass Energy Facilities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of standardised characterisation procedures and design guidance for hybrid dust–gas explosions in biomass heating and pellet storage infrastructure. Experimental work used the group's 20-litre sphere and a purpose-built 1 m³ vented vessel to generate Kst and Pmax data for wood, miscanthus, and straw dusts across a range of sub-LEL methane and propane concentrations. CFD modelling complemented experiments to assess scaled-up vessel behaviour. Outputs included a proposed correction procedure for EN 14491 vent area calculations under hybrid conditions, training materials for facility safety officers, and a freely downloadable data repository of explosion parameters for eleven biomass dust types. Three partner SME facilities in Vojvodina served as case study sites.

Energija Panonija d.o.o., Sremska Mitrovica

projects.title: Cross-Border Safety Standards for Biomass Handling in Small Heating Enterprises
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BIOSAFELINK brought together three Serbian and two Hungarian partners to harmonise explosion protection practice in small biomass district heating enterprises operating on both sides of the border. Stojanović led the work package responsible for explosion parameter measurement and risk assessment methodology. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) practical guide to ATEX compliance for facilities below 1 MW thermal capacity, a joint training course delivered to 112 facility operators, and a cross-border database of equipment compliance status for 34 audited installations. Outputs were adopted by the Provincial Secretariat for Environmental Protection as reference documents for permit review.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Tactile Accessibility of Pharmaceutical Packaging in the Western Balkans: Measurement Infrastructure and Regulatory Harmonisation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established a certified measurement reference laboratory for EN ISO 17351 dot geometry assessment at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad, and carried out the first systematic conformity audit of pharmaceutical secondary packaging on the markets of Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. A total of 620 packs were measured; non-conformity prevalence data were shared with national medicines agencies. The project also developed a freely accessible web-based calculator tool for converting embossing press parameters into predicted dot geometry, validated against the FEM model published by the research group. Training workshops were delivered to eight packaging manufacturers and two regulatory inspectors.
partners: Agency for Medicinal Products and Medical Devices of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sarajevo
Faculty of Technology, University of Banja Luka

projects.title: Braille Print Integrity Across Pharmaceutical Cold-Chain Packaging: From Substrate Selection to End-User Verification
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BRAILLECHAIN addressed the gap between embossed Braille quality at point of manufacture and actual readability at point of patient use after cold-chain distribution. The project combined accelerated ageing experiments, real distribution chain monitoring (temperature loggers attached to shipments), and user testing with blind participants recruited in Novi Sad and Pécs. The Novi Sad team led the work package on substrate characterisation and measurement methodology, contributing profilometry data on 840 specimens. Results fed into a joint guidance document for pharmaceutical packaging converters operating across the Hungary–Serbia border region. A pilot training programme for quality-control staff at two participating manufacturers was completed in the final year.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary
Regional Blind Association of South Transdanubia, Pécs, Hungary
Pharmapack d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Substrate-Fuser Interaction Maps for Specialty Electrophotographic Printing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to construct validated process-window maps for electrophotographic fusing on a range of uncoated and textured specialty paper substrates. Work packages covered substrate characterisation (topography, thermal, and mechanical properties), systematic fusing trials across a temperature–pressure matrix, finite-element and probabilistic model development, and machine-learning integration of the resulting dataset. A shared database of substrate descriptors and corresponding fusing outcomes was produced and made available to project partners. The project involved three institutions and produced laboratory protocols now used in teaching at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Total value was approximately 6.8 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Pulp and Paper, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Printing and Packaging Technology
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between printing technology departments in Serbia and Hungary addressing joint curriculum development, equipment sharing, and short-run specialty printing research. Todorović led the work package on substrate testing and quality measurement harmonisation, establishing common test protocols across partner laboratories. The project produced three jointly authored technical reports and facilitated exchange visits for six PhD students. Equipment purchased under the project included a multi-angle scanning glossmeter and a dynamic vapour sorption instrument, both located at the Novi Sad facility and accessible to partner institutions. Total project budget was approximately €420,000.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology
Graphic Arts Chamber of Vojvodina

projects.title: Digital Typography Infrastructure for the Minority Languages of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project addresses the absence of professionally engineered OpenType fonts for the six officially recognised minority languages of Vojvodina: Hungarian, Slovak, Romanian, Rusyn, Bunjevac, and Romani. The work plan covers character set analysis, encoding decisions, parametric master design, OpenType feature engineering, and release under open licences. Goran Radović is responsible for the Rusyn and Bunjevac workstreams, building directly on his doctoral research. The project also includes a teacher-training module for secondary-school graphic design programmes in Vojvodina, providing educators with structured materials for teaching multilingual desktop publishing. Deliverables include six font families, a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat, and a public web repository.
partners: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat for Culture and Information, Vojvodina

projects.title: Perceptual Benchmarking of Halftone Screening Algorithms for Packaging and Label Print Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed standardised observer-based benchmarking protocols for evaluating halftone screening artefacts relevant to packaging and pharmaceutical label printing. Activities included construction of a stimulus library of 2,400 halftone patches spanning AM, FM, and hybrid screening variants across five substrate categories; recruitment and training of a standing observer panel of 60 participants stratified by age, visual acuity, and professional background; and derivation of viewing-distance and illuminant correction factors for use in industrial quality control. A freely available benchmark dataset and an accompanying scoring tool were produced. The project involved collaboration with a regional label printing company for validation of protocols under production conditions.

projects.title: Environmental Impact Reduction in Commercial Printing SMEs in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to reduce the environmental footprint of commercial printing SMEs in the Vojvodina–Southern Hungary cross-border region by producing sector-specific LCA tools, training materials, and a shared environmental reporting template. Kovačević led the work package on data collection and LCA modelling, coordinating data gathering from seven Serbian and four Hungarian printing companies. The project produced a freely available web-based carbon footprint calculator calibrated to regional energy mixes and local substrate supply chains. A final workshop delivered training to 34 SME representatives. The project also generated a jointly authored technical report submitted to both national environmental agencies.

projects.title: Sustainable Printing Chemistry: Toxicity and Recyclability Trade-offs in Ink and Substrate Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SUSPRINT investigates the interplay between chemical composition of printing inks and coatings, substrate recyclability, and toxicity-related environmental impacts. The project combines laboratory deinkability testing, chemical characterisation of ink systems by GC-MS, and LCA modelling to produce integrated environmental profiles for eight commercially relevant ink-substrate combinations used in Serbian and regional printing. A secondary objective is to develop a simplified screening tool for printing companies to rank ink and substrate combinations by combined toxicity and climate impact before procurement. The project involves collaboration with the Faculty of Forestry in Belgrade for paper testing and a label converter in Subotica as an industrial observer providing production data.
partners: Faculty of Forestry, University of Belgrade, Serbia
LabelPrint Subotica d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Machine-Readable Diffractive Security Features for Flexible Pharmaceutical and Food Packaging
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed fabrication and verification workflows for covert polarisation-contrast diffraction gratings embossed directly onto aluminium blister foil and BOPP food packaging film, eliminating the separate adhesive label step. Work packages covered master fabrication by laser interference lithography, electroformed nickel tool characterisation, roll-to-roll embossing parameter optimisation, and portable-reader algorithm development. A pre-production trial at a pharmaceutical packaging converter produced 200 000 labelled blister units; reader sensitivity and specificity exceeded 97 % in post-trial auditing. Outputs include a freely available spectral reference database of 1 600 genuine samples and two co-authored publications. The project trained two doctoral students and one master's student.

projects.title: Digital–Physical Authentication Bridges Using Spectral Fingerprinting of Embossed Holograms
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates the integration of spectral fingerprinting of embossed holographic labels with blockchain-based provenance records to create a tamper-evident digital–physical link for regional agri-food producers. The approach does not require serialised printing; the hologram's inherent micro-variation serves as the identifier. The project maps the fingerprint stability across temperature and humidity cycling representative of cold-chain logistics, assesses the minimum number of spectral features required for reliable re-identification, and develops an API specification for connecting mobile reader output to a distributed ledger entry. A pilot with two Vojvodina wine producers is planned for the second project year.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Regional Chamber of Commerce Novi Sad

projects.title: Legibility Standards for Age-Inclusive Hospital Signage in Cross-Border Healthcare Facilities
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of harmonised age-inclusive wayfinding standards in cross-border healthcare contexts between Serbia and Hungary. Activities included legibility testing of symbol–text combinations with older adult participants at partner hospitals on both sides of the border, development of a shared design specification document, and production of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) signage template package. The project also delivered training workshops for facilities managers at four hospitals. The University of Novi Sad team led the perceptual testing work package and coordinated production of the final guideline document. The project resulted in a tested and piloted sign system implemented in one hospital facility in each country.

County Hospital Bács-Kiskun, Kecskemét, Hungary

projects.title: Towards a National Guideline for Wayfinding Sign Systems in Serbian Public Healthcare Facilities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project compiles empirical legibility data across a range of target user groups, lighting conditions, and sign configurations encountered in Serbian public hospitals, with the goal of generating evidence-based minimum requirements for a national guideline. The research programme includes field audits of 20 hospital facilities, controlled laboratory experiments on type size, symbol design, colour contrast, and material reflectance, and an extended consultation process with the Serbian Chamber of Engineers and the Ministry of Health. A draft guideline document is under preparation for submission to the Institute for Standardisation of Serbia as a basis for a national pre-standard.

projects.title: Rheological Design Criteria for Screen-Printable Functional Inks on Rigid Substrates
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish a quantitative link between the full rheological profile of functional inks — spanning yield stress, thixotropic recovery, and viscoelastic moduli — and measurable print quality outcomes including deposit thickness, edge acuity, and pin-hole density on glass and FR4 substrates. A database of rheological and print-quality measurements was assembled for over 30 paste formulations covering silver, carbon-black, ruthenium oxide, and dielectric chemistries. Statistical modelling of this dataset produced ranked predictor sets that were validated in a blind test on ten pastes not used in model training. The project also developed standard operating procedures for rheological characterisation in printing laboratories, subsequently incorporated into the department's graduate-level printing technology course.

projects.title: Spectral Properties of Non-Self-Adjoint Operators Arising in Mathematical Physics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates spectral instability, pseudospectral phenomena, and resolvent estimates for classes of differential operators with complex-valued coefficients or dissipative boundary conditions. Tasks include deriving rigorous asymptotic formulae for eigenvalue distributions, computing pseudospectra numerically for benchmark families of operators, and comparing results with predictions from semiclassical analysis. Lukić contributes to the numerical computation workstream and to analytical estimates for fourth-order operators. The project involves monthly working seminars with the two partner institutions and exchange visits to Belgrade and Zagreb.

projects.title: Multiscale Methods for Structured Heterogeneous Materials: Rigorous Homogenisation and Computational Schemes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MicroHom develops mathematically rigorous homogenisation methods for composite materials whose microstructures deviate from strict periodicity, including quasi-periodic, randomly perturbed periodic, and hierarchically structured configurations. The project has three main threads: (1) extension of two-scale convergence theory to weakly non-periodic settings; (2) development and error analysis of finite element solvers for the resulting cell problems, with particular attention to interfaces with limited regularity; (3) validation against experimental effective-modulus data from polymer-matrix composites provided by two industrial partners. The project funds two PhD students and supports short-term research visits to partner institutions in Prague and Patras. Deliverables include open-source Python cell-problem solver modules and a set of benchmark problems for the homogenisation community.

projects.title: Thermal Management of Electronic Packages Using Microstructure-Informed Effective Medium Models
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: THERMICRON addressed the demand from the regional electronics industry for fast, physics-based thermal models that go beyond empirical rules of thumb. The project combined homogenisation-derived effective conductivity tensors with package-level finite element thermal simulations to predict steady-state and transient temperature distributions in multi-layer printed circuit board assemblies. Microstructural data from three industrial samples (copper-filled polymer composites and ceramic substrates) were characterised by X-ray microtomography at a partner laboratory, and the resulting three-dimensional geometries were used to solve the homogenisation cell problem directly. The project produced a validated modelling workflow and trained two MSc students who subsequently joined the industrial partner.

projects.title: Lattice Polytopes: Combinatorial Structure and Computational Methods
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project supports a small research group at the Faculty of Technical Sciences working on combinatorial properties of convex lattice polytopes, with particular focus on Ehrhart theory, reflexivity, and unimodular triangulations. The activities include systematic computational enumeration of polytope families using Polymake and SageMath, development of efficient algorithms for checking triangulation existence, and dissemination of results at regional conferences. The project also funds the maintenance of open-access databases of classified lattice polytopes assembled during the research. Jokić contributes to computational experiments and the writing of research outputs. The expected deliverables include at least two journal publications and participation in one international conference by project end.

projects.title: Fluctuation Bounds and Optimal Protocols in Mesoscopic Non-Equilibrium Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigates fundamental constraints on dissipation and current fluctuations in small driven systems, with three main directions: (i) deriving and testing thermodynamic uncertainty relations beyond the Gaussian regime, (ii) constructing optimal driving protocols that minimise dissipated heat for prescribed transitions between steady states, and (iii) extending the Hatano–Sasa framework to systems with non-Markovian noise. The group develops both analytical methods (variational calculus, Floquet theory for master equations) and high-accuracy numerical solvers (sparse Fokker–Planck integration, kinetic Monte Carlo). Partners contribute expertise in single-molecule experiments and large-deviation statistics.
partners: Institute of Physics Belgrade, University of Belgrade, Serbia
Eötvös Loránd University, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Thermodynamics of Information Processing in Nano- and Micro-Scale Devices
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: A European consortium project studying the thermodynamic costs of computation and sensing at small scales. Žarković's group leads Work Package 3, which covers theoretical analysis of Maxwell demon protocols, Landauer erasure under realistic constraints (finite latency, imperfect measurement), and the entropy budget of biochemical signal-transduction cascades. The work package delivers analytical bounds and simulation benchmarks used by experimental partners who implement colloidal and electronic model systems. The group contributes approximately 0.8 FTE per year, with one postdoc and one PhD student directly supported. Deliverables include open-source Fokker–Planck solvers deposited on a project repository.

projects.title: Topological Analysis of Industrial Time-Series Data from Sensor Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TOPOLYZE develops methods for applying persistent homology to multivariate time-series data collected from industrial sensor networks, with test datasets provided by a partner company operating a manufacturing facility near Novi Sad. The project constructs joint attractor reconstructions from multiple correlated sensor channels and derives topological features robust to missing data and sensor drift. A secondary objective is to produce a validated open-source toolbox for industrial analysts that wraps the group's existing C++ filtration code in a Python interface with automatic parameter selection. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

projects.title: Dynamical Systems and Topological Methods: From Theory to Computation

projects.summary: DYNTOP supported foundational research on the theoretical underpinnings of applying persistent homology to the attractor reconstruction problem. The project investigated stability bounds for persistence diagrams under stochastic perturbations, developed the Mapper-plus-persistence pipeline later published in 2017, and initiated collaboration with partners in Romania and Hungary.
