projects.title: Rheological Instabilities in Dense Suspensions Under Oscillatory and Transient Shear
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi sistematskim istraživanjem nestabilnosti toka i tranzijentnih reoloških fenomena u gusto punjenim koloidnim suspenzijama pri oscilatorno primenjenoj smičnoj deformaciji. Cilj je uspostavljanje kvantitativnih korelacija između mikrostrukturnih parametara (veličina čestica, zapreminski udeo, površinska hemija) i makroskopskog reološkog odgovora merenog metodama LAOS i rheo-SAXS. Istraživanje se odvija u saradnji sa grupama na Univerzitetu u Segedinu i Tehnološkom institutu u Drezdenu. Planirani rezultati obuhvataju tri objavljena rada u časopisima sa JCR liste, doktorsku disertaciju jednog od saradnika i javno dostupan skup reoloških podataka.

projects.title: Scalable Formal Safety Analysis for Hybrid Embedded Control in Automotive and Industrial Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SAFEHYB addresses the computational bottlenecks that arise when applying formal reachability analysis to industrial-scale hybrid automata models of embedded control loops. The project develops compositional verification workflows, template-based invariant generation tools, and conformance checking procedures that bridge the gap between verified models and deployed firmware. Vojnović leads the work package on invariant synthesis and tool integration. Case studies are drawn from collaborating partners in the automotive supply chain and process automation sector. The project funds one PhD student and produces open-source tool extensions for the Uppaal and SpaceEx platforms. projects.title: Certification Evidence Generation for Safety-Critical Control Loops via Hybrid Formal Methods

projects.summary: CERTLOOP investigates how the output artefacts of hybrid automaton verification — reachable state certificates, counterexample traces, and conformance reports — can be structured to satisfy documentation requirements under functional safety standards such as IEC 61508. projects.title: Fractional-Order Models for Transport in Structured Biological Tissues

projects.title: Anomalous Diffusion Benchmarks for Regional MRI Centres in Serbia

projects.title: Adaptive Decoding Algorithms for Long-Term Upper-Limb Neuroprosthetic Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат се бави развојем алгоритама за аутоматску рекалибрацију декодера покрета у интракортикалним нeuropротетским системима. projects.title: Neural Signal Datasets and Benchmarks for Upper-Limb Rehabilitation Devices

projects.summary: Пројекат има за циљ изградњу јавно доступног репозиторијума хроничних интракортикалних и електрокортикографских снимака прикупљених у сарадничким лабораторијама у Србији и Словенији. projects.title: Wearable Optical Oxygenation Monitoring for Field-Based Exercise Physiology and Rehabilitation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: OXFIELD focuses on the development and clinical validation of a miniaturised, wearable CW-NIRS device capable of ambulatory muscle oxygenation monitoring during free-living physical activity and guided rehabilitation programmes. The project combines hardware design work at the Faculty of Technical Sciences with validation studies conducted at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina in patients recovering from lower-limb vascular surgery. Specific aims include reducing motion artefact below 5% signal contamination, establishing normative oxygenation profiles for graded field exercise in healthy Serbian adults aged 20–65, and piloting the device in a six-week post-surgical rehabilitation cohort of 30 patients. Reference measurements use FD-NIRS in the laboratory and Doppler flowmetry. The project directly informs industrial discussions with a medical device startup at NTP Novi Sad.

projects.title: Optical and Metabolic Imaging of Skeletal Muscle in Cardiovascular and Metabolic Disease
projects.programme: Horizon Europe

projects.title: Bayesian Dose Individualisation Platform for Narrow-Therapeutic-Index Drugs in Patients with Renal Impairment

Work packages include retrospective population PK model development and refinement, software implementation of a web-based Bayesian feedback interface, and a multicentre prospective clinical evaluation at three hospitals in Vojvodina. projects.title: Elastography Artefact Suppression in Steatotic and Fibrotic Liver Tissue

Szabó leads the work package responsible for algorithmic development and scanner implementation. projects.title: Topological Methods for Industrial Data Analysis

projects.title: Privacy-Preserving Statistical Inference over Distributed Health and Administrative Data

projects.summary: The project develops theoretically grounded differentially private mechanisms for statistical inference tasks—estimation, hypothesis testing, and regression—over data distributed across multiple administrative and healthcare institutions in Serbia. The work targets the specific constraints of the Serbian health information system, where data are held by regional institutes that cannot share raw records. The project produces open-source software tools for deploying privatised sufficient statistic aggregation and federated Bayesian inference, validated against synthetic datasets modelled on national registry structures. Capacity building for data holders is a secondary objective, delivered through two practitioner workshops. The project involves three partner institutions and funds two doctoral students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
University of Niš, Faculty of Electronic Engineering, Serbia
Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Federated and Privacy-Aware Analytics for Cross-Border Statistical Infrastructures
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: FEDPRIVA is a Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Action bringing together eight partners from five countries to build interoperable federated analytics infrastructure for national statistical offices. Pejić leads Work Package 3, which is responsible for the design and formal analysis of the privacy mechanisms embedded in the federation protocol. The work package covers noise calibration, composition accounting, and the adaptation of local DP protocols to the specific query workloads of official statistics production. The University of Novi Sad team contributes expertise in Rényi DP accounting and adaptive budget allocation. The project targets a demonstrator deployment at two partner statistical agencies by month 30.

projects.title: Stochastic Continuum Models: Numerical Analysis and Simulation for Engineering Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STOCON addresses the development and rigorous analysis of numerical methods for stochastic partial differential equations arising in structural and fluid mechanics with uncertain material data. The project focuses on stochastic Galerkin and collocation discretisations for elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic problems, with a particular emphasis on deriving computable a posteriori error bounds that can drive adaptive refinement in both physical and stochastic degrees of freedom. Starčević contributes to the design and implementation of adaptive algorithms for problems with random microstructures, including random void and inclusion distributions in elastic solids. The project involves close collaboration with the Mathematical Institute in Belgrade and includes benchmark studies against experimental data provided by an industrial advisory partner in the polymer processing sector.
partners: Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Uncertainty Quantification Methods for Coupled Flow and Transport Problems in Environmental and Industrial Contexts
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: UQFLOW is a cross-border collaboration between research groups in Novi Sad and Debrecen focusing on uncertainty quantification for coupled fluid flow and solute transport models relevant to groundwater management and industrial filtration. The project develops quasi-Monte Carlo and sparse collocation solvers for models with high-dimensional stochastic input spaces arising from uncertain hydraulic conductivity fields and uncertain boundary forcing. Starčević leads the work package on algorithm development and validation, coordinating the implementation of randomised quasi-Monte Carlo estimators and their integration with finite-volume solvers. The project includes joint student supervision and short-term staff exchanges between the two partner institutions, with results disseminated through a shared open-source code repository.
partners: Department of Applied Mathematics, University of Debrecen
Institute for Environmental Sciences, Novi Sad

projects.title: Fuzzy Decision Frameworks for Regional Infrastructure Planning under Uncertainty
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project develops decision support tools for regional authorities in Vojvodina that need to evaluate infrastructure investment options—road, water supply, and waste management—under conditions of data scarcity and expert disagreement. The mathematical core relies on interval type-2 fuzzy aggregation operators and sensitivity analysis procedures. Nada Dobanovački contributes to the design of the expert elicitation instruments and the implementation of the type-2 fuzzy computation modules in Python. The project collaborates with the Institute for Regional Development of Vojvodina to validate prototypes on real planning cases, and final tools are intended to be released as open-source libraries compatible with standard GIS platforms.
partners: Institute for Regional Development of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Semantic Foundations of Typed Effectful Computation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the mathematical foundations of programming languages that track computational effects in their type systems, with an emphasis on graded and indexed monads, quantitative type systems, and their relationship to formal verification. The team consists of three researchers at the University of Novi Sad and one collaborator at the University of Zagreb. Work packages cover: (1) the 2-categorical structure of graded monads, (2) quantitative logical relations for differential privacy, and (3) an Agda library of certified constructions. The project has produced four peer-reviewed publications and one preprint. A one-week summer school on categorical methods in programming language theory was co-organized in Novi Sad in September 2023.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
University of Zagreb, Department of Mathematics

projects.title: Denotational Semantics for Probabilistic and Continuous-Distribution Programming Languages
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral Serbia–Austria scientific exchange project with the Technische Universität Wien, supporting joint research visits and a shared graduate student co-supervision arrangement. The scientific focus is the adequacy and full abstraction theory for higher-order languages with continuous probability distributions, using quasi-Borel spaces and synthetic measure theory as semantic frameworks. The project funds four researcher visits per year, one jointly supervised PhD student at TU Wien, and a small workshop held alternately in Novi Sad and Vienna. Outputs are expected to include two journal papers and contributions to the Lean 4 library of measure-theoretic results.
partners: Technische Universität Wien, Institute of Logic and Computation, Austria

projects.title: Varijacioni i geometrijsko-merinski metodi za kapilarne površi sa slobodnom granicom
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi razvojem matematičke teorije za kapilarne površi na nehomogenim i neregularnim podlogama, korišćenjem aparata teorije geometrijskih mera i varijacionog računa. Centralni ciljevi su: (1) dokaz egzistencije i regularne strukture slobodnih granica u prisutnosti hrapavosti podloge, (2) izvod oštrin izoperimetarskih nejednakosti za kapljice pod gravitacijom, i (3) numerička implementacija Level-Set i Surface Evolver metoda prilagođenih ovim geometrijama. Tim čine tri istraživača sa PMF-a i jedan saradnik sa FTN-a. Planirani rezultati obuhvataju šest radova u međunarodnim časopisima i jednu doktorsku disertaciju.
partners: Univerzitet u Novom Sadu, Prirodno-matematički fakultet
Univerzitet u Novom Sadu, Fakultet tehničkih nauka

projects.title: Mathematical modelling of capillary-driven flow in microfluidic devices for life-science applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project establishes a collaboration between the Department of Mathematics and Informatics at the Faculty of Sciences and two technology companies at NTP Novi Sad working on microfluidic diagnostic devices. The mathematical component covers variational modelling of equilibrium and quasi-static capillary surfaces in non-standard channel cross-sections, derivation of reduced one-dimensional models for capillary rise kinetics, and development of validated simulation tools. The industry partners provide channel geometries, wettability measurements, and experimental validation data. The project supports one PhD student and aims to produce a joint simulation workflow usable by the industry partners for device design.
partners: Naučno-tehnološki park Novi Sad — Fluenta d.o.o.
Naučno-tehnološki park Novi Sad — BioSens Instruments d.o.o.

projects.title: Symbolic Formula Recovery from Structured Scientific Data
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat SYMFORM bavio se razvojem metoda za automatsko otkrivanje analitičkih matematičkih formula iz strukturiranih naučnih podataka u obliku tabela. Centralna tema bila je integracija ekspertskog znanja o domenu u gramatiku koja vodi prostor pretrage genetskog programiranja, sa ciljem pronalaženja interpretabilnih modela koji ne zahtevaju manuelnu izgradnju karakteristika. U okviru projekta razvijeni su: biblioteka otvorenog koda za gramatički vođenu simboličku regresiju, metodologija za automatsku inferenciju gramatike iz poznatih jednačina domena, i protokol za validaciju otkrivenih formula na ekstrapolacionim skupovima podataka. Rezultati su primenjeni na podatke iz agronomije, procesne hemije i biomedicinskih istraživanja u saradnji sa institucionalnim partnerima.
partners: Prirodno-matematički fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Lattice Security Parameters for Post-Quantum Embedded Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the concrete security of lattice-based KEM parameters when deployed on resource-constrained embedded hardware, with a focus on ARM Cortex-M4 and RISC-V targets. Research activities cover three areas: (1) empirical sieving experiments on module lattices to update concrete security estimates, (2) constant-time implementation and formal verification of NTT-based polynomial arithmetic, and (3) analysis of failure probability inflation due to imperfect entropy sources in embedded RNGs. The project funds two PhD students, travel to international conferences, and access to a 48-core computing cluster at the Faculty of Sciences.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Telecommunications, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Bridging Post-Quantum Standards and Industrial Embedded Security
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PQBRIDGE is a cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian partners aimed at transferring post-quantum cryptographic knowledge to small and medium enterprises producing embedded devices for industrial automation. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on algorithm selection and parameter recommendation, producing guidelines for integrating ML-KEM and ML-DSA into industrial communication protocols. The project includes two industry workshops per year, an open-source reference implementation repository, and a joint summer school for graduate students from both countries. The Faculty of Sciences contributes expertise in hardness analysis; industrial partners provide hardware targets and real-world protocol constraints.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Computer Science and Information Technology, University of Pécs
Elektrosoft d.o.o., Novi Sad
Digitális Ipar Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Harmonic Analysis and Sampling on Irregular Geometric Structures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: HASING investigates sampling and reconstruction problems for functions defined on non-Euclidean domains—specifically nilpotent and solvable Lie groups, homogeneous trees, and Riemannian manifolds—using tools from abstract harmonic analysis and frame theory. The project has three main workstreams: (1) extending coorbit space theory to groups without square-integrable representations, (2) deriving sharp sampling density thresholds in terms of geometric invariants of the domain, and (3) prototyping numerical reconstruction algorithms for graph-structured sensor networks. Partners contribute expertise in representation theory, sparse recovery, and applied signal processing. The project supports two PhD students and funds collaborative visits with Budapest and Turin.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade
Budapest University of Technology and Economics

projects.title: Game-Theoretic Mechanisms for Peer-to-Peer Energy Markets in South-East Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a theoretical and computational framework for designing incentive-compatible trading mechanisms suited to the regulatory and grid conditions of South-East European distribution networks. Work packages cover equilibrium analysis of double auctions and VCG mechanisms, fairness properties, and platform pricing. Empirical calibration is performed using metering and survey data from Vojvodina. The project funds one PhD student and two research associates at the University of Novi Sad and involves a visiting researcher exchange with the Czech Academy of Sciences. An open-source Python library for simulating peer-to-peer auction outcomes is a planned output, along with at least five journal publications and a policy brief targeted at the regulatory body for energy in Serbia.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Information Theory and Automation, Czech Academy of Sciences

projects.title: Flexibility Procurement in Community Microgrids: Market Design and Pilot Implementation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FLEXCOM addresses the design and piloting of flexibility markets for community microgrids spanning the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Ljubomir Babić leads the work package on mechanism design, responsible for specifying auction rules, incentive structures, and settlement procedures to be implemented in a pilot involving twelve prosumer households in Subotica and eight in Baja. The project combines engineering partners responsible for metering infrastructure with economics and mathematics teams working on market rules. Babić's team provides equilibrium analysis and formal proofs of truthfulness for the proposed mechanisms, as well as simulation-based stress testing prior to the live pilot. Regulatory alignment with Serbian and Hungarian energy law is addressed in a separate work package.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Certified Compilation Chains for Safety-Critical Embedded Software
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CERTCHAIN investigates methods for constructing end-to-end verified compilation chains for safety-critical software targeting resource-constrained embedded processors. The project formalizes a multi-pass compiler from a restricted imperative source language to a simple RISC assembly model in Coq, proving that each pass preserves the denotational semantics of programs. A particular focus is the interaction between memory models and pointer arithmetic, which breaks compositionality assumptions common in earlier certified-compiler work. The project supports two Ph.D. students and collaborates with the University of Ljubljana on the memory-model component. Deliverables include a publicly available Coq development and a prototype toolchain extractable to OCaml.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Department of Mathematics and Informatics
University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics

projects.title: Type-Theoretic Foundations for Formally Verified Mathematical Libraries
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: TYPFORM supports the development of a reusable library of machine-checked mathematical results in Agda and Coq, covering abstract algebra, number theory, and basic combinatorics. The motivation is to lower the entry barrier for researchers in mathematics and computer science who wish to use proof assistants without deep expertise in type theory. The project funds the development of documentation, worked examples, and a web interface for browsing proof statements. A secondary goal is to integrate library components into undergraduate teaching on formal methods. One M.Sc. student is funded through the project.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Department of Mathematics and Informatics

projects.title: Signature-Based Learning Methods for Irregular Sequential Data in Science and Engineering
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SIGLEARN is a three-year project led by Prof. Dragan Jevtić at the University of Novi Sad, funded under the Science Fund of Serbia IDEAS scheme. The project investigates the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of path-signature and rough-path methods for learning from time series that arrive with irregular timestamps, missing observations, or heterogeneous sampling rates. Application domains include hydrological monitoring, industrial sensor streams, and medical waveform analysis. Tamara Ilić contributes to the work package on numerical methods for signature computation and to the experimental evaluation on biomedical datasets. The project involves a collaboration with the Faculty of Mathematics, University of Belgrade, and an associated industrial partner providing anonymised sensor data.
partners: Faculty of Mathematics, University of Belgrade
SensoriQ d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Evolutionary Optimisation of Embedded Neural Architectures for Industrial IoT
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: EMBEVO developed multi-objective evolutionary methods for designing neural network architectures that satisfy strict memory and latency constraints imposed by low-power microcontrollers used in industrial monitoring applications. The project built a shared benchmark of 12 embedded target boards and associated profiling toolchains, enabling reproducible comparison of NAS methods across hardware platforms. Research produced tabular and surrogate-assisted NAS benchmarks, constraint-handling strategies, and architectural patterns suited to sub-512 KB devices. The project involved three research groups at the University of Novi Sad and one at the University of Belgrade, and supported two doctoral students through completion of their dissertations.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences
University of Belgrade, School of Electrical Engineering

projects.title: Cross-Border Embedded AI for Smart Manufacturing
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSEDGE brings together universities and technology parks in the Vojvodina and southern Hungary region to develop AI inference solutions for small and medium-sized manufacturers lacking dedicated AI staff. The University of Novi Sad team, led by Kmeťová, is responsible for the work package on architecture search and model compression, delivering compressed models for vibration monitoring, visual quality control, and energy consumption prediction use cases. Partner companies contribute anonymised sensor datasets and define deployment constraints. The project includes a shared testbed of embedded platforms at the Science Technology Park Novi Sad and a corresponding facility at the Miskolc Innovation Park.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Department of Automation and Applied Informatics

projects.title: Sparse Signal Models for Accelerated Medical Imaging Reconstruction
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SPARSEMED investigates the mathematical foundations and practical implementation of sparse recovery algorithms tailored to the matrix structures that arise in MRI and CT reconstruction. The project addresses three interconnected problems: characterising recovery conditions for structured sensing matrices common in clinical imaging devices, designing fast solvers suitable for real-time or near-real-time reconstruction on GPU hardware, and validating reconstruction quality on anonymised patient datasets provided by a partner clinical centre. Jovana Ljubojević contributes to the theoretical workpackage on recovery guarantees and to numerical benchmarking. The project involves researchers from two Serbian universities and one clinical partner and has a total budget of approximately 45 000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Prime Gap Distributions: Computational Verification and Probabilistic Models
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project funds the construction and maintenance of a prime gap database covering all primes up to 10^15, computed using the faculty's 48-node Linux cluster. Research activities include large-scale testing of the Cramér–Granville model and its refinements, analysis of gap ratio sequences, and entropy-based characterisations of the gap sequence as a symbolic dynamical system. The project supported two doctoral students and enabled collaboration visits with partners in Hungary and Romania. Deliverables include publicly available gap tables, open-source sieve code, and a monograph chapter summarising computational evidence for and against existing probabilistic models of prime gaps. Budget: approximately 4.2 million RSD.

projects.title: Trajectory and Manifold Analysis for Single-Cell Profiling Pipelines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops mathematically grounded algorithms for trajectory inference from single-cell RNA-seq data, with emphasis on manifold curvature estimation and velocity-augmented embeddings. Key objectives include a scalable landmark-based variant of diffusion-potential embeddings suitable for atlas-scale datasets, a benchmarking framework covering topology classification and pseudotime recovery, and integration protocols for spatial transcriptomics data. The project funds two PhD student positions and supports bilateral exchange visits with Uppsala University and Masaryk University. All software is released under an open-source licence, and benchmark datasets are deposited in a publicly accessible repository hosted at the Faculty of Sciences.

Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Geometric Methods for Multi-Modal Single-Cell Data Analysis
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SCGEOM focuses on the mathematical challenges arising from multi-modal single-cell measurements, specifically the joint analysis of transcriptomic and spatial data. The project develops graph-coupled manifold alignment methods and analyses their theoretical properties under perturbation of the correspondence set. One junior researcher position is funded. The project also supports a graduate seminar series in computational geometry at the Faculty of Sciences and covers travel to two international conferences per year. Results are expected to feed directly into the DiffMap-tools Python package maintained by the research group.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Memory Safety Verification for Embedded C Software in Safety-Critical Domains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and evaluated abstract interpretation techniques tailored to C code running on resource-constrained embedded platforms, with a focus on firmware used in industrial control and automotive systems. Activities included the construction of a benchmark suite of embedded C modules with manually labelled memory safety defects, the adaptation of existing analysis passes to handle non-standard compiler extensions common in embedded toolchains, and a small industry validation study conducted with the assistance of a local electronics manufacturer. The project supported two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. The analysis tool developed within the project was released as open-source software at the project's conclusion.
partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš
Institute Mihajlo Pupin, Belgrade

projects.title: Verified Simulation Methods for Safety-Critical Dynamical Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VERISIM aims to extend the reach of validated numerical methods for ODEs to classes of problems that arise in engineering safety certification: stiff systems, systems with uncertain parameters, and systems with delayed terms. The project funds development of the ValODE software library, its documentation and testing infrastructure, and three application case studies in chemical process safety, structural health monitoring, and pharmacokinetics. A secondment arrangement allows one PhD student from Novi Sad to spend six months at the University of Warsaw to collaborate on the delay differential equation component. The project supports two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics, University of Warsaw
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Regional Network for Rigorous Computing in Engineering Applications
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RIGONET is a cross-border cooperation project establishing a network of researchers and engineers in Serbia and Hungary who work on certified numerical methods. The project organises annual joint workshops, a shared repository of benchmark problems, and a mobility scheme for master's students. Kosanović leads the work package on ODE enclosure methods and is responsible for producing a publicly available software module integrating ValODE with the CAPD library. The project also supports two student internship exchanges per year between the University of Novi Sad and Széchenyi István University in Győr. Practical engineering test cases are contributed by an industrial advisory board drawn from automotive and process-control sectors in both countries.

projects.title: Automated Learning and Verification of Communication Protocol Models
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops algorithms and tools for automatically constructing finite automaton models of communication protocols from network traffic, without access to protocol specifications. The main research directions are: improving the scalability of state-merging inference to protocols with large alphabets; integrating fuzzing-based counterexample generation into the inference loop; and establishing theoretical sample complexity guarantees for the resulting hybrid active-passive framework. A secondary objective is producing a verified automaton-based anomaly detector applicable to industrial control system traffic. The project involves collaboration with the School of Electrical Engineering in Belgrade and the Faculty of Informatics at Masaryk University in Brno. The team consists of four researchers at the University of Novi Sad plus two external collaborators.
partners: School of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Informatics, Masaryk University, Brno

projects.title: Formal Models for IoT Device Behaviour Verification in Smart Infrastructure
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: FORMIOT investigates the application of formally inferred finite automaton models to the problem of verifying expected behaviour of IoT devices deployed in smart-building and smart-city infrastructure. The project establishes a testbed of 30 representative consumer and industrial IoT devices, collects long-term traffic datasets under normal and fault-injected conditions, and evaluates multiple inference algorithms on their ability to produce accurate and compact behavioural models. A particular focus is on encrypted-traffic scenarios where only metadata is available. Results are intended to inform procurement guidelines for IoT devices in public-sector infrastructure in Vojvodina. The project involves a local engineering company as an industry partner providing device access and domain expertise.
partners: Elektromont d.o.o., Novi Sad
Department of Mathematics and Informatics, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Danube Extreme Event Dependence: Multivariate Statistical Methods for Trans-boundary Flood and Drought Risk
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANEX addressed the lack of harmonised multivariate statistical tools for assessing compound flood and drought risk across the Hungarian–Serbian border reach of the Danube and its tributaries. The project assembled a shared archive of daily hydrometeorological records from 38 stations in the two countries, developed copula-based joint return period models calibrated on the pooled dataset, and produced risk maps at 1:25 000 scale for municipalities in the Bačka and Baranya regions. Training workshops were held in Novi Sad and Pécs for staff at regional water directorates. Open-source software implementing the statistical methods was released under an MIT licence. The project delivered three peer-reviewed publications and one technical standard recommendation submitted to the International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences, Hungary
Directorate for Water Management Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Compound Hazard Probability Assessment for Serbian Critical Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: COMPAS developed a probabilistic framework for quantifying compound hydrometeorological hazard at locations hosting critical infrastructure — water treatment plants, road bridges, electricity substations — in Serbia. The core methodological contribution was a vine copula model for simultaneous extreme discharge, extreme wind speed and extreme ice loading, with parameters estimated from heterogeneous observational records of differing lengths using a censored composite likelihood. Risk metrics including annual failure probability and 50-year maximum expected loss were computed for 27 infrastructure sites identified in consultation with the Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure. The project ran five stakeholder workshops and produced a publicly available hazard atlas covering Serbia at county resolution. Two graduate students completed their doctoral research within the project.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Combinatorial Methods for Reliable Distributed Storage Codes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the systematic use of combinatorial design theory—resolvable designs, transversal designs, partial Steiner systems—as a unifying framework for constructing locally repairable codes with availability and hierarchical locality. Core activities include developing new existence and non-existence results for design families relevant to storage codes, building computational tools in GAP and Magma for exhaustive search and classification, and benchmarking the resulting codes against information-theoretic bounds and existing algebraic constructions. The project also maintains open tables of optimal LRC parameters for short lengths over small fields, which serve as a reference resource for the broader coding-theory community. Three researchers and two Ph.D. students at the University of Novi Sad are involved.
partners: Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade

projects.title: Statistical Methods for Causal Analysis of Panel Data in Behavioural and Social Research
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project develops and evaluates statistical procedures for causal inference in observational longitudinal studies typical of behavioural and social science research, where randomisation is impossible and data quality issues such as attrition and measurement error are endemic. The work covers three methodological areas: identification strategies using directed acyclic graphs for complex panel designs, estimation of direct and indirect effects under time-varying confounding, and treatment of non-ignorable missing data. Empirical demonstrations use existing survey datasets from the Western Balkans region. Nevena Kecman contributes to the simulation studies evaluating estimator performance under model misspecification and is responsible for preparing reproducible analysis code deposited in an open repository.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Sociological Research, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Chaos Indicators and Diffusion Timescales for Orbital Stability in Multi-Resonance Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops benchmark protocols for assessing the computational efficiency and physical reliability of chaos detection methods in multi-resonance Hamiltonian systems relevant to planetary science. Activities include constructing a curated test suite of Hamiltonian models with analytically known stability boundaries, running large-scale parallelised indicator comparisons on the University of Novi Sad computing cluster, and applying the validated methods to selected problems in asteroid belt and Kuiper Belt dynamics. A secondary goal is the derivation of improved Nekhoroshev-type estimates for systems with more than two degrees of freedom. Partners from Budapest and Belgrade contribute expertise in perturbation theory and observational constraints, respectively.
partners: Department of Mathematics, University of Novi Sad
Astronomical Observatory of Belgrade
Department of Applied Mathematics, Eötvös Loránd University, Budapest

projects.title: Serbian–Romanian Network for Nonlinear Dynamics in Astrophysical Systems
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between physics and mathematics groups in Serbia and Romania aimed at joint training and research in nonlinear Hamiltonian dynamics with applications to astrophysical problems including ring particle dynamics and mean-motion resonance modelling. Zec led the work package on numerical integration methods and chaos indicator benchmarking. Activities included two joint summer schools, shared access to computing resources, and a co-supervised PhD student. The project produced seven jointly authored publications and established a lasting collaboration framework between the Novi Sad and Timișoara groups.
partners: Department of Physics, West University of Timișoara, Romania
Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics, University of Craiova, Romania

projects.title: Magnetic Frustration and Emergent Phenomena in Oxide Pyrochlores and Spinels
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FRUSTOX focuses on understanding how geometric frustration in pyrochlore and spinel oxides gives rise to unconventional magnetic ground states such as spin liquids and spin ices. The project combines neutron powder and single-crystal diffraction, inelastic neutron scattering, and muon spin relaxation at large-scale European facilities (ILL and ISIS) with laboratory magnetometry and specific-heat measurements at the University of Novi Sad. Target materials include rare-earth and transition-metal pyrochlores and breathing spinels. A secondary aim is to synthesise and characterise thin-film versions of selected compounds by pulsed-laser deposition to probe strain-tuning of frustrated interactions. The project supports one PhD student and two master's students.
partners: Institute of Physics Belgrade, Serbia
University of Kragujevac, Serbia
Institut Laue-Langevin, Grenoble, France

projects.title: Bilateral Cooperation in Magnetometry and Neutron Methods for Frustrated Magnets
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and the Slovak Academy of Sciences in Bratislava focused on exchange of researchers and shared access to SQUID magnetometry infrastructure on the Serbian side and low-temperature dilution-refrigerator susceptibility on the Slovak side. Within the project, two researcher exchanges of two weeks each were conducted, resulting in comparative magnetometry measurements on a set of eight frustrated oxide powders. The project also facilitated a joint neutron beam-time proposal submitted to ILL.
partners: Slovak Academy of Sciences, Institute of Physics, Bratislava, Slovakia

projects.title: Surface Composition and Catalytic Activity of Bimetallic Pd-Based Catalysts from First Principles
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to establish quantitative connections between the surface composition of Pd-based bimetallic alloys (Pd–Cu, Pd–Ag, Pd–Ni) and their catalytic activity for selective hydrogenation and CO oxidation reactions. DFT calculations combined with ab initio thermodynamics are used to construct surface phase diagrams as a function of temperature, pressure, and gas-phase composition. Microkinetic models parameterised from DFT data are developed and validated against experimental turnover frequencies from collaborating experimental groups. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher at the University of Novi Sad and includes a collaboration with the Jožef Stefan Institute in Ljubljana for experimental surface characterisation.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana

projects.title: Perovskite Thin Film Carrier Dynamics for Laser-Based Quality Screening
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed ultrafast spectroscopic protocols for rapid, non-destructive assessment of carrier quality in solution-processed perovskite films. The main goal was to correlate sub-nanosecond transient absorption signatures with device-relevant parameters such as trap density and diffusion length, thereby reducing reliance on time-consuming device fabrication for material screening. Work packages covered instrument development (expanding the existing Ti:sapphire system with an optical parametric amplifier), film preparation under controlled atmospheres, and a cross-validation campaign with partner groups at the University of Szeged and the National Institute of Chemistry in Ljubljana. The project trained two PhD students and one MSc student and resulted in four peer-reviewed publications and a measurement protocol document distributed to participating laboratories.
partners: Department of Physics, University of Szeged, Hungary
National Institute of Chemistry, Ljubljana, Slovenia

projects.title: Defect Control in Wide-Bandgap Halide Perovskites for Monolithic Tandem Photovoltaics
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: WIDEGAP is a collaborative Horizon Europe project coordinated by a research institute in Germany, addressing the main efficiency losses in wide-bandgap perovskite top cells for silicon–perovskite tandem devices. Kovač's group leads Work Package 3, which is responsible for ultrafast spectroscopic characterisation of defect densities and non-radiative recombination rates across a library of wide-bandgap compositions provided by synthesis partners. The workpackage produces quantitative recombination rate constants that feed into drift-diffusion device models developed by an engineering partner. The Novi Sad group specifically contributes transient absorption, TRPL, and transient grating measurements. The project involves partners in Germany, the Netherlands, Slovenia, and Serbia, with an expected duration through late 2026.
partners: Centre for Solar Energy Research, Freiburg, Germany
Department of Photovoltaics, Delft University of Technology, Netherlands
National Institute of Chemistry, Ljubljana, Slovenia
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Scaling and Critical Phenomena in Polymer Systems near Structured Interfaces
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi teorijskim i računarskim proučavanjem kritičnih fenomena i skalirnih zakona za polimerne lance u blizini strukturisanih i nehomogenih površina. Osnovna metoda je Wang–Landau Monte Karlo sampling na kubnoj rešetki, dopunjena analitičkim pristupima renormalizacione grupe. Planira se sistematska studija uticaja geometrije površinskih šara, zakrivljenosti i hemijske heterogenosti na universalnost adsorpcionog prelaza. Rezultati treba da pruže temelje za modelovanje adsorpcije funkcionalnih polimera u mikro- i nanofluidičkim sistemima. Tim se sastoji od dva doktoranda i jednog postdoktoranda na PMF-u Novi Sad.
partners: Prirodno-matematički fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Institut za fiziku, Beograd
Masarykova univerzita, Brno

projects.title: Phonon Engineering at Semiconductor Heterointerfaces for Power Device Thermal Management
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi kvantitativnim razumevanjem i kontrolom transporta fonona na granicama faza u III-nitridnim poluprovodničkim heterostrukturama, s ciljem da pruži fizički utemeljene smernice za poboljšanje odavanja toplote u snažnim elektronskim uređajima. Kombinacijom TDTR i FDTR merenja, Ramanove termometrije i numeričkih simulacija zasnovanih na NEGF i BTE formalizmima, projekat generiše bazu podataka TBR vrednosti za relevantne interfejse (GaN/AlN, AlN/SiC, β-Ga₂O₃/SiC) u realnim radnim uslovima. Poseban akcenat stavlja se na uticaj metode rasta i gustine defekata. Rezultati su namenjeni kako fundamentalnoj fizici tako i primenjenom projektovanju naprava za energetsku elektroniku.
partners: Institut za fiziku, Beograd, Srbija
Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu, Srbija

projects.title: Razvoj mernih protokola za karakterizaciju toplotnih svojstava tankih filmova u mikroelektronici
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Pokrajinski projekat usmeren na uspostavljanje standardizovanih mernih protokola za određivanje toplotne provodnosti i termičkog kontaktnog otpora tankih filmova primenom 3ω metode i Ramanove termometrije. Nabavljena i kalibrisana je oprema za niskotemperaturna merenja do 80 K u okviru PMF laboratorije. Razvijeni protokoli verifikovani su na referentnim uzorcima SiO₂ i Si₃N₄ poznatih toplotnih svojstava, a zatim primenjeni na uzorke dostavljene od strane dva domaća istraživačka instituta. Projekat je omogućio izgradnju kapaciteta koji se koriste u naknadnim istraživanjima i u obuci postdiplomskih studenata.
partners: Institut za mikroelektronske tehnologije, Novi Sad, Srbija

projects.title: Radonski potencijal tla Vojvodine: kartiranje, modelovanje i primena u prostornom planiranju
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je obuhvatio sistematsko merenje geogenog radonskog potencijala na 180 lokacija ravnomerno raspoređenih po teritoriji Vojvodine, sa ciljem izrade regionalne karte u razmeri 1:250.000. Primenjene su pasivne i aktivne metode merenja radona u tlu, uz dopunska merenja Ra-226 i propusnosti tla. Izrađena je GIS baza podataka koja je javno dostupna i koja omogućava integraciju u urbanistička planiranja i procene radijacionog rizika. Projekat je uključio i edukativne aktivnosti namenjene opštinskim urbanistima i zaposlenima u inspekcijama za zaštitu od jonizujućeg zračenja.
partners: Departman za geografiju, turizam i hotelijerstvo, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Institut za javno zdravlje Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Pokrajinski sekretarijat za urbanizam i zaštitu životne sredine

projects.title: Harmonisation of Radon Measurement and Mapping Protocols in the Pannonian Basin Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aims to create a unified radon risk map for the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region by harmonising national measurement standards, calibrating passive detector systems against a common reference source, and conducting joint field campaigns at 60 shared measurement sites. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on data quality assurance and inter-laboratory comparison. Outputs include a shared open-access database, a bilingual technical guide for local authorities and a set of recommendations for building regulations concerning radon-resistant construction in the border region. The project involves six partner organisations from Serbia and Hungary and will produce the first continuously validated cross-border radon potential layer for the region.
partners: Institute of Nuclear Techniques, Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Georadon Research Centre, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Iron-Oxide Fingerprinting of Aeolian Dust Sources in the Pannonian Basin Using Mössbauer and Diffuse Reflectance Spectroscopy
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат PANNODUST финансиран је у оквиру програма IDEAS Фонда за науку Републике Србије. Циљ пројекта је развој спектроскопске базе података Fe-оксидних отисака прстију карактеристичних за различите изворишне области еолске прашине која се таложи у Панонском басену (локалне лесне заравни, источни Медитеран, северна Африка). Комбинују се трансмисиона Мезбауерова спектроскопија на температурама 20–300 K, дифузна рефлектанца спектроскопија и аутоматско клупско тестирање на новоуспостављеним мониторинг станицама у Војводини. Партнерска институција у Мађарској обезбеђује аеросол узорке са подручја источних Карпата. Очекивани исход је статистички модел за рашчлањивање удела локалне и далеке прашине у лесним архивама.
partners: HunDust Atmospheric Research Centre, Debrecen, Hungary
Институт за атмосферске науке, Универзитет у Клужу, Румунија

projects.title: Statistical Inference Methods for Multi-State Ion Channel Gating Models
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated statistical inference methods—including Bayesian MCMC, ABC-SMC, and continuous hidden Markov model approaches—for extracting kinetic parameters from single-channel recordings. Synthetic benchmark datasets with known ground-truth parameters were constructed for five canonical gating model topologies, and software tools implementing the inference pipelines were developed and made publicly available. Collaborating electrophysiology groups in Belgrade and Debrecen provided experimental single-channel recordings from neuronal and reconstituted channels to validate the methods against real data. The project trained two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: BioStat Research Group, University of Kragujevac
Institute for Biological Research, University of Belgrade
Department of Biophysics and Cell Biology, University of Debrecen

projects.title: Noise-Driven Dynamics in Biological Membrane Systems
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigated the role of stochastic fluctuations in ion-channel gating with an emphasis on the constructive effects of noise, including stochastic resonance and noise-induced transitions. The work combined analytical Fokker–Planck and Langevin formulations with numerical simulation and addressed the dependence of gating statistics on membrane properties such as lipid composition and temperature. The project supported one PhD student and produced five peer-reviewed publications. Equipment access was primarily through the existing Faculty of Sciences HPC cluster and the biophysics laboratory infrastructure maintained by the Department of Physics.
partners: Department of Physics, University of Novi Sad
Ruđer Bošković Institute, Zagreb

projects.title: Microfluidic Droplet Platforms for Environmental Water Analysis in the Vojvodina Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project developed PDMS and glass lab-on-chip devices capable of extracting and pre-concentrating trace heavy metal ions and pesticide residues from river water samples collected at five monitoring points on the Danube and Tisa rivers in Vojvodina. The main technical outputs were a flow-focusing droplet extraction module and a downstream colorimetric detection zone integrated on a single chip. The project involved collaboration with the Department of Chemistry at the University of Novi Sad for analytical validation and provided laboratory training for four master's students. Results contributed to two journal publications and one conference presentation.
partners: Department of Chemistry, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province

projects.title: Radiation-Induced Microstructural Defects and Embrittlement in Ferritic Steels for Serbian Research Reactor Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish a systematic PALS database for reactor-relevant ferritic and ferritic–bainitic steels irradiated in the RA-6 research reactor at Vinča. Key objectives included quantifying vacancy cluster evolution as a function of fluence, temperature, and alloy composition; correlating PALS parameters with Charpy impact properties and hardness; and developing a semi-empirical model linking positron lifetime data to displacement damage level. The laboratory's slow-positron beam was upgraded to extend the implantation energy range to 35 keV. Two Ph.D. students were supported by the project. Results contributed to the IAEA coordinated research programme on RPV steel embrittlement assessment.
partners: Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences, Belgrade, Serbia
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Integrated Assessment Methods for Reactor Pressure Vessel Integrity in Ageing VVER Reactors
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: INTEGRA-RPV was a multi-partner European project coordinating experimental characterisation and modelling activities for VVER-440 and VVER-1000 RPV steels under extended service conditions. Pantelić's group led the work package on positron annihilation and small-angle neutron scattering characterisation of surveillance specimens, contributing data to an integrated embrittlement database. The group performed PALS measurements on over sixty archive and irradiated specimens, supplied results to a common data repository, and participated in uncertainty quantification exercises. Collaboration with reactor operators in Hungary and Slovakia provided access to genuine surveillance capsule material not available through standard research channels.
partners: Hungarian Academy of Sciences Centre for Energy Research, Budapest, Hungary
Nuclear Research Institute Řež, Czech Republic
Institut Laue–Langevin, Grenoble, France
Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences, Belgrade, Serbia
Slovak University of Technology, Bratislava, Slovakia

projects.title: Vibration-Controlled Jamming and Flow in Dense Granular and Suspension Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VIBROFLOW investigates the mechanisms by which controlled mechanical vibration shifts the jamming boundary in dense granular packings and granular slurries. The project combines force-sensor array measurements, high-speed optical imaging, and acoustic emission monitoring to build a consistent picture of how vibration energy couples to force-chain dynamics at the particle scale. A central deliverable is a validated empirical phase diagram linking packing fraction, vibration amplitude, frequency, and particle polydispersity to flow or jammed states. The second strand develops a modified μ(I)-rheology framework that incorporates vibration as an effective temperature parameter. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoc at Novi Sad, with collaborative measurement campaigns at partner institutions.
partners: University of Szeged, Department of Theoretical Physics
University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade

projects.title: Granular Flow Diagnostics for Industrial Powder Handling
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: GRANTECH was a regionally funded project that transferred laboratory diagnostics for granular flow—specifically force-sensor arrays and high-speed imaging protocols—into practical measurement tools relevant to food and pharmaceutical powder handling in Vojvodina. The project produced calibration standards for the force-sensor platform, trained two MSc students in experimental granular characterisation, and delivered a technical report benchmarking the clogging behaviour of five industrial powders (flour, starch, lactose, calcium carbonate, and polymer pellets) under vibration conditions representative of industrial conveying lines. Results fed directly into the VIBROFLOW project design.
partners: Faculty of Technology Novi Sad, Department of Process Engineering
Vojvodina Chamber of Commerce, Food Technology Cluster

projects.title: Spin-Orbit Torque Engineering for Advanced Memory
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SOTEAM addressed the material and device physics bottlenecks limiting the integration of spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory cells with CMOS back-end processes. The project focused on three objectives: (i) systematic comparison of Pt, W, Pd, and Cr underlayer systems for torque efficiency and thermal budget compatibility; (ii) characterisation of exchange-bias schemes for field-free switching using IrMn and PtMn antiferromagnets; (iii) measurement of write-error rates and thermal stability in scaled Hall bar devices. The Faculty of Sciences group handled deposition, structural, and magnetic characterisation, while collaborators at the Faculty of Technical Sciences contributed electrical measurement setups and device modelling. Four journal publications and two conference contributions resulted from the project.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences

projects.title: Magnetic Nanostructures for Volatile and Non-Volatile Device Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This provincially funded project supported the early-stage development of the spin-orbit torque characterisation infrastructure at the Faculty of Sciences, including the commissioning of the vector network analyser ferromagnetic resonance setup and the magneto-optical Kerr effect microscope. Research activities included the first systematic harmonic Hall voltage measurements performed in the Novi Sad laboratory and the domain wall velocity study in Ta/CoFeB/MgO wires. The project provided funding for one doctoral student and supported several international short visits to partner laboratories in Ljubljana and Madrid. Results fed directly into the subsequent SOTEAM proposal.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana

projects.title: Atmospheric Electricity and Severe Convective Weather in the Danube Basin: Building a Transboundary Observation Capacity
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project established a cross-border network of five electric field mill stations (three in Vojvodina, two in Bács-Kiskun county, Hungary) with real-time data telemetry to a shared processing server at the University of Novi Sad. Vojnović led the work package responsible for sensor deployment, calibration, and data management. Collected data are used to investigate spatial coherence of atmospheric electric field anomalies ahead of severe convective events and to evaluate whether multi-station field observations can improve lead times for convective warnings issued by national hydrometeorological services. A joint data portal accessible to partner meteorological agencies was delivered. The project involved approximately 18 months of continuous parallel operation before a handover phase.
partners: Department of Physics, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Earth Sciences and Geophysics, University of Pécs
