Hungarian Meteorological Service, Budapest

projects.title: Long-Term Variability of Atmospheric Electric Field as an Indicator of Regional Aerosol and Climate Change Signals over Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This IDEAS grant supports the construction of a continuous, quality-controlled 10-year atmospheric electric field record at two Serbian stations and its analysis in the context of changes in aerosol loading, land-use, and regional climate variability. Key tasks include retrospective homogenisation of existing field mill records back to 2012, deployment of a co-located aerosol photometer at the primary site, and development of a statistical model separating global circuit signals from local pollution contributions. Collaboration with the National Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology in Bucharest enables cross-border signal comparison. The project supports one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher. Expected outputs include a publicly archived dataset and three peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Department of Physics, University of Novi Sad
Department of Meteorology and Climatology, University of Novi Sad
National Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology, Bucharest

projects.title: Thermodynamic Constraints on Collective Behaviour in Active Particle Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how the second law of thermodynamics constrains the emergence and stability of collective motion in active matter. The main objectives are to derive tight bounds on entropy production in MIPS and polar flocking transitions, to develop microfluidic experimental protocols for entropy production measurement, and to test stochastic thermodynamics frameworks beyond the weak-driving regime. Activities include Langevin and Monte Carlo simulations, microfluidic chip fabrication and imaging, and analytical calculations. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher at the University of Novi Sad and includes exchange visits with partner groups in Montpellier and Warsaw.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Laboratoire Charles Coulomb, Université de Montpellier
Institute of Physical Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences

projects.title: Active Matter Sensing and Control for Microfluidic Biotechnology Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project connects fundamental research on active particle sensing costs with practical microfluidic applications relevant to the regional biotech sector. The work focuses on three aims: quantifying the thermodynamic cost of gradient sensing in synthetic microswimmer systems, designing microfluidic channel geometries that exploit active particle self-organisation for passive sorting, and developing data analysis tools compatible with standard brightfield microscopy hardware. Collaboration with BioSens Institute in Novi Sad provides access to fabrication facilities. The project supports one master's student and one research assistant, and includes an industry engagement component with a Novi Sad-based microfluidics startup.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
BioSens Institute, University of Novi Sad
MicroFluidix d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Optical Constants of Carbon Nitride Coatings for Photonic Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established a systematic database of optical constants for a-CNx films deposited under controlled sputtering conditions, covering a wide range of nitrogen fractions and substrate temperatures. Spectroscopic ellipsometry spanning visible to mid-infrared wavelengths was the primary tool, supplemented by XPS, Raman, and nanoindentation. The database was validated against independent measurements at partner institutions in Bratislava and Warsaw. A secondary objective was the development of a sequential ellipsometric monitoring protocol applicable to multilayer coating processes. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications. Results were made openly accessible through a repository hosted at the University of Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Physics, Slovak University of Technology, Bratislava
Faculty of Materials Science and Engineering, Warsaw University of Technology

projects.title: Advanced Carbon-Based Coatings for Optical and Tribological Engineering
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between research groups in Novi Sad and Debrecen addressing deposition and characterisation of hard carbon-based coatings. Jeremić led the optical characterisation work package, responsible for establishing a common ellipsometric measurement protocol accepted by both partner laboratories and for training two Hungarian researchers in Tauc–Lorentz modelling. The project also had a tribology work package led by the Debrecen team. Deliverables included a joint characterisation handbook, three joint publications, and a short course offered to MSc students at both universities.
partners: Department of Applied Physics, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Pore-Scale Characterisation of Pannonian Basin Aquifer Rocks Using Multi-Method NMR Relaxometry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled a systematic database of NMR relaxometry, mercury injection, and helium porosimetry measurements for sedimentary rock samples from water-supply and geothermal boreholes across Vojvodina. Key objectives were to establish regionally calibrated surface relaxivity values for common Pannonian Basin lithologies, to evaluate NMR permeability models against pump-test data, and to develop open-access data processing scripts for Laplace inversion with automated regularisation. Field campaigns coordinated with the Provincial Secretariat for Energy and Geology provided access to archived drill cores from sixteen boreholes. The project supported two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. All calibration datasets have been deposited in an open institutional repository.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
Provincial Secretariat for Energy and Geology, Autonomous Province of Vojvodina
University of Pécs, Faculty of Natural Sciences, Hungary

projects.title: Magnetic Resonance Methods for Nanoscale Pore Characterisation in Tight Reservoir and Caprock Formations
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and Eötvös Loránd University Budapest investigating tight carbonates and claystones relevant to CO₂ storage caprock integrity and unconventional hydrocarbon potential in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Uzelac leads the work package responsible for low-field NMR and cryoporometry measurements on rock samples collected from both sides of the border. Partner responsibilities include micro-CT imaging and geomechanical testing. Joint workshops are held alternately in Novi Sad and Budapest. The project funds one PhD student at Novi Sad and contributes to upgrading the bench-top NMR instrument with a variable-temperature probe head for cryoporometry experiments.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences
Eötvös Loránd University, Institute of Geography and Earth Sciences, Budapest, Hungary
Geological Survey of Serbia

projects.title: Pulsed Glow-Discharge Nitriding: Plasma Chemistry, Ion Fluxes, and Layer Formation in Tool Steels
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PULSENIT investigated whether controlled pulsing of the discharge voltage in low-pressure N2–H2 plasma nitriding offers measurable advantages over DC operation in terms of compound layer phase control and nitrogen diffusion depth. The project combined time-resolved OES, Langmuir probe, and mass spectrometry diagnostics with systematic steel-nitriding trials on AISI H13, H11, and M2 grades. A purpose-built pulsed power supply (5–200 kHz, 25–75% duty cycle, up to 700 V peak) was designed and constructed within the project. Partners contributed metallurgical characterisation and corrosion testing. The project produced five journal articles and one patent application.
partners: Department of Physics, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology and Metallurgy, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Thermal Fatigue and Surface Treatment of Hot-Work Die Steels for Aluminium Die Casting
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research project funded by Termex d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based producer of die-casting tooling. The project evaluated plasma nitriding as a replacement for gas nitriding on H11 and H13 grades used in aluminium die-casting dies, with particular attention to thermal fatigue cracking under cyclic immersion in liquid aluminium. Dragić's role was to provide plasma process diagnostics and to specify nitriding parameters that would yield a controlled compound layer below 4 μm with a deep diffusion zone. The project resulted in a transfer of two sets of optimised plasma nitriding parameters to the company's production reactor.
partners: Termex d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Speciation and Mobility of Cadmium and Lead in Sediment Pore Waters of Transboundary Watercourses in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project investigated seasonal and spatial variability in Cd and Pb speciation across five transboundary river systems shared by Serbia and Hungary, focusing on the role of humic substances and redox gradients in controlling metal mobility from sediment to overlying water. Activities included development and cross-laboratory validation of stripping voltammetric protocols for pore water analysis, a joint 24-month monitoring campaign at 12 sites, and a risk assessment component for drinking water abstraction points near the Tisa and Begej corridors. The project produced validated standard operating procedures adopted by both the Serbian Environmental Protection Agency and the Hungarian partner institute.
partners: Department of Applied Chemistry, University of Pécs, Hungary
South Pannonian Environmental Research Institute, Subotica, Serbia
Directorate for Water Management of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Miniaturised Electroanalytical Platform for Real-Time Heavy Metal Monitoring in Estuarine and Fluvial Sediment Pore Waters
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project aims to develop a compact, field-ready electroanalytical platform combining a replaceable modified carbon paste electrode cartridge with a low-power potentiostat and a microcontroller-based data logger for autonomous deployment at river monitoring stations. Research tasks include optimisation of bismuth and antimony film electrodes for simultaneous Cd, Pb, and Zn determination in the presence of variable dissolved organic matter, design of a temperature and ionic-strength compensation algorithm, and a 12-month autonomous deployment trial at two sites on the Danube. The platform will be evaluated against the current regulatory monitoring methods specified in the Serbian Water Framework Directive implementation plan.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Visible-Light Photocatalytic Treatment of Textile Azo Dyes Using Bismuth-Based Semiconductor Composites
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the synthesis, structural characterisation, and photocatalytic performance of BiVO₄/TiO₂ and BiVO₄/TiO₂/rGO composites for the degradation of priority textile azo dyes under visible and solar irradiation. Work included optimisation of doping strategies, reactor design from batch to pilot scale, ecotoxicological assessment of treated effluents, and a comparative life cycle inventory of green versus conventional synthesis routes. The project trained two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher, produced eight peer-reviewed publications, and generated preliminary data on catalyst immobilisation methods now being pursued in a follow-up industry collaboration.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Vinča Institute of Nuclear Sciences, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Photocatalytic Pre-treatment of Industrial Textile Wastewater in the Vojvodina Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project examined the feasibility of photocatalytic pre-treatment as a step upstream of biological wastewater treatment for dyeing facilities in Vojvodina. Real effluent samples from three collaborating dyeing operations were characterised and treated using the BiVO₄/TiO₂ system. Biodegradability indicators (BOD₅/COD ratio) were tracked before and after photocatalytic treatment; in all cases the ratio improved from below 0.1 to above 0.3, indicating enhanced amenability to subsequent biological processing. A cost estimation for a 50 m³ day⁻¹ pilot installation was produced. Results were shared with the three cooperating companies under non-disclosure agreements.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Saponin Diversity in Threatened Caryophyllaceae of the Balkan Peninsula: Chemical Characterisation and Conservation Relevance
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SAPOBAL set out to document the triterpenoid saponin profiles of twelve Caryophyllaceae species listed as threatened or endemic on the Balkans, combining preparative HPLC isolation, multi-dimensional NMR structural elucidation, and HPLC-HRMS screening. The project produced reference compound libraries for six genera and established HPLC-UV quantification methods applicable to population-level surveys. Fieldwork was conducted across Serbia, Montenegro, and North Macedonia in cooperation with local botanical institutions. The chemical data are being integrated with distribution records to assess whether saponin chemotype diversity correlates with population fragmentation. Results are relevant to conservation prioritisation and to basic chemotaxonomy of the family.
partners: Institute of Botany and Botanical Garden, Faculty of Biology, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Sciences, University of Montenegro, Podgorica

projects.title: Agro-industrial Potential of Saponin-Rich Crops in the Pannonian Region: Extraction Optimisation and Quality Control
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project examined Vaccaria hispanica and Gypsophila paniculata as candidate crops for saponin production in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. The Novi Sad team led the work package on analytical quality control, developing and validating HPLC-UV and HPLC-HRMS methods for batch-level saponin quantification in raw and processed plant material. Extraction yield was benchmarked against industrial-scale parameters provided by the Hungarian partner. The project also included greenhouse trials to select high-yielding chemotypes. The analytical protocols developed will be made available to agricultural extension services in both countries as a basis for raw material standardisation.
partners: Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences (MATE), Kaposvár campus
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Vojvođanski Biljni Ekstrakti d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional company)

projects.title: Ion Pairing and Solvent Effects in Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution: Mechanistic Transitions and Predictive Kinetic Models
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish quantitative relationships between ion-pairing equilibria, solvent properties, and measured rate constants for SNAr reactions in aprotic and mixed aqueous–organic media. Experimental work combined stopped-flow spectrophotometry and conductometry with a systematic variation of cation identity (Li⁺, Na⁺, K⁺, Cs⁺) and solvent composition. Kinetic data sets were assembled for eight substrate–nucleophile combinations. A predictive model was developed that uses the cation–nucleophile association constant and two Kamlet–Taft solvent parameters to estimate k2 within a factor of three for new systems. The project supported two doctoral students and produced seven journal articles.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Kragujevac
University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Hydrolytic Stability of Halogenated Heterocyclic Intermediates Relevant to Agrochemical and Pharmaceutical Synthesis
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research project with a regional chemical distributor and formulation company, assessing the aqueous stability of ten chlorinated and fluorinated heterocyclic building blocks under storage-relevant pH and temperature conditions. Experimental work was carried out entirely within the Faculty of Sciences laboratory. Deliverables included measured pH–rate profiles, recommended storage pH windows, and shelf-life projections at 5 °C, 25 °C, and 40 °C. Results informed the partner's product specification sheets. One co-authored technical report was produced; journal publication of selected data is planned.
partners: Hemikal d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Biocatalytic platforms for lipase-mediated synthesis of enantiopure pharmaceutical precursors in engineered solvent systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the relationship between lipase immobilisation chemistry, solvent microenvironment, and enantioselectivity for four racemic pharmaceutical substrates (ibuprofen, naproxen, ketoprofen, 1-phenylethanol). Systematic variation of support polarity, pore architecture, and solvent composition was combined with computational docking to rationalise selectivity trends. The group developed a small library of 24 immobilised lipase preparations and screened them in a 96-position parallel reactor. Selected preparations were characterised by operational stability under industrially relevant conditions including solvent recycling. A laboratory protocol for ee > 90% at conversion ≥ 45% was established for ibuprofen and naproxen. Results fed into two journal publications and one conference contribution.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade

projects.title: Enzymatic synthesis of specialty wax esters and flavour esters using waste fatty acid feedstocks
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: GREENWAX investigated the use of fatty acid fractions from deodoriser distillate of sunflower oil refining as low-cost substrates for lipase-catalysed wax ester and flavour ester synthesis. Rhizomucor miehei lipase and Candida antarctica lipase B, each in three immobilised forms, were compared in batch and repeated-batch modes. Process parameters (temperature, substrate concentration, water activity) were optimised using response surface methodology. Product purity and ester composition were assessed by GC-FID and GC-MS. The project also evaluated biodegradability of the synthesised esters using OECD 301B. Collaboration with a regional edible oil company provided the waste feedstock stream and contextualised the cost calculations, though no formal IP transfer resulted from the engagement.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodinaoil d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner)

projects.title: Internal Phosphorus Loading Dynamics in Shallow Lakes of the Pannonian Plain under Changing Climate Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the geochemical controls on internal phosphorus loading in five shallow lakes of Vojvodina, combining long-term monitoring, sediment core analysis, and laboratory incubation experiments. A particular focus was placed on how interannual climate variability—specifically drought frequency and summer temperature anomalies—modulates the balance between iron-bound and organic P fractions in the sediment and their release to the water column. A mass-balance model parameterised with site-specific data was developed for each lake and validated against independent monitoring datasets. Results are intended to support water management decisions by the Institute for Water Resources Management of Vojvodina.
partners: Institute for Water Resources Management Jaroslav Černi, Belgrade
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Phosphorus Transformation Processes in Vojvodina Wetlands as Buffers between Agricultural Catchments and Open Water Bodies
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: WETPHOS examined the role of floodplain wetland complexes along the Tisa and Kereš rivers as phosphorus transformers and buffers between intensively farmed catchments and the shallow lakes they drain into. The Serbian team, led by Bulatović, was responsible for sediment geochemical characterisation across the Carska Bara and Monoštorski Rit wetland complexes, including sequential extraction, pore water profiling, and flux estimation during and after flood pulse events. The Hungarian partners focused on suspended sediment P content and catchment loading estimates. Joint mesocosm experiments compared P retention capacity of reed-bed versus open-water sediments under matched hydrological conditions.
partners: University of Debrecen, Department of Geography and Tourism, Hungary
Körös-Maros National Park Directorate, Hungary
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Tunable Hydrazone Ligands for Selective Sequestration of Transition and Heavy Metals from Industrial Aqueous Streams
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how the E/Z ratio, tautomeric state, and intramolecular hydrogen-bond pattern of hydrazone Schiff bases can be rationally adjusted by substituent choice to achieve selective chelation of Cu(II), Pb(II), and Cd(II) in the presence of competing Ca(II) and Mg(II). The approach combines systematic variable-temperature NMR characterisation in solution, DFT conformational analysis, potentiometric stability constant determination, and liquid–liquid extraction experiments. Twelve target ligands are prepared per year. The longer-term aim is to identify a small set of ligands with sufficient selectivity and water solubility for application in monitoring or removal of heavy metals from water streams in industrial settings.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Kragujevac

projects.title: Ligand-Based Detection and Removal of Heavy Metals in Danube Basin Water Systems
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Cross-border project addressing elevated Cu, Pb, and Cd concentrations in tributaries of the Danube in the Hungary–Serbia border region. The University of Novi Sad team is responsible for synthesis and NMR characterisation of hydrazone ligands proposed as selective extractants and colorimetric indicators. The Hungarian partner carries out field sampling and environmental modelling; a regional water-management authority provides analytical infrastructure for validation. Lalić's group delivers ligand batches, stability constant data, and extraction protocol documentation to partner laboratories. The work package includes training of two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher, one on each side of the border.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Chemistry, University of Pécs
Regional Environmental Agency Subotica–Baja (fictional)

projects.title: Valorisation of Vojvodina Agricultural Residues as Low-Cost Biosorbents for Textile Dye Removal from Industrial Wastewater
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project systematically screened eight Vojvodina-specific agricultural by-products as biosorbents for cationic textile dyes under conditions representative of Serbian textile industry effluents. Work included physicochemical characterisation (FTIR, XPS, BET, SEM-EDX), isotherm and kinetic modelling in batch mode, and column experiments using the two most promising materials. A laboratory-scale pelletisation protocol was developed in collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Final deliverables included a ranked biosorbent database, a pre-screening procedure based on XPS surface composition, and publicly available sorption data. The project supported two MSc theses and one doctoral candidate.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Dynamic Modelling and Scale-Up of Pelletised Biosorbent Fixed-Bed Systems for Textile Effluent Treatment
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DYNABED aims to bridge the gap between laboratory biosorption research and pilot-scale application by developing and validating dynamic mathematical models for pelletised biosorbent columns treating real mixed-dye textile effluents. The project combines experimental column campaigns at three scales (laboratory, bench, and a 50 L pilot unit to be constructed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences), mechanistic modelling of intraparticle mass transfer, and a machine learning layer for parameter estimation from easily measured biosorbent properties. Partners include a Slovenian university group with expertise in process modelling and a Romanian institute for pilot infrastructure. Two doctoral students are funded by the project.
partners: Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, University of Maribor, Slovenia
National Institute for Environmental Research and Engineering, Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Pannonian Aerosol Ionic Composition and Regional Source Attribution
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANAIR establishes a coordinated bi-national monitoring network at four sites spanning the Hungarian–Serbian transboundary region to characterise water-soluble ionic aerosol composition and identify shared emission sources. Sampling is conducted using standardised Partisol 2000 samplers, with centralised ion chromatographic analysis at Novi Sad and Debrecen laboratories. The project delivers a harmonised dataset of PM2.5 and PM10 ionic fractions covering at least 24 months, feeds a joint PMF receptor model applied to the pooled dataset, and produces recommendations for coordinated emission reduction measures targeting secondary sulfate and nitrate formation. Rajić contributes to field sampling, sample digestion and IC analysis, and co-authors the receptor modelling deliverable.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Environmental Sciences, University of Debrecen
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Northern Hungarian Environmental Inspectorate, Miskolc

projects.title: Stability and Functionality of Oilseed Protein Fractions for Plant-Based Food Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the conformational stability, aggregation behaviour, and functional properties (solubility, emulsification, gelation) of albumin and globulin fractions from four locally cultivated oilseed crops: sunflower, hemp, rapeseed, and flaxseed. Biophysical characterisation was combined with functional testing under conditions mimicking industrial processing steps. A key objective was to establish quantitative links between thermodynamic stability parameters and technofunctional outcomes, generating data useful for selecting oilseed protein sources for specific food product categories. The project involved collaboration with the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad and the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, and resulted in four journal publications and one master's thesis.
partners: Department of Food Technology, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Validation Strategies and Applicability Domain Methods for Antifungal QSAR Models
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the reliability of external validation procedures and applicability domain methods for QSAR models targeting antifungal azole compounds. A curated benchmark database of 11 published azole datasets was assembled, and six validation protocols and five AD methods were systematically compared. The work produced ranked recommendations for each combination of dataset size and model type, which were disseminated through journal publications and a freely accessible validation checklist. A secondary objective was to assess the degree to which OECD QSAR Principles are met in recently published antifungal QSAR literature; a survey of 84 papers showed that fewer than 40 % reported a true external validation set.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
BioInformatics Center, University of Belgrade
Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Integrated Computational and Experimental Screening of Triazole Antifungals in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project linking computational QSAR modelling groups in Novi Sad with synthetic chemistry and microbiological testing laboratories in Pécs, Hungary, and a regulatory science group at the University of Banja Luka. The Novi Sad team is responsible for building and validating QSAR models from experimental MIC data generated by partners and for providing ranked lists of candidate structures for synthesis. The project aims to establish a shared triazole antifungal dataset of at least 200 compounds with consistent microbiological testing protocols across three species. A joint training programme for early-career researchers in computational methods is an additional output.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Pharmacy, Hungary
Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Banja Luka
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Reconstruction of Urban PAH Contamination Histories in Vojvodina Cities Using Soil Core Archives
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project collects undisturbed soil cores from parks and green spaces in five Vojvodina cities and uses combined radionuclide dating and PAH fingerprinting to reconstruct combustion-related contamination over roughly the past 80 years. Weathering-correction procedures are being standardised for the regional soil types, which are predominantly calcareous Chernozem and Fluvisol. Vuković is responsible for PAH extraction, GC-MS quantification, and the application of weathering-correction algorithms. Results will be compiled into a freely accessible regional baseline database intended for use in urban planning and soil remediation prioritisation. The project involves collaboration with the Institute of Nuclear Sciences Vinča for radionuclide measurements.
partners: Institute of Nuclear Sciences Vinča, University of Belgrade, Serbia
City Institute for Public Health Novi Sad, Serbia
Department of Geography, Tourism and Hotel Management, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Aqueous-Phase Palladium Catalysis with Defined NHC Pre-Catalysts: From Mechanistic Understanding to Scalable Synthesis
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the activation mechanisms of (NHC)Pd pre-catalysts in aqueous and mixed-aqueous media and developed a library of water-tolerant complexes for Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling under mild conditions. Work packages covered ligand synthesis and pre-catalyst preparation, mechanistic studies by NMR and DFT, catalytic benchmarking across a diverse substrate set, and a scale-up demonstration at the gram scale. The project produced eight peer-reviewed publications, trained two PhD students and three master's students, and established a standardised benchmarking protocol adopted by the partner groups. Dissemination included presentations at four international conferences and an open-access dataset of catalytic performance data.
partners: Faculty of Physical Chemistry, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Sciences, University of Niš
Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Technology, University of Ljubljana

projects.title: Metagenomic Monitoring of Nitrification Risk in Vojvodina Drinking Water Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed sequence-based tools for early detection of nitrification risk in chloramine-disinfected distribution networks supplying Vojvodina municipalities. Core activities included deployment of standardised biofilm coupon networks across four utilities, construction of the regional metagenomic reference catalogue, and development of a qPCR-based three-marker panel (amoA, nxrB, cyc2) benchmarked against water quality records. A risk-scoring algorithm was calibrated on 36 months of paired molecular and regulatory data. Deliverables included an open-access reference sequence database, field sampling protocol documentation, and a training workshop for utility technicians held in Novi Sad in November 2022.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina
JKP Vodovod i Kanalizacija Novi Sad
BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Iron-Oxidising Biofilm Communities in Danube Basin Drinking Water Infrastructure: Ecology, Corrosion and Treatment Interactions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Cross-border project examining the ecology of iron-oxidising microbial communities in drinking water distribution infrastructure in the Hungarian–Serbian Danube corridor. Prof. Ljubojević leads Work Package 3, which covers metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiling of iron-oxidiser guilds in Serbian network sections and comparative analysis with Hungarian partner data. The work package addresses the relationship between Gallionella and Sideroxydans population dynamics, corrosion tubercle chemistry and discolouration events. Sampling campaigns involve 11 utilities in Vojvodina and three in Bács-Kiskun county. A joint protocol for microbiological corrosion assessment applicable to both regulatory environments is being developed as a key output.
partners: Department of Environmental Science, University of Pécs
Hungarian Water Utilities Research Institute (fictional)
JKP Vodovod i Kanalizacija Novi Sad
JKP Vodovod Sremska Mitrovica

projects.title: Lanthanide Chelate Equilibria in Aqueous and Mixed-Solvent Systems for Rare-Earth Separation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to generate a consistent set of thermodynamic stability constants, enthalpies, and entropies of complexation for trivalent lanthanides with a series of polyaminocarboxylate and phosphonate ligands in aqueous and aqueous–methanol media. Potentiometry, microcalorimetry, and luminescence spectroscopy are combined with computational speciation modelling. A secondary objective is to evaluate conditional stability constants under conditions relevant to hydrometallurgical separation of rare-earth elements from secondary raw materials. The project involves collaboration with the University of Debrecen and Masaryk University. Two doctoral students are funded within the project.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Inorganic and Analytical Chemistry, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Department of Chemistry, Masaryk University, Brno, Czech Republic

projects.title: Lanthanide Tracers and Chelating Agents for Environmental Monitoring of Rare-Earth Contamination in Sediments
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigated the speciation and mobility of rare-earth elements (principally La, Ce, Nd, and Gd) in river sediment and water samples from the Vojvodina region, Serbia. Equilibrium modelling of lanthanide distribution among humic, carbonate, and phosphate fractions was carried out using stability constants from the group's database. Field sampling was conducted at twelve sites along the Danube and Tisa rivers. ICP-MS measurements were performed at the Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy in Belgrade. A practical guideline document for environmental monitoring of REE contamination was produced for the Provincial Environmental Protection Agency.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade
Provincial Environmental Protection Agency of Vojvodina

projects.title: Bivalve Biomarker Networks for Trace Metal Monitoring in Vojvodina Waterways
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project established a network of fixed monitoring stations on the Tisa, Tamiš, Begej, and Zlatica waterways in Vojvodina, using transplanted Dreissena polymorpha cages and a standardised nine-biomarker panel. Field campaigns were conducted in spring and autumn across three years. A regional baseline dataset for Cu- and Cd-related biomarker responses was compiled and made available to provincial environmental authorities. Protocols for sample collection, preservation, and analysis were harmonised across three participating laboratories. The project trained four postgraduate students in the full sampling-to-analysis workflow and produced data directly applicable to WFD ecological status reporting for the Vojvodina canal network.
partners: Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province, Novi Sad
Institute for Water Management Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Metallothionein Proteomics as Diagnostic Tools for Multi-Metal Contamination in Danubian Bivalve Populations
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project develops isoform-specific protein and transcript-level assays for three Dreissena polymorpha metallothionein isoforms, aiming to determine whether their distinct metal-induction profiles can be used to fingerprint copper-dominated versus cadmium-dominated contamination in field populations. Work packages cover isoform characterisation by 2D-PAGE and LC-MS/MS, antibody production and validation, RT-qPCR assay development with certified reference materials, and field validation at sites spanning a known metal gradient on the Danube and Sava. Partners in Ljubljana and Pécs contribute proteomics infrastructure and independent field sites. A simplified ELISA-based field kit for DpMT-2 is being developed as a practical outcome for environmental monitoring laboratories.
partners: National Institute of Chemistry, Ljubljana, Slovenia
Department of Hydrobiology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Monitoring and Risk Assessment of Antibiotic Accumulation in Agricultural Soils of the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed the transboundary accumulation of veterinary antibiotic residues in agricultural soils along the Serbian-Hungarian border zone. Emilija Prodanović led the analytical methods work package, responsible for developing and harmonising extraction and LC-MS/MS quantification procedures applicable to both Serbian and Hungarian soil types. The work package delivered three validated multi-residue methods, a shared sample archive of 180 paired soil and water samples, and a joint database of antibiotic occurrence data. Field monitoring covered 80 sampling sites across two seasons. Results were used to produce a cross-border risk characterisation report submitted to agricultural authorities in both countries.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Agro-Environmental Studies, Hungarian University of Agricultural and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Provincial Institute for Public Health, Novi Sad
Research Institute for Soil Science, Kecskemét

projects.title: Baseline Survey of Veterinary Pharmaceutical Residues in Vojvodina Arable Soils
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project established a systematic baseline dataset on the occurrence and concentration ranges of sulphonamide and tetracycline antibiotic residues in intensively farmed arable soils across all seven Vojvodina districts. Prodanović led a team of four researchers and two MSc students. The project validated a single-laboratory QuEChERS-EDTA-LC-MS/MS method, conducted two seasonal sampling campaigns covering 90 sites, and produced a publicly accessible geospatial dataset. A technical report with policy recommendations regarding manure application limits was submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture. Three journal articles resulted from the project, and the dataset is archived at the University of Novi Sad Open Research Repository.
partners: Department of Chemistry, Biochemistry and Environmental Protection, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Public Health, Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermal Behaviour and Evolved Gas Signatures of Multi-Component Carbonate Mixtures Relevant to Industrial Calcination
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to build a comprehensive experimental database of TG-DSC-FTIR signatures for binary and ternary alkali and alkaline earth carbonate mixtures under industrially representative atmosphere conditions (variable CO2 partial pressures, 0–50%). Specific objectives included establishing kinetic models for mixed-phase systems, developing DTG deconvolution protocols for mineral quantification, and evaluating the influence of trace alkali contaminants on calcite decomposition temperatures relevant to lime and magnesia production. The project involved three researchers at the Faculty of Sciences (Novi Sad) and one external collaborator at the Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy in Belgrade. A total of six peer-reviewed papers and one conference presentation were produced.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Population genomics of freshwater amphipods as indicators of connectivity in Pannonian floodplain wetlands
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to characterise fine-scale population genetic structure and landscape connectivity in three amphipod species across the Vojvodina wetland network using RADseq genomics and eDNA metabarcoding. Key questions concern how the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal system modifies natural gene flow among wetland patches and whether historically isolated floodplain remnants retain unique genetic diversity worth considering in conservation planning. Fieldwork covers 45 sites sampled in two seasons. Bioinformatic pipelines are being developed jointly with a partner at the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad. The project funds one postdoctoral researcher and supports participation of three MSc students. Outputs include a public georeferenced genetic database of Pannonian amphipod populations.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Department of Ecology, University of Pécs

projects.title: Biodiversity assessment and habitat connectivity in cross-border Danubian wetlands using molecular tools
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUWET was a cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian partners focused on biodiversity survey and habitat connectivity in Danubian floodplain wetlands between Mohács and Novi Sad. Petrović led the work package on molecular biodiversity, coordinating eDNA sampling at 62 sites across both countries and managing the resulting sequence dataset. The project also included hydrological modelling and citizen science components led by Hungarian partners. A joint species occurrence database was produced and shared with the national nature conservation authorities of both countries. The project supported fieldwork infrastructure including purchase of sampling equipment and contributed to training of two Serbian PhD students in eDNA methods.
partners: Kiskunság National Park Directorate, Hungary
Institute for Nature Conservation of Serbia, Novi Sad office
Danube Research Institute, Budapest

projects.title: Endophytic Fungal Diversity and Function in Remnant Pannonian Steppe Grasslands
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STEPFUNG aims to produce a comprehensive inventory of endophytic fungi from ten protected steppe grassland sites across Vojvodina and the Banat region, combining culture-based and metabarcoding approaches with functional assays. The project addresses two specific questions: whether host-plant identity or habitat quality is the stronger predictor of endophyte community composition, and whether isolates from climatically stressed plants show elevated production of bioactive secondary metabolites. Sampling spans two full growing seasons. Metabolomics work uses HPLC-QTOF and molecular networking. The project funds one PhD position and supports undergraduate fieldwork training. Results are intended to inform conservation management of steppe remnants and to build a curated culture collection of characterised Pannonian grass endophytes.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad

projects.title: Carpathian Basin Endophyte Network: Cross-border Comparison of Grassland Fungal Communities
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CARPENDO brings together three research institutions from Serbia and Hungary to compare endophytic fungal communities across shared grass species distributed on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. The project applies standardised metabarcoding protocols developed jointly in the first project phase to ensure comparability. Biljana Andrić leads the work package on metabolite screening of isolates collected from both countries, with the goal of identifying strains that produce compounds of potential agricultural interest, particularly in biocontrol of cereal diseases. The project also includes a public outreach component for grassland conservation awareness and hosts two joint student exchanges per year.

projects.title: Ecophysiology and Conservation of Biological Soil Crusts in Pannonian Steppe Habitats under Changing Precipitation Regimes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated how shifts in precipitation frequency and intensity, projected for the Pannonian region under climate change, affect the ecophysiological performance and community structure of biological soil crusts on loess and sand habitats in Vojvodina. Activities included long-term mesocosm experiments with manipulated rewetting regimes, seasonal field monitoring of antioxidant capacity and chlorophyll fluorescence, transcriptomic characterisation of dominant moss species under stress, and development of a UAV-based crust mapping protocol. A secondary objective was to provide baseline data supporting habitat management decisions at protected loess bank sites. Partners included the Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province and the University of Szeged.

projects.title: Biodiversity Indicators for Loess Steppe Habitat Quality Assessment in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian partners aimed at harmonising biodiversity monitoring methods for loess steppe habitats listed under regional conservation frameworks. Hriešiková led the work package on cryptogamic indicators, contributing field survey data from 22 Vojvodina loess sites, developing standardised rapid ecophysiological assessment protocols, and co-authoring the joint indicator framework report. The project also included training workshops for conservation practitioners from both countries and a publicly accessible georeferenced database of loess habitat quality scores. Results were used by the Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province in habitat management planning.

projects.title: Thermal Ecology and Genetic Connectivity of Freshwater Turtles in Vojvodina Canal Networks Under Climate Change
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: THERMOCANAL examined how the geometry and hydraulic management of the Vojvodina canal network shapes thermoregulatory opportunities and gene flow for Emys orbicularis. Field campaigns in 2021–2023 combined iButton nest temperature logging, mark–recapture, and microsatellite genotyping across 14 canal segments. The project developed a GIS decision-support layer identifying canal bank sections where low-cost interventions—emergent vegetation strips, artificial basking platforms—could raise habitat thermal quality above the threshold needed for successful reproduction. Results were communicated to the Vojvodina Water Directorate and incorporated into a management guidance document. Two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher were trained under the project.

projects.title: Cross-Border Monitoring and Conservation Planning for Declining Reptile Species in the Serbian–Hungarian Agricultural Lowlands
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HERPBORDER established a harmonised monitoring protocol for six priority reptile species in a 120 × 80 km cross-border agricultural zone. Ivković led the work package on thermal ecology and activity modelling, contributing field data from 18 Serbian sites that were integrated with Hungarian partner data to produce joint species distribution models under current and projected 2050 climate conditions. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) field monitoring handbook distributed to environmental inspection bodies and resulted in a joint recommended list of agri-environment scheme measures for reptile conservation submitted to both national ministries of agriculture.

projects.title: Isotopic fingerprinting of migratory passerine flyway connectivity across the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ISOFLY aims to build the first multi-tissue, multi-isotope (δ13C, δ15N, δ34S, δ2H) reference database for migratory passerines along the Central European and Adriatic flyways as they pass through Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. The project combines standardised ringing station sampling at eight sites with captive diet-switch experiments to produce validated tissue-specific discrimination factors for six target species. Outputs include a freely accessible regional isoscape layer and a species-specific discrimination factor database. The project supports two PhD students at the University of Novi Sad and one at the University of Banja Luka.

projects.title: Shared wetland stopover habitats as indicators of transboundary avian connectivity between Hungary and Serbia
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: WETBIRD-IPA examined reed-bed and floodplain stopover habitats straddling the Hungarian–Serbian border as functional corridors for migratory passerines. The University of Novi Sad team led Work Package 3 on isotope-based trophic assessment, contributing stable isotope analysis of feather and blood samples from 11 shared ringing stations. The project produced joint habitat quality indicators and a cross-border bird monitoring protocol adopted by both national nature conservation agencies. Mijatović's group processed approximately 320 blood samples and contributed to the joint final report and a shared public geodatabase of stopover habitat polygons.

projects.title: Allelopathic footprint of invasive Fallopia and Ailanthus in Pannonian riparian corridors: chemical mechanisms and native community responses
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат је усмерен на систематско картирање хемијских трагова које оставља инвазивна вегетација рода Fallopia и Ailanthus altissima дуж рипаријалних коридора у Панонској низији. Циљеви обухватају: (1) квантификацију главних алелохемикала у земљишним растворима под инвазивним становима уз примену HPLC-MS технике, (2) лабораторијска и мезокосм испитивања токсичности на одабраним аутохтоним врстама, и (3) просторно моделирање алелопатског ризика интеграцијом теренских и даљинским осматрањем добијених података. У пројекту учествују истраживачи са ПМФ-а у Новом Саду и партнерске институције из Србије и Мађарске. Резултати треба да пруже основу за приоритизацију управљачких мера у заштићеним рипаријалним подручјима.

projects.title: Invasive plant chemical ecology in Danube riparian zones: cross-border monitoring and phytochemical baseline assessment
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Прекограничним пројектом успоставља се заједнички мониторинг инвазивних биљних врста дуж дунавских рипаријалних зона у Србији и Мађарској. Милица Радић руководи радним пакетом за фитохемијску карактеризацију, у оквиру кога се прикупљају стандардизовани узорци са 30 локалитета на обе обале и анализирају кључни алелохемикали. Пројекат ће резултирати заједничком базом података, протоколима за теренско узорковање и препорукама за управљање намењеним надлежним установама за заштиту природе у обе земље. Планирано је и заједничко издавање научне монографије са прегледом резултата мониторинга.

projects.title: Karyotype Evolution and Genome Architecture in Polyploid Complexes of the Balkan Biodiversity Hotspot
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the mechanisms driving karyotype diversification in five polyploid plant genera endemic or near-endemic to the Balkans: Campanula sect. Medium, Dianthus sect. Plumaria, Onosma, Seseli, and Sesleria. Field sampling covered Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Laboratory work combined flow cytometry, FISH mapping of rDNA and satellite repeats, GISH for allopolyploid genome discrimination, and RepeatExplorer-based repeatome analysis from low-coverage genome sequencing. The project produced chromosome-level cytogenetic maps for 22 taxa, identified at least three independent polyploidisation events, and characterised four previously undescribed satellite DNA families. It funded two PhD students and supported two short-term research stays at partner institutions abroad.

projects.title: Cytogenetic and Phylogeographic Diversity of Plant Endemics in the Dinaric Karst: Linking Genomic Data to Conservation Priorities
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project involving partners from Serbia and Hungary focused on rare and endemic plant species of the Dinaric karst and Pannonian margin. Turčan's group was responsible for the cytogenetic work package, delivering genome size estimates for 40 taxa, ploidy screening for 12 taxa with previously ambiguous chromosome numbers, and FISH-based karyotyping for eight priority species. Data were integrated with cpDNA phylogeographic results generated by the Hungarian partner. Project outputs included a shared database of cytogenetic and genetic data used to prioritise populations for ex situ conservation at partner botanical gardens. Three undergraduate thesis projects were carried out within the project framework.

projects.title: Soil Biological Monitoring Network for Agricultural Land in Vojvodina Using Nematode Bioindicators
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project established a network of 48 permanent monitoring sites distributed across the main soil types and agricultural land-use categories in Vojvodina. Sampling was conducted annually in spring and autumn. The primary aim was to compile a baseline dataset of nematode community indices suitable for detecting long-term trends linked to intensification or extensification of land management. Secondary outputs included a standardised regional extraction and identification protocol, a training workshop series for agricultural advisory services, and a publicly accessible data repository containing genus-level abundance tables from all sampling rounds. Five partner institutions contributed field access and agronomic data.

projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project comparing soil biological health indicators — including nematodes, earthworms, and microbial biomass — across matched pairs of land-use types in Hungary and Serbia. The project aims to harmonise monitoring methodologies across the two countries and produce a joint report usable by national agricultural advisory bodies. A shared bilingual database of nematode genera with morphological keys and reference images is among the deliverables. The project also supports two PhD students, one at each partner university.

projects.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Light Acclimation in Submerged Macrophytes Under Eutrophication Pressure in Pannonian Lakes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated transcriptomic and morphological plasticity in four submerged macrophyte species across a eutrophication gradient in Vojvodina shallow lakes. Mesocosm experiments combined with field sampling generated RNA-seq datasets covering light-harvesting, photoprotection, and carbon fixation gene families. A key deliverable was a standardised sampling and RNA extraction protocol for field macrophytes, and an integrated morpho-transcriptomic phenotyping framework for water quality bioassessment. The project funded two PhD students and included a research exchange with the Institute of Plant Genetics in Poznań and the Biological Research Centre in Szeged.

projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project coordinated by the Kiskunság National Park Directorate, Hungary, with Lukić's group leading the work package on biological quality elements including submerged macrophytes. Activities included harmonised survey protocols for lakes on both sides of the Serbian–Hungarian border, calibration of existing macrophyte indices to Pannonian conditions, and preparation of joint management recommendations. The project produced a shared geodatabase of macrophyte distribution records for 47 lake sites and contributed to regional WFD reporting. Workshops for environmental authorities in both countries were organised.

projects.title: Quantifying the Relative Strength of Pre- and Post-Mating Isolation Barriers in Sympatric Chorthippus Grasshoppers of the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project aimed to produce a comprehensive isolation barrier profile for two pairs of sympatric Chorthippus species in Vojvodina using a standardised framework. Work packages covered field surveys of species co-occurrence, phonotaxis assays under controlled conditions, controlled crossing experiments to quantify post-mating incompatibilities, and population genomic analysis of contact zone samples. A total of 24 field sites were surveyed across two field seasons, acoustic playback trials were conducted on over 400 females, and whole-genome sequencing was applied to contact zone individuals. Results contributed to three publications and one manuscript in preparation. A publicly accessible dataset of acoustic recordings and genotype calls was deposited in a national repository.

projects.title: Phylogeography and Population Connectivity of Orthoptera Across the Carpathian Basin: Implications for Conservation Genetics
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CARPATHGRASS was a cross-border collaboration examining population structure and gene flow in grassland Orthoptera shared between Serbia and Hungary. Bogićević led the work package on Chorthippus species, coordinating sampling and genomic analysis on the Serbian side. The project combined mitochondrial sequencing, microsatellite genotyping, and RADseq for multiple target species. Fieldwork covered 22 localities in Vojvodina and 18 in southern Hungary. Outputs included a joint species occurrence database shared with both national nature protection authorities and a set of management recommendations for maintaining connectivity of meadow habitat patches. Two joint papers were published and one student exchange visit was supported under the project.

projects.title: Moisture-Driven Regulation of Organic Matter Turnover in Oak Forest Floors of the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigated how topographic moisture gradients and interannual precipitation variability regulate rates of litter decomposition and saprotrophic fungal activity in oak-hornbeam forests of Fruška Gora. A network of eight permanent monitoring sites was established spanning xeric ridge-top to mesic valley-bottom positions. Standardised litterbag experiments, ergosterol extraction, and enzyme activity assays were conducted seasonally over three years. The project produced long-term baseline data on decomposition kinetics, fungal biomass dynamics, and enzyme activity profiles, which subsequently contributed to the interannual variability synthesis published in 2014. The project also supported two doctoral students who completed their dissertations within the theme.

Fruška Gora National Park Management Authority

projects.title: Saprotrophic Fungal Succession and Carbon Dynamics on Coarse Woody Debris in Fruška Gora National Park
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project established a cohort of 24 naturally fallen Q. robur logs across three replicate forest plots in Fruška Gora National Park and initiated the ten-year monitoring programme that would later yield the 2015 woody debris publication. Annual measurements of wood density, moisture content, and fruiting body inventories were standardised during this project. The project also conducted a preliminary survey of saprotrophic macrofungal diversity across decay classes and produced an annotated checklist of 89 saprotrophic fungal taxa associated with oak coarse woody debris in the national park, deposited as a technical report with the park authority.

projects.title: Sediment Metal Contamination and Biological Responses in Vojvodina Watercourses
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project mapped metal contamination in surface sediments of twelve watercourses in Vojvodina using sequential chemical extraction and assessed biological responses in sentinel invertebrate species (Gammarus fossarum, Dreissena polymorpha, Chironomus sp.) through antioxidant enzyme activity, lipid peroxidation, and metallothionein quantification. Field campaigns were conducted in spring and autumn across two years. A geo-referenced database of sediment metal concentrations and biomarker data was produced and shared with the Vojvodina Institute for Nature Conservation. Results fed directly into the multi-biomarker index publication and established baseline data for future monitoring programmes.
partners: Vojvodina Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Interactive Effects of Climate-Related Thermal Stress and Metal Contamination on Oxidative Stress in Freshwater Bivalves
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigates how projected increases in river water temperature modify the toxicokinetics and biochemical effects of cadmium and copper in two native freshwater mussel species, Unio crassus and Anodonta anatina. Controlled mesocosm experiments at the University of Novi Sad are combined with field sampling at thermally altered river reaches downstream of cooling water discharges. The work integrates enzyme activity assays, transcriptomic profiling (RNA-seq), and metal accumulation measurements. The Novi Sad team is responsible for field sampling logistics, enzyme biochemistry, and RT-qPCR validation. A collaborative modelling component is led by a partner institution in Budapest.

projects.title: Population differentiation and adaptive potential in common carp under oxygen stress in floodplain lakes of the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the degree to which differences in hypoxia tolerance among common carp populations from Vojvodina floodplain lakes reflect local adaptation versus phenotypic plasticity. Activities included reciprocal transplant experiments, common garden rearing of F1 offspring, population genomics using RADseq on 280 individuals from 10 lake populations, and a comparative transcriptomics component. A standardised respirometry protocol for wild-caught cyprinids was developed and disseminated. The project produced five peer-reviewed publications and trained two PhD students. Field sampling was coordinated with the Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province. Results are being used to inform recommendations for carp stock management in state-owned fishing lakes in the region.

projects.title: Pollen Monitoring and Allergy Risk Mapping in Urban Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project establishes a coordinated aerobiological monitoring network of five Burkard trap stations across northern Vojvodina, targeting allergenic wind-pollinated taxa including grasses, birch-family trees, and Artemisia. Data from weekly tape readings are compiled into a regional pollen database and linked with meteorological records to develop simple concentration-forecast models. A companion component involves morphometric verification of ambiguous pollen types identified in field samples against a reference slide collection assembled within the project. Tihomir Mamužić is responsible for trap maintenance at the Novi Sad urban station, microscopy counts, and morphometric data entry. The project produces quarterly public pollen bulletins shared with the Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina.

projects.title: Konektivnost i diverzitet: metacomunity dinamika zooplanktona izolovanim slatinskim vlažnim staništima Panonske nizije
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje faktore koji određuju distribuciju i diverzitet zooplanktona u mrežama izolovanh slatinskih jezera u Vojvodini, s posebnim osvrtom na ulogu konektivnosti staništa i uticaj promena u korišćenju zemljišta. Szegedi Tudományegyetem, Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Transboundary assessment of Pannonian wetland biodiversity for evidence-based conservation planning
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANWET brings together research institutions from Serbia and Hungary to produce a harmonised biodiversity dataset for Pannonian sodic wetlands across the two countries. Outputs include a shared geodatabase, a joint monitoring protocol proposed to national environmental agencies, and a series of public information materials aimed at local agricultural stakeholders.

projects.title: Lichen-Based Biomonitoring Network for Heavy Metal Deposition Across Industrial Gradients in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: LICHENGRAD aims to establish a systematic biomonitoring network using native lichen species across Vojvodina, focusing on areas influenced by industrial activities including processing facilities, power plants, and urban traffic corridors. The outputs will include a publicly accessible dataset and recommendations for integrating lichen biomonitoring into regional air quality assessments.

projects.title: Pannonian Basin Palaeoclimate from Terrestrial Archives: Integrating Loess and Speleothem Records over the Last 350,000 Years

projects.summary: PANNPAST aimed to produce a spatially consistent Quaternary palaeoclimate reconstruction for the Pannonian Basin by integrating loess-palaeosol sequences and speleothem records from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. projects.summary: LOSSCROSS examined loess exposures on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border to establish stratigraphic correlation, assess geomorphic stability, and evaluate selected sites for geoheritage status. Ninkov was responsible for grain-size analysis and contributed to the joint stratigraphic correlation report submitted to the respective national nature protection agencies. projects.title: Depopulation and Land Abandonment Dynamics in the Serbian–Hungarian Border Zone: Monitoring, Modelling and Policy Implications

projects.summary: A two-year project funded by the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research of Vojvodina, focused on constructing a parcel-level longitudinal dataset of land use change in 60 selected settlements using cadastral records, CORINE data, and drone imagery. projects.title: Thermal Comfort Monitoring and Mapping in Vojvodina Urban Centres

projects.summary: The project established a coordinated microclimate measurement network across five cities in Vojvodina (Novi Sad, Subotica, Zrenjanin, Sombor, Vršac), deploying fixed monitoring stations and conducting seasonal mobile traverse campaigns. projects.title: Heat Stress and Urban Green Infrastructure in Pannonian Cities: Cross-Border Assessment and Planning Tools
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANONHEAT is a cross-border cooperation project involving research institutions and municipalities in Serbia and Hungary. It assesses the cooling effectiveness of urban green infrastructure (parks, street trees, green roofs, constructed wetlands) in reducing outdoor thermal stress in seven cities straddling the Hungarian–Serbian border. Tamara Lekić leads the work package responsible for field measurement campaigns, ENVI-met simulation of green infrastructure scenarios, and production of city-level thermal comfort planning guidelines. The project develops a web-based decision support tool allowing municipal planners to compare projected UTCI outcomes under different green infrastructure investment scenarios. Results are being disseminated through municipal planning workshops in all seven partner cities.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences, Hungary
Municipality of Subotica
Municipality of Baja, Hungary
