projects.title: Vernacular Architecture Heritage Trails in the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: VERNPATH aimed to develop a joint cross-border heritage trail linking surviving vernacular architecture complexes in Bács-Kiskun County (Hungary) and the northern Vojvodina settlements. Tošić led the work package responsible for site inventory, condition assessment, and interpretation content development on the Serbian side. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) printed trail guide, a set of 24 interpretation panels installed at 12 sites, and a shared digital database of 156 documented structures. A final conference in Subotica in 2022 presented the trail to local tourism stakeholders. Partner organisations on the Hungarian side conducted parallel inventories and managed the trail infrastructure in their territory.
partners: Municipality of Baja, Hungary
Subotica Tourism Organisation
Regional Development Agency Bács-Kiskun, Hungary
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Systematic Documentation and Heritage Register Preparation for Vernacular Architecture in Fruška Gora Foothill Settlements
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: FRUHERITAGE funded the first comprehensive, photogrammetry-assisted documentation campaign covering all surviving earthen-wall and timber vernacular structures in the administrative territories of four municipalities with Fruška Gora foothill settlements: Irig, Beočin, Sremski Karlovci, and Petrovaradin. The project produced condition assessments for 389 individual buildings, 3D models for 42 priority structures, and a draft heritage register submitted to the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments of Vojvodina. A geodatabase compatible with open GIS platforms was prepared and made publicly accessible. The project employed two doctoral researchers and three student assistants, and included a public exhibition held in Novi Sad in October 2024.
partners: Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Municipality of Irig
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Planform Dynamics and Sediment Connectivity of Regulated Reaches in the Middle Danube Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANPLAN examined how nineteenth-century channelisation and twentieth-century gravel extraction have altered sediment connectivity and channel planform along shared Hungarian–Serbian reaches of the Danube and Tisa. The Serbian team led by Milić was responsible for historical channel reconstruction using archival cartographic sources and for field sediment budget surveys on two embanked Danube sub-reaches. Results were integrated with hydrodynamic modelling carried out by the Hungarian partner to produce management recommendations for embankment maintenance authorities. Project outputs included a geodatabase of channel change indicators accessible to water management agencies in both countries and a joint scientific paper submitted to an international peer-reviewed journal.
partners: Department of Physical Geography, University of Szeged, Hungary
Hungarian Institute for Water Management, Budapest
Public Water Management Company Vode Vojvodine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Tracing Post-Regulation Fluvial Adjustment in the Sava–Danube Confluence Zone Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FLOWTRACE investigates how the Sava River confluence zone with the Danube has morphologically adjusted since large-scale embankment and channelisation works completed in the early twentieth century. The project combines multitemporal satellite imagery analysis (Landsat 1972–2024, Sentinel-2 2017–2024) with UAV-based topographic surveys of exposed bar forms and dendrogeomorphological analysis of bank trees to establish a consistent record of lateral mobility and bar development. A particular focus is placed on how river training structures at the confluence constrain sediment exchange between the two rivers. The project is coordinated from the University of Novi Sad and involves two collaborating institutions in Serbia and one in Croatia.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad
Geographical Institute Jovan Cvijić SASA, Belgrade
Faculty of Geodesy, University of Zagreb, Croatia

projects.title: Cross-Border Cycling Corridor Linkage for Rural Revitalisation in the Hungary–Serbia Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CYCLELINK connected three existing cycling route fragments on the Hungarian side with two underdeveloped segments on the Serbian side to form a continuous 210 km transboundary corridor. The project involved route surveying, signage harmonisation, production of bilingual printed and digital maps, and a joint marketing campaign. Vukica Erić led the work package on route assessment and visitor monitoring, coordinating field surveys at ten counting stations and producing the project's baseline and final visitor flow reports. The project also funded small infrastructure improvements at four rest points and trained twelve local guides in both countries. An operational maintenance agreement between four municipalities was signed at project closure.
partners: Subotica Tourism Organisation, Serbia
Baja County Rural Development Agency, Hungary
EuroVelo Regional Coordination Office Belgrade (fictional)
Municipal Assembly of Bačka Topola, Serbia

projects.title: Slow Tourism Networks as Drivers of Economic Resilience in Pannonian Peripheral Municipalities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PANSLOWNET investigates the conditions under which slow tourism networks generate measurable economic resilience in rural municipalities of the Pannonian zone with populations below 5,000. The project applies a mixed-methods longitudinal design across twelve case municipalities in Serbia, combining annual economic indicator tracking with periodic qualitative fieldwork. Key outputs include a typology of slow tourism network configurations, an open-access dataset of route usage and local spending, and a policy brief series targeted at provincial and national government bodies. The project employs one junior researcher and supports two doctoral students. Collaboration with the Institute for Spatial Planning of Vojvodina provides access to official land use and demographic datasets.
partners: Institute for Spatial Planning of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Ruralis Research Institute, Trondheim, Norway

projects.title: Rural Accommodation Quality Benchmarking for Vojvodina: Instruments, Norms, and Operator Capacity Building
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to create a standardised quality benchmarking framework for licensed rural accommodation in Vojvodina province. Activities included the revision and further validation of the RGS-19 instrument with a province-wide sample, establishment of regional norm scores by accommodation category, and a series of eight practical workshops delivered to rural accommodation operators across four Vojvodina districts. The project produced a freely downloadable self-assessment workbook (in Serbian and Hungarian), a training manual for local tourism organisations, and a recommendation report submitted to the Vojvodina Secretariat for Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management. A database of benchmark scores from 74 participating properties was maintained and made available to future research.
partners: Vojvodina Rural Tourism Association 'Salaš i Kućica', Novi Sad
Centre for Sustainable Rural Development, Sombor
Faculty of Economics, Subotica, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Rural Tourism Quality Assessment and Joint Labelling in the Serbia–Hungary Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANQUAL brought together researchers and tourism development agencies from the Hungarian counties of Csongrád-Csanád and Bács-Kiskun with counterparts from the Vojvodina region of Serbia to develop a harmonised cross-border quality label for rural guesthouses. Puzović led the work package on measurement instrument harmonisation and guest survey data collection, coordinating parallel surveys in both countries across two seasons. The project produced a joint quality assessment checklist, a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) operator self-assessment guide, and a pilot labelling scheme tested at 34 properties. Findings on cross-border guest preferences informed the design of label criteria. The project concluded with a joint conference in Szeged presenting the labelling framework to regional tourism policy makers.
partners: South-Pannonia Regional Tourism Development Agency, Pécs, Hungary
Csongrád-Csanád County Tourism Association, Szeged, Hungary
Centre for Sustainable Rural Development, Sombor
Department of Economic and Social Geography, University of Debrecen, Hungary

projects.title: Trilateral Participatory Assessment of Cross-Border Tourism Carrying Capacity in the DKMT Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRIPACT brought together academic partners and regional tourism organisations from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania to develop a harmonised methodology for assessing tourism carrying capacity at shared natural and cultural heritage sites along the tri-border zone. The project conducted on-site visitor counts at eleven agreed heritage sites, administered satisfaction and crowding perception surveys to approximately 2,400 visitors, and produced a joint carrying capacity assessment guide published in Serbian, Hungarian, and Romanian. Zarić coordinated the Serbian research team, led fieldwork design, and authored the comparative synthesis report. Project outputs were disseminated to provincial tourism authorities and municipal development offices in all three countries.
partners: Faculty of Natural Sciences and Informatics, University of Szeged, Hungary
Faculty of Geography, West University of Timișoara, Romania
Tourism Organisation of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Csongrád County Tourism Agency, Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Border Region Identities and Development Trajectories in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: BORDID investigates how regional identity narratives in Serbian border zones relate to differential development trajectories, examining the Serbia–Hungary, Serbia–Romania, and Serbia–Croatia border strips through a comparative mixed-methods design. The project team has conducted three waves of survey data collection (2022, 2023, 2024) in 24 border municipalities, totalling approximately 1,800 questionnaire responses, and has produced qualitative interview archives with local officials, civil society leaders, and educators. The project tests whether higher cross-border institutional integration—as measured by Euroregion participation and Interreg project activity—correlates with stronger transnational identity orientation at the municipal level. Findings are being disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and policy briefs directed at the Serbian Ministry of European Integration.
partners: Department of Sociology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Social Sciences, Belgrade
Centre for Regional Studies, Hungarian Academy of Sciences, Pécs

projects.title: Tracking Aeolian Sand Dynamics in the Pannonian Basin Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project constructed a unified multi-temporal geodatabase of aeolian landform change for three Serbian sand fields (Deliblato, Bačka, Subotičko-Horgoška Peščara) using archival aerial photographs from 1953–2000 and satellite imagery from 2000–2023. Activities included standardised photogrammetric processing of analogue photograph archives, development of a reproducible classification scheme applicable across all three sites, field validation campaigns, and computation of a wind erosion sensitivity index under historical and projected climate conditions. The project produced three peer-reviewed publications and an open-access geospatial database deposited with the National Repository of Serbia. Two PhD students were partially funded through the project budget.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province, Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Nature Protection, Novi Sad

projects.title: Comparative Dune Stabilisation Histories of the Central Pannonian Sand Fields: Hungary, Serbia, and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project assembled a regionally consistent archive of aerial photographs and satellite imagery for six sand field areas straddling the Hungary–Serbia border and compared stabilisation trajectories, vegetation composition, and current erosion sensitivity. Dijana Kovač led the work package on remote sensing methodology and coordinated the production of comparable land-cover maps for each national sub-area. Joint field campaigns were organised in both countries to calibrate the classification schemes. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) atlas of Pannonian sand landscapes and a set of recommendations for transboundary nature reserve management, submitted to the relevant ministries of both countries.
partners: Department of Physical Geography, University of Pécs
Kiskunság National Park Directorate, Kecskemét
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Public Enterprise Vojvodinašume, Petrovaradin

projects.title: Food-Based Destination Identity in Spa Tourism Corridors of the Central Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined how spa tourism destinations in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina construct and communicate destination identity through locally sourced food, addressing a gap in both academic literature and practical destination management. Research tasks included stakeholder surveys across eight municipalities, GIS mapping of food supply chains, and a comparative analysis of destination branding documents. The project produced three peer-reviewed papers, a policy brief distributed to the National Tourism Organisation of Serbia, and a training workshop for destination managers held in Vrnjačka Banja in November 2022. Total funding was approximately 3.8 million Serbian dinars over 30 months.
partners: Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Banja Luka, Bosnia-Herzegovina
Regional Development Agency Zlatibor District

projects.title: Cross-Border Spa and Bath Tourism: Sharing Heritage, Building Sustainable Visitor Economies
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSBATH is a broader collaborative project coordinated by the Babeș-Bolyai University Tourism Faculty focusing on heritage documentation and sustainable visitor management in spa towns straddling the Serbia–Romania border region. Milica Đukić leads the work package on gastronomic heritage inventory and cross-border food tourism product development, responsible for field data collection in four Serbian municipalities and co-production of a joint culinary heritage map published in print and digital formats. The work package also oversees a small grant scheme for local producers wishing to develop tourism-oriented product packaging.
partners: Faculty of Geography, Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Tourism Organisation of Banja Koviljača
Timișoara Metropolitan Area Association, Romania
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Phenological Observation Network for Cereal Crops in Vojvodina: Harmonisation and Model Validation
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project established a coordinated phenological observation protocol at five experimental stations across Vojvodina, replacing the previously inconsistent station-level methods with a single BBCH-based protocol. Retrospective harmonisation of records back to 2005 was carried out by cross-referencing historical field notebooks with available meteorological data. A shared database of over 4 000 stage-date records for winter wheat and maize was assembled and made accessible to partner institutions. The harmonised dataset was used to validate and re-calibrate degree-day models for the main cultivars in use. Training workshops for station technicians were delivered at Rimski Šančevi and Sombor experimental stations. The database infrastructure is maintained by the Faculty of Agriculture.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Provincial Hydrometeorological Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Subotica

projects.title: Climate-Adaptive Phenology Modelling for Cereal Crops Across the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBECROPS brings together six institutions from Serbia and Hungary to improve phenology model parameterisation for winter wheat and maize under the warming trend observed in the Pannonian Basin. Stojanović leads Work Package 2, responsible for field data collection and controlled-environment experiments on cardinal temperature calibration. The project will produce a jointly maintained parameter library for 24 cultivars used on both sides of the border, along with a simple web tool for growers to estimate crop developmental stages from local weather data. The project also includes a training component for agricultural advisory services in both countries. Expected outputs include at least four peer-reviewed papers and the public release of all experimental datasets.

projects.title: Seedbank Feedback Modelling for Decision Support in Sunflower–Soybean Rotations in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ROTSEED developed and validated a seedbank feedback model to support weed management decision-making in sunflower–soybean rotations across Vojvodina and adjacent areas of Hungary and Croatia. The project combined four years of field seedbank monitoring data from twelve sites with species-specific seed survival and fecundity parameters to parameterise a population dynamics model. The model was implemented as a user-accessible spreadsheet tool calibrated for the 12 most prevalent weed species in the region. Field validation in the final year showed predictions within ±15% of observed seedbank density for eight of twelve species. The project involved collaboration with University of Debrecen and the Faculty of Agriculture in Osijek.
partners: University of Debrecen, Faculty of Agriculture, Hungary
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Osijek, Croatia
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Monitoring and Management of Emerging and Invasive Weed Species in Arable Systems of the Pannonian Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANNWEEDS addresses the accelerating spread of invasive and range-expanding weed species, including Amaranthus tuberculatus, Conyza canadensis, and Iva xanthiifolia, across the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border agricultural zone. Fehér leads the work package on competitive dynamics and threshold determination for newly established weed populations. The project runs coordinated annual field surveys on both sides of the border, collects herbicide sensitivity data, and develops multilingual advisory materials for extension services. The Serbian component is centred on Vojvodina fields with documented first occurrences since 2018. An online occurrence map updated with georeferenced survey data is maintained jointly by the two lead institutions.
partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Science and Informatics, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Novi Sad, Serbia
Csongrád-Csanád County Agricultural Chamber, Hungary

projects.title: Genetic and Biochemical Determinants of Post-Anthesis Nitrogen Remobilisation Efficiency in Maize under Low-Input Conditions in South-East Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to identify the molecular and genetic basis of variation in nitrogen remobilisation efficiency across a panel of maize genotypes adapted to Vojvodina conditions. Work included GWAS on a 214-accession panel, transcriptome profiling of near-isogenic lines contrasting at a key QTL, and functional characterisation of candidate GS1 paralogues. Field phenotyping was conducted at Rimski Šančevi and two partner locations under two nitrogen rates over three seasons. The project produced the GWAS dataset published in Plant Genome (2022) and generated CRISPR lines subsequently used in the ZmGS1-5 study. Total budget was approximately 42 million RSD.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Maize Research Institute Zemun Polje, Belgrade

projects.title: Nitrogen Use Efficiency in Grain Maize Along the Danube Corridor: Genetic Resources, Agronomy, and Environmental Indicators
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian partners focused on shared evaluation of maize germplasm for NUE under comparable climatic and soil conditions in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. Žarković led the work package on physiological and biochemical characterisation of nitrogen remobilisation, coordinating joint 15N labelling experiments at Rimski Šančevi and Szarvas. Other work packages covered soil nitrogen dynamics, remote sensing, and economic analysis of reduced-input scenarios. A joint germplasm database of 280 evaluated accessions was developed and made available to both national breeding programmes. Total project budget was approximately €1.1 million.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Agricultural Research Institute, Szarvas, Hungary
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat Experimental Farm, Novi Sad

projects.title: Seed priming protocols for low-temperature vegetable production in the pannonian climate zone
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of regionally calibrated seed priming protocols for the continental climate of Vojvodina, where early spring vegetable sowing frequently encounters soil temperatures of 6–12 °C. Research teams from the Faculty of Agriculture Novi Sad and the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops evaluated hydropriming, osmopriming, and solid matrix priming across seven vegetable species — pepper, tomato, carrot, onion, leek, spinach, and cucumber — over two growing seasons. The main outputs were species-specific priming parameter tables (agent, concentration, duration, temperature, drying protocol) validated under both controlled-environment and field conditions. A short practical guide for producers was published in Serbian and distributed through the agricultural extension service of Vojvodina.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-border harmonisation of vegetable seed vigour testing and priming standards in the Danube region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SEEDLINK brings together seed science teams from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania to harmonise laboratory vigour testing protocols and on-farm priming recommendations for five key vegetable crops. The University of Novi Sad team leads Work Package 3, which focuses on priming optimisation under temperature stress conditions representative of the participating regions. Activities include inter-laboratory ring tests of germination protocols, joint field trials at three sites in each country, and the development of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) practitioner decision tool for selecting priming strategy based on sowing date, target temperature, and available equipment. The project includes a short-stay researcher exchange programme involving two PhD students from Novi Sad.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Kecskemét campus, Hungary
University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Seed Association of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
National Agricultural Research and Innovation Centre, Gödöllő, Hungary

projects.title: Population structure and dispersal pathways of soilborne oomycetes in Pannonian vegetable production systems
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project maps genetic diversity of key Phytophthora and Pythium species across the Pannonian region using microsatellite and SNP-based approaches, with the aim of identifying dispersal routes and estimating the relative contributions of seed trade, irrigation water, and machinery movement to pathogen spread. Sampling is coordinated across Vojvodina, covering six crop species and 80 locations over three seasons. Milan Fejsa is responsible for DNA extraction, microsatellite genotyping, and fragment-analysis data processing. Results are being integrated into a georeferenced database intended for use by regional extension services and seed producers.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Plant Protection Institute, Centre for Agricultural Research, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Cover Crop Mixtures as Drivers of Nitrogen Flow Efficiency in Pannonian Arable Systems
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: COVERFLOW established a network of 12 paired field trial sites across Vojvodina and southern Hungary to measure nitrogen mineralisation dynamics from a standardised set of cover crop mixtures on chernozem and calcareous chernozem soils. The project combined incubation subplots with on-farm demonstration trials and developed a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) advisory leaflet and a simple spreadsheet tool for farmers to select cover crop mixture composition and termination date based on their target cash crop and local soil type. Three workshops for extension advisers were held in Novi Sad, Subotica and Pécs. The project also produced a shared soil enzyme activity dataset that fed into the multi-site calibration study published in 2025.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Georgikon Faculty, University of Pannonia, Keszthely
Agricultural Advisory Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
County Agricultural Chamber of Somogy, Kaposvár

projects.title: Biological Indicators for Cover Crop Performance Assessment in Arable Rotations of Northern Serbia
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: BIOCROP-NS funds the development and validation of a set of biological indicators—soil enzyme activities, microbial biomass carbon, earthworm abundance indices and AMF colonisation rates—that can be used to assess whether cover crop management is delivering intended biological soil improvements. The project runs parallel sampling campaigns at the Rimski Šančevi long-term trial and at six commercial farms across Vojvodina. A key deliverable is a diagnostic protocol, tested with non-specialist technicians, for annual monitoring of cover crop biological effects, intended for uptake by the agricultural advisory network in the province. Student internships and two PhD student positions are embedded in the project.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of the City of Novi Sad

projects.title: Pollen Biology and Fertilisation Efficiency in Hybrid Vegetable Seed Production Under Changing Vojvodina Climatic Conditions
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project addressed how increasing frequency of summer heat episodes in Vojvodina affects pollen viability, stigma receptivity windows, and ultimately seed set and purity in commercial pepper and tomato hybrid seed production. Field trials at two locations (Rimski Šančevi and Bečej) were combined with controlled-environment chamber experiments to disentangle temperature and humidity effects. An image-analysis scoring protocol for pollen viability was developed and validated. Practical outputs included revised pollination timing recommendations for seed producers and threshold pollen viability values below which roguing of parental lines should be triggered. The project supported one PhD student and produced four journal publications.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer for Sustainable Hybrid Vegetable Seed Production in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project involving seed technology groups at the University of Novi Sad and the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences (MATE), Kecskemét Campus. The Serbian team led the work package on reproductive biology quality indicators, standardising assessment protocols for pollen viability and stigma receptivity that can be adopted by small and medium seed enterprises on both sides of the border. Joint field trials were established in Subotica and Kiskunhalas comparing open-field and tunnel-protected hybrid pepper seed production systems. Training workshops for seed company technicians were organised in both countries. The project also established a shared reference pollen collection for calibration purposes.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Kecskemét Campus
Regional Development Agency Subotica
Agro-Seed Kft., Kiskunhalas

projects.title: Physiological Basis of Drought Tolerance in Sunflower: Linking Root Architecture to Canopy Water Status and Yield Stability in the Vojvodina Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates the mechanistic links between root depth, osmotic adjustment, and yield stability in sunflower genotypes grown under rain-fed conditions in Vojvodina. Field and pot experiments at Rimski Šančevi are used to characterise root architecture with destructive core sampling and WinRHIZO scanning, while leaf-level water relations are measured with pressure-chamber and osmometer methods. Canopy temperature infrared measurements supplement gas exchange data. The project covers twelve commercial and pre-commercial genotypes across two contrasting drought years. Ilić is responsible for field phenotyping, root sampling logistics, and data analysis of water potential dynamics. Outputs are intended to provide practical screening criteria for regional sunflower breeding and advisory services.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Rotation Effects Under Changing Climate: Decomposing Long-Term Yield Records from Multi-Site Experiments in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ROTACLIM assembled multi-decade yield datasets from four experimental stations across the Pannonian Basin — two in Serbia and one each in Hungary and Romania — to perform cross-site rotation effect decomposition. The project standardised historical input and climate covariate series, developed a shared data schema, and applied hierarchical Bayesian mixed models to estimate site-specific and pooled rotation effect sizes. Climate reanalysis data from E-OBS and CHESS-TERA were spatially matched to each station. The project produced a publicly archived dataset of 18 harmonised rotation series, quantified how the rotation yield advantage has changed over successive decades, and assessed whether the advantage narrows or widens under warmer and drier growing seasons. A guidance document for experimental station managers on metadata collection was also produced.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Institute of Crop Production, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine, Cluj-Napoca

projects.title: Long-Term Experiment Network of South-East Europe: Data Rescue, Harmonisation, and Open Access Provision
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: LTESEE addressed the fragmented and at-risk state of long-term agricultural experiment records in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The project digitised paper farm-book archives at three stations, developed a bilingual metadata portal, and trained station staff in data management protocols. Sara Starčević led the work package responsible for rotation experiment data harmonisation, defining common variable taxonomies and quality-control procedures. Digitised datasets covering soil, yield, and management variables were transferred to a shared repository. The project also produced an atlas of active and discontinued long-term experiments in the region and held two cross-border stakeholder workshops attended by agricultural extension services and research institutes.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Research Centre for Agricultural and Food Sciences, Martonvásár
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Novi Sad

projects.title: Pollination service delivery across agricultural landscape gradients in the Pannonian basin: linking bee community structure to crop yield outcomes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project quantified wild bee diversity and pollination service delivery at 40 farms across a gradient of landscape heterogeneity in Vojvodina, linking bee community data to crop yield outcomes in sunflower and oilseed rape using standardised field protocols. Field campaigns were conducted in 2021, 2022, and 2023. The project produced a landscape-scale assessment of where pollination service gaps are greatest in the intensively farmed Pannonian Plain and tested whether Sentinel-2-derived land cover metrics could replace manual mapping for scalable monitoring. Training materials and a decision guide for agronomists were produced as extension outputs. Four peer-reviewed publications resulted from the project, along with an open dataset deposited in the PANGAEA repository.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Optimising flower strip composition for pollinator support in cereal and oilseed agroecosystems of Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral applied research project testing the performance of eight flower strip seed mixtures at replicated sites in Vojvodina (Serbia) and Csongrád-Csanád County (Hungary). The project evaluates wild bee attraction, establishment success, cost of maintenance, and compatibility with standard farm operations. Vera Perišić leads the pollinator monitoring work package, coordinating standardised weekly pan-trap and transect protocols at all Serbian sites and overseeing joint data harmonisation with the Hungarian partner team. Results feed into a jointly developed practical handbook for farmers seeking to establish pollinator habitat within arable landscapes in the cross-border region, to be disseminated through agricultural extension networks on both sides of the border.
partners: Department of Field and Vegetable Crops, University of Novi Sad
Research Station for Plant Protection, Szeged, Hungary
Regional Agricultural Advisory Centre, Subotica

projects.title: Resistance Mapping and Mechanism Characterisation in Dominant Arable Weeds of the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce the first systematic molecular resistance map for A. retroflexus and C. album across the major crop production zones of Vojvodina. Biotype collections were made in three annual sampling rounds from maize, sunflower, and soybean fields. Collected plants were characterised using whole-plant bioassays, target-site sequencing, CYP and GST activity profiling, and RT-qPCR. A georeferenced database of resistance mechanism frequencies was developed and shared with the Plant Protection Directorate of Serbia. The project also funded purchase of the laboratory's current real-time PCR platform and supported two PhD students co-supervised by Ranković. Results fed directly into several of the peer-reviewed publications listed in his profile.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Novi Sad
Plant Protection Directorate of the Republic of Serbia, Belgrade

projects.title: Coordinated Herbicide Resistance Surveillance in the Pannonian Agroecosystem: Serbia, Hungary, Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: WEEDPAN is a trilateral surveillance project designed to detect new resistance cases and track the spread of resistance alleles across national borders in the Pannonian Plain. Ranković leads the work package on biochemical and molecular mechanism characterisation, while Hungarian and Romanian partners lead the field collection and geographic information system components respectively. Standardised sampling protocols were developed jointly to ensure cross-country comparability of bioassay results. The project includes a short-course training programme for national plant protection inspectors and plans a shared online database of confirmed resistance cases accessible to advisory services. First-year data covering 210 field samples from Serbia are currently being processed.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő, Hungary
University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Microclimate-Informed Strip Design for Reduced Fungicide Use in Vegetable Intercrops
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish quantitative relationships between intercropping strip geometry and canopy microclimate variables—radiation interception, relative humidity, and leaf wetness duration—and to express these relationships as operational decision rules for fungicide timing. Field experiments were conducted at three sites in Vojvodina using standardised sensor networks and a panel of vegetable intercrop combinations. A web-accessible decision support tool was developed and pilot-tested with five cooperating farms. The project produced eight peer-reviewed publications and trained two doctoral students. The decision tool integrates strip geometry inputs with real-time weather station data to generate daily spray-timing advice.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Belgrade
Provincial Institute for Plant Protection, Novi Sad

projects.title: Living Mulch Practices for Climate-Adapted Cross-Border Vegetable Production
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project comparing living mulch systems for vegetable production on both sides of the Vojvodina–southern Hungary border. Struhár led the work package on microclimate and disease monitoring, responsible for deploying and maintaining sensor networks at two Serbian trial sites (Rimski Šančevi and Bačka Topola) and for harmonising data collection protocols with the Hungarian partner. The project produced a joint grower handbook in Serbian and Hungarian summarising practical mulch species selection, mowing management, and associated disease risk by crop type. Four field demonstration days were organised with an attendance of approximately 140 farmers.
partners: Kaposvár University, Faculty of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
Agricultural Extension Service of South Bačka District
Chamber of Agriculture of Vojvodina

projects.title: Monitoring and Modelling of Insecticide Resistance Allele Dynamics in Aphid Pests of Oilseed Crops in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je usmeren na uspostavljanje zajedničke mreže za praćenje rezistentnosti lisnih vaši na insekticide u uzajamno povezanim agroekosistemima Mađarske i Srbije. U okviru srpskog dela projekta realizuje se godišnje uzorkovanje na 15 lokacija u Vojvodini, molekularna dijagnostika ciljno-mestne i metaboličke rezistentnosti i izrada modela prostorno-vremenskog širenja rezistentnih alela. Mađarski partner obezbeđuje komparativne podatke i kapacitete za genotipizaciju mikrosatelitima. Krajnji ishod je zajednički protokol za procenu rizika i preporuke za ažuriranje šema rotacije insekticida namenjene savetodavnim službama u obe zemlje.
partners: Plant Protection Institute, Centre for Agricultural Research, Budapest
Katedra za zaštitu bilja i životne sredine, Poljoprivredni fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Pokrajinski zavod za zaštitu bilja, Novi Sad

projects.title: Dinamika alela rezistentnosti na insekticide kod ekonomski štetnih vrsta lisnih vaši u usevu uljane repice i suncokreta u Vojvodini
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat finansira Pokrajinski sekretarijat za visoko obrazovanje i naučnoistraživačku delatnost AP Vojvodine. Cilj je utvrđivanje aktuelnih frekventnosti alela kdr, MACE i metaboličke rezistentnosti (esteraze, P450) kod Myzus persicae, Brevicoryne brassicae i Lipaphis erysimi u Vojvodini, kao i identifikacija pedoklimatskih i agronomskih faktora koji modulišu razvoj rezistentnosti. Projekat uključuje terensko uzorkovanje, standardizovane bioeseje i real-time PCR analize. Planirano je objavljivanje serije naučnih radova i izrada smernica za poljoprivredne savetnike na teritoriji AP Vojvodine.
partners: Poljoprivredni fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Institut za pesticide i zaštitu životne sredine, Beograd

projects.title: Rotation Design for Yield Stability of Oilseed and Protein Crops in the Pannonian Lowland Under Variable Climate
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to quantify how rotation sequence length, preceding crop identity, and tillage intensity jointly influence yield stability of soybean and sunflower across a network of seven experimental and commercial field sites in Vojvodina. Multi-environment trial data collected over four growing seasons were combined with soil physical and chemical measurements and weather records to parameterise stability models and develop decision rules for rotation planning. A particular focus was placed on years with spring drought, which increasingly stress germination and early crop development. The project produced calibrated DSSAT model scenarios and practitioner-oriented rotation planning guidelines disseminated through extension workshops and a publicly available data repository hosted at the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Plant Protection, Novi Sad
Agricultural Advisory Service of Vojvodina

projects.title: Conservation Tillage and Cover Crops for Sustainable Soybean Production in Hungary and Serbia
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed the adoption barriers for conservation tillage and cover cropping systems among soybean producers in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Ana Radulović led the work package on field experimentation and agronomic assessment, which included replicated strip-till and roller-crimper trials at two Serbian sites and coordinated data collection with partner institutions in Hungary. The project also included stakeholder surveys of 120 farms and a series of joint farmer field days. Outputs included a bilingual technical guide on cover crop selection and management for soybean systems, distributed to 340 farms on both sides of the border, and a publicly accessible dataset of three-year trial results deposited with the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, University of Pécs
Regional Development Agency of South Pannonia, Pécs
Agricultural Extension Centre Subotica

projects.title: Chemical Ecology of Ragweed in Vojvodinian Agroecosystems: Secondary Metabolite Variation and Phytotoxic Impact
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigated spatial and temporal variation in secondary metabolite composition of A. artemisiifolia across Vojvodinian agricultural landscapes and quantified phytotoxic impacts on economically important arable species. Field surveys covered 24 sites across three land-use categories. Laboratory work included HPLC-DAD and GC-MS profiling of phenolic acids and sesquiterpene lactones, and standardised bioassays with eight crop and weed species. The project produced a georeferenced dataset of metabolite concentrations linked to soil and agronomic covariates. A practical output was a decision-support table ranking crop and weed species by sensitivity to ragweed secondary metabolites under Vojvodinian field conditions, disseminated to agricultural advisory services.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Department of Soil Science, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Monitoring and Bioactive Profiling of Invasive Weeds in Pannonian Arable Systems
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian, Hungarian, and Romanian institutions aimed at characterising the distribution, density, and chemical ecology of key invasive weed species—Ambrosia artemisiifolia, Sorghum halepense, and Conyza canadensis—in shared Pannonian arable landscapes. Čolić leads the work package on secondary metabolite profiling and bioactivity testing, coordinating sample exchange protocols and harmonised bioassay methodology among three partner laboratories. The project involves annual field campaigns, shared analytical databases, and joint training workshops for agricultural advisors in both countries. Outcomes include a regional weed-monitoring platform and joint guidelines for ecologically informed weed management.
partners: Faculty of Natural Sciences, University of Pécs
Faculty of Agriculture, Banat University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine, Timișoara
Institute for Plant Protection, Kecskemét Agricultural Research Institute

projects.title: Riparian Buffer Zones as Barriers Against Neonicotinoid Transfer to Freshwater Systems in Pannonian Agricultural Landscapes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RIPAGUARD investigated the effectiveness of riparian buffer zones of varying widths and plant compositions in reducing neonicotinoid transport from seed-treated maize fields to adjacent drainage ditches in Vojvodina. Field experiments combined with laboratory microcosm studies quantified pesticide attenuation rates and identified soil microbial community properties that accelerate dissipation. Ecotoxicological endpoints measured included survival, feeding rates, and enzymatic biomarkers in three locally relevant invertebrate species. The project produced design recommendations for buffer strip widths and management practices tailored to Pannonian soil and hydrological conditions, intended for integration into Serbian agri-environment scheme policy documentation.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Pesticide Pressures on Freshwater Macroinvertebrate Communities in the Hungarian–Serbian Pannonian Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANNOWATER coordinated biological and chemical monitoring across 30 shared agricultural catchments spanning the Hungarian–Serbian border to characterise pesticide pressure on aquatic macroinvertebrates under harmonised EU Water Framework Directive-compatible methods. Jasna Petrović led the ecotoxicological risk assessment work package, which developed a cross-border weight-of-evidence framework and produced joint risk maps for neonicotinoids and triazine herbicides. The project established a shared reference species sensitivity database for Pannonian invertebrate fauna and delivered training workshops for environmental inspectors from both countries. Results informed the first joint transboundary pesticide risk management report for the Tisza sub-basin.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Environmental Sciences, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Directorate of Water Management North–South Bačka, Novi Sad
Körös-Maros National Park Directorate, Szarvas, Hungary

projects.title: Биолошки потенцијал аутохтоних изолата Trichoderma spp. у сузбијању фузаријских трулежи корена и круне паприке и парадајза у условима заштићеног простора
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат је имао за циљ свеобухватну карактеризацију колекције од преко 150 аутохтоних Trichoderma изолата, утврђивање механизама антагонизма, оптимизацију формулације и вишелокацијску евалуацију у комерцијалним стакленичким системима. Спроведени су огледи у контролисаним и пилот условима за одређивање нивоа биолошке ефикасности, термотолеранције и компатибилности са фунгицидима. Развијен је протокол за производњу WP формулације са дефинисаним параметрима стабилности. Пројекат је такође обухватио молекуларне студије индуковане системске резистентности у паприци и парадајзу. Резултати пројекта чине основу за поступак регистрације биофунгицида.
partners: Институт за заштиту биља и животну средину, Београд
Пољопривредни факултет, Универзитет у Крагујевцу

projects.title: Биолошка заштита поврћа у заштићеном простору: размена знања и пренос технологије у прекограничном региону
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Прекогранични пројекат окупио је истраживаче из Србије и Мађарске са циљем хармонизације протокола за одабир биоконтролних агенаса против Fusarium болести корена у производњи паприке и парадајза. У оквиру пројекта организоване су заједничке теренске мисије, размена изолата из националних колекција и упоредне студије ефикасности. Израђен је заједнички приручник за произвођаче у прекограничном региону на српском и мађарском језику. Организоване су три интерактивне радионице за произвођаче поврћа у Войводини и Бач-Кишкун жупанији. Пројекат је допринео формирању заједничке банке изолата доступне оба истраживачка партнера.
partners: Faculty of Horticulture, Hungarian University of Agriculture, Budapest
Регионална пољопривредна станица Суботица

projects.title: Orchard Floor Vegetation as a Reservoir for Phytoseiid Biological Control Agents in Low-Input Apple Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined how different orchard floor plant communities—permanent grass, legume-grass mixtures, and Phacelia intercrop strips—affect resident phytoseiid mite populations and their capacity to suppress Panonychus ulmi in apple orchards of Vojvodina under reduced-acaricide management. Field experiments were conducted at the Rimski Šančevi station and in two commercial orchards. Key activities included seasonal dispersal tracking by trunk sticky-band traps, mesocosm predator-prey ratio studies, and the development of a decision-support spreadsheet tool for growers. The project trained two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. Outcomes were communicated to regional agricultural extension advisors through a series of workshops held in Novi Sad and Sremska Mitrovica.
partners: Vojvodina Institute of Horticulture, Novi Sad
Institute for Plant Protection, Novi Sad
Provincial Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina

projects.title: Biodiversity-Based Pest Consortia in Temperate Fruit Orchards Across the Pannonian and Adriatic Regions
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: BIOCONSORT was a multi-partner Horizon 2020 project coordinated by Hochschule Geisenheim University that assessed the potential of resident natural enemy communities—including phytoseiid mites, coccinellids, and parasitic wasps—to provide economically acceptable pest control in apple and pear orchards across six European countries. The Novi Sad team led Work Package 3, which covered ground cover management effects on mite communities in the Pannonian region. Activities included comparative field trials in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, an inter-laboratory ring test for predator identification methods, and the development of harmonised monitoring protocols. Todorović's group contributed three seasons of field data and co-authored the WP3 synthesis report.
partners: Hochschule Geisenheim University, Germany
University of Pécs, Hungary
Research Station for Fruit Growing Dolj, Romania
Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Greece
INRAE Bordeaux-Nouvelle Aquitaine, France

projects.title: Phytostabilisation Capacity of Native Vegetation Assemblages on Mining-Disturbed Soils in the Vojvodina–Banat Cross-Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project mapped spontaneous vegetation and soil contamination across 18 post-mining and post-industrial sites straddling the Serbia–Hungary border area in the Pannonian Basin. Field campaigns produced a combined dataset of over 600 plant–soil paired samples analysed for Pb, Zn, Cd, Ni, and As. A publicly available database and an online species selection tool for practitioners planning phytostabilisation interventions were developed as main outputs. Training workshops were delivered to municipal environmental officers in both countries. The project also produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) field guide for site assessment. Ivana Ivanović led the Serbian side and coordinated overall project reporting.
partners: Institute of Environmental Engineering, University of Pécs
Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Vojvodina
Regional Development Agency of Southern Transdanubia

projects.title: Rhizosphere Processes Controlling Metal Immobilisation in Spontaneous Plant Communities on Industrial Spoils
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RHIZOMET investigates the mechanisms by which the rhizosphere of metal-tolerant spontaneous plant species immobilises Pb, Zn, and Cd in post-industrial soils. The project combines in situ rhizobox measurements, sequential extraction, organic acid profiling by ion chromatography, and SEM–EDX imaging to characterise spatial and temporal patterns of metal speciation in the rhizosphere. Four target species—Silene vulgaris, Calamagrostis epigejos, Festuca rubra, and Lotus corniculatus—are studied across two contaminated field sites in Vojvodina. Isotope dilution mass spectrometry is applied at one site in collaboration with a partner laboratory to quantify labile metal pools. The project runs until mid-2025 and has so far produced three peer-reviewed articles.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Soil Science, Mendel University in Brno

projects.title: Long-term Effects of Herbicide Use on Soil Microbial Communities in Vojvodina Agroecosystems
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project established long-term monitoring plots at three sites in Vojvodina to track the effect of repeated glyphosate and acetochlor applications on soil microbial community structure using PLFA profiling, enzyme activity assays, and soil residue analysis. The project trained two MSc students in PLFA extraction and GC-FID analysis, standardised the extraction protocol for the Faculty laboratory, and produced a regional reference dataset of PLFA profiles for untreated chernozem and meadow soils. Final deliverables included a monitoring protocol report submitted to the Vojvodina Secretariat for Agriculture and a set of three journal publications.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Comparative Assessment of Herbicide Fate and Soil Biological Indicators across Pannonian Plain Agroecosystems
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaborative project involving partners from the Faculty of Agriculture Novi Sad, the University of Debrecen, and the Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek. The project harmonised soil sampling and herbicide residue analytical protocols across three countries, conducted paired field studies in representative maize-growing regions on both sides of the Serbian–Hungarian border, and assessed glyphosate and acetochlor fate and soil biological indicators using a common methodology. Emilija Mitrović led the work package on soil microbial indicators, coordinating PLFA analysis and data integration across three national partner laboratories. The project produced a shared database of 480 soil samples and co-authored publications in peer-reviewed journals.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad (lead)
University of Debrecen, Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, Hungary
Faculty of Agrobiotechnical Sciences Osijek, Croatia

projects.title: Nitrogen Deposition Gradients and Grassland Flora Conservation in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: NITROGRAD connected research groups in Novi Sad, Szeged, and Pécs to harmonise nitrogen deposition monitoring methods and produce comparable floristic monitoring data on both sides of the Serbia–Hungary border. The project deployed a joint network of 80 ALPHA passive samplers and conducted synchronised plant community surveys in 120 plots across three paired transects. The Serbian work package, led by Puzović, was responsible for site selection, sampler maintenance, floristic survey coordination, and cross-border data integration. Key outputs included a bi-national N deposition database, a joint report on critical load exceedances, and a guidance document for municipal nature protection officers on nitrogen-aware grassland management.
partners: Department of Ecology, University of Szeged
Institute of Biology, University of Pécs
Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning and Environmental Protection, Vojvodina
Körös-Maros National Park Directorate, Szarvas

projects.title: Low-Cost Sensor Infrastructure for Near-Real-Time Atmospheric Nitrogen and Weed Pressure Monitoring in Agricultural Landscapes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENSORWEED investigates whether a network of low-cost electrochemical ammonia sensors, deployed at 20 sites across the Novi Sad agricultural fringe, can generate deposition data at sufficient temporal resolution to predict seasonal peaks in nitrophilous weed emergence. The project combines sensor hardware development (in collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences), quality-controlled data pipelines, and field-validated weed pressure indices derived from monthly floristic assessments. A secondary objective is to develop an open-access web interface for real-time display of deposition-weed pressure indicators, targeting use by agricultural advisory extension services. The project team includes plant ecologists, atmospheric scientists, and a software engineer seconded from NTP Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Silicon as a Tool for Reducing Lodging and Fungicide Inputs in Winter Wheat Production in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to quantify the extent to which soil and foliar silicon amendments can replace or reduce the use of growth regulators and fungicides in intensive winter wheat production on Vojvodina soils. Field experiments are conducted at two locations (Rimski Šančevi and Sremska Mitrovica) across three wheat cultivars representing a range of lodging susceptibilities. The programme combines anatomical and biochemical characterisation of culm tissues with multi-season agronomic performance data. A sub-task analyses economic thresholds for amendment application. Partners include the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops in Novi Sad and the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences in Gödöllő, enabling cross-border validation of results in comparable Pannonian agroecological conditions.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő

projects.title: Micro-CT Methods for Quantitative Crop Anatomy: Standardisation and Application in Cereal Breeding Support
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This short-term provincial project established protocols for routine use of micro-CT scanning in anatomical studies of small-grain cereal culms and spikes. Velimir Obradović led the work package on culm cross-section imaging and parameter extraction. The project produced a standard operating procedure for sample preparation and scan settings, validated against classical histological methods. Training workshops were delivered to four research groups at the University of Novi Sad. The micro-CT infrastructure at the Faculty of Technical Sciences was made accessible to agricultural researchers under a formal inter-faculty agreement brokered through this project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Genetic characterisation and conservation planning for Vojvodina Mangalica pig: from pedigree to genomics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish the first comprehensive genomic database for the Vojvodina Mangalica population by combining SNP array genotyping of 600 registered animals with existing pedigree records spanning 25 years. Objectives included estimation of effective population size using both pedigree and linkage disequilibrium approaches, identification of runs of homozygosity, and development of a minimum-kinship mating algorithm suitable for use by the Vojvodina Mangalica Breeders Association. Đuro Mirković was responsible for the quantitative genetics component, including variance component estimation and breeding value computation. The project produced updated heritability estimates for production and reproduction traits and delivered a practical mating decision tool tested on two pilot farms.
partners: Institute for Animal Husbandry, Belgrade-Zemun
Vojvodina Mangalica Breeders Association, Novi Sad
Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-validation of genetic evaluation methods for small pig populations in the Pannonian region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral applied research project between Serbian and Hungarian institutions focusing on the comparison of pedigree-based BLUP, ssGBLUP, and Bayesian genomic prediction methods applied to reproduction and growth traits in locally adapted pig breeds and their crossbreeds. Đuro Mirković leads the work package on litter size trait analysis, coordinating data sharing between Vojvodina Mangalica × Landrace herds in Serbia and Mangalica × Hungarian Large White herds in southern Hungary. The work package includes joint cross-validation studies, standardisation of phenotyping protocols, and preparation of unified genetic evaluation reports for participating breeding associations. Training workshops for farm recorders were held in both countries.
partners: Institute of Animal Sciences, Hungarian University of Agricultural and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Vojvodina Mangalica Breeders Association, Novi Sad
South-Pannonian Agricultural Research Centre, Kecskemét

projects.title: Rumen Microbiome Responses to Bioethanol Co-products in Young Ruminants: Linking Fermentation Profiles to Growth Outcomes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RURUMIX examined how commercially available corn and wheat DDGS batches sourced from Serbian bioethanol plants affect rumen microbiome composition, fermentation end-products, and growth performance in dairy heifers from weaning to first service. The project combined in vitro fermentation assays, longitudinal in vivo trials at the university farm, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing to build a dataset linking batch sulphur and fibre variability to rumen outcomes. A decision support table for safe DDGS inclusion levels based on batch composition was developed and shared with extension services in Vojvodina. Three journal articles and two conference presentations were produced. The Faculty of Agriculture provided the animal housing, and the Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering in Belgrade contributed sequencing infrastructure.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering, University of Belgrade
Provincial Institute for Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Validated Welfare Scoring Protocols for Commercial Broiler Production in Serbia: Baseline Data and Regional Adaptation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce a validated set of on-farm welfare scoring protocols specifically adapted to the climate, farm structure, and regulatory situation of broiler production in Serbia. Activities included a large-scale cross-sectional survey of 60 farms across Vojvodina and Central Serbia, seasonal welfare assessments, environmental monitoring with dataloggers, and a training programme for farm personnel and veterinary inspectors. The project generated reference datasets for footpad dermatitis, gait scores, and thermal environment metrics stratified by season, house type, and stocking density. A freely distributed scoring manual and assessor training kit were produced as outputs, distributed through the Provincial Veterinary Directorate.
partners: Institute for Animal Husbandry, Zemun-Belgrade
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry of Vojvodina
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Harmonising Broiler Welfare Monitoring Across the Pannonian Region: Serbia, Romania, Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PanBroilWel is a cross-border cooperation project addressing the lack of harmonised welfare monitoring standards for broiler production across the Hungarian-Serbian border region and extending methodology sharing to include Romanian partners. The University of Novi Sad leads the work package on protocol harmonisation and assessor training. Activities include joint field validation trials using a common assessment instrument, shared training workshops for farm advisors and official veterinarians, and the development of a trilingual (Serbian, Hungarian, Romanian) digital scoring app. The project involves six partner organisations across three countries and is scheduled to complete by mid-2026.
partners: Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, University of Debrecen
Faculty of Animal Science, University of Agricultural Sciences Cluj-Napoca
Regional Chamber of Agriculture of South Bačka District
AgriCoop Subotica d.o.o.
Alföldi Baromfi Termelői Szövetség, Hungary

projects.title: Endocrine Disruption from Feed Contaminants in Vojvodina Dairy Herds: Exposure Assessment, Hormonal Outcomes, and Risk Management Tools
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ENDOFEED aimed to quantify the combined estrogenic burden imposed by mycotoxins, phytoestrogens, and pesticide residues in commercial dairy cow diets across Vojvodina and to correlate exposure with measured reproductive hormone outcomes in field populations. The project operated in three phases: a large-scale feed and urine survey (22 farms, 220 animals); controlled feeding trials in the University experimental herd to establish dose-response relationships; and development of a farm-level cumulative estrogenic burden scoring model. The project employed LC-MS/MS, ELISA, and reporter gene bioassays. The final deliverable—a practical spreadsheet tool for veterinary practitioners—was disseminated through the Provincial Veterinary Association of Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Institute of Pesticides and Environmental Protection, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Surveillance of Feed Mycotoxin Contamination and Animal Health Impacts in the Pannonian Agricultural Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TOXBRIDGE was a cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian agricultural research institutions focused on harmonising mycotoxin monitoring methodology and establishing a shared database of feed contamination records and associated livestock health indicators. Bajić led the work package covering reproductive and endocrine biomarker collection on the Serbian side, coordinating sampling on 14 farms in Vojvodina and contributing to a joint LC-MS/MS ring-trial to verify inter-laboratory comparability. The project produced a bilingual farmer advisory booklet on silage management practices to reduce Fusarium contamination risk, distributed to approximately 600 farms through agricultural extension services in both countries.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences, Hungarian University of Agriculture, Gödöllő
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Vojvodina
Hajdú-Bihar County Farmers' Association, Debrecen

projects.title: Optimising Extrusion Parameters for Sustainable Cyprinid and Siluriform Aquaculture Feed Production in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project brought together researchers and feed producers from Serbia and Hungary to examine how extrusion processing variables—barrel temperature, moisture, screw speed, and die geometry—affect digestibility, pellet quality, and production cost in feeds for common carp and European catfish. Malešević led the work package on in vivo digestibility and animal performance trials conducted at the University of Novi Sad experimental farm and at partner facilities in Szarvas. The project produced harmonised feeding trial protocols across three partner institutions and generated digestibility coefficient databases intended for use in regional feed formulation software. A set of recommended processing parameter ranges for carp and catfish extrudates was published as a technical guideline document.
partners: Research Institute of Fisheries and Aquaculture, Szarvas, Hungary
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Debrecen, Hungary
AquaFeed Pannonia d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Insect Meal as a Fishmeal Substitute in Extruded Aquafeeds for Pond Species: Digestibility, Growth, and Environmental Assessment
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Funded by the Provincial Secretariat of Vojvodina, this project evaluated black soldier fly and mealworm prepupae meals as partial or complete fishmeal replacers in extruded compound feeds for common carp and European catfish. The research covered digestibility trials, growth performance assessment, whole-body and fillet composition analysis, and a simplified environmental footprint calculation comparing insect-based and conventional fishmeal-based diets. A local insect rearing company collaborated on substrate optimisation to produce insect meal with defined and consistent proximate composition. The project resulted in three peer-reviewed publications and two presentations at regional conferences, and established a collaborative framework with BioProtein d.o.o. for continued applied research.
partners: BioProtein d.o.o., Novi Sad, Serbia
Department of Water Management, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Assessment and Improvement of Passive Immunity in Neonatal Pigs on Smallholder Farms in Autonomous Province of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aims to generate region-specific reference data on colostrum immunoglobulin concentrations and FPT rates across smallholder pig farms in Vojvodina, and to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of practical on-farm interventions such as supervised suckling, supplemental colostrum feeding, and modified farrowing protocols. Activities include field sampling across four districts of Vojvodina, laboratory analysis at the Faculty of Agriculture in Novi Sad, and the development of a simple scoring tool for farm veterinarians and advisors. Milica Savić contributes to field sampling, ELISA analyses, and data management. The project is coordinated by Associate Professor Dragan Kovačević.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Veterinary Specialist Station Novi Sad
Rural Development Extension Service of Vojvodina

projects.title: Practical Cooling Strategies for Vojvodina Dairy Farms and Their Impact on Milk Fatty Acid Quality Under Summer Heat
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project assessed the cost-effectiveness of three retrofittable cooling interventions—sprinkler–fan systems, evaporative pad systems, and floor cooling mats—across eight commercial dairy farms in Vojvodina. The research team installed sensor networks, conducted fatty acid profiling of bulk-tank milk over two consecutive summers, and gathered farm economic data. A decision-support spreadsheet tool was developed for farmers and extension advisors to compare investment payback periods under different herd sizes and milk price scenarios. Outputs included two peer-reviewed articles, a practical guide distributed through the Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, and a dataset of microclimate and milk quality records available for further research.
partners: Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute for Animal Husbandry, Belgrade
Agrofarma Bačka d.o.o., Vrbas

projects.title: Adaptive Management of Dairy Herds Under Increasing Summer Heat: Cross-Border Evidence from Serbia, Hungary and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: THERMADAPT brings together partners from three countries to compile a joint database of heat stress exposure, cooling infrastructure, and milk quality records from over 40 commercial Holstein-Friesian herds in the Pannonian Plain. The project evaluates whether management recommendations developed under Hungarian or Romanian conditions transfer to Serbian farm contexts given differences in barn construction, herd size, and feeding practice. Vladimir Radulović leads Work Package 3 on nutritional mitigation, coordinating supplementation trials across partner farms and harmonising fatty acid analysis protocols between laboratories. Results will feed into a multilingual extension toolkit and a regional policy brief on climate adaptation in the livestock sector.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Agri-Consult Tisza Kft., Szeged
Dairy Farmers Association of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Genomic Characterisation and In Situ Conservation of Autochthonous Sheep Breeds of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to generate the first comprehensive SNP-based genomic dataset for six autochthonous sheep breeds from Serbia and neighbouring countries. Fieldwork involved sampling approximately 500 animals across four countries. Objectives included estimating effective population sizes, detecting selection signatures associated with local adaptation, optimising gene bank sampling panels, and producing management recommendations for national breed conservation authorities. Project outputs included three peer-reviewed journal articles, a conference symposium, and a technical report submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Serbia. Partner institutions provided field access and co-funded genotyping costs.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture and Food Science, University of Sarajevo
Biotechnical Faculty, University of Montenegro
Faculty of Agricultural Sciences and Food, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Institute for Animal Husbandry, Belgrade

projects.title: Genetic and Phenotypic Diversity of Wool-Type Sheep Breeds in the Danube–Sava Watershed
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral project investigating the genetic resources and wool quality traits of autochthonous sheep populations along both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. Vulin led the genetic characterisation work package, contributing microsatellite genotyping and population structure analyses for three Serbian breeds. The Hungarian partner was responsible for wool fibre diameter and staple length phenotyping. The project produced a joint genomic and phenotypic database, identified genetic clusters with potential relevance to wool product differentiation, and explored the feasibility of a regional certification scheme for artisan wool products. Results were shared with rural development agencies in Vojvodina and the Southern Transdanubia region of Hungary.
partners: Institute of Animal Science, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Kaposvár Campus
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Novi Sad
Vojvodina Rural Development Agency
