projects.title: Optimisation of pen design parameters for improved uniformity of growth in intensive beef bull production
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigated the combined effects of pen geometry, feeder configuration, and group size on within-pen variation in average daily gain in finishing Simmental bulls at the University of Novi Sad experimental cattle unit. Three pen layouts and two group sizes (8 and 16 animals) were tested in a factorial design over two production cycles. Primary outcomes were coefficient of variation in daily gain, displacement rate at the feeder, and feed conversion ratio. The project produced two peer-reviewed papers and a technical recommendation document distributed to provincial extension services. Total budget was approximately 2.4 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, Vojvodina

projects.title: Social rank, cortisol dynamics, and growth suppression in group-housed finishing bulls
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project examined the physiological pathways through which low social rank suppresses growth in finishing beef bulls. Working with the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine in Belgrade and a partner laboratory in Prague, the team measured cortisol, behavioural indicators of stress, and production parameters across a 90-day finishing cycle in Simmental bulls. Path analysis was used to partition the growth difference between high- and low-rank animals into feed-intake-mediated and cortisol-mediated components. Findings informed revised guidelines for group management and pen design communicated to producers in Vojvodina. The project funded one PhD studentship.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Belgrade
Department of Ethology and Companion Animal Science, Czech University of Life Sciences, Prague

projects.title: Locally Adapted Lactic Acid Bacteria as Maize Silage Inoculants: Isolation, Characterisation, and Field Evaluation in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish whether lactic acid bacteria strains naturally occurring in Vojvodina maize silage could serve as the basis for a domestically developed inoculant product. Activities included sampling of spontaneously fermented silage from 30 farms, isolation and culture-based plus molecular characterisation of over 200 isolates, and selection of candidate strains based on acetic acid production, growth at 10–35°C, and absence of acquired antibiotic resistance genes. Three candidate strains passed preliminary screening and were evaluated in multi-site mini-silo trials across two growing seasons. The project produced a characterised culture collection held at the Department of Microbiology, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, and provided the microbial foundation for a potential future inoculant development partnership.
partners: Department of Microbiology, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Maize Silage Quality and Fermentation Management Practices in Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SILQUAL surveyed 120 commercial dairy and beef farms (60 per country) to characterise maize silage quality, inoculant use, and face management practices. Laboratory analysis covered all major fermentation parameters plus mycotoxin screening. The project produced the first bilingual technical guide on silage management under Pannonian Plain conditions, distributed to participating farms and agricultural advisory services. Ristić led the work package covering fermentation laboratory analysis on the Serbian side and coordinated sample logistics. The project identified a high prevalence of aerobically unstable silage at farm opening (41% of Serbian samples) and documented a negative correlation between inoculant use and yeast counts at feedout. Recommendations were submitted to both national agricultural advisory agencies.
partners: Institute of Animal Nutrition, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Agricultural Advisory Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Research Station for Animal Husbandry, Debrecen

projects.title: Chilling Deficits and Hormonal Dormancy Control in Stone Fruit under Pannonian Climate Variability
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated how reductions in winter chilling alter the hormonal programme governing dormancy release in sweet cherry and sour cherry in Vojvodina. Work packages covered field phenology monitoring across five orchard sites, quantification of ABA, gibberellins, and cytokinins by LC-MS/MS throughout the dormancy cycle, controlled-chamber experiments with defined chilling treatments, and candidate gene expression analysis targeting ABA catabolic and gibberellin biosynthetic genes. A secondary objective was comparison of three chilling accumulation models for local predictive accuracy. The project produced a publicly available 15-season phenological and meteorological dataset and a set of hormonal reference thresholds intended for use in regional crop management advisories. One postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students were funded through the project.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering, Belgrade
Department of Meteorology, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Sustainable Stone Fruit Production under Changing Winter Conditions in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration addressing the agronomic and physiological consequences of milder winters for stone fruit producers in southern Hungary and Vojvodina. Ljubomir Grbić led the work package on dormancy physiology, coordinating field data collection and hormonal analyses at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station. Hungarian partners provided complementary datasets from three orchard sites near Szeged and Kecskemét. Joint outputs included a bilingual grower advisory leaflet on dormancy management, a shared database of cultivar-specific chilling requirements, and two peer-reviewed papers. The project also funded a short-course workshop for extension officers delivered at the Faculty of Agriculture in Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Hungarian Institute of Horticulture and Viticulture, Kecskemét
Agricultural Chamber of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Mycorrhizal Community Monitoring as a Soil Health Indicator in Organic Viticulture of the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj uspostavljanje zajedničkog protokola praćenja AMF zajednica u organskim vinogradima duž mađarsko-srpskog prekograničnog pojasa. Kovács je vodio radni paket koji se bavio standardizacijom metoda uzorkovanja i sekvenciranja između partnerskih laboratorija. U okviru projekta razvijen je zajednički referentni skup od 22 lokaliteta, prikupljeno je više od 500 uzoraka i uspostavljena je zajednička baza podataka o sekvencama dostupna svim partnerskim institucijama. Rezultati su korišćeni za formulisanje preporuka o minimalnim indikatorima zdravlja zemljišta za sertifikaciju organske vinogradarske prakse.
partners: Szegedi Tudományegyetem, Mađarska
Pécsi Tudományegyetem, Mađarska
Agencija za ruralni razvoj Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Udruženje organskih vinara Fruška gora, Sremski Karlovci

projects.title: Dinamika rizosfere vinograda u uslovima klimatskih promena: integracija mikrobiomu, funkcije korena i agrotehnike
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje kako promenjeni režimi padavina i temperatura menjaju funkcionalne osobine rizosferne mikrobiote vinograda u Srbiji. Kovács učestvuje u podprojektu koji se bavi AMF komponentom, konkretno godišnjom varijabilnošću strukture zajednice pod različitim scenarijima navodnjavanja i mulčiranja. U okviru projekta koriste se metagenoske metode zajedno sa izotopskim trasiranjem ugljenika (¹³C-PLFA) kako bi se kvantifikovao tok ugljenika kroz AMF miceliju. Planirano je uzorkovanje na 18 parcela tokom tri vegetacione sezone, sa finalnim modelovanjem odgovora zajednice na projekcije klimatskih scenarija RCP 4.5 i 8.5.
partners: Biosense Institut, Novi Sad
Institut za zemljišta Srbije, Beograd
Università degli Studi di Udine, Italija

projects.title: Polyphenol-enriched elderberry raw materials from Pannonian accessions: phytochemical characterisation and agronomic protocols for sustainable production
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project characterised polyphenol profiles of 18 elderberry accessions from the Vojvodina plain under varying water availability regimes, with the objective of identifying best-performing accessions for commercial cultivation and defining agronomic protocols—particularly irrigation management—that maximise anthocyanin and rutin yields without unacceptable reductions in berry fresh weight. Field trials were conducted at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station; analytical work used HPLC-DAD and spectrophotometric assays. Deliverables included accession ranking tables, irrigation guideline recommendations, and a small handbook for agricultural extension services in Vojvodina. Total funding was approximately 3.2 million RSD.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptation of berry crop production systems to projected late-summer drought in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project examining how elderberry, blackcurrant, and sea buckthorn respond to drought stress scenarios projected for the Pannonian Basin by 2050. The Novi Sad team led the elderberry work package, contributing controlled-environment drought experiments and field monitoring data from two sites in Serbia, while the Hungarian partner contributed data from two sites in Bács-Kiskun County. The project produced a joint database of physiological and phytochemical drought response indicators and a set of adapted cultivation guidelines. Dissemination included a bilingual Serbian–Hungarian producer brochure and two workshops for growers and extension staff. The Novi Sad team budget was approximately €38,000.
partners: Faculty of Horticultural Science, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Kecskemét
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Historical Orchard Landscape Atlas of Vojvodina: Cadastral and Aerial Sources 1880–1980
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce a comprehensive georeferenced dataset of orchard land-use in Vojvodina from late nineteenth-century cadastral maps and mid-twentieth-century aerial photographs. Activities included systematic scanning and georeferencing of cadastral sheets from the Archive of Vojvodina and the Republic Geodetic Authority, digitising of orchard parcels for 88 municipalities, quality control of positional accuracy, and compilation of an open-access vector atlas. A secondary component documented vernacular orchard parcel terminology from cadastral and notarial records. The resulting dataset was deposited in the Vojvodina Open Research Data Repository and published as a data paper. The project employed two research assistants and one GIS technician over three years.
partners: Archive of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Republic Geodetic Authority, Regional Office Novi Sad
Department of Geography, Tourism and Hotel Management, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Pannonian Orchard Heritage: Cross-Border Comparison of Historical Land-Use Change in Hungary and Serbia
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project compares rates and spatial patterns of historical orchard loss in adjacent areas of southern Hungary (Baranya and Bács-Kiskun counties) and northern Vojvodina using parallel datasets constructed from equivalent cadastral and aerial photographic sources for both countries. Dragišić leads the work package responsible for the Serbian side of the analysis, including data harmonisation across national cadastral conventions and joint georeferencing protocols. The project produces bilingual map products, a joint conference proceedings volume, and policy briefs directed at regional heritage protection agencies. A public-facing exhibition on traditional orchard landscapes is planned for Subotica and Pécs in the final project year.
partners: Institute for Rural Development Research, Debrecen
Baranya County Museum, Pécs
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency Subotica

projects.title: Rootstock-Driven Mineral Partitioning as a Tool for Reducing Postharvest Disorders in Intensive Apple Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ROOTMIN addressed the applied need to reduce bitter pit and cork spot losses in Vojvodina apple production by investigating the rootstock as a modifiable variable in mineral management. The project established multi-rootstock field trials at Rimski Šančevi and at a cooperating commercial orchard, combined ICP-OES tissue analysis with phloem exudate sampling, SEM-EDX graft union characterisation, and storage quality assessment. A secondary objective was to produce revised leaf mineral diagnostic reference ranges calibrated to specific rootstock types in use across Serbia. The project trained two doctoral candidates and produced seven peer-reviewed outputs. Final recommendations on rootstock–fertilisation combinations have been compiled into an extension bulletin distributed to apple growers in Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Cooperative Orchard Zlatno Voće, Sremski Karlovci

projects.title: Sustainable Mineral Management in High-Density Orchards of the Danube Basin: Linking Rootstock Biology and Fertilisation Practice
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBE-FRUIT is a cross-border project comparing rootstock performance and mineral nutrition outcomes across apple production zones in Vojvodina (Serbia) and Bács-Kiskun County (Hungary), two regions with contrasting soil carbonate levels and common apple varieties. The Serbian team led by Ranković is responsible for Work Package 3, covering tissue mineral analysis, soil micronutrient fractionation, and integration of data into a shared decision-support tool. Joint field sampling campaigns were conducted at four sites per country over three growing seasons. The project aims to harmonise leaf diagnostic reference ranges across the two national systems and to identify rootstock options that perform consistently well under both soil regimes. A shared open-access dataset is planned for release at project closure.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Horticultural Research Institute, Cegléd, Hungary
Regional Agricultural Chamber of Bács-Kiskun, Kecskemét, Hungary

projects.title: Sensory and Chemical Characterisation of Autochthonous Vojvodina Wine Varieties for Geographic Indication Support
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce a systematic sensory and physicochemical reference database for five autochthonous wine grape varieties cultivated in Vojvodina (Neoplanta, Sila, Začinak, Tamjanika crvena, and Kovačevića crna), with documentation supporting applications for geographic and variety-level origin claims. Activities included multi-vintage sampling across three subregions, construction of variety-specific sensory lexicons, and consumer acceptance trials with urban Serbian respondents. Deliverables included a publicly available sensory database, two journal articles, and a technical report submitted to the Vojvodina Development Fund and the Serbian Chamber of Commerce wine section. The project involved four researchers from the Faculty of Agriculture and one external collaborator from the Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad.
partners: Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad
Vojvodina Rural Development Agency

projects.title: Native Grape Varieties and Sustainable Winemaking Practices for Cross-Border Wine Tourism Development
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project brought together viticulture and tourism researchers from Serbia and Hungary to develop shared methodologies for characterising native grape varieties and integrating their sensory profiles into wine tourism narratives and product positioning strategies. Jasmina Obradović contributed expertise on sensory evaluation protocols and led sensory training workshops for winery staff on both sides of the border. The project produced bilingual sensory descriptor cards for eight varieties (four Serbian, four Hungarian), a comparative consumer study conducted in Subotica and Pécs, and guidelines for small producers on sensory quality assessment without laboratory infrastructure. A total of eleven wineries participated as associated partners.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Eszterházy Károly Catholic University, Eger
Regional Development Agency of South Pannonia
Subotica Wine Cluster

projects.title: Green Roof Potential and Substrate Optimisation for Urban Heat Mitigation in Vojvodina Settlements
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project mapped eligible flat-roof areas across five Vojvodina municipalities (Novi Sad, Subotica, Zrenjanin, Sombor, and Vrbas) using publicly available cadastre and satellite data and conducted substrate optimisation trials at the Rimski Šančevi experimental station. The work produced species suitability rankings for eight succulent taxa under Vojvodina climatic conditions, a substrate specification guideline published in Serbian for use by municipal planners, and a set of continuous temperature records now serving as baseline data for follow-on modelling work. Two MSc students completed theses within the project.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
City Institute for Urban Planning, Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermal Comfort and Vegetated Surface Strategies in Cross-Border Pannonian Urban Areas
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: THERMURB is a cross-border collaboration between institutions in Novi Sad and Pécs addressing urban overheating in Pannonian lowland cities. László Nagy leads the work package on vegetated surface performance, responsible for establishing paired green roof monitoring stations at residential buildings in both cities and for coordinating a joint database of substrate and plant performance indicators. The project also includes a public outreach component producing bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) technical guidelines for housing associations considering green roof retrofits. Partner institutions cover urban meteorology, civil engineering, and municipal planning.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Pécs
Pécs Urban Development Agency
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad
City Institute for Urban Planning, Novi Sad

projects.title: Frost Risk Assessment and Adaptive Management for Prunus Orchards in the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses increasing frequency of late spring frost events affecting apricot and plum orchards in the Pannonian region of Serbia. Core activities include long-term phenological monitoring at three sites, controlled freeze experiments on pollen and pistil material from 30 genotypes, and development of a site-specific frost-risk scoring index combining meteorological and biological variables. Field trials of four frost mitigation technologies—agrotextile covers, kaolin film, wind machine operation, and supplementary pollination—were conducted over three growing seasons. A practical decision-support guideline booklet targeting fruit growers in Vojvodina has been prepared and distributed through the agricultural extension service. Partners include the Hydrometeorological Service of Vojvodina and the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops.
partners: Hydrometeorological Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Apricot Pollen Bank for Supplementary Pollination under Climate-Induced Bloom–Frost Overlap
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This smaller project funds the establishment of a reference pollen cryobank for frost-tolerant apricot genotypes at the Faculty of Agriculture. Activities include protocol optimisation for long-term storage, viability monitoring at 3-month intervals over two years, and pilot application of stored pollen in commercial orchards via hand-pollination and modified sprayer delivery after a simulated total pollinator loss scenario. The bank is intended to provide growers in Vojvodina with a practical insurance resource in years when frost damage is severe enough to eliminate viable pollen from local orchard trees. Results feed directly into Todorović's broader research on reproductive failure and complement the genotype screening work carried out under FROSTPRUN.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Riparian Invasive Shrub Expansion and Native Community Resilience in the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je obuhvatio monitoring, kartiranje i eksperimentalno upravljanje invazivnim žbunastim vrstama (Amorpha fruticosa, Reynoutria japonica, Fallopia sachalinensis) na zajedničkim riparijanskim koridorima uz Tisu i Begu na teritoriji Srbije i Mađarske. Uspostavljena je zajednička baza vegetacijskih snimaka (ukupno 620 relevantnih parcela) i testirana su tri protokola za restauraciju autohtonih žbunastih slojeva. Projektom su obuhvaćeni i edukativni moduli za komunalne i vodoprivredne službe u pograničnoj oblasti. Srbijanski deo projekta realizovan je na ukupno 11 lokaliteta, a rezultati su implementirani u preporuke za upravljanje zelenim koridorima Pokrajinskog sekretarijata za urbanizam i zaštitu životne sredine APV.
partners: Departman za biologiju i ekologiju, PMF, Novi Sad
Institut za nizijsko šumarstvo i životnu sredinu, Novi Sad
