projects.title: Procena ekosistemskih usluga riparijanskih zelenih koridora Srbije u uslovima invazije neofita
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi kvantifikacijom promena u ekosistemskim uslugama (regulacija poplava, sekvestracija ugljenika, biodiverzitet, rekreacija) na riparijanskim zelenim koridorima Srbije u zavisnosti od stepena invazije žbunastim neofitima. Metodološki pristup kombinuje terenski monitoring, daljinsku detekciju (UAV i Sentinel-2), modelovanje i anketiranje korisnika koridora. Poseban fokus je na razlici u ekosistemskim uslugama između autohtonih vrsta i invazivnih zamena. Rezultati treba da pruže naučnu osnovu za nacionalni akcioni plan upravljanja riparijanskim staništima, u saradnji sa Ministarstvom zaštite životne sredine.
partners: Departman za geodeziju i geomatiku, FTN, Novi Sad
Institut za zaštitu bilja i životnu sredinu, Beograd
Geografski institut Jovan Cvijić, SANU, Beograd

projects.title: Conservation of Wild Fruit Genetic Resources of Vojvodina Province Through In Vitro and Cryogenic Methods
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project targets five underrepresented wild fruit species native to Vojvodina and the broader Balkan region, including Pyrus communis subsp. pyraster, Malus sylvestris, and Prunus spinosa. Work packages cover field collection and morphological characterisation, establishment of in vitro cultures, optimisation of cryopreservation protocols, and deposition of cryopreserved accessions into a regional genebank repository hosted at the Faculty of Agriculture in Novi Sad. Prodanović contributes to the pear-specific tissue culture and cryopreservation tasks, maintaining embryogenic callus lines and testing alternative cryoprotectant formulations. The project involves collaboration with the Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province for field access permits and site data.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province, Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute for Fruit Growing, Čačak, Serbia

projects.title: Optimised Surface Coatings for Extended Service Life of Tillage Tools in Diverse Vojvodina Soil Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project systematically evaluated four coating technologies — HVOF WC-CoCr, plasma nitriding, pack boriding, and laser cladding with TiC — on mouldboard ploughshare and subsoiler tine blanks. Laboratory tribometer tests using repacked soils representative of the main Vojvodina texture classes established specific wear rates and friction coefficients for each coating–soil combination. Selected coatings were then validated in paired field trials on farms in Bačka and Srem over two ploughing seasons. The project produced a decision-support matrix linking soil texture class, expected annual tillage area, and recommended coating technology, along with cost-per-hectare estimates based on coating application cost and measured service-life extension.
partners: Department of Materials Engineering, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Agriculture, Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Agricultural Tribology: Tool Wear and Energy Efficiency in Hungarian–Serbian Farming Systems
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral project with the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Debrecen and an agricultural machinery cooperative in Subotica. Marković leads the work package on comparative field wear measurement across the two countries, where soil texture and tillage practices differ. Shared protocols for gravimetric wear assessment, draft-force logging, and fuel-consumption monitoring were developed in year one and deployed on eight farms (four per country) in years two and three. A secondary objective is training young engineers on both sides of the border through two joint summer schools hosted alternately in Novi Sad and Debrecen. The project also compiles an open-access database of field wear results.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Debrecen
Agrarna Zadruga Palić, Subotica
Agricultural Research Institute Karcag

projects.title: Particle-Scale Simulation of Grain Flow and Segregation in Combine Harvester Working Units
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed validated DEM simulation tools for the threshing and cleaning units of combine harvesters, targeting Serbian winter wheat and maize varieties. Key activities included measurement of crop-specific contact parameters at varying moisture contents, construction of a high-speed imaging station for trajectory validation, CFD–DEM coupled simulation of the cleaning shoe, and a parametric design study of sieve geometry. A total of four Ph.D. students and two M.Sc. students participated. Outputs include six journal papers, one book chapter, and an open-source parameter database for Serbian grain varieties hosted on the University of Novi Sad data repository.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Precision Harvesting Technologies for Wheat and Maize
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between the University of Novi Sad and the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő, focused on sharing computational and experimental methodologies for combine harvester performance evaluation. Andrić led the work package on simulation tool development, providing access to the Novi Sad DEM simulation cluster and co-supervising two joint M.Sc. theses. The project also organised a two-day training school for engineers from Serbian and Hungarian agricultural machinery companies attended by 34 participants. A joint test protocol for laboratory threshing unit evaluation was developed and published as a technical report.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Biosystems Engineering, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Vojvodina Agricultural Extension Service, Novi Sad

projects.title: Energy-Efficient Strip-Till Adoption in Vojvodina: Soil Mechanical Constraints and Implement Optimisation
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates barriers to wider adoption of strip-till technology on the heavy clay soils of Vojvodina, with particular attention to the elevated draft force and fuel consumption recorded in Vertisol profiles. Field trials on six representative sites across South Bačka and South Banat districts measure draft, fuel use, soil disturbance geometry, and subsequent crop establishment parameters for maize and sunflower. Implement configurations — coulter type, shank geometry, and working depth — are varied systematically. The goal is to produce a practical decision tool that helps farm managers select implement settings matched to their specific soil conditions. Dunja Ognjanov contributes to field measurement campaigns and data processing.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina

projects.title: Vibration Exposure Reduction Strategies for Agricultural Tractor Operators in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: VIBAGRI addressed the cross-border relevance of occupational WBV risk in flat agricultural regions shared by Hungary and Serbia. The project carried out comparative field measurement campaigns on both sides of the border, characterised road surface conditions on a shared network of 60 field road segments, and developed a bilingual decision-support tool for daily exposure estimation. Mirjana Stevanović led the work package on field measurement methodology, coordinating data collection protocols and harmonising them with ISO 2631-1 and the EU Physical Agents (Vibration) Directive. The project trained 45 agricultural safety inspectors and cooperative managers from both countries. A joint dataset of over 1,200 measurement runs was assembled and deposited in an open repository.
partners: Institute of Agricultural Technology, Hungarian University of Agricultural and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Regional Chamber of Agriculture Bács-Kiskun, Kecskemét
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptive Seat Suspension Monitoring for Long-Term Vibration Dose Management in Field Machinery
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SMARTSEAT investigates whether real-time vibration dose accumulation feedback displayed to tractor operators can change travel behaviour and reduce daily A(8) values. The project combines the low-cost monitoring hardware developed in earlier work with a small dashboard display showing instantaneous and accumulated dose. A randomised controlled field trial is being conducted across eight cooperatives in Vojvodina, with 40 operators in the intervention arm and 40 in a control group. Primary outcomes are daily A(8) and self-reported travel speed choices on rough road segments. Secondary outcomes include lower-back pain self-reports collected over a six-month follow-up. Interim analysis at month 12 showed a mean A(8) reduction of 0.09 m/s² in the intervention group.
partners: Department of Agricultural Engineering, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Department of Mechatronics, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Agricultural Cooperative Ravnica, Sombor

projects.title: Standardised field measurement protocols and correction tables for crosswind drift in variable-rate granular spreaders across European agro-climatic zones
projects.programme: Horizon 2020 (EIC Accelerator)
projects.summary: International consortium (University of Novi Sad, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, University of Bonn, INRAE Thiverval-Grignon) developed standardised protocols for measuring and correcting crosswind drift in VR spreaders. Generated multi-site field data (240 trials across four countries) and published open-access correction tables. Coordinated four work packages; managed budget €890,000; supervised three PhD students. Outputs: correction tables in public spreadsheet format, firmware updates distributed to five equipment manufacturers, and three journal publications.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences (Hungary)
University of Bonn (Germany)
INRAE Thiverval-Grignon (France)
Lemken GmbH (industry partner)
Amazone GmbH (industry partner)

projects.title: Precision fertiliser application for cereal production: spreader calibration, field validation, and agro-economic analysis in Pannonian agro-systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS)
projects.summary: Three-year project examining variable-rate spreader performance and agronomic/economic outcomes in winter wheat and maize across twelve farm sites in Vojvodina. Conducted calibration methodology development, field trials, yield mapping, and cost-benefit analysis. Trained two PhD students and five M.Sc. students. Generated twelve field validation datasets and five technical reports distributed to Serbian farm cooperatives. Budget: 48,000 EUR (Serbian domestic funding).
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agroindustrija Bačka Palanka (farmer cooperative)
Tehnoseeds d.o.o. (agronomy services company)

projects.title: Precision agriculture decision support for small and mid-sized farms: spreader selection, calibration, and variable-rate implementation in Pannonian region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Cross-border capacity-building project (University of Novi Sad, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Hungarian farm cooperative, Serbian farm cooperative) providing technical training and decision-support tools for spreader adoption. Conducted training workshops (n = 8, attended by 180 farmers across both countries), developed multilingual decision guide, and field-tested calibration procedures on eighteen farms. Participated in work package managing field trials; co-supervised two bilateral PhD students (joint degree). Budget: 280,000 EUR (EU co-financing).
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences (Hungary)
Farmers' Association Bács-Kiskun County (Hungary)
Poljoprivredna zadruga Kumodraž (farmer cooperative, Serbia)

projects.title: Biogas from Crop Residues and Livestock Waste for Small Farm Energy Independence in Vojvodina and the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BIOFARM-VP is a cross-border cooperation project that aims to generate practical knowledge and decision-support tools for small and medium-sized farms in the Hungarian–Serbian border region seeking to install on-farm anaerobic digestion systems. The University of Novi Sad team is responsible for characterising regionally specific feedstock combinations, running pilot-scale digestion trials, and developing a feedstock availability mapping layer for a web-based farm advisory tool. Čolić contributes to laboratory digestion trials and field data collection on the Serbian side. Partner activities in Hungary focus on digestate agronomic valorisation and permitting frameworks. Outputs include technical guidelines in Serbian and Hungarian and a series of farm demonstration days.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Pannon Institute for Rural Development, Pécs, Hungary
Regional Agricultural Extension Service of South Bačka District, Serbia

projects.title: Hydraulic Uniformity and Water Use Efficiency in Drip-Irrigated Vineyards on Sloped Terraces in the Pannonian–Carpathian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: VITHYDRO addressed the gap between hydraulic design practice and actual field uniformity in sloped vineyard drip systems along the Serbia–Romania border region, where terraced parcels on the Vršac and Timiș Hills share similar topographic and water quality conditions. The project installed reference monitoring networks on four commercial vineyards (two per country), developed shared design guidelines calibrated to local pipe materials and water chemistry, and produced a bilingual technical manual distributed to 140 irrigation practitioners. The University of Novi Sad led hydraulic modelling and field measurement activities, while partners at Timișoara contributed agronomic monitoring and sensory evaluation of wine from uniformly versus non-uniformly irrigated blocks.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Timișoara
Regional Chamber of Agriculture Timișoara
Viticulture Extension Service Vojvodina, Sremski Karlovci

projects.title: Modelling and Field Validation of Pressure-Compensating Drip Irrigation Laterals on Complex Terrain in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SLOPEIRR developed and validated an open-source hydraulic simulation tool for pressure-compensating drip laterals laid on slopes with variable gradient and terrace geometry, addressing design scenarios not covered by existing commercial software. The project combined laboratory pipe-bench experiments, a new dataset from 18 vineyard sites across Serbia, and computational fluid dynamics modelling of flow within pressure-compensating emitter chambers at different inlet pressures. A particular focus was placed on the behaviour of laterals in the 0.8–1.2 bar pressure range where compensating emitters transition between their compensating and non-compensating regimes. Project outputs include the simulation tool (released under an open licence), two journal articles, and a design handbook for practitioners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Acoustic Shielding Solutions for Stationary Agricultural Processing Machinery in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj razvoj i validaciju prenosivih akustičnih zaštitnih rešenja prilagođenih retromontirani na stacionarnu opremu za sušenje i čišćenje žitarica na malim i srednjim gazdinstvima u pograničnom regionu Srbije i Mađarske. Aktivnosti su obuhvatale inventarizaciju izvora buke na 18 lokacija, razvoj prototipova panela, terenska ispitivanja u Vojvodini i regiji Bač-Kiškun, i pripremu tehničkih smernica na srpskom i mađarskom jeziku. Partnerska organizacija iz Mađarske obezbedila je ispitni prostor i bazu podataka o fondu sušara. Krajnji korisnici su bili predstavnici zadruga koji su učestvovali u korisničkom testiranju prototipova.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Department of Agricultural and Food Process Engineering, Gödöllő
Regionalna razvojna agencija Bačka, Novi Sad
Zadružni savez Vojvodine

projects.title: Validacija protokola za merenje i verifikaciju emisije buke ventilatora u industrijskim sušarama žitarica
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Cilj projekta bio je uspostavljanje verifikacionog protokola koji bi omogućio nezavisnu proveru deklarisanih vrednosti zvučne snage ventilatora koje navode proizvođači, u skladu sa standardima EN ISO 3744 i EN ISO 11201. Na uzorku od 15 ventilatora iz pet različitih izvora nabavke sprovedena su paralelna merenja u laboratorijskim i terenskim uslovima. Razvijen je korisnički priručnik na srpskom jeziku namenjen inspektorima rada i tehničkom osoblju preduzeća za preradu žita. Rezultati projekta korišćeni su kao osnova za dve publikacije u međunarodnim časopisima i prezentovani su na skupu Ministarstva rada.
partners: Institut za javno zdravlje Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Sediment Budget Dynamics and Channel Adjustment in the Lower Tisa River Under Changing Hydrological Forcing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to quantify sediment budget components for the lower Tisa reach in Serbia and to identify dominant controls on observed channel incision. Field campaigns included seasonal ADCP transects, bedload trap deployments, and systematic floodplain coring. A hydraulic–sediment transport model was developed and run under historical and projected climate forcing. The project produced the first high-resolution longitudinal grain-size map of the reach, an updated sediment budget covering 2010–2023, and scenario simulations to 2070. Outputs inform Serbian Water Directorate maintenance planning. Three journal papers and one conference contribution have resulted from the project.
partners: Department of Water Management, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Water Management Jaroslav Černi, Belgrade
Provincial Hydrometeorological Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Comparative Assessment of Morphological Change in Middle Danube Regulated Reaches: Hungary, Serbia, and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A trinational team assembled harmonised bathymetric and grain-size datasets covering approximately 350 km of the Middle Danube to enable cross-border comparison of channel adjustment trajectories since major regulation works. Péter Halász led the work package responsible for field data collection and GIS-based volumetric change analysis on the Serbian sector. The project produced a joint monitoring protocol adopted by all three national water authorities and a synthesis report on incision hot spots requiring coordinated management response. Results were presented to the International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River.
partners: Department of Water Management, University of Novi Sad
Research Centre for Lowland Water Management, Debrecen, Hungary
Faculty of Hydrotechnics, Technical University of Timișoara, Romania
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Vojvodina

projects.title: Constructed Wetlands as End-of-Drain Treatment Systems for Nutrient Retention in Intensive Agricultural Landscapes of the Middle Danube Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project established four demonstration constructed wetland systems — two in Serbia (Vojvodina) and two in southern Hungary — for treatment of tile drainage from cereal and vegetable farms. Vladana Erić led the work package on technical design, monitoring protocol harmonisation, and cross-site performance analysis. The project produced a bilingual design handbook distributed to extension services in both countries, and generated the monitoring dataset subsequently used in the 2024 journal publication on hybrid system performance. A total of approximately 38 ha of drained cropland was connected to treatment wetlands by project end, with combined design capacity of 850 m³ day⁻¹ during peak drainage periods.
partners: Department of Land and Water Management, University of Debrecen
Research Institute for Irrigation and Water Management, Szarvas, Hungary
Provincial Directorate for Water Management, Novi Sad
Agricultural Extension Service of South Bačka District

projects.title: Nitrogen Recovery Potential and Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Constructed Wetlands Treating Subsurface Agricultural Drainage
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project examines the nitrogen mass balance of constructed wetlands treating tile drainage, with particular focus on quantifying N₂O and N₂ emissions as poorly constrained loss pathways. Closed-chamber and open-path FTIR measurements are conducted monthly at the Rimski Šančevi pilot facility to estimate N₂O fluxes under different operational regimes. Denitrification completeness is evaluated by comparing N₂O:(N₂O + N₂) emission ratios using helium-filled incubation chambers on intact sediment cores. The project also investigates whether design modifications — elevated water table, carbon-amended inlet zones — can shift the denitrification product ratio toward N₂. Results are intended to improve greenhouse gas accounting for agricultural constructed wetlands in the Serbian national inventory.
partners: Department of Water Management, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad (Department of Chemistry, Biochemistry and Environmental Protection)
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Groundwater Recharge and Bank Filtration Resilience Under Climate and Land-Use Change in the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AQUAPAN brought together four institutions from Serbia and Hungary to produce a joint assessment of groundwater recharge trends and bank filtration performance under combined climate and land-use change pressures. The Novi Sad team was responsible for the Serbian case study sites, including monitoring network installation and data collection at two BF sites on the Danube and two recharge transects in Vojvodina. Work package outputs included a shared monitoring protocol, a publicly accessible database of head and water quality records, and scenario analysis using coupled hydrological and groundwater models. Results were communicated to water utility operators and provincial water authorities through two technical workshops.
partners: University of Miskolc, Institute of Environmental Management
Institute for Water Management Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Hungarian Directorate General of Water Management, Budapest
Public Utility Company Vodovod i Kanalizacija, Novi Sad

projects.title: Recharge Estimation and Groundwater Vulnerability Assessment for Public Water Supply Zones in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: REGROZ addressed a practical need of provincial water managers: updated, spatially distributed recharge estimates and groundwater vulnerability maps for the 14 public water supply zones of Vojvodina. The project combined existing monitoring data with new field campaigns (tracer tests, streambed measurements, unsaturated zone profiling) and applied the DRASTIC vulnerability indexing method recalibrated against local contamination data. A key output is a GIS-based decision-support layer provided to the Provincial Secretariat for Water Management. The project also supported two master's theses and a PhD candidate's field data collection. Total budget was approximately 4.2 million RSD.
partners: Institute for Water Management Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Non-Stationary Flood Frequency Estimation for Ungauged Agricultural Catchments in Vojvodina Under Climate Change
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a regionalised non-stationary flood frequency framework for the approximately 400 ungauged agricultural sub-catchments of Vojvodina. Core activities include: extension of the provincial short-record station database by digitising historical water-level registers from the Provincial Water Directorate archive; detection and attribution of non-stationarity in flood series using covariate-driven GEV models; derivation of updated regional growth curves with Bayesian pooling; and production of a web-accessible flood frequency atlas. The atlas delivers design flood estimates at ungauged sites with associated uncertainty bounds for return periods from 2 to 500 years. Results are intended to inform revisions to provincial drainage design standards. Partners contribute climate model downscaling capacity and field discharge measurement equipment for low-flow rating curve extension.
partners: Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia, Belgrade
Provincial Directorate for Water Management, Novi Sad
Jaroslav Černi Water Institute, Belgrade

projects.title: Integrated Flood and Drainage Risk Assessment for Cross-Border Agricultural Catchments in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DRAINPAN addresses cross-border flood risk in the Tisza–Maros confluence zone where Serbian and Hungarian drainage systems interact hydraulically. The Serbian team, led by Pekez, is responsible for Work Package 3: stochastic flood scenario generation and infrastructure stress-testing on the Serbian side of the border. Joint activities include harmonisation of hydrological databases across the two countries, a shared EURO-CORDEX downscaling exercise, and development of a binational flood early-warning indicator based on spatially correlated stochastic event generation. A joint drought–flood risk decision-support tool is being developed for use by drainage management authorities on both sides of the border. Three cross-border field campaigns for discharge gauging and geomorphological mapping are planned.
partners: National Water Directorate of Hungary (OVF), Budapest
Faculty of Civil Engineering, Budapest University of Technology
Lower Tisza District Water Directorate, Szeged
Provincial Directorate for Water Management, Novi Sad

projects.title: Reclamation Strategy for Salt-Affected Soils in the Danube–Tisa–Danube Irrigation Zone under Changing Climate
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop integrated reclamation strategies for salt-affected irrigated soils in the cross-border Danube–Tisa–Danube irrigation zone, covering approximately 120,000 ha across southern Hungary and Vojvodina. Activities included joint soil monitoring using standardised protocols, calibration of SALTMOD and HYDRUS-1D models to cross-border conditions, and preparation of a bilingual reclamation planning manual distributed to regional water management authorities. The University of Novi Sad team led field work in the Serbian sector, while the Hungarian partner managed modelling activities. Two pilot reclamation demonstrations were established, one on each side of the border, with matched monitoring equipment for comparative analysis.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Research Institute for Irrigation, Szarvas, Hungary
Provincial Directorate for Water Management, Novi Sad

projects.title: Sodicity and Alkalinity Dynamics in Vojvodina Heavy Clay Soils: Linking Processes Across Scales for Improved Reclamation Design
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SODALKA addressed the mechanistic gap between plot-scale reclamation experiments and field-scale drainage design by combining isotopic tracer studies (²H₂O and ³⁶Cl⁻) with crack network characterisation using X-ray computed tomography on undisturbed soil columns, and a distributed MODFLOW-MT3DMS salt transport model. Twelve experimental plots at the Rimski Šančevi station were instrumented with TDR probes, suction cups, and automated water table recorders over three complete irrigation seasons. The project produced new pedotransfer functions for shrink-swell clay hydraulic properties and revised drainage spacing recommendations for soils with CEC above 40 cmol kg⁻¹, submitted to the national drainage design standard revision committee.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Governance Capacity of Water-User Associations in the Western Balkans: Diagnostic Framework and Policy Recommendations
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral research cooperation between the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, and the Faculty of Agronomy, University of Zagreb, funded under the Serbian–Croatian scientific exchange programme. The project developed a standardised diagnostic toolkit for evaluating WUA governance capacity, comprising 47 indicators across financial, technical, social, and legal dimensions. The toolkit was piloted in 14 associations (8 Serbian, 6 Croatian) and results were used to produce national-language practitioner guides for WUA board training. Final outputs included two journal articles, a bilingual practitioner handbook, and a joint policy brief submitted to both countries' water management directorates.
partners: Faculty of Agronomy, University of Zagreb
Serbian Water Management Directorate, Novi Sad Regional Office
Croatian Waters Agency, Zagreb

projects.title: Adaptive Water Allocation Governance in the Pannonian Transboundary Canal Systems Under Climate Variability
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project examining the governance and technical dimensions of water allocation in the shared canal systems spanning southern Hungary and northern Serbia, with particular attention to the institutional responses to the 2012 drought. Mijatović led the work package on institutional analysis and stakeholder engagement, overseeing fieldwork in six Serbian WUAs and contributing to a comparative database shared with Hungarian partners. The project produced a joint transboundary water-sharing protocol proposal, submitted to both national water authorities, and a public-facing handbook on drought preparedness for WUA managers. Three joint scientific publications resulted from the collaboration.
partners: National Agricultural Research and Innovation Centre, Gödöllő, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Novi Sad
Association of Water-User Associations of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Pannonian Farm Resilience Under Agri-Environmental Policy Change: Indicators, Drivers and Cross-Border Comparisons
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANRES brought together four partner institutions from Serbia and Hungary to develop a harmonised farm resilience monitoring framework applicable across the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region. The Novi Sad team led the work package on indicator development and data collection, conducting annual surveys of approximately 100 farms on the Serbian side of the border over three years. Activities included design of a shared FADN-compatible survey instrument, organisation of two regional practitioner workshops in Subotica and Szeged, and production of a joint policy brief addressed to regional agricultural authorities. The project resulted in a publicly available resilience indicator dataset and a comparative report on farm adjustment patterns under differing national policy regimes.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Research Institute for Agricultural Economics, Budapest, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Subotica
Chamber of Agriculture of Csongrád-Csanád County, Hungary

projects.title: Structural Adjustment and Income Risk Among Smallholders Under Payment Reform in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AGROSHIFT is a three-year project funded under the PROMIS programme investigating the unintended structural consequences of direct payment reforms in Serbia. The project combines administrative microdata from the Serbian Ministry of Agriculture with original farm surveys in three Vojvodina districts to identify farm exit triggers, income risk accumulation pathways, and the role of advisory services in mediating adjustment. A microsimulation model is under construction to project farm population dynamics under alternative reform scenarios relevant to Serbia's EU accession commitments. The project involves a postdoctoral researcher and two doctoral students based at the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, and includes a research exchange with the Institute for Agricultural and Food Economics in Budapest.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Agricultural and Food Economics, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Gender-Differentiated Land Tenure Arrangements and Their Consequences for Agricultural Productivity in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GENLAND-VOJ examines whether and how gender differences in formal land ownership, informal use rights, and management authority affect agricultural productivity outcomes at the household level in Vojvodina. The project combines a panel household survey of 420 farming households surveyed in 2021 and 2023, parcel-level cadastral data, and semi-structured interviews with 60 households to build a dataset linking tenure arrangements to yield and income indicators. It also analyses how EU-funded agri-environment schemes are accessed differently by male and female landowners. A policy brief targeted at the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture and the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Serbia is among the planned outputs.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Agricultural Economics, Belgrade
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Comparison of Gendered Land Inheritance in Vojvodina and Banat (Romania)
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSLAND is a bilateral research and capacity-building project comparing gendered inheritance practices in the Serbian Vojvodina and the Romanian Banat, two historically connected agricultural regions separated by the national border since 1918 but sharing common agrarian traditions. The project conducts parallel household surveys, cadastral analyses, and focus groups on each side of the border to identify convergent and divergent trajectories since the end of socialism. Đurić leads the Serbian data collection and analysis work package. Joint training workshops for rural advisors and local government staff on gender-sensitive land administration are planned for 2025. A comparative monograph will be published in English and Romanian-Serbian bilingual editions.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sociology and Social Work, West University of Timișoara
Banat Regional Development Agency, Timișoara
Centre for Rural Research and Policy, Zrenjanin

projects.title: Short Food Supply Chains as Instruments of Rural Resilience in Vojvodina: Assessment, Mapping, and Policy Recommendations
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project assessed the current state, spatial distribution, and economic significance of short food supply chains in Vojvodina province. Activities included a GIS-based census of SFSC outlets, a household survey of 203 participating producers, and an analysis of municipal market regulations across 27 local self-government units. The project produced a publicly available digital map of SFSC infrastructure, a policy brief submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, and a set of model municipal ordinances to facilitate farmers' market establishment. A workshop series brought together producers, municipal officers, and agricultural extension advisors. The project also generated two peer-reviewed publications and provided thesis topics for three master's students.
partners: Institute of Agricultural Economics, Belgrade
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Novi Sad
Regional Chamber of Commerce Novi Sad

projects.title: Linking Small Producers and Urban Consumers Through Sustainable Local Food Chains in the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FOODLINKS-IPA is a cross-border cooperation project examining consumer demand and producer capacity for SFSC development on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. Despotović leads the work package on producer economic capacity assessment, coordinating surveys of 160 producers across Bács-Kiskun county and South Bačka district. The project is developing a joint producer–consumer digital platform prototype to be piloted in Subotica and Baja, alongside shared labelling guidelines and a cross-border farmers' market calendar. The Novi Sad team's contribution feeds into broader project outputs including a binational SFSC strategy document and training materials for producer associations. Expected completion is mid-2025 with a final conference planned in Subotica.
partners: Faculty of Horticulture, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Kecskemét
Regional Development Agency Bačka, Novi Sad
Bács-Kiskun County Farmers' Association, Kecskemét

projects.title: Adaptive Water Governance in Irrigated Agriculture across South-Eastern Europe
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: AQUAGOV-SEE investigates how irrigation governance institutions in six South-Eastern European countries adjust to increasing drought frequency and altered precipitation patterns. The project combines longitudinal household surveys, institutional mapping, and agent-based modelling to assess adaptive capacity of water-user associations. Valentina Hadžić leads Work Package 3, which covers social capital measurement, collective action diagnostics, and the design and testing of participatory rule-revision processes in pilot associations in Serbia and Hungary. The work package runs field activities in 24 associations over the project period. Outputs include a governance assessment toolkit intended for use by national water agencies and a comparative database of association-level social capital and governance indicators.
partners: Wageningen University, Netherlands
Hungarian University of Agricultural and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Agricultural University of Plovdiv, Bulgaria
University of Bucharest, Romania
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Mediterranean Agronomic Institute of Chania, Greece

projects.title: Social Capital and Collective Infrastructure Maintenance in Vojvodina Irrigation Schemes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SOCWATER addressed the question of how different dimensions and sources of social capital affect collective contributions to irrigation canal maintenance in Vojvodina. The project conducted a baseline social capital survey of 22 water-user associations (n = 612 farm households), followed by two annual follow-up waves. Longitudinal regression and difference-in-differences estimation were used to identify causal pathways. A sub-study examined the role of formal rule revisions as mediating factors. Results were disseminated to the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture and Waterways and to the Union of Irrigation Associations of Vojvodina. The project supported two doctoral students and produced six journal articles.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Institute of Agricultural Economics, Belgrade

projects.title: Land Access, Tenure Security, and Farm Adjustment in Pre-Accession Agricultural Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The LANDACC project investigates how tenure insecurity and fragmented land markets constrain farm structural adjustment in Serbia during the pre-accession period. The project collects longitudinal farm panel data across six municipalities in Vojvodina and the Šumadija region, combining cadastral records, FADN-compatible farm accounts, and semi-structured interviews. Key research questions concern the relationship between tenure arrangements, investment behaviour, and farm size dynamics. Crnković contributes to data collection, econometric analysis of farm exit and expansion decisions, and policy scenario modelling related to different CAP direct payment decoupling trajectories. The project is led by the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, and involves a partner team from the Institute for Agricultural Economics in Belgrade.
partners: Institute for Agricultural Economics, Belgrade
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Vojvodina

projects.title: Demographic Decline and Agricultural Land Use Change in Peripheral Rural Municipalities of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines how population contraction and aging in peripheral rural areas translate into changes in agricultural land use, focusing on Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia-Herzegovina. The team combines harmonised census microdata, land cadastre records, satellite imagery, and targeted household surveys to build a longitudinal dataset covering approximately 250 municipalities. Specific objectives include quantifying land abandonment rates attributable to labour force decline, modelling the spatial distribution of successor-less farms, and evaluating the demographic assumptions embedded in national rural development programmes. Partners at three regional universities contribute country-specific expertise and data access. The project has produced a publicly accessible GIS dataset of rural demographic indicators at settlement level for all three countries.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Sociological and Political-Legal Research, University Ss. Cyril and Methodius, Skopje
Faculty of Agriculture, University of East Sarajevo

projects.title: Cross-Border Demographic Dynamics and Rural Service Accessibility in the Hungary–Serbia Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSDEM investigates how demographic shrinkage on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border affects the viability and accessibility of rural public services, including health posts, schools, and transport connections. The Serbian component, led by Savić's team, covers 11 municipalities in the northern Vojvodina sub-regions. The work package focuses on mapping service closures between 2000 and 2022, conducting accessibility analyses using network distance metrics, and identifying settlements where cross-border service sharing could be administratively feasible. Results feed into a joint policy brief addressed to regional authorities on both sides of the border. A household survey component assesses whether residents are aware of and willing to use cross-border service alternatives.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Research Institute for Regional Studies, Pécs
Centre for Regional Development, Subotica

projects.title: Price Transmission Pathways in Western Balkan Livestock Value Chains: Evidence for Policy Design
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project collects and harmonises weekly farm-gate, wholesale, and retail price data for pork and beef across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia over a fifteen-year window and estimates threshold vector error correction models for each value chain stage in each country. A second component links estimated asymmetry parameters to structural indicators—retail concentration, cold-chain investment, contract coverage—using a cross-country panel regression. Policy briefs aimed at national agriculture ministries and competition authorities translate findings into recommendations on price reporting obligations and procurement rules for public catering institutions. The project runs a shared price database accessible to partner institutions and maintains a stakeholder advisory group including representatives of pig farmer cooperatives, the meat processing association, and the Serbian Commission for Protection of Competition.
partners: Institute of Agricultural Economics, Belgrade
Faculty of Agriculture and Food Sciences, University of Sarajevo
Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Faculty of Agricultural Sciences and Food, Skopje

projects.title: Agri-Food Market Integration and Value Chain Upgrading in the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed market linkages and supply chain efficiency for pork, fresh vegetables, and dairy products in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The University of Novi Sad team led the work package on price analysis and market integration, providing econometric assessments of price co-movement between Hungarian and Serbian wholesale markets and interviewing sixty-two producers and processors located within 80 km of the border on both sides. Outputs included a bilingual report on cross-border trade barriers and a pilot joint price information portal for producers, subsequently transferred to the Vojvodina Pig Producers Association for maintenance. The project facilitated introductions between Serbian processing firms and Hungarian retail chains operating in the border region.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences (MATE), Gödöllő
Vojvodina Pig Producers Association, Novi Sad
Bács-Kiskun County Chamber of Agriculture, Kecskemét

projects.title: Payment Instrument Design for Farmland Biodiversity in the Pannonian Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project examined the feasibility and design of coordinated agri-environment payment instruments across the Hungarian–Serbian border section of the Pannonian Plain. Bajić led the work package on economic instrument design and farmer preference analysis, overseeing field surveys in four Serbian border districts and contributing to joint auction experiments with the Hungarian partner. The project produced a comparative assessment of institutional readiness for cross-border scheme alignment, a toolkit for provincial authorities, and a set of tested auction protocols. Three policy briefs were submitted to the Serbian Ministry of Agriculture and the Hungarian National Rural Network. Total project value approximately 1.1 million EUR, with the Novi Sad team receiving roughly 340,000 EUR.
partners: Institute of Agricultural Economics, Budapest
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency of Southern Transdanubia, Pécs
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry, Novi Sad

projects.title: Multi-Criteria Framework for Biodiversity Payment Scheme Prioritisation in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project developed and validated a multi-criteria decision framework to assist Serbian environmental and agricultural authorities in selecting and sequencing biodiversity payment instruments across diverse agroecological zones. The research combined ecosystem service mapping at the cadastral-parcel level with MCDA methods and stakeholder preference surveys. Field work covered 12 planning units in Vojvodina and the Mačva region. The project produced open-access GIS layers for four ecosystem services, a decision support tool implemented in R, and five peer-reviewed articles. Two graduate students completed their master's theses within the project. Funded by the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia under the PROMIS programme; total budget approximately 180,000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province
Faculty of Forestry, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Integrated Metabolic Monitoring for Early Detection of Subclinical Disorders in Dairy Cattle: From Biomarker Profiles to Herd Decision Support
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish validated reference intervals for a ten-analyte metabolic panel in periparturient dairy cows under Vojvodina production conditions and to develop a statistical scoring tool enabling farm veterinarians to stratify cows into risk categories at dry-off and at calving. Data were collected from eight commercial farms over three consecutive years. The project funded the acquisition of a portable automated biochemical analyser dedicated to cow-side use and supported three PhD candidates. A scoring algorithm was developed and delivered as a spreadsheet-based decision aid, with user testing conducted in cooperation with three veterinary practices in the region. Publications and guidelines were disseminated to the regional veterinary professional association.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Animal Husbandry, Belgrade
Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Dairy Herd Health Management: Metabolic Disease Surveillance and Benchmarking in Hungarian and Serbian Farms
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Debrecen focused on harmonising metabolic disease surveillance methods across participating farms in southern Hungary and Vojvodina. The project involved establishment of a shared database of periparturient cow health records covering approximately 2,800 lactations, development of a bilingual herd health recording form, and joint training workshops for farm veterinarians and technicians on standardised BCS recording and BHB measurement. Jovanović led the work package on biomarker data collection and quality assurance. Project outputs included a joint technical report and a series of training materials translated into Serbian and Hungarian, distributed to approximately 180 practitioners across both countries.
partners: University of Debrecen, Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences and Environmental Management
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Regional Veterinary Chamber of Vojvodina (fictional body)
Southern Transdanubia Agricultural Advisory Centre (fictional body)

projects.title: Toxoplasma gondii in Backyard Animal Husbandry: Epidemiological Baseline and Risk Mitigation Strategies for Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to construct a comprehensive epidemiological baseline for T. gondii infection in backyard pigs and small ruminants across all seven Vojvodina districts. Activities included a large-scale cross-sectional serosurvey, farm-level risk factor profiling via structured questionnaire, molecular genotyping of selected isolates, and preliminary spatial analysis. A secondary component involved developing a simplified farm biosecurity checklist for distribution through district veterinary services. The project produced four peer-reviewed publications, one institutional technical report submitted to the Provincial Veterinary Directorate, and field training for four veterinary students in farm sampling and serology protocols. Budget was approximately 4.2 million RSD.
partners: Scientific Veterinary Institute Novi Sad
Provincial Veterinary Directorate, Novi Sad
Department of Epidemiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Surveillance of Selected Zoonotic Parasites in Livestock along the Pannonian Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANZOON brings together veterinary research institutions from Serbia and Hungary to harmonise surveillance methods for three priority zoonotic parasites: Toxoplasma gondii, Trichinella spp., and Cysticercus cellulosae, in backyard and small-scale commercial livestock on both sides of the Serbia–Hungary border. Dobanovački leads Work Package 2, responsible for T. gondii seroprevalence surveys, standardisation of diagnostic protocols across laboratories, and joint genotyping analysis. The project includes joint field campaigns, exchange visits for early-career researchers, and a shared data repository. A harmonised surveillance protocol document is a key deliverable intended for submission to competent national veterinary authorities in both countries. Total project budget is approximately 780,000 EUR.
partners: Department of Parasitology and Zoology, University of Pécs, Hungary
National Food Chain Safety Office Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory, Budapest
Scientific Veterinary Institute Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Unapređenje kontrole PPV i PRRSV ko-infekcija u svinjarskim zapatima pograničnog područja Panonske nizije kroz harmonizovane dijagnostičke protokole i strategije vakcinacije
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je obuhvatao 12 farmi svinja u pograničnom pojasu između Srbije i Mađarske. Cilj je bio harmonizacija seroloških dijagnostičkih protokola između laboratorija na obe strane granice i razvoj zajedničkih smernica za vakcinaciju i biosigurnost. Tim iz Novog Sada bio je odgovoran za prikupljanje i analizu uzoraka sa srpske strane, sprovođenje ELISA i VN testova, kao i obradu epidemioloških podataka. Izrađen je zajednički priručnik za terenske veterinare na srpskom i mađarskom jeziku. Projektom su obuhvaćena ukupno 1.240 serumskih uzoraka i 42 veterinarska preduzeća konsultovana kroz radionice.
partners: Department of Animal Hygiene, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Regionalna veterinarska uprava Subotica
Heves County Agricultural Chamber, Hungary

projects.title: Renal Biomarker Profiling for Early Detection and Dietary Intervention in Companion Animal Chronic Kidney Disease
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The RENAPET project aims to establish reference intervals for a panel of urinary tubular injury biomarkers—including uNGAL, kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1), and cystatin C—in healthy cats and dogs across age groups in the Vojvodina region, and to test whether dietary phosphorus and protein adjustment alters biomarker trajectories in early CKD. The study involves repeated sampling from approximately 80 animals over 18 months at the university veterinary clinic. Isidora Vukelić is responsible for sample collection, ELISA assay execution, and data entry. The project is coordinated by her supervisor. Results will feed directly into her doctoral thesis.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Veterinary Specialist Centre Bačka, Novi Sad

projects.title: Canine Mammary Tumour Receptor Characterisation as a Comparative Model for Breast Oncology
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled a prospective cohort of bitches undergoing mammary tumour surgery at veterinary clinics across Vojvodina, collecting standardised tissue samples, clinical data, and 24-month follow-up records. Tumours were characterised by histopathological grading, full receptor immunohistochemical profiling (ERα, PR, HER2, Ki-67), and molecular subtype assignment. A digital tissue archive with annotated whole-slide images was constructed. Secondary objectives included evaluation of tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte scoring and pilot application of machine-learning image analysis for HER2 quantification. The project produced a regional biobank of 180 characterised canine mammary carcinoma specimens available for further molecular and translational studies.
partners: Small Animal Clinic Novi Sad
Institute of Oncology Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica
BioImage Analytics Laboratory, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Biomarkers of Broiler Stress During Pre-Slaughter Handling: Linking Non-Invasive Endocrine Indicators to Farm Management and Transport Conditions in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish reference ranges for salivary and feather corticosterone in commercially reared broilers in Vojvodina and to identify farm-level, transport, and lairage factors that explain variation in these indicators. Fieldwork involved six commercial farms, four transport contractors, and two abattoirs. A prospective cohort design was used: each flock was followed from day 1 through slaughter, with on-farm welfare scoring, microclimate logging during transport, and corticosterone sampling at unloading and at the slaughter line. The project produced validated sampling and storage protocols suitable for adoption by veterinary inspectors, and a preliminary dataset linking farm stocking density and litter quality scores with feather corticosterone at slaughter. One MSc thesis and two journal publications resulted from the project period.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Veterinary Institute Novi Sad

projects.title: Harmonised Welfare Indicator Protocols Across the Broiler Supply Chain in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project works toward harmonised welfare data collection at the farm and abattoir levels in Hungary and Serbia, with a focus on broilers and laying hens. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on ante-mortem stress indicators, contributing feather and salivary corticosterone methodology developed in prior projects. Hungarian partners contribute data from their inspection systems and from two abattoirs near the border region. The shared protocol being developed includes standardised swab collection, storage, and ELISA analysis procedures, and a jointly agreed welfare scoring sheet compatible with existing official veterinary inspection procedures in both countries. Training workshops for slaughter-line veterinarians are planned in 2025.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Department of Animal Breeding and Nutrition, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Kaposvár Campus
Regional Veterinary Directorate Subotica, Serbia
Veterinary Inspection Directorate Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Fluoroquinolone Residue Depletion in Vojvodina Livestock: Field Pharmacokinetics, Population Modelling and Withdrawal Period Validation
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project examined fluoroquinolone residue depletion under authentic farm conditions across cattle, sheep, and goat holdings in Vojvodina, where animal husbandry practices and body weight distributions differ from the controlled study populations used in EU marketing authorisation dossiers. A total of 280 animals across 18 farms were enrolled. Population PK models were developed in NONMEM to identify farm-level and animal-level covariates affecting depletion. Monte Carlo simulations were used to evaluate whether current withdrawal periods are adequate across the observed range of animal weights and body condition scores. A practical decision-support tool for veterinary practitioners was developed and disseminated through the Veterinary Chamber of Serbia.
partners: Veterinary Institute Novi Sad
Institute for Food Technology Novi Sad
Veterinary Chamber of Serbia – Vojvodina Branch

projects.title: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Models for Predicting Fluoroquinolone Tissue Residues in Ruminants: Development, Validation and Regulatory Application
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project built and validated PBPK models for enrofloxacin and marbofloxacin in cattle, sheep, and goats to support regulatory extrapolation of withdrawal periods between species and dosing regimens without requiring full depletion studies. In vitro tissue binding assays, microsomal metabolic clearance measurements, and reanalysis of published and proprietary depletion datasets were used to parameterise the models. Sensitivity and uncertainty analyses quantified the principal sources of predictive error. Regulatory applicability was assessed against EMA CVMP validation criteria, and a pre-consultation with the Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia was conducted to explore the pathway for PBPK-supported withdrawal period submissions.
partners: Faculty of Veterinary Hygiene and Ecology, University of Veterinary Sciences Brno
Institute of Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology, University of Zurich
Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia

projects.title: Tick-borne Pathogen Diversity and Transmission Risk in Wild Ungulate Populations of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project aimed to establish comprehensive baseline data on tick-borne pathogen prevalence in roe deer and wild boar at twelve hunting ground sites distributed across Vojvodina's three historical sub-regions (Bačka, Banat, Srem). Field sampling covered two full annual cycles. Molecular screening targeted Borrelia spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Babesia spp., and Theileria spp. using standardised real-time and conventional PCR protocols. Data were linked to host demographic parameters obtained from hunting records. A secondary objective was to produce educational material for hunting associations on personal tick-bite prevention and the importance of reporting tick-borne illness. Total budget approximately 4.2 million RSD.
partners: Hunting Association of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-border Surveillance of Vector-borne Zoonoses in the Danube Floodplain: Serbia and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBE-VECTOR addresses gaps in harmonised vector-borne disease surveillance along the Danube corridor shared by Romania and Serbia. The project combines entomological field surveys, wildlife host sampling, and human seroprevalence studies at paired sites on both banks of the river. Milena Jovanović leads Work Package 2, which covers tick collection from wild ungulates and small mammals and pathogen screening on the Serbian side. Partners share standardised protocols and a common database to allow direct cross-border comparison. The project also trains veterinary and public health professionals from both countries in field collection and molecular diagnostic methods. Outputs include a joint risk assessment report and recommendations for national surveillance agencies.
partners: Institute of Biological Research, Cluj-Napoca
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Timișoara
Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad

projects.title: Selective Enzymatic Production of Arabinoxylan Oligosaccharides with Defined Chain Length from Serbian Cereal Milling By-products
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between laboratory-scale AXOS synthesis and industrially relevant quantities with defined DP profiles. Wheat, rye, and corn bran from Serbian flour and wet-milling operations were used as substrates. The work involved enzyme screening, kinetic modelling of hydrolysis and inhibition, membrane fractionation optimisation, and assessment of prebiotic function in fermentation models. A pilot-scale process was designed and evaluated through three production runs at the Faculty of Technology. The project also tested AXOS incorporation into selected bakery products. Partners provided analytical support and faecal fermentation assays.
partners: Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad (FINS)
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Food Science, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Valorisation of Cereal Bran Hemicellulose Streams for Functional Food and Feed Applications
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project investigating the conversion of wheat and rye bran hemicelluloses into prebiotic oligosaccharide ingredients and dietary fibre concentrates for food and animal feed use. Bulatović led the work package on enzymatic and chemical hydrolysis processes and product characterisation. Hungarian partners contributed microbial screening and feed trial design. The project established protocols for comparing GH10 and GH11 xylanases on substrates of differing botanical origin and produced data on energy use and process economics at 50 L pilot scale.
partners: Research Institute for Agricultural Economics, Budapest, Hungary
Faculty of Animal Science, Kaposvár Campus, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad (FINS)

projects.title: Fizičkohemijska stabilnost tradicionalnih sušenih voćnih proizvoda Vojvodine pri promenljivim klimatskim uslovima skladištenja i distribucije
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je bio usmeren na sistematsko mapiranje uslova koji uzrokuju gubitak kvaliteta tradicionalnih sušenih voćnih proizvoda (šljiva, kajsija, breskva, dunja) tipičnih za region Vojvodine tokom skladištenja i distribucije u promenljivim klimatskim uslovima. Primenjene su metode dinamičke sorpcije para, DSC i instrumentalne teksturalne analize. Izgrađena je baza podataka sorpcionih izotermi i Tg vrednosti za 14 komercijalnih proizvoda, a razvijeni su dijagrami stabilnosti i smernice za male i srednje prehrambene proizvođače u regionu. Projekat je rezultirao sa pet naučnih radova i jednim priručnikom za industriju.
partners: Institut za prehrambene tehnologije Univerziteta u Novom Sadu
Udruženje prerađivača voća Vojvodine

projects.title: Razvoj sistema ambalažiranja za međuvlažnu hranu sa poboljšanom barijerom prema fluktuacijama relativne vlažnosti u regionalnom lancu distribucije
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Cilj projekta je razvoj i validacija inovativnih ambalažnih rešenja za međuvlažne prehrambene proizvode (sušeno voće, konditorska punjenja i voćne grickalice) koji se distribuiraju u prekograničnom regionu Srbija–Mađarska. Srpski partner odgovoran je za karakterizaciju fizičkohemijskog ponašanja modelnih sistema pri promenljivim uslovima vlažnosti (radni paket 2), dok mađarski partner razvija nove barijerske materijale. Gordana Radić rukovodi radnim paketom koji obuhvata definisanje kritičnih aw i Tg parametara i projektovanje protokola za ubrzano ispitivanje stabilnosti. Predviđena su dva pilotna ispitivanja u realnim distributivnim lancima.
partners: Fakultet za prehrambene nauke, Mađarski univerzitet za poljoprivredu i nauku o životu, Budimpešta

Institut za prehrambene tehnologije Univerziteta u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Valorisation of Vegetable Processing By-products through Dense-phase Extraction of Lipid-soluble Bioactives
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the gap between laboratory-scale extraction data and pilot-scale implementation for carotenoid and tocopherol recovery from tomato, pepper, and carrot residues generated at food processing plants in Vojvodina. Work packages covered feedstock characterisation and seasonal variability, SC-CO₂ process parameter optimisation using design-of-experiments methods, mass transfer modelling, extract stability, and a techno-economic feasibility study. The project operated the 5 L pilot extractor at the Faculty of Technology and engaged two partner institutes for analytical support. A final report with scale-up guidelines was submitted to four regional processing companies.
