Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Center for Process Engineering, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-border Cooperation for Carotenoid-rich Ingredient Development from Vegetable Industry Residues
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project linking the Faculty of Technology at the University of Novi Sad with the Faculty of Food Science at a Hungarian partner university to develop a shared methodological framework for carotenoid extraction from pepper and tomato by-products prevalent on both sides of the border. Dobanovački led the work package on extraction process development and standardisation of analytical protocols. The project produced a joint technical guideline document and enabled two joint publications. Three student exchanges were carried out between the two institutions during the project period.
partners: Faculty of Food Science, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Debrecen, Hungary
Agri-Processing Cluster Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Microbiological and Metabolomic Characterisation of Traditional Fermented Vegetable Products as a Basis for Quality Standardisation in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project assembled a multi-season dataset on LAB diversity and organic acid profiles in sauerkraut and pickled peppers from registered small producers across Vojvodina. Sample collection was standardised across five production sites. Culture-independent sequencing was combined with traditional isolation to build a strain collection of approximately 200 LAB isolates. Organic acid and volatile metabolite data were obtained by HPLC and SPME-GC-MS. Outputs include a recommended analytical protocol for routine quality monitoring in artisanal production and a freely accessible strain data repository shared with the Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad. The project supported two master's theses and one doctoral dissertation.
partners: Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina (facilitator)

projects.title: Selection and In Vitro Characterisation of Indigenous Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Strains from Serbian Fermented Vegetables for Defined Starter Culture Development
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: LACTOSELECT aims to move selected indigenous strains from the existing culture collection through a structured in vitro evaluation pipeline covering technological properties (acidification kinetics, NaCl tolerance, texture effects) and safety criteria (antibiotic resistance, biogenic amine production, absence of virulence genes), culminating in a shortlist of candidate strains for pilot-scale defined starter culture testing. Metabolomic profiling by ¹H NMR and GC-MS is used to distinguish strain-specific flavour contributions in model medium fermentations. Collaboration with the University of Szeged provides access to complementary analytical infrastructure. The project supports one postdoctoral researcher and two doctoral students, and is expected to produce a provisional technical specification document for starter culture use in Serbian artisanal production.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad (lead)
Department of Food Science, University of Szeged, Hungary
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad

projects.title: Freeze–Thaw Stability of Structured Biopolymer Matrices for Extended-Shelf-Life Frozen Foods
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the mechanisms by which combinations of native and modified starches, plant and dairy proteins, and small-molecule cryoprotectants confer mechanical stability to gel matrices subjected to industrial freeze–thaw regimes. Ognjen Novaković contributes to rheological characterisation, DSC measurements, and low-field NMR experiments within the project. The consortium combines expertise in biopolymer chemistry, food texture analysis, and industrial freezing technology. A target application is the reformulation of sauce and filling components in frozen ready meals to reduce freeze–thaw-induced quality loss without increasing the number of declared food additives, a commercial and regulatory concern for domestic Serbian food producers.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Carbohydrate Chemistry, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Cryogenic Food Processing and Frozen Product Quality Assurance
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project links food technology research groups in Novi Sad and Szeged to harmonise methods for evaluating frozen food quality, with a focus on textural and rheological assessment protocols applicable to both academic and industrial quality control settings. Novaković's specific contribution involves establishing joint experimental protocols for freeze–thaw cycling experiments and low-field NMR measurements, and conducting a comparative study of frozen ready-meal gel components manufactured under Serbian and Hungarian production conditions. The project includes a technology transfer component that will produce a best-practice guide for frozen food SMEs in the cross-border region.
partners: Department of Food Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Migration Safety of Additive Packages in Multilayer Food Contact Materials Under Real Distribution Conditions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined additive migration from five commercial multilayer film types under temperature and mechanical stress conditions representative of Serbian food distribution chains. Migration was measured for twelve target compounds including plasticisers, antioxidants, and slip agents using validated HPLC-DAD and GC-MS methods. A database of temperature-dependent diffusion and partition coefficients for the most common polymer–simulant pairs encountered in the Serbian market was compiled and made publicly available. The project also produced a practical compliance guide for small and medium food packaging converters operating under EU Regulation No 10/2011, aligned with Serbian food safety legislation. Two industry workshops were held in Novi Sad and Belgrade.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Faculty of Chemistry, University of Belgrade
Packaging Converters Association of Serbia (fictional)

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Food Packaging Safety Testing Protocols in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSPACK aimed to harmonise laboratory protocols for food-contact material testing between accredited laboratories in Subotica, Serbia, and Szeged, Hungary. Slobodan Vulin led the work package on fatty food simulant migration testing, coordinating round-robin exercises involving PVC and polyolefin film samples distributed to both partner laboratories. Measurement uncertainty budgets were compared and a joint standard operating procedure was drafted for adoption by both laboratories. The project also supported staff mobility: one early-career researcher from Novi Sad completed a three-month placement at the University of Szeged. A bilingual Serbian–Hungarian technical guidance document was produced as the primary deliverable.
partners: Department of Food Engineering, University of Szeged, Hungary
Subotica Food Safety Testing Centre (fictional)
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Process Parameter Optimisation for Acrylamide Reduction in Extruded Legume-Based Foods
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how barrel temperature profiles, feed moisture, and screw design interact to determine acrylamide formation and colour in twin-screw extrusion of chickpea, lentil, and faba bean flours. Work packages cover precursor analysis in raw materials, in-process monitoring using fluorescence spectroscopy, kinetic modelling of Maillard intermediate build-up, and optimisation of process windows that satisfy both food safety thresholds (EU Regulation 2017/2158 benchmarks) and product quality criteria. A secondary aim is to validate colour as a surrogate safety marker. The project supports two PhD students and includes a three-month exchange visit to the Czech University of Life Sciences, Prague.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Food Technology, Czech University of Life Sciences, Prague

projects.title: Development of Nutritionally Optimised Gluten-Free Extruded Snacks from Local Legume Varieties
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SNACKFIT aimed to characterise ten domestic legume varieties (chickpea, lentil, pea) for extrusion suitability, with emphasis on asparagine content, starch characteristics, and protein quality. Marko Mitrović led the extrusion trials and food safety work package, conducting pilot-scale runs and benchmarking acrylamide against EU guidance levels. Nutritional profiling and consumer testing were handled by partners at the Institute of Food Technology. The project produced a variety selection guide and a set of recommended process parameters for two of the tested varieties, and contributed primary material to three journal publications.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Agricultural Research Institute Sremska Mitrovica

projects.title: Stability and Bioaccessibility of Encapsulated Bioactive Lipids from Hemp Seed Oil in Functional Food Matrices
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the formulation of spray-dried hemp seed oil microcapsules intended for incorporation into bakery and dairy products. Research objectives included optimisation of wall material composition (WPI, maltodextrin grades, and lecithin), accelerated shelf-life modelling, and quantification of omega-3 fatty acid bioaccessibility using the standardised static INFOGEST protocol. A secondary objective was evaluating the antioxidant contribution of whey-derived peptides released during simulated digestion. The project employed Rancimat oxidation kinetics, DSC, and confocal microscopy as principal analytical tools. One master's thesis and two doctoral theses were co-supervised under this project. Results generated 4 journal publications and were presented at 3 regional conferences.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Chemical and Food Technology, Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava, Slovakia

projects.title: Utilisation of Hemp By-Products in Functional Food Development: Oil, Protein and Fibre Fractions
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A broader multidisciplinary project coordinated by the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, covering the full valorisation chain of industrial hemp processing residues grown in the Vojvodina region. Vesna Mitrović led the work package on oil extraction, quality characterisation, and microencapsulation, contributing cold-pressing optimisation and baseline fatty acid characterisation for three hemp cultivars. Her team supplied characterised oil fractions to partners working on hemp protein isolates and fibre composites. The encapsulation data from this project fed directly into the subsequent HEMPSTAB application. Deliverables included two joint publications and a regional workshop for food technology practitioners.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Exopolysaccharides from Indigenous Lactic Acid Bacteria as Functional Texture Modifiers in Dairy Analogues
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project characterised EPS produced by lactic acid bacteria isolated from traditional Serbian fermented dairy products and evaluated their functional performance in plant-based analogues of yoghurt and fresh cheese made from soy, oat, and lupin milk. Work packages covered strain screening and EPS yield optimisation, structural characterisation by NMR and methylation analysis, rheological and textural profiling, and a consumer acceptability component involving a sensory panel of 60 participants. The project supported two PhD students and resulted in three journal publications and one book chapter. Laboratory-scale prototype formulations of oat-based set yoghurt with acceptable texture and 21-day shelf stability were developed and presented to two regional food producers.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad
Faculty of Food Science, Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca

projects.title: Fermented Legume-Based Beverages: Microbiology, Texture, and Consumer Acceptance in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FERMLEG is a cross-border project developing fermented protein-rich beverages from locally grown legumes (soy, pea, lupin) for the Hungarian and Serbian markets. Ostojić leads the work package on starter culture selection and EPS-mediated texture development, coordinating activities between the Novi Sad team and partners at the University of Pécs. Tasks include selection and characterisation of EPS-producing strains with desirable rheological profiles in legume substrates, optimisation of fermentation parameters at 50 L pilot scale, and transfer of starter culture protocols to the industrial partner. The project has a total budget of approximately EUR 580 000 with the Novi Sad team receiving EUR 180 000.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Food Technology, University of Pécs
Vojvodinaplod d.o.o., Novi Sad
Pannonia Food Innovations Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Improving Techno-Functional Performance of Domestically Grown Plant Proteins Through Enzymatic and Chemical Modification
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates systematic enzymatic hydrolysis and Maillard conjugation strategies applied to protein isolates from sunflower, pea, and hemp cultivars grown in Vojvodina. Laboratory-scale modifications are benchmarked against functional targets relevant to plant-based dairy and meat analogues: gelation strength, emulsification stability, and foam capacity. Process parameters—pH, temperature, ionic environment, enzyme type and load—are optimised using response surface methodology. Functional outcomes are linked to structural changes characterised by circular dichroism spectroscopy, DLS, and rheology. Vuk Tešić contributes to the gelation and rheological characterisation workstream. Outputs are intended to inform both future industrial upscaling and ongoing PhD research within the group.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Quorum Sensing Inhibition as a Strategy to Reduce Pseudomonas Biofilm in Refrigerated Meat Processing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje mehanizme kvorum senzinga kod sojeva Pseudomonas izolovanih iz rashladnih pogona za preradu mesa u Srbiji i procenjuje mogućnost njihove inhibicije prirodnim jedinjenjima i enzimskim preparatima. Obuhvata identifikaciju AHL molekula LC-MS/MS metodom, transkriptomsku analizu biofilmskih ćelija u uslovima stresa izazvanog sanitizacijom, kao i razvoj i testiranje površinskih premaza na bazi laktaza imobilizovanih na hitozanskim nosačima. Poseban cilj je razvoj protokola za praćenje QS aktivnosti u otpadnim vodama pogona kao indikatora biofilmskog opterećenja. Rezultati projekta imaju direktnu primenu u industriji prerade mesa i mogu se koristiti za poboljšanje HACCP planova.
partners: Institut za molekularnu genetiku i genetičko inženjerstvo, Univerzitet u Beogradu
Szegedi Tudományegyetem, Mađarska

projects.title: Термодинамичке основе оптимизације суперкритичне екстракције терпеноида из аутохтоног балканског лековитог биља
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат је усмерен на изградњу базе термодинамичких података за системе суперкритичног CO₂ с одабраним монотерпенима, сесквитерпенима и дитерпенским киселинама карактеристичним за аутохтоно балканско лековито биље. Мере се растворљивости у статичкој и динамичкој ћелији, а подаци се користе за прилагођавање параметара неколико кубних и молекуларних ЈС. На основу тих параметара развијају се процедуре предикције за нова јединимо помоћу метода груписаних доприноса. Пројекат финансира набавку нових сапирних прозора за визуалну ћелију и унапређење GC-MS методе. Пројекат сарађује са Природно-математичким факултетом у Нишу и Хемијским факултетом у Београду.
partners: Природно-математички факултет, Универзитет у Нишу
Хемијски факултет, Универзитет у Београду

projects.title: Scaling supercritical terpenoid extraction from medicinal herbs: from thermodynamic data to pilot demonstration
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project brings together research institutions and small herb-processing enterprises in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region to develop and validate scale-up protocols for supercritical CO₂ extraction of terpenoid-rich fractions from lavender, sage, and thyme. The Novi Sad team is responsible for thermodynamic characterisation and process modelling (Work Package 2), while a Hungarian partner provides pilot-scale extraction facilities for validation trials. A shared experimental database of solubility and fractionation data is being compiled and made available to regional SMEs. The project includes two industrial partners operating herb farms in Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád counties, who contribute raw material supply and define target product specifications for pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications.
partners: Vegyészmérnöki és Biomérnöki Kar, Budapesti Műszaki és Gazdaságtudományi Egyetem
Laborex Illatszer és Kozmetikai Kft., Сегедин
ВојводинаХерб д.о.о., Нови Сад

projects.title: Fermented Legume Ingredients for Mineral-Enriched Bread: From Laboratory to Pilot Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the feasibility of using fermented legume flours (lentil, chickpea, common bean) as functional ingredients in composite wheat breads, with the primary objective of improving iron and zinc bioaccessibility through phytate reduction. Work packages covered starter culture selection, fermentation optimisation at bench and pilot scale, dough rheology characterisation, in vitro and Caco-2 cell-based mineral bioavailability assessment, and a small consumer acceptance study (n = 80 participants from Novi Sad). The project produced a pilot-scale production protocol and a dataset of anti-nutritional factor profiles across 15 fermentation conditions. Two master's theses were completed under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Anti-Nutritional Factor Profiling of Balkan Landrace Legumes for Sustainable Food System Applications
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Romanian institutions to characterise nutritional and anti-nutritional properties of landrace legume accessions held in gene banks in Novi Sad and Cluj-Napoca. Radić's group leads the work package on phytate, oxalate, tannin, and trypsin inhibitor quantification and coordinates in vitro mineral bioaccessibility testing across the accession panel. The project also includes agronomy, sensory analysis, and consumer awareness components led by partner institutions. Results will be compiled into a publicly accessible database and used to recommend accessions for breeding programmes targeting reduced anti-nutritional factor content.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Research Station for Legume Crops Turda, Romania

projects.title: Directed Evolution of Ligninolytic Laccases for Valorisation of Vojvodina Agro-Industrial Residues
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to engineer fungal laccase variants with improved activity and stability under industrially relevant conditions—specifically alkaline pH and elevated temperature—and to demonstrate their utility in processing sunflower husks and corn stover, the two highest-volume agro-industrial residues in Vojvodina. Activities included isolation and characterisation of indigenous laccase producers, directed evolution by error-prone PCR, semi-rational mutagenesis guided by homology modelling, and proof-of-concept delignification trials at 1-litre reactor scale. The project employed three researchers and produced six journal publications. Collaboration with ITQB NOVA (Lisbon) was established for structural bioinformatics support.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
ITQB NOVA, Universidade Nova de Lisboa, Portugal

projects.title: Residue-Based Biorefinery Chains in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project bringing together research groups and SMEs from Vojvodina (Serbia) and Csongrád-Csanád county (Hungary) to develop biorefinery value chains anchored on agricultural residues—primarily wheat straw, sunflower husks, and maize cob—common to both regions. Kovačević's contribution focuses on the enzymatic delignification work package, supplying engineered laccase preparations and optimised treatment protocols to partners conducting saccharification and fermentation trials. The project targets a minimum pilot scale of 100 kg batch by the final year. A joint patent application on immobilised enzyme preparations for residue processing is under preparation within the consortium.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
BioAgro Innovation Centre Szeged
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Agricultural Research Centre of Csongrád-Csanád County, Hódmezővásárhely

projects.title: Plastid Genome Stability as a Determinant of Secondary Metabolite Consistency in Micropropagated Medicinal Plants
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the relationship between chloroplast genome integrity and secondary metabolite biosynthesis in five economically important medicinal plant species regenerated through tissue culture. Work packages covered protocol benchmarking, whole-plastome sequencing, transcriptomic profiling of plastid-encoded biosynthetic genes, and metabolite quantification across multiple subculture cycles. The project funded two PhD students and produced infrastructure improvements to the plant tissue culture and HPLC facilities at the Faculty of Technology, Novi Sad. Results were expected to provide a molecular basis for defining acceptable cpDNA variation thresholds in quality certification schemes for plant nurseries and phytopharmaceutical raw material suppliers.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Biology, Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Molecular Quality Standards for Micropropagated Herbal Plants
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral cross-border project aiming to harmonise molecular marker-based quality assessment standards for commercially propagated medicinal and aromatic plants in the Serbian–Hungarian border region. Marković's group leads the work package on chloroplast marker panel development and validation, contributing the cpSSR multiplexing protocol and reference allele databases for 12 target species. The Hungarian partner coordinates nuclear microsatellite genotyping and variety identification. The project includes joint training workshops for nursery technicians and a shared online database of reference marker profiles accessible to growers and certification bodies in both countries.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Horticultural Science, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Kecskemét, Hungary
Regional Chamber of Commerce for Medicinal Plants, Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Stoichiometric and Kinetic Modelling of Volatile Flavour Formation in Controlled Maillard Reactions for Bakery Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and experimentally validated stoichiometric and kinetic models describing the formation of Strecker aldehydes and alkylpyrazines in amino acid–carbonyl model systems representative of wheat bread crust conditions. Experimental work covered binary and multicomponent amino acid mixtures reacting with methylglyoxal and glyoxal across a factorial design of temperature (140–200 °C), water activity (0.30–0.60), and pH (5.0–8.0). GC–MS/MS with stable-isotope dilution assays provided quantitative volatile yield data. Model parameters were estimated by non-linear regression and tested on independent pilot-scale baking experiments. A spreadsheet prediction tool was produced and made publicly available. Two PhD students and one MSc student were trained within the project.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technology
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
University of Debrecen, Faculty of Agricultural and Food Sciences

projects.title: Volatile Quality Fingerprinting of Heritage Cereal Varieties for Regional Food Identity and Added-Value Product Development
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project linking Vojvodina-region heritage grain producers, the University of Novi Sad, and Hungarian research partners to establish volatile and non-volatile quality markers for heritage wheat and spelt varieties. Tóth's work package covers GC–MS flavour profiling of model crust and artisan bread samples from twelve varieties grown in parallel field trials on both sides of the border. Profiling data feed into a shared open-access database and a regional quality label specification document. The project also includes a knowledge-transfer component with three artisan bakeries in the cross-border area. Total project budget is approximately 780 000 EUR; Tóth's work package represents approximately 140 000 EUR.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technology
University of Szeged, Faculty of Engineering
Vojvodina Agricultural Extension Service
North-Hungarian Regional Development Agency

projects.title: Carotenoid Stabilisation in Colloidal Food Systems: Coupled Thermal and Photo-oxidative Stress
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the mechanisms by which thermal and photo-oxidative stresses interact to accelerate carotenoid degradation in oil-in-water nanoemulsions, and tests biopolymer-based interfacial strategies to mitigate combined stress effects. Work packages include degradation kinetic modelling, design and characterisation of chitosan and Maillard-conjugate-coated emulsions, and in vitro bioaccessibility assessment using the INFOGEST static digestion protocol. Ivona Kovačević contributes to kinetic modelling, sample preparation by high-pressure homogenisation, and HPLC-DAD analysis. The project is coordinated by the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad in collaboration with the Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Nanostructured Carriers for Bioactive Fortification of Plant-Based Dairy Analogs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project develops nanoemulsion and nanoparticle delivery systems for carotenoid and phytosterol fortification of oat- and soy-based dairy analog products targeting both Serbian and Hungarian markets. Partners combine expertise in emulsion technology, sensory analysis, and pilot-scale processing. Kovačević's role covers carotenoid stability characterisation under processing and storage conditions relevant to plant-based beverages, including UHT thermal profiles and refrigerated distribution. The project includes a consumer acceptability study and regulatory labelling assessment. Results are intended to feed directly into product development at the industrial partner.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Food Science, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Budapest
Voćar d.o.o., Novi Sad
BioAliment Kft., Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Fermentation–Methanogenesis Syntrophy Under Variable Feedstock Composition: Monitoring and Control Strategies for Agricultural Biogas Plants
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FERMSYN investigates how fluctuating feedstock composition — typical of Vojvodina's agro-industrial landscape — disrupts syntrophic partnerships between fermentative bacteria and methanogens. The project operates 6 parallel CSTRs under controlled perturbation scenarios (substrate switches, OLR shocks, ammonia pulses) while combining online VFA sensors, weekly qPCR profiling, and amplicon sequencing to build a mechanistic picture of community response and recovery. A core deliverable is a decision-support protocol enabling plant operators to interpret simple online measurements (VFA:alkalinity ratio, biogas composition) in terms of underlying microbial state. Two small agricultural biogas plants in Vojvodina serve as field validation sites. The project involves one doctoral student and two master's students.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad, Serbia
Biogas Plant Ratarstvo Bačka d.o.o., Srbobran, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Mapping and Co-Digestion Testing of Agro-Industrial Sludges for Small-Scale Biogas in Vojvodina and Southern Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGROBIOMATCH compiled a georeferenced inventory of food-processing and agricultural by-product streams available for anaerobic digestion within 80 km of the Vojvodina–Southern Hungary border. Tadić's team led the laboratory characterisation workpackage: 34 substrates were collected from partner plants, characterised for VS, COD, nitrogen, LCFA, and BMP-tested in standardised 250 mL batch assays. The database of substrate parameters and BMP values was made publicly available. Pilot co-digestion trials at three partner sites compared predicted and observed methane yields. The project supported two master's theses at the University of Novi Sad and produced practical substrate selection guidelines distributed to regional agricultural extension services.
partners: Department of Environmental Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary
Agro-Environmental Centre Baja, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Vojvodina, Serbia

projects.title: Grain Boundary Engineering in ODS Ferritic Steels for High-Temperature Structural Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ODSBOUND investigates the relationship between sintering parameters, grain boundary character distribution, and high-temperature creep resistance in Fe–Cr ODS ferritic alloys. The project combines dilatometric sintering experiments, EBSD-based grain boundary analysis, and creep testing at 650–800 °C to establish quantitative processing–microstructure–property links. A key objective is to determine whether targeted multi-step sintering can increase the fraction of coincidence-site-lattice boundaries and thereby reduce grain boundary diffusion rates at service temperatures. The project involves three institutions in Serbia and one partner in the Czech Republic. It supports one Ph.D. student and two undergraduate thesis projects, and provides access to SPS and high-temperature mechanical testing infrastructure.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš
Institute for Nuclear Sciences Vinča, Belgrade
Institute of Physics of Materials, Brno, Czech Republic

projects.title: Strengthening Powder Metallurgy Capacities at Universities in Serbia through Equipment Sharing and Joint Research
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project supported the acquisition of a dilatometric sintering furnace and associated gas handling equipment for the Department of Materials Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, Novi Sad, and established a formal equipment-sharing protocol with the Faculty of Technical Sciences, also in Novi Sad. Joint experimental campaigns were conducted on oxide-dispersion-strengthened and WC–Co powder systems. Ivković contributed experimental design and analysis for the ODS component of the project, focusing on porosity evolution and densification kinetics. The project also funded two short-term staff exchanges with AGH University of Science and Technology in Kraków.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
AGH University of Science and Technology, Kraków

projects.title: Bainite Formation Kinetics and Austenite Stabilisation in Medium-Manganese TRIP Steels for Lightweight Structural Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the interplay between prior austenite grain refinement, deformation-induced defect density, and carbon partitioning during isothermal bainite formation in medium-manganese TRIP steels. Using quenching dilatometry, ex situ XRD, and EBSD, transformation kinetics were determined for carbon contents from 0.15 to 0.25 wt% and Mn from 3.5 to 6 wt%. The aim was to establish composition–process windows that simultaneously achieve retained austenite fractions above 15 vol% and mechanical stability sufficient for cold-forming. Three PhD students were supported and collaborative dilatometric campaigns were carried out with partner laboratories in Budapest and Timișoara.
partners: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Budapest University of Technology
Faculty of Materials Science and Engineering, Politehnica University of Timișoara

projects.title: Microstructure-Controlled TRIP Steel Processing for Automotive Structural Members: From Laboratory to Pilot Scale
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral Interreg project aiming to transfer laboratory-scale two-step heat treatment protocols for TRIP steels to pilot strip-processing conditions at a Hungarian partner facility. Kosanović led the work package on microstructure characterisation and process validation, coordinating XRD and dilatometric measurements in Novi Sad and EBSD analysis in Budapest. The project involved heat treatment trials on strips of 50–200 mm width, mechanical testing according to EN ISO 6892-1, and correlation of pilot-scale results with laboratory dilatometric data. Outputs included a process parameter database covering intercritical annealing temperature tolerance ±20 °C and isothermal holding time ±60 s.
partners: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Budapest University of Technology

projects.title: Defect Identification and Fatigue Strength Prediction in Dissimilar Aluminium FSW Joints for Automotive Panels
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the relationship between process parameter-induced microstructural defects and fatigue performance in dissimilar 6xxx/5xxx FSW joints intended for automotive body panel applications. Activities include systematic parametric welding trials on the department FSW platform, full EBSD characterisation of nugget and TMAZ zones, X-ray diffraction residual stress mapping, and four-point bending fatigue testing of standardised specimens. A semi-empirical fatigue life model is being developed that incorporates nugget hardness minimum, kissing bond length, and residual stress asymmetry as input variables. Industrial relevance is established through collaboration with an automotive component supplier in the Vojvodina region. A total budget of approximately 4.8 million RSD funds equipment consumables, a Ph.D. student stipend, and three international short-term visits.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Adriacar Components d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Aluminium Panel Joining Technologies for Cross-Border Transport Manufacturing Clusters
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project bringing together research groups and SMEs in Vojvodina and southern Hungary to evaluate and compare solid-state joining technologies — friction stir welding, self-piercing riveting, and flow drill screw joining — for lightweight aluminium structures in road transport vehicles. Knežević leads the work package on microstructural qualification, responsible for standardised cross-sectional characterisation, hardness mapping, and tensile coupon testing of FSW joints produced at partner facilities. Results feed into a joint design guideline document intended for regional SMEs. The project includes two student mobility exchanges between Novi Sad and Pécs.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

Pannonia Light Structures Kft., Pécs

projects.title: Wear Regime Mapping of Hard PVD Coatings for Cold-Forming Tool Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates load- and temperature-dependent wear transitions in TiAlN and CrN coatings deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering, targeting operating conditions representative of cold-forming tooling in regional manufacturing. The work involves systematic pin-on-disc campaigns at controlled temperatures up to 500 °C, construction of quantitative wear maps, and microstructural characterisation of worn surfaces by SEM-EDS and XRD. Ksenija Mijatović is responsible for all tribological experiments, wear map construction, and SEM characterisation as part of her doctoral research. The project is coordinated by her supervisor at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, with contributions from the Institute for Materials Testing in Belgrade. Results are intended to provide process selection guidelines for companies producing coated forming tools.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Materials Testing, Belgrade

projects.title: Thermodynamic and Kinetic Basis for Inclusion Control in High-Cleanliness Steels Produced by EAF Route in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to establish validated thermodynamic and kinetic models for non-metallic inclusion formation and removal during ladle refining of high-cleanliness steel grades produced via the electric arc furnace route in Serbian steelmaking. Activities include laboratory equilibration experiments, industrial sampling campaigns at a domestic steel producer, and development of a slag composition optimisation tool. Stanković is responsible for the laboratory equilibration experiments, SEM-EDS inclusion characterisation, and FactSage modelling tasks. Results are intended to provide practical slag chemistry guidelines that can be implemented without major capital investment by regional steelmakers. The project is coordinated by the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Materials Testing, Belgrade
Balkan Steel and Alloys d.o.o., Smederevo

projects.title: Corrosion Failure Mechanisms of High-Strength Fasteners in Aggressive Industrial Atmospheres
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the conditions under which high-strength structural fasteners fail by stress corrosion cracking or hydrogen embrittlement when exposed to polluted industrial atmospheric environments typical of petrochemical and power-generation facilities in the Vojvodina region. Research activities include laboratory simulation of atmospheric condensate chemistries, slow strain rate testing of candidate steel grades, electrochemical hydrogen permeation measurements, and post-fracture microscopic characterisation. Miloš Ivanović is responsible for the SSRT experimental programme and fractographic documentation tasks. The project consortium includes partners from the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad, the Institute for Testing of Materials Belgrade, and an industrial observer from the fastener manufacturing sector.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade
Kovačnica Vojvodina d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Mushy-Zone Permeability and Flow in Light-Alloy Billet Casting
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MUSFLOW aimed to improve quantitative understanding of interdendritic liquid flow in the mushy zone during DC casting of aluminium alloys by combining experimental permeability measurements with pore-scale lattice-Boltzmann simulations and macro-scale solidification models. The project produced a set of permeability correlations for AA2xxx, AA6xxx, and AA7xxx alloy families as functions of solid fraction and SDAS, and implemented these in a two-dimensional macrosegregation solver validated against laboratory ingot castings. A postdoctoral researcher and two doctoral students were supported under the project. Results contributed to five journal publications and informed an ongoing collaboration with a casting company from the Vojvodina region.

projects.title: Cross-Border Transfer of Aluminium Casting Process Knowledge for SMEs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: ALICAST-IPA addressed the need for improved casting process competence in small and medium-sized foundries in the Banat region on both sides of the Romanian–Serbian border. The project organised technical training workshops, established a shared database of casting defect case studies, and developed a simplified process monitoring tool for use on the casting floor. Rajić led the work package on microstructure characterisation, providing metallographic analysis services and short-term technical secondments for engineers from partner companies. The project resulted in training of 34 foundry technicians and the creation of a bilingual (Romanian–Serbian) casting defect atlas distributed in print and digital form.

projects.title: Optimisation of Spark Plasma Sintering Parameters for Phase-Pure Hydroxyapatite–Bioglass Scaffolds with Controlled Porosity
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish processing windows for spark plasma sintering of HA–bioglass composites that simultaneously achieve high relative density, minimal TCP formation, and controlled open porosity suitable for osteoconduction. Experimental work included systematic variation of SPS temperature, pressure, dwell time, and BG particle size, complemented by thermodynamic modelling of the HA–SiO2 reaction. Porous scaffolds were produced using PMMA and naphthalene as sacrificial pore formers. In-vitro dissolution tests in SBF and uniaxial fatigue tests were performed to screen formulations for bone substitute suitability. The project supported two MSc students and produced five journal publications.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Technical Sciences, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Characterisation Platform for Calcium Phosphate Bioceramics
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: BIOCROSS established shared protocols for characterising calcium phosphate–based ceramic materials at partner laboratories in Novi Sad and Timișoara. The project harmonised procedures for XRD-based phase quantification, SBF dissolution testing, and compressive strength measurement. Đorđe Pekez led the work package responsible for mechanical characterisation and fatigue testing, contributing scaffold samples and test protocols. The collaboration produced a joint database of reference materials and a published comparative study of characterisation variability across laboratories. Exchange visits involved two researchers from each institution.
partners: Politehnica University of Timișoara, Faculty of Chemistry and Environmental Engineering, Romania
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Valorisation of Oilseed By-Products from the Vojvodina Food Chain through Supercritical and Pressurised Extraction Technologies
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project targets the recovery of lipophilic bioactives — tocopherols, phytosterols, and carotenoids — from sunflower, rapeseed, and hemp press cakes produced by cold-pressing facilities in Vojvodina. Work packages cover raw material characterisation, bench-scale extraction optimisation, solubility and kinetic modelling, and a preliminary techno-economic analysis for a regional contract extraction service model. Aleksa Ninkov leads the extraction process design and modelling tasks, with responsibility for the bench-scale experimental programme and for integrating kinetic data into process simulation models. The project involves collaboration with the Institute of Food Technology in Novi Sad and a regional oilseed pressing cooperative as an industrial observer.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Vojvodina Oilseed Cooperative Čenej
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Scale-Up Methodology for Supercritical Fluid Extraction of Phytoactives: From Laboratory to Pilot Plant
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad and the Department of Chemical Engineering at the University of Pannonia in Veszprém, this project aimed to develop a shared protocol for translating bench-scale supercritical extraction parameters to pilot-plant operation. Ninkov led the Serbian work package, which covered pilot-scale experimental campaigns at an industrial partner's facility and construction of a unified mass balance and energy model applicable to both CO₂ and CO₂/co-solvent systems. Outputs included a joint technical guideline document, training workshops for engineers from both countries, and a co-supervised master's thesis. The project also produced a joint database of extraction curves for sunflower and rapeseed by-products accessible to both partner institutions.

Extratum Kft., Budapest
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Green Solvent Selection for Azeotropic Separation Processes in the Pharmaceutical and Fine Chemical Industries
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a computational–experimental workflow for identifying bio-derived and low-toxicity entrainers for azeotropic and extractive distillation. COSMO-RS screening was combined with targeted VLE measurements and energy optimisation in process simulation to evaluate at least 60 candidate solvents across eight industrially relevant azeotropic systems. The laboratory acquired a high-pressure optical VLE cell and extended its GC calibration database for oxygenated bio-solvents. The project produced 6 journal papers, trained 2 PhD students, and delivered a freely available Python screening tool for entrainer ranking. A direct link was established with a local pharmaceutical manufacturer to provide real separation challenges for the case studies.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technology

Farmavita d.o.o. Novi Sad

projects.title: Phase Equilibrium Data and Separation Process Design for Organic Carbonate Solvent Recovery
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research project with Karbosol d.o.o., a company producing electrolyte-grade organic carbonates, to generate phase equilibrium data and distillation design recommendations for the recovery and purification of dimethyl carbonate, ethylene carbonate, and propylene carbonate from reaction mixtures. Work includes VLE measurements for six binary and two ternary systems, COSMO-RS and NRTL modelling, and design of a two-column distillation sequence validated by simulation against pilot plant data provided by the company. Results are subject to a confidentiality agreement for a period of three years.
partners: Karbosol d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Moisture-Stable Encapsulated Feed Additives by Integrated Fluidised-Bed Processing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop fat- and polysaccharide-coated versions of three hygroscopic feed additive premixes (lysine sulphate, sodium bicarbonate and a B-vitamin blend) using pilot-scale fluidised-bed coating. Process windows were defined based on coating level, bed temperature and spray rate. Moisture-sorption isotherms were used to predict shelf-life under warehouse storage conditions representative of the Pannonian region (summer: 35 °C, 70 % RH). A simplified economic assessment compared the cost of encapsulation with the financial loss from premix caking in unprotected storage. Two journal publications and one conference paper were produced; one MSc thesis was completed within the project.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Agroprodukt Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Exchange on Drying and Encapsulation Technologies for Functional Food Powders
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad and the Department of Food Engineering at the University of Szeged. The Novi Sad team led the work package on characterisation and modelling of moisture-sorption behaviour, contributing sorption isotherm data for eight pilot-scale spray-dried and granulated prototypes of fruit and dairy powders. The Szeged team led a parallel work package on thermal analysis. Joint training events for industry representatives from both countries were organised, and shared access to DVS equipment at both sites was established. Three co-authored publications resulted from the partnership.
partners: Department of Food Engineering, University of Szeged
Délvidéki Élelmiszeripari Klaszter, Subotica

projects.title: Microreactor-Based Continuous Production of Biodiesel Using Regenerable Solid Acid Catalysts
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates the design and optimisation of continuous-flow microreactor systems for biodiesel synthesis from low-grade feedstocks rich in free fatty acids, where conventional base catalysts are unsuitable. The work encompasses catalyst preparation and characterisation, microreactor hydrodynamics, kinetic modelling including deactivation, and periodic regeneration protocols. Lidija Ivanović contributes to the experimental catalyst deactivation campaigns and RTD characterisation tasks. The project is coordinated by Prof. Dragan Tešić at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, and involves a collaboration with the Faculty of Technology in Leskovac for feedstock preparation experiments.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Niš – Campus Leskovac

projects.title: Freeze-Crystallisation Unit Operations for Gentle Bioprocess Stream Concentration
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the application of progressive and suspension freeze-crystallisation to the concentration of thermolabile bioprocess streams including lactic acid broth, kombucha, and fermented plant extracts. Research tasks include experimental characterisation of ice crystal growth kinetics and solute inclusion across representative multicomponent media, development and validation of semi-empirical inclusion models, and evaluation of energy efficiency in bench- and pilot-scale crystalliser configurations. Svetlana Marković is responsible for cryomicroscopy experiments, distribution coefficient determination by chromatographic analysis, and model parameter fitting. The project is coordinated by Prof. Miroslav Vukić at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, with a collaboration partner at the Faculty of Industrial Chemistry and Environmental Engineering, Politehnica University Timișoara.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Industrial Chemistry and Environmental Engineering, Politehnica University Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Starch–Protein Reactive Extrusion for Biodegradable Food Packaging with Defined Barrier Profiles
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STARPAK addresses the formulation and process design of reactive extruded starch–protein blends intended for single-use food packaging applications where petroleum-based films are currently standard. The project uses a central composite experimental design covering corn and wheat starch as base polymers and pea and sunflower protein concentrates as secondary phases, with citric acid as a reactive compatibiliser. Key objectives include establishing quantitative process–property correlations, developing an in-line monitoring framework combining slit-die rheometry and NIR spectroscopy, and producing prototype trays and wraps suitable for cold-chain dry food products. Life-cycle inventory data are collected to support a preliminary environmental impact comparison with conventional packaging. The project supports two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technology, University of Niš
Ambalažna Industrija Vojvodine d.o.o. (packaging company, Novi Sad)

projects.title: Cross-Border Valorisation of Agricultural Protein Co-Streams into Biopolymer Packaging Materials
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: BIOCROSS addresses sunflower and rapeseed protein meal generated as co-products in oilseed processing in the Vojvodina and western Romania regions. The project characterises the functional properties of these protein streams (solubility, water absorption, thermal denaturation profiles) and tests their performance as the protein phase in reactively extruded starch–protein blends. Lalić's team leads the work package on extrusion processing and mechanical characterisation, while partners in Timișoara focus on protein fractionation and upstream characterisation. The project aims to produce a technical specification document usable by regional packaging manufacturers and to demonstrate a 50-kg pilot batch. Three joint publications are planned across the project duration.
partners: Politehnica University of Timișoara, Department of Food Engineering

projects.title: Functionalised Adsorbent Beds for Purification of Organic Micropollutant-Contaminated Industrial Process Condensates
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the preparation and characterisation of surface-modified activated carbons and natural zeolites for use in fixed-bed columns treating pharmaceutical and corrosion-inhibitor micropollutants in industrial process condensates typical of the food processing and chemical manufacturing sectors in Vojvodina. Core activities included systematic isotherm and breakthrough curve measurement for a panel of twelve target compounds, multi-cycle regeneration studies, and development of a corrected Bohart–Adams column design procedure valid across laboratory and pilot scales. A six-month pilot test was conducted in collaboration with an industrial partner operating a condensate stream containing ibuprofen, metformin, and benzotriazole. The project produced eight journal publications and one conference contribution and trained two master's students.

projects.title: Regional Agricultural Waste-Derived Adsorbents for Emerging Pollutant Removal from Industrial Waters
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: REGSORP is a cross-border cooperation project developing adsorbent materials from agricultural residues available in the Hungarian–Serbian border region (sunflower husk, corn cob, wheat straw). Vladan Đurić leads the work package on column design and pilot-scale validation, responsible for producing standardised fixed-bed adsorption testing protocols and transferring laboratory-derived Thomas and Bohart–Adams parameters to a mobile pilot unit operated at partner sites. The project targets three micropollutant classes: pharmaceuticals, corrosion inhibitors, and pesticide degradation products. Deliverables include a joint test protocol document, two peer-reviewed publications, and a short course on adsorbent column design delivered to industrial engineers at both partner institutions.

projects.title: Biomass Saccharification Process Intensification for Vojvodina Agricultural Residues
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the full process chain from mild organosolv pre-treatment to fed-batch enzymatic saccharification for three Vojvodina agricultural residues: wheat straw, sunflower stalks, and corn stover. Key objectives included developing pre-treatment condition maps relating structural characterisation metrics to enzymatic digestibility, calibrating and validating the mechanistic fed-batch hydrolysis model, and demonstrating the process at 5 L reactor scale. A secondary objective was to evaluate enzyme recycling by ultrafiltration. The project involved four researchers from the Faculty of Technology and one from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, and produced seven journal publications and two conference contributions.

projects.title: Integrated Valorisation of Lignocellulosic Side Streams from Agro-Industrial Processing in the Danube Region

projects.summary: LIGNOVALUE brought together four institutions from Serbia and Hungary to develop integrated biorefinery concepts for lignocellulosic side streams from agro-industrial processors (sunflower processing, maize starch production). The project also included techno-economic screening of selected process routes and a joint training school for early-career researchers held in Novi Sad and Pécs. Results were disseminated to regional agro-industrial stakeholders through two workshops.

projects.title: Continuous Pharmaceutical Granulation Processes: Parameter Monitoring and Control for Small-Scale Manufacturing
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aims to establish validated NIR-based monitoring protocols for continuous wet granulation at laboratory scale, targeting formulation types relevant to regional generic drug manufacturers. Work packages cover calibration model development, uncertainty quantification, and a comparative study of twin-screw versus high-shear batch granulation for three model drugs. Maja Andrić contributes to spectral data collection, PLS model training, and the preparation of standard operating procedures for the NIR calibration workflow. projects.title: Valorisation of Vojvodina Oilseed By-products Through Supercritical Fractionation for Nutraceutical Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project examined cold-press cakes from sunflower, pumpkin, and hemp cultivated in Vojvodina as feedstocks for supercritical CO₂ fractionation. Activities included characterisation of raw material variability across three growing seasons, optimisation of fractionation conditions for tocopherol- and phospholipid-enriched fractions, and a preliminary techno-economic analysis of a hypothetical 50 L/day extraction unit. A total of 27 raw material samples from six registered producers were analysed. The project trained two MSc students and produced four peer-reviewed publications. projects.title: Bridging Laboratory and Pilot Scale in Supercritical CO₂ Extraction: Validated Models for Bioactive Lipid Recovery
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project addresses the well-documented difficulty of predicting extraction performance when moving from bench-scale (0.5 L) to pilot-scale (5–10 L) extractors. The work combines experimental extraction kinetics with computational fluid dynamics modelling to improve the predictive accuracy of the BIC and Sovová models under pilot conditions. Three lipid-rich matrices are used as model systems: grape seed cake, black cumin seed, and evening primrose seed. Experimental campaigns at both scales generate datasets for model validation. A web-accessible process simulation tool is planned as a project output. The project supports one PhD student and involves a short-term research visit to the University of Maribor.

Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Mechanistic Dissolution–Absorption Coupling for Amorphous Solid Dispersions of Lipophilic Drugs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how experimentally measured supersaturation-precipitation kinetics of amorphous solid dispersions in biorelevant media can be systematically translated into PBPK model inputs to improve the prediction of oral bioavailability for BCS Class II compounds. Work packages cover biorelevant dissolution assay development, parameterisation of precipitation inhibition by polymeric carriers, integration of results into GastroPlus and PK-Sim, and prospective validation against in vivo datasets available in the open literature. Čolić is responsible for experimental dissolution work and model construction for the carvedilol and fenofibrate model compounds. The project runs at the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad with a collaborating group at the University of Pécs.

Department of Pharmaceutical Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Stability Prediction of Amorphous Oral Formulations Under Real Moisture Conditions

projects.summary: The project aimed to establish a predictive framework linking thermodynamic miscibility parameters, measured by DSC and IGC, with long-term physical stability of spray-dried amorphous dispersions stored at realistic humidity profiles (cycling between 40% and 75% RH). A small software tool was developed that takes Flory–Huggins χ, Gordon–Taylor k for water, and storage conditions as inputs and returns an estimated crystallisation onset time. The project trained two PhD students and produced six peer-reviewed publications. The approach is being adapted for implementation in early pharmaceutical development workflows.

projects.title: Enzymatic Synthesis of Functional Phospholipids for Liposomal Drug Carriers

projects.summary: ENLIPO addressed the complete production chain for pharmaceutical-grade phospholipids, from enzyme immobilisation and reaction optimisation through preparative purification to liposome manufacture and characterisation. A collaboration with the Department of Pharmacy at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, provided access to in vitro cell-based permeability assays. The project supported one doctoral student and one postdoctoral researcher and produced six peer-reviewed publications. projects.title: Pilot-Scale Continuous Production of Phospholipid Liposomes for Pharmaceutical Applications

projects.title: Nitrosamine Safety Assessment Framework for Generic Pharmaceutical Manufacturers in the Western Balkans

projects.summary: The project developed practical risk assessment tools and analytical reference methods for nitrosamine impurity control, targeting small and medium-sized generic pharmaceutical manufacturers in Serbia who lack the in-house expertise to implement ICH M7-compliant programmes. projects.title: Optimisation of Starch Hydrolysis Processes for Tailored Saccharide Product Streams in the Vojvodina Cereal Processing Sector
