projects.summary: The project examined how process parameters in enzymatic starch hydrolysis—enzyme type, dose, temperature, pH, and dry-matter content—affect the composition of saccharide product streams in cereal starch processing relevant to Vojvodina producers. Pilot-scale trials were conducted at the Faculty of Technology, with analytical work covering sugar profiling by HPLC, rheology, and by-product stream characterisation. Dušan Perišić contributed to pilot reactor experiments, kinetic data analysis, and preparation of technical reports. The project generated datasets used in two subsequent journal publications and formed the basis for a student internship programme with one regional food ingredient producer.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Agrostar Ingredients d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer for Malto-Oligosaccharide By-product Utilisation in Starch Processing Industries
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MALOCHAIN addressed the valorisation of oligosaccharide-rich by-product streams from glucose syrup and maltodextrin production facilities in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The project combined process analysis, analytical characterisation of by-product streams, and feasibility assessment of fermentative and functional food applications. Perišić was responsible for by-product stream sampling and characterisation at the Serbian partner site, pilot-scale fermentation trials, and co-authoring deliverable reports. The project involved two site visits to the Hungarian partner laboratory and contributed data feeding into the group's ongoing modelling work on continuous starch processing.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Food Science, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Keménytő Kft., Hajdúböszörmény, Hungary
Vojvođanski Skrobni Kombinat d.o.o., Srbobran, Serbia

projects.title: Acrylamide Formation and Mitigation Strategies in Extruded Cereal Snacks: From Substrate Chemistry to Process Design
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the relationship between raw material composition—specifically reducing sugar type and free amino acid profile—and acrylamide formation across a range of barrel temperature profiles in twin-screw extrusion of corn, wheat and triticale blends. Mitigation strategies including asparaginase pre-treatment, calcium salt addition and process parameter optimisation were evaluated both individually and in combination. Analytical work covered LC-MS/MS acrylamide quantification, amino acid profiling by RP-HPLC, and RTD measurement. A predictive kinetic model was developed and validated on pilot-scale equipment. The project resulted in four journal publications and two conference contributions.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Fermentability and Prebiotic Potential of Dietary Fibre Fractions from Vojvodina-Grown Pseudocereals
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project characterised arabinoxylan and beta-glucan fractions from buckwheat, amaranth, and teff cultivated in Vojvodina, establishing links between fine molecular structure and fermentation outcomes in pH-controlled in vitro colonic models. Work packages covered agronomic variation in fibre content, fractionation process optimisation, structural characterisation by NMR and methylation analysis, in vitro fermentation with multi-donor inocula, and application of selected fractions in gluten-free bread prototypes. Deliverables included a compositional database of Vojvodina pseudocereal fibres, validated fermentation protocols, three peer-reviewed publications, and a set of bread formulations evaluated for fibre content, technological quality, and in vitro fermentability.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer on Fibre-Enriched Gluten-Free Cereal Products
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border collaboration between the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad and the Department of Food Engineering at the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences compared gluten-free bread formulation practices and dietary fibre analytical methods used in Serbia and Hungary. The project standardised in vitro digestion and fermentation protocols between the two laboratories, produced a joint training course for food industry technologists, and conducted a small consumer survey on fibre-enriched gluten-free products in both countries (n = 220 respondents per country). Jokić's team led the work package on in vitro fermentation protocol harmonisation. Two joint publications and one conference contribution resulted from the collaboration.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Department of Food Engineering, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő, Hungary

projects.title: Lactose Crystallisation Control in Dairy Powder Processing for Reduced Caking and Improved Reconstitution
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the relationship between crystallisation conditions during whey permeate and skim milk powder manufacture and the functional properties of the resulting powders, specifically hygroscopicity, caking propensity, and reconstitution behaviour. Work packages cover: characterisation of amorphous lactose content by complementary analytical methods; laboratory-scale crystallisation trials with controlled seeding; and modelling of crystallisation kinetics during spray drying using population balance equations. A secondary objective is to establish validated DVS and XRPD protocols suitable for routine quality control in dairy powder facilities. The project involves collaboration with the Department of Food Engineering at the University of Szeged and includes a short-term secondment programme for PhD students at both institutions.
partners: Department of Food Engineering, University of Szeged, Hungary
Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad (FINS)

projects.title: Crystallisation Defects in Confectionery: Linking Impurity Profiles to Crystal Habit and Texture
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A regionally funded project examining how the impurity composition of industrial sucrose (raffinose, betaine, invertase reaction products, and colour compounds) affects crystal habit, size distribution, and macroscopic texture in fondant and hard candy. The study combines bench-scale crystallisation experiments with impurity addition at concentrations representative of commercial sugar streams (0.01–0.2% w/w) and advanced characterisation by scanning electron microscopy, XRPD, and texture analysis. Results are used to develop a semi-quantitative impurity potency index to guide confectionery manufacturers in selecting appropriate sugar grades and storage conditions. The project supports one PhD student and one final-year undergraduate thesis.
partners: Department of Carbohydrate Food Engineering, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Dairy Exopolysaccharides as Functional Texture Agents: Structure–Function Relationships and Strain Selection for Industrial Application
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish quantitative relationships between EPS structural parameters (molecular weight, branching degree, monosaccharide composition determined by NMR and GC-MS) and functional performance (water-holding capacity, syneresis, G′) in set and stirred fermented dairy products. A collection of 64 EPS-producing strains from Serbian dairy environments was screened and the top 12 characterised in detail. Two strains were selected for pilot-scale validation trials in yoghurt and kefir matrices. The project also developed a rapid FTIR-ATR classification protocol for EPS type prediction without full acid hydrolysis. Results are being transferred into a strain repository maintained at the Faculty of Technology.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Exopolysaccharides in Sourdough Fermentation: Biosynthesis, Matrix Effects and Contribution to Bread Quality and Shelf Life
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project characterised EPS biosynthesis by heterofermentative lactobacilli in wheat, rye and spelt sourdough matrices, with particular attention to the influence of flour composition on EPS yield and structure. The study encompassed optimisation of fermentation parameters using response surface methodology, structural characterisation by NMR and FTIR-ATR, and baking trials measuring crumb firmness, specific volume, moisture retention and mould-free storage period. Three sourdough strains were benchmarked against commercially available starters. The project trained two doctoral students and produced five peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Starch Structural Dynamics in Pressure-Processed Legume and Potato Products During Refrigerated Distribution
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how high-pressure processing conditions interact with cold-chain temperature fluctuations to determine the resistant starch fraction, retrogradation rate and digestibility index in potato- and legume-based convenience foods. Laboratory-scale HPP trials are combined with pilot-line production runs and instrumented cold-chain simulations. The project develops and validates a predictive model (modified Avrami–Arrhenius) for RS dynamics under non-isothermal storage. A secondary objective is the characterisation of in-vitro fermentability of RS fractions generated under different HPP regimes. The consortium includes the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad, the Institute for Food Technology Novi Sad and the Faculty of Medicine Novi Sad. Results are intended to inform both process design and regulatory nutrition labelling of HPP convenience products in the Serbian and regional food industry.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Legume-Based Refrigerated Convenience Foods with Reduced Glycaemic Impact Through High-Pressure Processing
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: LEGUPRES is a cross-border cooperation project aimed at developing refrigerated convenience products based on Hungarian and Serbian legume varieties with improved nutritional profiles. The University of Novi Sad leads the work package on starch modification and digestibility assessment, while the Hungarian partner focuses on raw material characterisation and sensory evaluation. The project includes pilot production of chickpea and lentil patties and purees processed at 400–550 MPa, followed by in-vitro digestibility and texture studies. A joint training workshop for food industry technologists from both countries is part of the dissemination plan. The project has resulted in three jointly authored publications and two technology demonstration events held at the Science Technology Park Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Food Science, University of Szeged, Hungary
Vojvodina Food Cluster, Novi Sad

projects.title: Polymer–Oxide Composite Electrodes for Stable Capacitive Energy Storage
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the preparation and long-term stability of conducting polymer–metal oxide composite electrodes for supercapacitor applications, with emphasis on PANI–TiO₂ and PPy–MnO₂ systems. Key objectives included establishing structure–property relationships between deposition conditions and electrode performance, developing EIS-based diagnostic protocols for in-service condition monitoring, and building a semi-empirical degradation model applicable across multiple composite chemistries. Accelerated aging protocols were designed and validated against standard cycling data. The project supported two PhD students and resulted in four journal publications. Facilities at the Faculty of Technology were supplemented by SEM access at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade

projects.title: Flexible Polymer-Based Electrochemical Storage Elements for Printed Electronics
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project brought together electrochemistry and printed electronics groups from Serbia and Hungary to develop flexible supercapacitor electrodes compatible with roll-to-roll processing. The Novi Sad team was responsible for electrodeposition of conducting polymer composites on ITO-PET substrates and for electrochemical characterisation of assembled cells. Bending durability protocols were developed and standardised across partner laboratories. The project produced demonstrator cells with energy densities above 18 Wh kg⁻¹ in gel electrolyte and contributed to joint patent filing discussions, though no formal application was submitted. Two student internship exchanges were completed under the programme.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Physical Chemistry, University of Szeged
Printronics Research Centre, Pécs

projects.title: Photochemical Fate and Ecotoxicological Risk of Priority Pharmaceutical Micropollutants in Vojvodina Surface Waters
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PHARMSUN investigates the photochemical transformation of eight priority pharmaceutical compounds detected in Vojvodina surface waters, including antibiotics, antiepileptics, and antidiabetics, under realistic irradiation conditions incorporating seasonal light spectra, natural water matrix effects, and temperature variation. The project combines field monitoring at twelve sites on the Danube and Tisa rivers with controlled laboratory photodegradation experiments and LC-HRMS-based transformation product identification. Toxicological screening of irradiated water fractions uses a battery of bioassays including bioluminescence inhibition, algal growth inhibition, and zebrafish embryo acute toxicity. Outputs include a regional risk-based ranking of compounds and a publicly accessible TP spectral library. The project employs two doctoral students and collaborates with the Institute of Public Health Vojvodina.
partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Environmental Protection Agency of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Pharmaceutical Pollutant Loads and Degradation Potential in the Danube Catchment
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUPHARMA was a bilateral cross-border project jointly coordinated by the University of Miskolc (Hungary) and the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad. The project mapped pharmaceutical pollutant concentrations at 24 shared monitoring points along the Hungarian–Serbian stretch of the Danube and its tributaries, using harmonised UHPLC-MS/MS analytical protocols developed and validated by both partner laboratories. Marija Uzelac contributed to method validation, field sampling during three seasonal campaigns, and LC-HRMS profiling of transformation products detected in river samples. The project produced a joint database of occurrence data, a harmonised risk quotient assessment, and a set of recommendations for cross-border water quality management submitted to relevant environmental authorities in both countries.
partners: Department of Environmental Engineering, University of Miskolc, Hungary
Tisza River Basin Authority, Nyíregyháza, Hungary
Directorate for Water Resources Management of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Rational Solid-Form Selection for Poorly Soluble APIs: Integrated Screening and Scale-Up Workflows
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established a tiered screening workflow integrating computational co-former selection (hydrogen-bond propensity and complementary functionality scoring) with experimental LAG, solution, and spray-drying screening for five poorly soluble APIs provided by a local formulation company. Characterisation relied on in-house PXRD, DSC-TGA, and Raman mapping, supplemented by access to solid-state NMR at a partner facility. Successful co-crystals were scaled to 50–100 g by twin-screw extrusion and assessed for dissolution improvement and physical stability under ICH storage conditions. The project trained two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed papers and three conference contributions.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Belgrade
Farmaceutski Zavod Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner)

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Pharmaceutical Solid-State Science: Serbia–Hungary Joint Laboratory Initiative
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSFORM supported joint research mobility and shared instrumentation access between the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad and the Department of Pharmaceutical Technology at the University of Pécs. Radić led the work package on co-crystal characterisation methodology harmonisation, coordinating two joint experimental campaigns at Pécs (six-month stays of PhD students) and two reciprocal visits by Hungarian researchers to Novi Sad. The programme funded an upgrade to the laboratory's confocal Raman system (motorised stage, 785 nm laser line) and produced four co-authored publications and a joint summer school on pharmaceutical solid-state methods, attended by 34 students from both countries.
partners: Department of Pharmaceutical Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Continuous Enzymatic Production of Food-Grade Flavour Esters with Integrated Membrane Separation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj razvoj kontinualnog integriranog procesa za enzimsku sintezu kratkolančanih estara aroma sa in-situ odvođenjem vode kroz pervaporacionu membranu. Istraživanje je obuhvatalo: kinetičku karakterizaciju imobilisanih lipaza na različitim nosačima, optimizaciju operativnih uslova u reaktoru zapremine 2 L, integraciju PDMS membranske jedinice, i procenu tehno-ekonomske opravdanosti. Pilot postrojenje dizajnirano u okviru projekta testirano je u toku 500 radnih sati za sintezu butil-acetata i etil-heksanoata. Rezultati su primenjivi za mala i srednja preduzeća u sektoru aroma i prehrambenih aditiva.
partners: Tehnološki fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Esterification Process Intensification for Regional Flavour Industry: Cross-border Knowledge Transfer
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je finansirao prekograničnu saradnju između Tehnološkog fakulteta Univerziteta u Novom Sadu i Departmana za hemijsko inženjerstvo Univerziteta u Debrecinu u oblasti intenzifikacije procesa esterifikacije za prehrambenu industriju. Radni paket kojim je koordinirao prof. Tomić bavio se razmenom metodologije za dizajn reaktivnih destilacionih kolona i razvoj mikroreaktorskih sistema za brzo testiranje katalizatora. Organizovana su dva zajednička terenska poseta industrijskim postrojenjima za arome u Vojvodini i Hajdú-Bihar županiji, kao i tri zajedničke studentske radionice.
partners: Department of Food Science and Technology, University of Debrecen
Tehnološki fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Regionalna privredna komora Novi Sad

projects.title: Trace Metal Speciation in Calcareous Pannonian Soils: Building a Validated Stability Constant Database for Bioavailability Modelling
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project systematically measures stability constants for complexes of Zn²⁺, Cu²⁺, Mn²⁺, Fe²⁺/³⁺, Cd²⁺ and Pb²⁺ with the five most abundant low-molecular-weight organic acids found in Vojvodina calcareous soil pore water (citrate, malate, oxalate, succinate, gluconate). Potentiometry, UV-Vis spectrophotometry and isothermal titration calorimetry are used. Constants are critically evaluated against the NIST database and incorporated into an open-access, formatted dataset for MINEQL+ and MINTEQ. Field validation uses centrifuge pore-water extracts from 20 soil profiles under major Vojvodina crops (maize, sunflower, sugar beet). The project also produces a temperature-corrected dataset covering the 10–35 °C range.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Department of Soil Science, Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Department of Inorganic and Analytical Chemistry, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Micronutrient Cycling in Calcareous Agricultural Soils of the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project coordinated by the University of Szeged examining micronutrient (Zn, Cu, Mn, Fe) dynamics in calcareous agricultural soils on both sides of the Serbian–Hungarian border. The University of Novi Sad team, led by Nedić, was responsible for Work Package 2: laboratory determination of conditional stability constants under conditions representative of soils from the surveyed area, and integration of constants into site-specific MINEQL+ models. Field soil sampling was shared with Hungarian partners. Results were used to produce advisory leaflets for Vojvodina farmers on soil amendment strategies to correct Zn and Mn deficiencies without increasing Cd mobility.
partners: Department of Inorganic and Analytical Chemistry, University of Szeged, Hungary
Csongrád-Csanád County Agricultural Advisory Centre, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, Vojvodina, Serbia

projects.title: Реолошка оптимизација полисахаридних носача за активне козметичке супстанце
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Пројекат се бави систематском корелацијом хемијске структуре хидрофобно модификованих полисахаридних деривата са макроскопским реолошким и триболошким особинама у моделским козметичким формулацијама. Главни циљ је дефинисање квантитативних структурно-реолошких корелација применљивих у предиктивном пројектовању формулација. Рад обухвата синтезу серије деривата, реолошку карактеризацију, DWS мерења и сензорну процену на панелу. Резултати треба да обезбеде смернице за избор згушњивача у зависности од циљаног профила производа. Партнер је Хемијски одсек Природно-математичког факултета у Нишу.
partners: Природно-математички факултет, Универзитет у Нишу
Технолошки факултет, Универзитет у Новом Саду

projects.title: Non-Invasive Serum Biomarker Panel for Staging of NAFLD in the Western Balkans Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: NAFLD-MARK aimed to develop and validate a multianalyte serum panel—combining cytokeratin-18 fragments, ceramide species, adipokines, and standard biochemistry—for non-invasive discrimination of NAFLD stages in a regional cohort of 350 patients across three clinical sites in Serbia. The project funded expansion of the LC-MS/MS sphingolipidomics workflow and established a biobank of paired serum and liver biopsy specimens. Statistical modelling compared panel performance against existing scores (NFS, FIB-4, APRI) using biopsy as the reference standard. Secondary objectives included analysis of dietary patterns and physical activity as effect modifiers of biomarker performance. The project involved active collaboration with endocrinology and hepatology units at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Clinic for Gastroenterology and Hepatology, University Clinical Centre of Serbia, Belgrade
Institute of Biochemistry, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Metabolic and Histological NAFLD Determinants in Serbia and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: METAHEPA-CB was a cross-border collaboration between clinical research teams in Novi Sad and Timișoara designed to assemble a harmonised NAFLD patient registry and biobank across two healthcare systems. The project standardised biopsy grading protocols, biochemical assay platforms, and patient-reported dietary data collection using a unified electronic case report form. Tešić led the work package on metabolic phenotyping, overseeing hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp procedures and stable-isotope-based lipogenesis measurements in the Serbian cohort. Joint training workshops were organised for clinical staff at both sites. Data from this project contributed to the multicentre machine learning study published in 2022.
partners: Victor Babeș University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Timișoara, Romania
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
County Clinical Emergency Hospital Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Circadian Disruption and Metabolic Risk in Shift-Working Women in Vojvodina: A Prospective Cohort Study
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VojShift is a prospective cohort study following 489 female workers across four textile and food-processing factories in Vojvodina over five years, with follow-up assessments at 18, 36, and 60 months. The primary aim is to determine whether actigraphy-derived social jetlag predicts incident type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome beyond conventional risk factors. Secondary aims include characterising clock gene expression patterns in PBMCs and examining whether MTNR1B genotype modifies the association between shift exposure and glycaemic deterioration. The project involves three partner institutions and uses actigraphy, continuous glucose monitoring, laboratory metabolic profiling, and dietary assessment. Ethical approval was obtained from the Ethics Committee of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Department of Biochemistry, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Chronotype-Adjusted Screening Algorithms for Prediabetes Detection in Occupational Settings
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project aims to develop and internally validate a screening algorithm for prediabetes that incorporates chronotype and shift schedule information alongside standard clinical variables. A case-control design is used, enrolling 280 workers from occupational health clinics across Vojvodina—140 with confirmed prediabetes and 140 matched controls. Candidate predictors include chronotype questionnaire scores, actigraphy-derived sleep regularity, social jetlag, BMI, waist circumference, family history, and fasting glucose. Logistic regression and cross-validated classification tree methods are compared. If validated, the algorithm is intended for use by occupational physicians during routine annual health assessments without requiring expensive laboratory tests.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina – Occupational Medicine Unit

projects.title: Тубулски биомаркери као предиктори прогресије хроничне болести бубрега код хипертензивних болесника у Војводини
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Пројекат је обухватао проспективно праћење 150 хипертензивних болесника са раном ХББ из три центра на територији Војводине. Циљ је био утврдити предиктивну вредност комбинације урнарних тубулских маркера (NAG, NGAL, KIM-1, A1M) за прогресију ХББ током три године праћења. Поред клиничких мерења, реализована је стандардизација аналитичких протокола међу лабораторијама учесницама. Резултати су публиковани у два рецензована часописа и саопштени на двема конференцијама. Пројекат је такође омогућио формирање биобанке узорака урина за будуће протеомске анализе.
partners: Клиничко-болнички центар Нови Сад
Општа болница Суботица, Одељење за интерну медицину
Институт за јавно здравље Војводине, Нови Сад

projects.title: Regional Network for Renal Tubular Biomarker Standardisation in Early CKD
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project links nephrology and clinical biochemistry departments in Novi Sad, Subotica and Debrecen to harmonise pre-analytical and analytical protocols for urinary tubular biomarker measurement. The Novi Sad team leads work package 2, which covers external quality assurance and reference material preparation. The project includes joint recruitment of a patient cohort of 200 hypertensive CKD patients on both sides of the border, enabling the first comparative tubular biomarker dataset from two distinct healthcare systems with comparable patient demographics. Training workshops for laboratory staff and a shared electronic data capture platform are additional deliverables.
partners: Debreceni Egyetem, Belgyógyászati Klinika, Debrecen
Општа болница Суботица, Одељење за нефрологију

projects.title: Gut Microbiome Dynamics and Recovery After Helicobacter pylori Eradication in the Serbian Population
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MICROHELI is a three-year project funded under the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia Prizma programme, coordinated by the Department of Internal Medicine at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad. The project follows a prospective cohort of patients undergoing H. pylori eradication and collects fecal samples at multiple time points over twelve months. Research activities include 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, metagenomic shotgun sequencing in a subset, and analysis of short-chain fatty acid profiles in stool. Slobodan Grujić contributes to patient recruitment, sample collection, sequencing data preprocessing, and statistical analysis. The project also involves a dietary assessment component examining whether dietary habits in Vojvodina modulate dysbiosis severity.
partners: Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Biomarkers of Subclinical Myocardial Damage in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates the prevalence and determinants of subclinical myocardial fibrosis in an SLE cohort drawn from the Vojvodina region using quantitative cardiac MRI. The primary aim is to establish normative T1 and ECV reference ranges for the local scanning environment and to identify clinical, laboratory, and immunological predictors of elevated ECV. Secondary aims include longitudinal follow-up at 18 months to assess change in MRI-derived fibrosis markers in relation to disease activity and treatment modifications. Luka Paunović is responsible for patient recruitment, MRI data collection, and primary statistical analysis. The project is coordinated by Prof. Dr. Milica Đorđević.
partners: Department of Internal Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Department of Rheumatology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Department of Radiology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina

projects.title: Safe Medication Management at Care Transitions in Elderly Patients with Multimorbidity in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SAFEMED-AGE examined polypharmacy-related risks in elderly patients moving between primary and hospital care in four counties spanning the Hungarian-Serbian border region. Marija Marić led the work package on clinical risk assessment, coordinating data collection across two hospital sites in Vojvodina and contributing to the development of shared medication reconciliation protocols. The project enrolled approximately 1,200 patients across both countries, generated a harmonised electronic dataset of drug interaction events, and produced training materials for general practitioners and hospital ward staff. Results fed into recommendations for policy adaptation at both regional health authority levels. Partners included a health IT company and a nursing home network in Subotica.
partners: Department of Clinical Pharmacology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Health Centre of Subotica, Subotica, Serbia
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Pannonia MedData d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Mapping Multimorbidity and Inappropriate Prescribing in Older Adults Across Serbian Primary Care Regions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MULTIMED-SR is a multicentre descriptive and analytical study mapping the distribution of multimorbidity clusters and associated inappropriate prescribing practices among adults aged 65 or older registered with general practitioners across five Serbian regions (Vojvodina, Belgrade, Šumadija, Southern and Eastern Serbia, Western Serbia). Using routinely collected data from the national e-health platform and structured patient interviews, the project aims to identify regional disparities in polypharmacy prevalence, characterise the most common drug-disease and drug-drug interaction patterns, and assess the degree to which STOPP/START version 3 criteria are met in routine prescribing. A secondary aim is to develop region-specific deprescribing guidelines suitable for integration into continuing medical education programmes for general practitioners.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Serbia 'Dr Milan Jovanović Batut', Belgrade, Serbia
Department of Family Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Medicine, University of Niš

projects.title: Serum Ferritin as a Dynamic Prognostic Indicator in Hospitalised COPD Exacerbation Patients in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project aims to prospectively enrol 200 patients with acute COPD exacerbation across two clinical sites in Vojvodina, collecting serial ferritin measurements alongside a panel of inflammatory and iron-related parameters. Primary endpoints are in-hospital mortality, length of stay, and 90-day readmission. Secondary analyses will examine whether ferritin adds prognostic value beyond established scores such as CURB-65 adapted for COPD contexts. Vlaisavljević is responsible for patient recruitment, data collection, and primary statistical analysis. The project also includes a subgroup of patients with comorbid type 2 diabetes to explore whether metabolic context modifies the ferritin–outcome relationship. Results are expected to inform a future multicentre proposal.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin, Zrenjanin, Serbia

projects.title: Thyroid Dysfunction and Subclinical Cardiovascular Remodelling in Postmenopausal Women of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project enrolled 280 postmenopausal women from primary-care and specialist outpatient settings across Vojvodina in a prospective cohort study. Annual assessments include carotid-femoral pulse-wave velocity, 2D and 3D echocardiography with speckle-tracking analysis, 24-hour Holter ECG, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, and a panel of thyroid, lipid, and inflammatory biomarkers. The primary aim is to estimate the incidence of echocardiographic and vascular endpoints attributable to persistent subclinical hypothyroidism versus spontaneous TSH normalisation over three years. A nested case–control analysis will assess the role of selenium deficiency as a modifying factor. Results are expected to inform regional screening guidelines.
partners: Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases of Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Primary Health Centre Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Border Registry of Thyroid Disorders and Cardiometabolic Risk in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border initiative links the Faculty of Medicine Novi Sad with the University of Medicine, Pharmacy, Sciences and Technology of Târgu Mureș and the University Clinical Centre Timișoara to establish a shared registry of patients with thyroid disorders and associated cardiometabolic conditions. Valentina Mladenović leads Work Package 3, responsible for harmonisation of echocardiographic protocols and data quality assurance across sites. The registry will include at least 1,200 participants over three years, with standardised collection of imaging, laboratory, and patient-reported outcome data. Secondary analyses will examine regional differences in iodine and selenium sufficiency as determinants of cardiovascular phenotype in subclinical thyroid disease.
partners: University of Medicine, Pharmacy, Sciences and Technology of Târgu Mureș, Romania
University Clinical Centre Timișoara, Romania
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Clonal Haematopoiesis as a Modifiable Risk Factor in Early Atherosclerosis: A Prospective Vojvodina Cohort Study
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: NoviAthero is a prospective, single-centre cohort study aiming to recruit 500 adults aged 35–70 from cardiology and internal medicine outpatient services in Novi Sad. Participants undergo baseline targeted next-generation sequencing for CHIP, comprehensive lipid and inflammatory profiling, and carotid B-mode ultrasound, with follow-up visits at 12 and 24 months. The primary endpoint is annualised carotid intima-media thickness progression; secondary endpoints include incident major adverse cardiovascular events and changes in circulating inflammatory cytokines. Tibor Papp is responsible for participant recruitment, biological sample processing, and coordinating sequencing runs. The project is funded under the IDEAS programme of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
BioInformatics Unit, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Vitamin D Receptor Genotype as a Predictor of Relapse and Treatment Response in Inflammatory Bowel Disease in the Republic of Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established a prospective cohort of 200 IBD patients at three clinical centres in Serbia to evaluate whether VDR FokI, BsmI, TaqI, and ApaI genotypes predict one-year relapse, biologic therapy failure, and post-surgical recurrence. Biobanking of serum, stool, and colonic biopsies was conducted at enrolment and at relapse events. Secondary objectives included characterisation of gut microbiota composition by 16S sequencing across genotype groups, and development of a simple genotype-plus-vitamin D scoring model for relapse risk stratification. The project supported one doctoral student and generated pilot data for a planned Horizon Europe application.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Serbia, Belgrade
General Hospital Subotica

projects.title: Cross-Border Registry and Biobank for VDR Polymorphisms in Inflammatory Bowel Disease across the Western Balkans and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border initiative bringing together gastroenterology units in Serbia, Romania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina to build a harmonised registry and biobank for IBD patients with linked VDR genotype data, clinical outcomes, and serum vitamin D measurements. Jeremić leads the work package responsible for data harmonisation, genotyping standardisation, and joint statistical analysis. The registry protocol was published in 2024. Planned deliverables include a jointly authored clinical prediction rule and recommendations for vitamin D monitoring in IBD relevant to South-East European populations, where baseline vitamin D insufficiency rates are particularly high.
partners: University of Medicine and Pharmacy Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Faculty of Medicine, University of East Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina
Institute for Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Psychological Burden and Unmet Needs in Lupus Patients Across the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat PsyLUPUS-WB ima za cilj sistematičnu procenu psihološkog opterećenja i nezadovoljenih potreba pacijenata sa SLE u Srbiji, Bosni i Hercegovini i Severnoj Makedoniji. Bojan Ćirić rukovodi radnim paketom koji obuhvata razvoj i administraciju standardizovanih upitnika (PHQ-9, GAD-7, LupusQoL) u okviru multicentrične kohortne studije. Projekat uključuje i kvalitativan segment sa fokus grupama pacijenata i zdravstvenih radnika. Krajnji cilj je formulisanje regionalnih smernica za psihosocijalnu podršku integriranu u reumatološku zaštitu, prilagođenih zdravstvenim sistemima zemalja Zapadnog Balkana.
partners: Klinički centar Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Univerzitetski klinički centar Sarajevo
Klinički centar Majka Tereza, Skopje

projects.title: Central Venous Pressure Waveform Morphology as an Early Predictor of Right Ventricular Dysfunction in Septic Shock: A Multicentre Prospective Study
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to externally validate the CVPMS score derived in the 2025 single-centre study across three ICUs in Serbia and one in Romania. Approximately 300 patients with septic shock are enrolled. Primary endpoint is the AUC of CVPMS for echocardiographically confirmed right ventricular dysfunction at 24 hours, with secondary endpoints including ICU mortality and duration of vasopressor support. A sub-study examines whether incorporating waveform score into clinical decision-making alters attending physicians' haemodynamic interventions. The project also supports development of a semi-automated waveform segmentation tool for routine bedside monitors. Data are managed centrally at the University of Novi Sad and the final dataset will be made publicly available.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
University Hospital of Niš, Serbia
Military Medical Academy, Belgrade, Serbia
University Emergency Hospital, Bucharest, Romania

projects.title: Single-Session Biliary Clearance: Optimising Laparoscopic and Endoscopic Collaboration in Vojvodina Hospitals
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to standardise the laparoscopic-endoscopic rendezvous protocol across three hospitals in Vojvodina — the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, General Hospital Sombor, and General Hospital Zrenjanin — and to measure its effect on length of stay, stone clearance rates, and hospital costs compared with two-stage treatment. A shared clinical protocol was developed, nursing and anaesthesia staff were trained, and a prospective registry was established. Data collection covered 120 patients over 18 months. Secondary objectives included assessing fluoroscopy-related radiation exposure and developing a regional training module for the rendezvous technique.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Sombor
General Hospital Zrenjanin

projects.title: Viscoelastic-Guided Haemostatic Management in Major Abdominal Surgery: Toward a Regional Protocol
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project aims to develop and pilot-test a standardised ROTEM-guided haemostatic algorithm for elective major abdominal procedures performed at hospitals across Vojvodina. The work involves prospective data collection from three surgical centres, development of decision thresholds calibrated to locally available blood products and coagulation factors, and a structured training component for anaesthesiologists and scrub nurses. Đukić contributes to patient recruitment, data entry, and ROTEM sample collection and analysis at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina site. A draft algorithm document is planned for dissemination to participating hospitals in the final project year. The project does not involve a randomised trial; it is designed as a feasibility and consensus-building exercise prior to a future interventional study.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin
General Hospital Sombor

projects.title: Perfusion-Guided Colorectal Anastomosis: A Multicentre Randomised Trial and Predictive Modelling Platform
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The PERCO project funds the Serbian sites participating in the PERCO-RCT trial and supports development of the associated computational tools. Activities include standardised training of surgical teams in ICG fluorescence use, prospective data collection at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina and General Hospital Sombor, development and validation of the curve-analysis software and CNN-based segmentation tool, and preparation of the predictive model for external validation. The project also covers a biobank of intraoperative tissue samples from anastomotic margins for histological correlation with perfusion measurements. A dedicated data coordination unit manages trial data across Serbian centres and liaises with foreign partners.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
General Hospital Sombor, Serbia
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Data-Driven Anastomotic Safety in Colorectal Surgery: Cross-Border Evidence Synthesis and Technology Transfer
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANASTOM brings together surgical teams in Vojvodina and southern Hungary to harmonise intraoperative perfusion measurement protocols, share annotated case datasets, and jointly validate the XGBoost predictive model and CNN segmentation tool across patient populations on both sides of the border. The project includes a structured training programme for surgical residents at partner institutions, three joint workshops, and co-development of a clinical decision-support interface for the fluorescence laparoscopy platform. It also funds a small cohort study examining whether ethnically and metabolically distinct patient subgroups in the two countries show different perfusion kinetics after bowel resection.
partners: Department of Surgery, University of Pécs, Hungary
General Hospital Subotica, Serbia
Baranya County Teaching Hospital, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Optimising Wound Bed Preparation Protocols for Diabetic Foot Ulcers in the Vojvodina Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project aims to standardise wound bed preparation practices for diabetic foot ulcer patients treated in secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities across Vojvodina. Activities include prospective data collection from three clinical sites, microbiological profiling of ulcer biofilms at baseline and after debridement, and a structured comparison of NPWT parameter sets currently in use at participating centres. Nikolić contributes to patient enrolment, sample processing, and data entry, and has primary responsibility for the confocal microscopy component. An expected output is a regional clinical recommendation document and at least two peer-reviewed publications. The project is coordinated by the Department of Surgery, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Surgery, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin
Institute of Microbiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Fascial Scar Collagen Architecture and Incisional Hernia Recurrence: Mechanobiological Determinants
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project combines histomorphometry, second-harmonic generation microscopy, and ex vivo mechanical testing to determine which structural features of fascial scar collagen predict clinical recurrence after open mesh repair. Biopsy specimens are collected from patients enrolled at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina at the time of primary repair and, where revision surgery occurs, at recurrence. Quantitative fibre orientation indices and collagen subtype ratios are correlated with five-year recurrence status. A secondary aim is to develop a scoring system for intraoperative fascial quality assessment. The project involves collaboration with the Institute of Pathology and the BioImaging Core Facility at the Faculty of Sciences in Novi Sad.
partners: Institute of Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
BioImaging Core Facility, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Biomechanical and Biological Performance of Hernia Meshes: Comparative Long-Term Evaluation
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project evaluated nine polypropylene and polyester mesh types in a rabbit implantation model and retrospectively reviewed retrieved human explants from revision surgeries performed at two clinical centres in Vojvodina. Outcomes included morphometric assessment of fibrovascular ingrowth, macrophage infiltration, and residual mesh mechanical properties. Attenuated total reflectance infrared spectroscopy was used to characterise polymer degradation in long-term human explants. The project produced data directly informing mesh selection recommendations for open sublay repair. All animal experiments were approved by the Veterinary Directorate of Serbia.
partners: Department of Surgery, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin
Institute of Chemistry, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Стандардизација континуираног интраоперативног неуромониторинга у ендокриној хирургији: мултицентрична студија
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат је имао за циљ успостављање заједничког протокола за континуирани интраоперативни неуромониторинг у оперативном лечењу болести штитне жлезде и паращитастих жлезда у четири универзитетска центра на Западном Балкану. У оквиру пројекта развијени су стандардизовани обрасци за бележење интраоперативних електромиографских налаза, организована је заједничка обука хирургa и дефинисани критеријуми за значајни губитак сигнала. Планирано је укључивање 240 пацијената у проспективну студију. Резултати ће омогућити поређење исхода међу центрима и послужити као основа за израду регионалних смерница за примену IONM у ендокриној хирургији.
partners: Клиника за хирургију, Клинички центар Vojводине, Нови Сад
Универзитетска болница Осијек, Хрватска
Универзитетски клинички центар Сарајево, Босна и Херцеговина
Клинички центар Скопље, Северна Македонија

projects.title: Standardised Surgical Site Infection Surveillance Network for Elective Gastrointestinal Surgery in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project established a prospective, standardised SSI surveillance network across five hospitals in Vojvodina, covering elective gastrointestinal procedures. The network introduced harmonised data collection forms based on ECDC HAI-Net methodology, trained hospital infection control nurses, and created a shared electronic registry. Primary outputs included annual SSI incidence reports disaggregated by procedure type and hospital, a locally validated wound classification training module, and a publicly available anonymised dataset. The project also supported the development of the preoperative SSI risk score validated in subsequent work. Results were communicated to the Provincial Health Authority as evidence for policy recommendations on infection control staffing and antibiotic prophylaxis protocols.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin
General Hospital Sombor
General Hospital Vrbas

projects.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns in Surgical Site Infections Across the Serbia–Romania Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between surgical epidemiology and clinical microbiology teams in Vojvodina and Timișoara focused on characterising antimicrobial resistance in SSIs following elective gastrointestinal procedures at hospitals on both sides of the border. The project harmonised microbiological reporting standards, conducted joint whole-genome sequencing of selected resistant isolates, and produced a shared antibiogram for the cross-border region. Mirjana Marić led the work package responsible for clinical and epidemiological data collection, patient enrolment, and integration of microbiological results with surgical outcome data. The project contributed key data to the 2023 Infection and Drug Resistance publication and provided training for junior researchers from both countries in epidemiological methods.
partners: University of Medicine and Pharmacy Victor Babeș Timișoara, Romania
Institute of Microbiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin
County Emergency Clinical Hospital Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Senzitizacija bola i predikcija hroničnog postoperativnog bola nakon operacije ingvinalne hernije: biomarkeri, QST i psihološki faktori
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат SENSHER испитује вишеструке предикторе хроничног постоперативног бола у препони (CPIP) код пацијената подвргнутих елективној операцији ингвиналне херније. Главни циљ је да се интегришу квантитативне сензорне мере, серумски биомаркери неуроналне повреде (укључујући NfL) и психолошки упитници у јединствен предикторски модел. Студија прати 250 пацијената на КЦВ и у сарадничкој клиници у Нишу до 12 месеци после операције. Пројекат укључује поткомпоненту интервенције: фреквентни психоедукативни ресурс примењен у подузорку. Резултати ће послужити за израду скоринг алата за процену ризика применљивог у рутинском предоперативном прегледу.
partners: Klinički centar Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Klinika za hirurgiju, Klinički centar Niš
Institut za laboratorijsku medicinu, Klinički centar Vojvodine

projects.title: Augmented Renal Clearance and Beta-Lactam Dosing Optimisation in Serbian Intensive Care Units
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project addresses the under-recognised problem of augmented renal clearance (ARC) as a driver of sub-therapeutic beta-lactam exposure in adult ICU patients in Serbia. The project combines prospective pharmacokinetic sampling at two ICU sites (Clinical Centre of Vojvodina and the University Clinical Centre of Serbia), population PK modelling, and Monte Carlo simulation to generate locally validated dosing recommendations. A secondary objective is to evaluate cystatin C and novel urinary biomarkers as surrogate markers for ARC in routine care. The project also funds development of a prototype Bayesian dosing calculator adapted to resource-constrained TDM settings. The team comprises clinical pharmacists, intensivists, and a laboratory medicine specialist.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
University Clinical Centre of Serbia, Belgrade, Serbia
Institute for Laboratory Diagnostics, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Pharmacokinetic Data Sharing and Model Library for Critical Care Antibiotic Therapy
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PKBRIDGE is a cross-border collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs Medical School aimed at establishing a shared pharmacokinetic data repository and validated model library for antibiotics commonly used in critical care. The project collects prospective PK data from ICU populations on both sides of the border, harmonising sampling protocols and analytical methods. Validated population PK models are deposited in an open repository with standardised metadata. A joint training programme for clinical pharmacists in Bayesian forecasting software is delivered annually. The work package led by Sabo covers model development, validation, and the dosing simulation framework. The project also produces bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) clinical guidance documents on extended infusion strategies.
partners: University of Pécs Medical School, Hungary
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Baranya County Hospital, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Polifenolni metaboliti endemskih lekovitih biljaka Dinarida: hemijska karakterizacija i antioksidativni potencijal
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je usmeren na sistematsku fitohemijsku analizu odabranih endemskih vrsta iz rodova Centaurea, Stachys, Dianthus i Hypericum sa područja Dinarida i Panonske nizije. U okviru projekta primenjuju se HPLC-DAD i LC-MS/MS metode za identifikaciju i kvantifikaciju polifenolnih jedinjenja, a antioksidativni potencijal procenjuje se kombinacijom in vitro testova. Miloš Zdravković odgovoran je za pripremu uzoraka, instrumentalne analize i statističku obradu podataka. Rezultati projekta trebalo bi da posluže kao osnova za selekciju kandididata za dalja izolaciona i biološka ispitivanja, a planirane su i analize varijabilnosti hemijskog profila u zavisnosti od staništa i fenološke faze.
partners: Prirodno-matematički fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Institut za proučavanje lekovitog bilja 'Dr Josif Pančić', Beograd

projects.title: Optimisation of Solid Lipid Nanoparticle Systems for Dermal Delivery of Anti-Inflammatory Drugs with Low Aqueous Solubility
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish systematic structure–property relationships between lipid matrix composition and the dermal delivery performance of SLN-based formulations carrying poorly water-soluble NSAIDs. Work packages covered lipid screening and formulation development, physicochemical and structural characterisation (DLS, DSC, SAXS), in vitro and ex vivo skin permeation experiments, and cell-based anti-inflammatory activity assays. A secondary objective was to develop a predictive in vitro–ex vivo correlation model applicable to regulatory submissions. The project supported two PhD students and resulted in three journal publications. Collaboration with the Faculty of Technology (University of Novi Sad) provided access to pilot-scale homogenisation equipment.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Ljubljana, Slovenia

projects.title: Cross-Border Development of Nanotechnology-Based Topical Formulations for Musculoskeletal Conditions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between pharmaceutical research groups in Novi Sad and Pécs focused on the development and preliminary clinical assessment of nanoparticle-based topical gels intended for musculoskeletal pain management. The Novi Sad team (Kostić's group) was responsible for the formulation development and physicochemical characterisation work package, while the Pécs team contributed pharmacokinetic modelling and preliminary tolerability assessments in healthy volunteers. The project supported equipment procurement, staff exchange visits, and joint workshops for postgraduate students from both institutions.
partners: Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Pécs, Hungary
Institute for Rheumatology and Rehabilitation Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 Polymorphism Survey and Clinical Pharmacokinetic Implications in the Serbian Population
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project conducted a systematic population survey of CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 allele frequencies across Vojvodina, recruiting healthy volunteers through general practice surgeries in five municipalities. The study enrolled 420 participants, achieved genotyping for the full allele panel, and coordinated prospective pharmacokinetic sampling from psychiatric patients receiving antidepressants that are substrates of both enzymes. Outputs included allele frequency reference tables, a population pharmacokinetic model for sertraline, and a regional guidance document distributed to psychiatric practitioners. The project funded one postdoctoral researcher and contributed data to subsequent European collaborative comparisons.
partners: University Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
South Bačka District Institute of Public Health, Novi Sad

projects.title: Antidepressant Pharmacogenomics in South-Eastern Europe: Towards Regional Prescribing Harmonisation
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral research cooperation between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Zagreb School of Medicine, co-funded by the Serbian and Croatian ministries responsible for science. The project pooled existing pharmacogenomic datasets from both institutions and extended genotyping to include new participants from underrepresented subgroups, particularly ethnic Hungarians in Vojvodina and Bosnian Croats in Herzegovina via a partner subcontract. The central deliverable was a joint allele frequency comparison across four post-Yugoslav successor states, published in 2007, together with draft harmonised clinical guidance recommendations submitted to both national medicines agencies. Total budget was modest; the project supported researcher exchange visits and one PhD student co-supervision.
partners: Department of Clinical Pharmacology, University of Zagreb School of Medicine, Croatia
Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina

projects.title: Analytical Characterisation of Stability-Critical Cardiovascular Fixed-Dose Combinations for the Serbian Generic Pharmaceutical Sector
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aims to establish a systematic set of validated stability-indicating HPLC methods for five cardiovascular fixed-dose tablet combinations of regulatory relevance to Serbian generic manufacturers. Activities include forced degradation studies under ICH-prescribed stress conditions, chromatographic method development and full ICH Q2(R1) validation, and preliminary identification of degradation products using hyphenated techniques. The Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad serves as the lead institution. Tamara Malešević is responsible for experimental work on two of the five drug combinations and contributes to preparation of the technical reports submitted to the provincial funding body. Results are intended to be publicly available and directly transferable to quality-control laboratories.
partners: Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Quality Control of Medicines Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Fibre-Induced Microbiome Changes as Determinants of Oral Polyphenol Bioavailability
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FIBIOPOL aimed to establish quantitative relationships between specific prebiotic fibre interventions, gut microbiome compositional shifts, and the oral bioavailability of selected flavonoids using a stepwise platform of in vitro fermentation, Caco-2 permeability, rat in vivo studies, and a small human pilot. The project combined microbiome sequencing, targeted metabolomics, and pharmacokinetic modelling to generate data suitable for parameterising the in silico prediction tool developed in the final phase. Four graduate students and one postdoctoral researcher were funded through the project. Key deliverables included the simplified ODE pharmacokinetic model, a standardised fermentation protocol deposited as a methods preprint, and three peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Department of Pharmacy, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
BioSystems Research Institute, Belgrade
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Microbiome and Functional Food Network for Health Promotion
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MICROFEN is a cross-border cooperation project linking research groups in Novi Sad and Szeged to develop harmonised protocols for microbiome-based assessment of functional food ingredients. Ćirić leads the work package on polyphenol biotransformation assays, responsible for standardising the batch fermentation methodology, establishing shared quality control samples exchanged between laboratories, and co-supervising two student mobilities. The project also includes a stakeholder workshop series targeting food producers in the Vojvodina and Southern Great Plain regions to disseminate findings. A joint database of fermentation metabolite profiles under different fibre conditions is being developed as a common output.
partners: Institute of Food Biotechnology, University of Szeged
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Development Agency, Novi Sad

projects.title: Hydrazone-Based Compounds as Selective Cytotoxic Agents for Colorectal Cancer: From Synthesis to Mechanistic Characterisation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to identify and mechanistically characterise hydrazone derivatives with selective cytotoxicity toward colorectal cancer cell lines. Work packages covered QSAR-guided synthesis, in vitro biological evaluation across 2D monolayer and 3D spheroid models, metabolic stability profiling, and preliminary copper complexation studies. A library of over 60 compounds was synthesised and tested. The project funded one PhD student and supported two postdoctoral researchers part-time. Collaborating institutions provided microsomal assay infrastructure and fluorescence microscopy access. By project end, three lead compounds were identified with IC50 values below 5 µM against HCT 116 and selectivity indices above 5 over normal colon fibroblasts, providing a defined candidate set for subsequent pharmacological studies.
partners: Department of Chemistry, University of Novi Sad
Department of Biology and Ecology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, University of Ljubljana, Slovenia

projects.title: Benefit–Risk Optimisation for Regulatory Submission of Biosimilars in Central and Eastern Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: BIORSAFE aimed to develop a structured benefit–risk assessment toolkit tailored to biosimilar monoclonal antibody dossiers prepared for submission under the EMA centralised procedure and Serbian national procedures. The project produced a validated MCDA instrument for benefit–risk scoring, a gap analysis of Western Balkan regulatory frameworks against EMA requirements, and a regional training workshop series attended by 87 regulatory affairs professionals from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. The toolkit was piloted on three retrospective biosimilar dossier scenarios drawn from publicly available EPARs. A final guidance document was submitted to the Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia as input to a planned revision of the national biosimilar guideline.
partners: Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia (ALIMS), Belgrade
Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Pharmacy, Comenius University Bratislava, Slovakia

projects.title: Pharmaceutical Regulatory Capacity Building in Southeast Europe: Biosimilars and Advanced Therapies
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border capacity building project between Hungarian and Serbian institutions aimed at harmonising pharmaceutical regulatory education and practice, with a focus on biosimilar medicines and advanced therapy medicinal products. Đorđević led the work package on biosimilar regulatory competency assessment, which involved developing a 60-item competency framework and administering it to 145 pharmacy graduates and regulatory staff in both countries. The work package produced a comparative analysis of regulatory training gaps, a jointly taught online module (450 participants across two cohorts), and a published report submitted to the regional office of the WHO European Centre for Pharmaceutical Policy.
partners: Department of Pharmacognosy, University of Pécs, Hungary
National Institute of Pharmacy and Nutrition, Budapest, Hungary
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia (ALIMS), Belgrade

projects.title: Tick-Borne Encephalitis Risk Mapping and Prevention Planning in the Pannonian Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TBEPLAN brought together epidemiologists, entomologists, and regional public health authorities from Vojvodina and southern Hungary to produce harmonised cross-border TBE risk maps. The project compiled a joint case registry of 1,847 confirmed TBE cases from both sides of the border for 2010–2020, conducted joint tick surveillance at 36 sites, and developed a shared GIS web portal accessible to regional health authorities. Jovana Nedić led the work package on spatiotemporal analysis and risk map production. The project delivered risk maps at 1 km resolution and a joint prevention protocol adopted by the Vojvodina Provincial Institute of Public Health and two Hungarian county health centres.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
University of Szeged, Faculty of Medicine, Szeged, Hungary
Csongrád-Csanád County Government Office for Public Health, Szeged, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Health, Novi Sad

projects.title: Land-Use Dynamics and Vector-Borne Disease Risk in the Pannonian Lowland
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: LANDTICK is a three-year project funded under the PROMIS programme of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. The project tests the hypothesis that post-socialist land-use transitions in Vojvodina—including reforestation, canal-bank greening, and agricultural abandonment—have systematically altered tick habitat extent and connectivity, thereby driving observed shifts in TBE incidence patterns. The methodology combines annual remote-sensing derived land-cover maps with a 20-year TBE surveillance record and entomological field sampling at 30 permanent plots established across Vojvodina. Statistical outputs include predictive risk surfaces updated annually and a sensitivity analysis assessing how alternative reforestation policy scenarios would affect projected TBE incidence over a 20-year horizon.
partners: Institute of Lowland Forestry and Environment, Novi Sad
Department of Biostatistics, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Multigenerational Cardiovascular Risk Trajectories in Post-Industrial Vojvodinian Families: Biological and Social Determinants
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project extends the Vojvodinian household registry by recruiting a third-generation cohort (grandchildren aged 18–35) and linking their baseline cardiovascular profiles to archived data on grandparents and parents. Blood pressure, fasting lipids, fasting glucose, and anthropometric measurements are collected at two field visits. Occupational and residential histories are updated using administrative records. The analytical plan uses joint group-based trajectory modelling and structural equation modelling to disentangle biological from socially transmitted influences on cardiovascular risk accumulation. A secondary aim is to develop a family-level risk stratification score. The project involves collaboration with the Institute of Public Health Vojvodina and the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cardiovascular Risk Factor Trajectories in Ageing Populations Across the Danube Region: A Comparative Cohort Analysis
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CARDROUTES brought together epidemiological cohort teams from Novi Sad and Pécs to compare cardiovascular risk factor trajectory patterns in comparable post-industrial communities on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. Nina Gavrilović led the work package on harmonised trajectory modelling, standardising lipid, blood pressure, and anthropometric measurement protocols across the two registries. A joint analytical dataset of approximately 2,100 participants was constructed and analysed using GBTM. The project produced a comparative report for regional health authorities and two peer-reviewed publications. Fieldwork, data exchange, and dissemination activities complied with bilateral data protection agreements.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Health Sciences, Hungary
County Directorate of Public Health Baranya, Hungary

projects.title: One Health Surveillance of Antimicrobial Resistance Transmission on Mixed Livestock Farms in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FARMLINK is a three-year prospective cohort study following 200 mixed farming households across five Vojvodina districts. The project collects concurrent human, animal, and environmental samples at six-monthly intervals, applying whole-genome sequencing and metagenomics to characterise AMR transmission networks across the livestock–human interface. Key aims are to estimate household-level acquisition incidence, identify modifiable risk factors, and produce a quantitative transmission model suitable for evaluating intervention options. Partners include the Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, the Provincial Veterinary Institute, and epidemiology departments at the University of Pécs and Babeș-Bolyai University. The project also includes a farmer education module whose effectiveness will be assessed by comparing AMR acquisition rates between intervention and control arms in the second and third years.
partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Provincial Veterinary Institute, Novi Sad
University of Pécs Medical School, Hungary
Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania

projects.title: Cross-Border Transmission of Zoonotic Antimicrobial-Resistant Organisms between Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANSZONE investigated whether AMR organisms circulating in livestock and farming communities on both sides of the Serbia–Hungary border represent shared genomic lineages indicative of cross-border movement of animals, people, or trade products. Dobanovački led the epidemiological and human sampling work package, overseeing recruitment of 320 farming households within 30 km of the border on the Serbian side. Genomic data were integrated with livestock movement records provided by veterinary authorities. Results showed that CC398 MRSA and ST131 ESBL E. coli were shared across the border at low but detectable frequency, with animal trade events the most plausible driver. The project produced a joint risk communication brief distributed to farming associations in both countries.
partners: National Centre for Epidemiology, Budapest, Hungary
University of Pécs Medical School, Hungary
Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Provincial Veterinary Institute, Novi Sad

projects.title: Improving the Spatial Precision of Cancer Incidence Estimates in Serbia Through Registry Geocoding Enhancement and Bayesian Modelling
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the systematic gap between the geographic resolution of Serbian cancer registry records and the spatial precision required for evidence-based cancer control planning. Core activities included developing and validating probabilistic address imputation tools tailored to Serbian address formats, constructing a census-tract-level population denominator database for Vojvodina using 2011 and 2022 census microdata, and fitting spatio-temporal Bayesian models to colorectal and gastric cancer registry data. A secondary aim was to produce open-access incidence maps at census-tract level for Vojvodina for the period 2010–2020. The project trained two doctoral students and produced an R package for hierarchical geographic imputation. Partners contributed registry access, GIS infrastructure, and statistical expertise.
partners: Vojvodina Cancer Registry, Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Cancer Incidence Mapping in the Hungary–Serbia Borderland Using Jointly Modelled Registry Data
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMAP brought together cancer registry holders and spatial statisticians from Hungary and Serbia to produce the first jointly modelled colorectal cancer incidence maps covering contiguous administrative units on both sides of the national border. The Novi Sad team led the work package on data harmonisation and model development, adapting a shared conditional autoregressive spatial model to a combined adjacency graph spanning both country's administrative geometries.
