Outputs included harmonised incidence maps, a joint methodological report submitted to both health ministries, and a training workshop for registry staff on cross-border data sharing under GDPR-equivalent protections. The project also produced publicly accessible summary statistics at NUTS-3 equivalent level for the border region.
partners: Department of Public Health, Faculty of Medicine, University of Pécs, Hungary
South Transdanubia Cancer Registry, Pécs, Hungary
Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Hepatitis E Virus Occupational Cohort and Immunity Profile in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HEVOCCUP established a harmonised cross-border serological surveillance system for HEV in occupationally exposed slaughterhouse and pig farm workers across Vojvodina (Serbia) and Bács-Kiskun County (Hungary). The project enrolled approximately 340 participants across both countries, standardised ELISA and avidity testing protocols, conducted two annual blood draws, and developed a shared database and statistical analysis pipeline. A secondary objective was to train occupational health physicians in both countries on HEV testing indications and interpretation. Project outputs included the multi-country seroprevalence paper, a joint protocol document adopted by two regional public health institutes, and a risk communication leaflet for workers and employers.
partners: Institute for Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
National Institute of Epidemiology, Budapest, Hungary
Occupational Health Centre Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Serological Waning and Reinfection Dynamics of Hepatitis E in Exposed Workforce Cohorts
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SERWANE funds the ten-year follow-up re-contact of the original 2013 Vojvodina slaughterhouse cohort and expands it with a new arm enrolling 120 recently seroconverted workers for intensive quarterly titre and avidity monitoring over 18 months. The project applies Bayesian hierarchical modelling to distinguish primary waning from boosting due to re-exposure and estimate the probability and magnitude of serological boosting under defined occupational exposure conditions. An additional work package examines HEV serostatus in retired versus still-employed cohort members. Results are intended to inform evidence-based re-testing intervals in national occupational health guidelines.
partners: Institute for Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Department of Medical Statistics, Faculty of Medicine, University of Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Dietary Nitrate Exposure and Gastrointestinal Cancer Risk in Vojvodina: An Integrated Ecological and Individual-Level Study
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project funded the data collection and laboratory analysis phase of the Vojvodina gastric cancer case-control study, including FFQ development, validation against urinary nitrate biomarkers, and procurement of analytical chemistry capacity for vegetable nitrate measurement. It also supported construction of an updated regional food composition supplement covering 28 locally grown vegetable varieties. A secondary aim was to integrate drinking-water nitrate data from private wells into a combined exposure index. The project produced seven peer-reviewed publications, one validated dietary assessment instrument, and a regional food composition dataset deposited in an open repository. It involved collaboration with the Oncology Institute of Vojvodina, the Institute of Food Technology in Novi Sad, and the Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina.
partners: Oncology Institute of Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica
Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Comparative Gastric Cancer Risk Factors in the Danube Region: A Multi-Country Ecological Analysis
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project brought together epidemiology teams from Novi Sad, Pécs (Hungary), and Timișoara (Romania) to harmonise gastric cancer registry data and dietary exposure estimates across municipalities in the three countries' Danube corridor regions. Ivanović led the work package responsible for dietary nitrate exposure assessment and cross-country food composition harmonisation. The project produced a harmonised dataset of 187 municipalities with aligned incidence, dietary, H. pylori, and socioeconomic indicators, and an open-access methodological report on cross-national ecological cancer epidemiology in the region. Results contributed to a joint policy brief submitted to the regional health authorities of all three participating countries.
partners: Department of Hygiene, Faculty of Medicine, University of Pécs, Hungary
Department of Epidemiology, Victor Babeș University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Timișoara
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Mitochondrial Calcium Uniporter Complex as a Therapeutic Target in Cardiac Ischaemia-Reperfusion Injury
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project aimed to characterise how changes in the stoichiometry of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex subunits affect mPTP sensitivity in rat and mouse models of ischaemia-reperfusion injury, and to test selective small-molecule MCU inhibitors including the synthetic ruthenium compound Ru405. Work packages covered protein biochemistry of the MCU complex, single-cardiomyocyte calcium imaging, Langendorff infarct size studies, and an exploratory human biopsy sub-study in collaboration with the Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases of Vojvodina. The project supported two PhD students and produced six publications.
partners: Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases of Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica
Department of Inorganic Chemistry, Faculty of Chemistry, University of Belgrade
Department of Molecular Biology, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Sex- and Age-Dependent Modulation of Mitochondrial Permeability Transition in the Ischaemic Heart
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This regionally funded project investigated how biological sex and ageing independently and jointly modulate mPTP susceptibility in rat cardiac mitochondria. The study used ovariectomised and hormone-replaced female rats alongside aged male cohorts to dissect hormonal from developmental contributions. Key outcomes included identification of oestradiol as a factor raising the calcium threshold for mPTP opening independently of cyclophilin D, and quantification of the age-dependent upregulation of cyclophilin D as a mechanism amplifying vulnerability. Results fed into two journal publications and one master's thesis.
partners: Department of Endocrinology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Physiology, University of Graz

projects.title: Sex-specific hypothalamic neuropeptide reprogramming in rodent models of early-onset and adult diet-induced obesity
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines whether the timing of high-fat diet exposure—adolescent versus adult onset—produces distinct and sex-differentiated changes in hypothalamic neuropeptide circuitry. Using male and female Wistar rat cohorts exposed to high-fat diet at different life stages, the team combines gene expression profiling, immunohistochemistry, and metabolic phenotyping to identify neuropeptide systems that are persistently altered versus those that are reversible with dietary normalisation. A secondary aim is to determine whether arcuate nucleus NPY, AgRP, and POMC expression profiles in adulthood can serve as predictors of subsequent obesity susceptibility. The project funds one doctoral student and supports collaboration with the University of Medicine and Pharmacy Timișoara.
partners: Department of Physiology, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Timișoara
Institute of Endocrinology, University Clinical Centre Vojvodina

projects.title: Metabolic phenotyping infrastructure for biomedical research in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This infrastructure project co-funded the acquisition and commissioning of a four-chamber indirect calorimetry system with automated food intake monitoring at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad. The equipment was made available to multiple research groups studying metabolic disease within the faculty and through a formal access agreement with the Institute of Biology, University of Novi Sad. The project included training workshops for early-career researchers and the development of standardised operating procedures for rodent metabolic studies. Milošević coordinated procurement, oversaw installation validation, and led the training programme.
partners: Institute of Biology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Internal Medicine, University Clinical Centre Vojvodina

projects.title: Redox Regulation of Microvascular Tone in Type 2 Diabetes: From Bench to Bedside Biomarkers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the molecular mechanisms by which oxidative stress disrupts nitric oxide signalling in the microcirculation of type 2 diabetic patients and in rodent models. Specific objectives include mapping the temporal dynamics of eNOS uncoupling and BH4 depletion in the STZ rat aorta, characterising peroxynitrite-mediated protein modifications in the retinal microvasculature, and identifying circulating microRNA species that correlate with non-invasive FMD measurements in well-phenotyped patient cohorts. The project involves collaboration with the Endocrinology and Nephrology clinics of the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina and with partners at the Victor Babeș University in Timișoara and the University of Pécs. A translational outcome is the development of a small panel of plasma biomarkers suitable for monitoring microvascular endothelial function in clinical follow-up studies.
partners: Department of Biochemistry, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Endocrinology Clinic, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Department of Pathophysiology, Victor Babeș University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Timișoara
Department of Laboratory Medicine, University of Pécs

projects.title: Autonomic Biomarkers of Chronic Occupational Stress in Healthcare Workers
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates whether non-invasive HRV indices can serve as early warning markers of burnout and cardiovascular risk in healthcare professionals exposed to chronic occupational stress. It recruits nurses, physicians, and paramedical staff across three clinical centres in Vojvodina. Data collection combines ambulatory ECG, actigraphy, and quarterly saliva sampling for cortisol and alpha-amylase. Time-frequency spectral analysis forms the core analytical approach, with specific attention to within-day autonomic dynamics across different shift patterns. Boris Vuković contributes to data acquisition, signal processing pipeline maintenance, and statistical analysis. The project is coordinated by Associate Professor Dragana Milošević. Findings are expected to inform institutional occupational health guidelines for healthcare sector employers in Vojvodina.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina

projects.title: Dietary Fibre, Colonic Short-Chain Fatty Acids, and Central Serotonin: From Molecular Mechanisms to Human Intervention
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses three linked questions: (1) which histone modification marks at the Tph1 locus are activated by individual SCFAs in EC-like cell lines; (2) whether microbiota transplantation from high-fibre-fed donors reproducibly transfers elevated central serotonin to germ-free recipients; and (3) whether an 12-week oral butyrate supplementation trial in adults with low fibre intake and subclinical depressive symptoms raises plasma serotonin to a clinically detectable degree. The work integrates chromatin immunoprecipitation, germ-free mouse colonisation, and a double-blind randomised controlled pilot trial conducted at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Results are intended to inform dietary recommendations and support the design of a larger multicentre trial.
partners: Department of Biochemistry, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Clinic for Gastroenterology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina

projects.title: Microbiota–Enteric Nervous System–Brain Axis: Cross-Species Comparison and Dietary Modulation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral Serbian–Hungarian research project comparing gut microbiota composition, SCFA profiles, and enteric serotonin signalling in rat, pig, and human colonic tissue. The Novi Sad group led the work package on ex vivo pharmacology and isotope tracing, while the Hungarian partner coordinated the porcine model and clinical recruitment. A shared biobank of colonic tissue, faecal samples, and matched dietary records was established. The project produced harmonised protocols for SCFA measurement and EC cell isolation that are now used by both groups and shared with a Romanian partner laboratory.
partners: Department of Medical Microbiology, University of Pécs
Institute of Experimental Medicine, Hungarian Academy of Sciences analogue
Department of Physiology, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Cluj-Napoca

projects.title: Skeletal Muscle Capillary Remodelling and Fibre-Type Ageing in Sedentary Pannonian Populations: Morphometric and Lifestyle Determinants
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project recruited 120 sedentary men and women aged 60–80 years from Vojvodina to establish a comprehensive morphometric database of vastus lateralis fibre-type composition and capillarisation alongside accelerometry-based activity profiles, dietary assessments, and endocrine measurements. Standardised cryosection protocols and a semi-automated image analysis pipeline were developed and validated. The dataset supports cross-sectional and sub-cohort longitudinal analyses, and the anonymised image archive is being prepared for open access. The project funded two MSc student placements and contributed to the development of the muscle physiology practical module for the master's programme in sports medicine at the University of Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Physiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolic Diseases, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina

projects.title: Comparative Morphology of Ageing Skeletal Muscle in Hungarian and Serbian Border Regions: Towards a Cross-Border Reference Dataset
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Szeged targets harmonisation of skeletal muscle biopsy and morphometry protocols across two national health research systems. Szabó leads the work package on histochemical and immunofluorescence morphometry standardisation, coordinating the exchange of reference samples and staff between the two laboratories. The project will produce a joint reference dataset of fibre-type and capillarisation norms for sedentary adults aged 55–80 from the Hungary–Serbia border region, enabling future epidemiological comparisons. It also supports two joint PhD co-supervisions and a short-course training programme for laboratory technicians on both sides of the border.
partners: Department of Physiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Department of Physiology, Albert Szent-Györgyi Medical School, University of Szeged, Hungary
Subotica Health Centre, Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Elektrofiziološki bioreper kortikalne šireće depresije kod pacova kao osnova za translacioni model vizuelne aure migrene
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat ima za cilj izgradnju kvantitativnog repera elektrofizioloških parametara KŠD – brzine propagacije, amplitude DC pomaka, trajanja supresije – u standardizovanim animalnim modelima i njihovo poređenje sa dostupnim humanim podacima iz EEG studija tokom spontane migrenozne aure. U prvoj fazi formira se baza podataka iz sopstvenih in vivo eksperimenata na Wistar pacovima i FVB/N miševima (planirano n > 120 životinja). U drugoj fazi razvija se komputacioni skalabilni model koji pretvara parametre iz modela na glodarima u procenjene kortikalne prostorno-vremenske obrasce kod čoveka uzimajući u obzir razlike u veličini korteksa i debljini grijeve. Konačni rezultat je protokol za translacionu procenu antikortikalne-šireće-depresivne efikasnosti farmakoloških kandidata.
partners: Klinika za neurologiju, Klinički centar Vojvodine, Novi Sad
Institute of Neurobiology, Slovak Academy of Sciences, Košice

projects.title: Phosphorylated Tau Isoform Ratios as Diagnostic and Prognostic Biomarkers of Alzheimer's Disease in Balkan Population Cohorts
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TAUBALKAN aimed to establish region-specific reference intervals and diagnostic thresholds for CSF p-tau181, p-tau217, and p-tau231 in Serbian and Croatian dementia cohorts, and to evaluate their prognostic utility for MCI-to-dementia conversion over 24 months. The project recruited 450 participants across three sites (Novi Sad, Niš, Zagreb), implemented harmonised pre-analytical protocols, and deployed a Luminex xMAP multiplex platform alongside LC-MS/MS reference measurements. Secondary objectives included genetic modifier analysis (APOE, PICALM, BIN1) and the development of a machine learning classification tool for differential diagnosis. The project delivered 6 peer-reviewed publications and trained 2 PhD students.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Neurology Clinic, University Clinical Centre Niš, Serbia
University Hospital Centre Zagreb, Croatia

projects.title: Networked Biobanking and Harmonised CSF Biomarker Protocols for Neurodegenerative Disease Research in South-Eastern Europe
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: NEUROBALK-NET established a cross-border network for CSF biobanking and standardised biomarker measurement between the Faculty of Medicine Novi Sad and the University of Debrecen. Nikolić led the work package on assay harmonisation, overseeing the implementation of identical Luminex xMAP panels in both laboratories, exchange of reference materials, and a joint quality control scheme using blinded proficiency samples. The network created a shared repository of over 600 CSF samples with linked clinical and neuroimaging data, accessible to partner institutions. It also funded staff exchanges and a joint PhD co-supervision arrangement. The project laid the infrastructure for subsequent Horizon applications.
partners: Department of Neurology, University of Debrecen, Hungary
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Sleep-Stage-Specific Interictal Epileptiform Activity as a Biomarker for Presurgical Localisation in Drug-Resistant Focal Epilepsy
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates whether the distribution of interictal epileptiform discharges across sleep stages, measured by high-density EEG polysomnography, can improve non-invasive localisation of the seizure onset zone in patients being evaluated for epilepsy surgery. The study enrolls 60 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients undergoing stereo-EEG evaluation at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Polysomnographic recordings are obtained before electrode implantation and source estimates from sleep-stage-specific IED clusters are compared with iEEG-defined onset zones. Secondary aims include developing automated stage-stratified IED extraction tools in collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences and examining cognitive correlates of slow-oscillation–spindle coupling disruption.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Thalamocortical Mechanisms of Sleep Disruption in Focal Epilepsy: A Multicentre Polysomnographic and Neuroimaging Study
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: This bilateral Serbian–Italian project examines thalamocortical mechanisms underlying sleep macro- and microarchitecture disruption in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, combining polysomnographic data collected in Novi Sad with diffusion tensor imaging and thalamic segmentation performed in Bologna. The study compares 50 patients across three epilepsy subtypes (mesial temporal sclerosis, focal cortical dysplasia, and lesion-negative) with 50 matched healthy volunteers. Specific objectives include characterising slow-oscillation–spindle coupling asymmetries in relation to thalamic relay nucleus volume and identifying imaging–electrophysiology correlates that predict surgical outcome.
partners: Department of Neurological Sciences, University of Bologna, Italy
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Autonomic biomarkers as outcome measures in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis: establishing normative values and longitudinal trajectories in a Serbian cohort
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project systematically collects autonomic test data (QSART, short-term and 24-hour HRV, tilt-table) from a prospective cohort of 120 secondary progressive MS patients at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, with annual follow-up visits. Primary aims are to establish age- and sex-adjusted reference ranges for QSART in the Serbian population and to define annual rates of change in sudomotor and cardiovagal indices. Secondary aims include correlating autonomic trajectory with concurrent MRI atrophy measures and patient-reported outcomes. Partner institutions contribute OCT data and MRI volumetrics. The dataset will be made available to support sample size planning for future neuroprotective trials using autonomic endpoints.
partners: Department of Neurology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute of Physiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Department of Ophthalmology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Department of Neurology, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Somatosensory Phenotyping and Morphological Markers of Small-Fibre Damage in Diabetic Neuropathy: Towards Mechanism-Based Patient Stratification
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENSODIAN established a prospective cohort of 120 patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetic neuropathy followed with annual QST, skin punch biopsy, and sudomotor assessment. The primary aim was to determine whether QST-defined sensory phenotypes at enrolment predict the rate of morphological deterioration measured by IENFD. Secondary aims included examining the contribution of glycaemic variability, body composition, and inflammatory markers to phenotype and morphological trajectory. The project supported two PhD students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. A standardised operating procedure for multi-site biopsy in outpatient settings was developed and disseminated to two partner clinics.
partners: Department of Endocrinology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute of Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Department of Neurology, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Pre-Diabetic Neuropathy: Early Detection of Small-Fibre Pathology in Impaired Fasting Glucose Using Non-Invasive and Minimally Invasive Methods
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This smaller regional project addressed the question of whether small-fibre damage is detectable before the onset of clinical diabetes in individuals with impaired fasting glucose. The study recruited 70 participants (35 IFG, 35 normoglycaemic controls) from primary care centres in Vojvodina. Assessments included distal-leg punch biopsy, DFNS QST, and corneal confocal microscopy. Results showed measurable IENFD reduction and mild thermal threshold elevation in the IFG group relative to controls. The project provided infrastructure support for the confocal microscopy platform and contributed one Master's thesis and two journal publications.
partners: General Hospital Zrenjanin, Serbia
Primary Health Centre Novi Sad

projects.title: Longitudinal Cognitive Trajectories in Neurotoxicant-Exposed Industrial Workers in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project aims to establish a prospective cohort of 180 industrial workers across solvent-exposed and heavy-metal-exposed occupational groups in Vojvodina, with annual cognitive assessments over two years using parallel pencil-and-paper and computerised batteries. A key objective is to determine the minimal clinically important difference detectable by each format and to develop age- and education-corrected regional normative data, which are currently absent for the Serbian population. Biological monitoring of exposure biomarkers is conducted at each assessment wave. The project is coordinated by Prof. dr Dragan Milošević and involves collaborators from occupational medicine institutes across Vojvodina. Olivera Gligorić contributes to participant recruitment, neuropsychological testing, and data management.
partners: Institute of Occupational Medicine Novi Sad
Department of Neurology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Public Health Institute of Vojvodina

projects.title: Multiparametric Quantitative MRI Pipeline for Non-Invasive Hepatic Fibrosis Staging in Clinical Practice
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FIBROQUANT aimed to develop, validate, and partially automate a multiparametric quantitative MRI pipeline combining T1 mapping, T2* mapping, and texture analysis for staging hepatic fibrosis in adults without liver biopsy. The project recruited 320 patients across three clinical sites in Vojvodina and developed harmonisation procedures for protocol-heterogeneous retrospective data. A central output was a PACS-compatible post-processing module that generates a structured fibrosis staging report from routine MRI inputs. The project also produced the regional normative dataset for T1 and T2* values. Collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences provided software engineering capacity for the post-processing module.
partners: Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Border Validation of MRI Liver Fibrosis Biomarkers in Hungary–Serbia Cohorts
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: LIVERMATCH addressed the lack of shared clinical imaging data and standardised acquisition protocols between hepatology centres in southern Hungary and northern Serbia. The project established a joint patient registry covering 410 adults with chronic liver disease, harmonised MRI acquisition protocols across five scanners, and created a shared annotated dataset used for model development and cross-border validation. The Novi Sad team led the work package on quantitative MRI feature extraction and inter-scanner harmonisation. Secondary outputs included joint clinical guidelines on when to use MRI-based staging in place of biopsy, endorsed by participating gastroenterology departments.
partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Medicine, Hungary
Subotica General Hospital, Serbia
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Paediatric Radiation Dose Optimisation through Learned Reconstruction in Thoracic CT
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PEDIRAD aimed to develop and clinically validate deep learning–based CT reconstruction algorithms specifically optimised for paediatric thoracic imaging under Serbian healthcare conditions. The project combined phantom dosimetry, retrospective clinical data analysis, and prospective pilot validation at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Key deliverables included a publicly documented paediatric chest CT protocol benchmark, a trained and validated denoising network adapted to the Siemens SOMATOM Drive platform, and a set of task-based image quality metrics derived from channelised Hotelling observer modelling. The project also produced the national dose audit published in 2021 and contributed training data for the federated learning study. Three junior researchers were supported under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Institute of Radiology, University Clinical Centre of Serbia, Belgrade

projects.title: Federated Medical Image Analysis across Heterogeneous Hospital Infrastructures in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FEDIMAGE brings together radiology departments from Serbia, Hungary, and Slovenia to develop privacy-preserving federated learning pipelines for diagnostic imaging tasks, with CT denoising and lesion segmentation as initial use cases. Kristina Pejić leads the work package on CT reconstruction quality harmonisation, responsible for defining shared evaluation protocols, managing the paediatric chest CT data contribution from Novi Sad, and coordinating cross-site validation experiments. The project also includes a training component for radiography and medical physics staff on AI-assisted dose optimisation. Expected outputs include open-source federation code, a harmonised evaluation benchmark, and a joint workshop series hosted rotating between partner institutions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Paediatric Radiology, University of Pécs
Faculty of Computer and Information Science, University of Ljubljana
Institute of Medical Physics, University of Erlangen

projects.title: Permeability Mapping as a Microstructural Biomarker in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PERMICRO aimed to establish longitudinal DCE-MRI Ktrans measurements as a validated microstructural biomarker for CSVD progression. The project enrolled 90 patients across two sites (Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad and the University Clinical Centre, Kragujevac) and followed them over 24 months with annual MRI and neuropsychological assessment. Key outputs included the development of the automated WMH segmentation pipeline for DCE-MRI ROI placement, reference Ktrans ranges stratified by CSVD severity, and a machine learning model predicting one-year lesion growth. The project also supported one PhD student and two master's thesis projects. Total budget was approximately 4.8 million RSD.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
University Clinical Centre Kragujevac, Serbia
Department of Applied Mathematics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Multimodal MRI Connectomics and Barrier Integrity in Small Vessel Disease: A Serbia–Hungary Collaboration
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project combines DCE-MRI permeability mapping with diffusion-based connectome analysis to characterise how BBB disruption disrupts white matter network topology in CSVD patients from Serbia and Hungary. Ninkov leads the work package responsible for DCE-MRI acquisition harmonisation and pharmacokinetic analysis across both 3T scanner platforms. The project involves joint patient recruitment at three clinical sites, development of shared post-processing protocols, and training exchanges for junior researchers. A shared anonymised imaging database is being established under GDPR-compatible data governance. Planned outputs include at least three joint publications and a bilingual patient information resource.
partners: Department of Neuroimaging, Semmelweis University, Budapest, Hungary
Department of Neurology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute for Informatics, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Standardisation of Thyroid Elastography Protocols for Safer Biopsy Triage in South-East Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: THYSAFE aimed to establish platform-specific SWE reference intervals and cross-platform conversion factors for thyroid nodule assessment across three ultrasound systems widely used in Serbian and regional hospitals. The project enrolled patients at three sites (Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Niš) and collected paired measurements on Siemens, Canon, and Esaote equipment. Statistical models for stiffness conversion were developed and tested in a prospective validation cohort. Secondary objectives included training 12 radiology residents in standardised elastography acquisition and producing a freely available protocol handbook in Serbian and English. The project directly informed the 2024 cross-platform reproducibility study and contributed data to the ongoing biopsy-deferral validation trial.
partners: Centre for Radiology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Department of Radiology, Clinical Hospital Zemun, Belgrade
Department of Radiology, Clinical Centre Niš
Institute of Statistics and Bioinformatics, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Multicentre Network for Quantitative Elastography in Thyroid and Breast Pathology
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ELASTINET was a cross-border collaboration between radiology departments in Vojvodina and southern Hungary focused on building a shared annotated database of elastography cases for thyroid and breast lesions. Danijela Popović led the work package responsible for thyroid data collection, quality control, and harmonisation of reporting standards. The database collected 680 thyroid cases and 540 breast cases across four sites. Common image acquisition protocols and data dictionaries were developed jointly. The project also organised two joint training workshops for radiologists and provided equipment calibration audits at participating centres. Outputs included a shared pseudonymised dataset made available to regional researchers and a joint report on cross-border ultrasound practice variation.
partners: Centre for Radiology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Department of Radiology, University of Pécs Clinical Centre, Hungary
Department of Radiology, General Hospital Subotica
Department of Medical Imaging, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Radiation Dose Optimisation in Interventional Fluoroscopy Units of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish baseline occupational and patient dose data across interventional fluoroscopy units in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina and to develop a set of evidence-based written dose optimisation protocols adaptable to different facility sizes and equipment ages. Activities included on-site dosimetry measurements, structured staff interviews, equipment performance testing, and protocol drafting workshops attended by radiologists, cardiologists, and medical physicists from five institutions. Protocols were piloted at three institutions and evaluated over a 12-month follow-up period. The project produced a publicly available protocol document, a regional dose database, and training materials distributed to all participating units.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
General Hospital Subotica
General Hospital Zrenjanin
Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases, Sremska Kamenica
Serbian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency, Belgrade

projects.title: Kinetic PET Biomarkers for Early Response Stratification in High-Grade Sarcomas
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated a set of dynamic 18F-FDG PET kinetic biomarkers — primarily Ki from Patlak analysis and K1 from compartmental modelling — for classifying histopathological treatment response after induction chemotherapy in patients with osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma. A shortened 20-minute dynamic protocol was designed and validated against the full 60-minute standard. The project also investigated the added value of tumour perfusion indices derived from early PET frames. Participating clinical sites included the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina in Novi Sad and collaborating nuclear medicine departments in Ljubljana and Zagreb. Outcomes included multicentre reference values, a harmonised acquisition protocol, and an open-access dataset of anonymised kinetic parameters.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Nuclear Medicine, University Medical Centre Ljubljana, Slovenia
Department of Nuclear Medicine, Clinical Hospital Centre Zagreb, Croatia

projects.title: AI-Assisted Parametric Mapping from Dynamic PET in Musculoskeletal Oncology
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project addressed the computational bottleneck of voxel-wise kinetic modelling by developing and testing automated tools combining deep learning segmentation with batch processing of Patlak parametric maps. Collaboration with BioSig d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based medical software company, enabled integration of the parametric mapping pipeline into a DICOM-compatible workstation module. The project also examined the radiomic properties of Ki maps in soft-tissue sarcomas and compared them with standard SUV-map radiomics. A prospective validation cohort of 50 patients is being recruited through 2025. Deliverables include a validated software prototype and a peer-reviewed publication on Ki-map radiomics.
partners: BioSig d.o.o., Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Remineralisation Kinetics of Early Enamel Lesions: Combined Fluoride and CPP-ACP Protocols in Clinical and In Vitro Settings
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The REMKIN project aimed to characterise the temporal and spatial mineral deposition profiles in early enamel carious lesions treated with fluoride, CPP-ACP, and combined regimens, using a combination of TMR, micro-CT, and AFM. Laboratory experiments mapped ion release kinetics under controlled flow conditions, while a parallel randomised clinical trial in orthodontic patients provided in vivo validation. The project produced standardised protocol recommendations for combining the two agents in practice. Four master's students completed theses within the project. Equipment procured through the project included a micro-CT scanner and a tapping-mode AFM system, which remain available in the Faculty of Medicine research laboratory.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Medicine, University of Kragujevac

projects.title: Cross-Border Preventive Dentistry: Early Caries Detection and Remineralisation in School-Age Children in Hungary and Serbia
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project screened schoolchildren aged 6–12 in the Subotica–Szeged border region for early carious lesions using QLF devices. Children with white spot lesions were enrolled in a parallel prevention programme comparing fluoride varnish alone with fluoride varnish plus CPP-ACP mousse applied quarterly by school dental nurses. Đurđica Marić led the work package on QLF measurement standardisation and data analysis across both countries. Results informed updated school dental prevention guidelines submitted to the provincial health authorities of Vojvodina and Baranya County.
partners: Faculty of Dentistry, University of Pécs, Hungary (fictional)
Provincial Institute of Public Health Vojvodina
Municipal Health Centre Subotica

projects.title: Salivary Biomarker Panels for Periodontal Disease Monitoring in Type 2 Diabetes Patients in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aims to establish a shared reference database of salivary biomarker values in patients with comorbid periodontitis and type 2 diabetes from health institutions in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. Work Package 2, led by Paunović, focuses on harmonising saliva collection protocols, quality control for ELISA and multiplex assays across partner laboratories, and statistical modelling of biomarker reference intervals accounting for population-specific confounders such as diet and medication use. The consortium has enrolled approximately 280 participants by mid-project. Secondary outcomes include a training curriculum for dental staff on non-invasive diagnostic sampling and a jointly developed standard operating procedure document intended for adoption by regional primary health care centres.
partners: Department of Periodontology, Faculty of Dentistry, University of Pécs, Hungary
Clinical Centre Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
County Hospital of Baranya, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Longitudinal Salivary Proteomics and Inflammatory Profiling in Periodontitis-Diabetes Comorbidity
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SALDIAB is a three-year project that follows a cohort of 150 patients with type 2 diabetes and newly diagnosed stage III or IV periodontitis through active treatment and a 24-month maintenance phase. Saliva is collected at five time points and analysed by ELISA for a targeted panel (IL-1β, IL-6, MMP-8, TIMP-1, 8-OHdG, adiponectin, resistin) and by label-free mass spectrometry for exploratory proteomics. The primary objective is to identify biomarker trajectories that differentiate patients who respond well to non-surgical therapy from those who continue to deteriorate. Data will be used to develop a logistic regression-based risk score validated on a separate cohort. The project involves collaboration with the Faculty of Sciences biochemistry group for proteomics analysis and with the Faculty of Medicine's Endocrinology Department for metabolic follow-up data.
partners: Department of Biochemistry, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolic Diseases, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Early Orthodontic Screening and Craniofacial Growth Monitoring in Preschool Populations of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project carries out systematic orthodontic screening of children aged 4–7 years in kindergartens across three municipalities in Vojvodina, with a focus on identifying early signs of mouth-breathing-related skeletal changes. Enrolled children are followed at 12-month intervals with standardised clinical examination, photographic records, and study model analysis. A subgroup with confirmed nasal obstruction receives cephalometric imaging and is referred for ENT consultation as needed. The dataset being assembled will support longitudinal analysis of growth changes with and without early intervention. Šarić is responsible for clinical data collection, model digitisation, and cephalometric tracing under the supervision of the project principal investigator.
partners: Department of Dentistry, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Child and Youth Healthcare of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Municipality of Sremska Mitrovica – Public Health Office

projects.title: Wear Behaviour and Clinical Longevity Indicators of Monolithic Dental Ceramics in Posterior Load-Bearing Positions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CERAMWEAR investigates the mechanical and tribological performance of monolithic zirconia and lithium disilicate crowns under conditions that approximate clinical use over a five-year horizon. The project combines laboratory masticatory simulation with micro-CT and optical profilometry to track wear volume, marginal gap evolution, and surface roughness as a function of occlusal load, antagonist material, and surface finishing protocol. A secondary objective is to identify measurable laboratory parameters that correlate with clinically observed failure modes documented in a retrospective patient records review. The project team includes researchers from the Faculty of Medicine in Novi Sad and a collaborating group at the Faculty of Dental Medicine in Belgrade. Expected outputs include three peer-reviewed articles and a materials selection guideline for prosthodontists.
partners: Department of Dentistry, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
School of Dental Medicine, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Gastrointestinal Motility as a Pharmacokinetic Covariate in Type 2 Diabetes: From Biomarkers to Dose Adjustment
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project characterised the relationship between quantitative measures of gastrointestinal motility—gastric emptying breath tests, wireless motility capsule, and autonomic neuropathy scoring—and oral pharmacokinetic parameters of five commonly prescribed drugs in type 2 diabetic patients. A cross-sectional pharmacokinetic study enrolled 120 patients at the University Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Data were analysed using population PK modelling in NONMEM to estimate the contribution of motility-related covariates to absorption variability. A secondary aim was to develop a simple clinical index, derived from non-invasive motility measures, capable of flagging patients at risk of underexposure or overexposure. Findings are intended to inform product labelling considerations and clinical dosing guidance.
partners: University Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad (Bioinformatics Group)

projects.title: Motility-Drug Interaction Modelling for Oral Antidiabetics: A Regional Clinical Network
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MOTIDRUG builds a cross-border clinical research network between Hungarian and Serbian institutions to establish harmonised protocols for measuring gastrointestinal motility in type 2 diabetic patients and linking motility data to pharmacokinetic outcomes of oral antidiabetics. The Serbian team at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad leads the pharmacokinetic data collection and modelling work package, while Hungarian partners contribute patient cohorts and motility scintigraphy expertise. A shared database of paired motility and pharmacokinetic measurements from at least 200 patients across four study centres is being assembled. The project also includes a training programme for junior clinical pharmacologists at both partner countries.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Medicine, Hungary
County Hospital Pécs, Department of Nuclear Medicine, Hungary
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Mechanistic Assessment of Hepatotoxic Risk from Multi-Herb Combinations in Traditional Balkan Folk Medicine
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project systematically characterises hepatotoxic mechanisms of twenty-four two- and three-herb combinations commonly used in Vojvodina and across the Balkan region. It integrates in vitro hepatocyte and microsome models, ex vivo precision-cut liver slice assays, and a targeted 16S rRNA microbiome component. LC-MS/MS-based bioanalytical methodology is developed for simultaneous monitoring of twelve herbal marker compounds. A clinical component collects anonymised hepatology case data from three regional centres to compare with mechanistic predictions. The project aims to produce ranked combination risk profiles and draft evidence-based guidance for primary care physicians in Vojvodina regarding herb-drug interaction counselling. Two PhD students are supported on the project.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Clinic for Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad (BioInformatics Centre)

projects.title: Gut Microbiome as a Modulator of Phytochemical Hepatotoxicity: A Cross-Species Investigation
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral Serbia-Hungary research collaboration examining how gut microbiome composition influences the systemic bioavailability and hepatotoxic potency of phytochemicals derived from folk-medicine herb combinations. The project uses rodent germ-free and conventionally raised animal models alongside human volunteer pharmacokinetic sampling. Microbiome characterisation employs 16S rRNA sequencing and targeted metagenomic approaches. Hepatotoxic outcome endpoints include serum liver enzymes, hepatic transcriptomics (RNA-seq), and histopathology. Data are integrated through a computational modelling component developed by the Hungarian partner. The project is funded through the bilateral scientific cooperation programme between Serbia and Hungary administered through the Ministry of Science of the Republic of Serbia and the National Research Development and Innovation Office of Hungary.
partners: Department of Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapy, University of Szeged, Hungary
Institute of Microbiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Niš

projects.title: Sex-Specific Adverse Reaction Profiles in Elderly Patients on Antihypertensive Polypharmacy: A Multicentre Registry Study in Serbia and Romania
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established a prospective, multicentre clinical registry enrolling elderly patients on two or more antihypertensive agents at sites in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Timișoara. The primary aim was to quantify sex-based differences in adverse drug reaction incidence, severity, and time-to-onset across the major antihypertensive drug classes. Secondary aims included identifying clinical and biochemical predictors of sex-differential risk and developing a sex-disaggregated risk scoring tool for use at the point of prescribing. The registry enrolled 620 patients by the end of the funding period. Collaborating partners provided comparative data from a Romanian population to assess whether observed patterns were consistent across healthcare systems with differing prescribing traditions.
partners: University of Medicine and Pharmacy Timișoara, Romania
Health Centre Subotica, Serbia
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Dopaminergic Neurotoxicity of Agrochemical Mixtures in Vojvodina: From Rodent Models to Occupational Biomonitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how combinations of pesticides routinely applied in Vojvodina's cereal and fruit production affect the nigrostriatal and mesolimbic dopaminergic systems. The work has three interlocking components: (1) controlled rodent exposure studies using binary and ternary agrochemical mixtures at field-relevant dose ratios, with neurochemical, histological, and behavioural endpoints; (2) biomonitoring of agricultural workers in Vojvodina using urinary pesticide metabolites and validated neurotoxicity symptom instruments; and (3) in vitro mechanistic work in SH-SY5Y cells to dissect mitochondrial complex I and oxidative stress pathways. Findings are intended to contribute to revision of occupational exposure guidelines applicable to the region.
partners: Institute of Occupational Medicine, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Epidemiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Mixture Toxicity of Pesticides to the Dopaminergic Nigrostriatal System: Interreg Collaborative Study
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This bilateral project brought together the Department of Pharmacology at the University of Novi Sad and the Department of Neuropharmacology at the University of Pécs to conduct parallel rodent exposure studies using pesticide mixtures representative of each country's dominant agricultural practices. The Novi Sad team was responsible for neurochemical and receptor binding analyses, while the Pécs team led electrophysiological recording from midbrain slices. Cross-validation of findings across laboratories and rodent strains improved robustness of conclusions. The project also produced a joint graduate course module on environmental neurotoxicology that has been taught at both institutions.
partners: Department of Neuropharmacology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Pécs, Hungary
Institute of Experimental Pharmacology, Slovak Academy of Sciences, Bratislava, Slovakia

projects.title: Genotype-guided Tacrolimus Dosing in Renal Transplantation: Building Regional Evidence and Capacity
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GENTAC is a multicentre prospective study comparing standard weight-based tacrolimus initiation with CYP3A5 genotype-guided dosing in de novo renal transplant recipients at three centres in Serbia. The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients achieving target trough concentrations within the first two weeks post-transplant. Secondary endpoints include acute rejection rate at six months, eGFR at 12 months, and tacrolimus intra-patient variability. The project also funds installation of a real-time PCR platform in the department and training of two junior researchers in population PK modelling. An observational sub-study collects urinary biomarkers of nephrotoxicity at defined intervals to link pharmacokinetic data with early organ injury signals.
partners: Clinic for Urology and Nephrology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Clinic for Urology, Clinical Centre Niš
Institute for Genomics and Molecular Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Harmonisation of Therapeutic Drug Monitoring Practices for Immunosuppressants across Western Balkan Transplant Centres
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral cooperation project between the University of Novi Sad and Comenius University Bratislava, TRANSBALKAN aims to compare and partially harmonise TDM protocols for tacrolimus and everolimus across participating transplant units in Serbia and Slovakia. The Novi Sad team is responsible for a work package that surveys current analytical methods, reference ranges, and genotyping practices at Balkan centres, and designs a pilot inter-laboratory proficiency testing scheme. The project includes two researcher exchange visits per year and will produce a joint protocol recommendation document intended for submission to regional transplant societies.
partners: Department of Clinical Pharmacology, Comenius University, Bratislava, Slovakia
Clinic for Urology and Nephrology, Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Peptidni derivati benzimidazola kao antibiofilm agensi protiv multirezistentnih gram-negativnih bakterija
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi sintetom i biološkim ispitivanjem serije peptidnih derivata sa benzimidazolskim fragmentima usmerenih ka inhibiciji biofilma multirezistentnih gram-negativnih bakterija, pre svega A. baumannii i K. pneumoniae. U okviru projekta sprovode se hemijska sinteza jedinjenja, određivanje antibiofilm aktivnosti u in vitro modelima, ispitivanje citotoksičnosti prema humanim ćelijskim linijama i preliminarna farmakokinetička karakterizacija. Projektom je predviđeno angažovanje tri istraživačke grupe sa Medicinskog i Prirodno-matematičkog fakulteta u Novom Sadu. Stevanović je odgovoran za antibiofilm testiranje, interpretaciju mikrobioloških podataka i koordinaciju sa kliničkim mikrobiološkim laboratorijaма.
partners: Medicinski fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Prirodno-matematički fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Klinički centar Vojvodine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Fonetska dokumentacija i digitalna arhivizacija ugroženih vernakula u bačkom kontaktnom pojasu
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj sistematsku fonetsku dokumentaciju šokačkih i bunjevačkih govora u Bačkoj kroz terenska snimanja, uspostavljanje transkripcionog standarda i izgradnju otvorene digitalne arhive. U toku projekta snimljeno je dodatnih 86 sati spontanog govora, obučena su dva mlađa istraživača, a arhiva je opremljena serverskom infrastrukturom za dugoročno čuvanje. Poseban istraživački paket bavio se kvantifikacijom vokalske redukcije putem akustičkih merenja i poređenjem vrednosti unutar i između govornih zajednica. Rezultati su objavljeni u četiri referentna rada i prezentovani na tri međunarodne konferencije.
partners: Filozofski fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Zavod za kulturu vojvođanskih Hrvata, Subotica

projects.title: Prosodic and Vocalic Convergence in the Pannonian Hungarian-Slavic Contact Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Bilateralni projekat s partnerima sa Univerziteta u Pečuju i Segedinu koji istražuje fonološku konvergenciju između mađarskog i srpskog/hrvatskog u kontaktnom pojasu na obe strane državne granice. Paunović koordinira radni paket za srpsku stranu koji obuhvata terenski rad u tri bačke opštine, pripremu zajedničkog upitnika i uzajamno uparivanje korpusa za paralelne akustičke analize. Projekat finansira i zajednički letnji kurs fonološke dokumentacije namenjen doktorskim studentima iz obe države.
partners: Department of Hungarian Linguistics, University of Pécs

projects.title: Romani Identity and Language Practices in Vojvodina Schools
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: ROMID-VOJ investigates the relationship between Romani linguistic identity and school integration outcomes for bilingual students in Vojvodina primary schools. The project combines sociolinguistic fieldwork—interviews, observation, and attitude surveys—with analysis of administrative enrolment and attainment data provided by partner schools. Approximately 120 students across five municipalities are being followed over two academic years. The project aims to produce a set of evidence-based recommendations for teachers and school counsellors working in linguistically mixed classrooms. Zdravković is responsible for data collection in Novi Sad sites and contributes to attitude survey design and qualitative data analysis. Results will be disseminated through a public report and a teacher training workshop.

projects.title: Normative Codification of Standard Serbian: Divergence, Transmission, and Reform Options
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project produced a large annotated corpus of normative documents (orthographic manuals, grammar guides, editorial style sheets, university examination marking schemes) covering the period 1990–2022, totalling approximately 4,200 pages of primary text. Working with a team of three researchers, Dragišić coordinated the design of a shared coding schema for normative statements, supervised corpus compilation and annotation, and led the strand examining institutional divergence between Novi Sad and Belgrade. The project also ran three fieldwork rounds: a survey of secondary school teachers, a simulated proofreading experiment, and structured interviews with publishing editors. Findings were disseminated through five journal articles, two conference presentations, and a public round-table held at Matica srpska. The corpus is being prepared for open deposit.

projects.title: Learner Corpora and Morphological Acquisition in Serbian as a Foreign Language
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to expand the Novi Sad Learner Corpus of Serbian (NoSLeCS) to one million tokens and to conduct a systematic empirical investigation of morphological acquisition, focusing on verbal aspect and prefixation. Partner institutions contribute learner texts from Serbian language courses in Novi Sad, Belgrade, and two partner universities in Hungary and Poland. The project includes development of a freely accessible web interface for corpus search, a set of automatically applied morphosyntactic annotations, and a manually verified error tier. Research outputs include at least four journal publications and an open-access annotated dataset. The project also funds the development of a freely available diagnostic test for aspect knowledge in adult L2 learners of Serbian.

projects.title: Corpus Description of Metadiscourse and Hedging in Serbian Academic Journals 1990–2010
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project assembled and annotated a 1.2-million-word corpus of Serbian academic journal articles spanning twenty years and four broad disciplinary areas: humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and biomedicine. Corpus construction involved digitisation of print journals, orthographic normalisation, and manual annotation of metadiscourse categories by a team of three trained annotators. Inter-rater reliability was assessed at regular intervals. Quantitative and qualitative analyses of hedging density, booster frequency, and textual frame markers were conducted, with results published in four journal articles and presented at three regional conferences. The project also produced a publicly available annotation guide for Serbian metadiscourse research.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Matica srpska Library, Novi Sad

projects.title: Serbian Church Slavonic Hagiographic Corpus: Digitisation, Annotation, and Linguistic Analysis
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to build an open-access annotated digital corpus of Serbian Church Slavonic hagiographic texts spanning the thirteenth to fifteenth centuries, covering approximately 18,000 manuscript folios across 30 codices held in Serbian and regional institutions. Work packages addressed digitisation standardisation, TEI-based linguistic annotation, lexical database construction with emphasis on Greek borrowings, and corpus-based analysis of orthographic school variation. The project brought together philologists, linguists, and a computational specialist and produced a publicly accessible corpus release as well as updated entries for the Dictionary of Church Slavonic Language of the Serbian Redaction. Tanja Tešić contributed to the annotation design, Greek loanword analysis, and preparation of a protocol paper describing the digitisation and encoding methodology.

projects.title: Epistemic Stance in Academic Communication: Cross-Linguistic and Cross-Disciplinary Perspectives in South-East European Universities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: EPISACT brought together corpus linguists and applied linguists from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania to compile a multilingual, multi-disciplinary corpus of academic English texts produced by researchers from the three countries. The project assembled approximately 4 million words of annotated academic text and developed shared annotation guidelines for epistemic stance markers across four disciplines. Research activities included cross-institutional annotation workshops, a summer school for doctoral candidates on academic writing and corpus methods, and the publication of a shared corpus resource under an open licence. The project also piloted a short training module on epistemic stance for early-career researchers at three partner institutions.

projects.title: Academic Writing Development in Vojvodina Higher Education: Corpus Resources and Instructional Materials
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: ACAWRIT was a regionally funded project focused on the practical needs of Vojvodina university students and early-career researchers writing academic texts in English. The project produced three outputs: a 900,000-word annotated learner corpus of academic English from Vojvodina universities, a set of open-access instructional materials on hedging and cohesion for postgraduate students, and a one-semester elective course module trialled at the Faculty of Philosophy and the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad. The materials were evaluated by 112 postgraduate participants across two academic years.

projects.title: Framing EU Accession: Comparative Discourse Analysis in Western Balkan English-Language Media
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ACCFRAME brought together discourse analysts from four institutions in Serbia and one in Slovenia to construct and analyse a 4.2-million-word corpus of English-language media content related to EU accession from Serbia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. The project applied corpus-assisted CDA and appraisal theory to identify cross-country and diachronic patterns in how EU integration is evaluated in English-language journalism. Three working groups covered print press, institutional communication, and digital-native outlets respectively. The project produced a publicly available annotated corpus, four journal articles, and a regional practitioner workshop for journalists covering EU affairs.

projects.title: Pragmatic Competence and Multilingual Voice: English Communication Across Vojvodina Language Communities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PRAGVOICE examined pragmatic competence in English across the four major language communities of Vojvodina: Serbian, Hungarian, Slovak, and Rusyn. The project combined learner corpus methods with experimental pragmatics tasks administered to approximately 400 participants across six institutions. Core outputs included the Vojvodina English Learner Corpus (VELC) expansion to 450,000 words, a validated battery of pragmatic competence measures adapted for the regional context, and a set of evidence-based recommendations for EFL teacher training in multilingual Serbian classrooms. Four journal articles and two conference presentations resulted from project activities.

projects.title: Second-Language Pragmatics in Cross-Border Professional Communication: Serbia, Romania, Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: INTERWORK-L2 investigates pragmatic failures and successful accommodation strategies in English-mediated professional communication between employees in Hungarian, Romanian, and Serbian companies operating across borders. The Novi Sad team is responsible for data collection from Serbian business partners and for the shared analytical framework. Fieldwork involves recorded workplace interactions and structured interviews with HR managers at twelve partner companies. The project aims to produce a practical communication guide for multilingual border-region workforces and a training module pilotable by regional chambers of commerce. Žigić leads the work package on corpus collection and pragmatic annotation.

projects.title: Lexical Transfer in Habsburg Administrative Cultures: Serbian, Croatian, and Hungarian in the 18th Century
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled and annotated a trilingual corpus of administrative texts in Serbian, Croatian, and Hungarian from Vojvodina and Slavonia dated 1700–1800, totalling approximately 280,000 tokens across the three languages. Its principal aim was to identify shared and divergent patterns in the borrowing of Western European commercial and legal vocabulary under Habsburg governance. The Serbian team at Novi Sad coordinated corpus preparation and lexicographic output; partners in Zagreb and Pécs contributed their respective language datasets. The project produced a shared TEI-encoded corpus deposited with CLARIN.SI, a series of comparative journal articles, and the first instalment of the annotated Serbian historical glossary. Three early-career researchers received training in historical corpus methods.

projects.title: Environmental Narratives of West Africa: Literary Corpora, Teaching Materials, and Intercultural Reception in Central and Eastern Europe
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project built an annotated corpus of 40 Anglophone West African literary texts with environmental themes, developed and piloted teaching modules for use in university English literature courses in Serbia, and conducted reception research with student cohorts at the University of Novi Sad. Activities included two international workshops, a publicly accessible annotated reading list, and the curriculum study published in 2022. The project ran from the Department of English Studies with collaboration from partners in Hungary and Poland. It supported one junior researcher through a one-year contract and contributed to the MA programme in Anglophone Postcolonial Literatures at the faculty.

projects.title: Serbian at Home and Abroad: Phonological and Sociolinguistic Dynamics of Heritage Speech in the English-Speaking Diaspora
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SERHOME is a three-year project funded under the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia Ideas programme. It combines acoustic phonetic fieldwork, perceptual experiments, and sociolinguistic interviews to map the range and predictors of phonological attrition in Serbian heritage speakers across four English-dominant host countries. A core objective is the construction of the Heritage Serbian Spoken Corpus, a freely available annotated audio resource. The project also includes a secondary strand on attitudes and language maintenance practices, examining whether community-level factors such as Serbian weekend schools or cultural associations moderate the pace of phonological change. Two doctoral students are supported by the project, and a dissemination workshop aimed at Serbian cultural organisations in the diaspora is planned for the final project year.

projects.title: Sleep-Dependent Memory Consolidation in Young Adults: Electrophysiological and Behavioural Markers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigates the electrophysiological signatures of overnight episodic memory consolidation using 32-channel sleep EEG recordings in healthy young adults. The central aim is to map slow-wave activity topography and sleep spindle density onto performance on verbal, visuospatial, and emotional memory tasks. A sample of 120 participants is being recruited across three cohorts. Secondary objectives include testing whether individual differences in chronotype moderate the relationship between sleep architecture and memory outcomes, and whether brief afternoon naps produce topographically similar SWA profiles to nocturnal sleep. The project involves collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, for EEG signal processing.

Institute of Psychology, University of Pécs

projects.title: Adult and Adolescent Attachment in the South Balkan States: Normative Data, Measurement, and Developmental Predictors
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project aimed to establish representative psychometric norms for adult and adolescent self-report attachment instruments across five regional sites in Serbia and to trace developmental antecedents of attachment insecurity using retrospective and prospective data. The project collected data from approximately 2,200 participants across age groups (15–65), conducted measurement invariance testing across age, gender, and settlement type (urban vs. rural), and developed open-access normative tables and a brief practitioner scoring guide. A secondary objective was to train ten early-career researchers in advanced structural equation modelling and item response theory. All instruments and data management protocols were pre-registered on OSF.

projects.title: Family Dynamics, Parenting Quality, and Child Socioemotional Development in Vojvodina Families Under Economic Stress
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This two-year provincial project examined how economic stress in families in Vojvodina moderates associations between parenting quality, parental attachment style, and children's socioemotional development. Kovačević led the work package responsible for parent attachment measurement and psychometric data quality. The project recruited 180 families with children aged 4–8 years from three municipalities with differing economic profiles. Parenting alliance, attachment style, parental reflective functioning, and child emotional regulation were assessed at two time points twelve months apart. Findings informed a public guidance document distributed to preschool institutions in the AP Vojvodina region.

projects.title: Prolonged Grief Disorder in Older Adults in Vojvodina: Prevalence, Risk Factors, and Barriers to Support
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project produced the first systematic epidemiological data on prolonged grief disorder in community-dwelling older adults in the Vojvodina region. It combined a population-based cross-sectional survey (n = 412, aged 65+), qualitative interviews, and a mapping of available bereavement support services across the province. The project validated the Serbian Grief Severity Inventory in the target population, identified social isolation as the strongest modifiable risk factor, and documented a near-complete absence of structured bereavement support in primary care and social services. A policy brief and a brief workforce training outline for social care staff were produced as practice outputs.

projects.title: Grief Trajectories and Prolonged Grief Disorder in Older Adults Across the Post-Yugoslav Region: A Comparative Longitudinal Study
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This IDEAS grant funds a three-country longitudinal study tracking grief trajectories in bereaved adults aged 65 and above in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia over 24 months. The study follows 900 participants (300 per country) at six-monthly intervals using both standardised instruments and nested qualitative sub-studies. Key objectives include estimating cross-national variability in prolonged grief prevalence, identifying cultural and structural determinants of trajectory class membership, and examining how differences in post-Yugoslav social policy and healthcare organisation moderate grief outcomes. A harmonised assessment battery applicable across the region is being developed as a transferable output.

projects.title: Intergroup Contact Quality and Social Cohesion in Multiethnic Communities of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the conditions under which intergroup contact between ethnic majority and minority groups improves social cohesion in Vojvodina, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. It combined large-scale field surveys (total N > 2,400 across three countries), a laboratory experiment component, and the development and cross-cultural validation of a short contact quality instrument. The project produced a publicly available dataset, three peer-reviewed articles, and a policy brief submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research of Vojvodina. Two doctoral students were trained within the project. Partners included the University of Sarajevo and Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje.

projects.title: Mixed Schooling Environments, Identity Development and Interethnic Friendships in Adolescence
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MIXSCHOOL investigated how the degree of ethnic mixing in secondary school environments in the Hungary–Serbia border region shaped identity development and cross-ethnic friendship formation among adolescents. Bálint led the work package responsible for survey design, data collection in Vojvodina schools, and quantitative analysis. The project collected data from 1,140 students across 14 schools in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. Findings were used to develop a set of school-level recommendations for teachers and administrators, circulated through regional education networks. The lead partner was a Hungarian research institute; the University of Novi Sad team contributed the Serbian data and co-authored two peer-reviewed outputs.
