projects.title: Memory Revision and Self-Continuity Across Life Transitions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project, led by Prodanović's supervisor at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, investigates how people reconstruct autobiographical memories during major life transitions such as university entry, graduation, and early employment. The project uses a combination of longitudinal diary methods, laboratory recall tasks, and online survey panels to map the conditions under which self-enhancing memory revision intensifies or diminishes. Prodanović contributes to data collection, diary coding, and quantitative analysis within the laboratory component of the project, and is responsible for coordinating participant scheduling and the management of the structured diary protocol database. The project involves a collaboration with the University of Banja Luka and produces data that directly feeds into his doctoral dissertation.

projects.title: Autonomic Correlates of Perfectionism-Related Emotion Dysregulation in Student Populations
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates the psychophysiological underpinnings of emotion regulation failure in non-clinical perfectionism using multimodal autonomic recording. The study protocol combines electrodermal activity, electrocardiography, and respiratory monitoring during a battery of evaluative stress tasks adapted for repeated-measures designs. A sample of approximately 150 students from the University of Novi Sad will be recruited and followed across two academic assessment periods. Primary outcomes include RSA suppression magnitude, SCL reactivity, and recovery trajectories. Filipović contributes to data collection, signal processing, and manuscript preparation. The project is coordinated by the Psychophysiology Laboratory, Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.

projects.title: Vojvodina Early Development Study: executive function, language and school readiness in a prospective birth cohort
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project established a prospective cohort of children recruited through maternity wards in Novi Sad and two other Vojvodina municipalities. Families were enrolled during the third trimester and children were assessed annually from 12 months. The EF strand of the study, led by Todić, introduced observational task batteries at ages 36, 48, 60, and 72 months and linked EF trajectories to language development, home learning environment, and teacher-rated school readiness. The cohort comprised 231 families at baseline, with 189 retained through the age-72-month wave. Archived data are available for secondary analysis upon application to the project steering committee.

projects.title: Cross-national comparison of executive function development in preschool children from Serbia, Hungary and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: EXECFLEX examines whether EF developmental trajectories and assessment task performance are comparable across preschool children in border regions of Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. A secondary goal is training preschool practitioners from all three countries in structured observational methods.

projects.title: Grammatical Gender and Object Categorisation in Serbian–Hungarian Bilingual Children and Adults
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GENCAT investigates the developmental and bilingual modulation of grammatical gender effects on non-linguistic object categorisation in Serbian-speaking populations. The project compares monolingual Serbian children (ages 5–9), Serbian–Hungarian bilingual children, and adult bilinguals across three task types: free sorting, forced-choice similarity judgement, and a short-term memory interference paradigm. Data collection takes place at partner primary schools in Novi Sad and Subotica. Eye-tracking is used with adult participants to capture online processing. The project aims to produce a publicly available stimulus set of gender-balanced object images normed for Serbian and to deliver at least four peer-reviewed publications. projects.title: Collective Remembrance and Emotional Responses to Historical Wrongdoing in Post-Conflict Societies
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: COLLREM is a three-year project led by Prof. dr Milena Vukić at the University of Novi Sad examining the psychological mechanisms through which majority-group members in the Western Balkans process national memories of past inter-ethnic violence. The project employs a mixed-methods design combining experimental vignette studies, implicit association testing, and semi-structured interviews across Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian samples. projects.title: Standardizacija psihodinamskih formulacionih instrumenata u kliničko-istraživačkoj praksi zapadnog Balkana
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj harmonizaciju i standardizaciju instrumenata za psihodinamsku formulaciju slučaja kroz razvoj zajedničkog kodnog priručnika prilagođenog srpskom jezičkom i kulturnom kontekstu, te validaciju tog priručnika na kliničkim uzorcima iz Srbije, Bosne i Hercegovine i Crne Gore. projects.title: Green Space Access and Physiological Stress Burden in Mid-Sized Central European Cities
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines whether residential proximity to and quality of urban green spaces independently predicts ambulatory physiological stress burden—operationalised as 24-hour RMSSD profiles and salivary cortisol slopes—in working adults in Novi Sad. A cohort of 180 participants wears ambulatory ECG monitors and provides five daily saliva samples over three working days and one rest day. GIS-derived green space metrics (area, fragmentation, perceived quality) are linked to individual physiological outcomes using multilevel regression. A secondary aim is to test whether the association is mediated by subjective restorative experiences assessed through end-of-day ESM. The project also produces an open dataset and validated Serbian-language instruments for future epidemiological work.

projects.title: Active Travel Pathways Through Green Urban Infrastructure: Psychological and Physiological Outcomes
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigated whether redesigning commute routes to increase green corridor exposure affects stress, mood, and physical activity in office workers. Forty-two employees at two municipal institutions in Novi Sad were allocated to green-route versus control-route commuting for six weeks. Outcomes included weekly ambulatory EDA monitoring, self-reported stress, and accelerometry. The project was conducted in collaboration with the City of Novi Sad Urban Planning Department, which provided spatial data and assisted in identifying comparable route pairs. Results indicated modest but consistent EDA reductions in the green-route group. A brief report was submitted to the provincial secretariat and shared with the urban planning department.

projects.title: Bystander Behaviour in Online Environments: Situational and Dispositional Mechanisms Across the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates why individuals witnessing online harassment in social media environments choose to intervene or remain passive, focusing on social cost perception, norm ambiguity, and platform affordances as situational barriers, alongside empathy and moral disengagement as dispositional factors. The research uses a series of pre-registered experiments conducted through a purpose-built social media simulator, as well as multi-site survey studies at universities in Serbia. A secondary aim is to develop and pilot a short bystander-training module for higher-education institutions, evaluating it against a waitlist control group. Results are expected to yield practical recommendations for both platform policy and university student-conduct programmes.

projects.title: Generational Shifts in Gender Roles in Rural Vojvodina Households
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates how gender role expectations within rural households in Vojvodina have changed across three generational cohorts—women and men born before 1960, between 1975 and 1990, and after 2000—using a mixed design combining 120 qualitative interviews with a smaller survey component (n=310). Emilija Matić contributes to fieldwork coordination in Bačka municipalities, interview coding in NVivo, and preparation of outputs. The project is led by the Department of Sociology at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, in cooperation with the Centre for Gender Studies at the same faculty. Findings will feed into a report for the Vojvodina regional administration on rural women's economic participation.
partners: Centre for Gender Studies, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Municipality of Bačka Palanka (associate partner)

projects.title: Memory Landscapes in Vojvodina: Contested Sites, Minority Perspectives, and Municipal Practice
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MEMVOJ is a three-year project funded under the Ideas programme of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. The project maps contested memorial sites across 15 Vojvodinian municipalities, combining GIS-based spatial documentation with qualitative fieldwork. It investigates how minority communities—primarily Hungarian, Slovak, and Rusyn—seek recognition within official local commemoration frameworks and how municipal authorities respond to those claims over time. The project produces an open-access digital atlas of contested memorial sites, a comparative policy report addressed to municipal governments and the Provincial Secretariat for National Minorities, and a series of peer-reviewed publications. The team comprises four researchers from the University of Novi Sad and one associate from the University of Subotica.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Subotica
Regional Centre for Minorities, Novi Sad (NGO)

projects.title: Cross-Border Memory Communities: Hungarian Minority Commemoration in Serbia and Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMEM examined how Hungarian minority organisations on both sides of the Serbia–Hungary border coordinated commemorative practices, shared symbolic resources, and narrated a common minority memory across state boundaries. Uzelac led the Serbian case-study work package, responsible for fieldwork in five municipalities in northern Vojvodina, oral history collection, and comparative analysis with the Hungarian partner team based in Subotica and Szeged. The project produced three joint academic publications, a bilingual documentary film screened at community events, and a set of recommendations for cross-border cultural cooperation submitted to the Interreg programme authority. It was the first project in the programme cycle to focus explicitly on commemoration rather than heritage tourism or economic development.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
City Museum of Subotica
Research Institute for Linguistics, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Diagnostic Identity and Chronic Illness Self-Management in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The DIAGID project investigated the relationship between chronic illness diagnosis, patient identity formation, and self-management behaviour across three Western Balkan countries: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The project combined a large cross-sectional survey (total n=2,400) with a nested qualitative component of 90 in-depth interviews. Research questions centred on whether diagnostic label type, diagnostic pathway length, and institutional trust independently predict self-management outcomes when controlling for sociodemographic variables. A secondary strand analysed the training and communication practices of primary care providers. The project produced eight peer-reviewed publications, two policy briefs submitted to Serbian and Bosnian health ministries, and a publicly accessible dataset deposited with the CRIS UNS research repository.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Public Health Sarajevo
Faculty of Philosophy Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje

projects.title: Migration, Health Literacy, and Diagnostic Continuity for Returning Migrants in Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MIGROMED is a cross-border collaboration addressing the health service re-integration of labour migrants returning to Serbia and Hungary after extended periods in Western Europe. Pantelić leads the qualitative work package, responsible for the design and analysis of interviews with returning migrants and with general practitioners in the Serbian border region. His team produced a comparative qualitative report and contributed to a jointly developed pilot protocol for GP consultations with returnees, which was tested in four practices across Subotica and Szeged. The project has also supported the translation and adaptation of patient self-assessment tools originally developed in German. A final policy recommendation document is scheduled for submission to the Serbian Ministry of Health in late 2025.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Pécs
Primary Healthcare Centre Subotica
Csongrád-Csanád County Health Directorate

projects.title: Vojvodina Interdenominational Religious Landscape: Long-Term Survey Infrastructure and Data Archive
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project established a repeated cross-sectional survey infrastructure for monitoring religious behaviour and attitudes across denominations in Vojvodina. Over four annual survey waves (2019–2022), approximately 800 respondents per wave were interviewed using a standardised instrument covering attendance, prayer, affiliation, and institutional trust. All anonymised datasets were deposited in the Vojvodina Social Survey Archive hosted at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad. The project also produced a methodological report comparing the survey instrument with the 2022 census religious module. Three journal articles resulted directly from the data collection. The archive is publicly accessible to researchers at accredited institutions and has already been used by four external research teams.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Diocese of Subotica (advisory role)
Statistical Office of the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina

projects.title: Minority Religious Communities and Cross-Border Kinship Networks in the Hungary–Serbia Border Zone
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MINREL-CB examined how cross-border family ties between Hungary and Serbia shape the religious practice of ethnic Hungarians living on both sides of the border. Varga led the Serbian-side empirical work package, which combined a postal survey of 460 households in Subotica, Kanjiža, and Senta with 38 in-depth interviews. The project found that kin visits across the border are a significant occasion for religious practice (particularly attendance at rites of passage and major feast days) and that Hungarian-side parishes functionally serve some Serbian-resident family members. A joint conference was held in Subotica in November 2022, and a co-authored monograph was published in 2024 by an academic press in Pécs.
partners: University of Pécs, Department of Sociology
Bethlen Gábor Research Institute, Budapest
City of Subotica Cultural Affairs Office

projects.title: Educational Reproduction and Social Mobility in Serbian Cities: Longitudinal and Comparative Perspectives
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines mechanisms of educational reproduction across the secondary-school transition in Novi Sad, Kragujevac, and Niš, combining a new cross-sectional survey (N ≈ 1,100), a follow-up of an earlier panel cohort, and qualitative interviews with parents, pupils, and teachers. Core objectives include quantifying the relative contributions of economic capital, cultural capital, and social capital to gymnasium placement; analysing how the COVID-19 period altered these contributions; and identifying school-level and neighbourhood-level contextual factors. Outputs include peer-reviewed publications, a publicly available anonymised dataset deposited with the Serbian Social Science Data Archive, and a policy brief submitted to the Ministry of Education of Serbia. Two doctoral students are supervised within the project.
partners: Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade
Department of Sociology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Niš

projects.title: Cross-Border Comparison of Vocational and Academic Track Allocation in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSTRACK brings together sociologists and education researchers from Serbia and Hungary to map and compare the secondary-track allocation process in border regions on both sides of the Danube. The project collects survey and administrative data in Vojvodina municipalities and adjacent Hungarian counties, focusing on ethnic minority (Hungarian-origin) pupils whose families straddle cross-border educational systems. Tanja Hadžić leads the work package responsible for survey design, data collection in Vojvodina, and comparative analysis. The project will produce three joint publications, a bilingual educational guidance resource for minority families, and a joint doctoral seminar held alternately in Novi Sad and Pécs.
partners: Faculty of Arts, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina Institute for Social Research, Novi Sad
Baranya County Pedagogical Institute, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Editorial Autonomy and Ownership Accountability in Small-Market Television: Comparative Evidence from Four Post-Communist Democracies
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: The project conducted a systematic comparative study of editorial autonomy and ownership structures in commercial television in Serbia, Montenegro, Slovenia, and Slovakia. It combined survey methodology, newsroom interviews, content analysis of news output, and regulatory document analysis across 24 broadcasters in four countries. The Serbian team at the University of Novi Sad coordinated data collection, instrument harmonisation, and cross-country analysis. The project produced a comparative dataset archived at the Faculty of Philosophy data repository, a policy brief submitted to the European Commission's Media Freedom Rapid Response mechanism, and the 2023 monograph published by Peter Lang. Total project budget was approximately 1.4 million euros.
partners: Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Ljubljana
Department of Mass Media Studies, Comenius University, Bratislava
Faculty of Political Science, University of Montenegro, Podgorica

projects.title: Establishing a Media Production Research Archive and Qualitative Data Infrastructure at the University of Novi Sad
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This infrastructure grant funded the establishment of a qualitative data archive for media production research at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad. The archive stores anonymised interview transcripts, observation notes, and document sets from fieldwork conducted by the Media Production Research Group since 2008, amounting to approximately 340 interview transcripts and 1,200 pages of field notes. The grant also funded audio transcription workstations, secure data storage, and the development of a metadata schema adapted from the CLARIN infrastructure standards. The archive is available to vetted researchers at other Serbian institutions under a data sharing agreement.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Mnemonic Functions of Popular Music Video in Post-Yugoslav Serbia: A Corpus-Based Analysis
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project builds a searchable, annotated corpus of approximately 500 Serbian popular music videos spanning 1990 to 2024, with systematic metadata coding for visual memory markers, nostalgic register, and identity discourse. The corpus is being developed at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, in collaboration with the Radio Television of Vojvodina documentation centre. Vojnović contributes to the corpus annotation protocol design, performs multimodal coding on a subset of the corpus, and leads the analysis of regional and ethnic minority representation within memory-oriented visual tropes. The project will result in an open-access corpus available to researchers working on post-Yugoslav media and memory studies.
partners: Radio Television of Vojvodina – Documentation and Archive Centre, Novi Sad
Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Governing Pornography Online: Regulatory Discourse, Platform Architectures, and Democratic Accountability in Post-Socialist Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how online pornography regulation is debated and implemented in four post-socialist EU candidate and member states — Serbia, Hungary, Croatia, and Romania — and how national debates interact with EU-level governance developments. The research uses a multi-method design combining corpus-assisted discourse analysis of legislative and parliamentary documents, semi-structured interviews with regulators and civil society actors, and comparative case studies of platform enforcement decisions. A particular focus is placed on the gap between stated child-protection objectives and measurable enforcement outcomes. The project involves three partner institutions and produces a comparative policy report alongside academic outputs intended to inform Serbia's EU accession negotiations in the digital policy area.
partners: Faculty of Political Sciences, University of Belgrade
Institute of Communication Studies, University of Pécs, Hungary
Faculty of Political Sciences, Administrative and Communication Sciences, Babeș-Bolyai University, Romania

projects.title: Meme Circulation and Political Discourse in Western Balkan Online Publics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MEMPOL investigates how political memes function as vehicles for discourse formation and fragmentation in online public spheres across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The project combines automated corpus collection from Facebook, Telegram, and TikTok with semiotic annotation and qualitative interviews with content creators and consumers. Tihomir Pekez contributes to corpus design, the development of the multimodal annotation framework, and the analysis of Serbian-language material. The project is coordinated by the Department of Media Studies at the University of Novi Sad and includes partners from Sarajevo and Skopje. Expected outputs include an open annotated corpus, three peer-reviewed articles, and a policy brief addressed to media literacy organisations.
partners: Faculty of Political Sciences, University of Sarajevo
Institute for Communication Studies, Skopje
Department of Media Studies, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: News Avoidance Behaviour and Democratic Participation in Central and Eastern Europe: A Comparative Panel Study
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AVOIDNEWS-CEE investigated the prevalence, motivations, and civic consequences of news avoidance among adults aged 18–35 in Serbia, using a two-wave panel survey design and complementary qualitative components. The project produced the cross-national survey data that underpins several of Rakić's recent publications and developed a publicly available harmonised questionnaire instrument suitable for replication across post-communist media contexts. A national report with policy recommendations for the public service broadcaster and the Regulatory Authority for Electronic Media was submitted in late 2023. The project employed one postdoctoral researcher and supported two doctoral students.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Political Sciences, University of Belgrade
Institute for Social Research Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: News Trust and Avoidance Across the Western Balkans: Comparative Qualitative Mapping
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: BALNEWS is a bilateral research cooperation between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Sarajevo, co-funded by the Serbian and Bosnian ministries responsible for scientific cooperation. The project supports joint data collection through narrative interviews across five Western Balkan countries, researcher exchanges, and a joint edited volume on news culture in the region. The cooperation extends fieldwork reported in Rakić's 2026 preprint and is expected to produce three joint journal articles and one co-edited book. A joint doctoral workshop is planned for autumn 2026 in Sarajevo.
partners: Faculty of Political Sciences, University of Sarajevo
School of Journalism, University of Montenegro, Podgorica

projects.title: Digitisation, Annotation, and Analysis of the Vojvodina Interwar Periodical Press Heritage
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to digitise approximately 120,000 newspaper pages from twelve periodical titles held at the Matica srpska Library, the Archives of Vojvodina, and the Subotica City Library. Digitisation was followed by OCR processing with post-correction, manual structural markup, and thematic annotation of a representative subcorpus of 220,000 tokens. A searchable online repository was built to provide open access to the digitised images and annotated text. The project also produced a union catalogue of 214 Vojvodina interwar periodical titles across repositories in four countries and delivered three academic publications and two conference presentations. Partners contributed expertise in digitisation infrastructure, computational linguistics, and archival science.
partners: Matica srpska Library, Novi Sad
Archives of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
City Library Subotica

projects.title: Press, Memory, and Regional Identity in the Post-Habsburg Danube Basin, 1918–1941
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral research and heritage project bringing together teams from Novi Sad and Pécs to compare the interwar press landscape in the former Hungarian territories that became part of Yugoslavia and those that remained in Hungary after 1920. Gajić led the work package responsible for source identification and comparative content analysis across the two national corpora. The project produced a jointly edited bilingual volume, an exhibition mounted in Novi Sad and Pécs, and a shared online bibliography of interwar regional press research. Fieldwork included archive visits in Budapest, Vienna, Novi Sad, Subotica, and Osijek. The project contributed to ongoing discussions in both countries about cross-border cultural heritage documentation.
partners: Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, University of Pécs, Hungary
Petőfi Literary Museum, Budapest, Hungary
Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Narrative Identity Across School Transitions: A Longitudinal Study in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project followed 180 pupils from three municipalities in Vojvodina through the primary-to-secondary school transition over two academic years, combining diary-based and interview methods. Core objectives were to map the developmental trajectory of narrative identity coherence across the transition period, identify risk factors for identity distress, and test whether a brief structured narrative intervention delivered by school counsellors could support coherence development. A coding and annotation corpus of approximately 2,400 narrative texts was produced and is held at the Department of Pedagogy. The project involved collaboration with school psychologists and the Provincial Institute for the Evaluation of Quality of Education and Upbringing.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for the Evaluation of Quality of Education and Upbringing, Novi Sad
Primary and Secondary Schools Consortium Vojvodina (fictional administrative partner grouping)

projects.title: Narrative Approaches to School Transition Support in Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This bilateral project brings together researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest to compare how narrative identity processes unfold in Serbian and Hungarian school transition contexts, with particular attention to the role of cultural scripts about educational success and peer belonging. Zorica Gligorić leads the work package on data collection instruments and cross-national coding equivalence. The project includes a practitioner training component through which school counsellors in partner municipalities receive training in diary-based identity support activities. A joint practitioner handbook in Serbian and Hungarian is planned as a project output alongside academic publications.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Education, Eötvös Loránd University, Budapest
Municipal Education Authority of Subotica
Municipal Education Authority of Kecskemét

projects.title: Pedagogical Epistemologies in Post-Socialist Transition: Archival and Oral History Approaches to Educational Continuity in the Former Yugoslav Space
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PEDAGOST investigated the mechanisms by which socialist-era pedagogical knowledge frameworks persisted, transformed, or disappeared in Serbian and regional educational institutions after 1990. The project combined systematic archival research at the Archive of Vojvodina, the Archive of Serbia, and the Yugoslav Film Archive's educational holdings with a structured oral history programme involving 62 interviews with former and current educators across Serbia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. A searchable digital repository of 340 digitised primary documents was produced. The project trained two doctoral students and produced seven peer-reviewed publications. Findings were disseminated at four international conferences and in a public-facing policy brief submitted to the Ministry of Education of Serbia.
partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade
Faculty of Philosophy, University of Montenegro

projects.title: Kinship-Mediated Learning and School Readiness in Rural Roma Communities of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates the relationship between kinship-based informal learning networks and school readiness outcomes among Roma children in rural Vojvodina. Fieldwork is carried out in eight villages across three municipalities, combining ethnographic observation, household interviews, and consultation with local primary school staff. The project aims to produce a descriptive typology of kinship learning configurations and to assess how these configurations correlate with teachers' ratings of children's school readiness at the point of enrolment. A secondary objective is to develop a set of guidance notes for school-family liaison practitioners working in Roma communities. The project is coordinated by Valentina Despotović's supervisor and involves collaboration with local NGOs active in Roma education. Valentina Despotović contributes to fieldwork design, data collection, and analysis.
partners: Department of Pedagogy, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Foundation for Roma Educational Support Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Primary School Bratstvo-Jedinstvo, Opovo Municipality

projects.title: Play-Based Moral Reasoning in Early Childhood: Assessment, Classroom Implementation, and Practitioner Training
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop, validate, and pilot a standardised battery for assessing moral reasoning in Serbian preschool children aged three to six, and to design a practitioner-delivered classroom curriculum based on dilemma storytelling and structured peer discussion. The work proceeded in three phases: instrument development and norming with a sample of approximately 300 children across Vojvodina; a controlled trial of the curriculum in 12 preschool groups; and the design and evaluation of a one-day practitioner training programme. The project produced publicly available assessment materials in Serbian, a practitioner guide, and several peer-reviewed publications. A Hungarian adaptation was initiated through an informal collaboration with the University of Pécs.
partners: Preschool Teacher Training College, Novi Sad
Faculty of Education, University of Kragujevac
City of Novi Sad Preschool Institution 'Radosno detinjstvo'

projects.title: Early Childhood Educators and Moral Education: Cross-National Survey and Training Needs Analysis in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project conducted a harmonised survey of early childhood practitioners in the Hungarian–Serbian border region, examining attitudes, reported practices, and perceived training needs in the area of moral education. The Novi Sad team was responsible for the Serbian arm of the survey design, data collection with approximately 200 practitioners, and the joint analysis of cross-national patterns. A secondary output was the development of a bilingual resource pack for practitioners covering storytelling techniques and facilitation of peer discussion. The project included two joint workshops in Novi Sad and Pécs and resulted in a practitioner-facing web resource hosted by the University of Pécs.
partners: Department of Early Childhood Education, University of Pécs, Hungary
Pedagoški zavod Vojvodine (Vojvodina Institute of Education)

projects.title: Digital Market Regulation and Consumer Protection in Western Balkan EU-Accession Processes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the regulatory distance between current Western Balkan consumer-protection frameworks and the emerging EU digital single market acquis, with particular focus on the E-Commerce Directive replacement cycle and the Platform-to-Business Regulation. The research team collected and coded 120 legislative documents from six Western Balkan jurisdictions and conducted a series of expert roundtables with consumer-protection authorities in Belgrade, Podgorica, and Sarajevo. Deliverables included a comparative report submitted to the Ministry of Internal and Foreign Trade of Serbia, three peer-reviewed articles, and a public-facing policy brief. The project ran for 30 months with a team of four legal researchers from the University of Novi Sad and the Institute for Comparative Law in Belgrade.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Comparative Law, Belgrade
Faculty of Law, University of Montenegro

projects.title: Transposition Readiness Assessment for the EU Digital Services Act in Western Balkan Candidate Countries
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral research collaboration between the Faculty of Law at the University of Novi Sad and the Institute for European Private Law at the University of Hamburg, co-funded by the German Academic Exchange Service and the Serbian Ministry of Science. The project produced a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction readiness matrix assessing 34 DSA obligations against the current legislative and institutional situation in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Albania. Đurić led the work package on liability and enforcement mechanisms, coordinating three doctoral researchers. The project concluded with a workshop in Novi Sad attended by representatives from the Serbian Ministry of Trade and the Serbian Chamber of Commerce, and produced a final report submitted to both funding bodies.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Institute for European Private Law, University of Hamburg
Faculty of Law, University of Tirana

projects.title: Minority Shareholder Remedies in Western Balkan Company Law: Convergence and Divergence
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje stepen konvergencije mehanizama zaštite manjinskih akcionara u pravnim sistemima Zapadnog Balkana prema standardima EU direktiva o društvenom pravu, naročito Direktive 2017/1132 i Direktive o reorganizaciji i insolventnosti. Interdisciplinarni tim pravnika iz Srbije, Sjeverne Makedonije i Bosne i Hercegovine prikuplja i kodira sudske predmete, izjave zakonodavaca i komparativne normativne analize. Bjelica je odgovoran za srpski nacionalni izvještaj i za komparativnu analizu vrednosnih standarda u squeeze-out postupcima. Krajnji cilj je izrada policy dokumenta sa preporukama za zakonodavne reforme u svakoj od obuhvaćenih zemalja.
partners: Pravni fakultet Justinijan Први, Univerzitet Sv. Kiril i Metodij, Skoplje
Pravni fakultet, Univerzitet u Sarajevu
Institut za uporedno pravo, Beograd

projects.title: Secured Transactions Reform in the Western Balkans: Comparative Analysis and Legislative Recommendations
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: BALSETRA is a three-year research project coordinated by the Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad, examining the state of secured transactions law across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and North Macedonia. The project combines doctrinal comparative analysis with empirical data gathered through interviews with commercial practitioners and reviews of court decisions. Its primary output is a set of model legislative recommendations tailored to the legal traditions of the Western Balkans region and compatible with UNCITRAL standards and EU acquis. Lačok contributes to the work package on Serbian domestic law, focusing specifically on pledge law, fiduciary transfer, and registration system design. The project is expected to produce a policy brief addressed to the Serbian Ministry of Justice.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of East Sarajevo
Faculty of Law 'Justinijan I', Saints Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje

projects.title: Legal Frameworks for Smart-Contract-Based Settlement in Agricultural Commodity Markets of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines the doctrinal and regulatory preconditions for the valid and enforceable use of smart-contract settlement mechanisms in agricultural commodity trades governed by the laws of Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Research activities include a comparative statutory analysis, a survey of commodity exchange operators and brokerage firms, and the development of a model contractual framework including natural-language and code components. The project produces three journal articles, a policy brief addressed to the Serbian Securities Commission, and a model contract template reviewed by practitioners. A final workshop brings together legal academics, commodity exchange representatives, and technology companies to disseminate results.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Comparative Law, Belgrade
Faculty of Economics and Law, University of Banja Luka

projects.title: Cross-Border Legal Interoperability of Distributed Ledger Technology in Agricultural Trade Finance
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSS-DLT is a cross-border cooperation project examining the legal and regulatory barriers to using distributed ledger technology for trade finance instruments—letters of credit, warehouse receipts, and payment guarantees—in Hungarian–Serbian agricultural trade corridors. Janković leads the work package on legal harmonisation, responsible for mapping divergences between Serbian commercial law and Hungarian private law, identifying mutual recognition gaps, and drafting recommendations for regulatory alignment. The project also develops a practical guide for agri-food SMEs and a training module for customs and banking compliance officers. Two pilot transactions are documented as case studies in collaboration with partner financial institutions.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina Agro-Finance Centre, Novi Sad
Pannonia Rural Development Association, Pécs

projects.title: Harmonizacija preventivnih okvira za restrukturiranje malih i mikro preduzeća sa pravom EU u Srbiji
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat ispituje usklađenost srpskog stečajnog i predinsolventnog zakonodavstva sa zahtevima Direktive (EU) 2019/1023, s posebnim fokusom na mikro i mala preduzeća. Istraživački tim sprovodi uporednu analizu zakonodavstava zemalja regiona, empirijsku analizu sudske prakse i intervjue s praktičarima, s ciljem izrade konkretnih preporuka za zakonodavne izmene. U okviru projekta planira se i organizacija stručnog skupa s predstavnicima pravosudnih institucija i privrednih komora. Žigić je odgovoran za segment koji se odnosi na standarde potvrde plana reorganizacije i cramdown mehanizme. Projekat koordiniše Pravni fakultet Univerziteta u Beogradu, a Pravni fakultet u Novom Sadu je partner institucija.
partners: Pravni fakultet, Univerzitet u Beogradu
Institut za uporedno pravo, Beograd
Privredna komora Vojvodine

projects.title: Digital Accountability and Liability in Automated Legal Relations: Southeast European Perspectives
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DIALAW examines how private law frameworks in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina are adapting to liability questions posed by automated and algorithmic systems in commercial and consumer contracts. The project team of four researchers from Novi Sad and two partner institutions conducts doctrinal analysis, comparative studies with EU member state law, and empirical surveys of judicial and regulatory practice. Outputs include a comparative monograph, ten peer-reviewed articles, a model legislative proposal for the Serbian Ministry of Justice, and three workshops for judges and legal practitioners. The project is funded under the Ideas programme of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University Saints Cyril and Methodius, Skopje
Faculty of Law, University of Sarajevo

projects.title: Alignment of Serbian Private Law with the EU Digital Acquis: Contract and Liability Dimensions
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral research cooperation between the Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad, and the Institute for European and Comparative Law, University of Vienna. The project maps the divergences between Serbian contract and liability law and the EU digital law acquis—including the Digital Services Act, the AI Act, and the Product Liability Directive (revised)—relevant to ongoing Serbian accession negotiations. The collaboration produced two joint publications, a joint workshop held in Vienna in April 2024, and a policy brief submitted to the Serbian Ministry of European Integration in October 2024.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Institute for European and Comparative Law, University of Vienna

projects.title: Succession Law Reform in Post-Socialist European States: Comparative Foundations and Policy Options
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project conducted a comparative legal analysis of succession law reform trajectories in six post-socialist European states (Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Bulgaria), focusing on the tension between testamentary freedom and protected heirship. Research activities included legislative text analysis, a systematic review of published court decisions across the six jurisdictions (approximately 900 decisions coded), 47 semi-structured interviews with notaries and judges in Serbia, and two comparative workshops held in Novi Sad (2022) and Ljubljana (2023). The project produced draft legislative recommendations for reform of the Serbian succession law provisions within the Civil Code drafting process and delivered a publicly accessible bilingual (Serbian/English) database of post-1990 succession legislation in the six target states. Three journal articles and one edited book chapter were submitted from the project.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Ljubljana
Institute of Private International Law and Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Succession in the Western Balkans–EU Border Region: Legal Uncertainty and Practical Solutions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed the practical difficulties encountered by families in the Hungary–Serbia border region when dealing with cross-border estates after the entry into force of EU Succession Regulation 650/2012. The Faculty of Law, Novi Sad, led the work package on legal analysis and practitioner training. Activities included mapping of conflict-of-law problems through 60 notary case file reviews in Subotica and Sombor, preparation of a bilingual practitioner guide (Hungarian/Serbian) on cross-border estate procedures, and delivery of five joint training seminars for notaries and court officials on both sides of the border. The project also produced a policy brief addressed to the Serbian Ministry of Justice recommending bilateral treaty negotiations with Hungary and Croatia. The Novi Sad team consisted of three researchers and one doctoral student.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Pécs
Notarial Chamber of Vojvodina
Hungarian Chamber of Notaries, Southern Region

projects.title: Personality Rights and Damage Assessment in Post-Yugoslav Legal Systems
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates how courts in Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina assess non-pecuniary damages for personality rights violations, with emphasis on judicial reasoning and inter-court consistency. It involves collection and coding of approximately 600 court decisions across the three jurisdictions, construction of a comparative quantitative dataset, and doctrinal analysis of underlying legal frameworks. The project aims to produce a comparative monograph and a set of practical recommendations for judicial training programmes. Predrag Ćirić is responsible for the Serbian case law component, including database searches, decision coding, and drafting of the Serbian national report. The project is coordinated by the Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Rijeka
Faculty of Law, University of Sarajevo

projects.title: Urban Property Governance: Legal Frameworks for Sustainable Residential Building Management in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines the legal conditions for effective governance of multi-unit residential buildings across six Western Balkan jurisdictions, comparing property rights frameworks, homeowners association rules, and public enforcement mechanisms. The research team collects court decisions, administrative records, and building management data from Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. One work package, to which Mladenović contributes, is dedicated to the property law treatment of shared technical infrastructure—heating systems, elevators, and utility risers—and how maintenance costs are allocated when infrastructure serves mixed residential and commercial units. Outputs include comparative country reports, a model legislative commentary, and a policy brief directed at the relevant Serbian ministry.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Law, University of Sarajevo
Institute for Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Energy Renovation and Property Rights: Cross-Border Legal Challenges in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ENRENO brought together legal scholars and urban policy researchers from Novi Sad and Pécs to identify property law and administrative barriers to energy renovation of residential condominium buildings in the Hungarian-Serbian border region. Mladenović contributed to the comparative legal analysis work package, mapping Serbian co-ownership rules as they apply to façades, roofs, and basement technical rooms that are targets of insulation and heating system replacement projects. The project produced a bilingual handbook for building managers, a comparative legal report submitted to both national energy agencies, and two academic publications. It also organised three joint workshops for building managers, municipal officials, and lawyers on both sides of the border.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Law, University of Pécs
City of Subotica – Directorate for Construction and Urban Planning
Municipality of Mohács

projects.title: Administrative Silence and Effective Judicial Protection in the Western Balkans: Comparative Standards and Reform Pathways
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje normativne, institucionalne i empirijske dimenzije ćutanja uprave u Srbiji, Severnoj Makedoniji, Bosni i Hercegovini i Crnoj Gori. Cilj je izraditi komparativnu bazu podataka sudske prakse i zakonodavnih rešenja, sprovesti anketu o administrativnim kapacitetima u 120 opština u regionu i formulisati konkretne preporuke za zakonodavne reforme usklađene sa EU standardima. Poseban fokus stavlja se na interskciju između digitalizacije uprave i primene rokova. Projektni tim čine istraživači iz Novog Sada, Skoplja i Sarajeva. Predviđeni rezultati uključuju dva naučna članka u međunarodnim časopisima, jedan policy brief namenjen ministarstvima i organizaciju regionalne naučne konferencije.
partners: Pravni fakultet Iustinianus Primus, Ss. Ćirilo i Metodije Univerzitet, Skoplje
Pravni fakultet, Univerzitet u Sarajevu
Institut za komparativno pravo, Beograd

projects.title: Strengthening Legal Frameworks for Local Asset Management in Vojvodina Municipalities
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project examines deficiencies in the legal and administrative frameworks governing local asset management across twelve municipalities in Vojvodina, with a focus on property registration gaps, inter-agency coordination failures, and the practical capacity of local self-government units to exercise ownership functions over public goods. The project team, led by a senior professor at the Faculty of Law in Novi Sad, collects data through structured interviews with municipal legal officers and review of municipal property inventories. Ninkov is responsible for the comparative legal analysis component, reviewing analogous frameworks in Hungary and Croatia. Deliverables include a policy report addressed to the Provincial Secretariat and a set of model procedural guidelines for municipalities.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Association of Municipalities and Cities of Vojvodina
City Administration of Novi Sad – Department for Property and Legal Affairs

projects.title: Administrative Justice Traditions and EU Integration in the Western Balkans: Historical Roots, Present Deficits, Reform Paths
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examined the relationship between inherited administrative-judicial institutions and the effectiveness of EU-driven administrative justice reforms across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. The research team combined archival and doctrinal legal history with empirical analysis of court statistics and a structured interview programme (n=48 interviews with judges, lawyers, and civil servants). The project produced seven journal articles, two edited book chapters, a policy brief submitted to the Serbian Ministry of Justice, and a comparative database of administrative court legislation in the region covering 1919 to 2023, made publicly available through the Faculty of Law repository.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Regulatory Transplants and Constitutional Limits: Sub-legislative Rulemaking in Western Balkan Accession States
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat ispituje ustavnopravna ograničenja prenosa normativnih ovlašćenja na regulatorna tela u Srbiji, Bosni i Hercegovini i Severnoj Makedoniji, s posebnim fokusom na tehničke oblasti pod uticajem procesa pridruživanja EU. Tim od sedam istraživača sa Pravnog fakulteta Univerziteta u Novom Sadu i partnerskih institucija analizira sistematski korpus od oko 300 podzakonskih akata i tehničkih propisa donetih između 2015. i 2023. godine. Krajnji ishodi uključuju izradu komparativne studije, bazu odluka relevantnih ustavnih i upravnih sudova u regionu, i set preporuka za zakonodavnu praksu.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Sarajevo
Iustinianus Primus Faculty of Law, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Institute for Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Decision Support Frameworks for Strategic Investment Planning in South-East European Public Institutions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated multi-criteria decision support frameworks specifically adapted to institutional, regulatory, and data-availability constraints of public organisations in South-East Europe. Activities included a cross-country survey of decision practices in 45 public institutions across Serbia, North Macedonia, and Montenegro; development of tailored AHP and fuzzy TOPSIS instruments; and delivery of three stakeholder workshops. The project produced a methodological guide for procurement committees and budget officers, piloted in four Serbian municipalities. Two journal articles and one conference paper were published. The project was hosted at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, with research collaboration from partner universities in Niš and Skopje.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Niš
Faculty of Economics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje, North Macedonia

projects.title: Cross-Border Validation of Public Procurement Evaluation Tools in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSVAL aims to harmonise public procurement evaluation practices between Hungarian and Serbian municipalities along the shared border region by testing and adapting MCDM-based evaluation tools in a cross-border context. Sara Radović leads the work package on criteria framework development and stakeholder consultation, coordinating activities across four Serbian partner municipalities in Bačka. The project involves joint training events for procurement officers, development of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) decision support toolkit, and production of policy briefs for regional development agencies. Expected outputs include a transferable evaluation protocol suitable for EU-funded cross-border procurement procedures.
partners: Subotica Development Agency
Municipality of Baja, Hungary

projects.title: Детерминанте прихватања дигиталних плаћања међу старијим одраслима у прекограничним регионима Србије и Мађарске
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Пројекат је испитивао факторе прихватања мобилних и бесконтактних плаћања код особа старијих од 55 година у пограничном региону Суботица–Сегедин. Применом заједничких анкетних протокола на обе стране границе прикупљено је 940 упитника у две тачке мерења. Резултати су коришћени за израду препорука за банкарске и трговинске партнере у региону. Пројекат је такође обухватао два радионичка циклуса за сениоре о безбедном коришћењу дигиталних платних апликација, реализована у партнерству са локалним удружењима пензионера у Суботици и Сегедину.
partners: Széchenyi István University, Győr
Удружење пензионера Суботица

projects.title: Финансијска дигитализација и понашање старијих корисника у Србији: панел студија
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат финансира трећу и четврту таласну фазу longitudinalne панел студије започете 2015. године, проширујући узорак испитаника из Војводине на Централну Србију. Поред анкетних метода, уводи се анализа анонимизованих трансакционих података у сарадњи с партнерском штедионицом. Истражују се ефекти политике обавезне дигитализације исплате пензија на понашање корисника и субјективно финансијско благостање. Планирани излазни резултати укључују три научна рада у рецензираним часописима, скуп анонимизованих панел података доступан за поновну употребу и извештај за доносиоце политика на српском језику.
partners: Економски факултет, Универзитет у Београду
Регионална штедионица Панонија (измишљена организација)

projects.title: Readiness Assessment Framework for ERP Adoption in SMEs of the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed and piloted a bilingual (Hungarian and Serbian) change readiness assessment toolkit tailored to SMEs operating in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The toolkit comprised a validated 32-item diagnostic questionnaire, a facilitated workshop protocol, and an interpretation guide for use by business consultants without academic backgrounds. The toolkit was piloted in 22 SMEs across both countries, with paired pre- and post-pilot data collected to assess usability and predictive validity against six-month implementation progress markers. Training sessions for regional business support organisations were conducted on both sides of the border. All materials were released as open-access resources in both languages.
partners: Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina (Novi Sad)
West Pannonia Regional Development Agency (Győr)

projects.title: Post-Implementation Knowledge Retention in ERP-Dependent SMEs: Mechanisms, Measurement, and Intervention Design
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project addresses the systematic erosion of ERP system knowledge that occurs in SMEs in the years following implementation, a phenomenon that limits long-term return on investment and drives costly re-implementation cycles. The project combines longitudinal competency measurement across a cohort of 30 Serbian SMEs, development and testing of a low-burden knowledge retention protocol, and construction of an open benchmark dataset. A key deliverable is a diagnostic instrument enabling SME managers to estimate their current knowledge retention risk without engaging external consultants. The project also funds two doctoral researchers and includes a policy brief directed at the Serbian government's digitalisation support programmes.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Serbian Chamber of Commerce – Directorate for SMEs

projects.title: Integrity Verification Frameworks for Long-Term Audit Log Archives in Serbian Regulated Sectors
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project addressed the absence of standardised integrity verification procedures for long-term audit log archives held by regulated entities in Vojvodina and Serbia more broadly. Activities included a survey of log management practices at twenty financial and healthcare institutions, development of a reference verification protocol based on hash-tree structures, and preparation of a public guidance document addressed to compliance officers and IT auditors. A small software toolkit was produced implementing the verification protocol for PostgreSQL and IBM DB2 audit log formats. The toolkit was tested at three partner institutions under non-disclosure agreement. Results informed the policy recommendations submitted to the National Bank of Serbia's IT supervision working group in 2012.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat for Finance, Vojvodina

projects.title: Microstructure Dynamics and Regulatory Design for Thin Commodity Exchanges in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: THINEX investigates the microstructure properties of agricultural commodity spot markets in the Western Balkans region, with a focus on how thin trading conditions interact with regulatory choices about transparency, market-maker licensing, and circuit-breaker rules. The project combines empirical analysis of transaction-level data from Serbian and regional exchanges with agent-based simulation experiments. The primary deliverables are a validated simulation platform, three journal articles, a policy brief directed at the Serbian Ministry of Agriculture and commodity exchange operators, and a publicly available dataset of cleaned historical grain price series. The project funds one doctoral student and two research visits to partner institutions.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Belgrade
Department of Economics, University of Pécs

projects.title: Cross-Border Agricultural Data Infrastructures for Regional Market Monitoring in the Hungary–Serbia Border Area
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGRILINK builds a shared data reporting and market monitoring infrastructure connecting agricultural producers, warehouses, and exchange operators on both sides of the Hungarian-Serbian border. Fehér contributes the market simulation module, which uses aggregated price and volume feeds from the shared infrastructure as calibration inputs and generates quarterly market condition reports. The module flags anomalous price deviations and thin-market liquidity warnings for distribution to registered participants. The project involves three workshops per year and a joint pilot deployment at two border-region commodity warehouses. Fehér's role is approximately 20 percent of his working time over the project duration.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Semantic Standards for Interoperable Public Procurement in South-East Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a family of OWL 2 ontology profiles and SHACL validation constraint sets covering the procurement systems of Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Montenegro, and North Macedonia. Core outputs include a regional procurement ontology registry, a set of SPARQL-based alignment tests, and a bilingual (Serbian/English) ontology documentation portal. The project also produced policy briefs submitted to the national public procurement offices of all four countries and to the Regional Cooperation Council in Sarajevo. Two PhD students completed dissertations within the project.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Sarajevo
Faculty of Economics, University of Montenegro
Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University Skopje

projects.title: Cross-Border Public Procurement Interoperability Along the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSBUY addressed the practical barriers preventing joint cross-border procurement under the Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia programme. Krstić led the semantic interoperability work package, which delivered a semantic mediation layer connecting the Hungarian EKR and Serbian e-procurement platforms, a shared SKOS qualification vocabulary in Hungarian and Serbian, and a set of RDF mapping rules for bidder registration data exchange. The project involved piloting joint simplified tenders with two contracting authorities (one municipality on each side of the border) and produced a replication guide for other border region programmes.

projects.title: Longitudinal Modelling of Revenue Retention and Churn Dynamics in B2B Software Markets of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat ispituje dinamiku zadržavanja prihoda i odliva klijenata u B2B segmentu tržišta poslovnog softvera u zemljama Zapadnog Balkana, s naglaskom na Srbiju i Severnu Makedoniju. Glavni cilj je izgradnja longitudinalnog analitičkog okvira koji kombininju survival analizu s metodama strojnog učenja za rano upozoravanje na rizik od odliva. Pored akademskog istraživanja, projekat predviđa razvoj prototipskog alata za analitiku zadržavanja koji će biti testiran u saradnji s dva partnerska softverska preduzeća. Dunja Simić učestvuje u prikupljanju i pripremi podataka, specifikaciji survival modela i izradi izveštaja. Projektom rukovodi njen mentor s Ekonomskog fakulteta u Subotici.
partners: Ekonomski fakultet u Subotici, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Privacy-Aware Federated Analytics Protocols for SME Industry Clusters in the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project develops and pilots a federated analytics platform for two existing industry clusters, one in Subotica and one in Pécs, covering food processing and light manufacturing respectively. The technical work covers the design of a secure aggregation server, a standardised data connector that maps heterogeneous ERP schemas to a common ontology, and a governance toolkit for cluster coordinators. Fejsa contributes to the privacy protocol design and to the evaluation of utility–privacy trade-offs in the pilot deployments. The project also includes workshops for cluster member firms on data sharing rights under GDPR and Serbian data protection law. The platform is intended to remain operational after project completion, administered by the two cluster organisations.

projects.title: Accounting Information System Quality and Decision Confidence in Vojvodina Family Manufacturers
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project systematically mapped AIS quality conditions across a representative sample of family-owned manufacturing enterprises registered in the Vojvodina region, linking quality indicators to behavioral outcomes at the managerial level. Field data collection involved 214 firms across five manufacturing subsectors. The project produced the refined 18-item PIQ scale, a regional benchmark database of AIS quality scores made available to participating firms, and three peer-reviewed publications. A practical audit checklist distributed to the Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina emerged from the project's final dissemination workshop. Two doctoral students participated in data collection and co-authored conference papers from the dataset.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina

projects.title: Digital Readiness and Information Governance in Family SMEs of the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DIGIFAM is a cross-border cooperation project bringing together researchers and business support organizations from Vojvodina and southern Hungary to assess digital readiness and information governance maturity in family-owned SMEs. Žarković leads the work package focused on accounting information governance, coordinating data collection in Serbia and contributing to the joint assessment framework developed with Hungarian partners. The work package has produced two harmonized survey instruments translated and validated in Serbian and Hungarian, a comparative database of 180 firms across the border region, and an advisory guide for SME support agencies. The project also supports student mobility between the partner universities.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Process Mining Methods for Continuous Improvement of Administrative Services in Higher Education
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates the feasibility of deploying lightweight process mining pipelines as permanent monitoring tools within the administrative units of two faculties in Vojvodina. The work plan covers log extraction automation, the definition of institution-specific conformance reference models, and the design of a dashboard that presents key performance indicators—cycle time, deviation rate, rework frequency—to administrative managers without process mining expertise. Vesna Orlović is responsible for the conformance checking component and contributes to the dashboard specification. The expected outcome is a reusable methodological template and a pilot deployment at one participating faculty, with documentation sufficient for adoption by other institutions in the region.

Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Bihejvioralni faktori nedovoljne stope štednje domaćinstava u Srbiji: eksperimentalna i anketna analiza
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat ispituje zašto stopa štednje domaćinstava u Srbiji ostaje ispod regionalnog proseka uprkos rastu realnih dohodaka. Kombinuju se laboratorijski eksperimenti sa studentima i terenski eksperiment sa 600 domaćinstava u Autonomnoj pokrajini Vojvodini. Mereni su parametri hiperboličnog diskontovanja, averzija prema gubitku i poverenje u finansijske institucije. Poseban radni paket bavi se rodno specifičnim razlikama u štednom ponašanju. Projekat finansira Pokrajinski sekretarijat za visoko obrazovanje i naučnoistraživačku delatnost AP Vojvodine. Rezultati će biti dostavljeni pokrajinskim organima kao osnova za preporuke u oblasti podsticanja finansijske pismenosti i razvoja dobrovoljnih penzijskih proizvoda.

projects.title: Fiscal Credibility, Debt Market Development, and European Integration Trajectories in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled a harmonised quarterly dataset on sovereign borrowing costs, fiscal frameworks, and exchange rate arrangements for six Western Balkan economies covering 1998–2023. It tested competing hypotheses about the drivers of fiscal credibility signals visible in secondary bond market spreads, with particular attention to the interaction between IMF programme anchors, domestic fiscal rules, and currency regime choices. The team produced seven working papers, three journal submissions, and a policy brief series distributed to the Serbian Ministry of Finance and the EU Delegation in Belgrade. A public dataset of cleaned and documented spread series is being prepared for release via the University of Novi Sad data repository.

projects.title: Financial Market Integration Between the Western Balkans and the European Union: Institutional and Market-Based Channels
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project examined the degree of financial market integration between Hungary and Serbia and the broader Western Balkan region, focusing on bond and money markets. Natalija Lekić led the work package on sovereign fixed income market linkages, overseeing data collection from the National Bank of Serbia and the Hungarian Government Debt Management Agency, and coordinating joint workshops in Novi Sad and Budapest. The project produced comparative analyses of yield co-movement and identified regulatory and institutional barriers to deeper integration, with recommendations addressed to both national authorities and the European Commission's DG NEAR.

projects.title: Corporate Tax Base Erosion Through Transfer Pricing in Central and Eastern Europe: Measurement, Determinants, and Policy Responses
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project constructs a longitudinal database linking Serbian Business Registers Agency financial statements, customs declaration microdata, and Orbis records for approximately 1,200 foreign-owned subsidiaries active in Serbia between 2010 and 2022. The database is used to estimate annual corporate income tax revenue losses attributable to transfer pricing manipulation, to identify the industry sectors and ownership structures where manipulation is most intense, and to evaluate the effectiveness of Serbian legislative responses to OECD BEPS recommendations. The project also includes a comparative module covering Hungary, Romania, and Croatia. A policy brief series targets the Serbian Tax Administration, the Ministry of Finance, and the Secretariat for Finance of the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
