projects.title: Transfer Pricing Regulation Harmonisation and Tax Revenue Sustainability in the Western Balkans EU Accession Process
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANSPREG is a cross-border research and capacity-building project that addresses the alignment of transfer pricing regulatory frameworks in Serbia with EU acquis requirements as part of the accession negotiation process, with a comparative focus on the Hungarian experience during its own accession period. Activities include a systematic legislative gap analysis, a quantitative assessment of revenue effects of regulatory harmonisation using simulation methods, three regional workshops for tax officials, and the production of a transfer pricing audit manual adapted to the resource constraints of Western Balkan tax administrations. The project funds two doctoral researchers, one based in Novi Sad and one in Budapest.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Corvinus University of Budapest, Department of Finance
Hungarian National Tax and Customs Administration Research Institute

projects.title: Remittance Volatility and Macroeconomic Stabilisation in Western Balkan Labour-Exporting Economies
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REMSTAB examined whether and under what institutional conditions remittance inflows reduce macroeconomic volatility in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The project combined panel econometric analysis of central bank and World Bank data with two diaspora surveys—one in Germany and one in Austria. Key outputs included a policy brief submitted to the National Bank of Serbia and three peer-reviewed articles. The project financed two field survey rounds, econometric software licences, and supported one PhD student who contributed to the survey design and data cleaning. Total budget was approximately 4.2 million RSD. The project concluded with a public event at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica attended by representatives from the Provincial Secretariat.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Niš
Institute of Economic Sciences, Belgrade
University of Banja Luka, Faculty of Economics

projects.title: Diaspora Financial Behaviour and Its Development Implications for Cross-Border Regions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DIASFIN is a cross-border project examining how diaspora financial behaviour—including remittances, savings, and investment decisions—affects development outcomes in the Hungarian-Serbian border region, including Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád county. The Faculty of Economics in Subotica leads Work Package 3, which covers survey design, fieldwork, and econometric analysis of household-level data from both sides of the border. The project coordinates with three Hungarian partners and one Romanian observer institution. Expected outputs include a joint database of diaspora financial flows, two policy reports, and capacity-building workshops for municipal financial officers. Krisztina Takács leads the Serbian side of the survey design and is responsible for all quantitative analysis deliverables under WP3.
partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Economics and Business Administration
Csongrád-Csanád County Development Agency
Subotica Business Incubator
Hungarian Central Statistical Office, Southern Plain Regional Directorate

projects.title: Secondary Market Development for Non-Performing Loans in South-Eastern Europe: Regulatory Barriers and Resolution Outcomes
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral research project between the Faculty of Economics in Subotica and the Corvinus University of Budapest, funded under the Serbian–Hungarian intergovernmental scientific cooperation scheme. The project assembled a comparative database of NPL transaction records, servicer contract terms, and legal enforcement timelines for Serbia and Hungary over the period 1998–2005. Fieldwork included structured interviews with bank resolution officers, licensed servicers, and insolvency court administrators in both countries. The main output was a joint working paper series, two journal articles, and a policy brief submitted to the National Bank of Serbia and the Hungarian Financial Supervisory Authority on minimum data standardisation requirements for cross-border NPL portfolio sales.
partners: Corvinus University of Budapest, Institute of Finance and Accounting
National Bank of Serbia, Financial Stability Department

projects.title: Determinants of Resolution Costs in Serbian Corporate Insolvency: Implications for Creditor Recovery
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A two-year project funded by the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina to investigate the direct and indirect costs of formal corporate insolvency proceedings in Serbia and their impact on unsecured and secured creditor recovery rates. The project built a primary dataset from commercial court records in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Zrenjanin covering 212 closed insolvency cases from 2007 to 2012. Cost components analysed included administrator fees, legal representation, asset appraisal, and court dues. The project produced three working papers, one journal article, and a practitioner guide on cost-efficient insolvency administration submitted to the Serbian Bankruptcy Supervision Agency.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad
Serbian Bankruptcy Supervision Agency

projects.title: Gender Gaps in SME Credit Markets: Cross-Border Evidence and Supervisory Implications for the Hungary–Serbia Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project built a joint research infrastructure for analysing gender-differentiated SME lending across the Hungary–Serbia border region. Activities included harmonisation of loan file sampling protocols, creation of a bilingual coded dataset of approximately 6,000 anonymised loan applications from banks on both sides of the border, and a series of joint workshops with banking supervisory staff. The project produced four research outputs, a policy brief submitted to the National Bank of Serbia and to the Magyar Nemzeti Bank, and a public dataset deposited at the University of Novi Sad institutional repository. It also supported two doctoral students, one at each partner institution, and funded two short-term research exchanges.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs
Vojvodina Development Agency
Southern Transdanubia Regional Development Council

projects.title: Audit Trail Evidence and Discretionary Bias in Serbian SME Bank Lending
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project systematically analyses credit audit trail completeness and its relationship to gender-differentiated lending outcomes in Serbian commercial banks. The team digitised and coded over 9,000 loan files from six partner banks under data-sharing agreements, building a structured file-quality index. Quantitative work investigates how documentation gaps interact with loan officer characteristics and branch-level policy variation to produce differential terms for female and male SME applicants. The project also develops and pilots a supervisory audit-trail checklist for use by bank internal audit departments and is producing a set of recommendations for the National Bank of Serbia's banking inspection unit.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Association of Serbian Banks (research committee)

projects.title: Islamic Finance Regulatory Frameworks for the Western Balkans: Comparative Analysis and Legislative Recommendations
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project produced a systematic comparative analysis of legal and regulatory preconditions for introducing Islamic finance products in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The team reviewed banking, tax, securities, and insolvency legislation in each jurisdiction, conducted interviews with central bank officials and commercial bankers, and ran two stakeholder workshops with representatives of Muslim community organisations and finance practitioners. The primary output is a set of three jurisdiction-specific legislative reform proposals, each accompanied by a regulatory impact assessment. Secondary outputs include a regional database of Islamic finance legal provisions and a university-level teaching case collection. Total budget approximately RSD 12 million.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Sarajevo
Faculty of Economics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Institute for Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Green Sukuk Market Development and EU Sustainable Finance Integration
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project examines the conditions under which green sukuk could be issued by public or private issuers in Hungary and Serbia as a tool for financing environmental infrastructure. Orlović leads the work package on regulatory harmonisation, examining alignment between green sukuk frameworks and the EU Taxonomy Regulation and the European Green Bond Standard. Partner activities cover market demand analysis and investor profiling in both countries. The project includes a joint training programme for financial sector professionals in both jurisdictions delivered through a series of five workshops, and a policy brief addressed to the Hungarian and Serbian ministries of finance.
partners: Department of Finance, Corvinus University of Budapest
Green Investment Advisory Centre Novi Sad (GIAC NS)
Hungarian Development Bank Research Institute

projects.title: Financial Reporting Quality and Capital Market Development in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project builds a harmonised, longitudinal database of financial statements and earnings management indicators for all non-financial firms listed on the stock exchanges of Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina from 2010 to 2022. Key activities include collection and standardisation of raw financial statement data, estimation of accrual-based and real-activities earnings management proxies using multiple benchmark models, and analysis of the relationship between reporting quality and capital market outcomes including liquidity, cost of capital, and institutional investor participation. The project also compares regulatory and enforcement frameworks across the three jurisdictions to identify governance factors associated with higher reporting quality, and produces policy briefs addressed to the relevant securities commissions.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of East Sarajevo
Institute of Economic Sciences, Belgrade

projects.title: Structured Digital Financial Reporting and Analyst Information Environment in South-East Europe
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: XBRL-SEE examines the consequences of mandatory XBRL tagging of financial statements for information asymmetry and earnings management in Serbian and Hungarian listed companies. The project collects all available XBRL-tagged annual reports filed with the Serbian Business Registers Agency and the Hungarian National Tax Authority from 2019 onward and compares reporting quality metrics before and after tagging mandates using a staggered difference-in-differences design. The work package led by Srđan Sabo is responsible for constructing earnings management estimates and for the econometric identification strategy. Cross-border collaboration with the Hungarian partner provides access to proprietary analyst forecast data enabling information asymmetry proxies not available from public sources in Serbia.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs
Vojvodina Development Agency

projects.title: Rebuilding City Brand Capacities in the Autonomous Province of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project examines the place branding capacities of eight municipalities in Vojvodina with populations between 30,000 and 100,000 inhabitants. The research team is conducting a comprehensive audit of each municipality's promotional infrastructure, including investment promotion offices, staffing levels, budgets, and digital presence. A benchmarking framework adapted from comparable Central European municipalities is being developed and piloted. Attila Szabó is responsible for the content analysis workstream, coding promotional materials and coordinating a series of practitioner workshops in which preliminary findings are presented to municipal officials. The project will deliver a publicly available capacity-building handbook in Serbian, Hungarian, and English, aimed at helping Vojvodina municipalities improve the coherence and targeting of their investment promotion communications.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Economic Research of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Association of Municipalities and Cities of Vojvodina

projects.title: Atmospheric Management Strategies for Traditional Open-Air Markets in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project examined how low-cost atmospheric interventions—sound, scent, and visual display adjustments—can support the economic sustainability of traditional open-air markets in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The Subotica team, led by Ranković, was responsible for the consumer behaviour work package, conducting shopper surveys and observational studies at four partner market sites. The project produced a practical guidelines document for market administrators, a joint training workshop attended by 38 market managers, and three peer-reviewed publications. Partner organisations included the City of Subotica Market Administration, the Debrecen Market Operators Association, and the Regional Development Agency of Southern Transdanubia.
partners: City of Subotica Market Administration
Debrecen Market Operators Association
Regional Development Agency of Southern Transdanubia, Pécs
Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs

projects.title: Sensory Retail Environments and Consumer Wellbeing in Post-Socialist Urban Markets
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENSRET investigates whether improvements to atmospheric conditions in Serbian open-air markets affect not only commercial outcomes (dwell time, spending, unplanned purchases) but also subjective wellbeing and place attachment among regular shoppers. The project combines longitudinal survey panels (three Vojvodina markets, approximately 600 tracked shoppers), sensor-based environmental monitoring (temperature, noise level, particulate matter), and in-depth qualitative interviews with 40 vendors and 40 frequent shoppers. A secondary objective is to develop open-source data collection protocols that municipal market managers can apply independently. The project is hosted at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica and involves a collaborating team from the Department of Psychology at the University of Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Urban Planning of Subotica
Novi Sad City Market Enterprise

projects.title: Brand Equity Measurement Systems for Agri-food SMEs in the Pannonian Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project developed shared protocols for tracking brand equity among agri-food SMEs operating across the Hungarian-Serbian border region, with a focus on harmonising survey instruments, sampling frames and reporting templates for use by regional development agencies. Molnár led the work package on measurement methodology, coordinating adaptation of the panel instrument for cross-border use, organising two training workshops for agency staff in Subotica and Pécs, and producing a practical guidebook in Serbian and Hungarian. The project also delivered a comparative report on brand equity levels and drivers across 34 SMEs observed over two waves, used by participating chambers of commerce for sector benchmarking.
partners: Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Regional Development Agency of Southern Transdanubia, Pécs, Hungary
Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Qualitative Panel Methods for Small Enterprise Market Research in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: QUALTRACK addresses the absence of standardised qualitative longitudinal methods in Serbian market research practice. The project is developing a methodological framework that integrates repeated semi-structured interviews with quantitative panel surveys in SME marketing studies. Empirical work focuses on agri-food and food-processing micro-enterprises in Vojvodina as the primary sector, but the framework is designed for broader application. Activities include field testing of interview protocols across three annual rounds with 20 firms, development of a coding scheme for longitudinal qualitative data in NVivo, and publication of an open-access methods handbook. A PhD student is co-supervised under the project. The project runs at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica with one collaborating partner.
partners: Institute of Economic Sciences, Belgrade

projects.title: Barriers to Green Purchasing in Vojvodina: A Multi-Method Investigation of the Attitude–Behaviour Gap
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project funded the consumer diary study, the discrete choice follow-up work, and the first wave of the longitudinal panel described in Molnár's publication record. The project team comprised four researchers from the Faculty of Economics in Subotica and one external collaborator from the University of Debrecen. Activities included two public workshops in Novi Sad and Subotica presenting results to local business associations, and the development of a publicly available dataset of green purchasing surveys in Serbian and Hungarian. Total budget: approximately 1.8 million RSD. The project produced three journal articles, two conference presentations, and one master's thesis co-supervised by the PI.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, University of Debrecen

projects.title: Central and Eastern European Approaches to Sustainable Retail Environments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CEASURE is a cross-border applied research and knowledge transfer project involving retail industry partners and academic teams in Hungary and Serbia. Molnár leads Work Package 3, which focuses on consumer-side barriers to sustainable retail adoption, including packaging preferences, labelling comprehension, and in-store sustainability communication. The work package combines two rounds of consumer surveys (Serbia: n ≈ 400; Hungary: n ≈ 400) with qualitative store intercept interviews and co-creation workshops with retail partner staff. Outputs include a regional consumer segmentation report, a practitioner handbook for in-store green communication, and two peer-reviewed articles. The project involves three academic partners and four retail or industry partners across both countries.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Commerce, Hospitality and Tourism, Budapest Metropolitan University
Zeleni Korak d.o.o. (sustainable retail consultancy, Novi Sad)
Pannónia Kereskedelmi Zrt. (retail company, Pécs)

projects.title: CRM Adoption Fit in Industrial SMEs of the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project examined the conditions under which CRM system adoption leads to performance improvements versus resistance and disengagement among industrial SMEs located in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. Activities included a baseline survey in 140 firms (70 per country), three participatory workshops with sales managers, development of a CRM readiness diagnostic instrument, and a pilot deployment of a customised lightweight CRM configuration in four partner companies. The project produced a bilingual practitioner guide (Serbian/Hungarian) for CRM readiness assessment and delivered training modules used in continuing education programmes at both partner universities. Total project budget: approximately 380,000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica
Association of Small and Medium Enterprises of Csongrád-Csanád County, Hungary

projects.title: Adaptive Selling Competencies and Digital Sales Tools: Measurement and Training Framework for Industrial Markets
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project develops and validates a psychometric toolkit for measuring adaptive selling competencies that are relevant to digitally augmented sales environments, with a focus on industrial B2B firms in Serbia. The research programme includes scale development and validation across three industrial sectors, a longitudinal field experiment testing a competency-based training intervention in three partner companies, and the construction of an open-access benchmark database of adaptive selling scores linked to CRM usage metrics. The project employs PLS-SEM, multilevel modelling, and experimental design. A secondary objective is to produce training materials suitable for executive education programmes and to generate empirical guidance for sales force hiring criteria in industrial SMEs.
partners: Faculty of Organizational Sciences, University of Belgrade
Faculty of Economics, University of Niš
Industrija Metalnih Komponenti Novi Sad d.o.o. (fictional partner company)

projects.title: Congruence, Locality, and Brand Memory in Non-Broadcast Sports Sponsorship Across the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project compared sponsorship recall patterns at amateur sporting events in three Hungarian counties (Baranya, Csongrád-Csanád, Bács-Kiskun) and three Serbian districts (South Bačka, North Bačka, North Banat). Fieldwork covered 38 events across handball, volleyball, and futsal, collecting data from approximately 2,400 spectators. The main deliverables were a joint dataset of recall benchmarks, a congruence assessment guide for clubs and sponsors published in Serbian and Hungarian, and three peer-reviewed articles. The project also supported two student exchanges between Subotica and Pécs and funded attendance at two international conferences.
partners: Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs
Vojvodina Sports Development Institute, Novi Sad
Baranya County Sports Federation, Pécs

projects.title: Sponsorship Memory Decay and Congruence: A Multi-Wave Panel Study in Serbian Amateur Sport
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This provincial grant funded the longitudinal panel infrastructure used in the 2021 recall-decay study and a parallel qualitative strand interviewing club presidents about sponsor selection decisions. The project produced one journal article, two conference papers, and an internal report delivered to the Provincial Secretariat. Funding covered survey software licenses, field staff compensation, and travel to sporting venues across Vojvodina. The project also supported the master's thesis of one student who subsequently enrolled in the doctoral programme at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sport and Physical Education, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Digital Integration Barriers in Small and Medium Enterprises of the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project examines structural and behavioural barriers preventing SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region from integrating digital tools into core business processes. Partner teams in Subotica and Pécs are conducting parallel firm-level surveys and a series of workshops with enterprise owners. Bojana Rajić contributes to survey instrument design, data collection in Vojvodina, and the preparation of regional comparison reports. The project will produce an openly available benchmark dataset of digitisation indicators for approximately 300 SMEs across both regions, as well as a practitioner handbook with sector-specific recommendations. Final outputs are due in late 2025 and will be disseminated through partner chambers of commerce.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs
Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica
South-Transdanubian Enterprise Development Centre, Pécs

projects.title: Corporate Governance Mechanisms and Minority Investor Protection in Family-Controlled Firms of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project builds a longitudinal firm-level dataset covering approximately 600 family-controlled companies in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro for the years 2015–2024, sourced from national business registries, stock exchange disclosures, and hand-collected annual reports. The research team investigates how board structure, ownership concentration, and the presence of institutional minority shareholders interact to determine dividend policy, related-party transaction frequency, and the incidence of minority oppression litigation. Sabo is responsible for data collection and cleaning for the Serbian subsample and contributes to econometric modelling. The project is coordinated by the Faculty of Economics in Subotica.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of East Sarajevo
Institute for Economic Research, Podgorica

projects.title: Revenue Optimisation Under Asymmetric Demand Signals in Pannonian Tourism Accommodation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops and validates a revenue management decision-support toolkit tailored to independently owned accommodation businesses in the Pannonian region. Core activities include assembly of a multi-year daily rate and occupancy panel from partner hotels and rental properties, estimation of asymmetric demand models that distinguish high-side and low-side forecast errors, and design of rule-based pricing triggers suitable for operators without dedicated revenue management staff. Fieldwork involves structured interviews with 80 accommodation managers and a randomised advisory intervention with 22 willing participants. Deliverables include an open-access dataset, a calibrated forecasting module, and a practitioner handbook distributed through the Tourism Organisation of Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Tourism Organisation of Vojvodina
Institute for Economic Research, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Yield Management Benchmarking for Small Hotels in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project compared revenue management practices, technology adoption rates, and seasonal pricing outcomes in small hotels on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. Krstić led the work package responsible for data collection, benchmarking methodology, and training material development on the Serbian side. The project surveyed 160 hotels (80 per country), conducted 40 paired depth interviews, and ran three joint training workshops in Subotica and Szeged attended by 140 participants. A bilingual best-practice guide was produced and distributed to regional tourism associations. The project documented a 14-percentage-point gap in revenue management tool adoption between the two sides and proposed a shared regional pricing observatory.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
University of Szeged, Faculty of Economics and Business Administration
Regional Development Agency of South Great Plain
Business Incubator Subotica

projects.title: Informal Network Responses to Institutional Voids in Serbian and Romanian SME Markets
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: INFOVOID examined the conditions under which informal relational networks emerge, stabilise, and erode as substitutes for formal market intermediaries in Serbian and Romanian SME markets. The project combined large-sample survey work (460 firms across Serbia in two industries) with paired qualitative fieldwork in matched sites in Romania. Key outputs included a comparative dataset on intermediary use, a typology of informal void-filling mechanisms coded across six intermediary functions, and four peer-reviewed publications. The project supported two doctoral students and involved a research visit exchange with Babeș-Bolyai University. Results were presented at four international conferences and disseminated through a public policy brief submitted to the Serbian Chamber of Commerce.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca
Serbian Chamber of Commerce and Industry – Vojvodina Regional Chamber

projects.title: Cross-Border Market Integration and Informal Brokerage in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMARKET investigated how SMEs on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border conduct cross-border trade in the absence of well-functioning bilateral market intermediaries—trade finance providers, customs brokers, and standards-certification bodies. Bjelica led the work package on informal brokerage structures, overseeing fieldwork in Subotica, Senta, and Horgoš on the Serbian side. The work package documented 31 individual cross-border brokers active in agri-food, light manufacturing, and construction materials trade. Findings fed into a joint Hungarian–Serbian policy brief on reducing informal transaction costs in the border zone, presented to both national Chambers of Commerce. The project coordinated four partner institutions and included student mobility placements.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Szeged, Hungary
Subotica Development Agency
Csongrád-Csanád County Enterprise Development Centre, Hungary

projects.title: Knowledge Spillover Mechanisms in Cross-Border R&D Partnerships along the EU–Western Balkan Frontier
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Пројекат је истраживао механизме преноса знања у заједничким истраживачко-развојним пројектима дуж мађарско-српске границе. Тим са Економског факултета у Суботици руководио је радним пакетом посвећеним анализи апсорптивних капацитета у малим и средњим предузећима у обе регије. Прикупљени су подаци за 83 предузећа путем упитника и 40 дубинских интервјуа. Израђени су регионални профили иновационих капацитета за Војводину и Чоноград жупанију, а препоруке за политику достављене су надлежним регионалним развојним агенцијама у Суботици и Кечкемету. Укупан буџет пројекта износио је 480.000 евра.
partners: Факултет пословних наука, Универзитет у Печују, Мађарска
Регионална развојна агенција Бачка, Суботица, Србија
Привредна комора Чоноград жупаније, Мађарска

projects.title: Апсорптивни капацитети домаћих предузећа у иновационим партнерствима са страним улагачима: фактори, баријере и политика
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат финансиран у оквиру програма IDEAS Фонда за науку Републике Србије испитује детерминанте апсорптивних капацитета српских предузећа која послују у иновационим партнерствима са страним директним инвеститорима. Главни истраживачки тим базиран је на Економском факултету у Суботици и Институту економских наука у Београду. Тим покрива студије случаја у секторима ИКТ, аутомобилске индустрије и прехрамбене технологије, комбинујући панел-регресије на бази Orbis Europe базе података са квалитативном грађом из 60 предузећа. Золтан Пап одговоран је за анализу прекограничних спилловера и за упоредну анализу са налазима из Хрватске и Румуније. Пројекат има предвиђени трајни буџет од 180.000 евра.
partners: Институт економских наука, Београд, Србија
Факултет економије и туризма, Јурај Добрила Универзитет у Пули, Хрватска

projects.title: Retention Dynamics of Knowledge Workers in the Western Balkans: Psychological Contracts and Organisational Commitment in Technology-Intensive Firms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RETAIN-WB investigated the mechanisms through which psychological contract breach drives turnover among knowledge workers at technology firms in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The project conducted three coordinated surveys (total N ≈ 900) and twelve in-depth organisational case studies over three years. Key outputs include a validated measurement instrument for distributed contract agency in flat organisations, three peer-reviewed journal articles, and a policy brief addressed to the Serbian Chamber of Commerce on retention practices for ICT employers. The project also supported two PhD candidates and organised a regional workshop at the Faculty of Economics in Subotica attended by 47 HR practitioners and researchers from the Western Balkans region.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
School of Economics and Business, University of Sarajevo
Faculty of Economics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje

projects.title: Cross-Border Work Relationships and Organisational Attachment in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSWORK examined employment relationships and worker attachment in companies operating across the Hungary–Serbia border, with particular attention to software development and shared-service centre workers. The project conducted a matched-pair survey of 320 workers on each side of the border, two focus groups per country, and an employer workshop in Subotica and Szeged. The Faculty of Economics in Subotica led the work package on psychological contract content and breach perception, while Hungarian partners led the labour mobility mapping work package. Project deliverables included a comparative HR guideline document translated into Hungarian, Serbian, and English, and a joint conference session at the Annual Meeting of the Regional Science Association for Central Europe.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
University of Szeged, Institute of Business Studies
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina
Csongrád-Csanád County Economic Development Agency

projects.title: Regulatory Stakeholder Mapping Tools for SMEs in the Energy and Pharmaceutical Sectors of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REGMAP developed a practical toolkit—combining a validated survey instrument, a facilitated workshop protocol, and a lightweight software dashboard—that allows medium-sized firms in the energy and pharmaceutical sectors to construct and update stakeholder salience maps without external consultants. The project ran in three phases: instrument validation (year 1), toolkit development and piloting with twelve partner firms in Serbia (year 2), and dissemination through NTP Novi Sad and two sectoral industry associations (year 3). The toolkit was tested against independently assessed salience maps prepared by academic researchers and achieved acceptable convergent validity. Project outputs include two journal articles, one conference contribution, and a publicly available manual. Three NTP-resident firms participated in the piloting phase.
partners: NTP Novi Sad
Serbian Energy Chamber of Commerce (fictional)
Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Regulatory Convergence and Non-Market Strategy in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSREG examined how regulatory differences between Hungary and Serbia in the energy, agri-food, and financial services sectors affect firm-level non-market strategies in the border region. Lukács led the work package on stakeholder analysis methodology, coordinating research teams in Subotica and Pécs. The project produced a comparative regulatory audit covering 14 sub-sectors, a practitioner guide for cross-border non-market strategy, and a shared database of regulatory divergence indicators updated annually. Firm-level workshops were held in Subotica, Szeged, and Pécs. One key finding was that agri-food firms faced the largest regulatory distance and had the least-developed non-market strategy capabilities of the three sectors studied. The project ended on schedule with all deliverables completed.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Business and Economics
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina (fictional)
Szeged Regional Development Agency (fictional)

projects.title: Cross-Border Harmonisation of Sustainability Standards in Agri-food Supply Chains of the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGRISUST brought together four organisations from Hungary and Serbia to reduce the administrative burden on agri-food suppliers operating across the common border by developing harmonised sustainability documentation templates, delivering joint training for supplier compliance officers, and piloting a shared audit calendar mechanism. Ristić led the work package on supplier capacity building, overseeing the design and delivery of training modules, the collection of pre- and post-training compliance data, and the preparation of the project's final evaluation report. The project reached 87 supplier firms directly and produced a publicly available bilingual documentation toolkit adopted by the Hungarian Chamber of Agriculture.
partners: Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs
Hungarian Chamber of Agriculture, Southern Great Plain Region

projects.title: Governance Diffusion Mechanisms in Agri-food Supplier Networks of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SUPGOV is a three-year research project funded under the IDEAS programme of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. The project constructs the first longitudinal network dataset covering inter-firm governance relationships among agri-food suppliers in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, combining official trade registry data with primary survey waves in 2022 and 2024. The central research question is whether governance standard requirements propagate beyond the first tier of supply chains and under what structural conditions this propagation is strongest. The project team of five researchers applies exponential random graph models to the network data and mixed-methods case studies to three commodity chains: raspberries, sunflower oil, and dairy. A publicly accessible anonymised dataset will be deposited on the OpenAIRE repository upon project completion.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Agricultural Economics, Belgrade
Faculty of Economics, University of Sarajevo

projects.title: Reporting Quality and Earnings Management in SMEs of the Western Balkans: Institutional and Firm-Level Drivers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines what institutional and firm-level factors drive variation in financial reporting quality among SMEs across Serbia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. The research team constructs a harmonised panel dataset from national company registers and the AMADEUS database, spanning 2015 to 2023. Work packages cover accrual model calibration under regional accounting standards, enforcement intensity measurement using court and regulatory records, and a firm-level survey on owner-manager reporting incentives administered to 300 SMEs. The project produces methodological guidelines for adapting Jones-type models to thin-panel regional data and delivers policy recommendations to the Serbian Ministry of Finance on disclosure requirements for medium-sized entities.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina
Faculty of Economics, Saints Cyril and Methodius University of Skopje, North Macedonia

projects.title: Fiscal Transparency and Consolidated Reporting Standards in Serbian Local Self-Government
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project examined the fiscal transparency practices of 45 municipalities and cities in Vojvodina, focusing on the quality of annual financial reports submitted to the Treasury Administration and the degree to which they conform to the informational requirements of IPSAS. The research team collected and coded financial statements for four fiscal years, conducted structured interviews with 30 municipal accountants, and produced a fiscal transparency index specific to Vojvodina local governments. The project delivered a practical guide for municipal chief accountants on improving consolidation-ready reporting, distributed in collaboration with the Standing Conference of Towns and Municipalities of Serbia. Two journal articles and one conference paper were produced.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Standing Conference of Towns and Municipalities of Serbia
Institute for Public Finance, Novi Sad branch

projects.title: Structured Data Standards for Public Financial Reporting in EU Candidate Countries
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS)
projects.summary: This project investigates the technical and institutional conditions for adopting machine-readable structured formats — specifically XBRL and JSON-LD — in public sector financial reporting across Serbia, Montenegro, and Albania. The research team is developing a prototype structured reporting taxonomy aligned with IPSAS disclosure requirements and national chart-of-accounts codifications, conducting pilot submissions with volunteer municipalities, and measuring compliance verification efficiency gains. A secondary objective is to produce policy recommendations for the ministries of finance in all three countries and to engage with the IFAC IPSASB working group on digital financial reporting. The project involves partners from Montenegro and Albania and aims to contribute an open-source taxonomy tool for use by national treasuries.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Information Technology, University of Donja Gorica, Montenegro

Treasury Administration of the Republic of Serbia

projects.title: Audit Quality and Regulatory Effectiveness in Western Balkan Family Business Sectors
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project builds a longitudinal database of audit engagements, fees, and auditor characteristics for family-owned firms across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and North Macedonia, covering the period 2012–2023. The core objectives are to quantify how recent regulatory changes in audit oversight—including rotation requirements and NAS restrictions—have affected audit quality and fee structures specifically in family business contexts. The project employs panel econometric methods and, in a qualitative strand, semi-structured interviews with audit partners in each country. Deliverables include a publicly accessible anonymized dataset, three peer-reviewed articles, and a policy brief addressed to national audit oversight bodies. The Faculty of Economics in Subotica is the lead institution, with research partners in Sarajevo and Skopje.
partners: School of Economics and Business, University of Sarajevo
Faculty of Economics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University in Skopje

projects.title: Non-Financial Disclosure Quality Improvement in Serbian Capital Markets
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assessed the quality of non-financial disclosures produced under Serbia's transposition of the EU Non-Financial Reporting Directive. The research team collected and coded annual and non-financial statements from 60 public-interest entities over three reporting cycles (2019–2021), applied the validated 91-item scoring instrument, and conducted survey and interview research with preparers and auditors. The project produced a benchmarking report submitted to the Serbian Securities Commission and the Serbian Chamber of Auditors, three peer-reviewed journal articles, and an open dataset of coded reports. A policy brief recommending minimum-quality standards for non-financial statement content was presented at a roundtable co-organised with the Faculty of Economics in Subotica and the Serbian Chamber of Commerce.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Niš
Serbian Chamber of Auditors (observer)

projects.title: Cross-Border Comparability of Sustainability Reporting in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSREP is a bilateral research and capacity-building project comparing sustainability reporting practices among large companies in Vojvodina (Serbia) and the Southern Transdanubia region of Hungary. Radmila Gligorić leads the work package on disclosure quality measurement, coordinating content analysis of approximately 80 company reports per year. The project also includes a training component for accountants and sustainability officers, delivered jointly with the Hungarian partner university. A joint database of scored sustainability reports is being built as a public research infrastructure. The project produced one shared methodology guide in Serbian and Hungarian and is running two doctoral co-supervision arrangements.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Tax Compliance and Formalisation of Micro-Enterprises in Vojvodina and Southern Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project investigated the determinants of business formalisation and tax compliance among micro-enterprises on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. Activities included harmonised enterprise surveys in Vojvodina and Csongrád-Csanád County, construction of a shared microdata infrastructure, and joint training workshops for tax practitioners. Key outputs were a comparative compliance cost report, two peer-reviewed journal articles, and a policy brief submitted to the respective national tax authorities. Fehér led the Serbian research team, coordinated data collection, and was responsible for cross-country comparability of survey instruments and econometric methodology.
partners: Faculty of Finance and Accountancy, Budapest Business School
Vojvodina Development Agency
Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Csongrád-Csanád County

projects.title: Informality, Institutions, and Small Business Taxation in the Post-Transition Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS)
projects.summary: This project examines the institutional and behavioural drivers of informality among small and micro-enterprises in Serbia, with comparative case studies in North Macedonia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. The research combines large-scale enterprise surveys, administrative tax record analysis under data-sharing agreements with the Tax Administration of the Republic of Serbia, and qualitative fieldwork in three regional centres. Specific objectives include estimating compliance elasticities with respect to tax rate changes, constructing a regional informality index at the municipal level, and evaluating the impact of the 2021 digitalisation mandate for entrepreneur bookkeeping. Policy recommendations are being developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Serbia.
partners: Institute of Economic Sciences, Belgrade
Faculty of Economics, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Faculty of Economics, University of Sarajevo

projects.title: Morphodynamic Thresholds and Sediment Budgets in Flood-Pulsed Lowland Rivers of the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to quantify sediment budgets and identify morphological change thresholds in three lowland river reaches—Tisa, Sava, and Bosut—during flood events of varying magnitude and duration. Field campaigns combined repeat multibeam surveys, suspended sediment sampling, and acoustic bedload monitoring. A numerical model library calibrated for each reach was assembled and shared with the Vojvodina Water Management Authority. The project employed two research assistants and supported one PhD student. Outputs include the 2023 Catena paper on dune geometry under drought, the 2024 phosphorus partitioning study, and a technical report delivered to the provincial water authority on conveyance risk under managed flood scenarios.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Jaroslav Černi Water Institute, Belgrade
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia

projects.title: Floodplain Reconnection as a Nature-Based Measure for Sediment Management and Flood Attenuation in the Hungarian–Serbian Tisa Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project involving institutions from Hungary and Serbia that piloted and monitored two controlled floodplain inundation experiments—one near Padej (Serbia) and one near Martonvásár (Hungary)—to evaluate sediment trapping efficiency and downstream flood peak reduction. Bajić led the work package covering field instrumentation design and sediment budget assessment on the Serbian side. The project produced design guidelines for managed floodplain reconnection that were incorporated into draft revisions of Serbia's flood risk management plan. The Padej experiment results were published in the 2020 journal paper on floodplain reconnection.
partners: Environmental Engineering Faculty, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Vegetation resistance parameterisation for flood hazard assessment in Vojvodina lowland canals
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates how seasonal variation in aquatic and riparian vegetation affects flow resistance and flood inundation extent in the drainage canal network of Vojvodina. Field campaigns are conducted at six canal reaches during low- and high-growth seasons, measuring vegetation density, stem flexibility, and water surface profiles. Laboratory flume experiments replicate representative vegetation configurations and provide drag coefficient data for use in 2D shallow-water models. Nedić contributes to flume experiments and numerical model calibration. Results are intended to improve flood hazard maps used by the Provincial Water Directorate. The project team includes researchers from the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica and the Jaroslav Černi Water Institute.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Jaroslav Černi Water Institute, Belgrade

projects.title: Bank Filtration as a Sustainable Drinking Water Source in the Pannonian Alluvial Zone under Changing Hydrological Conditions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project assessed the capacity of existing and potential bank filtration sites along the Danube and Tisa rivers in the cross-border region to provide reliable drinking water as river flow regimes shift. Ivona Kovač led the work package on field characterisation of exchange fluxes, coordinating monitoring campaigns at four sites. Partners collected comparable data on the Hungarian side. Joint modelling scenarios examined how projected low-flow periods of increased duration would affect travel times and filtrate quality. Outputs included a technical guideline document for municipal water operators and a shared data repository accessible to both national water authorities.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Department of Water Sciences, University of Miskolc, Hungary

projects.title: Quantifying Contaminant Transport Pathways through Alluvial Aquifers Adjacent to the Regulated Danube
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ALLUVTRACK focuses on identifying the dominant transport pathways through which dissolved contaminants migrating from industrial sites on the Danube floodplain reach drinking water abstraction points. The project combines multi-tracer experiments using fluorescent dyes and stable water isotopes with reactive transport modelling in FEFLOW. Field campaigns are conducted at two contrasting sites: a heavily regulated embankment reach near Novi Sad and a semi-natural reach downstream. The project will produce calibrated reactive transport model configurations and probabilistic estimates of contaminant breakthrough times that can be used directly by water utility operators for risk assessment. One PhD student and two MSc students are supported by the project.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Water Resources Management, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Non-stationary Rainfall Design Standards for Urban Drainage Infrastructure in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: NORDRAIN brings together hydraulic engineers and hydrologists from two Serbian and two Hungarian institutions to revise urban drainage design guidelines for the Pannonian Plain, where trends in short-duration rainfall extremes have been documented but are not yet reflected in national technical regulations. The project collects sub-hourly rainfall data from an expanded monitoring network, performs regional frequency analysis under both stationary and non-stationary assumptions, and produces guidance documents for practitioners. Lidija Todić contributes to the Serbian data harmonisation task and to the SWMM-based case studies that underpin the revised design tables. Project outputs include a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) practitioner handbook and an open dataset of updated IDF curves.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Gravel-Bed Scour at Composite Pier Foundations: Laboratory Calibration and Field Monitoring Protocol
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the scarcity of validated scour data for composite bridge foundations (pile cap and shaft combination) in gravel-bed rivers within the Western Balkans and Pannonian region. Work package 1 conducts 120 physical model experiments at two flume scales, systematically varying pile cap geometry, embedment depth, and bed material gradation. Work package 2 develops a standardised field monitoring protocol using repeated multibeam bathymetric surveys at six instrumented bridge sites on Vojvodina rivers, with annual surveys timed after peak flood discharge. Work package 3 synthesises laboratory and field data to assess the adequacy of current Serbian bridge design standards for scour estimation at composite foundations. The project funds two doctoral students and one postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
University of Niš, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Architecture
Roads Directorate of Serbia – Novi Sad Regional Office

projects.title: Transboundary Inspection Framework for Flood-Exposed Road Bridges on Tisa Tributaries
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TIBRIDGE developed harmonised inspection and risk-classification procedures for road bridges crossing gravel-bed tributaries of the Tisa River on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. Tóth led the work package responsible for laboratory validation of simplified scour screening tools that field inspectors can apply without numerical modelling. The work package delivered a set of look-up charts relating normalised scour depth to pier geometry and discharge class for seven representative bridge configurations identified in the inventory. A joint training exercise was held at the Subotica flume laboratory, attended by bridge engineers from both national road authorities. The project produced a bilingual inspection manual adopted by both partner road agencies.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
University of Pécs, Department of Environmental Engineering, Hungary

projects.title: Creep Model Calibration from Non-Invasive Monitoring of In-Service Prestressed Concrete Bridges in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CREMONIT brought together the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica and the Budapest University of Technology to establish a joint dataset of long-term bridge monitoring records spanning both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border. Seven instrumented bridges contributed creep, shrinkage, and deflection data. The project calibrated the EC2 and fib MC2010 creep models specifically for the climatic and concrete production conditions of the Pannonian basin, where continental humidity and local aggregate sources differ from the conditions underlying standard model coefficients. Outputs included a shared database, a calibrated regional creep coefficient correction table, and a bilingual technical guide for bridge owners.
partners: Budapest University of Technology, Department of Structural Engineering
Vojvodina Roads Directorate, Novi Sad
National Motorway Non-profit Ltd, Budapest

projects.title: Time-Dependent Behaviour of Concrete Slabs with Supplementary Cementitious Materials Under Sustained and Variable Loading
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: TIMESLAB investigated creep and shrinkage of concrete containing locally sourced fly ash from the Kolubara power plant and GGBS from a Serbian steelworks, under both constant and step-variable sustained loads representative of actual bridge loading histories. Forty-eight prism specimens and six full-scale slab strips were cast and monitored in the Subotica laboratory over two years. The project produced revised age-at-loading correction factors for fly ash concrete and documented the reduction in long-term creep achievable with GGBS at moderate replacement rates. Results were disseminated to bridge design offices in Novi Sad and Belgrade.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade

projects.title: Fatigue Life Management of Aging Transmission Tower Networks in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FATNET addressed the shared challenge of aging 110 kV and 220 kV steel lattice transmission towers in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border region. The project combined field monitoring, laboratory fatigue testing, and probabilistic life assessment methods to produce a decision-support tool for maintenance prioritisation. The Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica led the project and contributed structural modelling and fracture mechanics expertise. The Hungarian partner provided wind climatological data and finite-element model validation. JP Elektrovojvodina supplied access to operational towers, inspection records spanning up to 30 years, and decommissioned test specimens. The main output was a web-based assessment platform that ingests inspection data and wind monitoring records to generate updated remaining-life estimates and maintenance priority rankings for tower portfolios.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary

MAVIR Hungarian Transmission System Operator, Budapest

projects.title: Stochastic Wind Load Modelling for Service Life Assessment of Steel Lattice Structures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: WINDLIFE focuses on improving the accuracy of stochastic wind load models used in fatigue life calculations for steel lattice structures, including transmission towers and meteorological masts. The project collects full-scale wind pressure and structural response data from two instrumented towers using a network of MEMS accelerometers and cup anemometers. Recorded data are used to validate and calibrate Monte Carlo and frequency-domain load simulation procedures that are currently based on wind tunnel or standardised empirical parameters. A secondary objective is to quantify how non-stationarity in thunderstorm and bora wind events affects fatigue damage accumulation relative to stationary Gaussian wind models. The project is carried out at the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica with contributions from the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia for wind climatological data provision.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia

projects.title: Soil–Structure Interaction Effects on the Seismic Fragility of Shallow-Founded Buildings in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Пројекат PANSSIF бавио се квантификацијом ефеката интеракције тла и конструкције на сеизмичку крхкост армиранобетонских зграда плиткозасноваих у Панонском басену. Партнери са универзитета у Суботици и Пећу заједнички су спровели теренска мерења на 23 зграде, нумеричке студије са преко 500 модела и припремили заједнички препоруке за примену у регионалним прорачунима хазарда. Резултати су подељени са локалним инспекцијским службама у оба пограничне региона. Буџет суботичке институције износио је 118.000 EUR.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Мађарска
Институт за испитивање материјала Србије, Београд

projects.title: Субгрундни модели за сеизмичку процену постојећих зграда у Србији
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат SUBSEIS финансира Фонд за науку Републике Србије кроз програм IDEAS. Циљ је развој и верификација нелинеарних модела подлоге примерених профилима тла карактеристичним за урбане средине северне Србије, на основу теренских и лабораторијских испитивања у осам општина. Укупни буџет пројекта износи 3,2 милиона динара.

Рударско-геолошки факултет, Универзитет у Београду

projects.title: Field-Compatible Assessment Methods for Punching Shear Capacity of Existing Reinforced Concrete Flat Slabs
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FLATCHECK addresses the absence of validated, field-applicable procedures for evaluating punching shear in existing flat-slab structures whose original documentation is incomplete or missing. The project combines minimally destructive core sampling, GPR surveying, and probabilistic capacity models derived from the critical shear crack theory. Laboratory campaigns involve testing of slab segments prepared from cores extracted at known positions, allowing direct comparison of in-situ and laboratory-derived material properties. The project also compiles a regional database of building-stock flat slabs constructed in Vojvodina between 1965 and 1990, covering structural typology, typical reinforcement layouts, and measured concrete quality. Outputs include a practitioner-oriented assessment guideline submitted for adoption by the Serbian Chamber of Engineers.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Shear-Enhancement and Reliability of Post-Installed Anchors in Reinforced Concrete Flat Slabs
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SHERPA-SLAB is a cross-border research and knowledge-transfer project examining the use of post-installed mechanical and adhesive anchors as punching shear reinforcement in flat slabs existing in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project involves parallel experimental programmes at partner institutions, testing installation procedures under realistic site conditions including partially carbonated concrete and congested reinforcement zones. The Serbian team, led by Vladana Pavlović, is responsible for the experimental campaign at the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica laboratory, covering anchor bond characterisation and full-slab punching tests. Shared test data are used to calibrate a unified reliability-based design approach acceptable under both Hungarian and Serbian national annexes to Eurocode 2. The project also includes short-term staff exchanges and a joint master's-level course on structural assessment.

projects.title: Thermal Bridge Characterisation and Renovation Prioritisation for Prefabricated Housing in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project compiled the first systematic database of thermal bridge geometries and ψ-values for prefabricated panel systems used in Vojvodina, drawing on archival construction drawings held at three municipal planning archives and thermographic field surveys of 31 buildings. Two-dimensional finite-element simulations were conducted for 38 junction types in as-built and four retrofit configurations. The resulting catalogue was formatted for direct use in Serbian energy certification software and distributed to licensed energy auditors in the province through a workshop series attended by 47 practitioners. The project also produced a draft technical recommendation submitted to the Serbian Chamber of Engineers.
partners: Urban Planning Institute of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials IMS, Belgrade

projects.title: Data-Driven Renovation Planning for Post-Socialist Prefabricated Housing Neighbourhoods
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANRENO brings together two Serbian and two Hungarian partner institutions to develop a GIS-integrated decision-support tool for neighbourhood-scale renovation planning of prefabricated panel housing. The Subotica team leads the work package on building diagnostics, responsible for drone-assisted thermographic surveying of 22 buildings in Sombor and 18 in Pécs, georeferenced defect mapping, and integration of thermal bridge data into the shared GIS platform. The tool is intended for use by municipal housing companies and energy agencies. A joint dataset of surveyed buildings is being compiled to allow cross-border comparison of defect patterns and renovation cost-benefit outcomes.

projects.title: Reliability-Based Serviceability Assessment of Lightweight Composite Floors in the Built Environment of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project developed probabilistic models for vibration serviceability assessment of cold-formed steel composite floor systems prevalent in the residential and office building stock of Vojvodina. Activities included an in-situ measurement campaign across 30 buildings, statistical characterisation of load and resistance variables, Monte Carlo reliability analyses, and calibration of serviceability reliability indices against occupant survey data. The project produced an open dataset of measured floor frequencies and damping ratios, a set of calibrated Bayesian prior distributions for use in reliability updating, and a technical report with recommendations submitted to the Institute for Standardisation of Serbia for consideration in the Serbian National Annex to EN 1990.

projects.title: Composite Floor Vibration Standards Harmonisation across the Hungary–Serbia Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed the inconsistent application of vibration serviceability criteria for composite floors in construction practice on both sides of the Serbia–Hungary border, where identical building systems are subject to different national standard interpretations. The project carried out joint measurement campaigns on comparable building typologies in Subotica, Senta, Szabadka, and Baja, produced a harmonised measurement protocol, and delivered a bilingual technical guidance document. The Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica led the work package on structural reliability modelling and was responsible for producing comparative reliability analyses using both Hungarian and Serbian National Annex parameters.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Floodplain Liquefaction Risk Assessment for Infrastructure in the Pannonian Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project addressed liquefaction risk to linear infrastructure (roads, railway embankments, pipelines) in the Hungarian–Serbian cross-border floodplain zone. Work included compilation of a joint CPT and borehole database, harmonisation of cyclic laboratory testing protocols between the two partner institutions, and production of cross-border liquefaction susceptibility maps in GIS format. Field reconnaissance after minor seismic events (Mw 4.3–4.8) was used to validate map predictions against observed ground behaviour. Final deliverables included a bilingual technical manual for infrastructure designers and a set of GIS layers deposited with provincial planning authorities on both sides of the border.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Széchenyi István University, Department of Structural and Geotechnical Engineering, Győr

projects.title: Seismic Cyclic Softening and Post-Earthquake Settlement of Fine-Grained Soils in Low-Seismicity Lowland Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop a physically based framework for estimating post-earthquake settlement caused by cyclic softening of fine-grained soils in the Pannonian lowland, where seismic hazard is moderate but the prevalence of soft Holocene silts and clays creates significant vulnerability. Research activities included systematic cyclic simple shear and cyclic triaxial testing of specimens from eight sites in Vojvodina, development of an empirical post-cyclic volumetric strain model, and integration of model outputs into a 1D ground response and settlement calculation procedure. The project produced an open-access dataset of 180 test records and a freely downloadable spreadsheet tool for post-earthquake settlement estimation.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Geotechnics and Foundations, Belgrade
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Long-Term Behaviour of Infrastructure Embankments on Soft Organic Ground in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project established a transboundary network of field monitoring stations at six embankment sites in northern Serbia and southern Hungary, all founded on soft organic soils. Each station was equipped with settlement plates, piezometers, and surface-level GPS benchmarks. Data were collected at monthly intervals over three years and integrated into a shared database. Laboratory testing programmes at partner institutions used harmonised procedures to allow direct comparison of consolidation parameters. The project produced a joint design guidance document for embankments on soft organic ground, which was submitted to road authorities in both countries. Three joint workshops with practitioners were held in Subotica, Novi Sad, and Pécs.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Geotechnics, Győr, Hungary
Public Enterprise Roads of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Hungarian Public Road Non-profit Ltd., Budapest

projects.title: Mechanisms of Long-Term Creep in Organic Soils of the Vojvodina Lowland and Their Relevance to Infrastructure Serviceability
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated the microscale mechanisms responsible for long-term creep in organic clays and peats from Vojvodina through a combination of advanced laboratory testing and microstructural analysis. Testing included CRS and stepped-load oedometer tests, triaxial creep tests, mercury intrusion porosimetry, and X-ray diffraction. A series of numerical isotache model calibrations were performed and validated against three monitored embankment sites. Special attention was given to the effect of seasonal groundwater variation on creep rate, motivated by observed discrepancies between predicted and measured long-term settlements in drainage-affected agricultural land. Results from the project contributed to four journal publications and one book chapter, and supported two doctoral dissertations in progress.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mining and Geology, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Landslide Risk Assessment and Early Warning for Loess Bluffs Along the Danube–Tisa Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop a cross-border landslide risk assessment framework for loess bluffs along the Danube and Tisa rivers in the Hungarian–Serbian border zone. The University of Novi Sad team was responsible for the geotechnical characterisation work package, which covered site investigation at six instrumented profiles, laboratory testing of approximately 200 samples, and development of coupled seepage–stability models calibrated to field piezometer records. A prototype early-warning threshold system based on rainfall and river stage triggers was tested against the three-year monitoring dataset. The project produced a joint risk map at 1:25000 scale and a technical guideline document for local water management authorities. Partners contributed complementary remote sensing and hydraulic modelling components.
partners: Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Department of Geotechnics, Hungary
Vojvodina Water Management Enterprise, Novi Sad, Serbia
