projects.title: Collapsibility and Unsaturated Behaviour of Pannonian Loess under Dynamic and Quasi-Static Loading
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigates the collapse behaviour of loess from the Vojvodina region when subjected to wetting under both static and cyclic loading conditions, relevant to slope stability during rapid flood events and agricultural irrigation. The experimental programme includes oedometer collapse tests, triaxial tests with suction control using the axis translation technique, and large-scale column wetting experiments. Numerical implementation of a collapsible constitutive model in FLAC is validated against the laboratory data and applied to representative Danube and Tisa bluff cross-sections. The project funds one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher at the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica. Results are being published in open-access journals and all experimental datasets will be archived in the University of Novi Sad repository.
partners: Department of Geotechnics, Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Materials Testing, Novi Sad

projects.title: Foundation Behaviour on Collapsible Loess Soils in the Vojvodina Region: Field and Laboratory Characterisation
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates the geotechnical behaviour of loess deposits across the Vojvodina plain with respect to their suitability for shallow foundation construction. Activities include a systematic borehole campaign at five representative sites, laboratory testing of undisturbed samples, and a series of instrumented plate load tests under natural and inundated conditions. The aim is to produce regional correlations between index properties and collapse susceptibility, and to propose practical adjustment procedures for bearing capacity and settlement calculations applicable to standard engineering practice in the region. Starčević is responsible for laboratory oedometer testing and field test data processing.
partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Development of Water Resources Jaroslav Černi, Belgrade
Municipality of Vrbas, Serbia

projects.title: Peripheral and Central Contributors to Neuromuscular Fatigue in Team Sport Repeated-Sprint Exercise
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates the relative contributions of peripheral and central fatigue during repeated-sprint exercise in handball and football players. The study uses tensiomyography, twitch interpolation, and isokinetic dynamometry to track muscle contractile properties and voluntary activation across sprint protocols of varying intensity and recovery duration. A secondary aim is to establish sex-specific fatigue profiles. Participants are recruited from university sports clubs in Novi Sad. Data collection is ongoing and will feed into Ana Tošić's doctoral dissertation. The project is led by Associate Professor Dragan Ilić and involves two additional researchers from the faculty. Findings are intended to inform sport-specific conditioning and return-to-play protocols.
partners: Faculty of Sport and Physical Education, University of Novi Sad
RK Vojvodina Handball Club, Novi Sad

projects.title: Psychophysiological Stress Monitoring and Coping Support in Competitive Youth Sport
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project examines the feasibility of integrating routine psychophysiological monitoring—specifically salivary cortisol sampling and resting HRV assessment—into the training and competition schedules of youth sport clubs in the Vojvodina region. Working with four clubs across three sports (swimming, handball, athletics), the project collects longitudinal data over a full competitive season and evaluates whether feedback provided to coaches and athletes influences coping strategy use and perceived stress load. Tóth contributes to data collection protocol design, athlete testing sessions, and data analysis related to cortisol and HRV measures. The project is coordinated by Associate Professor Dragana Milošević at the Faculty of Sport and Physical Education, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Sport and Physical Education, University of Novi Sad
Vojvodina Youth Sport Federation
Sports Club Proleter Novi Sad

projects.title: Hydrodynamic and Coordinative Efficiency in Aging Swimmers: A Multi-Site Cross-Sectional Study
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates how passive drag and inter-limb coordination jointly decline across the adult lifespan in regular masters swimmers from Serbia, Hungary, and Romania. Data are collected at three aquatic facilities using the same standardised tow-line protocol and underwater camera system to ensure cross-site comparability. The project includes 120 participants across five age decades. Mirjana Marković is responsible for data collection and processing at the Novi Sad site, underwater video coding, and contribution to joint publications. Results are expected to inform age-adapted coaching guidelines and flag hydrodynamic screening thresholds for masters swim clubs.
partners: Faculty of Physical Education and Sport Sciences, University of Pécs, Hungary
Faculty of Physical Education and Sport, West University of Timișoara, Romania
Plivački Klub Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Participation Pathways and Attrition in Youth Team Sports: A Longitudinal Study Across Post-Transitional Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PATHWAY-YS is a four-year longitudinal project tracking participation trajectories and dropout risk factors in youth team-sport athletes aged 10–16 in Serbia. The project follows two cohorts across football, handball, and basketball clubs in Vojvodina and Central Serbia, collecting annual data on physical fitness, psychosocial indicators, coaching environment quality, and participation status. A secondary strand audits national federation development policies and compares them with systems in Hungary, Slovakia, and Croatia through a structured document review. The main outputs are validated monitoring tools for clubs, evidence-based policy recommendations for federation licensing, and open-access datasets deposited in the University of Novi Sad repository.

projects.title: Cross-Border Youth Sport Participation and Talent Development: Comparing Institutional Frameworks in Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSS-SPORT compared youth sport participation rates, club governance structures, and talent development practices in border-region municipalities of Serbia (South Bačka District) and Hungary (Csongrád-Csanád County). Milana Kovačević led Work Package 3, responsible for athlete development environment assessment and dropout rate mapping. The project produced a joint Serbian–Hungarian youth sport participation database, a shared coach professional development curriculum piloted in 12 clubs on both sides of the border, and a policy brief submitted to both national sport ministries. Two bilateral summer academies for youth coaches were organised as dissemination activities.

projects.title: Postural Control Monitoring and Training Optimisation in Visually Impaired Goalball Athletes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project built a longitudinal database of force-plate and IMU-derived balance variables in 60 visually impaired goalball athletes across three national clubs. A standardised perturbation battery was administered at four time points, producing normative reference intervals stratified by classification group. Parallel work validated the IMU against force-plate gold standard (resulting in a 2021 publication). A tablet-based feedback application was developed in collaboration with two goalball coaches to display individualised sway metrics after each monitoring session, and its usability was evaluated in a short pilot with junior athletes. Final-year data analysis focused on nonlinear entropy metrics and trunk EMG responses.

projects.title: Grip Asymmetry and Its Influence on Kinetic Chain Efficiency in Olympic Weightlifting
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates whether and to what degree bilateral grip force asymmetry alters joint moment distribution and barbell trajectory in competitive Olympic-style weightlifters. The study combines multi-segment rigid-body modelling, dual force platform measurements, and motion capture in a longitudinal design involving 40 competitive lifters from clubs in Vojvodina and central Serbia. A secondary aim is to develop and validate a portable instrumented collar for field monitoring of lateral loading. Training intervention protocols targeting grip symmetry will be tested in a randomised controlled trial with junior lifters. Results are intended to inform both coaching practice and sports equipment design.
partners: Serbian Weightlifting Federation
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Sedentary Behaviour Patterns and Cardiometabolic Health in Serbian Office Employees: An Accelerometry-Based Cohort Pilot
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This pilot project recruits 200 desk-based employees across three organisations in Vojvodina to characterise weekday and weekend sedentary behaviour accumulation patterns using triaxial accelerometry and to link these patterns to a panel of cardiometabolic biomarkers measured at baseline and at 12-month follow-up. The project will also test the psychometric properties of a Serbian-language self-report sedentary behaviour questionnaire validated against the accelerometry reference. Danijela Tešić is responsible for participant recruitment, accelerometer data processing, and statistical modelling components. Results will inform occupational health guidelines applicable to the regional public administration sector.
partners: Faculty of Sport and Physical Education, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina
City Administration of Novi Sad – Human Resources Directorate

projects.title: Sweat Electrolyte Mapping and Personalised Hydration Strategies for Endurance Events in Continental Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SWEATMAP is a three-year project building a longitudinal database of sweat sodium and chloride profiles for recreational ultra-trail runners in Vojvodina and the Southern Banat region. The project recruits approximately 120 runners per year across four participating races, collecting Macroduct patch samples, pre- and post-race blood samples, environmental logs, and dietary recall data. A key output is a regional reference range for sweat sodium concentration under continental humid summer conditions, which does not currently exist for this population. The project also tests whether a two-session laboratory sweat profiling protocol can reliably predict field sodium loss, enabling coaches and athletes to receive individualised supplementation recommendations without requiring race-day measurement.
partners: Faculty of Sport and Physical Education, University of Novi Sad
General Hospital Zrenjanin
Ultra Trail Serbia Race Organisation

projects.title: Thermoregulatory Monitoring in Mountain Ultra-Running: Wearable Sensor Integration and Validation
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: THERMORUN was a 24-month applied research grant examining whether commercially available wearable biosensors provide sufficiently accurate real-time data on sweat electrolyte status and skin temperature during ultra-trail racing. The Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad contributed embedded systems expertise to develop a field data-logging harness compatible with existing sensors. The project delivered a calibration protocol that reduced mean absolute error in sweat [Na⁺] estimation from 13.7 to 7.4 mmol·L⁻¹ under field conditions when a personalised offset correction was applied. Results were shared with race medical teams and contributed directly to the wearable sensor validation paper published in 2025.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Fruška Gora Trail Running Association

projects.title: Procedural Soundscape Authoring Tools for Participatory Heritage Interpretation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SONOPATH developed a suite of open-source authoring tools enabling museum curators and heritage professionals without specialist audio programming skills to create procedurally generated soundscapes for permanent and temporary exhibitions. The project combined perceptual research into visitor attention and spatial audio with software development work producing a node-based authoring environment and a lightweight runtime engine tested in three partner institutions in Vojvodina. A community sound recording methodology was also piloted to build locally sourced audio asset libraries. The project delivered two peer-reviewed publications, the open-source tool suite, and trained over 30 heritage professionals through workshops held in Novi Sad and Subotica.
partners: Museum of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
City Museum Subotica
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Adaptive Score Systems for Interactive Documentary: Cross-Sector Methodologies
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: ADAPTSCORE was a cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian partner institutions focused on developing shared methodologies for composing and implementing adaptive musical scores in interactive documentary productions. Stojanović led the work package on audio engine architecture and integration with web-based documentary platforms. The project produced three interactive documentary prototypes, a joint authoring workflow specification, and a shared toolkit for WebAudio API-based adaptive scoring. Training exchanges were conducted for early-career researchers and documentary filmmakers at partner sites in Novi Sad and Pécs. The project also included a public screening series presenting the prototypes to audiences in both countries.
partners: Faculty of Arts, University of Pécs
Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad
Documentary Film Centre Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Preservation and Digital Access to the Vojvodina Moving Image Heritage, 1945–1975
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project surveyed, assessed, and digitised a corpus of approximately 120 film reels held at municipal and institutional archives across Vojvodina, representing newsreel, documentary, and short fiction production from the first three decades of Yugoslav cinema in the region. Activities included condition assessment using A-D strip testing and shrinkage measurement, wet-gate scanning at 2K and 4K resolution depending on material condition, and development of a publicly accessible catalogue compatible with FIAF metadata standards. The project also produced a training module for archive staff on basic condition monitoring. Two restoration technicians were employed on fixed-term contracts, and the department's scanning laboratory was upgraded with a new densitometer unit funded through the project budget.

projects.title: Transnational Approaches to Socialist-Era Film Preservation in the Adriatic–Danubian Region
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: A consortium project involving eight institutions from Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Hungary, and Austria, focused on establishing shared protocols for the preservation and digital access of socialist-era moving image materials. Babić led Work Package 3, which addressed photochemical and hybrid digitisation workflows, coordinating practice-sharing visits between laboratory facilities, conducting a comparative equipment audit across partner institutions, and co-authoring the workflow guidance document distributed to all partners. The project also produced a freely downloadable condition-assessment toolkit for small archives lacking dedicated conservation staff. Total project budget was approximately €1.9 million; the Novi Sad team managed a sub-grant of approximately €180,000 covering personnel, consumables, and equipment.

projects.title: Wearable Biosensor Systems for Participatory and Collaborative Live Performance in Southeast Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and tested an integrated wearable biosensor toolkit—combining sEMG, IMU, HRV, and EDA modalities—for deployment in collaborative live performance contexts involving multiple performers. Working with three performance groups based in Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Niš, the project produced four publicly performed works, an open-source hardware design for a custom multi-channel biosensor garment, and a software library for routing physiological data to TouchDesigner and Unity environments. The project also ran three practitioner workshops attended by 38 performance makers and digital artists from Serbia and neighbouring countries. A methodological guide for artists working with biosensors was produced in Serbian and English and distributed freely through partner institutions.

projects.title: Script Visibility and Community Literacy in Multilingual Vojvodina: Towards Evidence-Based Public Typography Standards
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SCRIBO investigated how script choice and typographic quality in publicly posted materials affect reading behaviour and subjective inclusion among residents of multilingual municipalities in Vojvodina. The project combined fieldwork in twelve municipalities—producing a corpus of over 2,000 photographed public documents—with controlled legibility experiments and community focus groups in Hungarian, Serbian, Slovak, and Romani. Deliverables included a publicly accessible annotated image database, a set of evidence-based typographic guidelines for public administration print materials, and a short professional development workshop delivered to staff at three municipal administrations. A final report was submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for consideration in revising provincial communication standards.
partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina
Centre for Minority Studies, Subotica
Faculty of Arts, University of Pécs

projects.title: Print Heritage Pathways: Conservation and Digital Access for Typographic Artefacts in Small Vojvodina Cultural Institutions
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: PRINTPATH aimed to establish lightweight digitisation and metadata protocols suited to small municipal museums and cultural centres in Vojvodina that hold printing-related collections—type cases, specimen books, and composing equipment—without dedicated conservation staff. Nedeljković led the work package responsible for developing the typographic object cataloguing standard, drawing on the letterpress survey fieldwork she had conducted previously. The project produced a freely downloadable cataloguing toolkit and trained staff at four institutions in its use. A joint online catalogue aggregating holdings from all four partner institutions was launched in 2021 and is maintained by the Matica srpska library.
partners: Matica srpska Library, Novi Sad
Museum of Vojvodina

Cultural Centre Sombor

projects.title: Mapping Net.Art Practices and Institutional Critique in Central and Eastern Europe: A Comparative Digital Archive
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: NETMAP-CEE built the first systematic digital archive and relational database of net.art and tactical media works produced in Central and Eastern Europe between 1993 and 2012. The project team, based at the Academy of Arts Novi Sad with partners in Timișoara and Prague, digitised and described 634 works in a shared metadata schema, conducted oral history interviews with forty-one practitioners, and developed a public annotation interface for researcher and community use. The project also produced two peer-reviewed articles, a doctoral dissertation supervised by Milošević, and a methodological handbook for net.art archivists distributed to twelve regional institutions. All database records are publicly accessible under a Creative Commons licence.
partners: Faculty of Arts and Design, West University of Timișoara
Academy of Arts, Architecture and Design, Prague

projects.title: Cross-Border Tactical Media Practices and Solidarity Networks in the Serbia–Hungary Borderland
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BORDERSTREAM examined and supported cross-border art activist collaborations between practitioners in the Vojvodina region of Serbia and southern Hungary, with a focus on tactical media responses to border enforcement and population movement. Activities included academic research (interviews, archival analysis), three public symposia co-organised with partner institutions, a joint artist residency programme hosting eight artists, and a co-produced online exhibition of new works by participating artists. The project produced a bilingual research report, a peer-reviewed article, and an open-access toolkit of tactical media methods for use by civil society organisations in border regions. Milošević coordinated the project and led research design.
partners: Faculty of Arts, University of Pécs
Cultural Centre Subotica
Civic Media Institute, Szeged

projects.title: Perceptual Metrics for Timbral Texture Quality in Spatial Audio Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: TEXTURA investigates whether psychoacoustically grounded metrics—specifically composite roughness index and spectral fusion probability—can serve as reliable predictors of perceived quality in spatial electroacoustic audio. The project combines controlled listening experiments with signal-processing model development. In the first phase, a corpus of 300 purpose-built multi-layer stimuli covering granular, wavetable, and FM synthesis was assembled. Listening experiments are conducted in the department's anechoic chamber and over a 16-channel array. In the second phase, the validated metrics are used to build a real-time analysis plug-in prototype tested by professional sound designers. Partner institutions contribute expertise in acoustic measurement and music cognition. Project outputs include three journal papers, a publicly available dataset, and an open-source Python library.

projects.title: Sound Architecture: Psychoacoustic Foundations for Immersive Installation Design
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: SONARC was a two-year provincial project that examined how psychoacoustic parameters—primarily masking, roughness, and spatial diffusion—affect listener experience in immersive sound-art installations. Rita Kiss led the perceptual measurement work package, coordinating experiments conducted in temporary installation environments at two Vojvodina art venues. The work package delivered empirical data on how architectural reverberation modifies perceived roughness and density in multi-speaker setups, data which directly fed into the TEXTURA project. The project also produced educational materials used in undergraduate sound-design courses at the Academy of Arts. Total duration was 24 months with funding from the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research of Vojvodina.
partners: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad
Cultural Centre Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Distributed Archive of Vanishing Soundscapes of the Pannonian Plain: Documentation, Preservation, and Public Access

projects.summary: PANNOSOUND brought together researchers from three Serbian institutions to build a publicly accessible, geographically indexed archive of environmental audio collected across Vojvodina over the preceding fifteen years. The project digitised approximately 600 hours of legacy analogue and early digital recordings held in fragmented institutional and private collections, applying the metadata schema developed in earlier work by the team. New fieldwork was conducted at 28 sites identified as acoustically significant through a nomination process involving local cultural institutions. The archive was published as an open-access repository with full metadata and embedded map interface, and a methodology guide for future deposit contributions was produced. An associated educational module was developed and piloted in secondary schools in Novi Sad and Sombor.

projects.title: Cross-Border Soundscape Heritage of the Bačka–Baranya Region: Joint Documentation and Archival Practice
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSSOUND was a bilateral documentation initiative connecting acoustic ecology researchers in Vojvodina with colleagues at two Hungarian institutions to produce a shared soundscape archive covering the borderland region spanning both sides of the Bačka–Baranya administrative boundary. Žarković led the work package responsible for field methodology harmonisation, ensuring that recording protocols, metadata standards, and archival formats used on the Serbian side were compatible with those of the Hungarian partner. The project produced 340 hours of new recordings, a bilingual metadata template, and a joint online exhibition hosted on servers at both institutions. The project also organised two joint summer fieldwork schools for students from both countries.

projects.title: Sonic Archives of Socialist Yugoslavia: Cataloguing and Contextualising Analogue Recording Materials in Serbian Public Institutions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SONOARCH aims to produce the first systematic catalogue of surviving analogue recording materials—magnetic tape reels, session documentation, and equipment records—held at public broadcasting and cultural institutions in Serbia. The project team visits seven institutional archives, assesses physical condition of tape holdings, digitises selected materials at high resolution, and creates a structured metadata database accessible to researchers. Beyond cataloguing, the project develops a degradation-risk scoring instrument for reel-to-reel tape in institutional storage and produces practical guidelines for archivists working without specialist audio conservation expertise. A final edited volume presenting case studies from each archive is planned for publication in the project's final year. Partners include the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad, the Faculty of Music in Belgrade, and the Serbian Broadcasting Archive.

projects.title: Small-Room Acoustic Reference Correction: Measurement Protocols and Filter Optimisation Methods for Educational Recording Facilities
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project addressed the lack of standardised measurement and correction procedures for teaching studios at Serbian higher education institutions. Partner rooms at four academies and faculties in Vojvodina and Central Serbia were mapped using a common measurement protocol. A software tool implementing the gradient-descent parametric optimisation method was developed and applied in each room. The project produced the first regionally consistent dataset of small-room transfer functions, trained twelve junior researchers and graduate students in acoustic measurement practice, and delivered written correction guidelines distributed to participating institutions. Results fed directly into the larger database paper published in 2016.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Music Arts, University of Arts in Belgrade
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš

projects.title: Dual-Source Subwoofer Arrays for Pre-Equalisation Modal Control in Asymmetric Monitoring Environments
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: A bilateral research collaboration between the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad and the Department of Acoustics at Budapest University of Technology and Economics. The project investigated the theoretical and practical conditions under which a two-subwoofer system can replace or complement electronic modal equalisation in asymmetric control rooms. Work packages covered analytical modelling, finite-difference time-domain simulation, and experimental validation in test rooms at both partner institutions. The collaboration produced two journal papers and a shared measurement dataset. Exchange visits involved four researchers from each institution over the two-year period.
