projects.title: Verification and Runtime Assurance for Safety-Critical Real-Time Embedded Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated formal verification workflows for real-time embedded software in safety-relevant domains, specifically targeting the gap between offline model checking and runtime assurance. Research activities covered parametric timed automata synthesis, observer-based runtime monitoring, and compositional verification of hierarchical controllers. A toolchain connecting UPPAAL with ARM Cortex-M firmware was developed and released as open-source software. The project involved collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and School of Computing in Belgrade. Two master's theses and one doctoral dissertation were partially supported by the project. Results were disseminated in three journal papers and four conference contributions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
School of Computing, Union University, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Automotive Software Verification Competence Network
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project between Serbian and Hungarian academic institutions aimed at building shared competence in formal verification methods for automotive embedded software. The Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' leads the work package on tool integration, responsible for mapping AUTOSAR timing constraints to formal verification queries and developing training materials for engineers at partner companies. The University of Szeged leads the Hungarian activities. The project includes two joint workshops per year, a shared verification benchmark repository, and short-term staff exchange visits. Tijana Vulin coordinates the technical content of the Serbian side and supervises two research assistants funded under the project.
partners: University of Szeged, Hungary
Subotica Tech – College of Applied Sciences, Serbia
Pannonia Automotive Research Consortium, Hungary

projects.title: Spatial Analysis and Performance Modeling for Rural Heterogeneous Networks in the Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: SPARNET addressed the poor mobile coverage in rural cross-border areas between Serbia and Hungary by developing stochastic geometry-based planning tools tailored to low-density deployment scenarios. The Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' Zrenjanin team led the work package on interference and outage modeling, contributing analytical frameworks and calibrated simulation tools. Field measurements at 24 test points in the Bačka region were used to validate propagation models. A coverage planning guideline document was produced for use by regional telecom regulators and operators. Rita Molnár coordinated the deliverables for the modeling work package and contributed to the final joint report.
partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology
Regional Development Agency Subotica
Pannonia Telecommunications Research Institute, Pécs

projects.title: Heterogeneous Network Interference Control and Optimization Using Stochastic Methods
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: HETICOS investigates interference management strategies in heterogeneous 5G networks through stochastic geometry analysis and controlled experimentation on a small-scale testbed. The project focuses on three themes: joint uplink-downlink interference characterization under realistic fading and shadowing models, load-aware coverage optimization for densely deployed pico cells, and the incorporation of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces into the interference model. The team consists of Rita Molnár as principal investigator, two doctoral students, and a part-time research associate. Results are being disseminated through journal publications and conference contributions, with a planned open-source repository of MATLAB simulation scripts to be released at project completion.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' Zrenjanin, University of Novi Sad
University of Niš, Faculty of Electronic Engineering

projects.title: Privacy-Preserving Integration of Federated Health Registries in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed methods and software tools for privacy-preserving record linkage and k-anonymity enforcement across health registries in Serbia, with test deployments involving synthetic registry data modelling institutions in three municipalities. The work covered Bloom filter-based encoding, quasi-identifier discovery automation, and a federated query engine with differential privacy support. A Python toolkit with documented APIs was produced and made publicly available under an open licence. The project involved collaboration with the Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina and the University of Novi Sad Faculty of Medicine, and produced seven peer-reviewed publications and one M.Sc. thesis.
partners: Institute of Public Health of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Medicine
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences

projects.title: Cross-Border Patient Record Linkage for Epidemiological Research in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSLINK addressed the practical barriers to linking patient records across the Serbian–Hungarian border for epidemiological studies, focusing on cardiovascular and diabetes outcomes. The project implemented and piloted a hash-based PPRL protocol handling name transliteration differences between Serbian Cyrillic/Latin and Hungarian orthography. A jointly operated coordination server was set up between Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' and the University of Debrecen. The project produced a technical specification document adopted as an internal standard by one partner institution and trained eight researchers from both countries in privacy-preserving data integration methods.
partners: University of Debrecen, Faculty of Informatics, Hungary
Subotica Tech – College of Applied Sciences, Serbia
Regional Health Centre Csongrád-Csanád County, Hungary

projects.title: Algebraic Codes for Reliable Flash Memory in Embedded Industrial Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated the design, analysis, and hardware-oriented implementation of algebraic burst-error-correcting codes tailored to the error statistics of industrial-grade NAND flash memory operating under extended temperature ranges and high program/erase cycle counts. The team constructed new code families over non-binary finite fields, developed iterative decoding extensions, and validated results on a custom flash evaluation testbed. Partners contributed expertise in flash device characterisation and FPGA implementation. The project produced seven journal and conference publications and supported two doctoral students to completion.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, Serbia
Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia

projects.title: Adaptive ECC Architectures for Next-Generation 3D NAND Storage
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: ADSTORE addresses the reliability challenges of 3D NAND flash by developing rate-adaptive coding architectures that adjust redundancy in response to real-time wear estimates. The project team characterises burst-error statistics from 64-layer and 96-layer 3D TLC NAND devices, derives nested code families suitable for firmware-level tier switching, and implements prototype decoders on FPGA platforms. Collaboration with a partner at the Budapest University of Technology and Applied Sciences provides access to additional flash device samples. Results are expected to contribute to two doctoral theses and several peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' Zrenjanin, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Budapest University of Technology and Applied Sciences, Hungary

projects.title: Cognitive Load-Aware Dashboard Design for Industrial Monitoring Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Пројекат COGDASH бавио се развојем методологије за процену когнитивног оптерећења оператора у индустријским системима надзора заснованим на SCADA дашбордовима, коришћењем окулографије и ЕЕГ сигнала. У трогодишњем периоду спроведено је пет студија са укупно 148 учесника, развијен је терenски компатибилан протокол мерења и прикупљен је лабелирани скуп података доступан истраживачкој заједници. У оквиру пројекта реализована је и сарадња са регионалним комуналним предузећем ради тестирања протокола у реалним условима. Резултати су примењени у изради прелиминарног прототипа адаптивног интерфејса.
partners: Факултет техничких наука, Универзитет у Новом Саду
Institute of Cognitive Neuroscience, University of Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Neurophysiological Indicators of Learning Efficiency in Technology-Enhanced Classroom Environments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Пројекат NEUROLEARN испитивао је однос окулографских и ЕЕГ показатеља когнитивног оптерећења са исходима учења у мешовитим наставним окружењима у средњој школи и на факултету. Богдановић је руководио радним пакетом за прикупљање и обраду психофизиолошких података на српској страни. Прикупљени су подаци 212 ученика и студената из Зрењанина и Сегедина. Пројекат је произвео смернице за наставнике о дизајну наставних материјала, засноване на резултатима мерења оптерећења, и обуку за 40 наставника из обе земље.
partners: Технички факултет „Михајло Пупин“, Зрењанин, Универзитет у Новом Саду
Department of Educational Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary
ОШ „Доситеј Обрадовић“ Зрењанин

projects.title: Sensor-Assisted Evacuation Planning for Public Buildings in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SAFEPATH investigated the integration of low-cost occupancy sensor networks with agent-based evacuation simulation for public buildings in Serbia. The project instrumented three buildings — a university faculty building, a municipal cultural centre, and a secondary school — with PIR, CO₂, and door-contact sensors connected via LoRaWAN. Sensor data fed into a simulation engine to generate real-time exit recommendations. The project produced an open-source software toolkit, three peer-reviewed journal papers, and a set of practical guidelines distributed to local municipal authorities. A key outcome was the field trial reported in the 2023 journal paper on dynamic exit assignment. The project also supported two doctoral students and ran two public workshops on evacuation planning for building managers in Zrenjanin and Novi Sad.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin', University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Novi Sad
City Administration of Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Border Crowd Safety Assessment Methodologies for Public Events
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROWDS-IPA is a cross-border project addressing crowd safety at large public events held near the Hungarian–Serbian border, including open-air festivals and sports venues. Ilić leads the work package on simulation-based risk assessment, responsible for developing shared modelling protocols applicable in both countries. The project collects anonymised crowd flow data from three annual events on each side of the border using overhead cameras and manual counting. The simulation work package produces scenario analyses for worst-case conditions and delivers training materials for event safety coordinators. A joint Serbian–Hungarian guideline document is planned as a final deliverable. The project involves two universities, a regional emergency management directorate, and a private event management firm.
partners: University of Miskolc, Hungary
Vojvodina Emergency Management Directorate
ProEvent d.o.o., Novi Sad
Baranya County Disaster Management Directorate, Hungary

projects.title: Energy-Aware Compiler Optimisation for RISC-V Microcontrollers in Industrial IoT Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi razvojem skupa kompajlerskih prolaza za LLVM koji eksplicitno minimizuju potrošnju energije na RISC-V mikrokontrolerima korišćenim u industrijskim IoT sistemima. Cilj je formalizovati energetski troškovni model koji se može integrisati u postojeće TableGen i MIR infrastrukture bez narušavanja korektnosti generisanog koda. Planirani ishodi uključuju otvorenu biblioteku prolaza, javno dostupan skup mernih podataka za tri različite RISC-V ploče i dve recenzirane publikacije godišnje. Projekat finansira dvoje istraživača i jednog doktoranda. Hardverska infrastruktura obuhvata merne stanice s vremenskom rezolucijom od 1 µs i automatizovano testno okruženje.
partners: Tehnički fakultet 'Mihajlo Pupin', Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Naučno-tehnološki park Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Document Semantics for Serbia and the EU Enlargement Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Пројекат CrossDocSE окупља четири партнерске институције из Србије и Мађарске са циљем изградње прототипске платформе за семантичку размену управних докумената у прекограничном подручју Суботица–Бaja. Платформа се ослања на OWL онтологије и SPARQL сервисе за аутоматско усклађивање шема докумената. Драгана Недић задужена је за развој онтолошких модула и за спровођење валидационих радионица са представницима локалних самоуправа. У оквиру пројекта планирана је и израда смерница за усклађивање са EIF референтном архитектуром, које ће бити слободно доступне под Creative Commons лиценцом.
partners: Технички факултет „Михајло Пупин“, Универзитет у Новом Саду
Градска управа Суботица
Department of Information Systems, University of Pécs
Önkormányzat Baja – Служба за информатику

projects.title: Numerical Methods for Surface-Driven Thin-Film Dynamics on Engineered Microstructures
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates computational techniques for simulating thin liquid films on substrates with engineered surface features, combining lubrication-theory models with higher-order spatial discretisations. The research covers structured surfaces including grooved, pillared, and chemically patterned geometries relevant to microfluidic and coating applications. Dragan Janković contributes to the development and testing of finite difference and finite element solvers, the construction of benchmark test cases, and the analysis of numerical stability and convergence. Computational experiments are run on the faculty cluster in Zrenjanin and validated against published experimental datasets from literature. The project is coordinated by Associate Professor Milena Đorđević and involves collaborators from the Faculty of Sciences in Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Information Technology, Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' Zrenjanin, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Difficulty-Adaptive Instruction for Language Learning in Multilingual Classrooms of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project developed and tested a modular adaptive exercise engine for Serbian, Hungarian, and Slovak language learning targeted at multilingual secondary school classrooms in Vojvodina. The engine implemented a hybrid adaptation strategy combining offline IRT calibration with online Bayesian ability estimation. Classroom trials were conducted in six schools across three municipalities, involving approximately 380 students over three academic semesters. Project deliverables included a documented item bank of 1,200 calibrated grammar and vocabulary exercises, a teacher dashboard for monitoring class-level progress, and a technical report on server infrastructure requirements for school deployment. The project resulted in three peer-reviewed publications and a set of free instructional materials distributed to participating schools.
partners: Pedagogical Institute of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Gymnasium 'Jovan Jovanović Zmaj', Novi Sad
Secondary School 'Svetozar Miletić', Subotica

projects.title: Samopodmazujući polimerni klizni elementi za mašine prehrambene industrije bez upotrebe maziva
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat se bavi razvojem i karakterizacijom kliznih umetaka i vođica od polimernih kompozita namenjenih za upotrebu u mašinama prehrambene industrije koje rade bez podmazivanja. Istraživanje obuhvata optimizaciju sastava kompozita na bazi PA6, PTFE i PEEK punjenih grafitom, MoS2 i h-BN, tribološku karakterizaciju na laboratorijskom nivou i proveru u uslovima koji simuliraju realan radni ciklus. Poseban akcenat stavljen je na ispitivanje u prisustvu vlage i periodičnog kontakta sa prehrambenim tekućinama, uz validaciju prema relevantnim regulativama EU o kontaktu sa hranom. Rezultati projekta treba da posluže kao osnova za dalji razvoj prototipa u saradnji sa domaćim proizvođačima prehrambene opreme.
partners: Tehnički fakultet „Mihajlo Pupin“ Zrenjanin, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Fakultet tehničkih nauka, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Weld Condition Monitoring in Industrial Steel Structures Using Low-Cost Sensor Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and field-test a practical SHM system specifically targeting weld fatigue damage in industrial steel structures. Activities included laboratory fatigue testing of representative weld joint geometries, development of automated OMA routines for edge-computing hardware, and 18-month deployments on two real industrial structures (a crane girder and a mezzanine frame) in Vojvodina. The project produced sensor placement guidelines, an open-source data processing pipeline, and a damage detection threshold framework accounting for temperature and operational load variability. Four journal papers, one conference paper, and a technical guideline document were produced. Two MSc students completed their theses within the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade
Kovinarstvo Petrović d.o.o., Zrenjanin

projects.title: Cross-Border Exchange of Structural Health Monitoring Expertise for Industrial Infrastructure
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project involving two Serbian and two Romanian partner institutions aiming to harmonize SHM practices for industrial steel structures in the Danube region. Jokić led the work package on experimental methods, coordinating joint laboratory exercises, shared use of laser vibrometry equipment, and a training workshop held in Timișoara attended by 34 engineers from both countries. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–Romanian) technical manual on vibration-based monitoring for welded steel frames and funded two short-term researcher exchanges. Outcomes contributed to a regional position paper submitted to the relevant national standardization bodies.
partners: Politehnica University of Timișoara
National Institute for Research and Development in Construction, Urbanism and Sustainable Spatial Development, Bucharest
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Organic Rankine Cycle Waste Heat Recovery for Small and Medium Industrial Enterprises in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project brought together three universities and one industrial partner to assess the waste heat recovery potential of ORC technology in SMEs across the cross-border region. Bogdanović led the work package on thermodynamic modelling and system sizing, coordinating the Zrenjanin team's contributions to field measurement campaigns at four manufacturing sites, development of a shared simulation toolkit, and production of a publicly available pre-feasibility screening tool for SME energy managers. The project delivered two site-specific feasibility reports, the screening tool, and a joint technical workshop attended by 34 industry representatives from both countries.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin', University of Novi Sad (lead)
Faculty of Engineering, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina Development Agency, Novi Sad
Termoplast d.o.o., Subotica

projects.title: Low-Grade Heat Recovery Cycles: Thermodynamic Limits and Practical Constraints for Serbian Industry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS)
projects.summary: LOWREC investigates the gap between theoretically achievable and practically realisable efficiency in ORC and Kalina cycle systems applied to Serbian industrial waste heat sources. The project combines thermodynamic limit analysis, component-level experimental characterisation on the Zrenjanin test rig, and dynamic system simulation. Key objectives include: quantifying the contribution of expander off-design operation to annual energy loss, developing experimentally validated dynamic models for daily-cycling ORC operation, and producing design guidelines calibrated to the specific heat source profiles found in Vojvodina's food and ceramics sectors. The project funds one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin', University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Terrain-Responsive Load Management for Agricultural Tractor-Implement Linkages
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop validated multibody simulation methods for predicting fatigue-relevant load spectra in three-point hitch linkages under representative field conditions in Serbia. Core activities included terrain profiling campaigns across three soil type zones in Vojvodina, construction of flexible-body lower link models, and hardware-in-the-loop testing of draft control algorithms using the faculty servo-hydraulic rig as a load emulator. The project involved 5 researchers and produced 6 journal papers, one M.Sc. thesis, and a publicly available terrain profile database covering 18 fields. A simplified analytical model derived from the simulation results was disseminated to domestic implement manufacturers through two workshops.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Agriculture
Institute for Agricultural Mechanisation, Zemun

projects.title: Cross-Border Benchmarking of Tractor Dynamic Performance Standards for Hungarian-Serbian Agricultural Conditions
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral applied research and testing project between the Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' and the University of Debrecen Institute of Mechanical Engineering. The project established shared protocols for field measurement of tractor vibration and linkage loads under comparable Hungarian and Serbian terrain and operational conditions. Work package 2, led by Ristić, covered multibody simulation methodology harmonisation and production of a joint simulation benchmark dataset. Results were used to identify differences in typical operating conditions across the border and to recommend updates to regional tractor testing guidelines. Three joint conference papers and one co-authored journal article were produced.
partners: University of Debrecen, Institute of Mechanical Engineering, Hungary
Regional Development Agency Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Residual Stress Characterisation and Distortion Modelling in MIG-Welded Aluminium Structures for Transport Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish a validated experimental and computational methodology for characterising residual stresses and predicting distortions in MIG-welded thin-wall aluminium assemblies representative of transport sector components. Work packages covered thermal cycle measurement campaigns, XRD and hole-drilling measurement protocols, finite element model development and validation, and an inherent-strain-based fast prediction tool for multi-weld assemblies. Physical specimens in AA6061 and AA5083 were produced under controlled conditions at the Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' welding cell. The project produced 5 journal papers, 3 conference contributions, and trained 2 PhD students. Collaboration with partners provided access to contour method facilities and additional XRD equipment.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Naval Architecture, University of Zagreb, Croatia
Faculty of Engineering, University of Debrecen, Hungary

projects.title: Risk-Informed Supplier Selection Models for Agri-food Supply Chains in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: The project examined procurement risk management practices at small and medium-sized agri-food processors in the Serbian and Romanian parts of the Danube region. The Zrenjanin team led the work package on quantitative risk assessment, developing and field-testing MCDM-based supplier evaluation tools with eight partner enterprises. Data collection involved structured surveys at 34 firms and workshops with procurement managers. Deliverables included a freely accessible decision-support spreadsheet tool, a training manual for procurement officers, and three peer-reviewed publications. The project also produced a comparative report on regulatory differences in food safety supplier certification requirements between the two countries.
partners: Faculty of Economics and Business Administration, West University of Timișoara, Romania
Regional Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Danube Agri-business Cluster, Drobeta-Turnu Severin, Romania

projects.title: Sustainable and Carbon-Efficient Decision Support for Supplier Selection in Serbian Food Processing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project develops decision-support methods and software prototypes for agri-food processing companies seeking to reduce carbon exposure in their supplier portfolios without disproportionate cost increases. The work combines multi-objective fuzzy optimisation with life-cycle assessment data for inbound logistics in three agri-food sectors: vegetable processing, flour milling, and dairy. The project team includes researchers from Zrenjanin and the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad. Validation is being conducted in collaboration with three industry partners. The expected output includes two validated software modules, five journal papers, and a policy brief aimed at the Serbian Ministry of Agriculture. One doctoral student is being trained within the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Vojvodina Food Processors Association, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Measuring and Strengthening Organizational Resilience in Manufacturing SMEs of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops and cross-validates a battery of resilience measurement tools applicable to manufacturing SMEs operating in Western Balkan transitional economies. Activities include large-scale firm surveys in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia (target n = 450 firms), expert workshops with regional chambers of commerce, and the production of a freely downloadable diagnostic toolkit. The Zrenjanin team is responsible for instrument design, data collection coordination in Serbia, and statistical analysis. Saša Žarković contributes to survey administration, database management, and quantitative analysis tasks under the supervision of the project principal investigator.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' Zrenjanin, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Banja Luka
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Regional Chamber of Commerce Vojvodina

projects.title: Knowledge Management Frameworks for Regional Administration: Comparative Capacity Assessment in Serbia, Romania and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je obuhvatao komparativnu procenu zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u 36 regionalnih i lokalnih javnih institucija u Srbiji, Rumuniji i Mađarskoj. Istraživački tim razvio je zajednički dijagnostički protokol koji je primenjen u sva tri nacionalna konteksta, a nalazi su korišćeni za dizajn programa izgradnje kapaciteta namenjenih rukovodiocima u javnom sektoru. Kovačević je bila lider radnog paketa zaduženog za razvoj metodologije i koordinaciju istraživačkih aktivnosti u Srbiji. Projekat je rezultovao zajedničkim priručnikom za samodijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem i nizom radionica za javne službenike u pograničnim regionima.
partners: Universitatea de Vest din Timișoara, Facultatea de Științe Economice
Pécsi Tudományegyetem, Közgazdaságtudományi Kar
Regionalna razvojna agencija Banat, Zrenjanin
Asociația pentru Dezvoltare Regională Vest, Timișoara

projects.title: Merenje i unapređenje kapaciteta upravljanja znanjem u organima javne uprave u Vojvodini
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je finansiran od strane Pokrajinskog sekretarijata za visoko obrazovanje i naučnoistraživačku delatnost i usmeren je na razvoj i validaciju alatki za samodijagnostiku zrelosti upravljanja znanjem prilagođenih specifičnostima pokrajinske i lokalne uprave u Vojvodini. U okviru projekta sproveden je anketni upitnik u 22 opštinske uprave i pet pokrajinskih organa (N = 340), a rezultati su korišćeni za izradu javno dostupnog izveštaja o stanju upravljanja znanjem u Vojvodini. Projekat je takođe podržao izradu doktorske disertacije jednog od članova istraživačkog tima.
partners: Tehnički fakultet „Mihajlo Pupin“, Zrenjanin, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Pokrajinski sekretarijat za regionalnu politiku, međuregionalnu saradnju i lokalnu samoupravu
Stalna konferencija gradova i opština Srbije – Regionalna kancelarija Novi Sad

projects.title: Lean Production Readiness and Performance in the Serbian Food Processing Sector: Diagnostic Tools and Implementation Support
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to develop and validate diagnostic and implementation support tools for lean adoption in Serbian food processing companies. Activities included large-scale survey data collection from over 100 firms, longitudinal follow-up of kaizen events in selected companies, and the development of a web-based readiness self-assessment instrument piloted with twelve companies. The project produced five peer-reviewed publications, one edited book chapter, and a practitioner guide distributed through the Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina. A database of baseline operational metrics from participating firms was compiled and is maintained at the Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin'. The project funded one doctoral student whose dissertation focused on performance measurement in lean food companies.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin', University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Chamber of Commerce of Vojvodina, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Transfer of Lean Production Knowledge Between Food SMEs in Serbia and Hungary
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSS-LEAN was a cross-border cooperation project linking academic institutions and business support organisations in Vojvodina and southern Hungary to facilitate the transfer of lean production knowledge between food processing SMEs. Grbić led the work package responsible for baseline assessment of lean maturity in participating firms and design of a joint training curriculum. The project delivered eight joint workshops attended by representatives of 34 companies, a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) lean toolkit for food processors, and a comparative study of adoption barriers on both sides of the border. The project also supported two student exchange visits and established a network of lean-interested food companies that continues to meet informally.
partners: Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin', University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vojvodina Food Cluster Association, Novi Sad
South Transdanubian Regional Development Agency, Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: R&D Portfolio Governance in Technology SMEs of the Danube Region: Instruments, Barriers and Performance Outcomes
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: Projekat je ispitivao praksu upravljanja R&D portfoliom u 60 malih i srednjih tehnoloških preduzeća sa područja Vojvodine i pograničnih regiona Mađarske. Osnovni ciljevi bili su mapiranje trenutnih instrumenata prioritizacije, identifikovanje institucionalnih i kapacitetnih barijera, te merenje veze između formalnosti portfolijskog procesa i poslovnih performansi. Realizovana je serija od 4 radionice za preduzeća, razvijen je dijagnostički alat za samoprocenu (dostupan on-line) i objavljen zajednički izveštaj na srpskom i mađarskom jeziku. Projekat je rezultirao i pilot-programom mentoringa za 8 preduzeća.
partners: Óbuda University, Budapest, Hungary
Regionalna razvojna agencija Bačka, Novi Sad
Udruženje tehnoloških preduzetnika Vojvodine (UTPV)

projects.title: Prioritization Maturity and Technology Transfer in Serbian Manufacturing Firms
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje u kojoj meri zrelost procesa prioritizacije R&D portfolija utiče na uspešnost transfera tehnologije u prerađivačkim preduzećima Srbije. Istraživanje obuhvata longitudinalnu studiju na uzorku od 40 preduzeća praćenih tokom tri godine, uz godišnje merenje RPM-MM skor vrednosti i indikatora transfera (broj licenci, spin-off preduzeća, zajedničkih patenata s istraživačkim institucijama). Projektom je predviđena i izrada javno dostupnog priručnika za primenu alata prioritizacije, namenjen preduzećima bez OR stručnjaka, kao i organizovanje godišnje konferencije za praktičare u Zrenjaninu.
partners: Tehnički fakultet „Mihajlo Pupin“, Zrenjanin
Institut Mihajlo Pupin, Beograd
Privredna komora Vojvodine

projects.title: Metacognitive Regulation in Continuing Online Education: Rural Contexts in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: METACOR was a cross-border applied research project examining how structured asynchronous video instruction affects metacognitive regulation among adult learners in rural municipalities of Vojvodina (Serbia) and Baranya and Somogy counties (Hungary). The project produced a shared measurement protocol using the SMRS and its Hungarian adaptation, collected parallel longitudinal data from approximately 200 learners per country over two academic years, and developed a practitioner toolkit of video design guidelines and prompt templates distributed to 14 adult education providers. The project also organised three joint professional development seminars for instructional designers and distance education coordinators. Total budget: approximately 280,000 EUR.
partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Education, University of Pécs
Regional Adult Education Centre Subotica
Baranya County Lifelong Learning Association, Pécs

projects.title: Digital Self-Regulated Learning Indicators from LMS Interaction Data
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project developed and tested a set of behavioural indicators of self-regulated learning derived from Moodle log data, with a focus on video interaction events (replays, prompt completions, chapter navigation) as proxies for metacognitive monitoring and evaluation. Data were collected across five distance courses at the Faculty of Education in Sombor and validated against SMRS scores and course outcomes for approximately 320 learners. The project also produced an open-source Python script for extracting and categorising video interaction events from standard Moodle log exports, made available via the project repository. Budget: 1,800,000 RSD.
partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Teacher Identity Dynamics in Digitally Transformed Primary Schools: Cross-Regional Evidence from Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: IDENT-DIG was a three-year bilateral research project coordinated from the Faculty of Education in Sombor and involving partners in Zagreb and Pécs. The project pursued two main goals: first, to apply and further validate the DISTRA-T instrument in three national contexts with differing policy regimes for digital mandates; second, to document school-level practices that buffer identity strain during platform transitions. Data collection included repeated DISTRA-T administration in 54 schools across the three countries, 96 semi-structured interviews with teachers and principals, and policy document analysis. The project produced four peer-reviewed journal articles, the freely available DISTRA-T instrument in three languages, and a policy brief distributed to ministries of education in all three countries. One doctoral student at the Faculty of Education in Sombor was supported under this project.
partners: Faculty of Teacher Education, University of Zagreb, Croatia
Faculty of Education, University of Pécs, Hungary
Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade

projects.title: Evidence-Based Screencast Design Standards for Vocational Curricula in the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish an empirically grounded set of design standards for screencasts used in Serbian secondary vocational education across six subject domains. The core activities included a large corpus study of 240 teacher-produced screencasts, three experimental studies with vocational students, development and validation of the SQR-Voc rubric, and a professional development module for vocational teachers. Partner schools were recruited across Vojvodina and the Belgrade region. The project produced 8 peer-reviewed outputs, trained 64 teachers through a pilot development programme, and delivered rubric materials freely available to vocational school curriculum coordinators. Total budget was approximately 3.2 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Centre for Vocational and Adult Education, Belgrade
Secondary Vocational School Mihajlo Pupin, Kula
Technical School Nikola Tesla, Zrenjanin

projects.title: Multimodal Learning Materials in Cross-Border Vocational Education: Shared Standards and Teacher Competences
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: MULTIVOC was a cross-border cooperation project between vocational education institutions in Vojvodina and southern Hungary, focused on developing shared evaluation standards for multimodal learning materials, with screencasts as the primary material type. Dobanovački led the work package on research methodology and learning outcomes assessment, contributing experimental study designs and instruments used in both countries. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) teacher guide for screencast production, organised two cross-border training workshops attended by 91 teachers, and generated a comparative dataset of 80 screencasts evaluated against shared quality criteria. Outputs were disseminated through the vocational education authorities of both countries.
partners: Faculty of Education, University of Pécs, Hungary
Vocational Training Centre of Csongrád-Csanád County, Szeged, Hungary
Provincial Secretariat for Education, Administration and National Communities, Novi Sad
Economic School Svetozar Miletić, Novi Sad

projects.title: Family Digital Mediation and School E-Learning Outcomes in Vojvodina Primary Schools
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project examined how different parental digital mediation strategies relate to children's learning outcomes on school-mandated e-learning platforms across 28 primary schools in Vojvodina. The project collected longitudinal data from approximately 500 child–parent dyads over two school years, combining platform log data, parental questionnaires, and standardised achievement measures. A secondary strand produced practical guidance materials for school pedagogues and class teachers on how to communicate e-learning homework expectations to parents. Project outputs include four peer-reviewed articles, two practitioner reports distributed to partner schools, and a set of open-access parent-guidance leaflets translated into Serbian and Hungarian.
partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Primary School Đura Jakšić, Sombor
Primary School Sonja Marinković, Novi Sad

projects.title: Digital Parenting Practices and E-Learning in Trilingual Border Regions: Serbia, Hungary, Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DIGIPAR is a cross-border project comparing parental digital mediation practices and their educational consequences in Hungarian-Serbian and Romanian-Serbian bilingual and trilingual communities. The University of Novi Sad team leads the work package on instrument adaptation and data harmonisation, ensuring that parental mediation and child outcome measures function equivalently across linguistic and cultural contexts. Data collection involves approximately 900 families across four regions. The Sombor team contributes expertise on Hungarian-Serbian bilingual families in Vojvodina. Outputs include a harmonised measurement toolkit, policy briefs for each participating country's education ministry, and shared open-access datasets.
partners: Faculty of Education, University of Pécs, Hungary
Department of Educational Sciences, West University of Timișoara, Romania
Faculty of Education in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Municipal Institute for Education, Subotica

projects.title: Minority Identity in Children's Reading Cultures: Vojvodina Hungarian and Romanian Banat Hungarian Communities Compared
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project compared how Hungarian-minority children's literary cultures function in two adjacent cross-border regions: Vojvodina in Serbia and Banat in Romania. Anja Gajić led the work package on textual and paratextual analysis of published children's books, coordinating a joint corpus of 60 titles from both regions. The project produced a comparative thematic database, two joint publications, and a set of recommendations for cross-border minority literary education programmes. Fieldwork included teacher focus groups in four schools in Vojvodina and three in Romanian Banat. The project also funded a small exhibition of minority-language picture books displayed at libraries in Subotica and Timișoara.
partners: Hungarian Language Teacher Training Faculty Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Letters, History and Theology, West University of Timișoara, Romania
Banat Hungarian Cultural Association, Timișoara

projects.title: Children's Literature as a Vector of Minority Language Maintenance: Empirical and Textual Approaches in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates whether regular engagement with Hungarian-language children's literature in home and school settings correlates with measurable indicators of minority language maintenance among 8–14-year-olds in Vojvodina. The study combines a longitudinal survey of 320 pupils across 12 schools with qualitative textual analysis of the books most frequently reported by pupils and teachers. Instruments include a validated language-use diary adapted from existing minority-language maintenance tools, plus structured reading-log interviews. Midterm findings indicate that pupils with consistent home access to Hungarian-language books show higher self-reported Hungarian-language use in peer settings. Final results and a policy brief are expected in late 2025.
partners: Hungarian Language Teacher Training Faculty Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Education Quality and Evaluation, Novi Sad office

projects.title: Multilingual Numeracy Instruction: Cognitive and Linguistic Factors in Early Mathematics Learning in Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates how the interplay of language background and cognitive constraints shapes early mathematics performance in Hungarian–Serbian bilingual primary schools across Vojvodina. The team conducts classroom observations, administers working memory and numeracy assessments to children in grades one through three, and surveys teachers about instructional practices. A secondary goal is to develop and pilot a short set of teacher guidance materials on load-reducing instructional strategies. Valentina Ninkov contributes to data collection, eye-tracking sessions, and the preparation of teacher guidance materials. The project involves collaboration with schools in Subotica, Senta, and Ada municipalities. Results are intended to feed into recommendations for the regional curriculum authority.
partners: Hungarian Language Teacher Training Faculty Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Municipal Institute for Education Quality, Subotica
Primary School Petőfi Sándor, Senta

projects.title: Vojvodina Manuscript Corpus: Expansion, Annotation, and Open Access Infrastructure for 19th-Century Minority Language Documentation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project expanded the BacsBodrog Manuscript Corpus from approximately 78,000 to 180,000 annotated tokens through new archival digitisation campaigns at four repositories in Serbia and Hungary. A revised annotation scheme (Version 2.0) was implemented, covering morphological, syntactic, and document-level metadata. A web interface allowing concordance search, metadata filtering, and document-image display was developed in collaboration with the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad. The project also produced a prosopographical database of identified scribes and a set of handwriting identification guidelines for use in future attribution work. All corpus data were deposited in open access under a Creative Commons licence by the end of the project period.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Historical Archive of Subotica
Diocesan Archives of the Reformed Church in Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Institute for Archival Studies, Pázmány Péter Catholic University, Budapest

projects.title: Hungarian–Serbian Language Contact in Official and Religious Written Registers, 18th–20th Centuries
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project brought together linguists from Serbia and Hungary to document and analyse Hungarian–Serbian language contact phenomena in administrative, ecclesiastical, and educational texts from the former Bács-Bodrog and Torontál counties. Andrea Ognjanov led the work package on morphosyntactic contact phenomena, coordinating corpus collection and analysis activities on the Serbian side. The work package produced a comparative database of contact-induced changes in both languages and a joint methodological guide for historical contact linguistics research in the region. The project outcomes included three joint publications and a publicly accessible bilingual research bibliography.
partners: Department of Hungarian Linguistics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Department of Serbian Language and Linguistics, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad
Hungarian Language Teacher Training Faculty Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Slavic Studies, University of Miskolc, Hungary

projects.title: Remote Sensing-Based Monitoring Framework for Riparian Habitat Condition in the Danube Basin
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: RIPMON developed and validated a cross-border monitoring framework using harmonised Sentinel-2 time-series classification protocols for riparian habitat condition assessment in the Hungarian–Serbian Danube and Tisa corridor. The BioSense team led the work package on satellite data processing and classification, producing annual habitat condition maps at 10 m resolution for a 340 km transboundary river stretch. Outputs included a publicly accessible web map service and a technical protocol document adopted by both national nature protection agencies for future periodic reporting. The project trained twelve practitioners from the partner institutions in OBIA workflows and time-series analysis methods.
partners: Institute of Geography, University of Pécs, Hungary
Danube–Dráva National Park Directorate, Pécs, Hungary
Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province, Novi Sad, Serbia
Public Water Management Company Vode Vojvodine, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Satellite-Based Detection and Area Estimation of Priority Invasive Plant Species in Serbian River Floodplains
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FLORASAT addresses the lack of consistent, spatially explicit area estimates for the three highest-priority invasive woody and herbaceous species (Amorpha fruticosa, Reynoutria japonica, and Fallopia sachalinensis) in Serbian river floodplains. The project combines multitemporal Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope imagery with species distribution modelling to produce national-scale maps updated annually. Field validation campaigns in 2022, 2023, and 2024 covered 42 river reaches across eight major basins. An open-access classification dataset and a species phenology reference library are being developed as community resources. The project runs in close cooperation with the Institute for Nature Conservation of Serbia and the Environmental Protection Agency.
partners: Institute for Nature Conservation of Serbia, Belgrade
Faculty of Biology, University of Belgrade
Environmental Protection Agency of the Republic of Serbia, Belgrade

projects.title: Carbon Sensing in Agricultural Soils of the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CARBOSENSE-AP aims to develop a reproducible workflow for mapping SOC across the Vojvodina agricultural region by integrating airborne hyperspectral data, Sentinel-2 multispectral time series, and laboratory soil spectral libraries. The project builds a regional reference database of over 500 georeferenced soil samples spanning different soil types and management histories. Srđan Ognjanov contributes to field sampling campaigns, laboratory spectral measurements, and development of the PLSR and spectral unmixing components of the prediction pipeline. A secondary objective is to assess interannual SOC change detectability using repeat overflights. Results are intended to inform agri-environment scheme monitoring for provincial agricultural authorities.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: SAR-Based Monitoring and Susceptibility Assessment of Loess Slope Instability in the Central Danube Region
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: LOESSAR focuses on establishing a systematic SAR-based monitoring framework for loess slope failures along the Serbian stretch of the Danube and Sava rivers. The project integrates Sentinel-1 persistent scatterer time series, ALOS-2 L-band distributed scatterer processing, and field-deployed corner reflector networks to build a displacement catalogue for the 2015–2025 period. Susceptibility modelling combines the InSAR-derived velocity data with lithostratigraphic, hydrological, and morphometric predictors using logistic regression and random forest classifiers. Outputs include an open national loess landslide geodatabase, monitoring protocols suitable for adoption by the Geological Survey of Serbia, and a cost estimation tool for public infrastructure managers in affected municipalities.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Geological Survey of Serbia, Belgrade
Faculty of Mining and Geology, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Inventory and Early Warning Concepts for Danube Corridor Landslides
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: DANGERSLOPE is a cross-border project addressing landslide hazard along the Romanian and Serbian banks of the Danube, where loess and loess-like deposits create similar geomorphological and geotechnical conditions on both sides. Vranješ leads the work package on SAR-based displacement monitoring and joint inventory development, coordinating Sentinel-1 processing for approximately 3 800 km² of loess terrain. The project will produce a harmonised bilateral landslide geodatabase, bilingual public-facing hazard maps at 1:50 000 scale, and a prototype near-real-time alert system based on Sentinel-1 12-day coherence thresholds. Training workshops for local civil protection agencies in both countries are planned in the final project year.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
National Institute of Hydrology and Water Management, Bucharest
University of Timișoara, Department of Geography
Provincial Directorate for Civil Protection of Vojvodina

projects.title: Thermal Characterisation of Urban Environments in the Pannonian Region Using Multi-Source Satellite Data
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: THERMAPAN aims to produce a harmonised, multi-temporal LST dataset for urban areas in the Vojvodina province and neighbouring Pannonian regions by combining Landsat, ECOSTRESS, and Sentinel-3 SLSTR retrievals. The project develops downscaling and cross-sensor calibration procedures to enable consistent long-term trend analysis. Čolić contributes to the satellite data processing pipeline, field validation campaign design, and preparation of derived UHI climatology maps for five cities. An open data repository of processed LST time series will be made available to regional urban planners and climate adaptation authorities upon project completion. The project is led by BioSense Institute in collaboration with the Faculty of Sciences at the University of Novi Sad.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Lowland Forestry and Environment, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Satellite-Based Monitoring Framework for Informal Land Occupation on Peri-Urban Fringes in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PERIWATCH developed a shared satellite monitoring protocol for peri-urban informal construction detection, implemented across four cross-border municipalities in southern Hungary and northern Serbia. BioSense Institute led the work package on image processing methodology and change detection algorithm development, contributing annual informal settlement extent maps at 0.5 m resolution using Pléiades imagery. The project produced a publicly accessible web portal with map layers updated annually, used by municipal planning departments in both countries. Outputs included a harmonised training sample library of approximately 9,000 labelled VHR image patches and a technical report on data cost-sharing arrangements between partner municipalities. The project involved three field campaigns for ground truth collection.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Spatial Planning of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences, Hungary
Municipality of Senta, Serbia
Municipality of Baja, Hungary

projects.title: Automated Detection and Temporal Reconstruction of Informal Settlement Expansion in Serbia Using Deep Learning and VHR Archive Imagery
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: INFOMAP-RS aims to produce the first nationally consistent, annually resolved map series of informal settlement extent in Serbia for the period 2009–2024, using a deep learning classification pipeline applied to a multi-source VHR imagery archive. The project addresses three main challenges: handling radiometric heterogeneity across sensor types in a common classification framework, constructing a sufficiently large and geographically diverse training dataset, and validating outputs against independent cadastral and aerial survey records in six test municipalities. A secondary objective is to quantify the relationship between infrastructure investment events and informal construction acceleration at the peri-urban fringe. Results are shared with the Republic Geodetic Authority and the Ministry for Construction.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Republic Geodetic Authority of Serbia, Belgrade

projects.title: Carbon Stock Assessment in Temperate Forests of the Western Balkans Using Multi-Platform LiDAR and Sentinel Data
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aims to produce spatially explicit carbon stock maps for broadleaf forest ecosystems across northern Serbia and the Western Balkans by integrating airborne LiDAR point clouds, UAV surveys, and Sentinel-1/2 satellite time series. Darko Mirković contributes to the LiDAR data processing pipeline, specifically the voxelisation workflow and the derivation of structural metrics used as inputs to stand-level biomass models. He also leads the field campaign planning for plot-level destructive biomass sampling on Fruška Gora and in the riparian forests along the Danube. The project runs in collaboration with forestry institutes in Serbia and a university partner in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and its outputs are intended to support national greenhouse gas inventory reporting obligations under international climate agreements.
partners: Institute of Forestry, Belgrade
Faculty of Forestry, University of Banja Luka
Provincial Secretariat for Urban Planning and Environmental Protection, Vojvodina

projects.title: Multi-Source Satellite Monitoring of Flood Dynamics and Wetland Hydroperiods in the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PANNFLOOD aimed to produce the first systematic, SAR-based hydroperiod climatology for wetland complexes in the Serbian portion of the Pannonian Plain. The project generated a continuous Sentinel-1 inundation record spanning 2015–2024, validated against in-situ canal gauge data, drone surveys, and field campaigns at six representative wetland sites. A coupled SAR–hydrological modelling component was developed to handle shallow inundation under dense canopy, building on the water-cloud model inversion methods developed in Zorić's earlier work. Outputs include open-access raster datasets, a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Nature Protection, and peer-reviewed publications. The project employed one postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Wetland Connectivity Assessment Using Earth Observation in the Hungarian–Serbian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: WETPAN-IPA is a cross-border cooperation project addressing the declining connectivity of wetland patches along the Tisza and associated channels in the Hungarian–Serbian border zone. Zorić leads Work Package 3, responsible for producing harmonised Sentinel-1 inundation maps and hydroperiod indicators for a 120 km border transect. These spatial products feed into a connectivity modelling module led by the Hungarian partner and a habitat assessment component run by the nature conservation partner. The project also includes a public communication component and a joint training workshop for national park rangers and water management staff on interpreting satellite-derived flood maps. Results will be integrated into the regional wetland management strategy currently under revision by both national authorities.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Middle-Tisza Environmental and Water Directorate, Szolnok
Koviljsko-Petrovaradinski Rit Nature Reserve Management Unit
Kiskunság National Park Directorate, Kecskemét

projects.title: Agricultural Aerosol and Smoke Monitoring over the Pannonian Region Using Multi-Mission Satellite Data
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AGROSMOKE addressed the lack of high-spatial-resolution aerosol monitoring over the Pannonian Plain, where agricultural activities including tillage, harvest, and post-harvest burning are major but poorly quantified sources of particulate matter. The project integrated Sentinel-3 OLCI and SLSTR data with MODIS retrievals and ground-based AERONET and low-cost sensor observations to build a consistent multi-year AOD and PM2.5 dataset at 300 m resolution. Radiative transfer modelling with 6SV and SBDART was used to constrain aerosol optical properties specific to Vojvodina soil types and biomass burning aerosol. Deliverables included an open-access dataset, two peer-reviewed papers, and a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Environmental Protection of Vojvodina.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia

projects.title: Cross-Border Agricultural Dust Transport and Its Impact on Air Quality in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANSDUST investigated the transboundary transport of agricultural dust between southern Hungary and northern Serbia, a corridor with intensive arable farming on shared loess parent material. Danijela Đorđević leads the work package on satellite-based aerosol monitoring, providing MODIS and Sentinel-3 AOD time series and coordinating validation with the project's network of ground sensors on both sides of the border. Other work packages address atmospheric dispersion modelling, public health exposure assessment, and harmonisation of national air quality reporting methodologies. The project is co-financed through the Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia programme and involves municipalities, environmental agencies, and universities in both countries.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Geodesy and Geoinformatics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Provincial Environmental Protection Agency of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Csongrád-Csanád County Government, Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Flexible Piezoelectric Harvesters for Autonomous Agricultural Sensor Networks
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a complete prototype chain from PVDF-TrFE film deposition through harvester packaging to integration with low-power wireless sensor nodes targeted at precision agriculture in Vojvodina. BioSense Institute leads fabrication and electromechanical characterisation, while the Faculty of Agriculture contributes field deployment scenarios and the Faculty of Technical Sciences provides circuit design expertise. Arsić is responsible for thin-film deposition process development, poling optimisation, and the impedance and vibrometry characterisation campaign. The project includes a demonstration at three partner farms involving at least 30 sensor nodes operating autonomously for six months. Target deliverables include a process specification document suitable for technology transfer and two peer-reviewed publications.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Vibration-Based Sensor Systems for Cross-Border Infrastructure Monitoring
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: VIBE-IPA addresses the shared need of Serbian and Romanian municipalities for low-cost structural monitoring of ageing bridge and silo infrastructure in the border region. The BioSense Institute contributes flexible piezoelectric sensor patch development and laboratory characterisation; Technical University of Cluj-Napoca leads system integration and communication architecture; local infrastructure agencies in Timișoara and Zrenjanin provide test sites and logistical support. Arsić's tasks include fabricating and qualifying sensor batches for outdoor deployment, conducting environmental durability tests (temperature cycling, humidity exposure), and co-authoring the technical monitoring reports submitted to the programme authority. The project aims to instrument five structures with at least eight sensor nodes each by the end of 2025.
partners: Technical University of Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Public Enterprise for Roads and Infrastructure Zrenjanin, Serbia
Municipality of Timișoara, Romania

projects.title: Roll-to-Roll Printed Electrochemical Sensors for Agricultural Water Quality Monitoring
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENSOROLL developed scalable roll-to-roll inkjet printing processes for disposable electrochemical sensor strips targeting nitrite, phosphate, and heavy-metal analytes in irrigation and drainage water in the Vojvodina agricultural region. The project optimised ink formulations, drying profiles, and electrode layer sequences for web speeds up to 8 m·min⁻¹, achieving functional strip yield above 90% in pilot runs. Sensor performance was validated against reference laboratory methods using 120 field water samples. The project also produced an open-access printability database covering 18 ink–substrate combinations. Two M.Sc. theses and one Ph.D. thesis were completed within the project period.

projects.title: Flexible Printed Diagnostic Platforms for Point-of-Care Metabolite Monitoring
projects.programme: Horizon Europe
projects.summary: FlexDiag is a Horizon Europe project coordinated by Politecnico di Milano that develops fully printed flexible sensor platforms for simultaneous monitoring of metabolic markers (lactate, glucose, uric acid) in sweat and interstitial fluid. Crnković's group leads Work Package 3, responsible for aerosol-jet printing process development on silicone and thermoplastic polyurethane substrates, enzyme layer deposition, and mechanical reliability testing. The Novi Sad team contributes two aerosol-jet deposition engineers and a postdoctoral researcher. The work package interfaces with WP4 (signal conditioning electronics, TU Graz) and WP5 (clinical validation, University of Ljubljana Clinical Centre). Deliverables include a process specification document, a printed electrode library, and contributions to three joint publications.

projects.title: Microfluidic Passive Preconcentration Platforms for Low-Resource Diagnostic Applications
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The µFLOWDX project develops passive microfluidic chips capable of concentrating protein and nucleic acid biomarkers from dilute clinical samples without external pumps or power sources. The BioSense Institute team is responsible for PDMS device fabrication, fluidic characterisation, and evaporation-driven preconcentration experiments. Žarko Ivanović contributes to cleanroom processing, pressure-drop measurements, and preparation of test devices for partner evaluation. Target applications include early detection of urinary tract infection markers and C-reactive protein monitoring in community health settings in the Western Balkans. The project runs in collaboration with the Faculty of Sciences in Novi Sad and a clinical microbiology laboratory in Kragujevac.

Institute for Microbiology and Immunology, University of Kragujevac, Serbia

projects.title: Low-Noise Integrated Magnetic Sensing for Harsh Industrial Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MAGNOVA targets integrated Hall-effect sensor systems capable of achieving sub-15 nT/√Hz noise floors across the −40 °C to 150 °C range demanded by power electronics and automotive motor control. The project combines device-level process characterisation, compact noise modelling, and mixed-signal readout circuit design within a 0.35 µm CMOS technology available through a multi-project wafer service. Mladen Bjelica contributes to the noise characterisation workpackage, responsible for extracting temperature-dependent Hooge parameters, validating SPICE models against measurements, and assessing the impact of spinning-current phase timing on residual offset at elevated temperature. Two prototype readout chips are planned over the project lifetime.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Molecularly Imprinted Polymer Sensor Arrays for Multi-Analyte Screening of Pesticide and Pharmaceutical Residues in Vojvodina Water Bodies
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: AQUAMIP developed a multi-channel QCM array platform carrying distinct MIP receptor layers for six priority micropollutants—atrazine, chlorpyrifos, sulfamethoxazole, estrone, diclofenac, and metformin—relevant to agricultural and urban water bodies in Vojvodina. The project encompassed fundamental work on surface functionalisation protocols, MIP synthesis optimisation, and array integration, followed by field validation at six monitoring sites along the Danube–Tisa–Danube hydrosystem. A portable readout instrument with wireless data transmission was assembled and tested in collaboration with a local electronics firm. The project trained two doctoral students and resulted in six peer-reviewed publications and one patent application.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Cross-Border Sensor Network for Pharmaceutical Micropollutant Surveillance in Shared Water Resources
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: SENSPHAR established a cross-border monitoring network for pharmaceutical micropollutants in the Tisa River basin shared between Serbia and Romania. Dobanovački led the work package on QCM sensor fabrication and deployment, supplying MIP-coated transducers for six in-field stations operated jointly with the Romanian partner. The project validated sensor performance against accredited laboratory reference methods, assessed seasonal concentration variability of sulfamethoxazole, ibuprofen, and diclofenac, and produced a harmonised sampling and reporting protocol for binational environmental authorities. Field data from 18 months of continuous monitoring were shared with the Vojvodina Institute for Public Health and the Romanian National Environmental Protection Agency.

projects.title: Reliability Assessment of Wireless MEMS Sensor Networks for Open-Field Agricultural Monitoring in the Pannonian Climate Zone
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigated whether commercially available IoT sensor nodes meet reliability targets when deployed year-round in the field conditions of the Vojvodina plain, where diurnal and seasonal temperature swings are large and humidity is variable. Nedić's contribution covered the thermal modelling and lifetime prediction component: he developed finite-element models of two commercial sensor housings, correlated them to logged field temperature data, and produced quantitative lifetime estimates for solder interconnects and wire bonds. The project combined modelling with accelerated testing and a 14-month field campaign across five test sites. Outcomes included a reliability screening protocol and a data set of field temperature spectra now available to the research community.

projects.title: Thermomechanical Co-Design Framework for Multi-Die MEMS Modules in Harsh Agricultural Environments
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project, with Nedić as principal investigator, develops a simulation-based co-design workflow that integrates thermal, structural, and reliability analyses early in the packaging design phase for multi-die MEMS modules. The workflow combines parameterised finite-element models with a design-of-experiments approach to generate response surface models usable by engineers without specialist simulation expertise. A library of validated material property sets for encapsulants, substrates, and solder alloys relevant to agricultural IoT devices is being compiled and will be made openly available. Two sensor module demonstrators are being built and tested to validate the workflow predictions against experimental measurements of temperature distribution and fatigue life.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Grain Boundary Engineering for Selective Sub-ppm VOC Detection in Agricultural Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GrainSense aimed to establish quantitative relationships between grain boundary microstructure parameters and chemiresistive sensor performance toward VOCs relevant to grain storage and food logistics. The project combined FIB-SEM tomography, EBSD, and controlled permeation measurements with finite element modelling to build a predictive microstructure–response framework. A secondary objective was field validation in a working grain storage facility, generating the first multi-month drift dataset for SnO₂ and WO₃ sensors under real agricultural conditions. Two doctoral students and one postdoctoral researcher were supported. The project produced six peer-reviewed journal articles, two conference presentations, and one open dataset. Collaboration with the Provincial Institute of Agriculture provided access to the field test site and real-time atmospheric composition data.

Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Permeation-Controlled Transduction in Metal-Oxide Microsensor Arrays for Indoor Air Quality
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: PERMSENS was a multi-partner European project addressing fundamental limitations of metal-oxide gas sensor selectivity and humidity robustness for indoor air quality applications. Krstić led Work Package 3, which was responsible for thin-film deposition, microstructural characterisation, and gas permeation measurements across four material systems (SnO₂, ZnO, WO₃, In₂O₃). The BioSense team supplied characterised sensor elements to other partners for integration into microelectromechanical platforms and electronic nose systems. The work package delivered a materials database linking sputtering process parameters to microstructure descriptors and measured permeation kinetics, used as input for sensor array design optimisation in downstream work packages. Four peer-reviewed publications and one book chapter resulted from the BioSense contribution.

projects.title: Fibre-Optic Sensor Networks for Long-Term Structural Health Monitoring of Ageing Bridges in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: FIBROSENSE addresses the monitoring needs of ageing road and railway bridges across the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region by deploying and validating fibre-optic sensing networks capable of long-term unattended operation. The project covers sensor design and packaging, interrogation hardware development, data communication to cloud-based dashboards, and comparative analysis against conventional inspection protocols. Vuković contributes to the interrogation system design and the multiplexing architecture work package, and is responsible for field installation support and data quality validation during test campaigns on two bridges in the Vojvodina region. The project involves structural engineering and transport infrastructure partners on both sides of the border, with outcomes intended to feed into regional bridge management guidelines.

projects.title: Probabilistic Network Models for Abiotic Stress Response in Pannonian Crops
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: STRESSNET develops and validates Bayesian network structure learning pipelines adapted to the small-sample, high-dimensional transcriptomic datasets that are typical of greenhouse crop stress experiments. The project focuses on wheat, maize, and sunflower varieties grown in the Pannonian plain region, which is increasingly exposed to combined heat and drought events. Methodological contributions include improved prior elicitation from orthologous species data, bootstrap-based edge confidence metrics, and open-source tooling distributed as an R package. Biological outputs include candidate regulatory hubs in stress-signalling pathways that have been confirmed through targeted qRT-PCR validation. The project involves close collaboration with the Faculty of Agriculture at the University of Novi Sad for field and greenhouse material.
