projects.title: Cross-Border Multi-Omics Data Infrastructure for Crop Resilience Research
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBEOMICS builds a shared data management and analysis infrastructure for multi-omics plant stress experiments conducted at partner institutions in Hungary and Serbia. Ivona Marković contributes to the data analysis work package, focusing on harmonising RNA-seq preprocessing protocols across laboratories and implementing Bayesian network inference as one of several integrative analysis modules available through the project's shared computational platform. The project also includes training workshops for researchers and PhD students at both partner sites. Data sharing protocols and GDPR-compliant metadata standards for plant genomics data are being developed jointly across all partners.

projects.title: Standardised Computational Reproducibility in Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Pipelines
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the gap between published scRNA-seq results and their reproducibility by independent groups. The core activities are: systematic audit of parameter reporting in scRNA-seq publications, development of a containerised benchmarking suite covering ten dimensionality reduction and five clustering methods, and empirical testing of how preprocessing choices propagate into final cell-type annotations. The benchmarking suite is validated on ten reference datasets with experimentally confirmed cell-type labels. Outputs include the benchmarking software deposited as an open-source R/Python package, a preprint describing the minimum reporting checklist, and a training workshop for MSc and PhD students at member institutions. Partners contribute datasets and participate in the workshop series.

projects.title: Reference Single-Cell Transcriptomic Atlas of Agricultural Crop Root Tissues for the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project generates a reference single-cell RNA sequencing atlas of root tip tissues from three regionally important crop species under control and drought-stress conditions. Igor Čolić leads the work package on data integration, dimensionality reduction, and cluster annotation, applying and extending the benchmarking methodology developed in SCREP to plant scRNA-seq data, which presents distinct challenges compared to mammalian data including different cell-wall digestion protocols and lower transcript counts per cell. The atlas is deposited in a publicly accessible repository with standardised metadata and is intended to serve as a reference for future studies of root development and stress response across the partnership region.

University of Pécs, Department of Plant Biology

projects.title: Causal Methods for Environmental Exposure Assessment in Cross-Border Cohorts
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia

His tasks include constructing instrument candidates from meteorological and policy variation data, assessing parallel trend assumptions in DiD designs, and drafting the joint analysis protocol. The project involves approximately 18,000 cohort participants on the Serbian side and 22,000 on the Romanian side, with follow-up data spanning 2005 to 2023.

projects.title: Graph-Based Machine Learning for Precision Medicine: Integrating Multi-Omics Data for Drug Repurposing
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat GRAPHMED bavi se razvojem metoda zasnovanih na grafovskim neuronskim mrežama za repozicioniranje lekova integracijom heterogenih omiks podataka. projects.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Analytics for Multi-Site Clinical Decision Support in Southeast Europe

projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)

Filip Vučković led the work package on spatial statistical modelling, overseeing variogram analysis, kriging-based map production, and uncertainty quantification. The project also developed a shared open data repository for Pannonian microbiome surveys. Outputs include four peer-reviewed publications, a freely accessible map viewer for project partners, and a joint methodological protocol for cross-border soil sampling adopted by extension services in both countries.

Filip Vučković contributed to the soil-focused tasks, specifically the development and benchmarking of spatially aware Dirichlet-multinomial regression models. The project involved collaboration with a statistician at the University of Belgrade and a bioinformatician at the University of Kragujevac. Deliverables include an R package (deposited on CRAN) providing functions for spatial DM regression, a simulation-based benchmark paper, and training materials used in two postgraduate workshops at the Faculty of Sciences in Novi Sad.

projects.title: Multi-Omics Competing-Risks Models for Outcome Prediction in Balkan Oncology Cohorts
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project built and validated penalised competing-risks survival models integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data for three cancer types (colorectal, lung, and pancreatic) using retrospective cohorts from oncology centres in Serbia and North Macedonia. Key objectives included developing reproducible cross-validation pipelines for multi-block elastic net Cox and Fine–Gray models, assembling a curated multi-omics dataset of approximately 900 patients with complete follow-up records, and producing open-source R tooling for absolute risk estimation. External validation was conducted in collaboration with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina and the Institute of Oncology of Vojvodina. The project also supported two doctoral students and resulted in three peer-reviewed publications.

projects.title: Regularised Survival Analysis Methods for High-Dimensional Clinical Data: Training and Research Network

projects.title: Building Language Resources and Models for Serbian Biomedical Text Mining

projects.title: Force-Aware Robotic Systems for Selective Root Vegetable Harvesting in Heterogeneous Field Conditions

projects.summary: ROOTBOT addresses the lack of reliable force-control strategies for robotic harvesting of root vegetables in variable field soils across Serbian agricultural regions. projects.title: Sensor-Guided Selective Harvesting of Stone Fruits Using On-Robot Ripeness Staging

projects.title: Decentralised Swarm Protocols for Mixed-Function Ground Robot Fleets in Arable and Horticultural Crops
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FIELDSWARM investigates coordination algorithms that allow ground robot fleets composed of mechanically distinct platforms to perform complementary field operations concurrently. The project targets two use cases: inter-row weeding combined with targeted drip irrigation in maize, and under-canopy scouting combined with spot-treatment in apple orchards. Jana Brtka contributes to the design and field validation of the task-allocation and communication layers. Field trials are conducted on partner farms in Vojvodina. The project also produces open datasets of robot telemetry, soil condition measurements, and weed-density maps from the trial sites, which will be released under a Creative Commons licence at project end.

projects.title: Rapid Spectroscopic Authentication Framework for Cold-Pressed Edible Oils in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: OilSAFE brings together food analytical laboratories from Novi Sad and Szeged to develop and validate a shared reference spectral library and chemometric authentication protocols for cold-pressed oils commercially important in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border area, including pumpkin seed, sunflower, and flaxseed oils. The project focuses on building a publicly accessible spectral database of at least 400 authenticated samples per oil type and on harmonising measurement and preprocessing protocols across the two partner institutions. Emilija Ivković contributes to sample collection coordination on the Serbian side, NIR data acquisition, and PLSR and PLS-DA model development. A secondary objective is the preparation of a joint standard operating procedure document for SME laboratories.
partners: Institute of Food Technology (FINS), University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Bioaccessibility of Masked Mycotoxins in Cereal-Based Foods: From Digestion Models to Exposure Estimates
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The MYCODIG project investigates how masked and modified mycotoxins behave during human gastrointestinal digestion, with the aim of improving dietary exposure estimates for the Serbian population. The project applies the INFOGEST static digestion model and selected dynamic digestion protocols to a panel of cereal products representative of Serbian consumption patterns, including bread, pasta, and corn flour. Radović contributes to sample preparation, in vitro digestion experiments, and HPLC-MS/MS analysis of masked mycotoxin conjugates and their transformation products. The project is coordinated by a senior researcher at FINS, with collaborating partners in Hungary and Austria providing reference standards and analytical validation support.
partners: Institute of Food Technology (FINS), University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Institute of Food Science and Technology, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Thermal Process Validation Tools for Plant-Based Foods in the Western Balkans Food Industry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops a set of experimentally grounded kinetic datasets and a freely accessible online calculator for process schedule validation of heat-treated plant-based foods manufactured by small and medium enterprises in Serbia and neighbouring countries. Work packages cover strain isolation and characterisation, isothermal and dynamic inactivation experiments in representative matrices, model selection and parameter estimation, and dissemination through practical guidance documents co-developed with industry partners. Validated datasets for five spore-forming species and ten plant-based matrices are planned. The project also trains two early-stage researchers in predictive food microbiology methods.

projects.title: Ohmic Heating as an Energy-Efficient Pasteurisation Route for Structured Plant-Based Foods: Microbial Safety and Process Design
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: OHMSAFE compared the energy consumption and microbial inactivation efficacy of ohmic and conventional thermal processes for three categories of structured plant-based foods (purées, spreads, and particle-in-liquid soups) processed at pilot scale in Serbia and Hungary. Danica Ljubojević led the work package responsible for microbiological challenge testing and kinetic modelling. The project delivered a co-authored process design manual and contributed to a joint patent application on electrode configuration for viscous plant matrices. Pilot runs were conducted at the FINS pilot plant in Novi Sad and at a partner facility in Szeged.

projects.title: Polyphenol–Starch Non-Covalent Complexes in Cereal-Based Functional Foods: Thermodynamics, Structure and Glycaemic Impact
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates the formation, thermodynamic stability, and structural characteristics of non-covalent complexes between selected dietary polyphenols (hydroxycinnamic acids, flavonols, proanthocyanidins) and isolated cereal starch fractions (amylose, amylopectin, starch granules) from wheat, barley, rye, and oat. Work packages address complex characterisation by ITC, DSC, WAXS, and fluorescence spectroscopy; molecular modelling of binding geometries; in vitro digestibility and glycaemic index estimation using INFOGEST and Englyst protocols; and a pilot reformulation study of flatbreads and extruded snacks. The project funds two PhD positions and involves equipment access at the Institute of Physics Novi Sad for WAXS measurements. Partners share reference phenolic standards and provide statistical consulting.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Phenolic Composition and Starch Digestibility of Landraces and Modern Varieties of Small Grain Cereals from the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: A collaborative study across four institutions surveying 38 accessions of wheat, emmer, einkorn, spelt, rye, and barley grown in Vojvodina for total and bound phenolic content, individual hydroxycinnamic acid profiles by HPLC-MS, and in vitro starch digestibility. Danilo Vojnović led the work package on polyphenol–starch interaction chemistry, responsible for complex extraction, DSC characterisation, and digestibility assays across all 38 accessions. The project generated a searchable database of phenolic acid and digestibility data for regional cereal germplasm, deposited with the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops Novi Sad.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Microbial Risk Reduction in Minimally Processed Vegetable Supply Chains in the Pannonian Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: VEGISAFE addresses microbial contamination risks in fresh-cut vegetable supply chains shared between Hungary and Serbia, focusing on spoilage bacteria and sanitation practices across small and medium-sized processing enterprises. The project combines field sampling at partner facilities, laboratory challenge studies, and on-site hygiene audits to generate region-specific risk data. Katarina Bjelica is responsible for the biofilm characterisation component at the Novi Sad partner site, carrying out surface sampling, biofilm quantification, and sanitiser efficacy trials. Project outputs include a risk assessment framework adapted to SME conditions and a training package for production staff. Two SME processing companies in Vojvodina participate as associated partners providing facility access and production data.

projects.title: Recovery and Stabilisation of Natural Colorants from Winemaking By-Products for Application in Functional Beverages
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated the full processing chain from grape pomace collection through optimised extraction, encapsulation, and application testing in model beverage systems. The work package led by Gligorić covered extraction parameter optimisation and pigment stability mapping across pH, light, and temperature conditions. Partners contributed encapsulation and sensory evaluation expertise. The project produced a laboratory-scale protocol for producing a spray-dried anthocyanin powder meeting colour intensity specifications for soft drink applications, and generated stability data supporting a shelf-life model applicable to transparent and amber packaging under typical retail conditions. Collaboration with a regional winery provided representative pomace batches across two harvests.

projects.title: Valorisation of Agri-Food By-Products Along the Danube Corridor for Sustainable Food Ingredients
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border initiative between research institutions in Serbia and Romania focused on converting fruit and vegetable processing waste into food-grade ingredients including colourants, fibres, and antioxidant concentrates. Gligorić's contribution centred on the characterisation and stability testing of anthocyanin fractions from grape and elderberry pomace originating from participating Serbian producers. Romanian partners provided expertise in membrane filtration and comparative analysis of berry by-products common to the Romanian side of the Danube region. The project included two joint workshops and an exchange visit allowing analytical cross-validation between partner laboratories.

projects.title: Probabilistic Modelling of Veterinary Drug Residue Transfer in Integrated Livestock Production Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: VETRESMOD aimed to build a modular probabilistic framework for estimating consumer exposure to veterinary drug residues in Serbia, covering swine, poultry, and cattle production chains. The project collected new carry-over data from controlled feeding experiments (three drug classes, two species), aggregated historical monitoring data from national veterinary inspection records, and integrated national dietary survey data. Exposure models were coded in R and made available as documented scripts. The project also produced withdrawal period estimation guidelines adapted to Serbian regulatory standards. Partners contributed feeding trial infrastructure, dietary data, and analytical capacity.

projects.title: Cross-Border Feed Safety Monitoring and Risk Communication in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian institutions aimed at harmonising veterinary drug residue monitoring protocols in compound animal feed, establishing shared reference material exchange, and developing bilingual risk communication materials for feed producers and veterinary practitioners. Zec contributed to the work package on exposure modelling, providing carry-over factor estimates for the Hungarian feed monitoring programme and supporting joint data analysis workshops. The project produced a shared database of coccidiostat cross-contamination incidents from participating feed mills in Vojvodina and Bács-Kiskun county.

projects.title: Razvoj fermentisanih mlečnih proizvoda poboljšane teksture primenom autohtonih EPS-produkujućih starter kultura Vojvodine
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj izolaciju, karakterizaciju i tehnološku evaluaciju autohtonih sojeva mlečnokiselinskih bakterija poreklom iz tradicionalnih mlečnih proizvoda Vojvodine sa sposobnošću produkcije egzopolisaharida. Tokom projekta izolovano je ukupno 47 sojeva, od kojih je 11 pokazalo potvrđenu EPS produkciju u mleku. Odabrani sojevi testirani su u pilot-fermentacijama (zapremine 50 L) u kombinaciji sa komercijalnim kulturama radi optimizacije teksturnih svojstava niskomasnih jogurta. Projektom je finansirana nabavka modula za teksturnu profilnu analizu i oprema za čuvanje radnih kultura. Rezultati su objavljeni u dva rada u recenzovanim časopisima i saopšteni na dva međunarodna skupa.
partners: Institut za prehrambene tehnologije, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu

projects.title: Kinetičko modelovanje i skaliranje procesa fermentacije mlečnih gelova obogaćenih prebioticima
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat istražuje matematičke modele acidifikacije koji uzimaju u obzir interakciju između puferskog kapaciteta recepture (inulin, pektin, β-glukan), aktivnosti starter kultura i reoloških promena tokom geliranja. Đurđica Žigić odgovorna je za eksperimentalno određivanje kinetičkih parametara acidifikacije i reološku karakterizaciju model-sistema. Planirano je razvijanje softverskog alata za predviđanje trajanja fermentacije pri promeni formulacije ili temperature inkubacije, uz validaciju na pilot skali od 200 L u saradnji sa industrijskim partnerom. projects.title: Integrated Sensor-Based Monitoring for Quality-Preserving Aeration Management in Cereal Silos
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: GRAINWATCH aims to develop and validate a low-cost sensor network and decision-support protocol for aeration management in flat-bottom silos storing maize and wheat in Vojvodina. The project combines temperature cable arrays, in-silo moisture probes, and an external weather data feed to generate aeration recommendations. Todić is responsible for the experimental grain sampling campaigns at the FINS pilot silo, data quality control, and laboratory reference analyses. The project works with two cooperating storage operators in the Bačka region to validate the monitoring approach under commercial conditions. Expected outputs include a validated sensor placement protocol and an aeration scheduling guide adapted to Pannonian climatic conditions.

projects.title: Optimisation of Extrusion Parameters for Triticale and Sorghum Expanded Food Products
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigated how die geometry, barrel temperature profiling, and screw speed interact to determine cell structure and starch digestibility in extruded triticale and sorghum products. A full factorial design at pilot scale was employed, covering three die diameters, three temperature profiles, and four screw speeds. In vitro starch digestibility assays, X-ray microtomography, and SME logging were the primary analytical tools. The project produced three journal papers and contributed to the PhD supervision of one student. Equipment upgrades to the FINS pilot extrusion hall, including additional in-line pressure transducers and a data logging interface, were funded under this project.

projects.title: Functional Cereal-Based Extruded Products from Underutilised Grain Species
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian research institutions and one SME partner, aimed at developing extruded snack and breakfast cereal prototypes from triticale, sorghum, and emmer wheat. The project combines agronomic characterisation of raw materials with extrusion processing optimisation and consumer acceptance testing. Ranković is responsible for the extrusion processing work packages conducted on the Serbian side, including pilot-scale trials and in vitro digestibility assessments. Outputs include a shared pilot production protocol and a joint training module for food technologists in the cross-border region.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Faculty of Food Science, Budapest
Keresgrain Ltd., Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Press Cake Protein Valorisation for Sustainable Monogastric Feed in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PRESKACE addresses the underutilisation of cold-press oilseed residues—primarily sunflower and hemp cake—as protein sources in conventional feed chains on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. The project maps regional press cake volumes, characterises protein fractions from industrial batches, and develops and validates pilot-scale fractionation protocols. Andrea Popović contributes to Work Package 2, responsible for laboratory-scale fractionation trials and anti-nutritional factor analyses at FINS. Outcomes include standardised fractionation guidelines and a small-scale demonstration pellet produced with cross-border raw material. Project partners include an oilseed processing cooperative from Bačka Topola and an agricultural university department from Szeged.
partners: Vojvodinaoil Cooperative, Bačka Topola, Serbia
Department of Animal Husbandry and Feed Science, University of Southern Pannonia, Szeged, Hungary

projects.title: Optimising Controlled Malting of Vojvodina-Grown Barley and Rye for Enzyme-Active Sourdough Flatbread Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project set out to establish quantitative links between malting process parameters—germination temperature, duration, and kilning endpoint—and the resulting spatial enzyme activity profiles across barley and rye grain cross-sections, with the goal of identifying processing windows that simultaneously maximise phytate reduction and maintain acceptable dough functionality in sourdough flatbread applications. Work packages covered agronomic characterisation of six local barley and two rye varieties, laboratory malting optimisation, enzyme activity mapping using the vibratome micro-extraction protocol, flatbread formulation trials, and an in vitro mineral bioaccessibility study. Results were used to draft process guidelines for small-scale craft malt producers in Vojvodina.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Enzyme Activity Management in Regional Cereal Malt Production: Linking Grain Biology to Product Quality in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border project addressing enzyme activity management in malt production relevant to both artisanal and semi-industrial fermented cereal products across the Vojvodina–South Hungarian plain region. FINS led the work package on enzyme characterisation and spatial mapping. Hungarian partners contributed variety evaluation and malting trials on Hungarian-registered barley cultivars. A joint barley germplasm evaluation was conducted over two growing seasons, and comparative malting experiments were run in both countries under unified protocols developed during the project. Outputs included a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) technical guide for small malt house operators and a shared sample archive of malted grain from eleven varieties.
partners: Department of Food Science, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Szarvas Campus, Hungary
Agricultural Extension Service of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Structural Determinants of Prebiotic Activity in Cereal Hull Polysaccharides: From Molecular Characterisation to Gut Microbiota Response
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS)
projects.summary: The project investigated how specific structural features of arabinoxylan and beta-glucan isolated from oat and spelt hull fractions determine prebiotic outcome in simulated and ex vivo gut fermentation models. Work packages covered: (1) systematic extraction and fractionation of hull polysaccharides from genetically diverse oat and spelt accessions; (2) full structural and molecular weight characterisation by SEC-MALS, HPAEC-PAD, FT-IR, and NMR; (3) in vitro batch and semi-continuous fermentation with human faecal inocula; and (4) multivariate modelling linking structural descriptors to prebiotic index and SCFA profiles. The project produced a predictive structural screening tool and a curated dataset of 38 hull fractions across seven cereal species.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Food Technology and Biotechnology, University of Zagreb

projects.title: Valorisation of Cereal Processing By-Products Through Dietary Fibre Recovery and Functional Characterisation
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CERVAL brought together food research institutes in Vojvodina and southern Hungary to develop scalable processes for recovering dietary fibre from oat, spelt, and barley milling by-products. The Novi Sad team led the work package on physicochemical and functional characterisation, contributing SEC-MALS and viscometric analysis of fibre extracts produced at pilot scale (50 kg dry hull batches) by the Hungarian partner. Joint in vitro fermentation assays established baseline prebiotic activity data for fractions produced under varying extraction conditions. The project generated data relevant to both food ingredient manufacturers and agricultural processors seeking to add value to hull and bran streams currently used for animal feed.
partners: Institute of Food Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Food Science, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Budapest

projects.title: Vojvodina Quantum Network Feasibility Study and Demonstrator
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to assess the technical and infrastructural requirements for deploying a small quantum key distribution network across three institutional nodes in Novi Sad, using existing dark fibre from the academic network operator. Activities included fibre characterisation, polarisation drift modelling on deployed links, active compensation hardware development, and a security requirements study for potential institutional end users. The project funded the acquisition of InGaAs detector modules and time-tagging electronics, and supported two doctoral students. Results fed into the 2026 deployed-fibre entanglement distribution experiment. A public report with link budget data and infrastructure recommendations was delivered to the Provincial Secretariat.

projects.title: Photonic Entanglement Sources for Secure Optical Links
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PHOTOLINK targets improvements in the brightness and fibre-coupling efficiency of PPKTP-based entangled photon sources suitable for deployment in metropolitan QKD links. The project combines waveguide source fabrication in collaboration with a partner group in Ljubljana, detector characterisation at 1310 nm and 1550 nm, and integration testing on the group's campus testbed. A secondary workstream addresses the polarisation control hardware required for unattended operation over deployed fibre. The project supports two doctoral students and one postdoctoral researcher. Dissemination activities include a regional workshop on quantum photonics for industry and academic stakeholders scheduled for late 2025.

University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, Slovenia
Institute of Physics Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Fibre-Optic Sensing for Integrity Monitoring of Ageing Buried Pipeline Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the problem of monitoring strain, temperature, and ground movement on ageing buried gas and district heating pipelines in Serbia, where a large proportion of the network dates from before 1990. The core tasks included development of a rugged FBG sensor package suitable for outdoor and underground installation, laboratory validation on DN200 and DN300 steel pipe specimens under combined mechanical and thermal loading, and a field pilot on two pipeline sections in Vojvodina. A low-cost multi-channel interrogation unit was developed as part of the project. The project involved partners from the University of Novi Sad and an engineering consultancy, and trained two M.Sc. students and one doctoral candidate.

projects.title: Cross-Border Infrastructure Monitoring Using Distributed Optical Fibre Sensors
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSMON is a bilateral cooperation project between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs aimed at developing a shared methodology for monitoring road bridges and water supply pipelines that cross or are located near the Hungarian–Serbian border. The Novi Sad team leads the work package on sensor selection and installation protocols, contributing expertise in FBG packaging and field deployment. The Pécs team provides distributed Brillouin sensing capabilities. Together the teams are carrying out two pilot monitoring campaigns: one on a reinforced concrete road bridge and one on a DN400 water main. A joint training workshop for infrastructure engineers from both countries is planned for the final project year.

projects.title: National Normative Database for Cognitive and Scholastic Ability Tests in Serbian School-Age Children
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project aimed to collect a nationally representative normative dataset for three cognitive and two scholastic ability instruments, covering children aged 6–16 across all four Serbian statistical regions. Data collection involved 42 primary schools and 6,800 children, with stratification by region, settlement size, school type, and parental education. The project produced continuous norming tables using the cNORM methodology, developed open-access scoring software for school psychologists, and created a reusable anonymised dataset deposited with the Institute for Educational Research. projects.title: Adaptive Cognitive Screening for Early Educational Intervention in Vojvodina Schools
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research

A feasibility trial in 12 Vojvodina schools (approximately 480 children) will evaluate usability, administration time, data quality, and school psychologist acceptance. projects.title: Improving Outcomes in Lactational Breast Infection through Standardised Protocols and Patient Education in the Vojvodina Region
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project aimed to reduce disease severity and treatment delays for lactational mastitis and breast abscess in Vojvodina by developing, piloting, and disseminating region-specific clinical protocols for primary care and hospital settings. projects.title: A Multicentre Prospective Registry for Breast Abscess in the Western Balkans: Epidemiology, Microbiology and Treatment Outcomes
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: This bilateral project between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Sarajevo establishes a shared prospective registry of breast abscess cases across five centres in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. projects.title: Membrane Microdomain Regulation of Nutrient Transporters in Cereal Crops Under Nitrogen and Phosphorus Limitation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates how sterol-enriched membrane microdomains regulate the localisation and activity of high-affinity nutrient transporters, specifically nitrate transporters (NRT2 family) and phosphate transporters (PHT1 family), in wheat and maize roots under nutrient-deficient conditions. Objectives include mapping transporter distribution by immunofluorescence and DRM fractionation, characterising sterol–transporter interactions through molecular modelling and mutant analysis, and measuring uptake rates with stable isotope tracers. Field-relevant wheat cultivars bred at the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, are used as biological material. Results are expected to inform strategies for improving fertiliser use efficiency in cereal crops grown on Serbian agricultural soils.

projects.title: Lipid Composition and Biophysical Properties of Plasma Membranes in Stress-Tolerant Crop Varieties: A Cross-Species Comparison
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This bilateral cooperation project compared plasma membrane lipid and protein composition in drought- and aluminium-tolerant varieties of maize, sunflower, and sorghum between partner teams in Novi Sad and Szeged. Fejsa led the work package on membrane biophysical characterisation, contributing fluorescence anisotropy, DRM isolation, and stopped-flow water permeability measurements from the Novi Sad side. The project produced a joint reference dataset of lipid profiles and DRM proteomes for six cultivar pairs under control and stress conditions, deposited in a shared open-access repository. Training exchanges for two PhD students and a joint summer school were included. The project supported the purchase of a stopped-flow spectrophotometer now available in the Novi Sad laboratory.

projects.title: Soil Physical Degradation Pathways and Recovery Under Conservation Agriculture in the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project examines mechanisms and rates of soil physical degradation — primarily compaction and structural breakdown — on Chernozem and Fluvisol soils across Vojvodina under conservation and conventional tillage systems. Field campaigns at five long-term experiment sites combine cone penetrometry, tension infiltrometry, and undisturbed core sampling with laboratory retention and conductivity measurements. A sub-task quantifies the contribution of controlled versus random wheel traffic to compaction depth distribution. The project also tests the capacity of freeze–thaw cycles and biological activity to restore soil structure in the absence of mechanical loosening. Final outputs include site-specific recovery trajectories and a decision-support worksheet for farm advisors recommending periodic subsoil intervention thresholds.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Tillage Impacts on Soil Water Dynamics and Crop Productivity in the Hungarian–Serbian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: PANNO-TILL compared soil water retention, compaction, and infiltration characteristics across eight paired farm sites straddling the Hungarian–Serbian border, where similar soil parent material and climate allow isolation of management effects from pedological variability. Branka Grujić was responsible for all Serbian field sampling campaigns, laboratory retention curve analysis, and co-authorship of the joint comparative report. Results showed that Hungarian farms in the sample applied deeper tillage on average, resulting in lower CPR in the 20–35 cm layer, whereas Serbian no-till sites exhibited higher surface macroporosity. An agronomic cost–benefit worksheet for tillage intensity choices under Pannonian climate variability was produced as a policy output.
partners: Department of Soil Sciences, Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő
Vojvodina Agricultural Extension Service, Novi Sad
Chamber of Agriculture of Bács-Kiskun County, Kecskemét, Hungary

projects.title: Telephone Speech Resources and Processing for Under-Resourced South Slavic Languages
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project targets the creation of annotated telephone speech resources and the development of robust ASR components for Serbian and related South Slavic languages with limited existing data. Activities include corpus collection from call-centre partners in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, annotation toolchain development, and acoustic model training and evaluation. The project also covers dialect variation analysis and prepares data in formats compatible with CLARIN and META-SHARE infrastructures. Emilija Kapor contributes to corpus design, data collection coordination, and acoustic modelling experiments, and her doctoral research on noisy-channel ASR is embedded within the project's technical workplan.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of Sarajevo
Institute for Serbian Language, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade

projects.title: Pressure Management and Leakage Reduction in Vojvodina Municipal Water Networks
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project supported the design and field implementation of district metered areas and optimised PRV setpoints in three mid-sized municipal water systems in Vojvodina. Activities included hydraulic model construction and calibration, MNF survey campaigns, installation and monitoring of six pressure reducing valves, and development of a practical leakage assessment protocol tailored to data conditions typical of Serbian utilities. The project produced three peer-reviewed publications, one conference paper, and a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat. Two utility partners provided field access and repair crew time as in-kind contributions. A training workshop for utility engineers was organised in Subotica in 2012.
partners: JKP Vodovod Subotica, Serbia
JKP Palić Vodovod, Serbia
Provincial Directorate for Water Management, Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Transient-Based Methods for Leak and Condition Assessment in Buried Water Mains
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: TRANSLEAK was a cross-border cooperation project examining the applicability of controlled transient pressure tests for simultaneous leak detection and pipe condition screening in Hungarian and Serbian distribution networks. The Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica led the work package on field data collection and signal processing, conducting transient surveys on 35 km of pipe across four sites. Hungarian partners contributed laboratory validation experiments and signal interpretation software development. The project delivered a joint field protocol document, two conference papers, and a bilateral database of transient test results matched against independent condition assessment records. Results informed one subsequent journal publication co-authored by project partners.
partners: Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Department of Sanitary Engineering, Hungary
University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering, Hungary
JKP Vodovod Subotica, Serbia

projects.title: Cross-border Agricultural Monitoring and Yield Forecasting Using Copernicus Data in the Hungarian–Serbian Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish a shared satellite-based monitoring service for agricultural parcels in the cross-border region spanning South Bačka (Serbia) and Csongrád-Csanád (Hungary). The BioSense Institute was responsible for processing Sentinel-2 time series, constructing parcel databases from national LPIS sources, and delivering seasonal yield forecast maps. Branislav Lekić contributed the yield modelling component, adapting and validating regression models trained on Serbian data for application to Hungarian parcels. The project produced a web-based dashboard for regional agricultural authorities and published protocols for harmonising cross-border parcel datasets. Final yield forecast maps for winter wheat and maize were delivered to partner organisations at the end of each growing season.
partners: Department of Geoinformatics, University of Pécs
South Bačka Regional Development Agency, Novi Sad
Csongrád-Csanád County Government, Hungary

projects.title: Operational Crop Yield Estimation for the Vojvodina Region Using Fused Optical and SAR Satellite Data
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: CROPSENSE addressed the practical deployment of parcel-level yield prediction for five major crops grown in Vojvodina, with particular focus on reducing dependence on cloud-free optical imagery by incorporating Sentinel-1 SAR data. Branislav Lekić led the work package on data fusion and model development, overseeing the assembly of a multi-year parcel dataset from combine-harvester records provided by three agricultural cooperatives, satellite data processing, and the design of a modular prediction pipeline. The project produced open-source Python tooling for time series fusion, a calibrated yield model ensemble, and a set of validation reports for each crop type. Dissemination included two journal articles, one conference paper, and a technical report delivered to the Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Agricultural Cooperative Zlatna Njiva, Sombor
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Monetary Archives of the Western Balkans: Digitisation, Standardisation, and Historical Analysis of Central Bank Records 1944–1992
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MONARHIV aims to systematically locate, catalogue, and digitise surviving central bank records from the successor states of socialist Yugoslavia, with a primary focus on Serbia, and to make a curated selection available to researchers through an open-access repository. The project involves partnership with the Archive of Yugoslavia, the Historical Archive of Vojvodina, and the National Bank of Serbia's historical collections unit. A secondary objective is the construction of harmonised annual time series for key monetary aggregates—money supply components, credit to government, and foreign exchange reserves—for Yugoslavia and its successor states for the period 1944–1992, filling gaps left by discontinuous official publications. Perišić leads the research team of four, which includes one postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students.
partners: Archive of Yugoslavia, Belgrade
Historical Archive of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Economics, University of Belgrade
